### The room shader, and a build that needs no shader compiler
2026-09-05 - 2026-09-06

**What.** The HD room path is one HLSL source, `specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl`, with
its compiled bytecode checked in beside it as `hd_room_vs.inc` and `hd_room_ps.inc`; the
model path is the same pair around `hd_model.hlsl`. No shader compiler is part of the
build, so the project still builds with nothing but the C++ toolset.
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/bshader.bat` regenerates the `.inc` files with `fxc` from the
Windows SDK, and the call is written at the top of the `.hlsl`. Every generated `.inc`
carries the MD5 hash of the `.hlsl` it was compiled from on its last line, and the engine
build compares the two before it builds, regenerating a shader that is out of step on the
spot.

**Why.** GPLv3 is why the source sits next to the bytecode: a reader of the history gets
the form that can be changed, not only the form the card runs. The shaders are written
against what shader model 3 guarantees - 512 instruction slots - and the device's `ps_3_0`
figure is read at start-up and refused below 512 rather than letting `CreatePixelShader`
fail with an HRESULT. `ps_3_0` has no relative addressing of constant registers, only
`vs_3_0` has, so the dynamic-light loop is unrolled against a compile-time maximum with
the run-time count as a dynamic `if`; written as a plain loop, `fxc` emulates `gLights[i]`
with 32 `cmp` instructions per access, about 140 instructions per light per pixel. The fog
bulb loop stays dynamic because its body is long and its array is short. The hash is of
the content and not a file date, because a fresh clone gives every file the same date. A
checked-in `.inc` can drift from its source when the HLSL is edited without the compiler
being run again: the room pixel shader once stood at 636 slots with eight `pow`
instructions - a Blinn highlight that had been built and rejected for passing 512 - while
its source compiled to 453 slots with none.

**How.** The full register table lives in `hd_room.hlsl` beside the code, and
`specific/hd/hd_render.cpp` is its only writer. `bshader.bat` writes the hash in its
`:stamp` step as a comment line `bshader-stamp <MD5 of the .hlsl>`;
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/be.bat` compares each `.inc`'s line against the hash of its
`.hlsl` and, where they differ, prints `be: regenerating shaders - ... out of step with
the HLSL` and calls `bshader.bat`. Regenerating the `.inc` files by hand reproduces the
checked-in bytecode byte for byte apart from that line. The generated `.inc` files carry
no licence notice of their own, being compiler output. `tomb5.vcxproj` carries the new
`.cpp` files with `/std:c++17` per file and no precompiled header, the new headers, and
the `.hlsl` as a `None` entry, so it is visible in the solution without becoming a build
step. The shipped room shaders stand at 476 pixel-shader and 348 vertex-shader instruction
slots, the model pair at 348 and 553.

**Decisions.** A shader out of step is rebuilt rather than reported, because a build that
quietly draws the wrong thing is the failure the check exists to stop.

**Commits.** `2435068`, `1087750`, `893f999`, `05aeddc`

### The engine's own per-vertex lighting, as shader arithmetic
2026-09-05 - 2026-09-07

**What.** Everything the classic path computes per room vertex on top of the baked light
(`specific/drawroom.cpp`, `aRoomletTransformLight`, lines 305-685) is computed for HD
rooms as well: the dynamic lights of torch, flare, muzzle flash and explosions (pixel
shader, up to 8 per room); the WaterTable choppy displacement (vertex shader, on the
marked vertices); shimmer, mist and reflection (vertex shader, selector per room, switched
by `tomb5.shimmer`); underwater darkening; the Red Alert gas rooms; the underwater screen
wobble (vertex shader, clip-space offset); the distance fog (pixel shader,
`tomb5.distance_fog`, 3..30 blocks); the 128 overbright split; and the fog bulbs (pixel
shader, `tomb5.fog`), of which `HD_MAX_BULBS` = **16** reach the shaders in one frame. The
additive pass multiplies by at most one, as the classic path does, and is weighted from
its own material: material 2 (shafts, lamp cones, window and candle glows) from
`param[1]`, material 14 from `param[1]`, material 15 from `param[2]`, with material 2's
weight breathing `HD_RAY_SWING` = 0.06 of itself once per `param[3]` seconds. A material-2
part whose weight falls outside (0, 1) takes the median weight of its own `(param[0],
param[2])` preset, and an unknown preset takes 0.20. A fog bulb's intensity falls smoothly
to zero at its silhouette and is not cut by a 45 degree cone. An HD item's ambient is
`aAmbientR/G/B` after the engine's own `InitObjectLighting(current_item)` and its light
list is the item's own `il.pCurrentLights` converted to view space one for one,
`HD_MAX_OBJ_LIGHTS` = 12 of them.

**Why.** Without it a torch did not light an HD wall, the distance fog stopped at the door
and three option switches were dead in HD rooms. Sixteen bulbs because a level holds up to
17 (ANDREA2, and TITLE likewise), a single room up to 5 (ANDY3), and up to 16 fall inside
the 20480-unit circle `aBuildFogBulbList` keeps around the camera at once (16 ANDREA2, 14
RICH2, 13 ANDY1, 11 TITLE, 10 RICH1); sixteen is also the classic path's own ceiling,
`RoomletFogBulbs[16]` in `drawroom.cpp` being filled with no bound check at all, and at
six the title screen lost bulbs. The additive ceiling of one: the classic path switches
the specular off for its additive draw type (`specific/polyinsert.cpp`), so a classic
additive polygon is at most `texel * 1`, while the HD pass multiplied up to `texel * 2`
and blended ONE/ONE - 56.3 per cent of RICH1's additive channels exceed 1.0 (mean 1.26,
max 2.00) and 10.9 per cent of ANDREA1's; beyond that, the HD art's shafts and lamp cones
are fans of dozens of quads that all meet at the lamp and therefore SUM, and painting them
with no weight of their own saturates them to white. A quarter-swing moved a candle glow
by 8 to 9 per cent of the whole pixel between two arbitrary moments; at 0.06 the worst
pixel of a sampled room moves 5.4 per cent instead of 17.0. The chord through a fog
sphere, `2*sqrt(r^2 - d^2)`, has an infinite derivative at the rim, so a per-pixel
evaluation stands the intensity up vertically at the silhouette where the classic
per-vertex evaluation lets the rasteriser smear it; and the classic cull - a 45 degree
cone about the view axis - was affordable at 4:3, where the frame reaches 40 degrees to
the side, while `AlterFOV` (`specific/3dmath.cpp`) builds the perspective from `height *
320/240` and uses that value across as well, so 16:9 turns a nominal 80 degrees into about
96 across and the first person view's 90 to 100 into 107 to 118, which is 53 to 59 degrees
to the side and draws the cut as a straight vertical line with fog on one side and none on
the other. Two brightness scales are bridged: the classic path builds a colour in 0..255
and splits it at 128, doubling below and putting the halved excess into the specular
colour, which the fixed-function pipeline adds after the texture modulation
(`D3DRS_SPECULARENABLE` on, `specific/function_table.cpp:104`); a classic surface
therefore covers 0..2, and the `.TRG`'s baked light covers the same 0..2 as `colour1 +
colour2`, used as a straight multiply. That the two triples ADD is this project's own
count, not a reading of anybody's renderer: on the 107,118 classic room vertices a `.TRG`
vertex of the same room stands on exactly, the sum orders the vertices the way the classic
prelight does better than the product, `colour1` or `colour2` alone (`TrgProbe
-shadeorder`; the table is in the entry "Where the HD rules come from", section 2.4).
Below 128 the two are the same line, and that is the bridge. The split itself is not
reproduced, and that is the single place this work leaves the classic path: the split is a
hardware workaround for fitting a brightness of 2 into two bytes, and a shader has floats;
following it would dull every bright surface the HD art bakes - 20 of 384 sampled light
channels in ANDREA1 room 19 are above 1, 111 of 384 in room 69, and RICH1 room 12 reaches
the full 2.0, so `texel x 1.5` would become `texel x 1 + 0.25`. The fog bulbs keep the
split, because for them it is not a workaround: a bulb is haze between the camera and the
surface, so its density has to darken the multiply and its colour be added on top, or a
bulb in front of a black wall would not glow. The HD path's brightness is a strictly
linear function of the ambient it is handed (the model's own mean rises at a constant
ratio of 0.31 to 0.32 of the ambient over ambients 8 to 255), so a creature at ambient 8
is dark because the room is dark, which is the classic answer too; the twelve-light limit
against the classic list's 21 (`ITEM_INFO::il.CurrentLights[21]`) is the one term that can
differ, so it is counted on the log rather than argued.

**How.** Each contribution hangs off the very global the classic path reads, in one place
- `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`, `FillFrameLighting` and `FillRoomLighting` - so a switch
cannot be on in one path and off in the other; `tomb5.fog` does not reach the shader at
all but gates `aBuildFogBulbList` (`game/draw.cpp:1011`), so with fog off both paths lose
their bulbs in the same frame. Every contribution is computed in the classic path's own
units and order and converted with the one line `f = light * 127.5`, back with `light = f
* 2 / 255`. `specific/hd/hd_light.cpp` holds two transcriptions of one vertex colour - one
of `aRoomletTransformLight` with its longs and its truncations, one of the HLSL - and
`RoomProbe -paritycheck` runs both over 128 of a room's vertices, printing the
contribution in 0..255 before the split and the final brightness on a white texel. What is
per pixel and what is per vertex is decided by the function: dynamic lights, fog bulbs and
distance fog are smooth functions of a position and are per pixel; the WaterTable effects
stay per vertex, the table being indexed by the position quantised to 64 x 64 x 128 units,
so per pixel would paint visible blocks. The water marks are computed, not read - the
`.TRG` marks nothing - and are worked out once at level build on the classic vertices
(`aRoomVertexWaterMarks`, new) and carried to the HD vertex at the same room-local
position through a hash, the road TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931 - takes for its own water flag; three bits per vertex in
a fifth vertex element of four bytes, the vertex growing from 20 to 24, and which bit the
shader looks at is decided per frame out of `r->flags`, because a room can flood while a
level runs. That project's `hd.light_stage` A/B switch, whose stage 0 throws the baked
`.TRG` light away for a flat `vec3(0.75)`, was not carried over: here `hd_enable` already
gives that comparison. The 16 bulbs occupy pixel registers `c40`-`c71`, two per bulb,
uploaded once per frame by `HDRenderFrameBegin` with `SetPixelShaderConstantF(40, ...)`,
and both pixel shaders share that upload and must agree (`hd_room.hlsl`, `hd_model.hlsl`);
the pixel shaders come to 355 (room) and 340 (model) of 512 slots at that point, about 4.5
slots per bulb. The additive ceiling is keyed on `gPass.y` in both shaders;
`MaterialAddWeight` (`hd_render.cpp`) reads the weights, 20 to 131 parts per level take
one and the smallest is 0.025, the sun shafts being keyed on the one tuple carrying
`param[3]` = 16 seconds (34 parts in three levels) and brought to a mean of 1.7 per cent
of white with a peak of 15.7, under the 16 to 31 per cent a reference picture supplied for
this project shows for such a streak; where the file gives no usable number a part falls
through to 1 or to its preset median, and materials 0, 1, 6, 7, 8, 13 and the destructible
high-bit numbers draw exactly as they did. The swing dies with `hd_motion` 0. The fog bulb
chord is weighted with a `smoothstep` over its own range, rim weight `kRim` = 0.35f, in
the shader and in its twin in `hd_light.cpp` behind a `soften` flag so `RoomProbe
-paritycheck` can run both formulas side by side; what remains of the cone is the half
that is exact rather than conservative, `P.z + rad <= 0` on the bulb, which also settles
the camera-inside-the-bulb case, and the branch that returned a density for a bulb behind
the camera returns zero. The deviation is named rather than hidden: the classic path culls
fog at 45 degrees off axis and this one does not. The model shader takes the same bulb
term, and a material 2 swing under half a second stands still: see "The light shafts
compose as screen, a stacked sea is drawn once, a fast swing stands still" below. A step
in the baked light at a room boundary is the art's own - the HD path culls a dynamic light
against the whole room's box where the classic path culls against a roomlet's, with the
same test and the same falloff, and across four sampled portals the two sides' baked light
at the same world position differs by up to 0.234 on a 0..2 scale with no side above 1.
Item lighting: `HD_MAX_OBJ_LIGHTS` in `specific/hd/hd_model.h` (mirrored in
`hd_model.hlsl`), the item lighting and the `HDLOG creaturelight` line in
`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp`, Lara's own list in `hd_laradraw.cpp`, the `clipped=` count on
the `HDLOG frame` line in `hd_level.cpp`. Seams behind `-log`: `clipped` counted for a
whole level - one line at the first frame that clips, naming the room and how many lights
and bulbs were offered, and one total at the level's end, both `Fill...Lighting` functions
counting what they turn away instead of stopping at the cap - `HDLOG creaturelight` once a
game second for up to six `objects[].intelligent` items with the classic colour, the HD
colour, their difference, the distance to the lens, the ambient and the light counts, and
the level's `motion=` line with the weighted parts, the smallest weight and the swinging
parts. Tools: `RoomProbe` (`-paritycheck`, the `additive:` line, a bulb dropped at the new
maximum) and `ModelProbe -name SWAT -shade N`.

### The light shafts compose as screen, a stacked sea is drawn once, a fast swing stands still
2026-09-26

**What.** In the HD additive pass the draw calls of `.TRG` material 2 - the light shafts,
lamp cones and window and candle glows - compose as screen, dst + src - dst * src, instead
of the ONE / ONE sum, and are sampled with the anisotropic filter; every other additive
material keeps the sum and the trilinear filter. An additive material 16 part whose
triangles the file carries three or more times, stacked in y, is drawn once. A material 2
part whose swing period (`param[3]`) is under half a second draws still. The model
shader's fog-bulb term is the room shader's: the exact behind-the-camera cull and the
softened rim.

**Why.** The shafts were harsh because their cards stack, not because a card is bright.
ANDREA2 room 131's window shaft is about 130 overlapping cards, 6.2 over the average pixel
and 12 at most; one card reaches at most 0.46 of white, but the unclamped sum averages
1.22 and peaks at 3.54 times white, so 56.7 per cent of the shaft's pixels clipped in the
additive pass alone and the core was a flat white slab crossed by the cards' own edges.
RICH1 room 3's grate shaft is 405 triangles in one square whose vertex light is 2.0 at
every vertex, capped to a flat 1.0, and washed Lara out inside it. The harsh cyan of JOBY4
room 19 was mostly its sea: group 19 part 3 is 73,728 additive triangles, four exact
copies of 18,048 footprints at y -4269, -4253 and twice -4237, drawn at weight 1 with a
vertex red of 0, so green and blue clipped and the hue locked to cyan; JOBY5 carries the
same fourfold sheet in groups 65 and 82 and a threefold one in group 117. ANDREA2's 0.06 s
period made its swing a 16.7 Hz flicker. And the model shader's own bulb term kept the
classic 45-degree cone, whose per-pixel edge cut haze away in a first-person frame, and
the raw chord, whose rim stood brighter than the room term. The numbers come from
RoomProbe on the additive pass over black and from a footprint count over the fifteen
`.TRG` files through the vendored TRForge reader.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`: the screen blend - `draw_pass` sets `D3DRS_SRCBLEND`
`D3DBLEND_INVDESTCOLOR` against the pass's `D3DBLEND_ONE` when a run of material 2 draw
calls starts and puts `D3DBLEND_ONE` back when it ends, src * (1 - dst) + dst being the
screen; the sampler goes to `D3DSAMP_MINFILTER` `D3DTEXF_ANISOTROPIC` with
`D3DSAMP_MAXANISOTROPY` min(16, `MaxAnisotropy`) for the same run, when the device reports
`D3DPRASTERCAPS_ANISOTROPY` and `D3DPTFILTERCAPS_MINFANISOTROPIC`, and back to
`D3DTEXF_LINEAR` and the anisotropy it found. The screen composition of the glow is the
rule of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931, credited at
the blend. Screen and the sum do not commute, so where a glow overlaps another additive
material (JOBY4 room 19's rays over its sea) the picture follows the draw order: within a
group the sort key's, led by the page slot, and between groups the order of the groups.
Every additive draw call holds one material: `HDTri::material` and `HDRange::material`,
`MaterialBase(part)` in pass 2 and 0 in the other two passes, in the sort key after the
destructible id and in the range merge. The stacked sea: `MarkStackedCopies` builds a
footprint key per triangle of an additive material 16 run - the corners' x and z in (x, z)
order and the two other corners' height above the first, so only an exact vertical
translate is a copy - sorts the keys, and where a footprint holds three or more triangles
marks every one whose y sum is above the smallest (the topmost copy stays, y counting
downwards). The build loop calls it per part and skips a marked triangle after the
horizontal-plane rows, so the water-surface tables still see every copy; two-sheet stacks
never qualify. The period fence: `MaterialAddPeriod` returns 0, a still part, below
`kAddStillBelow` = 0.5 s; 0.05 to 60 s stays the range that is read at all. Diagnostics
for the tools alone, never called by the engine: `HDRenderStackOverride`,
`HDRenderSwingOverride`, `HDRenderAdditiveOnly` and `HDRenderGlowOverride` (declared in
`hd_render.h`), and three counts in `HDRenderStats` (`addStillParts`, `stackedParts`,
`stackedTris`). `specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_model.hlsl`: `BulbIntensity` culls on `P.z + rad
<= 0` and weights the chord with `smoothstep(0, kRim, chord / diameter)`, `kRim` 0.35,
line for line as `hd_room.hlsl`; `hd_model_ps.inc` and `hd_model_vs.inc` regenerated by
`bshader.bat`, the model pixel shader at 353 instruction slots. Tools: `RoomProbe -glow`
(`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/RoomProbe.cpp`) draws the additive pass of every drawn group
again after the full frame, alone over black, once over the frame's depth and once over a
cleared one, each in its own state bracket; `-glowblend add|screen`, `-aniso 0|1`,
`-fastswing`, `-stackedseas` and `-addmat <n>` draw the earlier pictures and one
material's glow out of the same build, and the `additive:` block prints the new counts.
`ModelProbe -bulb <x y z radius density [r g b]>` puts view-space fog bulbs into the
frame's lighting block. With `hd_enable` 0 nothing of it runs; no engine file outside
`hd_render.cpp`, `hd_render.h`, `hd_model.hlsl` and its two `.inc` changed.

**Decisions.** `param[3]` stays a period, and anything under 0.5 s draws still. Screen for
material 2 only; every other additive material keeps ONE / ONE. The presets stay unless a
shaft's mean falls under 55 per cent of before, and then that preset's weight rises until
it does not, never past 1 per cent clipped - none did. A sea stacked three times or more
is drawn once; the double sheets two units apart stay double. The model shader takes the
room's bulb term. No face culling of material 2, no sun rays, no fine modulation. The
depth fade, and the near, `|N.V|`, edge and end fades of a dedicated glow shader, are left
to the entry that follows, "The light shafts have a pixel shader of their own".

### The light shafts have a pixel shader of their own
2026-09-26

**What.** The additive draw calls of `.TRG` material 2 - the light shafts, lamp cones and
window and candle glows - are drawn with a pixel shader of their own, `hd_glow.hlsl`,
behind the room's own vertex shader. It draws what the room pixel shader draws in the
additive pass and multiplies four fades onto it: near the camera, where a card is seen
edge-on (`|N.V|`), at the card sides of a part cut out of the middle of its page, and at
both ends of an asset cut out of its page along v. Three weight presets of material 2 are
raised where the fades would take a glow under 55 per cent of the mean the sum drew (the
entry that follows sets the gains anew). Every other additive material, material 16
included, is drawn by the room shader as before.

**Why.** After screen composition the clipping was gone, and what stayed in the glow alone
over the scene's depth (RoomProbe `-glow`) was: the cards' own edges, neighbour steps of
more than 40 of 255 by the thousand in ANDREA2 room 131's and RICH1 room 3's shafts - the
window shaft takes u 48..206 of page 3038, whose columns there still carry 61 to 64 per
cent of the brightest one, so every card side is a line; the camera inside a shaft, the
glow covering 85.6 and 88.1 per cent of the frame at a mean near half of white; a card
seen in its own plane, its streaks converging on the plane's vanishing point (TITLE room
6); and RICH1's grate shaft, a cylinder of cards whose vertex light is a flat 1.0, a block
of equal brightness with the rings of its foot showing, where `|N.V|` gives the chord
profile of a column.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_glow.hlsl` (new) includes `hd_room.hlsl` and so reads
the same `VS_OUT`, registers and `BulbIntensity`; `GlowPS` is `RoomPS` in the additive
pass - texel, alpha test, vertex and dynamic light, WaterTable term, distance fog, the
ceiling of one, the bulbs' darkening, the caustic, texel alpha, weight and swing - less
the ripple, the gloss and the bulbs' added colour, which are zero on these draw calls, and
times the fades: near, `smoothstep` over `HD_GLOW_NEAR` = 1024 units of `|viewPos|`;
facing, `|N.V|` with the interpolated file normal, or with the face normal out of
`ddx`/`ddy` of the view position, chosen per part by a constant; edge, `smoothstep` over
the outer 15 per cent of the part's used u range; ends, `smoothstep` over the fade length
at both ends of the asset along its page-v axis, `dot(roomPos, axis)` against the asset's
ends in the drawn room's frame. The fade near the camera and the `|N.V|` term are the
rules of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931 - for its
glow material, credited in the shader's header; the file-normal variant, the edge and the
end fade are this project's. The per-draw constants sit in c77 to c79, which no pixel
shader of the renderer reads or holds a literal in; the glow shader's own literals take c0
to c15 outside c4 and c10 and c36 to c39, so gRipple (c36) is written again when the room
shader comes back. `hd_glow_ps.inc` is 479 instruction slots; `bshader.bat` compiles it
with the others and `be.bat` guards it. `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`: `BuildGlowParts` runs
before the build loop and takes per material 2 part with additive triangles the u and v
range; the edge fade where u spans less than 90 per cent of the page; the face normal
where `|N.f|` is under 0.9 on more than half of the part's corners; the page-v axis as the
mean of dP/dv over its triangles. Parts of one tuple and one page whose world boxes come
within a sector (`kGlowTouch`) join one asset; the rooms' origins for that come with the
room boxes, `HDRoomBox::originX/originZ` (`hd_render.h`, filled in `hd_level.cpp` and
`RoomProbe.cpp`), and without them an asset is one group's parts. The asset's axis is the
sum of its parts', its ends the extent of all their vertices along it; the end fade is 512
units (`kGlowEndFade`), at most a quarter of the extent, and only for an asset with a part
that uses less than 90 per cent of the page's v. `GlowConstants` turns a part into the
three registers; a fade that does not apply gets a range the pixel never leaves. The glow
part is in the additive sort key after the material and in the range merge; the parts are
numbered in file order, so the triangle order is the one before. `draw_pass` switches to
the glow shader for a range with a glow part and back to the room shader for any other and
at the end of the pass, the per-part registers written when the part changes. `GlowGain`
multiplies the weight of a glow part by its preset's gain. `HDRenderGlowOverride` takes a
third switch, `noShader`, and `HDRenderGlowPartCount` / `HDRenderGlowPartInfo` hand the
decisions to the tool; `HDRenderStats` counts `glowParts`, `glowEdgeParts`,
`glowFaceParts`, `glowAssets`. Over the fifteen levels the loader takes 253 material 2
parts in 182 assets, 13 with the edge fade, 31 on the face normal and 94 in 78 assets with
an end fade; ANDREA2's window shaft is one asset of rooms 93, 131 and 217. Tools:
`RoomProbe -glowps 0|1` draws material 2 with the room shader (0) or the glow shader (1,
the renderer's own), and the additive block prints a `glow:` line and one `glow part:`
line per part. With `hd_enable` 0 the glow shader is never created (`HDRenderInit`), no
part is taken (`HDRenderLevelBegin`) and no origin filled (`BuildRoomBoxes`), all behind
`HDEnabled`.

**Decisions.** The fade near the camera works within 1024 units. The fades belong to
material 2 alone; no part is spared them, haze and mist included (settled in the entry
that follows). `|N.V|` takes the file normal where it agrees with the faces and the face
normal elsewhere; this per-part choice is this project's own, re-derived on this project's
own A/B over the 46 views (RoomProbe `-glowps`, each normal forced everywhere against the
per-part choice) in the entry "The glow's normal, re-derived", where neither normal
everywhere wins a view. The end fade takes the asset's whole extent, so that the parts of
one shaft do not seam at the room borders, and only where the art is cut out of its page
in v: over an asset that uses the page's whole v the page fades by itself, and an end fade
there took JOBY2's lamp cones of page 3070 the light at the lamp. Three presets were
raised by the 55 per cent rule, never past 1 per cent clipped: (1.5, 0.4) to 1.45, (0.5,
0.6) to 1.25 and (0.5, 0.8) to 1.03. No depth fade where a shaft meets a wall, no sun
rays, no fine modulation, no face culling of material 2.

### The light shafts are as faint as the church mist
2026-09-27

**What.** The glow shader's gain on a `.TRG` material 2 part is set per preset - the whole
parameter tuple - so that every light shaft, ray fan, lamp cone and window glow shows at
the strength of the church mist of ANDY2 room 6: in its brightest view it is no brighter
than that mist, barely visible. The mist itself, the candle halos beside it, ANDREA1's
haze and RICH2 room 78's glow keep a gain of 1.

**Why.** The mist of page 2100, preset (1, 0.2, 2, 1), is the strength that is right as
the game draws it after the fades, and it is the measure here: in a RoomProbe view of
ANDY2 room 6 matched to that room as seen in play, its share of the frame's luma over the
pixels it lights is 5.1 of 255 on average and 8.0 at the 95th percentile. The rule of the
entry before - no preset under 55 per cent of its brightness before the fades - kept the
shafts far above the mist: the 95th percentile of the share of the frame, in each preset's
brightest view, was 191.8 in ANDREA2 room 131, 223.5 in room 225 and 42.6 at the title's
ray fans. A reference picture supplied for this project shows the title flyby's far ray
fan of page 2146, seen past the churchyard wall, with no lift above its surroundings
within the background's own error, where this build drew it about 20 of 255 above them.
One factor for all does not do: the gains that reach the mist lie from 0.0128 (ANDREA3
room 36's window glow) to 0.584 (JOBY5 room 115's glow), ANDREA2 room 131's shaft at
0.0273 and the title's fans at 0.171. The flash that comes now and then in ANDY2 room 6 is
not a gain of material 2: bursts of 0.8 to 1.3 seconds, three to four seconds apart,
stepping at the 30 Hz logic rate, lift the lit surfaces of the room's middle and right and
with them the beams of page 2100, because the glow shader multiplies the page by the
room's light; no file of the HD path reads the storm's `LightningRGB` (`game/draw.cpp`),
and the bursts' length and spacing match the storm clock there (`LightningCount` runs 16
to 47 steps, a strike starts with a chance of 1 in 128 per step), so the storm reaches the
room by some path other than the sky's.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`: `GlowGain` holds 22 entries keyed by the four
parameters exactly as the file stores them (literals checked bit for bit against all 26
material 2 tuples of the fifteen files); a tuple the table does not name draws at 1. The
gain multiplies the weight of a draw call that carries a glow part, which exists only for
the glow shader: with `-glowps 0`, as in `HDRenderGlowOverride`'s `noShader`, no glow part
is built and no gain applies. Each gain was found by drawing: the brightest RoomProbe view
of the tuple, `-glow -addmat 2` against `-addmat 99`, the 95th percentile of the share of
the frame over the pixels the glow of `84841d8` lit above 2, the gain scaled by 8 over it
and the view drawn again, four passes at most; an 8-bit frame drops a card's share once it
falls under half a step, so the picture does not follow a gain this small in proportion.
The 95th percentile of the share then lies between 7.71 and 8.09 in all 21 tuples with a
gain below 1 and a view that sees them; RICH2 room 78's glow shows 6.86 at gain 1 and is
not lowered, and RICH1 room 17's glow, which no camera in its room sees, takes the gain of
its sibling (1, 0.2, 0.1, 0.6). With `hd_enable` 0 or `-glowps 0` there is no glow part
and no gain; the shaders, the four fades, screen composition, the anisotropic filter, the
stacked seas, the still fast swings and every additive material other than 2 stay as they
were, and so does the weight each part reads from the art (`MaterialAddWeight`), the sun
shafts' 0.08 included: the gain multiplies it.

**Decisions.** The strength follows the church mist and the reference picture, not a share
of the brightness the glow had before its fades: the 55 per cent rule of the entry before
is withdrawn. The haze and mist layers keep the fades: ANDY2's mist at its faded level is
the target, and ANDREA1's page-3232 haze needs no exemption. Each preset gets its own
gain, because the presets need gains 45 times apart; the measure is the 95th percentile of
its share of the frame in its brightest view, 8 of 255 like the mist's. Nothing is raised
above the gain it had. ANDY2 room 6 stays as it is, the candle halos beside the mist
included, and so does the storm flash in that room.

**Commits.** `84841d8` (comparison base), `d39ac2e`

### The sky
2026-09-05 - 2026-10-18

**What.** Where a level's `.TRG` carries a sky group, the HD path draws the sky of the HD
art - a panorama band and one to three cloud sheets - in the classic horizon mesh's place;
the moon, the stars and the lightning flash still run. Where a level has no sky group the
engine's procedural sky is drawn as before and the HD walls paint over it: JOBY3 and JOBY5
have none, TITLE has two, and the other twelve levels have one, always the last group. The
sky is drawn in a depth slice of its own at the back of the depth buffer. Its alpha pass
blends - source alpha against one minus source alpha, alpha reference 0 - with the depth
write on, and is drawn in the order the `.TRG` lists its parts, back to front, with no
depth test among those parts. The script's two classic flat layers are left out where the
HD sky stands for them - where the sky group holds a cloud sheet or a band in the opaque
pass, and in a level that takes the deep water look while the water sheets are on - and
are drawn over the band otherwise; layer 1 is drawn over the dome when `GF_LIGHTNING` is
set, and only then, because the game paints the flash through that layer in the
lightning's own colour. Where layers are drawn over an HD sky that has a cloud sheet
(ANDY1 to ANDY3, where layer 1 carries the lightning), they wear that sheet's HD page
instead of the level's classic sky page. Both poles of the band are closed by a cap of the
band's own. Rain and snow are not touched. A volumetric cloud layer exists in RoomProbe
alone and nowhere on the game's path.

**Why.** Every `.TRG` whose level has a sky ends in one group past the last room: an
origin-centred dome of one band and up to three flat sheets. The band is a sphere of
radius about 4,100 about the camera (ANDREA3's 4,891, its centre 818 units off; the others
centred up to 1,271 units above or below it), 1,280 triangles in 21 rings from elevation
-75 to +75 degrees, wearing one 4096 x 2048 panorama out of the page block 7000..7011
whose v runs linear in the band's elevation, alpha 0 above about 27 degrees and opaque
below about 9. A sheet is a flat square of 5 x 5 or 10 x 10 tiles of one 512 x 512 page
each at 1,752 to 4,996 units over the camera, up to 24,000 units in half width, material
1, scrolling on its own parameters (`p1` -0.03 to 0.06 page units per second), with baked
light of 0.26 to 2.00. The band's baked light is exactly zero on every vertex of every
level, so through the room formula it would be black. The two alpha-pass sky pages carry a
soft ramp with every value in between, and a test at 0.5 leaves a feathered cloud as a
hard-edged silhouette and puts a hard rim across the dome. The discs hang in front of the
band overhead and behind it at the horizon, so no single draw order with the depth test
gets both right: with the band drawn first, the band's sphere wrote depth over its whole
empty upper half and every sheet failed the depth test wherever it lies beyond the sphere
- a sheet at height h is nearer than the sphere only above asin(h/4100) - which showed in
JOBY2 as a cap of one cloud picture, a ring of another and black between them with a hard
circle round the cap. The `.TRG`'s part order is back to front in all thirteen sky levels
(the sheets from the highest to the lowest, the band last). JOBY4's sky group is the band
alone, one flat colour (page 7006), while its script draws both layers on the level's own
sky page, which in JOBY4 is the sea's surface seen from below; leaving the layers out over
that band dropped the moving surface, drawing them puts a classic surface over the whole
sea, and in the deep look with the water sheets on, the HD art of room 19 and this
project's water look stand for that surface. The level's classic sky page is opaque in
ANDY2 and ANDY3, so on the flat path layer 1 covered the HD dome with the classic clouds.
The band ends at its last ring on either side - 68 to 79 degrees under the horizon and 75
to 79 over it in the thirteen sky levels - and left both poles open, the frame's clear
colour showing as a disc overhead or underfoot.

**How.** A sky part with no light anywhere is drawn at light 1 and its page is the whole
picture. No scaling and no rotation: the sphere sits far inside the far plane of 20480,
the discs reach past it, which only cuts a disc where the band already covers it, and the
group is centred on the origin, so it takes the matrix the classic path builds for its own
horizon - `phd_TranslateAbs(camera.pos)` and nothing else - and rides on the camera
exactly as the horizon did. The viewport's `MinZ` is pushed to `HD_SKY_MINZ` = 0.996 for
the length of the call, folding the whole sky into the last four thousandths of the depth
buffer, outside which every pixel of the world is nearer, the classic depth of the far
plane itself being only 0.995 (`SetupZRange(20, 20480)`: a - b/z = 0.99500); the viewport
is read back and put together again before the call returns. The dome is drawn in
`SkyDrawPhase` (`game/draw.cpp`), in the classic horizon mesh's own place in that function
- after the moon and before the stars, because none of the three writes depth and the
order in that function is the order on the screen. It rides on the classic path's own two
gates because it is drawn inside them - `outside`, which `GetRoomBounds` sets when a room
that sees the sky is in view, and `objects[HORIZON].loaded`, which `SkyDrawPhase` returns
on - so a level with an HD sky group but no classic HORIZON object draws no sky at all.
The blend branch is in `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`, in the alpha pass state block
(`gPass.x` carrying the alpha reference); only a group past the last room takes it, and
`HDRenderRoomMask` is the one place that still knows a group's number.
`HDRenderSkyPartOrder` (`hd_render.cpp`, in "The sky dome") keeps the alpha pass in the
`.TRG`'s part order by each range's lowest vertex, since the `.TRG` writes each part's
vertices as one ascending block, and the pass is drawn with `D3DCMP_ALWAYS`, the previous
function read back and restored. An opaque sheet (ANDY's 7112 at 4,996, RICH's 7112 at
2,836, ANDREA2's 7109 at 2,441, each the highest sheet) is nearer than the band above the
elevation where it meets the sphere, and the band drawn over it there adds nothing, the
band page's alpha being 0 at and above each of those crossings. Texture addressing needed
no change: the renderer already sets `D3DTADDRESS_CLAMP` for every range that does not
scroll and `WRAP` only for the ones that do, which is what the sky finding of TROne
(GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931 - asks for (a clamp-to-edge
sampler for the painted dome). The layers: `HDSkyLayersLeftOut(sheet, opaque band, deep)`
(`hd_water_under.h`) and `HDRenderSkyCoversLayers` decide, and `SkyDrawPhase` draws the
script's layers over the band as the classic path draws them (`HDFrameSkyCoversLayers`),
on the path `PSX_skies` names; the deep look comes from the level's water data (`WATERLOG
under_deep=1`, the fallback rooms more than four times the rooms under a sheet: JOBY4, and
RICH3 on one flipped room, whose sheets leave its layers out already) and counts only with
the sheets on (`g_caustic_on`, `tomb5.hd_water` 1), so with `hd_water` 0 JOBY4's layers
stay in. The HD page for the layers: the sheet nearest the camera (the last sheet of the
alpha pass in part order; 7113 in ANDY) is lent into the classic page's slot
`Textures[nTextures - 1]` for the one `OutputSky` that draws them and given back right
after (`HDFrameSkyLayerPage`, `hd_level.cpp`); motion (`UpdateSky`), quads, colour and the
lightning stay classic, and JOBY4, which has no sheet, keeps its classic page. The PSX
path never reads that slot - `DrawSkySegment` takes each tile's page from its
`SKY_GRAPHICS` sprite, 65 x 65 windows of a shared object page - so while a page is lent
`SkyDrawPhase` draws the layers on the flat quads whatever `PSX_skies` says, and puts the
setting back before `OutputSky`; where nothing is lent the setting is honoured as before.
The caps (`hd_sky_cap.h`, `HDSkyCapBuild`, called as `HDRenderSkyCaps` in
`HDRenderLevelBegin`): in the sky groups, every pass run of a part with no baked light
whose corners stand at three heights or more (the band; a flat sheet of one height is
none, RICH3's unlit ground sheet among them) gets, at its highest and its lowest height,
one wedge per triangle edge with both corners there - the edge reversed and a corner at
the middle of the ring's box, in the ring's plane, with the first corner's page, colours
and v and the edge's middle u; a ring with no width gets none. The wedges are inserted
after the run's own indices and every later run moves up by as many, so the band stays one
draw call in its pass, its painter's order and its depth slice; 64 triangles per band (32
a pole). The cap takes the place of the water look's third draw, the fill of the clear
colour (`water_look_draws`' `fill`, `gLookFill` c215), which left the game path; the look
lays its light over the cap as over the band. The volumetric layer: `hd_sky.hlsl`
`CloudPS` (RoomProbe `-skycloud`, `HDRenderSkyCloudProbe`) walks every pixel's ray through
a slab over the camera in 16 steps, the density a lattice of values from a hash of the
cell's integer coordinates (two octaves, smoothly interpolated), carried along x as
`UpdateSky` carries a layer, composed front to back over the sky and faded towards the
horizon; 333 of 512 shader slots, about 1.8 to 1.9 ms full screen at 2,560 x 1,440, six
times the dome. Logs and tools: the engine writes one `HDLOG ... sky groups=` line per
level and an `HDLOG sky` line with `calls=`; RoomProbe gained `-sky` (whose line ends with
the layer rule's answer, `layers out 0|1`), `-skyonly` (whose device-state bracket reports
no watched state left changed after the sky call), `-groups`, `-skycensus` (what the sky
of a level is made of), `-skydump`, `-skylayer`, `-skylayerpage psx`, `-skygpu`,
`-skycloud` and `-skycap 0|1` (draws without the caps and prints `skycap: on|off bands=
poles= triangles= vertices=`); ModernTest's `sky_cap` group (11 checks). With `hd_build` 0
nothing of it runs and `SkyDrawPhase` lends no page, so its classic branches draw as
before.

**Decisions.** The sky's own depth slice instead of a draw order, because the discs stand
in front of the band overhead and behind it at the horizon. The alpha pass in the file's
part order with no depth test, because the file is back to front and band-last with the
depth test kept would leave a step where a sheet crosses the sphere with the band's alpha
not 0 there. The layer rule follows the water data, not the sky: the deep look is the one
place the level's own data says the water is a sea seen from below. A lent HD page
overrides the PSX sky setting for the layers it draws. The cap is the band's last texel
row drawn inward, not a colour of this project's, so it shows whatever that row shows: one
colour in JOBY4, nothing where the alpha test cuts the row away; a flat disc in the ring's
plane rather than the sphere's apex, since from inside both cover the same hole and the
disc needs no centre or radius beyond the ring's own; both poles of every band, so that no
pitch and no state leaves the frame's clear colour in the sky. The heavy grey clouds of
ANDREA2 room 150 seen in play are that level's own opaque storm sheet 7109 drawn as its
files say, and ANDREA1's night sky matches a reference picture supplied for this project;
no rule changes for the clouds. The volumetric layer is not on the game's path.

**Commits.** `1087750`, `e12f8e8`, `e2c8d29`, `2341a7f` (comparison base), `b654c174`
(comparison base), `00cde6a0`, `db5a08b9`, `986631f9`, `0344eaea`, `37ffe727`, `3f4d68c1`,
`578ebab9`, `baba72b2` (comparison base), `e05e64a1`, `3e34a6e7` (the layers' `hd_water` 0
case), `838748f2` (comparison base), `6beaac58`, `ebc1525f` (the cap comments), `79ef9e4f`
(the record's ranges)

### A floor whose page is part-way clear is drawn blended, and a mirror shows the room's items
2026-09-29

**What.** Two rules of the HD level. The alpha-pass triangles of a room whose page is
part-way clear in every texel - every texel at or above the alpha test's 0.5, the smallest
at most 243 of 255 - are no longer drawn with the alpha test but blended, `SRCALPHA` over
`INVSRCALPHA` with the depth write on, in a phase of their own (`HD_PASS_CLEAR`) after
every room's solid art and before the models and the classic buckets. And the two washroom
mirrors of RICH2 show Lara and the items in front of them: with an HD level active, every
item whose reflection in a mirror's plane lands in the copy of the room behind the glass
is drawn once more through a view reflected in that plane, and Lara the same.

**Why.** The HD art builds RICH2's polished floors as a floor on pages at alpha 231 to 239
lying over an upside-down copy of the room: the lobby, room 8, is 657 floor triangles on
pages 1047 and 1045 over 2,895 triangles of copy. The alpha test at 0.5 kept every texel
of those pages and drew the floor solid, so the copy was drawn and never seen. Over every
alpha-pass page of the fifteen `.TRG` files, decoded with the engine's own BC7 reader, the
class occurs in three levels: RICH2, 13 pages (1029, 1045, 1047, 1049, 1053, 1079 and 1081
at 231 to 239, the inlaid floors 3314 to 3319 at 231 to 255) with 17,989 triangles;
RICHCUT2, page 1103 (211 to 255) with 936; TITLE, pages 2147, 2149 and 2154 (174 to 255)
with 1,860. The glass pages of the same range (3068 and 3309, 165 to 247) are material 14
and were blended already. The mirrors: TR5 has no mirror of its own in these levels.
Neither the game's SCRIPT.DAT nor the original one carries a `CMD_MIRROR` or sets
`GF_MIRROR` for any level, so `gfMirrorRoom` stays unset and `Draw_Mirror_Lara` never
runs. The HD art builds its two washroom mirrors out of art, a copy of the room reflected
in the wall behind a pane, and the copy holds nothing that moves: seen in play, the glass
showed the cabins and a toilet, no Lara and no doors.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_pageclass.h`, `HDPageClassOf`, is the class, a pure function of
the smallest and the largest alpha. `hd_pagecache.cpp` measures both over every texel of
the top mip a page keeps, beside the cut-out share and on the decoding thread, keeps the
class per slot, and `HDPageCacheSlotClear` answers it. `hd_render.cpp` decides per
triangle: an alpha-pass triangle of a room group, not glass already, on a clear page gets
blend 1 (its page's own alpha) and `HDRange::clear`. `draw_pass` draws the clear ranges
alone when asked with `clearOnly`, `HDRenderRoomMask` draws them after a room's alpha
pass, and `hd_level.cpp` draws `HD_PASS_CLEAR` for every room of the frame that has one,
after the solid loop. `FindMirrors` (`hd_render.cpp`) runs at the level build over the
four walls of every room's inside box and records a mirror where the wall has a pane
(triangles in its plane in the additive pass or of material 14), a room's worth of the
group's art behind it (100 triangles or more, reaching 1,024 units deep) and 90 per cent
of that art the reflection of the level's art in front to one 8-unit cell;
`HDRenderMirrorInfo`, `HDLevelMirrorCount` and `HDLevelMirrorAt` (`hd_level.cpp`) hand
them to the game. In RICH2 that finds room 134 (plane x = 33792) and room 135 (x = 30720)
and nothing else in the fifteen levels. `game/draw.cpp` calls `Draw_Mirror_Items`
(`game/mirror.cpp`) after Lara's own draw and before the rooms' objects are printed, while
the mirror room's portal window is still this frame's, behind `HDLevelActive()`. For a
mirror whose room is on the draw list and whose glass faces the camera, `DrawOneMirror`
copies the view - `w2v_matrix`, `aW2VMx` and the bases of both matrix stacks - and
reflects it (`game/mirror_math.h`, `MirrorView`: the view's column of the plane's axis
negated, the camera reflected). It draws every item in front of the glass whose reflected
origin lands in the copy's box, with 256 units of slack along the glass's normal and in
height and none along the glass (`MirrorLandsInCopy`), through `PrintObjectReflection`
(`game/draw.cpp`, the item loop's body with the mirror's room as the clip room), moves
Lara's fifteen matrices into the reflected view (`MirrorViewSpaceApply`) and draws her
with `DrawLara(lara_item, 1)`, and copies the view back. The classic path's winding test
is turned round with `SetCullCW` as `Draw_Mirror_Lara` turns it; the HD models are drawn
double sided and need nothing, and HD Lara in first person culls the other side on her
mirror flag (`hd_laradraw.cpp`), drawn as the first-person draw draws her, without her
face and her braid. `HDObjectReflection` (`hd_object.cpp`) tells the object seam the items
are a reflection: they are left out of the two light checks and counted for the mirror's
log line. A reflected item casts no shadow - its slot's `shadow_size` is 0 for the call -
and its ambient fade, which `CalcAmbientLight` steps per draw, is put back. `DrawLara`
steps its look-transparency fade once per call, so while a mirror draws Lara the fade back
from look mode runs twice as fast; a Lara drawn the classic way keeps the light arrays
across mirrors, so in one mirror she is drawn before its items. The frame line's object
counts include the reflected draws. Logs: the motion line of `HDLOG level=` ends in `
clear_pages=%d clear_parts=%d mirrors=%d`, the level's first frame line in `
clear_calls=%d`; one `HDLOG mirrorwall` line per mirror at the build, and `HDLOG mirror
items=%d plane=%ld room=%d axis=%c lara=%d hd=%d` once a second while a mirror draws.
`RoomProbe` draws the clear phase in its frame and in the alpha-pass picture of `-all`
(`HDRenderRoomPass`), gives the earlier picture with `-noclear`, and prints a `clear:`
line and, with `-roombox`, the mirrors. ModernTest pins the class, the reflection and the
point past a copy's end. With `hd_enable` 0 the clear phase and the page class do not
exist and `Draw_Mirror_Items` is not called; the classic mirror of Lara, the classic item
loop, the logic camera and the savegames are not written - the reflection lives in the
view and in copies of it, and an item's own position and pose are never touched.

**Decisions.** A rule from the data and no list per level: a page part-way clear in every
texel is meant to be seen through. The class reads the smallest alpha: from the alpha
test's reference, 128, up to 243 - halfway between the highest smallest alpha of a floor
over a copy (233, TITLE page 2149) and the first near-opaque page (254, JOBY3 pages 14070
and 14071, ANDY1 page 793, three sky sheets); a page that also carries texels at 255 stays
in the class, because the floors of TITLE and RICHCUT2 and RICH2's inlaid ones do, and a
texel at 255 blends as solid. The floor keeps the depth write and is drawn in a phase of
its own before the models, not with the glass after everything: Lara stands on it, her
shadow falls 16 units above it, and the glass and the glows of the copy must stay beneath
it. HD only. The mirrors come from the art, because the script has none, and every item
whose reflection lands in the copy is drawn, not a list of objects. The reflection is put
into the view and not into the item, so every item keeps the pose the frame draws: a pose
written into the item needs the -1 scale `CalcLaraMatrices(2)` gives Lara and
`DrawAnimatingItem` does not have, and both mirrors stand in planes of constant x, which
the z plane of `Draw_Mirror_Lara` does not serve. A reflected item casts no shadow of its
own and its effects are not reflected; the lobby floor shows its static copy only.

**Commits.** `e77fc52`, `a8ff098`, `12250e8`, `c0d6e3c`, `aa676dd`, `1093689`

### The reflection stays behind the glass
2026-09-29

**What.** A mirror's reflection is drawn only where the copy of the room behind the glass
is. The HD draws of a reflection, the items and every piece of Lara with the braid, are
clipped per pixel in the model shader against three planes: the copy's side of the glass
and the copy's two ends along it. The classic draws of a reflection are cut by the classic
clipper to the copy's rectangle on the screen. When an item or Lara is reflected does not
change.

**Why.** The mirror decides by an origin (`MirrorLandsInCopy`) and nothing bounded the
body drawn about it. In RICH2, with Lara at the west side of the doorway between corridor
room 56 and room 177, her origin reflected in glass 135's plane stands 20 units inside the
copy's end, and a body 150 units about it reaches 130 units past that end, over room 56's
floor, which is open west of the glass's plane: from the corridor a second Lara stood
beside the doorway, her other half inside the wall of room 177. The same cause has a
second face: a Lara against the glass has a reflection whose shoulders, arms and braid
reach through the plane into the room in front of it.

**How.** `game/mirror_math.h`, `MirrorClipPlanes`, gives the three planes in the view
space the reflected draw lands in, from the reflected float view matrix: an image test n*
. p* + d* >= 0 becomes n = R (S n*), d = d* + 2 plane n*[axis] + (S n*) . c on the drawn
point, R the matrix's rotation, c its camera, S the reflection's diagonal; `MirrorClipOff`
is (0, 0, 0, 1) three times, which keeps every point. `MirrorBoxWindow` projects the box's
eight corners through the real view as the classic path projects (x = centre + persp vx /
vz) and intersects their bounding rectangle with a window; a corner nearer than the near
plane gives the window itself. `DrawOneMirror` (`game/mirror.cpp`) takes the rectangle
inside the mirror room's portal window (the whole screen for a room left without a window;
the room window's right and bottom are inclusive, as the camera room's `phd_winxmax` and
`phd_winymax`, so they go into the intersection one past their edge and come back one
short of the rectangle's), sets `f_left` .. `f_bottom` and `phd_left` .. `phd_bottom` to
it, narrows the room's own window to it, works out the planes after the view is reflected
and hands them to `HDObjectReflection(true, planes)`; all of it is put back at the end.
`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp`: `FrameItem::clip` carries twelve floats, written with the
mirror's planes while a reflection is recorded and with the planes that keep every pixel
otherwise, in `HDObjectEnd` for an item and in `HDObjectPush` for Lara's pieces and the
braid; `HDInvEnd` gives the ring and the pickup display the planes that keep every pixel.
`HDObjectFrameDraw` hands each entry's planes to `HDModelClip` beside `HDModelOffCentre`
and puts them back after the list. `HDModelClip` (`hd_model.cpp`) uploads c5 - c7 of the
pixel file only when the planes change; `HDModelFrameBegin` uploads the planes that keep
every pixel at every bracket's start, so the pickup display's bracket, which never calls
it, keeps every pixel. `hd_shader/hd_model.hlsl` declares `gClip[3]` in c5 - c7, and
`ModelPS` clips after the neck cut on the smallest of the three dots with `viewPos`, the
skinned point in view space; the literals the compiler kept in c5 - c7 moved to other
registers, and the room shader writes no pixel register c5 - c7. The classic cut:
`phd_PutPolygons` and its variants copy `f_left` .. `f_bottom` into `clip_left` ..
`clip_bottom` (`specific/output.cpp`) and `XYUVGClipper` cuts a polygon to `f_left` ..
`f_bottom` when it is inserted (`specific/clipping.cpp`, `specific/polyinsert.cpp`);
`phd_left` .. `phd_bottom` only drop a whole object (`S_GetObjectBounds`), and `DrawLara`
sets them to the whole screen, so the rectangle goes into `f_left` .. `f_bottom`, which
reaches Lara's classic body and braid as well. `PrintObjectReflection` (`game/draw.cpp`)
takes its window from `f_left` .. `f_bottom` instead of the whole screen;
`calc_animating_item_clip_window` cannot pass the rectangle: its room branches read the
mirror room's window, narrowed to the rectangle for the call, and its door branch sets
nothing and keeps what `PrintObjectReflection` set. The classic rectangle cannot cut along
the glass's plane, so a Lara drawn the classic way (the TR3 outfit the randomizer rolls
per level) or a classic item reaching through the plane itself is not cut there. The
planes are worked out from `aW2VMx`, and a poison shake scales the matrix stack's base and
not it, so under the shake they stand off the body by its few per cent. The mirror's log
line ends in ` win=%ld,%ld,%ld,%ld` (`mirror.cpp`), the rectangle's left, top, right and
bottom, right and bottom exclusive. ModernTest pins the planes over a grid on both sides
of glass 135 and past both copy ends, a plane of constant z, the planes that keep every
point, and the rectangle's corners, centre and near fallback. With `hd_enable` 0
`Draw_Mirror_Items` is not called and `f_left` .. `f_bottom` never change there.

**Decisions.** The reflection is clipped to the copy's box behind the glass - the glass's
plane and the copy's two ends along it - for every reflected draw; the box's floor and
ceiling are not clipped, the copy's own art hides what stands beyond them. The HD draws
clip per pixel in the model shader against the three planes in view space; the classic
draws take the copy's rectangle on the screen, inside the mirror room's portal window, as
the classic clipper's rectangle - a coarser bound, the only one that path has. When a
thing is reflected stays as it was: a reflection that stops at the copy's end is the
mirror's picture, one that vanishes a sector before it is not. No stencil from the pane's
own triangles: once the body is bounded, the copy's own walls hide the reflection
everywhere but through the glass, and the mirror keeps the pane's count and not its
triangles. HD only.
