### A seam for the poison sway
2026-09-29

**What.** With `-log`, two `POISONLOG` lines while Lara is poisoned (`lara.poisoned` or
`lara.dpoisoned` not zero). A `view` line per build of the view matrix: `call=`, `tick=`,
`tween=`, `rebuild=`, `who=`, `poisoned=`, `dpoisoned=` and `scale=`, the three factors
the sway applied to the matrix stack's base (16384 when it applied none). A `frame` line
per drawn frame: `frame=`, `tick=`, `tween=`, `alpha=`, `base=` and `poisoned=`, `base=`
being the three column lengths of the float stack's base times 10000 (10000 unscaled). The
fix the lines pointed to is the next entry.

**Why.** In RICH3's gas the sway was absent or faint at the interpolated frame rates and
normal at 30; after a stretch at 30 the interpolated rates looked right. Two readings fit.
The sway's amplitude never rises at the interpolated rates, because the ramp that walks
`lara.poisoned` towards `lara.dpoisoned` does not step there; or the scale sits on the
frames that carry a logic step and is missing on the frames between them, because a
rebuild of the view builds it without. The `view` line tells the first (a `poisoned=` that
stands while `dpoisoned=` moves), the `frame` line the second (a `base=` at 10000 on the
in-between frames only).

**How.** `specific/3dmath.cpp`, `PoisonLogView`, writes the `view` line; `aGenerateW2V`
calls it behind `gLogEnabled` after its scale block with its own scale vector, which holds
the factors only when the block scaled. `who=` reads two flags: `PoisonLogRebuild`, set by
`RebuildView` around its `phd_LookAt` (`game/interpolate.cpp`), and `PoisonLogTickCamera`,
set by `ControlPhase` around the logic step's camera block, `CalculateCamera` or
`CalculateSpotCams` (`game/control.cpp`); every other view build is `other` - the pickup
icon, the gun's aim view in `FireWeapon`, the load screen, the inventory. `PoisonLogFrame`
(`3dmath.cpp`) writes the `frame` line from `aMXPtr`; `DrawPhaseGame` reads
`InterpAlphaNow` once into a local, hands it to `InterpBeginFrame` (`game/draw.cpp`) and
then to `PoisonLogFrame` behind `gLogEnabled`. `phd_GenerateW2V`'s own scale block has no
line: it runs right before `aGenerateW2V` in the same call, one ramp step earlier and with
the same phases. Nothing the engine does changes: the ramp, the scale, the camera, the
matrices and the draw order stay as they were; the two flags are written whether `-log` is
on or not and only the log reads them, and the two counters step only with `-log`.

**Commits.** `3f6e004`

### A tick is never a tween frame
2026-09-29

**What.** A logic step lowers the tween latch at its first statement, so the poison ramp
that the step's own camera steps runs once per step at every frame rate: in RICH3's gas
the green veil and the sway rise, and the poison deals its damage, at the interpolated
rates as at 30. The counters that sit before `DrawPhaseGame` in a loop read the latch of
the frame drawn last, which the step leaves standing. A frame drawn between two steps
builds its view at the sway's phases of its own time instead of the step's.

**Why.** The game loop draws first and steps after: `DoLevel` calls `DrawPhaseGame` and
then `ControlPhase` (`game/gameflow.cpp`), `DoTitle` the same. The latch
`InterpBeginFrame` sets at the top of a frame was lowered only by the next frame, a 30 Hz
present or an invalidation, so it outlived its frame and stood through the logic step that
followed. At fps_mode 2 the frame that carries a step is the first one drawn after it, so
whenever a step lasts two frames or more the frame before the next step is a tween frame.
The ramp guard in both halves of `phd_GenerateW2V`, `lara.dpoisoned != lara.poisoned &&
!InterpIsTweenFrame()`, read that latch from `CalculateCamera`, the spot cameras and
`FireWeapon`'s aim view, and `lara.poisoned`, the sway's amplitude, stood: POISONLOG in
RICH3 at 165 Hz showed `poisoned` at 0 throughout while `dpoisoned` climbed, and at 30
`poisoned` following `dpoisoned`; the frames between two steps carried the same scale as
the step's frame, so the scale itself was never at fault. And the step's poison block
(`game/control.cpp`, `if (lara.poisoned && !GLOBAL_playing_cutseq)`: the climb of
`dpoisoned`, the office levels' decay and the poison damage) never ran while `poisoned`
was 0, so at 165 Hz a fresh poisoning dealt no damage either. The one ramp step left at
fps_mode 2 was `S_DrawPickup`'s `phd_LookAt` (`specific/output.cpp`) on the frame that
carries a step, while a pickup icon was on screen. At fps_mode 1 the frame before a step
is live, at fps_mode 0 the latch is never up. The sway's six phases step once per logic
step while at fps_mode 2 the camera moves on every frame, so the sway held each value for
five or six frames at 165 Hz and then jumped.

**How.** `InterpCapturePrev` (`game/interpolate.cpp`), the first statement of every logic
step (`control.cpp`), sets `g_tween = false` before `g_tickSerial++`; the next
`InterpBeginFrame` latches anew by its own rule. A second reading, `g_drawnTween`, is
written wherever the frame side writes `g_tween` - `InterpNoteClassicPresent`,
`InterpNoteMenuFrame`, `InterpBeginFrame`, `InterpInvalidate` - and never by the step;
`InterpDrawnFrameWasTween` (`game/interpolate.h`) returns it. Four readers that sit before
`DrawPhaseGame` in a loop take it, because on the lowered latch they would step on the
logic step and again on the frame that carries it: the level caption `gfLegendTime`
(`gameflow.cpp`), and, walked by `DoTitle` before its draw, the sky's lightning
(`game/draw.cpp`), the credits roll (`specific/alexstuff.cpp`) and the cutscene wind-up
(`game/deltapak.cpp`); after `DrawPhaseGame` and before the step the two readings are
equal, so the wind-up `DoLevel` calls there and the sky inside a frame read what they read
before. `FireWeapon` builds its aim view in the step (`game/larafire.cpp`) and is covered
by the same lowering. Every other `InterpIsTweenFrame` caller sits inside the frame, after
`InterpBeginFrame`, where the latch is the frame's as before; a modal loop entered from
the step (the pause, load, save and death menus) or right after it now finds the latch
down on its first present, as from its second present on it always did. The sway:
`InterpCapturePrev` captures the six phases; `InterpBeginFrame` blends them with
`LerpAngle` from the capture to the step's values at the frame's `alpha` and hands them to
`PoisonSwayBlend` (`specific/3dmath.cpp`) around its own `RebuildView` only; both halves
of `phd_GenerateW2V` read them through `PoisonSwayPhases`, the globals otherwise. The
ramp's arithmetic - a sixteenth per call, two calls per `phd_LookAt` - and its guard stay
word for word; `RebuildView` keeps its save and restore of `lara.poisoned`;
`InterpEndFrame`'s rebuild restores the step's view with the step's phases; the globals
`XSoff1` .. `ZSoff2` are written by the step alone. At fps_mode 0 the latch is never up,
the lowering changes nothing and no frame reaches the phase blend. InterpTest's
`tick_latch` walks the loop for a simulated minute at 60 and 165 Hz under fps_mode 2 and
at fps_mode 1 and 0 (the latch, the per-present counters, the caption and the wind-up once
per step), and `sway_phase` pins the blend on the six steps (the capture at 0, the step at
1, the wrap at 0x8000, never backwards).

**Decisions.** The latch describes a drawn frame, and a logic step is no frame: the step
lowers it at its first statement and the next frame sets it anew. The ramp guard stays
word for word; the step's own camera builds see the latch down at every rate, and with
`S_DrawPickup` stepping on the frame that carries the step the count per step is the
vanilla one at every rate. The sway's phases between two steps are blended for the view
the interpolator builds for the drawn frame and for nothing else. No change to the ramp's
speed, the damage or the office decay: they come back on their own with the amplitude. The
counters before `DrawPhaseGame` in `DoLevel` and `DoTitle` read the drawn frame's latch,
not the lowered one, which would step them twice per logic step. The phases are blended
from a capture, not from the six literal steps, so a step that returned before stepping
them draws them still.

**Commits.** `d73faaba` (the latch lowered), `ebad544c` (the sway between steps),
`cb43a425` (the suite), `fa283e01` (the record)

### A shine on metal, marble and ice
2026-09-30

**What.** In an HD room the surfaces of metal, marble and ice carry a sheen, whatever way
they face: floors, walls, crates, ducts, shelves and the props the .TRG bakes into the
room. It is a highlight from the room's own lamps, the level's sun and the viewer, and a
reflection of the room's light, weighted by Schlick's Fresnel term and added to the
surface's own lit colour. A second compiled variant of the room pixel shader draws it, for
the draw calls whose page resolves to a gloss while `hd_reflect` is on. Four sources name
a page's gloss: the .TRG's material 3 or 17, a file `hd_gloss.txt` beside the executable,
a page table compiled into the engine, and a seed out of the classic floor's footstep
materials. With `-log`, `GLOSSLOG` says which pages shine and why. The light the sheen
reads - lamps, sun, viewer and cube - is replaced by the level's light field in the next
entry.

**Why.** The .TRG has no metal class for props: ANDREA1 room 3's riveted crate, its
forklift and its overhead box are material 0 on pages whose alpha is flat (254 to 255 on
the top mip). The two gloss materials, 3 (165,897 triangles) and 17 (17,453), sit mostly
on walls, and 34 of the 35 pages that carry them hold a mask - a smallest top-mip alpha
below 250 - that selects window glass, armour, ice and puddles, or is coverage. The
classic floor marks metal (footstep material 8) on 6,258 squares in ten levels, marble (9)
on 95 and ice (4) on 211. The grazing-angle lift the room shader drew out of materials 3
and 17 was invisible even at strength 1. The room pixel shader used 476 of the 512 slots
shader model 3 guarantees. And the .TRG's 1,306 point lights and 91,569 light cubes were
read and counted (`hd_scan.cpp`) and drawn by nothing.

**How.** The variant is `hd_room.hlsl` compiled with `HD_GLOSS`
(`specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl`, `GlossSheen`) into `hd_room_gloss_ps.inc`, 499 of
512 slots; it leaves out the ripple, the caustic and the additive-pass lines, which no
glossy draw call needs, and every line that differs sits under the define. Its registers
are `gGloss` in c36, gRipple's (F0, how far the reflection takes the texel's colour, the
mask switch), `gGlossCube` c80 - c85, `gGlossAxes` c86 - c88 and `gGlossLights` c89 - c96
(four lamps); `gSpec` c19 keeps strength, exponent and `hd_reflect`. The shading is in
view space, where `viewNrm`, `viewPos` and the camera already are: Blinn-Phong with the (n
+ 8) / 8 normalisation per lamp, the viewer as a lamp added after that normalisation, so
that its peak is a quarter of the surface's own light whatever the exponent, the normal
and the half vector normalised under a floor, so that a zero normal gives no sheen and no
NaN, the ambient cube looked up along the reflection turned back into world axes,
Schlick's weight, the page's alpha as mask where the page has one, and the fog and the
bulbs' haze taken off the sum as off the surface. `bshader.bat` compiles it and `be.bat`
guards its hash line. `hd_render.cpp` creates it beside the plain variant (a device that
refuses it keeps the plain one); `draw_pass` picks it per draw call, writes `gGloss` and
the lamps and the cube (`upload_sheen_lights`), enters it after those writes, leaves it
before a plain draw call's writes and ends every pass on the plain variant, because each
variant keeps literals in registers the other one names. The lights: the level build keeps
each room's point lights room local and scaled, the cubes when their count is the count of
floor squares, and the sun towards it; `hd_level.cpp`'s `BuildRoomSectors` hands the floor
squares in (`HDRenderSetSectors`), x-major like `ROOM_INFO::floor` and like the cubes.
`LightSheen` gives a glossy draw call the mean cube of the squares under its triangles (a
wall triangle takes the square half a square in front of it), its room's lamps nearest its
box and, where the level has a sun, the share of it its cube says it sees. Which surfaces:
`ResolveSheen` runs after the sort and changes no range; `ResolvePage` and
`HDGlossResolve` (`specific/hd/hd_gloss_math.h`) take the material first, then the file,
the table and the seed; the seed walks the rooms' surface triangles (`hd_gloss_seed.h`,
`HDGlossSeedVote`): an up-facing triangle within 300 units of its floor square's height
votes for the square's footstep material, and a page takes metal, marble or ice when that
class holds half of its votes, at least two of them and at least one per cent of its
triangles (`HDGlossSeedClass`); the table is `hd_gloss_pages.h`, 40 lines; the file is
read at every level build (`ReadGlossFile`, `hd_render.cpp`) with `HDGlossParseLine` and
`HDGlossParseText` (`hd_gloss_math.h`), which steps over a UTF-8 byte order mark. The mask
is a page's smallest alpha below 250 (`HDPageCacheSlotAlphaMin`, `hd_pagecache.cpp`).
`MaterialGloss` (`hd_render.cpp`) reads the base material, so RICH3's destructible panes
0x8003 to 0x8403 count; `MaterialAlphaRef`, `MaterialAddWeight` and `MaterialBookTime` go
on comparing the whole number, which a destructible piece never matches (they exist over
bases 0, 3 and 14 only), so a destructible decal keeps the additive weight 1. The seam:
`GLOSSLOG` (`hd_level.cpp`), the HDLOG level line ends with `gloss_pages=` and
`gloss_draws=`, and the HDLOG frame line with `sheen_calls=`, the solid bracket's draw
calls on the variant; its `gloss_calls=` goes on counting the draw calls with a material's
gloss. The tools: TrgProbe `-gloss`, `-glossseed`, `-glossfile` and `-glosslight`;
RoomProbe `-glossmax` and `-glossfile`, and `-roombox` hands the floor squares in;
ModernTest's `gloss_*` family. With `hd_enable` off nothing of it is reached; with
`hd_reflect` off no draw call takes the variant, the plain variant draws with the
constants it always had, and the ranges, their order and their draw calls are as before -
the sheen is resolved after the sort and is in no sort key. The water, glow, flipbook,
book, glass, decal and clear-floor draws keep the plain variant, and the objects and Lara
are not touched.

**Decisions.** The shine is light-driven and orientation-free: a highlight and a
reflection of the room's light per pixel, no mirror image, no second room pass, no
stencil. The unit of selection is the texture page, beside the .TRG material per part, and
the order is the material, the file, the table, the seed: the table stands before the seed
because it holds the seed's misreadings (a relief, planks, a label atlas, the concrete
page 50 of RICH1 and RICH2) as well as what the seed cannot see, and the file before both,
so that a page the seed names can be tuned or taken out without a rebuild; a material part
keeps its own strength and exponent and takes only the class the file or the table names,
so neither can take a material 3 or 17 page out. RICH2's lobby is kept out page by page:
its clear-class pages (1029, 1045, 1047, 1049, 1053, 1079, 1081) and marble pages (1010,
1032, 1033) take nothing but the material, and every room with a clear floor takes nothing
at all (the next entry lets those rooms shine by page); the other pages numbered between
1029 and 1081 are not the lobby's class and may shine, the washroom's green mosaic 1054 by
the table and the steel shutter 1039 and tread plate 1040 by the seed. The lamps are the
room's own .TRG point lights, four at most, one of them the sun where the level has one,
and the viewer at a quarter of the surface's light at its peak, outside the exponent's (n
+ 8) / 8 scale; the dynamic lights give no highlight, because eight more lamps would pass
512 slots. One cube per draw call, the mean over the squares under it, lifted by a gain of
3, the median of the levels' gains (2.93) found by TrgProbe `-glosslight`. F0 is 0.5 for
metal, whose reflection takes the texel's colour, and 0.08 at strength 0.6 for marble, ice
and glass. `hd_reflect` is the one switch; there is no options row. The seed decides per
level, so a page can shine in one level and not in the next until a table line names it.

**Commits.** `4d2d0f6` (comparison base), `fd239210` (the gloss variant), `63d6e914`
(lights and cubes), `ac70d40d` (which surfaces shine), `28e15316` (tools, suite, class
defaults), `3955fc96` (the record, engine comments), `91cf38ff` (follow-up fixes)

### The shine belongs to the place, not to the draw call
2026-10-01

**What.** The sheen of an HD room surface reads its light out of a light field of the
level: a grid of cells, one floor square across and one square up, over the part of the
rooms' boxes the .TRG's point lights reach, built once with the level's HD data, in which
every cell holds one direction towards the light - a light probe's dominant direction, the
weighted mean of the directions to the lamps within six squares - how one-sided that light
is, and one bounded colour. Two volume textures carry it to the gloss variant of the room
pixel shader, which reads them with linear filtering at the pixel's world position and
forms one Blinn-Phong highlight out of them. The per-draw-call lamps, the level's sun, the
viewer as a lamp and the per-draw-call light cube are gone; the environment term is the
surface's own baked light. The whole sheen is held under the surface's own lit colour and
composed as a screen. Every room that wears a glossy page shines with it, the rooms with a
clear floor too, and a draw call with a UV scroll, a flipbook, a book or a caustic within
reach takes the sheen its page names; the water surfaces, the sky band and the clear
floors keep the plain variant and are counted per level in a new `GLOSSLOG skipped` line.
With `-log`, the GLOSSLOG level line also names the field's grid, cells, memory and build
time. The page table names three more pages, 43 lines in all: the locker doors' two
halves, 93 and 94, and 470, the twin of JOBY2's painted steel with a pipe across.

**Why.** Seen in play, the previous entry's sheen drew white discs with a cyan rim on
JOBY2's diamond-plate floors that travelled with the camera; steps along straight lines
where two rooms or two draw calls meet; combs where two layers of art lie on one plane;
burnt-out edges (ANDREA1 room 3's forklift cage and lamp bracket white); JOBY2's hull
plates washing to a pale lilac at a grazing angle; and rooms that wear a glossy page left
matt. The code said why. A directional light's highlight on a flat floor sits at a fixed
direction of view, so the sun's slot drew a disc that moves with the camera exactly, and
the viewer as a lamp is tied to the camera by construction. The four lamps nearest a draw
call's box out of its own room, the sun's share and the mean cube were chosen per draw
call, so the shine stepped wherever one draw call met another and differed on two layers
that lie on one plane. `HD_GLOSS_LAMP_SCALE` 0.1 made a median lamp one whole white or
more, the highlight was then multiplied by (n + 8) / 8, 7 at exponent 48, and metal's F0
0.5 at strength 0.8 left 2.8 whites at the peak of a median lamp. The cube was lifted by
3, and JOBY2's cubes are the brightest of all levels, so at Fresnel's full weight a whole
draw call of hull plates took up to 0.6 of a white of the cube's lilac. Every draw call of
a room with a part-way clear floor - 55 rooms of RICH2, 1 of RICHCUT2, 9 of TITLE - stayed
plain, as did every draw call with a scroll, a flipbook, a book or a caustic within reach,
although only the caustic is a line of the pixel shader. RICH1's locker wall stepped where
the seed named the lower lockers' page 94 metal and no source named the upper ones' page
93 - a page step, not a light step - and JOBY2's corridor wall the same way on pages 469
and 470.

**How.** The field is `specific/hd/hd_gloss_field.h`, a header of pure functions like
`hd_gloss_math.h`: the cell (`HD_GLOSS_FIELD_CELL`), the reach, a lamp's colour to the
field's scale (`HD_GLOSS_LAMP_NORM`), the falloff (1 - d^2 / R^2)^2, the exposure 1 - e^-m
that bounds a cell's colour below one and keeps its hue, the grid over the rooms' boxes
that a lamp reaches, one cell more each side, powers of two where a device asks for them
(`HDGlossFieldLayout`), the build (`HDGlossFieldBuild`) with an optional sight test by the
rooms that only the tools use (`HDGlossFieldSight`), and the sample as the shader reads
it. `hd_render.cpp` builds it at the level build out of every room group's point lights in
world units and the rooms' boxes made world (`BuildField`) into two `D3DFMT_A8R8G8B8`
volume textures in the managed pool (`MakeFieldTexture`) - a device without filtered
volume textures gets none, and the variant then draws its environment term alone; the
state bracket saves samplers 1 and 2 and their textures, sets them linear, unmipped and
clamped, binds the field in the room bracket and puts all of it back. Per room, `prepare`
writes six registers, `upload_gloss_rows`: `gGlossAxes`, the view rotation's transpose,
and `gGlossField`, the rows that take a view-space position to the field's texture
coordinate - the room's world-view matrix undone, the room group's origin kept from the
build added, the field's corner taken off and its size divided out - so the engine, whose
matrix is the finished D3DMView, and RoomProbe, which draws a room at its own origin, land
on the same world. Per glossy draw call only `gGloss` changes, its `w` the tool's field
picture. The shader: the note "The sheen" (`specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl`), the
constants, the registers and samplers, `GlossSheen` with the bound, the caustic in both
variants and the screen; `hd_room_gloss_ps.inc` uses 502 of the 512 slots. The bound's
twins for the suite are `HDGlossSheenBound` and `HDGlossSheenCompose` (`hd_gloss_math.h`).
Which draw calls keep the plain variant is `RangeKeepsPlain` (`hd_render.cpp`);
`ResolveSheen` no longer looks at the room and counts what it keeps plain, and the
GLOSSLOG part counts follow it. The log: the GLOSSLOG level line ends in `field=
field_lit= field_weak= field_kb= field_ms=` (`hd_level.cpp`), and `GLOSSLOG skipped level=
ripple= caustic= flat= scroll= flipbook= book= clear=` follows it (`HDRenderSheenSkipped`,
`hd_render.h`). The field per level runs from 2,925 cells (JOBY4) to 151,807 (RICH3), 22
KiB to 1,185 KiB in the two textures, at most 524,288 cells and 4 MiB where a device asks
for powers of two, built in 0.2 to 6.5 ms. The tools: TrgProbe `-glossfield`; RoomProbe
`-glossfield [colour|direction]` and `-fieldsight` (through `HDRenderGlossFieldView` and
`HDRenderGlossFieldSight`), and its state-bracket check watches samplers 1 and 2 and their
textures; ModernTest's `gloss_field_grid`, `gloss_field_texels`, `gloss_field_build` and
`gloss_field_bound` take the place of `gloss_cube` and the lamp ranking. With `hd_reflect`
off no draw call takes the gloss variant and every room is drawn as before; the field is
still built and bound, and the plain variant reads none of it. The resolver's order,
`hd_gloss.txt` and its format, the seed, the barred lobby pages and the objects and Lara
stay as they were.

**Decisions.** The shine is a function of the place: what the gloss variant reads for a
pixel is its world position, its normal, its page's gloss and the view direction, nothing
chosen per draw call or per room, so it steps nowhere the baked light does not step, and
two layers on one plane take the same shine. No light is tied to the camera: the viewer as
a lamp and the directional sun are gone, and a highlight belongs to a lamp of the level at
its place. No burn-out: a lamp's colour is scaled by `HD_GLOSS_LAMP_NORM` so that the 90th
percentile of the lamps' largest channel over the fifteen levels (20; the median is 10 and
the largest 120) gives one, a cell's colour is bounded below one by the exposure, the
lobe's normalisation is folded into `HD_GLOSS_HIGHLIGHT` 2, and the whole sheen is held
under the surface's own lit colour plus 4 of 255 - softly, B (1 - e^(-t / B)) - and
composed as a screen, so a dark surface stays dark and a lamp behind a wall cannot light a
surface the bake left dark. The environment is the surface's own baked light at a quarter,
continuous by the art, its Fresnel rise held by the same bound. A second direction per
cell is not built - cells less than one-third one-sided are 0 to 4.3 per cent of the lit
ones, and a second lobe and a third texture would not fit the ten slots left. No sight
test in the engine: no visible leak shows without one, a test by the rooms on this grid
takes a floor's own lamps half away where an unconnected room lies under it at a cell
boundary, and it would need the rooms' portal lists in the renderer; the tools carry it.
Lara's own sheen is not part of this entry: her draw path is untouched. Every room that
wears the page shines: the lobby's pages stay matt by page and the clear floors by class;
the caustic is back in the gloss variant (its slots came free with the lamp loop), the
scroll, the flipbook and the book need nothing of the pixel shader, and the water
surfaces' ripple and the sky band's flat light keep the plain variant and are counted. The
dynamic lights give no highlight in the gloss variant: ten slots are left, and one lobe
per light costs more. No per-frame work on the processor per glossy draw call beyond the
variant and the page's own constants: the rows go up once per room, the textures once per
bracket. The strengths chosen here are raised in the entry "The sheen at a strength that
shows". `HD_GLOSS_LAMP_NORM` came with the commit of the light field; the bound's commit
does not touch it, though its body names the lamps' normalisation.

**Commits.** `4d2d0f6` (comparison base), `b62344c9` (the light field), `4c511171` (the
sheen bounded), `e20c5523` (every room shines), `665abd70` (the tools and suite),
`d7081570` (the record), `4a02813e` (follow-up fixes, whole build)

### The sheen at a strength that shows
2026-10-01

**What.** The sheen of the previous entry at about two and a half times its strength at a
highlight: the highlight at six times the field's colour (`HD_GLOSS_HIGHLIGHT`, was 2),
the environment at 0.35 of the surface's light (`HD_GLOSS_ENV`, was 0.25), the bound at
two and a half times the surface's own lit colour plus 8 of 255 (`HD_GLOSS_BOUND`,
`HD_GLOSS_FLOOR`, were 1 and 4 of 255), and a cap the bound never passes, three quarters
(`HD_GLOSS_CAP`, new).

**Why.** In play the previous entry's sheen was hardly to be seen, and its own figures say
the same: on JOBY2 room 90's dark diamond plate the brightest place of the highlight
gained 23 of 255, on a locker wall 24. The bound at the surface's own lit colour held it
there - a floor that is 45 of 255 bright could gain about 45 at most - and the weight of
metal, 0.4 face on, left the highlight under that bound almost everywhere. A highlight on
dark steel is brighter than the steel; a bound of one cannot show it.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl`: the five defines over `gGloss`, and
`min(..., HD_GLOSS_CAP)` in the bound of `GlossSheen`; the gloss variant takes 503 of 512
instruction slots. `specific/hd/hd_gloss_math.h` carries the twins of the bound, the floor
and the cap in `HDGlossSheenBound`, and ModernTest holds the cap. With a bound above one
the screen alone would let a mid-bright surface reach white where the highlight saturates
- lit (1 + B (1 - lit)) is one at lit 0.4 for B 2.5 - so the cap holds the sheen under
three quarters, and the screen, lit + sheen (1 - lit), then closes at most three quarters
of the way to white. The plain room pixel shader and the room vertex shader differ from
the previous entry's in their hash line alone, so with `hd_reflect` off every room is
drawn as before. The light field, the pages that shine and their classes, strengths and
exponents, the order of the sources, `hd_gloss.txt`, the draw calls that take the gloss
variant and GLOSSLOG stay as they were.

**Decisions.** The environment is raised least: it lifts a whole surface evenly, which
reads as a paler picture and not as a shine. The cap at three quarters keeps a mid-bright
surface from reaching white.

**Commits.** `4d2d0f6` (comparison base), `897c00af` (the strength that shows)

### A light faded to nothing is not counted into an HD object's light list
2026-10-02

**What.** `fill_lights` leaves out an entry of the engine's two item light lists, the
current and the previous one, whose colour lies below `HD_OBJLIGHT_DARK_BOUND` - 1e-5 of
the engine's own 0..1 scale - in all three channels: at the suns and at the points and
spots, through one predicate, `HDObjLightIsDark` in the new header
`specific/hd/hd_objlight_dark.h`. Such an entry is neither handed to the model shader nor
counted. With nothing but such entries the count is 0, and the shader's own branch for an
empty list makes the viewer the lamp of Lara's sheen, as after a fresh load. A new log
line, `HDLOG laralights`, written from Lara's draw with `-log`, shows her list whenever it
changes.

**Why.** On a walk between rooms of different kinds Lara's sheen now and then went, and
came back when the game was saved and loaded at that place. The model vertex shader makes
the viewer the lamp of the sheen only when the object's list is empty (`hd_model.hlsl`,
the sheen); with one entry, only that entry's direction and falloff make a highlight,
whatever its colour. `FadeLightList` (`specific/lighting.cpp`) fades a light out by adding
an eighth of its colour eight times and clears `Active` only when red, green and blue are
all at or below 0 after a step. Eight float additions need not land on 0: run with the
engine's own statements and compiler settings (`/O2 /fp:precise`, SSE2), 1503 of the 2732
sun, point and spot lights in the rooms of the game's level files - 162 of 266 in ANDREA2
- and 139 of the 255 byte-grid colours n/255 end the fade with a channel a hair above 0
and keep `Active`; the largest remainder is 8.94e-8, under 2.3e-5 of a unit of 0..255. In
ANDREA2, walking from room 10 (two shadow lights) into room 9 (one sun) and back, room 9's
sun ends every return to room 10 in the previous list at a remainder, `Active` with `fcnt`
0, so her list holds one sun that gives nothing and there is no viewer lamp; nothing
touches the previous list again until the next room change. A load runs `InitialiseItem`
(`game/items.cpp`), which empties both lists, and the savegame's restore leaves `il`
alone, so the viewer lamp was back after a load.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_objlight_dark.h` (new; no engine header, like `hd_model_cut.h`):
`HD_OBJLIGHT_DARK_BOUND` and `HDObjLightIsDark`, with the measurement in the comment.
`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp`: `fill_lights` asks it after the type filter at the suns and
at the points and spots, in both lists; the comment above it says what is added to
`Active`. An optional `HDObjLightReport` (`hd_object.h`) comes back from `HDObjectLights`
with the two lists' counts, the dynamics handed on, the count handed on, the count left
out, the brightest channel left out and the dimmest handed on; `report_dark` and
`report_lit` fill it and do nothing without one. `specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp`: the `HDLOG
laralights` line, on her first frame of a level and whenever her room, the count handed on
or the count left out changes; the level's name is kept from `HDLaraDrawBuild`. The bound
lies a factor of 112 above the largest remainder and below every colour a step of a fade
leaves on a light that can add half a unit of 0..255 to a vertex: 0.5/255 has 2.45e-4 on
the first step of its fade-in, 1/255 has 4.9e-4 there and 6.1e-5 on the last step but one
of a fade-out that a room change began one step into its fade-in; the dimmest light of the
level files that is not black, 0.0624 in its brightest channel, has 7.8e-3 on its first
step. A left-out entry would have added to a vertex less than the bound times 255 times
its factor: 0.0051 of a unit for a sun in the inventory, 0.0026 for a point or a spot,
0.0019 for a sun in the world. ModernTest's group `objlight_dark` (20 checks) asserts the
predicate at, below and above the bound, on black, on negative and mixed remainders and on
a NaN, and walks the fade of `lighting.cpp`, transcribed statement for statement, over the
255 grey and the 255 red byte-grid colours and every state a room change can catch. The
fade counts drawn frames, not logic steps: `CalculateObjectLightingLara` runs once for
every frame drawn. `HDLOG lightcheck` and `HDLOG creaturelight` keep `diff=0.0,0.0,0.0`;
their `engine=` counts the engine's `Active` entries and can now exceed `hd_lights=`.
`specific/lighting.cpp` stays word for word, and the classic path adds the remainders as
it does; every shader file stays as it was. With `tomb5.hd_enable` 0 `HDLevelLoad` stops
at its guard before `HDObjectLevelBuild`, so `fill_lights` never runs. The two callers:
`HDObjectEnd` for every HD item and creature in the world, which wear no sheen and gain
the slots that remainders took, and `HDObjectLights` for Lara's composite, whose every
part shares the one list and gains the viewer lamp back.

**Decisions.** The rule is in the HD path and not in `FadeLightList`: the classic path
draws a remainder as nothing either way, and its fade stays the original's. The bound is a
colour in the engine's own scale rather than a test of the fade counter, because what is
left out is a light that gives nothing, wherever it came from; a fade-in starts from 0 and
is never dark on a step, its first step being an eighth of the colour. The log line is
Lara's alone: the items' lists are the same code, and Lara is where the sheen shows. The
current list keeps remainders too, and a light that comes back in range while its
remainder is `Active` is not faded in again (`CreateLightList` asks `!Active`) - a darker
diffuse in the classic path as here; `lighting.cpp` is not touched.

**Commits.** `2bd3f8ea` (the dark light left out), `276f24b6` (the suites), `27450fa0`
(the record), `390ca886` (follow-up fixes)

### Wire mesh on an HD object is cut out
2026-10-01

**What.** The HD object path draws a range of a model's opaque run with the alpha test
when the `.TRM` part it comes from carries a cut-out material - 6, 7 or 8, the room
renderer's three - and the page it wears has holes rather than a mask below the reference:
of the page's texels below alpha 128, at least 100 per mille are at alpha 0. The cache
measures that share on the same sample as its cut-out share, every fourth texel of the top
mip it keeps. The level's `HDLOG level=<L> models` line ends in `cut_ranges` and
`cut_models`.

**Why.** In the HD build the fans of the JOBY levels showed as a dark square behind their
wire grating. The fan of JOBY3 room 79, item 145, is bound to
`ANIMATING1_JOBY3_JOBY5.TRM`; in the classic level the grating is 16 faces of texture
attribute 1 (the colour key). The HD model carries the grating as its part 0, material 6
with param[0] 0.5, and sorts it into the OPAQUE run; the grating's page 11163 lies 71.2
per cent below the reference and 77.4 per cent of that at 0. The object path ran the alpha
test in the alpha run alone, so the holes were drawn with the texels' own dark colour. A
page's share below the reference cannot decide it on its own: `ROMAN_GOD_ANDREA_SWORD`'s
page 9000 is 64.1 per cent below it and 71.5 per cent of that at 0, on material 3. Nor can
the material on its own: Lara's `HAND_BARE_PISTOL` and `HAND_GLOVES_PISTOL` (4\ITEM) are
material 6 over the whole of page 8516, whose texels below the reference are the pistol
grips at alpha 3 to 5 - a mask, 0.4 per cent of them at 0. Over every `.TRM` of the
installation's 4 and 5 ITEM folders, 6 is the only cut-out material in an opaque run and 6
and 8 carry 0.5 in param[0] in every part, which is the reference the model shader already
clips at.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_model_cut.h` (new, no engine header): `HDTrmMaterialCuts`,
`HDPageHolesAreCoverage` against `HD_MODEL_CUT_ZERO_PERMILLE` 100 and the measured table.
`specific/hd/hd_pagecache.cpp`: `measure_cutout` counts the texels at 0 among those below
the reference, the slot keeps the verdict and the share, `HDPageCacheSlotHoles` and
`HDPageCacheSlotZeroPermille`. `specific/hd/hd_model.cpp`: `build` marks a triangle of the
opaque run whose part's material cuts and whose page has holes - the pages are in the
cache by then, because `HDModelLevelBegin` appends them before it builds a model -, sorts
the marked triangles behind the others as the first key, so a model without one sorts as
before, and gives the range a `cut` flag; the draw joins two ranges only with the same
flag and writes gPass.x, the model shader's switch for its clip at 0.5, when the flag
changes. `cut_ranges` counts per model; `HDModelCutRanges` serves the tools.
`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp` ends the level's models line in the two counts. ModelProbe
ends every page line in the share at 0 and a `<- holes` mark, prints `cut ranges` for the
build and the count on the `model` line; ModernTest's `model_cut` holds the rule's
arithmetic. The rule cuts models in ANDY1, ANDY3, JOBY2, JOBY3, JOBY5, RICH2, RICH3 and
TITLE - the fans, a louvred door, trapdoors, a grated staircase, `STEEL_DOOR`, the straw
around a bale (`ANIMATING9_ANDY1`) and the rim of ANDY3's chalk marking
(`ANIMATING16_ANDY3`) - and draws Lara's composite, the guards and the pickups as at
`897c00a`. The soft rim of a hole, the texels between 1 and 127, is cut at 0.5 as the
alpha run cuts it, not blended; the measure is taken on the mip the page keeps. No file
outside `specific/hd` changes, and nothing of it runs with `hd_enable` 0.

**Decisions.** The rule rests on the model file's own marking and a measured property of
the page, with no list of names; the threshold, 100 per mille at 0, lies between the
pistol grips' 4 and the lowest cut-out page's 325 (page 12052). The cut is the object
path's existing one, the shader's clip at 0.5; no blended pass is added for objects. TROne
(GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931 - documents on its own data
that the material and not the run decides, with material 0's alpha kept as a specular mask
(its `docs/SHADER_RULES.md`); which `.TRM` parts are cut, and the page condition, are this
engine's own. Page 16075, the fan blades' page, carries holes too but is worn by material
0 and stays as it is.

**Commits.** `897c00a` (comparison base), `3439980b` (the wire mesh cut), `9d73c697` (the
tools and suite), `8edfc956` (the record), `6f56a364` (follow-up fixes)

### The portal walk, the window on intruding art, and the doorway a randomized run opens
2026-09-07 - 2026-09-11

**What.** In the HD path a room's HD art is drawn over the whole screen, except for the
triangles that stand inside a *different* room: those are drawn inside the classic portal
window of the room they belong to, as a scissor rectangle. A triangle of room `b` is
windowed when its centroid lies inside the interior of some other room `a` - TR5's own
"does an item fit wholly inside its room" box (`game/draw.cpp:3593-3598`) pulled one whole
sector further in on each side - and `a` is not a portal neighbour of `b`, not linked to
it by a vertical floor link, and not its flipmap twin. Over the fifteen levels that is 105
room pairs and 81,261 triangles in 90 groups of 2,709, 0.54 per cent of the game's
15,052,011 triangles, and the only draw calls the scissor test is ever switched on for;
the overhang of a group is counted per triangle with 128 units of slack,
`HD_OVERHANG_SLACK`. The engine's own portal walk gained three changes that both paths
share or that the HD path alone uses. On a frame whose camera was interpolated,
`DrawRooms` seeds the walk with the room that *contains* the interpolated camera position
- `GetFloor(x, y, z, &room)` walked from the logic room - instead of
`camera.pos.room_number`; nothing is written back, and `outside` and `camera_underwater`
are still read from the logic room. Every portal now gets a second rectangle beside the
classic window, its own projection clamped against the screen with the parent room's
window left out of it: a portal *reaches* the room behind it when it faces the camera and
lands on the screen, and a room that only the reach brought in is drawn with all of its HD
art over the whole screen and none of its intruding art, its classic geometry not drawn
either. Each room is visited once; above `kReachBudget` = 128 rooms the walk drops
reach-only rooms farthest first, and a room with a classic window of its own is never
dropped. `GetRoomBounds` and `SetRoomBounds` refuse a room beyond the capacity of
`draw_rooms` and `draw_room_list`, unconditionally and counted. When a randomized level
opens a doorway, the room keeps its HD art: the randomizer records the box its edit opened
in the `.hdm` sidecar and the engine drops every HD triangle that really meets that box.
`makePortal`, `addViewWindow`, `makeVerticalPortal` and `clearWallFaces` record such a
box; only `moveRoom` with a dy and `buildRoomGeometry` still mark a whole room. The
sidecar is version 2, one new line `cut <x0> <y0> <z0> <x1> <y1> <z1>` - six integers,
world units, ascending corners, Y growing downward - and a file without one declares 1 and
stays readable by an older engine.

**Why.** Rooms that stand inside one another in the world bleed through each other's walls
and the depth buffer has nothing to say about it, because both rooms really are at that
distance: ANDREA1's room 53, an air shaft, has 45 of its 272 art cells more than one
sector deep inside room 207 with no portal between the two. Scissoring every HD room to
its classic rectangle is not equivalent to the classic clip and cuts away art that belongs
in the picture: the classic path drops a polygon only when every corner lies beyond one
edge of the window and otherwise draws it whole
(`specific/polyinsert.cpp:883/1055/1281/1422`), while a scissor cuts at the pixel, and a
room's border ring stands on the camera's side of the portal plane and from a shallow
angle projects far outside the portal's rectangle - ANDREA1's room 57 lost its pier to a
vertical strip of sky, and ANDREA2's courtyard rooms 134 and 203 met along a horizontal
black band across the palm trunk and the door lintels. The holder of intruding art never
needed a window at all, so the question is asked of the intruding triangle; it is asked of
a *point* because a cell test cannot be asked identically twice, `HDRenderGroupCellsIn`
counting a cell that merely touches the box and so being one 256-unit ring wider than a
corner test. The camera's own room: at sixty frames a second the camera position is
blended per frame while the logic camera's room steps once per logic step, and where the
two disagree two pieces of the walk throw a neighbour away - the side test in
`GetRoomBounds` (`if (x && (x ^ p->normal[0]) < 0)`) and `SetRoomBounds`' `tooNear == 4` -
leaving the near room drawn alone with the sky standing in the hole, its edges dead
straight along the portal line, for one frame; on ANDREA1's own portal records, room 2's
portal to room 57 lies at world x 48128 with normal -1/0/0, and a blended position at x
48200 seeded with room 2 is refused it in most sampled positions while seeded with room 57
the portal back is followed. At `fps_mode 0` no frame is drawn from a blended position, so
the two can never disagree. The reach: `SetRoomBounds` clamps a child portal against the
window of the room it is seen through, so a room whose doorway lies beside the parent's
rectangle is dropped as `empty` although its portal is plainly on the screen - JOBY2's
room 99 behind the stairs, whose portal projects to 542,116..754,389 while room 124's
window ends at 535, and ANDREA2's room 222, the brick tower of Trajan's Markets, in the
draw list at no level view direction from the courtyard at all and popping into the
picture as Lara walks up to it, while under the reach it is listed at about a third of the
directions. Clipping the child against the parent's *reach* instead is the same walk
unrolled and gains nothing; only leaving the parent out changes the answer, and the
seen-mark is what makes it terminate - with the parent gone, a ring of rooms whose portals
all face the camera can be walked round and round, over 20,000 dequeues on one ANDREA3
frame against the classic walk's 33, while one visit per room makes the worst frame in the
game 319 dequeues (JOBY4) against that walk's own 320. Neither capacity was ever counted:
`room_list_end` was written into the ring modulo 128 with no test and `number_draw_rooms`
incremented with no test at all, while a level may hold 256 rooms and JOBY4's classic
worst-case frame of 106 rooms is already six past the old `short[100]`. The cut boxes: a
whole-room mark paid four rooms for two sectors' worth of wall, among them an 11 x 14
sector courtyard, and where the classic geometry of a randomized level has a hole of its
own the void or the skybox shows through the boundary between the HD and the classic room.

**How.** The intrusion rule: `HDRoomBox`, `HDIntrusion` and the setters
`HDRenderSetRoomBoxes`, `HDRenderSetIntrusions`, `HDRenderIntrusionHits` and
`HDRenderGroupIntrudingTriangles` (`specific/hd/hd_render.h`) hand the boxes and the list
in before the build; `BuildRoomBoxes` (`hd_level.cpp`) fills the boxes out of `ROOM_INFO`,
`BuildRoomIntrusions` builds the list out of `room[]` alone - boxes, portals, floor links
- so an offline tool can reproduce it, and `ReportRoomIntrusions` writes `HDLOG level=%s
overlap pairs=%d intruding tris=%d in %d groups`; `hd_render.cpp` tags the triangle and
carries the tag last in `HDRange`'s sort key, so a level built with no list sorts exactly
as before, and `DrawRoomWindowed` (`hd_level.cpp`) draws the open half over the whole
screen and the intruding half inside the window. The scissor itself: `HDFrameRoom` takes
`ROOM_INFO::left/top/right/bottom` at the seam it already had in `InsertRoom`
(`specific/drawroom.cpp`, one line beside the matrix) and keeps them as a half-open
rectangle with one pixel of margin on every side - the numbers are taken there because
`PrintObjects` resets all four as soon as it is done with a room's items - and
`HDRenderScissor`/`HDRenderScissorOff`/`HDRenderScissorAvailable` (`hd_render.{h,cpp}`)
set `D3DRS_SCISSORTESTENABLE` in both room phases, because a lamp cone hanging in a portal
has to be cut by that portal like the wall beside it; `hd_object.cpp` switches the test
off for every item, items being handed the whole screen as the classic path hands it to
them. The window's units are backbuffer pixels one to one: `InitWindow`
(`specific/3dmath.cpp`) is called with `App.dx.dwRenderWidth/dwRenderHeight`, which are
the present parameters' `BackBufferWidth/Height` (`specific/dxshell.cpp`), and the engine
calls `SetViewport` nowhere except in the HD sky, which restores it. Without
`D3DPRASTERCAPS_SCISSORTEST` both scissor calls do nothing and the rooms draw whole. The
saved state bracket grew by one, the rectangle being a device state with its own
`Get/SetScissorRect` pair, so the bracket check counts 59 items. The walk:
`game/interpolate.h`/`.cpp` hold `InterpEyeRoom`, gated on `g_applied` so that a cutscene
frame and the first frame after a level start are left alone; `game/draw.cpp` holds
`DrawRooms` seeding the walk with it, `SetRoomBoundsReach` taking the projection once and
forming both rectangles from it while the side test, `tooNear == 4` and the fixup for a
portal straddling the camera plane are as they were, `FollowPortal` choosing between the
two, `ReachBeginWalk`, `GetRoomBounds` accumulating the classic window only for a dequeue
that had one, `ReachTrimRooms` removing a reach-only room with no `.TRG` art so its items
cannot be drawn in a room that is not in the picture, `classicHere` keeping `outside`, the
outside rectangle and `snow_outside` on the classic rooms, and the named capacities
`kDrawRoomsMax` = 256 (`draw_rooms`, was `short[100]`), `kRoomListRing` = 512
(`draw_room_list`, was a 128-entry ring, the wrap written `& (kRoomListRing - 1)`) and
`kReachBudget` = 128; `HD_MAX_FRAME` in `hd_level.cpp` follows to 256, one `FrameRoom` of
380 bytes per listed room. 256 is the engine's own maximum - `BuildOutsideTable` refuses a
level with more rooms outright - and a room enters `draw_rooms` once per frame
(`bound_active & 1`), so the array cannot be full while a room is still unlisted and no
eviction rule is needed; 512 is twice the deepest queue that can exist, a room being
queued only while `bound_active & 2` is clear, against a deepest queue of 70 in JOBY4; 128
for the budget because the worst list in the game is 139 rooms (ANDREA1) and at 64 the
list stood at exactly 64 for seconds at a stretch with up to 30 reach-only rooms dropped
in a frame. The cut boxes: the randomizer's `TR5Randomizer/src/core/Tr5Level.cpp`/`.h`
hold `Tr5Level::hdMarkCutBox` with `HD_CUT_OUT_NORMAL` = 512 (half a sector outward along
the opening's own normal, because the HD art builds a wall as a thick solid whose faces do
not sit on the classic wall plane) and `HD_CUT_IN_PLANE` = 128 inward along the other two
axes (because a cut room stays HD and never draws its classic roomlets, so every triangle
the box takes is replaced by nothing), clamped to half the extent so that an opening
narrower than 256 units collapses to a plane through its own middle; a wall opening's box
is derived from the view window now standing at that sector - the 32-byte portal record's
own four corners, which is the opening as far as `SetRoomBounds` is concerned - with the
one-unit inset of a view window undone first, and one derivation serves both ways into
`makePortal`; a vertical opening writes no window at all, so the box is the sector square
at the height the link was opened (byte 7 for a ceiling, byte 5 for a floor, times 256,
with the sector's other byte and then the room's own floor standing in for -127); `@Clear`
takes the box over the faces it really degenerated. Cut lines ascend by their six numbers
(a `std::set`), so the same seed writes the same file byte for byte. In the engine,
`specific/hd/hd_markers.cpp`/`.h` accept versions 1 and 2 and keep the boxes as
`HDMarkersCutCount`/`HDMarkersCut`, a line the reader has no rule for still being ignored
and counted; `hd_level.cpp`'s `BuildRoomCuts` hands the renderer one entry per (group,
box) pair in the group's own local frame; `hd_render.cpp`/`.h` hold the exact
separating-axis test over thirteen axes - the box's three face normals, the triangle's
plane, and the nine cross products of box axis with triangle edge - used because a
vertex-inside test leaves the doorway shut, one wall triangle crossing an opening with all
three corners outside being exactly the triangle that has to go, while a bounding-box
overlap eats more than the opening. The drop is the first thing in the per-triangle loop
of `HDRenderLevelBegin`, before the page slot, the horizontal-plane row, the overhang test
and the intrusion test, so a cut triangle costs no index, no draw call and no count, and a
group with an empty cut list pays one compare per triangle. The cost of the whole rule is
the intruding split alone: whole-level draw calls go from 1,859 to 1,874 in ANDREA1, 1,702
to 1,743 in ANDREA2, 1,553 to 1,563 in JOBY2 and 1,586 to 1,602 in RICH2. Nothing of it
runs with `hd_enable` off: `HDLevelBuild` returns at `HDEnabled()` before any box is
built, `HDLevelLoad` before `HDMarkersLoad`, `g_reach_on` stays false and `FollowPortal`
calls the `SetRoomBounds` that shipped, so the whole difference the classic path sees is
the two capacity guards, the two array sizes, the shape of the ring's wrap and the
camera-room correction in the walk both paths share. Seams behind `-log`, all staying in
the build: one line at the first frame that draws an HD room saying whether the device has
the cap and what the backbuffer is, one line per room with the window it got (`HDLOG
room=53 group=53 clip=812,391,1096,655`), the tally `HDLOG clip rooms=11 full=1
scissored=10 empty=0` once a game second, `ROOMFLASH` (a room in the list on the frame
before and after but not the one between, with the camera position the walk really used
and, per missing room, the reason - `side`, `toonear`, `empty`, `noportal` or `reach`),
`ROOMLIST` (on every membership change and every five seconds the whole list with each
room's window, its reach, which carried it, its distance, its `outside` flag, its undrawn
portal neighbours and the camera and target it was walked from), `ROOMPOP` (a room joining
the list while more than eight sectors away, four lines a second), `ROOMWALK` (once a
second: tween-frame corrections, reach rooms added, budget, trimmed, `cap hit=`), and for
the cuts a `cut=` field per room, the reason word `cut`, one `HDLOG ... cut N x .. y .. z
..` line per box naming the rooms it took art from and how much, and `cuts=`/`cut_tris=`
on the level line; `marker` now means only the whole-room case. Tools: `RoomProbe` carries
`GetRoomBounds` and `SetRoomBounds` over line for line and runs the walk out of the
classic `.TRC` with no device (`-walk`, `-walkyaw`, `-walkpitch`, `-walkpitchfan`,
`-walkwant`, `-walkeach`, `-walkcentre`, `-walkboxes`, `-reach`, `-reachsurvey [step]`
with nine budget columns), and gained `-scissor <l,t,r,b>`, `-roombox <classic folder>`,
`-window all|open|intruding`, `-clipgroup`, `-tround` and `-hdm`, with `-with` holding 32
groups; `TrgProbe` gained `-roomspace`, `-room <n>`, `-statics`/`-slot <n>`,
`-share`/`-slack`/`-deep` and `-near <x> <y> <z> <radius>`, and the two build an identical
intrusion listing, line for line, on all fifteen levels; `InterpTest` gained a `portal
walk` section, a `reach` section (316 checks, among them the JOBY2 rectangles, the
invariant that the classic rectangle lies inside the reach's, and the ring that shows what
the seen-mark is for) and `walk_capacity` (eight checks over the ring's power of two, the
queue depth over 256 rooms each with a portal to every other, and the same level against a
ring of 128 tripping the guard); `HdmDump` and `MapProbe` read version 2 and print the
boxes with their spans, `MapProbe` through the engine's own reader.

**Decisions.** The constants: the slack of 128 sits between the two clumps of overhang
distance - the HD art's relief within 64 units of the box edge, the facades and piers a
whole sector past it - and takes ANDREA2 from 77.6 per cent overhang to 4.5; pulling the
holder's box one sector in takes ANDREA1 from 158 pairs to 7 and ANDREA2 from 148 to 26,
and it is what tells two rooms that merely share a wall from a room that really stands
inside another. A triangle crossing a cut box may reach far outside it and is dropped
whole, which at one doorway costs a lintel band; clipping triangles against the box was
not attempted.

### The room's inside decides, per frame, and the back of a wall is not drawn
2026-09-27

**What.** Two changes to how the HD path draws the HD room art. The opaque room ranges -
pass 0 with no alpha test, no water and no sky - are drawn with their back faces culled
(`D3DCULL_CCW`); every other range stays two-sided as before. And the art of room `b` that
stands inside another room `a` is asked about with TR5's own inside of `a` - one sector in
from the edge of its grid, no second sector taken off - and is no longer windowed
unconditionally: each intruding triangle is bound at load to the nearest classic face of
`b` that it stands on, within 128 units of the face's plane and inside its outline, and
per frame a pair's claimed art is drawn whole when the classic path draws any of the
pair's claiming faces, inside `b`'s portal window otherwise. A triangle no face claims
keeps the answer of the box one sector smaller in x and z: inside the window when it
stands that far inside `a`, drawn whole otherwise. A pair whose holder is not on the
frame's room list is not asked and is drawn whole with the rest of the room. A room the
reach adds to the frame's list with no window of its own has no classic face to ask, and
all of its intruding art keeps the smaller box's answer: the pieces standing in that box
are not drawn, the rest is drawn whole.

**Why.** Seen in play were the bricks of one room on the wall of another (ANDREA1, from
the cafe awning in room 64, room 93's brick hull on the facade of room 101), marble in a
metal room (JOBY2, rooms 24 and 60 in the hub of rooms 28, 30 and 33), and in RICH2's
X-ray room a corridor wall seen from behind as a flat green pane where a reference picture
supplied for this project shows the corridor through the glass. The window the earlier
rule used was the intruder's own and its holder box one sector too small: room 93's hull
stands in room 101's second sector ring, inside no box of that rule, and was drawn whole;
JOBY2's rooms 30 (8 x 4 sectors) and 33 (4 x 3) had no box at all. With TR5's own inside
the hull is windowed, but room 101's facade, which stands inside room 93, is then cut to
101's strip of a window at the same view and room 93's interior shows in its place, while
from inside room 93 the same facade has to go. The box cannot tell those two apart and the
classic path can: it drops a face only when all its corners lie beyond one edge of the
room's window (`specific/drawroom.cpp:577-606`,
`specific/polyinsert.cpp:883/1055/1281/1422`). At the awning three of the six classic
faces of 101 that claim its facade survive that rule and none of room 93's six; inside
room 93 none of 101's six survives. The X-ray pane is not an overlap at all: the renderer
drew every range two-sided (`D3DCULL_NONE`), so the rear face of group 11's corridor wall
painted over the corridor. All 540 of room 101's triangles inside room 93 lie within 86
units of one of six classic faces of 101, and all 108 of room 93's inside room 101 within
1 unit of six faces of 93, so 128 units bind all of them.

**How.** The cull: `RangeCulls` (`specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`) decides per part at the
build, the answer rides in `HDRange::cull` and in the sort key, and `draw_pass` switches
`D3DRS_CULLMODE` per range and puts `D3DCULL_NONE` back at the end of the pass, so a model
drawn between two rooms finds the state the bracket installed; `D3DCULL_CCW` shows the
X-ray corridor, `D3DCULL_CW` at the same view shows the pane and no corridor. The box:
`BuildRoomIntrusions` (`hd_level.cpp`) takes `r->x + 1024 .. r->x + (y_size - 1) * 1024`
and the same in z, TR5's own box (`game/draw.cpp:3628-3633`), with the neighbour, flipmap
and touch tests as they were and a room of two sectors or fewer on a side left without an
inside. The classic faces: `BuildPairFaces` (`hd_level.cpp`) hands the renderer every
drawn quad and triangle of every intruder room, in the roomlets' order and in the room's
own frame, left out only where a face stands further than `HD_PAIR_FACE_REACH` from every
box of its room; `HDPairFace`, `HD_PAIR_FACE_REACH` and the inline `HDPairFaceDistance`
are in `hd_render.h`. The pairs: the index fill (`hd_render.cpp`) gives a triangle to the
first entry whose box holds it and to the nearest claiming face; a triangle no face claims
stays with the pair only when its centroid also lies in the box one sector smaller in x
and z, and goes to the open half otherwise; the same test marks every claimed triangle,
and the pieces (pair, face, mark) and (pair, no face) are numbered per group, so a face
can own two pieces of a pair; `HDRange::intruding` is one plus the piece, so the pieces
never share a draw call, and `HDRenderGroupPairRange` and `HDRenderPairWhole` read them
out and set the frame's answer. The per-frame test: `HDFrameRoom` (`hd_level.cpp`) runs
`ClassicFaceDrawn` on the faces of the room it collects, at `InsertRoom`, with the room's
own view * world matrix, `f_mpersp`, `f_centerx/y`, the underwater wobble and the four
numbers `r->left..r->bottom` - the classic path's coordinate space, a corner nearer than
`f_mznear` carrying -128 as in `aRoomletTransformLight`; the roomlet's box test is implied
by the corner rule and not asked, and so are the facing test and the water chop, which the
window does not decide. The answer: `DecidePairs`, called per room at the top of
`HDFrameDraw`, sets each piece whole or windowed and the glow phase keeps it; a room with
an empty window (one the reach lists and the walk gives no window) is answered by the mark
alone, the marked pieces not drawn and the rest whole; `draw_pass` draws the whole pieces
with the open half and the rest with the intruding half, which `DrawRoomWindowed`
(`hd_level.cpp`) scissors to the room's own window as before. The seams, all behind
`-log`: the level line ends in `holder=inside cull=opaque faces=%d bound=%d unbound=%d`,
each pair line in `faces=%d bound=%d` (a face counted once however many pieces it owns),
the clip line in `pairs=%d whole=%d scissored=%d` (the pieces asked, drawn whole and
windowed; the earlier `scissored=` counts rooms), `windowed_tris=` counts only the
triangles really drawn inside a window, and a line `HDLOG cull level=%s ranges opaque=%d
two_sided=%d` follows the build; the first frame's room list ends an `EMPTY` room's line
in ` where it stands in the box one sector smaller`. The pair line's triangle count is
every triangle the holder's inside holds, the level line's `intruding tris=` and
`unbound=` only those drawn with the window. `FrameRoom` grew to 384 bytes, the frame
array to 96 KiB. Draw calls: ANDREA1's level goes from 1,874 ranges to 2,470, ANDREA2
1,743 to 2,310, JOBY2 1,563 to 1,935, RICH2 1,602 to 2,110, the cull adding none. Tools:
`TrgProbe -roomspace` uses the same box by default (`-deep 1024` asks the old one, which
windows every triangle it holds) and the renderer's own inline face test and unclaimed
rule, and prints the same per-pair fields and the three totals; `RoomProbe` follows the
box and the faces out of the classic `.TRC`, prints the engine's two lines, and gained
`-cull none|opaque`, `-roomwin <g>:<l>,<t>,<r>,<b>[;...]` (a group's walk window, drawn as
`DrawRoomWindowed` draws it) and `-decide whole|scissor|frame|face` with one `decide:`
line per piece, ending in `inner` for a marked one; an empty `-roomwin` window is answered
as the engine answers it. With `hd_enable` off nothing of it runs: `HDLevelBuild` returns
at `HDEnabled()` before any box or face is built, `HDFrameRoom` returns at `GroupOfRoom`
before the corner test, and `HDFrameDraw` with an empty list returns before `DecidePairs`.
The portal walk and its rectangles, the reach, the overhang split, the items' exemption
from the scissor, the two-sidedness of the cut-outs, the alpha pass, the glass, the
additive pass, the water, the sky and the mirror floors are as they were.

**Decisions.** The cull is for the opaque ranges only: cut-out, blended and additive
ranges stay two-sided, and so do water and the sky; a near object's or a solid's back face
can then open onto the clear colour where the camera stands inside a roof, a floor slab or
a solid block. The holder box is TR5's own inside with no extra sector. A pair is decided
per frame from the classic faces its art crosses, and a triangle no classic face crosses
keeps the earlier answer, the window inside the box one sector smaller, and so does all
the intruding art of a room the reach lists with no window of its own, which has no
classic face to ask. The engine decides per pair and not per crossing face, drawing all of
a pair's claimed art whole when any of its claiming faces is drawn, because per face
leaves the lower storey of room 101's facade (144 triangles on a face wholly below 101's
window) cut at the awning; per face is one line in `DecidePairs`. A pair whose holder is
not on the frame's list is drawn whole, because scissored it brings the Piazza corner's
strip of sky back. The principle of deciding the art by the classic faces it crosses -
TROne keeps it per crossing classic face, this engine per pair of rooms - and the
back-face cull follow TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931
- as descriptions only; no code of it was read for this. The ANDREA1 viewpoints in rooms
93 and 101 and the triangle counts of that pair (540 and 90) are the TROne author's own
measurements. The second hull of RICH2's lift shaft in rooms 62 to 64 and the lobby's
mirror floors are not part of this entry.

**Commits.** `07b349e`, `e79b043`, `757bd81`, `a9d5e3c`, `1ca235c`

### A room the reach alone lists draws none of its art in a listed holder
2026-09-28

**What.** A room the reach lists with no classic window of its own draws none of its
intruding art inside a holder that is on the frame's room list; in a holder that is not
listed its art keeps the answer of the box one sector smaller, as before. That answer is
taken back two entries later ("The reach-only answer goes back to the smaller box"); what
stays from this entry is the holder lookup by group, the seams and the tool. The seams,
behind `-log`: the clip line ends in four `reach_` counters, a `reachart` line names every
such room and holder, the level line ends in `band_unclaimed=`, and the ROOMLIST
whole-list dump is also written on the first frame after every `WM_INACTIVE` and
`WM_ACTIVE`, its header ending in `why=`. RoomProbe answers the same way, walks with the
engine's own camera, holds 256 groups, prints a room's final window and replays a log's
whole-list dumps.

**Why.** Art of another room showed through a wall at five places: a dark block beside a
flag in front of a facade (ANDREA1, rooms 57 and 59), a marble ceiling above a metal stair
opening (JOBY2, room 28 looking into 32), window frames in a brick loft (ANDREA1, room
65), a lit floor in a doorway (ANDREA1, room 19) and black pipes beside a pillar (JOBY2,
room 153). Four of them are pieces of rooms the reach lists with no window, drawn whole by
the empty-window answer: room 93's brick hull in the air of room 101, room 24's marble
ceiling in the hub of rooms 30, 31 and 33, room 101's window frames inside room 93's loft
and room 215's floor in room 44's doorway; at the flag the same pieces were left out while
room 93 had a classic window and drawn a moment later with room 93 listed by the reach
alone. The fifth, the pipes, is room 30's art standing in alley 16, unclaimed art in the
holder's wall ring, which the index fill hands to the open half and nothing asks. The
earlier reason for the empty-window answer rested on RoomProbe's first walk note and not
on the room's final window: from inside room 93 toward the doorway to room 101, room 101
has a classic window, and the answer there does not change. After a flipmap a group is
drawn at its pair's room, and a lookup by room index misses it there: JOBY2 swaps five
pairs in its first seconds and keeps them swapped, and at the marble view rooms 87 and 89,
listed by the reach alone, are drawn by groups 54 and 53.

**How.** `DecidePairs` (`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`) looks each piece's holder up on the
frame's list (`g_frame`, whatever window the holder has) for every piece, not only for the
asked ones, and the empty-window branch reads `whole = piece.inner == 0 && !listed`. The
holder is a group, the room of that number at the build, and the lookup compares it with
the groups on the list; the ask branch shares that lookup and changes with it, on a level
with a flipmap only. A piece of an empty-window room that is not answered whole is not
drawn: `DrawRoomWindowed` skips its second, scissored call for an empty window. The ask
branch, the claimed-face loop and the answer for a holder that is not listed stay as they
were, and `pairs=` still counts the asked pieces alone. The counters `g_clip_reach_rooms`,
`_pieces`, `_whole` and `_hidden` count the empty-window rooms that have intruding pieces,
their pieces, the pieces drawn whole, and the pieces left out; the clip line ends in
`reach_rooms=%d reach_pieces=%d reach_whole=%d reach_hidden=%d`. `LogReachArt` writes
`HDLOG reachart level=%s room=%d reach=%d,%d..%d,%d holder=%d listed=%d pieces=%d tris=%d
answer=whole|hidden band_tris=%d`, one line per empty-window room and holder, with the
clip line and on the frame of a window event's dump; the reach rectangle comes from the
walk's log note through `HDFrameNoteReach` (`game/draw.cpp`), the event through
`HDFrameNoteDump`. The index fill counts per intrusion entry the unclaimed triangles it
hands to the open half (read by `HDRenderIntrusionBand`), `ReportRoomIntrusions` keeps
them for the level and the level line ends in `band_unclaimed=%d`; `TrgProbe -roomspace`
ends its level line in the same number. The dump: `RoomListWindowEvents` (`game/draw.cpp`)
is set by the window procedure with `-log` only (`specific/winmain.cpp`), and the
whole-list dump is written when the five-second timer is due or an event waits, a
`WM_INACTIVE` before a `WM_ACTIVE`, the header ending in `why=timer|inactive|active`.
RoomProbe's `-decide frame` answers an empty window the same way
(`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/RoomProbe.cpp`), a window being empty, as `ClipWindow` has
it, when it has no width or no height before any widening; a `decide: reachart` line per
holder and a `decide: clip` line after the picture give the engine's reachart fields and
clip counters over the named groups. The walk takes the engine's camera (`enginecam`): the
integer angles of `phd_GetVectorAngles` with `phd_atan`, `phdtantab` and `phd_sqrt`, the
rotation `aGenerateW2V` builds out of the float sine table, and `AlterFOV`'s integer
perspective. `-walktarget x y z` builds it from the camera position and a world target as
a ROOMLIST dump prints them, `-walkyaw` and `-walkpitch` are rounded once to angle units,
and without `-walk` the same switch hands the engine's yaw, pitch and perspective to the
picture, whose `LookAt` then builds the view from them. With `-reach` the list is trimmed
as `ReachTrimRooms` trims it, the art read from the `.TRG`, and the reach rectangle is
kept as `g_reach_box` keeps it. `-walkwant` and `-walkfinal` print a room's final window,
`final=l,t..r,b reach=l,t..r,b classic|REACH`, per direction with `-walkeach`; `-walkshut
<items|all>` walks with closed doors shut, whose portals `ShutThatDoor` zeroes; `-with`
and `-roomwin` hold 256 groups and refuse a 257th with a message. `-walkdump <log>
[frame]` walks every whole-list dump of a log again with the level, the field of view of
the last `ALTERFOV` line, the backbuffer, the art of the `HDLOG room= ... hd=` lines and
the flips of the `HDLOG flip` lines, searches for what no log line carries - which closed
doors are shut, and a flyby's roll - and prints per dump both lists, the rooms only one of
them has, how many windows are equal, within a pixel and further off, how many reach
rectangles are equal, `doors_shut=` and `roll=`. `-decide frame` counts a holder as drawn
when it is the seed or any `-with` group; the engine lists only the groups it draws in HD,
so the groups the log's `HDLOG room=` lines give `hd=0` stay out of `-with` for the two to
agree. With `hd_enable` off nothing of it runs, and the classic files change only in code
that runs with `-log`.

**Decisions.** The unclaimed band art keeps its answer: a change to it was weighed and is
not made. The tool follows the engine's camera exactly, so that a render is proof. A
narrower rule - a holder counts as listed only when it is the seed or has a window of its
own - was tried in RoomProbe and not adopted.

### The reach can be switched off
2026-09-28

**What.** A registry setting `hd_reach`, `1` by default, decides whether the portal walk
of an HD level carries its second rectangle, the reach. At `0` the walk is the classic one
in an HD level too: a room is listed only through the classic chain of portal windows, and
the art of a room the reach alone would have listed is not drawn. The ROOMLIST whole-list
dump ends in `reach=0|1`, so that a replay walks the same way. With `hd_enable` off the
setting is dead, as the reach is.

**Why.** The reach lists rooms the classic walk refuses, so that the art seen through a
wall the HD art opened is there: JOBY2's room 99 behind the stairs, whose portal lies
beside the window of room 124, and ANDREA2's room 222, the brick tower, in the classic
list from no view direction in the courtyard. The same rooms, listed with no classic
window, are what draws the art of one room through the walls of another at the places the
entry above describes, and every rule that hides that art in the frame opens a hole
somewhere else. The switch lets the classic list alone and the reach with its ghosts be
compared in play at the same place with the same build.

**How.** `global/types.h` holds `tomb5.hd_reach` beside `hd_reflect`; `tomb5/tomb5.cpp`
writes its default, reads it and saves it with the other settings; `game/draw.cpp` sets
`g_reach_on = HDLevelActive() && tomb5.hd_reach` at the start of the game walk and of the
cutscene walk, the head comment of the reach says so, and the whole-list dump's header
ends in ` reach=%d`. The manual's settings table (`docs/Engine-Manual.md`) has the row.
With the setting at `1` the walk is as before, line for line, and with `hd_enable` off
`HDLevelActive()` is false before the setting is asked.

**Decisions.** The setting is on by default, so that a player sees what the entries above
built, and it is documented as the way to see the classic walk's answer in an HD level.
There is no options row: the switch is a way to compare, not a taste.

**Commits.** `264a322`

### The reach-only answer goes back to the smaller box
2026-09-28

**What.** In `DecidePairs` the pieces of a room the reach lists with no window keep the
answer of the box one sector smaller than the inside whatever holder they stand in: drawn
whole outside it, left out inside it. That is the answer of "The room's inside decides,
per frame, and the back of a wall is not drawn", in place of the one of "A room the reach
alone lists draws none of its art in a listed holder", which left them out in a holder on
the frame's list. The seams stay: `reach_hidden` now counts the pieces inside the smaller
box, and a `reachart` line answers `whole` when any piece of that holder stands outside it
and `hidden` when none does. RoomProbe's `-decide frame` follows.

**Why.** The listed-holder answer cleared four places where the art of one room showed
through the walls of another and opened holes at five of the 396 views in which it changes
a piece - a wall panel beside a corridor in Trajan's Markets, the room behind a wire fence
in the Streets of Rome - because at those places the piece it left out is the holder's own
wall, modelled in the neighbour's group. Seen in play, beside the switch of the entry
above, the holes weigh more than the ghosts: a wall that is not there is a fault at every
angle, a hull in the sky at some.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`: the empty-window branch of `DecidePairs` reads `whole
= piece.inner == 0` again, the counter `g_clip_reach_hidden` takes every piece not drawn
whole, `LogReachArt` answers by the pieces of the holder, the first frame's room line no
longer names the holder, and the comments of the counters, of `DecidePairs` and of the
rule over `BuildRoomIntrusions` state the answer as it is.
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/RoomProbe.cpp`: the `frame` answer for an empty window, the
`decide: reachart` answer and the usage text. The manual's paragraph on the reach-only
room and the tools README's two rows say the same. The holder lookup by group, the ask
branch and the claimed-face loop, the format of every seam, the tool's camera and its
switches, the `hd_reach` setting and the walk stay as they were; with `hd_enable` off
nothing of it runs.

**Decisions.** The four places show their ghosts again. A rule that tells a ghost from a
wall is not to be had from the geometry alone - a hull in the sky and a wall panel in the
neighbour's group are the same kind of piece - and none is built; `hd_reach` stays as the
way to see the classic walk's answer. The next entry tells the two apart by the classic
rooms' air and their links.
