### Art in the air of an unlinked room draws inside its own window
2026-10-10 to 2026-10-20

**What.** The art of a room b that stands in the air of a room a that b has no portal,
floor portal or vertical link with, not even through a flipmap twin, is drawn only inside
b's own classic window, and is left out when that window is empty. The HD room art has two
paths, chosen at a level's build by the registry value `tomb5.hd_vis`: `1`, the default,
the visibility path; `0`, the earlier path, the classic portal walk with the reach and the
room-art rules. On the earlier path, besides the air rule, a room under the sky carries
the rooms whose art stands in its inside, a hull (a group whose art outside its own room
is a second copy of other groups' art) is drawn pushed back, and the art over a classic
face that lies inside a larger face of the room it stands in is drawn behind that face's
art. On the visibility path the room list is the engine's own portal walk from the
camera's room, extended by three tables built from the level's art and the classic level,
and every listed room's art is drawn whole; the earlier path's protections stand on it as
rules over the level data: the two depth pushes, the window on art standing in another
room (whole only on the wall of a claimed face drawn this frame), art held by its height
on a holder's wall plane, classic rooms the art replaces left out (with the sky opened
behind a closed lid), static meshes the art lies on left to the art, and the reveal art of
a baked object drawn in front of the classic faces it lies on.

**Why.** In play, art of another room showed through walls at five places in ANDREA1,
ANDREA2 and JOBY2: a dark block beside a flag, a window frame in a brick loft, a marble
strip above a metal stair opening, black bars beside a pillar, a lit floor in a doorway.
All five are art standing in the air of a room the art's own room has no portal, door or
vertical link with (rooms 93 and 101 each in the other's air, room 215 in 44, room 24 in
30, 31 and 33, room 30 in 16), while the palm fronds over a wall in the Streets of Rome
stand in a linked room's air. Over the fifteen levels such art comes to 355,806 triangles
in 415 (group, host) pairs, from 136 in TITLE to 129,471 in ANDREA2. The room boxes alone
cannot tell such art from a room's own walls, since a box holds a room's walls and its
neighbours' overhang alike; the link status is the half they lack: art in the air of a
room it can be seen into belongs there, art in the air of a room it has no way into does
not. Rules that decided per piece which room's art wins still failed where rooms stand in
one another (JOBY2's stairwell, RICH2's lift shaft); what the HD path lacked was the
classic engine's knowledge of which room sees which, passed on from room to room by the
portal walk, and a list built by that walk was requested. On that path the earlier
protections were missed in play (rooms 12 and 212 of ANDREA1 fighting on one wall plane,
RICH2's lift shaft drawn twice, room 99 lost at JOBY2's broken corner by rooms 123 and
124, the container hall's flipmap showing both states, the sky showing through for a
single frame, the ghosts back), and later: a block of room 93 standing over a roof in
ANDREA1, ANDY3's painted classic canopy and forest lids standing across the new trees, the
classic statics of ANDY3's mill-wheel house fighting the art, a row of teeth where JOBY2's
rooms 30 and 60 overlap by 256 units, and JOBY2's facade windows showing the classic
rooms' black and clear tile where the window object's art carries the wall.

**How.** The air (`specific/hd/hd_render.h`: `HDRoomAir`, `HD_AIR_MARGIN` 32,
`HDRoomAirHolds`, `HDRoomAirReaches`, `HDFloorEntryWords`, `HDSectorAir`). The air of a
room is the space its floor squares enclose: a square that is no wall and names no portal
in its floor data, between its highest floor corner and its lowest ceiling corner, the
corners as GetHeight and GetCeiling compute them with the corner substituted for the
offset (the randomizer's `Tr5Level::cornerFloor` reading). A triangle stands in the air
when, at its centroid's x and z and at the four points 32 units from it along x and z, the
heights its corners span reach more than `HD_AIR_MARGIN` below the ceiling and above the
floor (`AirHostsOf` in `hd_render.cpp`); a square with no air between its margins is
reached by nothing. `BuildRoomAir` (`hd_level.cpp`) reads every room's air from
`FLOOR_INFO` and `floor_data` and the table of linked pairs - `next_door` (at file scope),
the floor portals and the flipmap twins, closed over the twins: b and a count as linked
when b or b's twin has a link with a or a's twin - right after `BuildRoomIntrusions`, and
hands both to the renderer (`HDRenderSetRoomAir`, `HDRenderAirPairs`, `HDRenderAirPair`,
`HDRenderGroupAirBoxed`). An intrusion entry's box holds a triangle by its centroid, and
also when the centroid lies in the box in x and z and the triangle reaches into the
holder's air above or below the box (the index fill's `pair_at` loop); boxed art in
unlinked air becomes a piece of its own (`HDPairRange::air`), while art in no entry's box
keeps the box's answer and is drawn with the open half. After the corner heights the class
is 364,423 triangles, 112,265 of them boxed. A triangle of a piece made only for the air
carries `openAir`, and the art a static mesh may take counts it as no piece, so the static
meshes keep their choice of art. Reading the air and asking it costs about 2 to 110 ms per
level.

The answer (`DecidePairs`, `hd_level.cpp`): the air's own pieces with no face outside the
smaller box take the open half's answer, whole; every air piece is held to its room's
window, and kept whole where the classic path draws a face the piece's pair claims, since
that face of the art's room is in sight and the art bound to it - doors, frames, wall
edges - stands proud of it where the window would cut; a piece whose holder is not drawn
takes the pair's claimed answer, its answer without the air rule. A group whose window is
empty keeps none of its boxed air art. `LogReachArt` answers `hidden` for air pieces and
`ReportRoomIntrusions` keeps them out of `intruding tris=` and `unbound=`. `tomb5.hd_air`
(`global/types.h`, written by `tomb5/tomb5.cpp` on a first run, read as `1` when absent,
saved; no options row, like `hd_reach`): `0` hands the renderer no room's air, and every
piece and answer is the one without the rule; `1`, the default; `2` also holds a hull's
art in unlinked air to its window (`MarkAirHulls`); any other value reads as `1`. With
`hd_enable` 0, `HDLevelLoad` returns before any of it.

The earlier path (`hd_vis` 0, with `hd_air` 1 or 2). A room the walk lists with a classic
window that lies under the sky (`ROOM_OUTSIDE`) takes in the rooms whose art stands in its
inside - a triangle whose centroid stands outside its own room's inside and inside the
inside of a room under the sky that is not its flipmap twin - as rooms with no window of
their own and with its reach; their portals are not followed, and the budget may trim them
like any room the reach brings (`CarryArt` in `game/draw.cpp`, `HDRoomCarries` in
`hd_level.cpp`, `CarryHostsOf` and `HDCarryBoxHolds` in the renderer). A pair whose
carried triangles are more than half copies of another group's (a triangle of another
group with its centroid in the same 8-unit world cell, `HDCarryCopyKey`, `MarkCarryCells`)
is no pair, since such copies fight the first copy for the depth: 451 of 583 pairs stay.
The carried room is answered by the flip state (`HDCarriedRoom`: the room the portals lead
to while the flip state has the carried group drawn there, none while its art is out of
the world), and a carrying room's list is that of the group it holds now. A group is a
hull when more than half of its art in unlinked air that no box holds stands on its hosts'
own art, asked per 256-unit world cell: the lowest hull lies at 0.59 and the highest other
group at 0.44. Fourteen groups on nine levels are hulls, among them RICH2's room 61, a
second copy of the lift shaft's floors 62 to 65. A hull's art outside its own room or in
unlinked air is drawn pushed back as a stand range answered `HD_STAND_BEHIND` is
(`HDRange::behind`), so the copy standing in its own room is the one seen.
`MarkCoveredFaces` finds the faces of a pair that lie inside a larger face of the holder
of an entry their room intrudes in (one plane within a unit, the same facing, every corner
within the outline); the pieces bound to them are drawn pushed back, so the larger face's
art wins: 40 faces on six levels (ANDREA1 1, ANDREA3 3, ANDY2 4, JOBY3 20, RICH1 7, RICH2
5).

The visibility path's list (`hd_vis` 1; `specific/hd/hd_vis.h`, `hd_vis.cpp`;
`game/draw.cpp`: `VisExtend`, `VisFollowPortal`, `VisQueue`, `VisNearPortals`). The list
is the engine's portal walk from the drawn camera's room (`InterpEyeRoom`, so at 60 frames
a second the list is the frame's), with the classic `SetRoomBounds` windows and the reach
off, built per frame on the processor as the walk always was. Three tables, built once per
level at the level's build out of the `.TRG` and the classic level and kept by the group a
room holds (so a flipmap swaps them with the rooms, `HDVisRoomOfGroup`), extend it; a room
a table lists is queued as a portal queues it, with the part of the window it is seen in,
so it walks on through its own portals and its window grows by union as the classic one
does. Guests: a group with eight or more triangles whose centroid stands in a room's
inside (the grid less its ring of wall sectors) and more than 128 units outside the
group's own room's box is that room's guest, and must be linked with it unless the room is
under the sky; it is listed by the box of that art, projected as a portal's corners and
clamped to the room's window. Openings: in a room whose own art covers at least half of
its wall samples, every classic wall face is sampled every 64 units, a sample is covered
where the room's own art facing the face's way stands within 128 units along the normal, a
face half bare or more is an opening, and the linked rooms whose box holds the point 512
units behind its middle are listed through the face's corners when the face faces the
camera; an opening whose room behind is the other room of a flipmap pair names the pair's
main room. Wide portals: a portal on an axis plane whose room has bare wall faces in that
plane touching it (bare from 0.3 of the samples, `wideBare`; the openings keep 0.5) is
followed a second time with the corners of the union, and each record of a portal also
takes in the bare faces of the record leading back (one plane within 2 units, the
rectangles touching) when that one is wide, since a portal is two records and the hole the
art leaves around it one hole. A wide opening that has no part in the window it is seen
through but lands on the screen lists the room behind with its rectangle clamped to the
screen. A portal whose projection meets the window on an edge, or stops within 2 pixels of
it at 2,560 pixels of width, lists the room behind with that strip. A portal whose
corners' box, grown by the art's reach of 128 units (`HDVisDefaults`), holds the camera
lists the room behind with the whole window of the room being walked. The tables cost 0.05
to 2.3 seconds a level at its build, only with `hd_vis` 1.

The approach - the walk as the list, every listed room's art drawn whole, a group listed
by its art in a listed room's box - and the count of eight triangles that makes a group a
guest are taken from the TR2 visibility prototype of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931, handed to this project (`THIRD-PARTY.md` entries 209
and 210, the origin sentence in `hd_vis.h`); no code of it was taken. The tables' other
rules - the centroid and its 128 units, the link test, the openings, the wide portals -
and the passing-on are this engine's own. The 128 units are the stand rule's reach: of the
wall faces the art covers wholly within 512 units, 91.4 per cent are covered within 32,
92.7 within 64, 95.8 within 128 and 97.7 within 256. The share 0.3 is the bare share of
JOBY2's broken pillar beside the portal of rooms 123 and 124, which lies between 0.3 and
0.4. The edge of 2 pixels lists again 81 of 181 rooms that dropped off the list for a
single frame between two frames that listed them (4 pixels 85, 8 pixels 90).

The visibility path's draw. Every listed group is one draw over the whole screen in the
opaque room pass, depth test and depth writes as before, the depth buffer deciding what
hides what; the phases are unchanged (`HDFrameDraw`: the glass and the clear floors after
every room's solid art, the glows after the classic buckets, the water, its cards and the
wet floor in their places), and the opaque ranges stay culled one way as `RangeCulls`
picks them, which closes every back face a two-sided draw would show. The HD sky stays
first in its own depth slice behind every point of the world. The level builds the
intrusion list and the rooms' air on this path as on the earlier one, and the two depth
pushes (hulls and covered faces) stay. `DecidePairs` answers each piece as on the earlier
path - inside its room's own window unless a claimed face is drawn this frame - and the
rest of the room's art is drawn whole. An air piece with a claimed face stays whole only
when a claimed face of its pair that the classic path draws this frame is one wall with
the piece's own face (`BuildVisWalls`, `HDVisFacesOneWall`, `HDVisWallLabels`): faces
joined where one stands in the other's plane (every corner within 1 unit), or where both
stand upright (the normal less than 1 in 100 off the horizontal) and meet along an edge at
two points a unit or more apart - the corners a wall turns, since the art of one wall
reaches over the seams of its faces in the wall's plane and around its corners. The labels
are made once per level, when the first frame asks, and a frame asks only whether a drawn
face carries the piece's label; a piece no face claims keeps the pair's answer.

Art held by its height (the index fill's `height_at` and `by_height` in `hd_render.cpp`;
`HDVisHeightReaches`, `HDVisOnBoxSide`; `DecidePairs`; the visibility path only): a
triangle no box and no air holds, whose centroid an entry's box holds in x and z, whose
three corners lie in one side plane of that box within a unit, and whose corners reach
into the box's height by more than `HD_AIR_MARGIN`, becomes a piece of its own (`air` 2);
while its holder is drawn it is art in unlinked air, held to its room's window, and
otherwise, and with `hd_vis` 0, it is the open half it was. Over the fifteen levels 1,179
triangles in 155 pieces.

Classic rooms left out (`VisHidesClassicRoom` in `hd_level.cpp`, asked by `HDFrameRoom`
for a room no group draws; `hd_vis.h`: `HDVisClassicRoomHidden`,
`HDVisClassicRoomVerdict`, `HDVisFloorOnArt`, `HDVisTables::floorRooms`; the visibility
path only). A room drawn classic whose own group holds no art and none of whose faces the
stand rule covers, wholly or in part, draws none of its faces when its inside holds a
guest, or when it has floor links and every one of them names a room drawn HD (the level's
verdict per room through the flip table, the same in every frame, not the frame's list); a
room a randomizer marker names stays classic. Over the fifteen levels it takes ANDY3's
rooms 88, 118 and 122 and ANDY1's 212, forest bands under the sky with guests, and ANDY3's
26, 28 and 210, lids of painted trunk walls and leaf ceilings over the hollows of rooms
24, 27 and 209, and no other room. A listed room so left out that is not under the sky
turns the walk's `outside` on, as a listed room under the sky does
(`HDVisClassicRoomOpensSky`, `HDVisRoomOpensSky`; `GetRoomBounds` in `game/draw.cpp`), so
the sky is drawn behind the trees: ANDY3's three lids alone. In such a frame the other two
readers of `outside` act as under the sky: the weather (`DoRain`, `DoSnow`) and
`S_GetObjectBounds`, which keeps an object past the far plane. A classic room enclosed by
another room's art keeps its faces: the enclosure table (`HDVisTables::enclosedBy`) is
kept for the `HDLOG vis` line and RoomProbe's `-vis` lines only.

Static meshes the art lies on (`hd_vis.h`: `HDVisStaticCovers`, `HDVisStaticDrawnByArt`;
`hd_vis.cpp`; `hd_level.cpp`: `VisStaticFaces`, the statics handed in by `BuildRoomVis`,
`VisStaticLeftToArt` asked by `HDStaticDrawnClassic`; the visibility path only). Once per
level, every static whose own room's art holds less than a twentieth of its box's cells,
and that is not flat (`HDStaticFlat`: a pane or a square laid on a wall lies on whatever
art stands behind it, which need not model it), is sampled over its faces every 64 units
(`HD_COVER_STEP`, the stand rule's step), and per group whose room's box holds the centre
of its faces the samples a triangle of that group's opaque or alpha art covers within 32
units, facing either way, are counted; a static the frame would draw classic is left to
the group with the largest share when that share is a half or more and the frame draws the
group. The reach and the share sit in the gap of the fifteen levels' census: the statics
the art models lie at 0.603 to 1.000, the others at 0.475 and below; with a reach of 16
units the two classes mix, and sampled every 16 units the shares move by 0.006 at most. 19
statics are taken, ANDY3's six of the mill-wheel house among them. The level costs 13 to
533 ms.

Baked objects (`hd_cover.h`: `HDStandItemBox`, `HDStandBoxHolds`, `HDStandBoxFind`,
`HDStandRangeBaked`, `HDStandDrawBaked`, `HDStandFrontMatrix`; `hd_level.cpp`:
`BuildBakedBoxes`, `BuildStandRanges`, `DecideStand`). The boxes of the level's items
whose slot the `.MAP` calls `DUMMY` (the map's own word, never a donor slot, never Lara's,
as `hd_object.cpp` names baked slots) are made from the object's first frame's bounds at
the item's place, its yaw in quarter turns. A stand range is that object's art when every
triangle of its (group, holder, kind) - kind 1 lying on the holder's faces whole, kind 0
reaching onto them, asked again with `HDCoverTriOnFaces` - stands in such a box by its
centroid. On the visibility path, where the frame lists the holder, draws its classic
faces and would leave such a range out or push it back, the range is drawn in front
instead, in its own group's window with its group's lighting, or in the holder's window
when the group is not listed, its `view * world` scaled towards the camera by
`HD_STAND_PUSH`, a five-hundredth of the distance (the stand rule's measured back push),
so it lands on the same pixels nearer; its group leaves it out. A relief range (kind 2)
and every other answer stay as they were; `hd_vis` 0 answers as before. Over the fifteen
levels' 404 `DUMMY` boxes and 150 stand ranges the rule takes four ranges of 226
triangles, the reveals of JOBY2's two facade windows (slot 444 `ANIMATING15`, items 173
and 174).

The switch. `tomb5.hd_vis` (`global/types.h`, read and written beside `hd_air` in
`tomb5/tomb5.cpp`) is `1` on a first run and for an absent value; `0` keeps the earlier
path. A second value, `hd_vis_rev` (`HD_VIS_REV`, `HDVisSetting` in `hd_vis.h`), tells a
`0` that an earlier build wrote on its first run from a `0` set by hand: below the
revision the saved value is moved to `1` and both values are written back; from the
revision on the value is kept as set, and any value above `1` reads as `0`. `BuildRoomVis`
(`hd_level.cpp`) takes the setting at the level's build and hands the classic side to
`hd_vis.cpp` (rooms, classic faces as `BuildStandFaces` reads them, portal records, floor
links); the renderer's build hands the `.TRG` it has open to `HDVisLevelBuild`. The walk
asks `HDVisWalkOn` (the level built with the path and `HDLevelActive()`), so the F12
switch and the HD textures row turn the path off with the rest of the HD path, and with
`hd_enable` 0 nothing of it runs.

Logs behind `-log`: the level line's `air_ms= air_tris= air_groups= air_pairs= air_boxed=
air=`, one `HDLOG unlinked level= group= host= tris=` line per pair, the `clip` line's
`unlinked_pieces= unlinked_drawn= unlinked_hidden=`, the intrusion level line's `covered=`
and one `HDLOG covered` line per face, the ROOMWALK reach line's `carried=`, one `HDLOG
carry level= host= group= tris= ... copies=` line per pair, one `HDLOG hull level= group=
air_tris= host_art= hull= behind=` line per hull, `HDLOG level= vis=1 rooms= art_rooms=
walls= bare= void= guests= guest_tris= wide= ms=` once per level, `VISLOG frame= eye_room=
rooms= walk= guest= opening= wide= dequeues= list= near=` once a second and when the
camera's room changes (a room listed through a portal the camera stands at is named `n`),
the `HDLOG settings` line's `hd_vis=` with a line before it when a value was moved, and
`HDLOG stand_baked level= boxes= ranges= tris=`. Tools: `TrgProbe -roomspace` (the air,
the links, the boxed count, the `hull census` lines), `-vistable` (the tables,
`openings_twin=`, `wide_mirror=`) and `-classicart -perface`; RoomProbe `-unlinked 0|1|2`,
`-air 0|1|2`, `-classicmark`, `-classicclip`, `-flip`, `-vis 1` with `-vissrc`,
`-visreach`, `-visbare`, `-visguest`, `-visguestrule`, `-visoverhang`, `-visedge`,
`-viscams` (a camera file run as a set), `-viswin`, `-visnear`, `-visplane`, `-visfaces`,
`-visportals`, `-visheight`, `-walkdoors`, `-staticcover`, `-hollow`, `-opensky`,
`-standlist`, `-ties`, `-push`, `-nofront` and `-gpu` (the frame's solid room draws
timed), and the walk's `-walkfinal` lines naming each room's source; ModernTest's
`vis_tables` and its checks on the wall, the hidden rooms, the statics, the height, the
box side, the migration, the lids, the sky and the baked ranges.

**Decisions.** The air rule may only remove art, never add it: a piece in unlinked air is
drawn inside its own room's window or not at all. Art in a linked neighbour's air keeps
its answer, because the palm fronds over the walls and the balustrade walls are of that
kind. A floor-data portal links two rooms as a portal does (without it ANDY1, ANDY3 and
TITLE lost art seen through such doorways), and a link through a flipmap twin links too,
since in one state the twin's portals lead out of the room at that place (without it 31
pairs of 24,936 triangles were held to their own window in every state). Only the art an
intrusion entry's box holds is held to its window: holding every triangle in unlinked air
took mostly art standing where the classic frame shows it (ANDREA2's street art and palm
crowns, RICH2's marble tints and lift shaft), while the boxed art alone removes the five
ghosts the same. The margin is 32 units: at 16 the class grows by 1 to 59 per cent and the
picture differs at three of nineteen places. No load-time cache: the slowest level takes
about 110 ms, under the 300 ms that would call for one. An empty window keeps none of its
boxed air art, as built: the hole it leaves in RICH2's room 114 looks out into the void
and is not seen in play; `RoomProbe -unlinked 2` draws the other answer. A rule that
decided per room which art wins was built and reverted (`7c1b98ec`); the visibility path
gives up that decision for the walk's passing-on. The guests and the openings need a link:
without it rooms standing in one another drew over the walk's art (JOBY2's room 24, whose
box shares 1,280 units of height with rooms 31 and 33, covered the stairwell with its
marble; ANDREA3's room 92 put a beam into the enclosed room 63). The listing of a portal
off the window holds for wide portals only: for every portal it brought JOBY2's court room
30 and its pipes into the court's wall. A classic face drawn behind the art is not built
(no place needs it, and drawn behind every room's art it would show classic faces through
every opening the art makes on purpose), nor is keeping the last frame's rooms one frame
longer (a state outside the level data). For the pieces on the visibility path the earlier
path's answer was chosen over every piece whole, the air pieces alone windowed, every
piece windowed, every piece left out and the whole group windowed: it differs least from
the earlier path, a cut by the room's own box takes art the earlier path draws, and a push
behind the listed room's art cannot hide art that stands against the sky. The claimed
face's wall, not its plane: held to the plane alone, the rule cut ANDREA3's wooden wall of
room 8 at its corner. The height rule asks the box's side plane and a drawn holder: by the
height alone it also cut a beam's end in ANDREA1's room 110 and cracks at a wall corner of
room 228. ANDY3's mill, listed from the house's roof through the guest art of rooms 93 and
95 and the walk on from it, is kept as it is. A rule that left out a classic room enclosed
by another room's art was built and taken back: JOBY2's sniper rooms 19 and 21 are hollow
groups whose bars and walls are their own art, which the engine never draws, so with their
faces left out the window showed the sky; their faces stay, and the reveal over them is
the baked rule's. The migration is a revision of this one key and not a version of all
settings, so a later move of another key cannot be read as this one. A room with floor
links is left out only when every link names a room drawn HD, so a room half over classic
ground keeps its faces. The baked reveal is drawn in front and not in place: in place it
fights the coplanar classic faces over its whole area, and the `DUMMY`'s own mesh is never
drawn, so no texture is brought twice.

### A classic room covered by another group's art is drawn as that art
2026-10-04

**What.** A room the engine draws classic - no group, an empty group, a hollow group - can
have its floor and walls modelled in another group's art, and the frame now draws such a
place once. At level build every classic face of every room the randomizer did not mark is
handed to the renderer (`BuildStandFaces`); the renderer keeps the rooms whose own group
draws nothing inside their box and gives every other room group's art on their faces, or
standing in their box, draw calls of their own - stand ranges, three kinds per (group,
holder): reaching onto the faces, lying on them whole, in the box on no face. After the
build a room is *covered* when one HD group's art covers every sample of every face; that
group is its *carrier*. Per frame, a listed covered room skips its roomlets and is drawn
as the carrier's art - with the carrier when the carrier's room is listed, inside the
room's own portal window with the carrier's matrix and lighting when it is not - and every
other group's copy of its faces is left out. A listed room no group covers at least half
of stays classic and the art lying on its faces whole is left out (a room covered in part
is the next entry's); the art that only reaches onto its faces is drawn with its group
pushed back in depth by 1/512 of its distance, so the classic face wins every pixel the
two share and the art beyond the face stays. Every other group's art in the box is drawn
with its group as before. A room with the mist or reflection flag, and a room whose
carrier has a flipmap twin or is one, stays classic whatever the art covers. In the game
two rooms are covered and drawn as art - ANDREA2 124 (carrier 121) and RICH2 15
(carrier 14) -, six are drawn in part by the next entry (RICH2 16, 18 and 19, RICHCUT2 2,
3 and 4), and fourteen stay classic with foreign art on their faces: ANDREA3 74, ANDY1
212, ANDY3 26, 28, 88, 103, 118, 122 and 210, JOBY2 19 and 21, TITLE 70, 101 and 103.
Sixty-one more classic rooms hold foreign art and have no classic face, so the classic
path draws nothing there (ANDREA2 102 among them); twenty have no foreign art. ANDREA1,
ANDY2, JOBY3, JOBY4, JOBY5, RICH1 and RICH3 have no such room.

**Why.** ANDREA2's courtyard room 124 is a hollow group and drawn classic, and group 121 -
the room through its west portal, never on the intrusion list because a neighbour is not -
carries 14,700 triangles inside it that cover all 46 of its classic faces. A frame that
listed both rooms drew both surfaces into one depth buffer: the floors coincide and
fought, the classic walls stand up to 128 units in front of the recessed art walls and
won, and looking away from the portal 121 left the list and the classic room was drawn
alone - which surface won depended on the angle. RICH2's stairwell (rooms 14 to 19, all
their art in group 14) is the same case. Calling such a room HD is not an answer: its own
group holds nothing in it, and in a frame without the neighbour it would be void, which is
what the hollow rule exists for. The covering group is one group and not the union of
several, because a second group that covers the faces is a second copy of the surface:
group 127 carries a copy of 36 of room 124's 46 faces beside 121's, and drawn in the
room's window as well it fought with 121's like the classic faces did. The art that lies
on the faces whole is what can be left out; a triangle that only reaches onto a face
leaves it - group 117's palm trunk grazes a face of room 124 and lost its lower half when
its 16 such triangles were left out - so it is kept; but in a room that stays classic it
lies in the classic surface - RICH2 16 showed a band of the two alternating along the top
of its walls and under its stairs - so while the room is listed it is drawn pushed back
rather than cut. The push is a fraction of the distance and not a fixed depth offset
because the depth buffer's step grows with the square of the distance: a fixed offset
would be hundreds of units far off and nothing close by. The relief in the room's box (a
planter, the jambs of an arch) is part of the carrier's art in the room's window: without
it the arches showed slivers of the clear colour.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_cover.h` is new and pure, shared by the engine, ModernTest,
TrgProbe and RoomProbe: `HDCoverMakeTri`, the sample test
`HDCoverHits`/`HDCoverSamples`/`HDCoverSet`/`HDCoverFaces`, the threshold
`HDCoverRoomCovered`, `HDCoverOverlaps` (the triangle clipped to the face's 128-unit slab
and both compared in its plane by separating axes), `HDCoverTriOnFaces` and `HDStandDraw`
(with `behind` for grazing art on a listed room drawn classic). `specific/hd/hd_render.h`:
`HD_STAND_OUT`/`_WITH`/`_BEHIND` and `HD_STAND_PUSH`. `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`:
`HDRenderSetStandFaces` on the contract of the intrusion list; before the build, the
holders the `.TRG` leaves classic - no group, or no triangle whose centroid lies in the
room's box with `HD_OVERHANG_SLACK`; per group the holders asked, its own room and its
flipmap twin left out; per triangle the tag (taken out of the intrusion piece and the open
half; the intrusion hits are still counted) and the range by holder and kind; the sort key
ends in `stand`; `draw_pass` and `draw_receive` draw a stand range alone in
`HD_WINDOW_STAND` or with its group while `HDRenderStandWith` says so, a range answered
`HD_STAND_BEHIND` with the group's matrix pushed back by `set_stand_matrix`, the clip z
raised by `HD_STAND_PUSH` times the projection's b, so the depth a - b / z becomes that of
the point 1/512 of its distance further away; `HDRenderRoomStand`.
`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`: `BuildStandFaces`, called beside `BuildRoomCuts`;
`BuildStandRanges`, run once every group's `g_group_hd` is decided, picks each holder's
carrier, leaves a room with `ROOM_MIST` or `ROOM_REFLECT` or a carrier that has a flipmap
twin or is one uncovered, and lists the ranges the frame answers; `StandHolderRoom`,
reached from `HDFrameRoom` for a room whose group is not HD, notes a holder with its
matrix and window and answers true for a covered one, so `InsertRoom` skips its roomlets;
`DecideStand` answers every range per frame and queues the in-window draws, and
`DrawStandInHolders` draws them in each phase; a covered room listed with no HD room still
opens the frame. The hollow rule's comment says what the room is drawn as. Log lines
behind `-log`, at the end of existing lines: `HDLOG room=` ends in `stand=` (triangles of
HD groups on its faces), `covered=` and `carrier=`; the build line in `stand_rooms=`,
`covered=`, `stand_tris=`; the clip line in `stand=` with five counts and `stand_behind=`,
the ranges drawn pushed back. TrgProbe `-classicart` prints a `union=stand` line, the
engine's threshold from the `.TRC` with each holder asked on its own; RoomProbe takes
`-stand` and `-coincide <units>`; ModernTest holds `stand_draw`, `stand_cover` and
`stand_overlap`. A triangle standing on the faces of two holders is tagged to the first
holder in room order.

**Decisions.** The threshold is strict per face - every sample of the face, sampled every
64 units, art within 128 units facing the way the face does: a face drawn as art that the
art does not cover shows the void where the art stops (RICH2 16 has no art under its 16
ceiling faces, RICH2 18 one bare face, RICHCUT2 3 two faces at 27 to 29 per cent), so such
a face stays classic (the next entry). The carrier is one group, of several the one
covering the most faces (the next entry), then the most triangles on them, then the
lowest. Art that only grazes a classic room's faces is kept rather than cut, and while
that room is listed and stays classic it is drawn pushed back rather than over the faces.
The push is 1/512 of the distance: 1/1024 reaches the same result on the views of RICH2
16, 18 and 19 and 1/2048 leaves 4,355 pixels to the art in one view of RICH2 19, so 1/512
keeps a factor of two for nearer views. A room with the mist or reflection flag, or with a
carrier a flipmap can swap away, stays classic rather than lose its water or be drawn by
nothing while the flip is on; neither is the case for ANDREA2 124 or RICH2 15 (flags
0x0040 and 0x0048, no flipmap partner of 121 or 14). The kind-2 ranges of a holder that is
not covered answer like untagged art and are kept apart all the same, at a cost in draw
calls (ANDREA2's opaque calls 2,235 to 2,297, RICH2's 1,839 to 1,972, the seven levels
with no such room unchanged). The palm statics of ANDREA2 124 are left to the art of
groups 117 and 127 by the next entry.

**Commits.** `666773b` (the base of this change), `1a5349e` (covered room drawn as art),
`e6de726` (the suites), `29df3a3` (first corrections), `1984539` (the suites)

### A place the art draws is drawn by the art alone: a classic room face by face, her shadow there, and the static meshes
2026-10-05

**What.** A classic room another group's art covers is drawn as that art face by face. Per
classic face of a classic-drawn room the test of the entry before decides whether a group
covers it (every sample, art within 128 units facing the way the face does); the room's
carrier is the group that covers the most faces (then the most triangles on them, then the
lowest group). A room whose carrier covers every face is drawn as its art as before; one
whose carrier covers at least half of them is drawn in part: its covered faces are left
out of `InsertRoomlet` one by one and drawn as the carrier's art - with the carrier's
group when that is listed, in the room's window when it is not -, its kept faces stay
classic, the carrier's art lying whole on a kept face is left out, and its art that stands
on a covered face and reaches onto a kept one is drawn pushed back, so the kept face wins
the pixels the two share. A room the carrier covers less than half of stays classic as
before. Lara's projected shadow runs in a room drawn as art that keeps no classic face she
can stand on (a face pointing up by more than half) and in a classic room with no classic
face at all, unless a floor sector of it that opens into no room below has no other
group's art in the room's box; every stand range drawn in a holder's window takes the
receive. The static meshes follow the art: a static is drawn the classic way only where no
art a frame draws at its place, while its room is listed, holds it. Its room's own group
is asked at the box, as before; the carrier's stand ranges that every frame listing a room
drawn as art draws, and every other HD group's overhang - its art outside its own room -
and its stand ranges drawn whenever it is listed, are asked at the static's own mesh
vertices. The own art or the carrier holding it gives the static to the art for good;
other groups holding it give it to their frames, and a frame that lists its room and none
of them draws its piece - the triangles of the holder with the most of its vertices that
make the object - in the room's window with that group's matrix, lighting and shadow
receive, so the object is the art at every angle; where no piece can be cut out of the art
without cutting a larger structure, the classic static stands in. Ten of the 21 statics
held by other groups have a piece: ANDREA2's two trunks and six crowns, ANDREA1's crown
and ANDY3's tree. A flat static is asked of no other group. A shatterable static pairs
with the destructible piece of any group in its box. A room drawn wholly as art that the
reach lists with an empty window stays on the list while its carrier is listed, so its
items are drawn. In the game ANDREA2 124 and RICH2 15 are drawn as the art, RICH2 16 (16
of 32 faces), 18 (15 of 16), 19 (13 of 15) and RICHCUT2 2 (46 of 49), 3 (106 of 112) and 4
(22 of 29) in part; TITLE 70, 101 and 103 and ANDREA3 74 stay classic under half, eleven
rooms with no covered face. 65 of the game's 2,845 statics change their answer: ANDREA2's
six palm crowns and two trunks of room 124, RICH2's 40 flights, railings and wall squares
of the stairwell, RICHCUT2's four hanging lamps, ANDY1's nine parts of a hut, ANDY2's two
roof beams, one crown in ANDREA1 and one roof in ANDY3.

**Why.** In play, the crowns of the palms were drawn twice everywhere in ANDREA2, and
RICH2's stairwell still flickered and was partly classic. A room with one uncovered face
stayed classic whole, so the walls of RICH2's three upper storeys were drawn classic and
the art on them left out although the art covers 16, 15 and 13 of their faces; and a
static was left to the art only in a room drawn HD and only for its own room's art, so the
51 statics of the four storeys of the stairwell, the trunks of ANDREA2 124 and the six
crowns - each modelled in the art of the room under it - were drawn beside the art that
holds them. In ANDREA2 124 and RICH2 15 Lara cast the round blob, because the shadow's
gate asked whether her room's own group is drawn HD. At some angles both palms turned
classic: the frame listed the courtyard and the room above it but neither room whose art
holds them (117 and 127).

**How.** Faces, one by one: `specific/hd/hd_cover.h` - `HDCoverFaceCovered`,
`HDCoverCarrierBetter`, `HD_COVER_PART_SHARE` 0.5 and `HDCoverRoomState` (classic, in
part, covered); `HD_STAND_FACES_*` and `HDStandDrawFaces`, which answers a covered or
classic room exactly as `HDStandDraw`. The renderer (`specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`): the
stand tag and a pre-pass over a group's triangles with the index fill's exclusions that
works out the faces each group covers of each holder
(`HDRenderStandCovers`/`HDRenderStandCoverAt`; `HDStandCover` in `hd_render.h`), then
splits the ranges of a group that covers a holder in part by the faces they stand on
(`HDStandRange::faces`); an in-window draw is pushed back through `g_stand_pick_behind`
(`HDRenderRoomStand`). `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`: `BuildStandFaces` records each face's
roomlet and slot, `BuildStandRanges` takes the carrier out of the renderer's records,
keeps the two guards and builds the drop flags; `HDRoomletDropped` hands them to
`InsertRoomlet` (`specific/drawroom.cpp`), which leaves a flagged quad or triangle out -
null at once with `hd_enable` off and for every room not drawn in part; `StandHolderRoom`
and `DecideStand` answer with `HDStandDrawFaces`, and `DrawStandInHolders` draws. The
shadow: `HDCoverFaceUp` (the sign `HD_COVER_UP_SIGN`, taken from RICH2 15's floor),
`HDCoverFaceFloor` (up over `HD_COVER_FLOOR_UP` 0.5) and `HDCoverRoomShadowHD`;
`HDRoomShadowHD` (`hd_level.cpp`), asked by the gate in `specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp`; a
classic-drawn unmarked room with no classic face counts HD for her shadow unless it has a
bare floor - a sector she can stand on that opens into no room below while no other HD
group but its flipmap twin has a vertex in a cell of the room's whole box
(`HDRenderGroupCellsIn`, `HDCoverRoomShadowHD`'s `bareFloor`); `ReceiveStandInHolders`
draws every in-window range into the receive through `HDRenderRoomShadowStand`. The
statics: the rule in `hd_cover.h` - `HD_STATIC_SHARE`, `HD_STATIC_OTHER_NUM`/`_DEN` and
the answers, `HDStaticCellsHold`, `HDStaticOtherHolds`, `HDStaticStandSure`,
`HDStaticStandWithGroup`, `HDStaticAnswer`, `HDStaticFlat`, `HDStaticPiecePaired`,
`HDStaticDrawClassic`, the piece's distances `HD_STATIC_PIECE_REACH`, `_SLACK` and `_OPEN`
and the frame's one source `HDStaticDrawSource`; the renderer keeps per group the cells of
its overhang of no intrusion piece and no stand range (`cellsFree`) and one list per stand
range, and `HDRenderStaticArt` answers one static for the engine and for RoomProbe alike.
The pieces: the statics' places (`HDStaticPlace`), handed by `BuildStaticPlaces` to
`HDRenderSetStaticPlaces` before the build, whose index fill notes every triangle of an
overhang of no intrusion piece or of a stand range whose centroid lies within the reach of
another room's static (`NotePlaceTri`); `HDRenderStaticArt`'s fourth step has
`MakeStaticPiece` cut the first holder's piece out of them, `HDRenderStaticPiecesWhole`
keeps a room's held statics pieces all or none, `HDRenderStaticPiecesUpload` puts them in
an index buffer of their own, and `HDRenderStaticPiece`/`HDRenderStaticPieceShadow` draw
one with its group's constants and pages; `NoteStaticPiece` notes the draw with the window
and the matrix of the static's room where `HDStaticDrawnClassic` answers the piece, and
`DrawStaticPieces` draws them after the stand ranges in the four phases and in the
receive. `BuildStaticTables` asks `HDRenderStaticArt` for every static of every room with
the static's mesh vertices out of `MESH_DATA::aVtx`, pairs the shatterable ones with any
HD group's piece, and `HDStaticDrawnClassic`, indexed through the flip table and answering
by the level as built, answers `DrawStaticObjects` (`game/draw.cpp`) with the frame's
`draw_rooms` and no test of the option before it. The other askers of `HDRoomIsHD`:
`ReachTrimRooms` (`game/draw.cpp`) asks `HDRoomArtListed` through `ReachDropArtless`, once
before the budget and once more after a budget trim, so a room drawn as art whose carrier
the budget trimmed comes off the list as well. Log lines behind `-log`, at the end of
existing lines: `HDLOG room=` ends in `faces=`, `faces_covered=`, `floors_kept=` and
`shadow=`, and its `carrier=` names the carrier of a room drawn in part too; the build
line in `part=` and `shadow_rooms=`; `HDLOG static ... classic` in `verts=`, `groups=`,
`answer=` and `piece=` (the piece's group and triangles, `held=`, `open=` and `others=`),
a new `HDLOG static ... classic_room` line for the statics of a classic-drawn room ending
the same way, `destructible piece=` in `group=`; the level's statics lines in
`classic_room_art=`, `classic_room_group=`, `paired_other=` and `art=`, `by_group=`,
`classic=`, `pieces=`. Three fields of the first statics line change their meaning:
`shatterable=` and `paired=` count the slot 50 to 57 statics of every room whatever their
answer (before, those of rooms drawn HD that the art held), and `classic=` counts a static
of a room drawn HD only when its answer is `classic` (one held by other groups' frames is
in the second line's `by_group=`). Tools and tests: RoomProbe `-statictable`, `-listroom`,
`-piece`, `-standreceive`; TrgProbe `-classicart -perface`; ModernTest's `stand_part`,
`stand_shadow`, `static_art` and `static_piece`.

**Decisions.** A room is drawn in part when its carrier covers at least half of its faces:
TITLE 103 drawn in part showed 741 empty pixels along the seams of kept and dropped faces
with the carrier listed. The carrier is the group covering the most faces, then the most
triangles, then the lowest group. The renderer splits a group's ranges by its own coverage
of a holder, so a room no group covers in part draws its old ranges; a carrier's own room
draws more calls for the split (RICH2 14 116 instead of 109). A face she can stand on
points up by more than half, decided per room; a classic room with no classic face counts
HD for her shadow, decided on the floor data of the 81 such rooms, unless it has a bare
floor: 64 count, and 17 with a sector she can stand on and no art in the box keep the blob
(ANDREA3 71 and 72, RICH1 142, RICH3 205, 212 and 217, five rooms of JOBY2 and six of
TITLE), since nothing under her would take the receive. A face counts as covered only by
the triangles the tag gives its own room: a triangle is drawn in one holder's window, so
art tagged to a neighbouring holder could not fill a dropped face while that neighbour is
off the list. In-window draws are pushed back like the ones with their group. A static is
asked of three sources and of its own vertices for all but its own room's art: a box count
cannot tell another place's floor from the object (the carrier of ANDREA2 124 holds 4 of
36 cells of a trunk's box, the floor under it, and 3 of its 12 vertices). Another group's
art counts only outside its own room (its overhang): inside it models its own room. A flat
static is asked of no other group: RICH2's room 6 has two panes whose twelve corners lie
in cells of room 11's art and which no art shows. The own art's twentieth is kept:
changing it would move statics of rooms with no such place, and the 2,776 statics of rooms
drawn HD show no gap to move it into (79 at nothing, 20 below a twentieth, the highest 1
in 21, 2,677 at a twentieth or more). Nine twentieths for the other sources sit in their
gap: of the 152 other sources none lies above 0.444 and below 0.50. A static held by
several groups is drawn classic only in a frame that lists none of them, up to eight
groups (four hold one crown of ANDREA2). Shatterable statics pair with any group's piece
whatever their answer; no static of the game pairs with another group's piece in the
fifteen levels. A static's piece comes from one holder, the one with the most of its
vertices (the lowest group on a tie), so the object is drawn once: 127 for the trunks (its
stand range in 124 and a ring reaching onto 124's faces, 64 triangles; 117 holds the trunk
in an intrusion piece, the carrier 121 only the floor under it), 117 for the crowns (2,048
and 2,052 triangles of its overhang, the top of the trunk with them). A triangle is the
static's whose box, grown by 64 units, holds its centroid, the nearest box's of several,
so the trunk's top goes with the crown and no triangle with two pieces; one in no box goes
with its run of welded triangles to the box that holds the most of the run - the leaf
tips. The art lying whole on a room's faces is that room's floor and is never taken. A run
that goes on past 768 units outside every box is a larger structure, and a room's statics
held by one group are pieces all or none: ANDY1's hut and ANDY2's beams keep the classic
fallback rather than half an art hut. The piece is drawn in the static's room's window, as
the classic static was, and takes her shadow, since a trunk stands on the floor she walks.
A room drawn in part that the reach lists with an empty window is not kept on the list, so
an enemy in it is not drawn: keeping it would leave out the carrier's art lying whole on
its kept faces.
