### The material 15 books in motion: a fan's shadow that turns, and flames that play
2026-09-27

**What.** A `.TRG` part of material 15 is drawn as a book of pages: its own page and the
pages after it by page number, one page per step of the time the part gives, starting
where its phase says. Every such part in the game plays, 168 part-passes in nine levels,
in the opaque pass and in the additive one alike. The five fan floors of the 13th Floor
(RICH1) show the blade shadow turning with the fan, and the monitor wall of the Security
Breach cutscene (RICHCUT2) plays its loop. The additive books - flames, smoke, candle and
gas flames, the X-ray scanner's figure and rain rings in eight levels - move, and keep the
weight they were drawn at while they stood still: their page time doubles as it. The page
follows the time of the state the frame draws, so at 60 frames a second a 0.05 second page
stands for three presents every time.

**Why.** Under a turning fan in RICH1 the shadow on the vent floor stood still, while a
reference recording supplied for this project shows it turning at the same place: a soft
four-blade shadow stepping every third frame at 60 frames a second, 0.050 seconds, 12
degrees anticlockwise seen from above per step, repeating after 1.5 seconds, with the
grille and the rivets still. The book is in the art: each fan floor is a material 15 part
with the parameters (0, 30, 0.05, 0) on page 3071, and pages 3071 to 3100 are thirty pages
of that floor with the shadow turned about 12 degrees further on each (355 degrees over
the thirty). The same scheme holds in every material 15 part of the game: `param[0]` is a
phase, a whole number below `param[1]`; `param[1]` is the page count, 14, 29 or 30;
`param[2]` is the seconds a page stands, 0.025 to 0.2; `param[3]` is 0 in all 168
part-passes. The next pages go by page number, not by texture layer: RICHCUT2 group 0 part
5 names layer 51 = page 1139, and layers 52 to 58 hold parquet, carpets and water (pages
1103, 1108, 1111, 1109, 1112, 3068 and 3006), while pages 1139 to 1168 are one clean loop
of the monitors' picture; by page number all 168 part-passes resolve, by layer that one
breaks. The renderer read `param[2]` as an additive weight and nothing else
(`MaterialAddWeight` answered material 15 with `param[2]`, as the entry "The engine's own
per-vertex lighting, as shader arithmetic" says); the number is a time, and no material 15
part ever left its own page, so the fan floors showed frame 0 for ever; the other pages
were already in the page cache, which loads every layer of the file, and nothing pointed
to them. The HD clock steps once per logic tick in thirtieths of a second and is never
interpolated: at 60 frames a second a 0.05 second page on it stands for 2, 4, 2, 4
presents, where the recording steps every 3; the time of the drawn state - the tick clock
less the part of a tick the drawn state stands behind it - steps every 3, 3, 3, and at
`fps_mode` 0 it is the tick clock itself. The file gives an additive book no weight at
all: at weight 1 the brightest fire adds 253.9 of 255 at the 95th percentile of its share
of the frame, against the church mist's 8, and a gain per picture sheet held to that
ceiling fails the small sprites (below); the page time, read as the weight all along,
draws the fires and the X-ray figure visibly and stays the weight.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_book.h` is new and holds the arithmetic alone, with no engine
header, so that the suite includes it as it includes `interpolate_math.h`: `HDBookClock`
(the drawn time, `max(0, clock - (1 - alpha) / 30)`) and `HDBookPage` (`((int)(t / step) +
phase) % count`, in double, the step read to the microsecond and a thousandth of a step
added before the truncation, so that a present landing on a page boundary shows the same
page every time and an hour of play does not drift). In `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`,
`MaterialBookTime` answers a material 15 part with its `param[2]` when `param[1]` is a
whole number from 2 to 64, `param[2]` lies in 0.02 to 0.5 seconds and `param[0]` is a
whole number below `param[1]`, and 0 for everything else; `MaterialBookSlots` resolves
pages 1 to N - 1 as `HDPageCacheSlotOf(page0 + k)` into `g_book_slots`, once per (first
page, count), and returns the index of page 1 or -1; `RunFirstPage` gives `page0`, the
page the first corner of the part's run names. A part whose numbers or pages do not all
resolve keeps its own page and is counted as dropped. In the part loop the book is
resolved in every pass; only triangles on the book's own first page carry it. `HDRange`
and `HDTri` carry `bookTime`, `bookFirst`, `bookCount` and `bookPhase`, all four in the
sort key and the merge test beside `flipSlot`, so parts with the same book, step and phase
share a draw call and parts that differ in any of them never do; `bookPart` names the
first triangle's part for the log and is not in the key. The draw takes
`HDBookPage(g_book_clock, ...)` and the page's slot out of `g_book_slots` where
`hd_motion` is on; page 0 is the range's own `pageSlot`, so `hd_motion` 0 shows page 0 and
a book costs no draw call more than a still page. `g_book_clock` is the frame's
`bookClock`: `HDFrameLighting` gains `bookClock` (`hd_render.h`), and `FillFrameLighting`
in `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp` fills it from `g_clock` and `InterpFrameAlpha()`, the factor
the frame's state was really blended at - 1 at `fps_mode` 0, on a frame drawn live, on a
camera cut and outside `DrawPhaseGame` - and the pickup and sky brackets read the same
value. The weight: `MaterialAddWeight` answers material 15 with `param[2]`, the page time,
as it did before the books turned; the note on the parameter slots says the same. The
weight goes into the sort key like every additive weight. `HDRenderBookPageOverride`
exists for the diagnostic tool alone. Log lines behind `-log` (`hd_level.cpp`): the motion
line ends in `book_parts=`, `book_pages=` (distinct pages), `book_dropped=`,
`book_additive=`, `book_step_min=`, `book_step_max=` and `book_ranges=`; one `HDLOG book
group= part= page=a..b frames= step= phase= pass= weight= dropped=` line per part and pass
after the build, where an additive book's `weight` equals its `step`; one `HDLOG bookstep
level= group= part= frame= clock= tick= alpha= present=` line for each of the first 31
page changes of the first book the level draws (`present` counts the HD frames filled in
the level); the frame line ends in `book_calls=`, the draw calls that turned a book in the
solid bracket and the glow bracket together - `g_frame_book_calls` takes the solid
bracket's count and adds the glow bracket's, as `g_frame_room_calls` does for all draw
calls, because `HDRenderFrameBegin` zeroes the renderer's counter per bracket and the
opaque books draw in the solid one. Tools: RoomProbe drives the books with `-time` and
`-nomotion` like everything else that moves, prints a `book:` total and one `book` line
per part after the build and the draw calls that turned a page after the draw, and gains
`-bookpage <n>` (every book on page n of its run); TrgProbe's `-parts` and `-mat` print
each material 15 part's run and how many of its pages the file's list holds, `-mat` from
each pass's own first page as the engine's `RunFirstPage` reads it. InterpTest includes
`hd_book.h` and gains 16 checks (`books`). With `hd_enable` 0 nothing of this runs; at
`fps_mode` 0 the books' time is the tick clock; the scrolls, the material 13 flipbooks and
the material 2 swings stay on the tick clock.

**Decisions.** Every material 15 part is a book, opaque and additive. The page comes from
the drawn frame's time, and `hd_motion` 0 shows page 0. The book is not linked to the fan
item: it is time-driven, like the classic range, which `S_AnimateTextures` steps for every
room whatever the fan does, and like the data, which gives a time and nothing else - so
the shadows under RICH1's fans 30 and 90 turn before those fans are triggered, as the
classic game's did. An additive book's weight is its page time, `param[2]`, as the
renderer read it before the books turned: the file carries no weight and no reference
exists to measure one against. A gain per picture sheet held to the church mist's ceiling
is not used, because one sheet holds fires and candles alike and the fires set it for all
of them: sheet 2101 holds JOBY5's stacked fires, the candles of ANDY2 and ANDREA3, ANDY1's
smoke column and RICH2's X-ray figure, and the gain of 0.00705 its brightest fire needs
left the candles at 0.43 and 2.0, the smoke at 0.00 and the X-ray figure at 0.72 against a
plainly visible 109 at weight 1 - the ceiling was set for room-sized haze and shafts, not
for small sprites whose own pixels are meant to be bright; a measured weight waits for a
reference picture. Parts with the same book, step and phase may share a draw call, others
never. A first build drew the additive books at a measured weight (`6995fd8`) and was
reverted (`f9a3b77`).

**Commits.** `062721d` (material 15 drawn as books), `6995fd8` (additive books at measured
weight), `f9a3b77` (reverts `6995fd8`), `2ff047c` (InterpTest steps the book), `60ef66f`
(first corrections)

### Water in the HD rooms
2026-09-06 - 2026-09-08

**What.** The mark that tells the HD mesh "this is a water surface" is flooded from the
classic mesh on **both** of the engine's water bits - a plain water room, and a
`ROOM_REFLECT` + `ROOM_REFLECT_CEILING` room - each into its own box per room and per
height, a vertex being marked only at a height and inside an extent the classic mesh
already marked. Geometry and UV ride on the marked set at the surface plane, the room's
own `minfloor`, and only on vertices whose normal is vertical; the colour term keeps the
whole mark. On that mask the HD water carries a vertical swell of `HD_WATER_SWELL` = 24
units, a UV wobble of six texels and a per-pixel caustic that modulates the multiply
without adding brightness of its own, the swell fading to nothing within one square of the
flood box's edge (`gWaterBox`, vertex register c15). Material 16 of a `.TRG` is the
still-water surface, drawn at full additive weight like every other material, its three
`param` floats read as a per-pixel ripple of the surface's texture coordinates. The
classic animated water faces a level draws keep the classic path but bind the HD painting
of the frame they are showing at that moment, read from the player's Remaster
installation. Where a level has a water surface and the `.TRG` has none, the level's
**own** face is drawn on top of the HD room by the classic path, with its own texinfo and
therefore its own animated texture range, its own light and the shimmer the classic path
has always given it; and where a room would carry both the level's own face and the
`.TRG`'s own water sheet in the same plane, the face the sheet stands on is not drawn (six
rooms: JOBY5 4, 27, 28, 83, 115, 184).

**Why.** The HD path carries the classic answer to the HD vertex at the same position, and
on a water surface the classic answers exist only at the corners of the classic quads; the
HD art remeshes a room, so a triangle whose three corners are all unmarked got weight zero
over its whole area - the busiest horizontal plane of a water room holds 1 to 15 times as
many HD vertices as the classic quad grid has corners (JOBY5 room 126: 544 against 36),
and in JOBY2's room 67 the corner rule finds 11 of 448. `ROOMLET::nWVtx` is zero in every
level of TR5, so the classic engine never displaces a water vertex either and what moves
its water is the animated texture range; the classic water term that does exist, the
WaterTable shimmer, is per vertex and on a few large quads reaches the screen as a slow
blotch, which TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931
describes in the same terms. Both bits were needed because in the Rome levels the water is
all on the second (ANDREA3 has 291 marked vertices and none on the first, ANDREA2 740 of
809), so nothing was flooded there and the surface stood still while ANDY1's animated. The
whole-room bit says yes to almost every vertex of such a room, walls and ceiling included,
so flooding it moved the walls in Rome, and the normal test costs three vertex-shader
instructions for the same reason: a wall standing at exactly the water's height inside the
pool's box answers the position test (34 of 257 marked vertices in one room, 205 of 374 in
another are not a flat surface) and would take the surface's UV wobble and caustic as a
sheared triangle on the waterline; the colour term keeps them because the classic path
asks the height and not the normal. The swell lifts a marked vertex by up to one and a
half times 24 units and the vertices at the water's own edge carry the mark like every
other, so the surface rose over the coping it should meet; it fades within one square
because a TR5 water quad is one square and anything shorter would fade inside a single
triangle and read as a crease - on a marked plane, the worst pixel then moves 111 of 255
instead of 255 while the number of pixels that move at all is unchanged. Material 16 had
been read as an additive weight and dimmed, and twelve rooms then had no visible water
surface at all (ANDREA2 231; JOBY5 2, 14, 49, 50, 52, 53, 61, 117, 139, 143, 151): it is a
surface and not a brightness - 28 parts in 6 of the 15 levels, 17 of them a double sheet
two units apart with opposite normals, standing 1 to 20 units above the classic `minfloor`
of a `ROOM_REFLECT` room, sharing no vertex with any other material, and its three numbers
scale monotonically with the area of the body of water, (0.1, 1.0, 0.035) for JOBY4's sea
of 3,538 floor squares down to (5.0, 0.1, 0.5) for a four-square puddle. Where the pool
looked like patternless blotches there was no water surface in the HD data at all: over
the game's 93 reflecting rooms the classic levels hold water faces in planes the `.TRG`
leaves empty - ANDY3 has 223 classic faces and 0 `.TRG` triangles, ANDREA1 33 and 0 - so
the HD room drew the pool floor and nothing over it. The animated faces show one tile of a
range that `S_AnimateTextures` rotates once every six game steps, and the player's HD
files hold a painting of each frame; without the binding they were the one classic surface
left in an HD room.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_level.{h,cpp}`, `specific/hd/hd_render.{h,cpp}`,
`specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl`, `specific/drawroom.cpp`. The flood takes, per room
and per height, the axis-aligned box of the marked corners and gives the surface bit to
every HD vertex of that room at that height inside that box - a box and not the whole
plane, so a walkway at the water's height on the far side of the room stays dry, and per
height, so two pools at two levels in one room stay apart; the classic answer for that bit
is itself a decision about a plane (`specific/drawroom.cpp` opens the branch with `pos.y
== CurrentRoomPtr->minfloor`). The swell, the wobble and the caustic are the water effect
of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931, re-derived here:
the WaterTable term stays untouched, and the caustic is added as a zero-mean modulation of
the multiply so that it carries no average brightness of its own. Its shape and its scale
of 0.018 per unit are TROne's own design; its amplitude, 0.32 either way, is this
project's, matched to the swing of a body of water between two frames (two reference
pictures of one pool supplied for this project differ by 8.4 of 255 on average, 17 per
cent of the pixels more than 16 apart against a mean of 34), where TROne gives its caustic
0.12. The ripple: `MaterialRipple` (`hd_render.cpp`) reads material 16's three numbers and
the per-draw-call constant `gRipple` (pixel register c36) carries them, `(0, 0, 0)` for
every other draw call in the game, where the shader's one compare on `.y` skips the whole
of it; `MaterialAddWeight` lets material 16 fall through to weight 1.0. The anchors come
from the TR5 data: `param[0]` = 0.8, the commonest value, is one wave per 1,536 units with
a floor of 0.05; `param[2]` = 0.2 is put on the classic water surface's own period of 64
steps of a 30 Hz clock (2.13 s), so 0.5 becomes 0.85 s and JOBY4's 0.035 twelve seconds;
`param[1]` = 1 moves the coordinate by a tenth of the part's own smaller UV span, 23 of
the 28 parts living in a sub-rectangle of their page with the sampler on CLAMP. The wave
is the smoothstep of a triangle, `abs(frac(p) * 2 - 1)` then `3f^2 - 2f^3`, doubled and
centred, which agrees with a cosine to within 6 per cent of its own amplitude and has the
same zero mean and continuous slope - four sines take the room pixel shader from 453 to
512 slots, exactly what shader model 3 guarantees, and four of these take it to 476. The
vertex shader does nothing for it: `sway` is 0 on 27 of the 28 parts and a bobbing sheet
would tear away from the stone rim it is let into; that structure - a texture ripple held
to the part's own UV span, nothing moving in the vertex - is TROne's own design for
material 16 (GPLv3). Which of `param[0]` and `param[2]` is the frequency and which the
rate is not decided by any measurement of this project's: it was this project's free
choice, written into `MaterialRipple` with its reversal beside it; since #212 the ripple
reads none of the three numbers (the entry "The water art's ripple from the project's own
data"). The water frames: `HDScanLevelTextures` (`specific/hd/hd_scan.cpp`) reads the
`.TEX` sidecar - a page count, that many page numbers, then one `uint16` per object
texture - written against TRForge's format description (MIT; `trf_remaster/Remaster.h` and
`HdPages.h` used as a description and not vendored). Seven of the fifteen levels have
animated water ranges, 81 frames in all, and every frame has a page; `HDWaterFrameFor`
(`hd_level.cpp`) matches by the content a texinfo holds at that moment - page and uv
corner, which the classic rotation copies whole - and two lines in `InsertRoomWater`
(`specific/drawroom.cpp`), inside the HD branch, swap the page and the four coordinates,
the face keeping its light, its shimmer, its sort, its blend and its double-sidedness.
Each frame is a 64 x 64 tile filling its cell, so its HD rectangle is the whole page.
Those pages are appended to the level's own page cache and borrowed into the classic
`Textures[]` array **above `nTextures`**, never by raising that count, because the font is
addressed as `nTextures - 2`, the sky as `- 1` and the menu pages as `- 4` and `- 5`; the
reference is given back by POINTER and not by slot number, because `FreeLevel` calls
`FreeTextures` over `0..nTextures-1` of the OLD level (`specific/texture.cpp`),
`LoadTextures` then refills for the NEW one (`specific/file.cpp`) and only then does
`HDLevelBuild` run, so a borrowed slot number belongs to the next level's pages by the
time it is released (JOBY4 has 13 pages and borrows `Textures[13..20]`, JOBY5 has 19 and
puts its own in `1..18`) - the rule rather than the exception in a randomized run, where
the randomizer's appended pages take a level from 19 to 21 up to 81 to 102; the `AddRef`'d
`IDirect3DTexture9*` is kept beside the slot and the slot cleared only while
`Textures[at].tex` is still it, and the `HDLOG` line says how many were given back and how
many slots the next level had taken over. The restored surface is the level's own art and
nothing is invented - a face qualifies on the engine's own two tests (every corner at the
room's `minfloor`, every corner marked by `aRoomVertexWaterMarks`), and whether the HD art
already covers that piece of plane is asked of a per-group table of horizontal art kept by
1024-unit **sector**, the decision then taken per room by majority, because the 24
triangles the art does hold at that height sit in two corners (the coping, not the water)
and one box around them would span the room, and half a restored pool is worse than either
whole; restoring gives 87 faces in 5 rooms of one level, 86 in 8 of 30 in another, 34 in 4
in a third, and nothing at all in the two levels whose surfaces the HD art really did
build, plus JOBY5's 72 faces in 8 rooms from the per-face rule (`HDRenderGroupWaterArt`
over a table built from the material 16 triangles alone). It costs one classic roomlet
transform per visible room that carries restored water and nothing for any other room;
with `hd_enable` off there are no restored faces at all and `InsertRoomWater` is not
reached. No page is missing: over all fifteen levels not one of 12,247,000 vertices is on
texture layer 0 and every level's `fallbackPageTris` is 0. A wave band from the HD effect
atlas was tried as an alternative and rejected - `EFFECT.DDS` rows 936..1008 and
1014..1060 are a dark modulation strip of mean luminance 24 of 255, not a surface
texture - so no page cache for named sheets was built. JOBY3's thirteen suppressed rooms
were left alone: the art covering those planes is opaque material 0, a diamond-plate deck,
and those rooms carry `ROOM_REFLECT` for wet sheen and not for a pool.
`HDRenderShoreOverride` and `HDRenderUprightOverride` exist for the diagnostic tools alone
and the engine never calls them. `docs/Engine-Manual.md` corrected along the way: JOBY3 is
`LVL5_SUBMARINE` and JOBY4 `LVL5_DEEPSEA_DIVE`, ANDREA2 is `LVL5_TRAJAN_MARKETS` and
ANDREA3 `LVL5_COLOSSEUM` (`game/gameflow.h`). Tools: `RoomProbe` (`-noshore`,
`-noupright`, `-roomplane`, `-plane`, `-watersurvey`, which prints per room how much of
the `.TRG`'s cover is the HD art's own water sheet, how many faces the room restores, the
level's water frames, their cells, HD pages and rectangles, and a simulation of the
classic rotation, `-flatart`, and the `water:` line with the water marks and the flooded
count), `TrgProbe` (`-layer0`, `-surface`, `-watergap`, `-matparts`), `DdsProbe` (`-rows`,
`-cut`), `Tr5Level` (`debugAnimTexBlock`).

**Commits.** `196849a` (flipbooks, water, statics), `05aeddc` (water on both bits),
`34dcb15` (the missing water), `7489453` (material 16 still water)

### Address space, the page cache and what the machine can pay for
2026-09-05 - 2026-09-16

**What.** The level's `.DDS` pages are BC7-decoded on the processor over a thread pool and
uploaded as A8R8G8B8 with the whole mip chain, lossless, into `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT` through
one reused system-memory staging texture; decoding runs in byte-budgeted batches, and both
Win32 configurations link `/LARGEADDRESSAWARE`. Two registry values steer the cost, both
registry-only: `hd_texture_budget_mb` (DWORD, default 0 = work the ceiling out from the
card) and `hd_texture_format` (string, default `rgba` = A8R8G8B8 lossless; `dxt5` = BC3, a
quarter of the memory). When the pages do not fit the budget the biggest pages give up
their top mip level, repeatedly if one pass is not enough and never past a page's last
level; pages themselves are never dropped. The device's own limits are asked and answered:
no `vs_3_0`/`ps_3_0`, fewer than 512 `ps_3_0` pixel-shader slots, no `UBYTE4` vertex
element or no `A8R8G8B8` texture put the session on the classic path with one line in the
log; no `DXT5` while `dxt5` is asked for falls quietly back to `rgba`; a
`MaxTextureWidth/Height` below a page starts that page far enough down to fit;
`CreateTexture` running out of video memory mid-level puts the whole level back to
classic, naming the page, and the same rule covers the models. A page that cannot be found
anywhere is white, the cache making four white texels itself. How many changes of outfit a
level still allows is worked out from the machine rather than from a constant: the card's
own texture budget, the free address space less a reserve, and whether one page still fits
in a single free block, with the old flat allowance of 64 MiB kept as the floor of the
card condition so the rule is never stricter than it was.

**Why.** The engine is a 32-bit process. For TITLE's 220 pages the peak commit is 270 MiB
in `DEFAULT` against 545 MiB in `MANAGED`, and the batches are counted in bytes and not in
pages because 2391 of the 2406 pages are 512x512 and decode to 1.4 MiB while eleven are
4096x2048 and decode to 42.7 MiB each (`TrgProbe -ddssizes`) - a batch counted in pages
would occasionally ask for most of a gigabyte. A missing page is a hole in a wall and
reads as a rendering fault, while a page that starts one mip level down is only a softer
wall, the texture coordinates being 0..1 of whatever the texture turns out to be. The cost
sort is stable because almost every comparison is a tie and an unstable sort would pick a
different set each run and make two pictures of the same wall disagree. The decision is
taken from the DDS headers because an estimate is not a thing to promise a card: the
earlier estimate of four times the file length is now exact to the mebibyte (TITLE plans
375.8 MiB and loads 375.8 MiB). The white page needed its own texels because
`TEX\WHITE.DDS` exists in `4\TEX` only, so an installation without the fourth game had no
white tile and the wall was not white but gone. 32-bit indices cannot be worked around for
the large levels: a `.TRG` numbers its vertices over the whole level rather than room by
room, so the widest single triangle reaches over 235,507 vertices in JOBY4 and 1,391,696
in RICH2, only RICHCUT2 (33,585) being under 65536, and the floor under any cut is one
triangle, which cannot be cut. The outfit rule: the page cache never gives a page back
inside a level - other models hold slot indexes - so every outfit worn in one level stays
in it, and that growth was capped at `HD_REDRESS_ALLOWANCE`, 64 MiB, which is the slack
the automatic budget already holds back on the card and was never a measurement of the
player's machine. The wall is not the address space: measured pool by pool, a 4096-side
A8R8G8B8 page in `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT` takes 0.04 MiB out of the address space and puts 85.25
MiB on the card, where the budget is already watching it, while the same page managed or
in system memory costs the process its own 85.37 MiB. The address space is still asked for
one reason: a `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT` texture cannot be locked, so every mip goes through one
reused `D3DPOOL_SYSTEMMEM` staging texture of the page's whole size - a single block of
85.34 MiB, which a process holding its free memory in crumbs cannot make.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_pagecache.cpp`/`.h` is the cache, with the cost sort, the mip
drop and `ensure_staging`; `specific/bc7.cpp`/`.h` gained `BC7DecodeDDSMip`,
`BC7DDSMipCount` (so a page can be decoded at any level of its chain, `BC7DecodeDDS` being
that call with mip 0 and unchanged in behaviour) and `BC7DDSShape`, which reads the
148-byte DDS header before a block is decoded. The automatic budget: `DXCreateD3DDevice`
(`specific/dxshell.cpp`/`.h`) asks `GetAvailableTextureMem()` one instruction after the
device exists, the only moment the answer means what it says, and
`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp` takes off the back and depth buffers from the present
parameters, `nTextures` classic pages of `App.TextureSize` squared (measured 7 to 96
pages, 1.8 to 24.0 MiB), this level's HD vertex and index buffers, and 64 MiB of slack for
the driver; the floor is 16 MiB. Over all fifteen levels the pages come to 190.6 MiB
(JOBY4) up to 423.9 MiB (ANDREA2), rooms, models and Lara adding without overlap since a
page number the rooms use and one a model uses are different name spaces in the HD art;
the title screen's reserve is 155 MiB against 397 MiB of pages, so any card offering 552
MiB loads it whole, and ANDREA2, the heaviest, needs 595 MiB.
`specific/hd/hd_dxt5.cpp`/`.h` is a BC3 encoder of about 150 lines written here - the
bounding box of each 4x4 block pulled in by a sixteenth at each end, endpoints quantised
to RGB565, indices chosen as the nearest of the four palette entries in the colour the
card will produce with the classic 2:4:1 weighting, alpha always in the eight-value mode -
and uses no `d3dx`, so the port still depends on `d3d9.dll` and nothing else; it carries
its own decoder for `RoomProbe -psnr`, which measures 40.28 dB mean and 35.41 dB worst
over sixteen pages of ANDREA1 while taking them from 279.9 to 70.0 MiB, at 1.46 s of
compression on eight cores and a peak process memory of 136 instead of 270 MiB. The 16-bit
index path is built and runs: a draw call is one range and a range is given 16-bit indices
rebased on its own lowest vertex with the stream moved there by `SetStreamSource`'s byte
offset; RICHCUT2 uses it today and its picture is byte-identical to the 32-bit one, so a
card without 32-bit indices draws RICHCUT2 in HD and every other level classic, with the
number in the log. The level change holds one level and not two: `HDLevelBuild` releases
the previous level's objects, buffers and pages at its top, and `HDLevelUnload` makes no
Direct3D call at all; `RoomProbe -seq TITLE,ANDREA2,TITLE` shows free texture memory
returning to its starting value after every level. The out-of-memory path is in
`HDRenderLevelBegin` (`hd_render.cpp`/`.h`) and `HDModelLevelBegin` (`hd_model.cpp`), the
settings in `tomb5/tomb5.cpp`/`.h` and `global/types.h`. The outfit rule is
`specific/hd/hd_memory.cpp`/`.h`, pure, with every input handed in (`HDRedressDecide`):
`spent = cache - this level's mark`; `card room = budget + HD_REDRESS_ALLOWANCE - cache`;
`addr room = ullAvailVirtual - HD_REDRESS_ADDRESS_RESERVE`; `allowed = (card room >= worst
|| spent < allowance) && addr room >= worst && largest free block >= one page`.
`HD_REDRESS_WORST` is 20.00 MiB, the measured cost of the dearest outfit's own pages over
a whole wardrobe - a measured worst case rather than the chosen outfit's exact bytes,
because the hint under the F4 list is drawn for the HIGHLIGHTED row on every frame and an
exact answer would mean reading that outfit's `.TRM` parts per row per frame against a
model build that costs 278 ms with nine mods. `HD_REDRESS_ADDRESS_RESERVE` is 512 MiB -
what a level load, a Bink film, the save screenshot and the driver's transients have to
find after a change has taken its share; it is not measured and is printed in every level
build line so that a log can settle it. If `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` refuses, the address
walk is not made and `allowed` is `spent < 64 MiB`, the old rule exactly, with a line of
its own. On a machine whose level reports a budget of 3878 MiB and a cache of 465 MiB the
rule gives room for 124 changes where the flat allowance refused the sixth; too generous a
card side costs mip levels and not a texture, and at the floor the pages are loaded anyway
rather than leaving holes. The answer is worked out where something changes it - at the
end of the level build, before and after every change, and once as the F4 window opens -
and `HDLevelRedressAllowed` hands out what was stored, because the answer stands on a
`GlobalMemoryStatusEx` and a walk of the whole address space (203 microseconds over 262
regions) while the F4 window asks on every drawn frame; the only callers of
`HDPageCacheAppend` are the level build and `HDObjectLevelBuild`. Everything new sits
inside `HDEnabled()`, nothing of it is on a drawn frame's path and nothing of it is in the
60 fps files; the two literal `false` pool arguments in `hd_level.cpp` became one named
`kPagesManaged` of the same value so that the `pool=` the log prints is the pool the calls
really use. Two places where a pointer meets a signed comparison were settled with the
compiler rather than by argument: in `game/savegame.cpp` the guard `if (creature->enemy
< 0) creature->enemy = 0;` was removed, with the reason written where it stood - MSVC
compiles the comparison of an `ITEM_INFO*` with the null pointer constant as an unsigned
comparison, so it is false for every address there is, `0x90000000` included, the cast the
original C had was lost in the decompilation, and the save writes `enemy - malloc_buffer`,
so a null enemy already comes back as 0, while "repairing" it to `(long)creature->enemy <
0` would be true for every address above 2 GB and would blank every enemy pointer in a
reloaded save; in `specific/alexstuff.cpp`, `(long)pR->door & 1` is a check that a
`short*` is not odd, `& 1` reads bit 0 whatever the sign and on Win32 a `long` is exactly
as wide as a pointer, so it is left as it is. A sweep of every `(long)`/`(ulong)` cast in
the engine found no other one whose operand is an address and whose result meets a
comparison, a division or a shift - `specific/file.cpp`'s `(long)meshes[lp] / 2` divides a
file offset the loader has just read. Seams behind `-log`: the level build line carries
`pool=`, `avail_virtual=`, `largest_free=`, `reserve=` and `walk_ms=`, a `redress room`
line says what is allowed and what refuses it, the per-change line carries `avail_virtual
%.0f -> %.0f MiB (-%.1f for +%.1f MiB of pages)`, a `redress deferred` line names the
condition that refused, one line covers a refused `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`, and the stats
carry `droppedMip0` and `droppedLevels`. Tools: `RoomProbe` gained `-budget <MiB>`,
`-format rgba|dxt5`, `-psnr`, `-caps maxtex <n>`, `-caps noidx32`, `-seq <A,B,C>` and
`-vramhog` (the two `-caps` switches bending the caps `HDRenderInit` read through
`HDRenderCapOverride`, which the engine never calls and for which there is no registry
value), `ModelProbe` gained `-withrooms <LEVEL>`, and
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/PoolProbe.cpp` is new - `-pool` makes real pages of the
cache's own shapes in all three pools and measures what each takes out of the address
space, the card and the process's commit, `-walk` walks the address space, `-grid` calls
`HDRedressDecide` itself so that the tables it prints are the rule and not a description
of it; it is built x86 and `/LARGEADDRESSAWARE` like the engine, without which the same
process reads 1995 MiB of free address space instead of 3986. `tomb5.vcxproj` sets
`LargeAddressAware` on both Win32 configurations.

**Commits.** `ec20d77` (loaders, discovery, binding), `2435068` (room renderer, page
cache), `3f4afea` (texture budget, missing pages), `7ffb871` (walk capacity, reach
budget), `0b23074` (outfit changer asks both), `eadc929` (PoolProbe measures the pools),
`de89861` (record and README limit), `572eccc` (record on the card side)

### HD loading screens from the Remaster, when they are there
2026-09-04 - 2026-09-04

**What.** Chronicles keeps its 21 loading pictures in `screens\SCREENS.STR`: raw 640x480
A1R5G5B5, 614400 bytes each, no header, picture n at offset n * 614400. The player's
Remaster installation holds the same pictures redrawn at 1920x1080 as BC7 `.DDS`, one per
level and named after the level; if the player copies those into `screens\HD\`, the engine
uses them, and if the folder is not there nothing changes. None of the pictures ship - the
release carries the empty `screens\HD` folder with a note saying where the Remaster keeps
them (`5\PIX\HD`). The 640x480 pictures are stretched onto the window and always were,
distortion included; the HD ones are 16:9 and are fitted instead, so on a 16:9 window they
land pixel for pixel and on anything else they get black bars rather than a squeeze. The
Security Breach cutscene borrows Red Alert's picture.

**Why.** The pictures are the player's own data from an installation the player already
owns, and the path costs nothing when they are absent. Direct3D 9 predates BC7 by about a
decade and cannot sample it, so the blocks have to be unpacked on the CPU. The bars are
painted with a `Clear`, since nothing clears the frame before a loading screen goes down.
`S_DrawTile` needed a filter argument because point sampling is right for a 640x480
picture blown up to the window and wrong for one already at the window's resolution.

**How.** `specific/bc7.cpp`, `specific/bc7.h`, `specific/hdscreen.cpp`,
`specific/hdscreen.h`, all new; call sites in `specific/file.cpp` and
`specific/LoadSave.cpp`. `bc7.cpp` unpacks the blocks to plain 32 bit pixels and is
written here against the published format definition - no third-party code was taken in,
and `THIRD-PARTY.md` therefore gained no entry for it. Its partition and anchor tables
check each other at run time in `BC7SelfTest`: every partition must start in subset 0,
must really use all of its subsets, and the anchor listed for subset n must be a pixel
that partition actually assigns to subset n; the engine refuses the HD path outright if
that check fails. `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/DdsProbe.cpp` compiles the same `bc7.cpp`
and writes a `.PNG`, so the decoder is provable without starting the game. The pixels go
into one square power-of-two `A8R8G8B8` texture, 2048 for a 1920x1080 picture, with the
picture in the top left corner: the engine counts texture coordinates in 256ths, and 1920
and 1080 out of 2048 come out as exactly 240 and 135, so the addressing stays lossless.
Which picture belongs to which level is the original code's own answer:
`S_LoadLevelFile(num)` gets `num` from `DoLevel(gf[3], ...)`, and `gf[3]` is the file name
index out of `CMD_LEVEL`, not the slot; the randomizer permutes only the script offset
table, never the file name table nor the indices pointing into it, so `num` is the level's
identity in a vanilla and in a shuffled campaign alike and `num + 2` is the correct
picture in both. The HD file name is taken from the same place,
`gfFilenameWad[gfFilenameOffset[num]]`; a comment in `file.cpp` records that changing this
to `gfIdFromSlot[num]` would look like a repair and would in fact index a slot table with
an identity. The loader writes `HD screen: ...` lines to the log for every file it
refuses, cannot read or decodes.

**Commits.** `84a192f` (HD loading screens), `af919a9` (cutscene borrows Red Alert's),
`fe143fe` (the empty `screens\HD` folder), `b168bbe` (the note names `5\PIX\HD`)

### The logo screen and the title menu wordmark
2026-09-04 - 2026-09-04

**What.** Picture 0, the game's logo screen, is the one picture the engine builds rather
than loads, and the only one that picks its HD file by `Gameflow->Language`: `LOGO_DE`,
`LOGO_FR`, `LOGO_US`, and `LOGO_EU` for English and for every language the HD files carry
no logo for. Those four files carry an alpha channel and are composed over black. The
wordmark is cut out of the `LOGO_` file and blended over `TITLE.DDS` at load time,
horizontally centred with the top edge of the lettering one seventy-second of the picture
height down; whichever of the two files is missing simply drops out, so a half-filled
`screens\HD\` still works. The title menu draws the same wordmark: with
`screens\HD\LOGO_<language>.DDS` present the mark out of that file replaces Core's
`data\logo512.pak`, and German, French and the US emblem then appear in the menu at all.
One always-on change goes with it: American English no longer loads `data\uslogo.pak`,
that branch is deleted, and a US player gets `logo512.pak` like everybody else - this
happens with `hd_enable=0` and with no `screens\HD\` folder, so it is a change a US player
sees.

**Why.** The HD files read from the player's Remaster installation hold the wordmark alone
on a transparent frame and the title picture without any lettering, so the two only ever
appear one after the other and the screen has to be composed to exist. Core's menu logo is
512x256 of 24 bit colour with magenta standing in for transparent, cut into two 256x256
pages and drawn as two quads filling a rectangle 2:1 wide; the language logos `grlogo.pak`
and `frlogo.pak` only ever existed on the respective CDs, so in an installation without
those CDs German and French fall back to the English one. The installed data's
`uslogo.pak` - and the unused `uklogo.pak` beside it - carry Tomb Raider IV's "The Last
Revelation" wordmark on opaque black, a leftover like `JAPAN.DAT`, and because the colour
key is magenta that black stayed as a box behind the wrong game's name.

**How.** `HDScreenComposeLogo` in `specific/hdscreen.cpp` and `LoadScreenHDLogo` in
`specific/LoadSave.cpp` for the loading screen; `LoadTitleLogoHD` and `SuperShowLogo` in
`specific/specificfx.cpp` with `HDScreenLogoSize` and `HDScreenCutLogo` in
`specific/hdscreen.cpp` for the menu; call sites and the deleted US branch in
`specific/file.cpp` (`file.cpp:681-685` carries the reason in a comment). Two bounding
boxes are involved and they are not the same: what has to be drawn is every pixel with any
alpha at all, because the lettering sits in a soft black halo reaching about 20 pixels
past it on every side, but what has to be placed is only the lettering, alpha above 128.
The blend premultiplies before it interpolates - the files store straight alpha, so
interpolating the colour would drag the black of the transparent pixels into the letter
edges and leave a seam. For the menu the mark is cut with that same alpha box, resampled
with the same premultiplied bilinear tap and put into one texture page, at most 1024x512
and a power of two, with its alpha intact; the page is addressed with texture coordinates,
so the unused part is never drawn. The menu then draws one quad instead of two, into
exactly the rectangle the pak logo filled, scaled to fit without distortion and hugging
the top edge - the three wordmarks are far wider than 2:1 and come out as a band across
the upper part of that rectangle, the US emblem is nearly 2:1 and fills it. The draw type
is the pak logo's own, `specific/polyinsert.cpp` case 1: alpha blending on,
`SRCALPHA`/`INVSRCALPHA`, alpha test against 0, which the pak logo only ever exercised at
alpha 0 or 255 but which blends the HD mark's soft edges properly. The new page takes the
place of the pak logo's left half rather than being added to the array, because every page
in the title level is addressed as a distance from the end of `Textures[]` - the font is
`nTextures-2`, the sky `nTextures-1`, the logo `nTextures-5` and `-4` - so the count has
to stay what it was. The pak is still decoded first and stays the fallback, which is why a
missing, unreadable or empty HD file costs nothing. `DdsProbe -logo <title> <logo>
<out.png>` compiles the same `hdscreen.cpp` with `HDSCREEN_NO_ENGINE` (which is why that
one file is built without the precompiled header) and writes the finished screen as a PNG,
reporting the boxes it used; `DdsProbe -crop <logo.dds> <out.png>` builds the same texture
page and writes it over a checkerboard.

**Commits.** `34a101c` (title screen composed at load), `8f31ed7` (US loads no TR4 logo),
`fedc08b` (menu draws the HD wordmark)

### HD models for items, enemies and machinery
2026-09-05 - 2026-09-25

**What.** With the HD runtime on, an item is drawn from the Remaster's own model instead
of its classic meshes: one `.TRM` per slot out of `<game>\ITEM`, skinned on the card and
drawn at every node the model covers. A registry value `hd_objects` (DWORD, default `1`,
same key as the other settings, no options row) switches it off; with `hd_enable` off it
is never entered. An HD object never switches to its MIP slot. `item->mesh_bits` is
honoured per node; `item->meshswap_meshbits` is not, because a `.TRM` is one whole model
with no second geometry for a node (counted per level as `swap_ignored`), with two
exceptions that ship their own models: the Mafia man drawing the pistols
(`MAFIA2_SWAP.TRM` for the torso swap 0x80) and the cyborg's opening panels (the eleven
`HITMAN_<n+1>.TRM` files 5,6,7,8,11,12,13,14,15,16,20 answering panel nodes
4,5,6,7,10,11,12,13,14,15,19 as cumulative bodies, the file chosen by the panel opened
last out of `item_flags[0]` and `hitman_nodes`). The level's own `<LEVEL>.MAP` is in hand
while the models are bound, so a slot gets the model the map names for it before any name
rule applies. Cutscene actors are drawn HD as well, all but actor 1 with the see-through
fade; a cutscene body whose name carries no part of the person's gets its face from a
table keyed on the model, and no `_MIP` prop gets a face. The model and page search covers
games 1 to 5, never game 6. ANDREA1 draws 50 of its 52 models in HD, JOBY3 65 of 66 and
RICH3 65 of 68; what stays classic is Lara's composite (slots 0-30), a slot with no model,
a model that fails the fit tests, and the fourteen objects whose draw routine is not
`DrawAnimatingItem` (scaled spikes, the three lasers, darts, lift doors, portal door, gas
cloud, flare in flight, thrown weapon). Every HD item is drawn against the whole screen,
not against its room's portal window.

**Why.** The install ships no repainted classic tiles for an object, only a model of its
own in the ITEM folder, so HD art for objects can only come from those models. The
randomizer puts foreign creatures into slots, so a model must be proved to fit the
skeleton it is hung on, or a body is torn across the room. The light is per vertex because
the classic path is per vertex (`aTransformLightClipMesh` runs the light formula with each
vertex's own normal); one flat colour per node would light a chest's front and back alike.
The matrices are taken from the engine rather than rebuilt so that animation, frame
interpolation and mesh-tree flags stay the game's own. Without the map in hand, binding
fell through to the slot's own name: ANDREA1 bound 46 models where its files hold 55, 18
of them out of game 4, and `ANIMATING10` asked for a file in no ITEM folder while the map
names `ANIMATING10_ANDREA1`. A `<NAME>_HEAD.TRM` is not a face alone: over the twelve head
files of game 5, `PIERRE_HEAD.TRM` reaches 165 units below its head joint and carries
head, neck and a piece of collar, and in seven of the eight files that use both base bones
the small bone reaches below the big one and is the neck. `DrawCutSeqActors` plays actors
back with its own frame buffer and its own light, so the object seam never saw them and
every actor but Lara kept the 1999 mesh. A cutscene body is named after the level slot it
fills (`ANIMATING4_RICHCUT2`) while its face keeps the person's name, so only three of
game 5's twelve faces were reachable by name and many actors stood without heads; of the
44 cutscenes of `DATA\cutseq.bin` (133 actors on 98 level slots), six bodies had a face
file that no rule reached, and the rule that strips a qualifier hung a face that was not
theirs on eight props. Game 6 is Angel of Darkness, a different engine with different
objects, so a name matched there would be a wrong model rather than a missing one. The
classic path hands every item the whole screen (`PrintObjects` sets
`phd_left`/`phd_top`/`phd_right`/`phd_bottom` to the frame around its item loop), so
clipping HD items to their room's window was a rule the engine has not got: an enemy in a
neighbouring room was cut to the doorway rectangle, and one whose window came out small
was not drawn at all.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_trm.cpp`/`.h` reads the format, written against TRForge's
measurement (MIT, `ItemModels.h`) and re-measured over the 566 models of game 5: a 24-byte
vertex of three position floats, a byte normal biased by 127, a 1-based texture layer,
three bone indices and three weights summing to 255, the two texture coordinates in the
fourth byte of each triple; a model's triangles never span two pages, a part's three
passes are contiguous, and the highest bone index a weighted vertex names is 28, which
allows a joint palette of 32. A `.TRM` bone index is the slot's classic mesh-tree node, so
`specific/hd/hd_model.cpp`/`.h` computes only a coverage list per slot; at a node the
model does not cover nothing is drawn, neither the model nor the classic mesh (in most
door slots that is node 0, the invisible root). The bind offset is folded into the node
matrix on the processor (`t' = t - bind * R`), the bind pose being the mesh tree's
accumulated offsets with every rotation left out. `hd_shader/hd_model.hlsl`
(`vs_3_0`/`ps_3_0`, generated to `hd_model_vs.inc`/`hd_model_ps.inc`) takes the disk
vertex unchanged through a `FLOAT3` + `UBYTE4` + `UBYTE4` + `UBYTE4N` declaration; 32
joints of three registers at `c8`, the projection at `c0`, the light list at `c136`-`c159`
with count and sun factor at `c160`; the pixel half shares `gPass` `c4`, `gFog` `c16`,
`gCounts` `c17` and `gBulbs` `c40` with the room shader, and an object writes `c17.x = 0`
so the room shader's per-pixel light loop does not light it twice, while `gPass.y` carries
the additive ceiling. `gPass` is written through `SetPixelShaderConstantF` only, because
`fxc` puts two `def` constants of its own at `c4` and `c5` in the vertex half. The seam is
five places in `DrawAnimatingItem` (`game/draw.cpp`): `HDObjectBegin` after `phd_RotYXZ`,
the MIP branch guarded, node 0 and the node loop in both the plain and the interpolated
branch, and `HDObjectEnd` outside `if (clip)`; the interpolated branch records the matrix
`phd_PutPolygons_I` would have drawn with. `specific/hd/hd_object.cpp`/`.h` is the
engine-facing half; `HDMapLoadForLevel` loads the map in `HDObjectLevelBuild` and
`HDObjectLevelEnd` frees it (`specific/hd/hd_bind.cpp`). Two fit tests per slot at level
build: a weighted vertex naming a node the slot does not have refuses the model outright
(`FIREROPE` fails this in eleven of the fourteen levels), and for a model with the right
node count the bind drift is measured pairwise - the distance between two nodes' vertex
centres in the model against the distance between their bind positions in the mesh tree,
each mesh's own RMS size subtracted - with a limit of **256**, set inside the measured gap
between the worst model that belongs where it stands (239) and the best that does not
(308); a one-node model has no pair and is never refused. Triangles are sorted by `(page,
node)`, every range carrying the node that holds most weight over its three corners, and
consecutive visible ranges of the same page are merged at draw time, so at `mesh_bits`
`-1` the draw-call count is unchanged (`SWAT` builds 16 ranges and draws 2). Light: suns,
points and spots go to the vertex shader in view space, one list for every node because a
node matrix is a rotation without scale; ambient is per object, a point light's direction
and falloff are worked out per surface point, and the activity flags, the eight-frame
fades and range culling stay the engine's own in `CreateLightList` inside
`CalculateObjectLighting`. HD objects are drawn in `HDFrameDraw` after the rooms and
before `DrawBuckets`, inside the bracket the rooms opened, sharing an exact depth buffer.
Shared pieces: `HDPageCacheAppend` (`hd_pagecache.cpp`/`.h`) so models and rooms keep one
texture per page, and `HDRenderStateSave`/`HDRenderStateRestore` (`hd_render.cpp`/`.h`).
`aW2VMx` in `specific/3dmath.cpp`/`.h` was un-`static`ed: the float twin of `w2v_matrix`
puts a light's world position into view space. Item pages keep the room path's rule, the
alpha test in the alpha pass only (the design of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931), because an item page's alpha is not a coverage mask
(`ROMAN_GOD_ANDREA_SWORD`'s three body pages have 64.1, 48.7 and 56.4 per cent of texels
below alpha 128, PIERRE and BLUE_GUARD share a page at 26.2); the number is kept as a
measurement in `HDPageCacheSlotCutoutPermille`. `HDFrameScissorForRoom` (`hd_level.cpp`)
gives an item the full frame and counts what the room window would have cut
(`items_spared=` on the `HDLOG clip` line); a view serial (`ViewSerial`, stepped once per
`phd_LookAt`, `specific/3dmath.cpp`/`.h`) is written beside every room matrix and every
collected object and reported as `view=`/`view_obj=`, a counter nothing branches on.
Binding by name goes through the hand table in `specific/hd/hd_bind.cpp`, which resolves
the randomizer's own slots (`CYBORG` 469 to `HITMAN`, `BLUE_GUARD2` 460 to
`BLUE_GUARD_JOBY`), carries `ROMAN_GOD` -> `ROMAN_GOD_ANDREA_SWORD` (consulted only when
the level's `.MAP` is silent: there is no `ROMAN_GOD.TRM`, and of the fifteen `.MAP` files
only ANDREA2 and ANDREA3 name the slot), and names `VULTURE_CHUNNEL` for slot 43, because
the randomizer's vulture comes from THE LOST ARTIFACT's `chunnel.TR2` and the I-III
Remaster ships `VULTURE.TRM` and `VULTURE_CHUNNEL.TRM` side by side. Mesh-swap sources are
read from `game/setup.cpp` (`MeshSwapSource`) and the run-time bits set in
`game/init.cpp`, `game/hitman.cpp`, `game/mafia2.cpp`, `game/romangod.cpp`, `game/sas.cpp`
and `game/imp.cpp`; the swap models are ordinary models on pseudo slots, and
`hitman_nodes` moved from a `static` in `game/hitman.cpp` into `game/hitman.h`. Faces: a
head file's neck bone hangs off the head node's PARENT with the file's own weights kept,
so the seam blends rather than tears; `bind_pose_of` returns the classic mesh tree beside
the bind pose. `find_head_model` (`hd_model.cpp`) has a STRIP rule that cuts the last
`_<QUALIFIER>` off and asks again, and `ends_in_mip` stops it at a stem that ends in
`_MIP`: over the 1,335 model names of the 4 and 5 folders, every one of the ten names that
reached a face through a `_MIP` reached one not theirs (the eight props `LARSON_MIP_ANDY1`
and `PIERRE_MIP_ANDY1`, planks in cutscene 14, `BLUE_GUARD_MIP_ANDY1`, a stone block with
a chain, `BLUE_GUARD_MIP_JOBY4`, a pillar, `LARSON_MIP_RICH1`, an ID card,
`LARSON_MIP_ANDY3`, the hussar, whose own face Larson's covered, `PIERRE_MIP_ANDY3`, a
horse, and `LARSON_MIP_JOBY3_JOBY5`, a rack of torpedoes, and game 4's
`JEAN_YVES_MIP_ANG_RACE` and `TROOPS_MIP_ANG_RACE`), and it now answers for seven names,
all right. The table `g_head_of_model` (`hd_model.cpp`) binds the bodies whose names carry
no part of the person's; each line carries a node (-1 measures it) and `halfTurnX`, and
`find_head_model` hands the line back: `ANIMATING4_RICHCUT2` -> `VON_CROY_SENIOR_HEAD`
(7.4 units apart by neck-ring measurement, next nearest face 11.4, sharing texture page
9075); `ANIMATING6_RICHCUT2` -> `VON_CROY_ELDER_HEAD` (2.7 against 35.3); `PATRICK_1`, the
priest (ANDY1's `SAILOR_MIP`, cutscene 19) -> `PATRICK_BROWN_HEAD`; `PATRICK_2`, the
priest (ANDY2's and ANDY3's `SAILOR_MIP`, 33, 35, 37, 38 and 44) -> `PATRICK_WHITE_HEAD`;
`ANIMATING6_MIP_JOBY2`, the admiral (JOBY2 25, and as `CRANE_GUY_MIP` in JOBY3 and JOBY5,
12, 13, 15 and 18) -> `ADMIRAL_HEAD`; `ANIMATING9_MIP_JOBY2`, Sergie (JOBY2 25, and as
`LION_MIP` 15 and 32) -> `SERGIE_HEAD` on node 3, which the body leaves empty;
`SNIPER_MIP_ANDY1`, the hanged man (21) -> `HANGMAN_HEAD` on node 21, turned half a turn
about the node's x axis; `SWAT_MIP_ANDY3`, the demon knight (37 and 44) -> `DEMON_HEAD`. A
face is never given a face of its own. Every binding rests on the engine's own sources and
the installation's data: `handle_actor_chatting` in `game/deltapak.cpp` names the slot and
the node each person speaks on (the priests and the admiral node 2, Sergie node 3, the
hanged man node 21, the knight node 15), the face's spoken-line files are named after the
audio track of the cutscenes that play them (`PATRICK_BROWN_HEAD_119.TRL` is cutscene 19's
track), and body and face share texture pages (9090 and 9091 the admiral, 9093 Sergie,
9107 the hanged man; the hussar beside the knight carries the demon's face on
`DEMON_HEAD`'s pages 9113 and 9114). The face rides on the speech table's node, not the
nearest node (for the hanged man that would be node 2, 40.4 units from the face's centre
against 44.6 for node 21). The hanged man's file stands upside down against the level's
own head mesh of node 21: its vertices lie 37.4 units from that mesh on average as they
stand and 7.6 turned half a turn about the node's x axis, the best of every turn in
30-degree steps about all three axes, where the other faces lie best as they stand; the
face pass turns it before the neck is looked for (y and z mirrored about the node's bind,
each normal byte 254 minus itself, so every triangle keeps its winding), and the face note
ends in `, turned half a turn about x`. `DrawCutSeqActors` (`game/deltapak.cpp`) hands the
node walk's MATRIX to the HD path with `duff_item` carrying slot number and mesh bits, and
draws a `_MIP` slot in HD like any other actor. The speech-head mesh swap is ignored over
an HD body (`HDObjectBegin` counts it); the actors drawn classic (`SWAT_PLUS_MIP`,
`DOG_MIP`, `GLADIATOR_MIP`, `CROW_MIP`, `LARSON_MIP` in RICH2, and `CHEF_MIP_RICH1`,
refused for drift) keep their classic head and its swap. With `hd_enable` off no cutscene
actor is drawn HD: `HDObjectBegin` returns false before anything. Seams with `-log`: per
slot one line with its reason (`baked`, `model_missing`, `skeleton_nodes`,
`skeleton_drift`, `no_geometry`), per level `hd=`/`classic=`/`baked=`, one `HDLOG cutseq
actor=` line per actor per cutscene, and on the first HD object of every level `HDLOG
itemcheck …` (each node's origin on the screen through the classic transform and through
the projection the card is handed, worst disagreement in pixels) and `HDLOG lightcheck …`
(the classic light formula and the HD one on the same normal).
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp` (built with `bmodel.bat`; `bshader.bat` builds
the model shader) links the engine's own sources and draws the same picture without the
game (`-nodes`, `-meshbits`, `-all`); `ModelProbe -all` over the fifteen levels, built
from `dc44597` and with the face table, differs in 19 of 1,820 bound slots, eleven gaining
a face and eight losing one. Files: `specific/hd/hd_trm.*`, `hd_model.*`, `hd_object.*`,
`hd_pagecache.*`, `hd_render.*`, `hd_level.*`, `hd_bind.*`, `hd_shader/hd_model.hlsl` and
its two `.inc`, `game/draw.cpp`, `game/deltapak.cpp`, `game/hitman.*`, `game/setup.cpp`,
`game/init.cpp`, `game/mafia2.cpp`, `game/romangod.cpp`, `game/sas.cpp`, `game/imp.cpp`,
`global/types.h`, `specific/3dmath.*`, `specific/output.cpp`, `tomb5/tomb5.cpp`,
`tomb5.vcxproj`, `docs/Engine-Manual.md`.

**Decisions.** Not bound, on purpose: `DEMON_HEAD` on `LARSON_MIP_ANDY3`, whose shared
pages are that body\'s own face; `ADMIRAL_HEAD` on any body but its own, although 55.8 per
cent of its neck vertices lie within 10 units of `PATRICK_2`'s collar against 42.5 on its
own body; the two priests' faces the other way round; `ZIP_HEAD`, which no cutscene body
speaks with; and every game 4 face on a game 5 body.
