### The cutscene faces speak: their lips follow the Remaster's track files
2026-09-25 - 2026-09-26

**What.** In HD the faces of the cutscene actors, and Lara's face in the cutscenes she
acts in, move as the installation's own track files move them: the lips part on the spoken
line, the jaw drops, the dark of the mouth and the teeth show, the mouth closes between
phrases, and now and then the eyes blink. The animation is the installation's own. A face
`<FACE>_HEAD.TRM` has one file per spoken line, `<FACE>_HEAD_<track>.TRL` in `5\ITEM`,
where `<track>` is the audio track the cutscene plays: 45 files for 13 faces, 18 of them
Lara's. Past the end of a file the face eases back to rest over ten frames. Between her
lines Lara's face plays the loop of its own block and bares its teeth while she fires (see
*Lara's face between her lines: the blink loop and the firing face*). One set of track
files serves every spoken language. A classic actor keeps its classic speech swap, the
speech-head swap over an HD body stays ignored, first person draws no face, and a face
outside a cutscene gets no track. With `hd_enable` off nothing of this runs: no level is
built, `HDObjectBegin` returns false so `DrawCutSeqActors` never calls `HDObjectLips`, and
Lara's plan and draw return before anything.

**Why.** The faces stood still while the voices played: the separate faces were bound (see
*HD models for items, enemies and machinery*), and nothing read their track files. A track
file moves a face's own joints, and which joint each of its matrix columns moves is
written in the face's `.TRM`: between the rig and the geometry every rigged head carries a
block with a header, `[N][id[N]][parent[N]][C][column[C]][frames]`, and frames of joint
matrices whose frame 0 is the pose the face was bound in. The header parses exactly in all
23 rigged `*_HEAD.TRM` of the IV-VI install's games 4 and 5. Column c drives rig joint
`column[c]` where that is below the rig's joint count and is a helper node otherwise, and
each matrix is local to its parent's. That header is the map, with no threshold and no
vote: a map voted from bind translations puts 12 of its 21 matches on helper columns that
stand where a joint stands and drives none of the 16 turning lip and mouth columns and not
the chin, so the jaw drops and the lips stay shut.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_trm.cpp` keeps the rig's inverse bind matrices, the block's
parents and columns and its frame 0 (`keep_block`; only when header and frames end exactly
where the geometry begins) and every vertex's own bones and weights, because `rig_neck_of`
renames a rigid face's body joints before it builds; the layout stands at
`HDTrmModel::rigBind` (`hd_trm.h`). `specific/hd/hd_trl.cpp` (new, with `hd_trl.h`) reads,
maps and deforms. `HDTrlFrames` is the frame-count rule: the first word is the frame count
where it fills the file at the face's column count, and its low half otherwise (15 of the
45 files, every file of `ADMIRAL_HEAD`, `DEMON_HEAD`, the two `PATRICK` faces and
`SERGIE_HEAD`); a file of another column count is refused. `HDTrlOpen` and
`HDTrlReadFrame` read one frame at a time, 1920 bytes at 40 columns, because a whole clip
is up to 11.5 MB (`DEMON_HEAD_135.TRL`) and cutscene 44 speaks three such faces at once.
`HDLipsMapBuild` turns the header into the driven joints, the parents in composition
order, the head joint (the rig joint the driven columns hang off: 4 in `LARA_HEAD`, 0, 1
or 2 in the others) and the axis order, a table keyed on the face file's name (`g_axis`:
`SERGIE_HEAD` (x,-z,y), `HANGMAN_HEAD` (x,-y,-z), `ZIP_HEAD` refused, the same axes for
the other ten), and inverts each column's composed bind with a general inverse, because
the columns carry a scale. `HDLipsSkins` composes a frame, `D_c = G_c * inverse(Gb_c)`,
and turns it about the head joint in the vertices' axes, `S_j = T(head) * A * D_c * A^T *
T(-head)`; every joint no column drives keeps the identity. `HDLipsDeform` blends every
vertex by the file's own bones and weights over 255, carries the normal through the
cofactor matrix at its own length, and copies a vertex whose weights lie only on joints
that do not move. `specific/hd/hd_model.cpp` keeps a `Lips` beside every separate face and
beside a rigid face whose file carries its block, which is Lara's (for the separate faces
taken before the hanged man's half turn, which the deformed copy gets back after the
deform). `make_lips` looks for the track files in game 5's `ITEM` alone, because track
numbers belong to a game: `4\ITEM`, where `LARA_HEAD.TRM` lies, holds 24 `LARA_HEAD` files
numbered after Tomb Raider IV's tracks, three of them under numbers this game uses for
other lines. `lips_stream` deforms a face when the frame changes into a buffer of its own,
`D3DUSAGE_DYNAMIC | D3DUSAGE_WRITEONLY` in `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT`, written with
`D3DLOCK_DISCARD` and made on the first speaking frame, and holds it while the frame
stands; `draw_model` binds it in place of the static buffer - the same stride, count and
order, so the index buffer, the ranges and the constants stay, and so do the static
buffer's bones and weights, which the deformed copy takes over. Buffer and file go in
`lips_close`, called by `HDModelLipsClose`, by `free_model` and so by `HDModelShutdown` in
the device-lost chain, because `Reset` refuses while a DEFAULT resource lives.
`HDModelLipsOpen` opens a face's clip, once per track. The seam: `DrawCutSeqActors`
(`game/deltapak.cpp`) calls `HDObjectLips` (`hd_object.cpp`) between `HDObjectBegin` and
`HDObjectEnd` with the cut's audio track - none while the credits run, which play no
audio - and `GLOBAL_cutseq_frame - 1`, the frame on screen, because
`do_new_cutscene_camera` decodes a frame and then steps the counter. The frame item
carries the pair to the draw. Lara's face gets the same pair (`hd_laradraw.cpp`) while a
cut she acts in plays: actor 0 of the cut is not `NO_ITEM`. `HDObjectFrameReset` closes
every clip once `GLOBAL_playing_cutseq` clears. The seam reads nothing of the game for an
actor drawn classic and writes nothing for any actor. The clock is the cutscene frame: a
file's frame index is the cutscene frame - its motion peaks against the engine's own
speech ranges (the `*_chat_ranges` tables) at a lag of 0 to -6 frames in 19 of the 20
speaker pairs they name - and a cutscene is drawn without a tween
(`game/interpolate.cpp`), so the deform runs on the integer frame, once per change and
never on a blend. No audio cursor is read. The end of a clip: `HDLipsSourceOf`
(`hd_trl.cpp`) shows the clip's last frame at (10 - k) / 10, k frames past it, and from
the tenth frame on the bind, which is the static buffer, because a file's last frame
stands up to 9.72 units off the bind (`LARSON_HEAD_108.TRL`). `LARA_HEAD_103` and
`LARA_HEAD_119` hold 5608 frames, more than their cuts, and the frame index never reaches
their ends. With `-log`: at level build `HDLOG level=<L> lips slot=<n> face=<STEM>
file=<STEM>_<track>.TRL frames=<n> cols=<c> joints=<driven>/<rig> axis=<identity |
(x,-z,y) | (x,-y,-z) | -> len=<s>s reason=<ok | no file | refused | columns>`, one per
face and track file, one with `file=-` for a face with none, and `from=4 trl_from=5` at
the end of Lara's; while a cut plays `LIPLOG f=<GlobalCounter> cut=<cutseq_num> frame=<n>
track=<n> slot=<n> src=<trl | ease | bind> jaw=<units> lang=<EN | DE | FR | IT | ES |
JP>`, once per frame change of a speaking face, `jaw` being the farthest vertex's distance
from the bind and `lang` the language the audio path looks for first; and at the end of
`HDLOG cutseq actor=` ` lips=<track>/<frames>` or ` lips=-`, at the end of `HDLOG frame
lara` ` lips=<track>` or ` lips=-`. The existing log lines are extended at their end only;
`INTERPLOG` is as it was. `ModelProbe -lips <FILE.TRL> <frame>` draws a face at a frame of
its track by the same road, `<a>:<b>:<step>` tiles a set of frames, and every run prints
the engine's lips lines. `LipsTest` (`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose`, built by `blips.bat`
out of `hd_trm.cpp`, `hd_trl.cpp` and `hd_install.cpp`, reading the installation
read-only) checks the map of the 12 faces it takes (`ZIP_HEAD` refused), each face's
composed frame 0 against its rig's own joints, that frame 0 through the deform returns
every vertex to itself and every normal byte exactly, the frame rule over all 45 files and
the ease, and agrees with an independent implementation of the same arithmetic to at most
0.0001 units.

**Decisions.** The six spoken languages' tracks are equal in length to the millisecond in
20 of 22 tracks (113 and 119 are half a second longer in English), so one set of track
files serves them all: the engine indexes a file by the cutscene frame and stretches
nothing, and a dubbed line that runs off the English timing keeps the English mouth. The
layout of the track files and the deform - a frame's matrix times the inverse of the
bind's - were found on the data files by TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931; both were measured again on the installation's files,
and the column map is the face's own header.

**Commits.** `caeda98` (base of the picture comparison), `455aed7` (head reader keeps the
rig), `ad268a2` (track reader, map, deform), `d9b7bb2` (a face's own buffer), `4e540c7`
(actors and Lara speak), `4f9a989` (ModelProbe draws a track frame)

### Lara's face between her lines: the blink loop and the firing face
2026-09-26

**What.** In HD, Lara's face moves between her cutscene lines. Her own `LARA_HEAD.TRM`
carries, behind the frame it was bound in, a block of 508 frames of its joints: frames
0-498 are one loop of 16.6 seconds in which her eyes blink eight times (once twice in a
row), glance up to 9.7 degrees and her brows move, while the ten mouth columns, the
nostrils and the cheeks stand at the bind. The engine plays that loop whenever her face
speaks no cutscene line, and stops it when she is dead. While the classic game has
`LARA_SCREAM`'s head on her - the fire key held with a gun ready, and the 16 ticks after
each shot a cutscene fires - her HD face shows the block's frame 501, bared and clenched
teeth under knitted brows, eased in over three ticks and out over three. `LARSON_HEAD`'s
block plays through the eyes alone; every other face keeps still between its lines,
because only Lara's draw asks for the loop.

**Why.** The classic scream head is `LARA_SKIN`'s head with the same vertices and other
paint, and the HD path draws nothing of it (`LARA_SCREAM` is `HD_LARA_ROLE_SUPPRESS` in
`hd_lara.cpp`): her HD face stood still while she fired. Between her lines it stood still
as well, although its own file carries the loop.

**How.** The block: `keep_block` (`specific/hd/hd_trm.cpp`) keeps where the block's frame
0 lies in the file, `blockAt` (2264 in `LARA_HEAD.TRM` and `LARA_YOUNG_HEAD.TRM`, 2260 in
`LARA_CREEPY_HEAD.TRM`, 2648 in `LARSON_HEAD.TRM`), and the first frame whose matrices
equal frame 0's byte for byte, `blockLoop` (499 in the three faces of Lara, 300 in
`LARSON_HEAD`, 0 or 1 in the eleven other rigged heads). `HDTrlClip` gains `at` and
`HDTrlReadFrame` reads at `at + frame * bytes` (`specific/hd/hd_trl.cpp`, 4 for a track
file as before); `HDTrlOpenBlock` opens the block in the `.TRM` as a clip, so its frames
are streamed 1920 bytes at a time like a track file's rather than held (975,360 bytes).
The mask: a table keyed on the face file's name, `g_loop` (`HDLipsLoopMask`): the three
faces of Lara play the eye columns 12-15, 22 and 23 and the brow columns 16-21 with the
helper columns they hang off, 26-29, 33 and 34 (`0x63cfff000`); `LARSON_HEAD` its eye
columns 12-15 alone (`0xf000`); every other face 0. `HDLipsSkins` takes the mask and the
block's frame 0: a column outside it takes frame 0's local matrix before the columns are
composed, and its joint keeps the identity, so `HDLipsDeform` copies every vertex on no
masked joint; a mask of every column, or no frame 0, is the plain call. `HDLipsBlinks`
marks the first frame of the loop at which the upper lids (columns 12 and 13, their turn
from the bind by `HDLipsTurn`) stand more than 15 degrees closed and the frame before them
does not. The two tracks: `HD_LIPS_TRACK_LOOP` 1000 and `HD_LIPS_TRACK_FIRE` 1001
(`specific/hd/hd_model.h`), above every audio track. `make_lips` (`hd_model.cpp`) fills in
the loop of a face - the path of its `.TRM`, `blockAt`, the loop, the mask, frame 0's
locals and the blinks, read once at level build - for a block that loops after 30 frames
or more and a name the table knows. `HDModelLipsOpen` opens the block for either track,
one clip for both, so a switch between them only forgets the frame shown. The frame a draw
hands is a key (`HDModelLipsLoopKey`, `HDModelLipsFireKey`), taken apart by
`pseudo_source` and `pseudo_skins` inside `lips_stream`, which deforms into the face's own
buffer on a change of key as for a track. The loop's key is the loop's frame; after she
dies it carries the ticks since, and the loop's frame eases to the bind the way a track
eases past its end (`HDLipsSourceOf`, ten ticks). The firing face is frame 501 in full,
`step / 3` of the way from the loop's frame of the moment through the mask (from the bind
while she is dead), by `HDLipsSkinsBlend` (`hd_trl.cpp`), which from the identities is the
ease of `HDLipsSkins` to the last bit; at the full step the key leaves the loop's frame
out, so a held fire key deforms once. A track whose file is not there is remembered, and
asked again it answers 0 without closing the loop, so a cut whose line her face has no
file for does not open the block again every frame. `HDObjectPush` marks a clip as playing
only for a track below 1000 (`hd_object.cpp`), so `HDObjectFrameReset` leaves the loop's
clip open outside a cut, and the LIPLOG writer passes over the two tracks' frame changes.
The choice: `scream_head` (`hd_laradraw.cpp`) is true when `lara.mesh_ptrs[LM_HEAD]` is
`LARA_SCREAM`'s head mesh and that mesh is not `LARA`'s. `choose_face` runs once in each
`HDLaraDrawFrame` before the face is pushed and picks, in this order: in first person the
face as built (first person pushes no face); the cut's track where her face has its file;
the face as built while the frame's mask hides the head node or the face has no loop; the
firing face while its step is above 0; the loop while `lara_item->hit_points` is above 0;
and once she is dead the loop's ease to the bind and then the face as built. The step
(`HDLipsFireStep`) goes up one a tick while the scream head is on and down one while it is
off: 1/3, 2/3 and 1 on, 2/3, 1/3 and the loop off (`HDLipsEaseIn`). The clock is
`GlobalCounter` (`game/control.cpp`, stepped once a logic tick): the loop's frame is
`GlobalCounter` modulo 499, so the inventory and the pause, which hold the counter, hold
the face, the mirror's second draw shows the same frame, and the counter's wrap at 65536
ticks jumps the loop once in 36 minutes. The state lives in `g_face` and is reset with the
level (`face_reset`, from `HDLaraDrawEnd`); the outfit changer (F4) rebuilds the objects,
which reaches `face_reset`, so the face starts over with its loop. The new code reads
`lara.mesh_ptrs[LM_HEAD]`, `lara_item->hit_points`, `objects[LARA_SCREAM]` and
`GlobalCounter` and writes none of them; the classic swaps (`game/larafire.cpp`,
`game/deltapak.cpp`) are untouched. With `hd_enable` off no face keeps a loop and Lara's
plan and draw return before `choose_face`. With `-log`: at level build one line per face
that keeps lips, after its track lines (`loop_line`), `HDLOG level=<L> lips loop slot=<n>
face=<STEM> frames=<block frames> loop=<n> at=<offset> mask=<hex> blinks=<n> reason=<ok |
no block | no loop | no mask | unmapped>`; on each change of face `LIPLOG
f=<GlobalCounter> lara face=<cut | fire | loop | static> was=<...> slot=<n> frame=<n>
why=<cutscene | fire on | fire off | first person | masked | dead | no block | start>`,
`start` for the first choice of a level and `frame=-1` for the face as built; on the first
frame of each blink `LIPLOG f=<GlobalCounter> lara blink frame=<n> lid=<degrees>`; and
`lips=loop` or `lips=fire` at the end of `HDLOG frame lara`. The existing log lines are
extended at their end only. `ModelProbe -loop <frame>` or `<a>:<b>:<step>` and `-fire
<on>[:<off>]` draw the loop and the firing face by the same road; `LipsTest` checks the
blocks' places and loops, the masks (no vertex off the masked joints moves over the loop),
the blink frames and the ease.

**Decisions.** The firing face follows the classic head swap and has no rule of its own:
it shows while the fire key is held with a gun ready - an empty gun included, the flare
never - and for the 16 ticks after each scripted shot of a cutscene, and where the classic
head stays on after the gun was put away some other way, the HD face stays with it -
except inside a cut whose line her face speaks, where the line comes first. Its frame is
the block's 501, the clenched teeth, as the counterpart of the classic painted face; 506,
the open shout, is the other candidate, and the number lives in one constant
(`HD_LIPS_FIRE_FRAME`, `hd_trl.h`). Three ticks soften the instant classic swap
(`HD_LIPS_EASE_IN_TICKS`). Her brows move with her eyes in her loop. `LARSON_HEAD`'s loop
leaves out the two slow presses of the lips the block also holds. In a cut she acts in
whose line her face has no file for, and in the credits, where the cutscenes replay
without their lines, the firing face and the loop come next in the order: there she
blinks, and after the scripted shots she bares her teeth with the classic head.

**Commits.** `8321293` (base of the comparison), `6ce284e` (block place, loop, streaming),
`11026db` (blink loop, firing face), `026be9e` (ModelProbe draws both)

### Statics: baked into the room, shot to pieces, or drawn classic where the art does not cover them
2026-09-05 - 2026-09-08

**What.** Three rules decide what happens to a static or animating inside an HD room. A
slot the level's own `.MAP` calls DUMMY is drawn by nobody, because the Remaster has baked
that object into the room mesh. A destructible static's HD copy is kept in draw calls of
its own and follows the classic mesh's shattered flag, so it disappears when it is shot.
And a classic static is suppressed in favour of the `.TRG`'s art only where that art
really covers it: at least a twentieth of the static's own bounding box, or another room's
art holds it; otherwise it is drawn the classic way inside the HD room.

**Why.** An HD room's `MESH_INFO` list was suppressed whole, and ANDREA1's lamp post and
the lantern on its wall arm each stood twice, slightly apart, once as the baked HD copy
and once as the classic mesh. A DUMMY line in a `.MAP` is a real file with no parts in
it - 240 of the 2,940 bindings across both installs point at `DUMMY.TRM` - and means draw
nothing here as an object, sometimes because the thing is baked into the room mesh
(Todesengel1931's own measurement, TRForge, MIT,
`vendor/trforge/src/trf_remaster/HdMesh.cpp`, the note at `items_dummy`). Counting
Remaster triangles inside each object's own box, in ANDREA1 every DUMMY slot that has
items has the art standing in it and no other slot does: the wall lantern 169 triangles
per million cubic units, the alcove 44, the lamp post 59, the arch 30, the waterfall 12,
against a highest of 4.0 for any slot the map does not call DUMMY and 0.01 to 0.04 for the
big ones, which is a room's own floor inside an enemy's box. A destructible static carries
its material with bit 15 set, bits 8..14 an instance counter 0..5 and bits 0..7 an
ordinary material number (0, 3 or 14 and nothing else): 69 such parts in six levels and 32
rooms (ANDREA1 6, ANDREA2 5, JOBY2 3, RICH1 5, RICH2 14, RICH3 36). The counter is an
instance index and not a damage stage: JOBY2 room 57 carries 0x8000, 0x8100 and 0x8200
with 552 triangles each side by side at x 1024..2048, 2048..3072 and 3072..4096, same y,
same z, 25 units thick; RICH2 room 151 has three 2,226-triangle copies at three corners
and RICH3 room 204 four. A group may also cover only part of its room: 21 statics of
ANDREA1 sit in no `.TRG` group at all, above all in rooms 121 and 221, whose groups do
have geometry (27,252 and 2,803 triangles) but whose boxes stop short of where the statics
stand. The coverage threshold sits in the measured gap between two clumps: over the
fifteen levels 271 statics catch nothing at all, 44 catch more than nothing but under a
twentieth, and 2,286 catch a twentieth or more. The 44 were suppressed with nothing to put
in their place: a TR5 palm is two statics, trunk in the ground room (slot 8) and crown in
the room above (slot 9), and ANDREA2 room 125's crowns caught 4 cells of 768, the wall
behind them, so the crown went and the trunk stayed; the same level's room 162 crown
catches 313 of 768 and really is in the art.

**How.** The DUMMY test is per ITEM and not per slot, so a room the sidecar marked classic
keeps its object the old way, and it sits ahead of the object path's own guard, because
the second copy comes out of the `.TRG` whether `hd_objects` is on or off; a model that
reads but carries no triangle counts as the same statement, and a donor slot is never
baked, because its model came out of another level file. Six of ANDREA1's DUMMY items have
no Remaster triangles in their box either and nothing is drawn there, which is what the
installation's art holds. For the destructible pieces, each (group, material) is one piece
whose triangles are kept in draw calls of their own with the id in the sort key so they
never merge with the wall behind them; `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp` pairs a piece with the
classic `MESH_INFO` standing inside its box out of the slots 50 to 57 that
`game/control.cpp` calls shatterable, and `MESH_INFO::Flags` bit 0, which `control.cpp`
clears when Lara shoots one, decides per frame. Coverage is asked per static rather than
per room: the renderer keeps, per group, a sorted list of the 256-unit cells its own
vertices fall in - a quarter of a floor square on a side, ten bits per axis, built while
the index buffer is filled, about 25 bytes per thousand vertices - and
`HDRenderGroupCellsIn` answers how many cells of a room-local box carry geometry
(`hd_level.cpp`). A static's box is its own visibility box turned by the mesh's `y_rot`
through the engine's own sine table. Where the coverage is under a twentieth,
`DrawStaticObjects` (`game/draw.cpp`) draws that static the classic way inside the HD room
unless another room's art holds it (see *A place the art draws is drawn by the art
alone*); a static baked into a NEIGHBOUR's group (room 136's crown sits in group 154) is
drawn classic only while that group is off the frame's list. Log: `baked_slots=` per
level, `reason=baked` per slot, `baked=` per frame, one `HDLOG ... statics classic=` line
per level, one `HDLOG static room=` line per static that changed sides and `HDLOG static
... classic cells=%d of %d` for the count. Tools: `RoomProbe -shatter`, `-hasgeom`;
`TrgProbe -statics` / `-slot <n>` lists every static mesh with its box and how much art
stands in it. Files: `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_render.cpp`/`.h`,
`hd_bind.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_object.cpp`, `game/draw.cpp`,
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/RoomProbe.cpp`, `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/TrgProbe.cpp`.

**Decisions.** Coverage is counted in cells, not by a part's bounding box, which cannot
answer it because one part of a Roman room spans the whole room, and not by walking
triangles per static, which would be a million tests per lantern. The `.MAP` `DUMMY`
family list of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931 is
about moveables baked into the room art and is not a statics rule; it is not adopted here.

**Commits.** `0cb9e8d` (level map, baked objects), `196849a`, `e2c8d29`

### The destroyable windows (#209)
2026-10-16 - 2026-10-20

**What.** A shot pane takes its destructible glass piece with it, and a static in a row
takes its own piece and no other: `HDStaticPiecePaired` (`specific/hd/hd_cover.h`) asks
for a real overlap and gives a pane's plane a slack of `HD_STATIC_PIECE_EDGE` = **16**
units. The pairing takes the statics of slots 50 to 59, never a piece of the room's
flipmap twin, and reads each static where its list stands after a flip, so ANDREA2's
window (rooms 132 and 65, static slot 59) is whole before its break and gone with it, in
play and after every save load. ANDREA2's grid is drawn in two halves: its bars solid,
with the depth write, among the alpha pass's solid ranges, its panes added ONE / ONE as
the classic adds its glass. The additive run's glass on a page with no clear texel
(RICH2's bridge among it) is added whole, as the classic adds its glass. Glass the room
draw draws as the classic's takes the hue of the classic glass at its place, its luma
kept; and ANDREA1's arched panes (page 15074) are added whole and take a green chosen for
them, from a table of looks by page, their breaking pane's pieces as well. Every other
glass is drawn as before. A plain glass part the art does not mark destructible (the arch
top above ANDREA1's panes) is not a piece and stays after the shot.

**Why.** In ANDREA1 and ANDREA2 the windows were hardly visible and stayed after they were
destroyed. The windows are no items but shatterable statics (slots 50 to 57 for a shot,
`control.cpp`), and their HD art is the `.TRG`'s destructible pieces (material bit 15, see
*Statics: baked into the room, shot to pieces, or drawn classic where the art does not
cover them*), hidden per frame from `MESH_INFO::Flags` bit 0 by `UpdateDestructibles`
(`hd_level.cpp`), which the save load restores (`savegame.cpp`). ANDREA1's classic pane is
flat, its box at z 968 in room 198 and x 968 in room 201, and its glass piece stands at
966..967, one unit off; the pairing took boxes that touch and nothing closer, so the frame
went with the shot and the glass stayed. In a row of panes (JOBY2 room 57, RICH3 rooms 120
and 169 to 171) the statics touch or overlap their neighbour's piece by one or two units,
so each took two or three pieces and the last pair written decided: one shot hid another
pane. ANDREA2's window is a static in each room of a flipmap pair, slot 59, mesh 571 at
67072, -2048, 41472 (rooms 132 and 65, flip 8, the same 30 classic faces in both, none in
the window's plane); mesh 571 draws 260 opaque quads (the bars, textures 2229 and 2230)
and 70 additive ones (the panes, 2231 and 2232). Its break is a heavy trigger in room 131
below (item 109 and FLIPMAP 8), tested by flyby sequence 5, camera 16: item 109 is an
`XRAY_CONTROLLER` at the static's own place with OCB 333, and `ControlXRayMachine`'s case
333 (`objects.cpp`) shatters every static of its room standing exactly at its place and
clears its Flags bit 0. FlipMap runs at the end of the trigger's walk and the controller
in the next frame, so the static it clears is in the list room 132 holds by then, the one
built for room 65; a save restored after the break flips map 8 and then restores Flags bit
0 of every static of slots 50 to 59. Groups 65 and 132 each hold the grid (`0x800e`, 2,146
triangles on page 3007 in the alpha run, `param` (2, 0.1)), the same box and triangles,
and nothing in the art marks one state's grid as broken; the pairing took slots 50 to 57
only, so neither piece had a static and the window stayed after the break and after every
load. The grid's bars lie on clear texels: of the 103,293 texels of page 3007 under it,
55,877 (54.1 %) have alpha below 16 and carry the bars' colour (mean RGB 106, 82, 60),
47,416 (45.9 %) lie between 16 and 239 (the panes), none is opaque, and 2,076 of the 2,146
triangles sample clear texels. The room's glass rule read `param[1]` as the opacity of the
whole part, so the bars were drawn at nothing and the panes at a tenth of their alpha; and
the grid was one draw call in the glass phase, SRCALPHA / INVSRCALPHA, the depth write off
and no cull, so the bars, boxes 51 units deep, had their back faces and far bars painted
over the near ones (single bars floating, a bar seen as a hollow body), and the hall's
mirror (`HDRenderMarbleDraw`, drawn after the rooms' glass) painted the floor over the
bars. The classic draws its glass with draw type 2, ONE / ONE, the texel times its light,
the specular off, and reads no alpha for it (`phd_PutPolygons`, `polyinsert.cpp`); RICH2's
bridge pane (item 183, `BRIDGE_TILT2`, slot 452, `DUMMY` in `RICH2.MAP` and baked into
group 125's part 2, additive run at 0.8181 on page 16103) was added as the texel times its
light times its alpha times `param[1]`, 0.36 of the classic's. The HD panes' added colour
came out grey (the art's blue texels under its warm vertex light) where the classic's is
blue at the window and green at the bridge; the tint is blue, closer to the original,
which is this engine's classic draw. ANDREA1's arched panes take a green tint. JOBY2's
facade window is the room art's, not a destructible piece (see *The translucent parts of
HD models and JOBY2's window (#226)*).

**How.** The pairing, from the engine's own state and never a room's number, in pure
functions of `hd_cover.h`. `HDStaticPiecePaired`: along an axis the static's box has an
extent on, the two boxes overlap by more than 16 units; along one it has none on
(`HDStaticFlat`'s measure, under one unit), its plane stands within 16 of the piece; every
true pair overlaps by 38 units or more and a pane stands 0 or 1 unit off its glass, the
false pairs overlap by 0 to 2, and none of the 72 shatterable statics of the fifteen
levels is thin but not flat (their smallest extent other than none is 59).
`HDStaticShatterSlot`: slots 50 to 59 (`HD_STATIC_SHATTER_FIRST`, `_LAST`), the ten whose
Flags bit 0 the savegame writes and restores, ten `ShatterSounds` per level; a shot takes
50 to 57, the gladiator's and the Roman god's blows any of the ten, the controller at OCB
333 any static at its place. `HDStaticPieceInState`: a static takes no piece of its room's
flipmap twin, because FlipMap puts the twin in the room's place and never beside it, so
the twin's grid is the other state's; the pairing loop finds the twin as `flipped_room`
names it, for the alternate by the main room that names it. `HDStaticListRoom`:
`UpdateDestructibles` reads each pair's static where the list it was built from stands now
(FlipMap swaps two rooms' records with their `MESH_INFO` lists, and `HDFlipRoom` the group
table with them), so the rule holds in any numbering of the pair. Over the fifteen levels
the pairs of the game are 69, one per piece, and no piece is shared. The split:
`GlassSplits` (`hd_render.cpp`): a see-through draw call (material 14 in the alpha pass,
`param[1]` under 1, not a clear floor) whose page has a texel under 16 of 255
(`HD_GLASS_CLEAR_BELOW`) and more than 500 per mille of its texels below the alpha test's
reference (`HDPageCacheSlotCutoutPermille`, `HD_GLASS_FRAME_PERMILLE`) is drawn twice by
`draw_pass`: its frame half with the alpha pass's solid ranges, without the alpha test,
the depth write on, `gPass.z` 1; its glass half in the glass phase, ONE / ONE, the
specular off (`gPass.w` 0), `gPass.z` -1. The room shader (`hd_room.hlsl`) keeps one
half's texels, `clip(gPass.z * (texel.a < 16 / 255 ? 1 : -1))` after the alpha test, a
product of 0 in every other draw call; and in a draw call whose see-through weight
`gSpec.w` is under 1 a texel with alpha under 16 is drawn opaque, every other texel at its
alpha times `gSpec.w`, a call at 1 untouched. 16 of 255 is the census's own bound of
clear: of the 74 material 14 parts with an alpha run and `param[1]` under 1 in the fifteen
levels, only ANDREA2's grid in group 65 and its twin 132 have clear texels, so no other
part is drawn differently. The page share sits in the census's gap: 856 per mille for page
3007 and 116 for the next see-through page (RICH3's 10084), so any number from 116 to 855
decides the fifteen levels alike, and half the page is where a page is mostly frame. Whole
glass: `AddGlass` (`hd_render.cpp`): an additive draw call of material 14 whose page has
no texel under 16 of 255 (`HDPageCacheSlotAlphaMin` at least `HD_GLASS_CLEAR_BELOW`), or
whose page is in the table of looks, is added whole: `draw_pass` writes its weight as 1
and `gPass.z` -1, and the room shader skips the multiply by the texel's alpha where
`gPass.z` is below 0 (`step(0, gPass.z)`, 1 for every other call). No draw call, state or
pass is added; of the 107 additive material 14 parts of the fifteen levels, 86 are added
whole by the page test and the seven on page 15074 by the table of looks. The two page
tests stand in `hd_debris_rules.h` (`HDGlassFramePage`, `HDGlassWholePage`), which the
pieces of a broken static read too. The hue (`hd_debris_rules.h`, "the glass's look";
`hd_render.cpp`, `GlassCandidate`, `GlassTintPrepare`, `HDRenderGlassTint`;
`hd_level.cpp`, `BuildGlassLooks`): at the room build the renderer keeps, for every draw
call that may be drawn as glass (a see-through range of the alpha pass, an additive range
of material 14), the boxes of its triangles in world units. Once the statics are paired
(`BuildStaticTables`), `BuildGlassLooks` walks the classic level: every face the classic
adds - room faces of draw type 2 with their vertex colours, the faces of every placed
static with effects bit 0 or draw type 2 at the prelight times the shade
(`HDGlassStaticLight`, which reads the shade as the classic does: red in its low five
bits, green in the middle five, blue in the high five, each shifted up by 3, times the
prelight over 256, as `aTransformLightPrelightClipMesh` and `ShatterObject` read it;
`GlassStaticLight` and RoomProbe both call the rule), those of every moveable of one mesh
at its item at its room's ambient - with its added colour, the mean over its texels on the
classic page (`Textures[]`, read locked once each) of the texel times its light
(`HDGlassFaceColour`). Each face whose centre lies in one of a call's triangle boxes grown
by 32 is matched once (`HDGlassAtPlace`), and the added colour summed by area becomes a
direction whose luma is 1 (`HDGlassTintOf`). `draw_pass` writes it to `gTint` (c37) where
the call is drawn as the classic's glass - the split's glass half, the additive run's
whole glass - and zero for every other call and at the top of every pass; the room shader
puts the luma of the call's add on the direction (`lit = gTint.w > 0 ? dot(lit, luma) *
gTint.rgb : lit`, after the weight), a select that leaves every other call's picture to
the bit. Of the 190 draw calls that may be glass, 43 have classic glass at their place and
take a hue, and 33 are drawn as the classic's glass and show it; a call with no classic
glass at its place keeps the art's colour. The looks (`hd_debris_rules.h`, `HDGlassLook`,
`kHDGlassLooks`, `HDGlassLookOf`, `HDGlassTintHue`; `hd_debris.h` for a piece's glass): a
page of the table is glass in every texel for the additive run, and its tint, the classic
glass's hue at the place, turns to the table's hue with its HSV saturation and its luma
kept, so the strength stays the art's and the saturation the classic's; where the classic
adds nothing at the place the tint stays zero. A piece's triangle on such a page is whole
glass too, and its look (the static's classic hue times the band's gain,
`HDGlassShardGain`) turns the same way. The table holds one line: page 15074, 120 degrees.
No room or level number is in the code; the page is the key, as in `hd_gloss_pages.h`.
Log: `HDLOG level=... glass classic_faces=... candidates=... tinted=... piece_looks=...
ms=...` at the build, behind `-log`. Tools: RoomProbe `-smash`, `-smashcensus`,
`-smashpiece` (hides a destructible piece anywhere), `-calltrace <page>`, `-lumaat`,
`-gpuall` at the end of the `-gpu` line, `-glasshue`, and `-pieceslook`, whose lines end
in `look` and `flies` (the table's hue for a paired material 14 part's page and the tint
its pieces fly with); RoomProbe's classic pieces take the room's ambient. ModernTest's
smash, window, glass split, glass hue and `glass_look` groups hold the rules, and its
glass checks hold the bodies of `GlassSplits` and `AddGlass` as the engine has them, blank
for blank, so a change to either rule fails the test until the test follows it.

**Decisions.** The rules read the engine's state (slot, flip twin, Flags bit 0), the draw
call and the page, never a level, a room or the classic mesh: the room build has no tie
from an HD part to the static whose place it takes, and the texels' classes split the grid
as the classic's face attributes do (the 70 partial triangles lie 86 % over the classic's
additive panes, the clear ones 57 to 71 % over its opaque bars). The flip pair's two
pieces stay apart by the twin rule rather than by the order of the pairs. The frame half
is drawn with the alpha pass's solid ranges, not in a depth pass of its own: one draw call
more, sorted with every cut-out and before the clear floors, the models and the glass,
where the classic's opaque faces go. The glass half takes the classic's blend, ONE / ONE
with the specular off, the one of four blends tried that lands in the classic's band and
adds light as the classic does; the texels' alpha decides which texels are pane, not how
much they add, and `param[1]` is not read for whole glass. The shadow receive pass is not
given the frame half, so no shadow falls on the bars. A first build added every additive
material 14 part whole; it turned the lamp glass of RICH2 and RICH3 (page 15101, smallest
alpha 12) white, so the page's clear texels bound the rule. The hue is the classic's added
colour, the texel times its light, so the classic's coloured room light comes with it
(RICH3's cyan rooms), faces weighted by their area as the picture weighs them; the place
is a triangle's box and not the part's (RICH2's group 125 has two additive floor faces
inside the part's box, none inside a triangle's box); a moveable counts where it has one
mesh, as the bridge's items do; the tint is computed once a level at the build, never per
frame and never from a picture, and no colour is named in the code. The hue 120, HSV's
green, is the look chosen for ANDREA1's panes, at the classic's saturation there (0.57);
the table is keyed by page and not by static or room, so a page's glass looks the same
wherever it is drawn and the breaking pane's pieces read the same line, and a look chosen
for this project goes into the table, recorded in the ledger as OWN.
