### The pieces of a broken static in HD (#222)
2026-10-18 - 2026-10-19

**What.** A shatterable static that breaks while the world is drawn HD throws pieces of
its own HD art: every triangle of the static's destructible part of the `.TRG` goes with
the classic face it lies on, and a piece made of that face carries those triangles, drawn
with the room's own shaders, its page, its light and its blend. The glass of a broken
window flies as the room draw draws the pane it came from: in two halves where the art is
a frame with glass in it (the frame's pieces solid, the glass added ONE / ONE), and added
whole where the art's glass is the additive run of a page that is glass in every texel;
what is added takes the hue of the breaking static's classic glass and is raised by the
classic band's top over its middle, so the pieces show. The pieces' place, flight, count,
life and sound are the classic break's, untouched (`game/debris.cpp`'s flight is
unchanged). A static with no part of the art, and every break while the world is drawn
classic, throws the classic pieces as before; the 30 statics of slots 50 to 59 that the
art bakes into the rooms' ordinary parts (TITLE 6, RICH1 12, RICH2 12) break classic and
their art keeps drawing after the break. The new files are `specific/hd/hd_debris_rules.h`
(the rule, pure) and `specific/hd/hd_debris.h` (the art's read, the break's table beside
the debris array, the draw; its definitions behind `HD_DEBRIS_BODY`, which `hd_level.cpp`
and RoomProbe define, so that neither the engine's project nor `broom.bat` changes);
`game/debris.cpp` opens the break in HD and notes each piece's face, `specificfx.cpp`'s
`DrawDebris` asks per piece, `hd_level.cpp` names the static's parts
(`HDStaticBreakParts`) and draws the pieces last in its two brackets. RoomProbe gains
`-debris`, `-debrisclassic`, `-debrisseed` and `-pieceslook`.

**Why.** When ANDREA2's window was destroyed in HD the pieces were still the classic blue
textures, so the glass pieces are drawn as glass, with a boost on top once they are blue.
`DrawDebris` draws a piece through the classic path with `textinfo[...]` and so with
`Textures[]`, the level's classic 256 x 256 pages (the HD path lends `Textures[]` an HD
page only for the water's animation frames, `HDWaterFrameFor`); a bar piece goes to
`AddTriZBuffer`, a pane piece, its effects word's bit 0 set, to `AddTriSorted` at draw
type 2 (ONE / ONE, no depth write, no specular), and the classic sort list draws them
after `HDFrameDraw`, tested against the HD depth, so the gold bars and blue panes of the
classic pages flew off the HD window. `ControlXRayMachine`'s case 333 (`objects.cpp`)
breaks the window with `ShatterObject(0, mesh, 128, room, 0)`: slot 59, mesh 571, 260
opaque bar quads and 70 additive pane quads, each quad standing twice, front and back, at
165 places; the break walks the quads in their order and makes the first 128 into pieces
(each the triangle of a quad's corners 1, 2 and 4), and the faces after them go with the
static. The window's HD art is one part in each flip state, `0x800e` in groups 132 and 65,
2,146 triangles on page 3007 in the alpha run at `param[1]` 0.1, every centroid 0 to 26
units off a classic face (median 16.7). Drawn at the art's 0.1, the HD glass pieces
darkened the picture by 1 to 3 levels and were not seen, where the classic panes fly blue
(hue 204) and add 24 to 34 levels on average.

**How.** The rule (`hd_debris_rules.h`) reads the static's own part, never a room or level
number. A triangle of the part goes with the classic face nearest its centroid
(`HDDebrisFaceOf`; a quad as its two halves, a face with a corner past the 256 vertices
the break reads as no face). No reach is set: the part is the static's art by its pairing,
and the farthest centroid of the game lies 151 units off its mesh (ANDREA2's slot 51, room
1). Faces that stand at one place corner for corner - a pane's two sides - share its
triangles, dealt by a hash of the triangle's number (`HDDebrisDeal`), so each piece of the
place carries a share and none is drawn twice. A face that became a piece flies its
triangles; a face the count left out takes them with it, as its classic face goes. A piece
whose face took no triangle draws nothing in HD (at ANDREA2 the crossings of two bars,
whose art the bars' long triangles carry): an HD break is the art the break hides. The
triangles ride on the piece's matrix, offset from its birth place as they stood in the
art. The blend is the part's run, as the room draw reads it: opaque solid, material 14's
alpha run glass at `param[1]` (`MaterialBlend`), another alpha run cut at 0.5, the
additive run a glow at weight 1 (`MaterialAddWeight` compares the whole number, and a
destructible part's carries bit 15). A triangle is glass when its kind and page say the
room draw draws it as the classic's glass: the alpha run of material 14 at a see-through
weight under 1 on a page that paints its frame on clear texels (`HDGlassFramePage`), drawn
in two halves - the frame's clear texels first (`gPass.z` 1), then the rest added ONE /
ONE with the specular off (`gPass.z` -1, `gPass.w` 0) - or the additive run of material 14
on a page with no clear texel (`HDGlassWholePage`), added whole (`gPass.z` -1). What is
added takes the part's look in `gTint`: the hue of the breaking static's own faces the
classic adds, by area (`HDGlassTintOf`, the shade read as `HDGlassStaticLight` reads it),
times the gain `HDGlassShardGain`, the band's top over its middle - the nine tenths over
the half of those faces' texels' added luma, in whole levels (`HDGlassBand`).
`BuildGlassLooks` (`hd_level.cpp`) hands every pair of a static and a part its look at the
level build (`HDDebrisPartLook`); the break carries it to the part's triangles; a static
whose faces the classic does not add takes no look, and every other triangle draws as
before. ANDREA2's window takes hue 0.479, 1.151, 1.592 at a gain of 2.300; RICH3's static
57 (ten statics) flies its 4 additive triangles whole; ANDREA1's, JOBY2's and RICH2's
pieces draw as their panes' rules say. The draw: `HDLevelBuild` reads the destructible
parts once a level pairs any (`HDDebrisLevelRead`): the file's head and parts, then only
their index runs and the vertices those name, by seeking (ANDREA2's five parts, 7,220
triangles, in a few milliseconds). `ShatterObject` (`game/debris.cpp`) asks
`HDStaticBreakParts` once it has turned the vertices: the pairs of `UpdateDestructibles`
name the static's parts, read where its list stands now. `HDDebrisBreakMesh` makes the
mesh's faces at the static's place in the order the walk takes them (`HDDebrisMeshFace`)
and opens the break; `TriggerDebris` notes each piece's face beside the debris array
(`HDDebrisNote`), and the end of the walk writes the break's line and closes it.
`DrawDebris` builds a piece's matrix as before; a piece with a look and the world drawn HD
(`HDLevelActive`) is noted with that matrix instead of going to the sort list.
`HDFrameDraw` draws the solid and cut-out triangles last in its bracket, `HDFrameDrawGlow`
the glass and the glows last in its: the vertices put into view space on the processor,
one `DrawPrimitiveUP` per kind and page, with the room's own vertex and pixel shaders
(`kHDRoomVS`, `kHDRoomPS`, compiled once more into the file that holds the definitions),
the projection and the frame's fog, fog bulbs and screen; every switch of the room's
vertex shader off, no dynamic light, no gloss, both sides drawn. The light is the art's
baked light where the triangle stood. Every device state the draw sets is put back; the
shader constants are the next bracket's to write. Behind `-log`: `HDLOG level=... debris
parts=... tris=... ms=...` and `HDLOG level=... glass pieces room=... mesh=... group=...
material=... faces=... tint=... band=... gain=...` at the build, and `HDLOG debris break
level=... room=... mesh=... parts=... faces=... places=... tris=... faces_with_art=...
pieces=... pieces_with_art=... tris_flying=... ms=...` at a break. RoomProbe `-debris`
builds its faces through the engine's own `HDDebrisBreakMesh`; `-debrisclassic` draws the
classic look and adds the room's ambient only for a mesh without a prelight, as
`ShatterObject` hands it to `DrawDebris` (a prelit mesh's pieces carry the prelight and an
ambient of 0). ModernTest's debris group holds the faces of the breaking mesh, the
distance, the place, the deal, a window's triangles alike with and without the box cut, no
reach and the blend; a harness that links `game/debris.cpp` shows the debris array and the
random generator's state after a break and 120 steps unchanged by the hooks.

**Decisions.** No reach and no distance in the rule: the pairing already says which art is
the static's. The deal is a hash, never the engine's random generator, which the break
must leave as it is. A piece with no art draws nothing rather than its classic page. The
pieces are drawn last in each bracket so that their shader constants touch no later draw,
which puts the glass after the rooms' glows; the room's own shader bytecode is used, not a
copy of its lines, so the pieces follow any change to the room's light and glass. The
glass of a piece is the room draw's glass by the same two page tests, so a pane and its
pieces never disagree on what is glass, and the hue from the breaking static's own faces
is the pane's hue. The gain is the classic's own band, its top over its middle, not a
number: the pane's add sits near the middle, and the boost takes the pieces towards the
top (to 0.85 of it at ANDREA2, where the art adds less); a gain of the top over the art's
own add would need the art's texels at the build, which only the page cache holds, on the
card. A multiplier on the add and not a fixed colour, so the art's texture stays in the
pieces. The deal's cost, 5 to 20 ms once per break of a large window, stays. The 30
statics without a part are parked: the `.TRG` bakes them into the rooms' ordinary parts
with no part of material bit 15, no other name and no twin, and a rule that cut a static's
art out of a room's part by its box would cut the room's walls and floors with it (RICH1
room 147: 9,092 of 10,545 triangles inside static 58's box). TROne (GPLv3) by
Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931 draws the pieces the classic way and
hides a broken static's art only where the `.TRG` gives it a part of its own (material bit
15 with the static's ordinal in bits 8 to 14), so nothing of it is taken for these 30.

**Commits.** `9fdd6498` (comparison base), `2341a7f` (comparison base), `8735c17e` (the
rule and the draw), `091ee90d` (the tools), `caeb52e6` (the records), `32797348` (break's
glue into debris.cpp), `1f1dafa6` (records follow the glue), `d9e637bd` (classic pieces
take ambient), `3a469090` (the glass pieces' look), `f80e567e` (ModernTest), `a68a9de0`
(comparison base), `b170d09d` (ambient only without prelight), `8235f46e` (the shade's
channels)

### The search objects' binding and the double doors (#224)
2026-10-19

**What.** Two rules of the HD object path, both from the level's own data and both in a
new pure header, `specific/hd/hd_object_rules.h`. The skeleton fit: a model the bind drift
refuses is asked, per node, how far the centre of its single-weight vertices stands from
the centre of the classic mesh of that node in the bind pose; within 256 units at every
node it is drawn HD with `reason=fit` (`hd_object.cpp`, `skeleton_fit_of` and the verdict;
`hd_model.cpp` keeps the drift's per-node centres, `HDModelNodeCentre`, which the header
declares). This draws the search lockers and cabinets of JOBY2, JOBY5 and RICH2
(`SEARCH_OBJECT1`, slot 164) in HD, and seven other slots the drift refused: RICH1's
`CHEF_MIP` (88, never drawn there), `DOOR_TYPE1` (284, a vent grille) and
`ANIMATING12_MIP` (439, slanted cabinets), RICH2's `ANIMATING1` and `ANIMATING13` (416 and
440, falling crates), RICH3's `KICK_DOOR1` (320, a brick wall in 14 pieces) and
`SMASH_OBJECT1` (397, two glass panes). The pocket: a slot whose animations carry it out
of its own box and fold it flat, with no node turning within an animation, is drawn
one-sided (`pocket_of`, the side in `HDObjectEnd`); over the fifteen levels that is
JOBY2's double door, slots 304 and 306. ModelProbe takes both apart (`-bindcheck`,
`-crossdrift`, `-slidecensus`, `-animframe`, `-itemanim`, `-itempush`, `-nopocket`,
`-itemcull`; `-cull` for `-slot`), holds the classic meshes over the HD picture
(`-classicdots`) and judges its `-all` table by the rules; ModernTest holds the rules (22
checks).

**Why.** RICH2's cabinets and JOBY2's lockers were not drawn HD at all, and in JOBY2 every
grey steel double door showed textures fighting with themselves at its place when it
opened. `SEARCH_OBJECT1` is three nodes, the body on node 0 and a door on each of nodes 1
and 2, hinged at x -507 and 507; the model stands where the classic meshes stand (in JOBY2
each node's `.TRM` centre lies 92 to 100 units from the classic mesh's centre), with no
node order, pivot or baked offset differing. The drift rule takes a node's vertex centre
to lie within its spread of its joint, but the cabinet's mesh hangs above its origin and
the animation frame's offset (y 1175) brings it down, so the body's centre lies 1,775
units from node 0's joint and the drift read 484 (JOBY5 428, RICH2 522) against its limit
of 256; every slot the drift refused had that shape, a node's mesh far off its own joint
with the model in place. The double door is the pair `CLOSED_DOOR3` (slot 304,
`CLOSED_DOOR4_JOBY2_R`) and `CLOSED_DOOR4` (306, `CLOSED_DOOR4_JOBY2`), four pairs in
rooms 1, 73, 106 and 108. Each leaf is three flat panels: node 0 the side at the middle,
nodes 1 and 2 the front and the back, 1,024 apart; anim 3 slides it 1,012 units sideways,
no node turning, and anim 2, the open rest, turns nodes 1 and 2 90 degrees so that the
front and the back panel lie in one plane, the plane of the doorway's jamb. Drawn whole
and two-sided, both panels stood at one depth: the fight was the leaf's own two panels,
not the two halves against each other, not a classic mesh drawn as well and not the room's
art (a push of the doors by up to 0.8 % of their distance left the fighting pixels in
place).

**How.** The fit (`HDSkeletonFitWorst`, `HDSkeletonJudge`): the drift first, as it was; a
model it refuses is placed when every node with 16 single-weight vertices and a classic
mesh stands within 256 units of that mesh's centre; a fit that measured no node vouches
for nothing. 256 stands in the measured gap: the models that belong read 21 to 153, and
over the 1,489 foreign pairs `ModelProbe -all -crossdrift` makes over the fifteen levels
(every bound model of two or more nodes on every other slot with its node count) the fit
takes only four of the 344 the drift refuses, all twins of the slot itself
(`SEARCH_OBJECT1` on its own `_MIP` slot in JOBY2 and JOBY5; RICH2's `ANIMATING1` and
`ANIMATING13`, one mesh in two slots), while the nearest truly foreign tree reads 383
(RICH1's `SPIDER` on slots 50, 302 and 304). On the randomized levels the foreign tree the
randomizer puts into ANDREA1's `SAS` stays refused (drift 807, fit 2,383). A node the HD
model leaves empty draws nothing, as every bound slot's empty node does (the crates' two
tumbling rods, the brick wall's stub node 0). The pocket (`HDSlotSlidesIntoPocket`): the
walk over the animations a slot can reach from its first (each animation's jump and its
state changes' ranges, followed into `anims[]` as the engine's own animation code follows
them), every keyframe against the first animation's first: some keyframe's box lies wholly
outside the rest box (touching counts), some keyframe's box is flat on an axis on which
the rest's is not, and no rotation word changes within an animation. Such a slot's items
are drawn one-sided (`HD_MODEL_CULL_BACK`, the mode that keeps a `.TRM`'s outside), as the
classic draws every object; under a reflection's mirrored matrix the other mode. Of the 21
slots that leave their box (`ModelProbe -all -slidecensus`), the doors of the three Rome
levels among them, two fold; no slot or level number is in the code. The log line `HDLOG
slot=... reason=... fit=... pocket=...` behind `-log` prints each slot's verdict.

**Decisions.** The fit only answers where the drift refuses, so every slot that bound
before binds as before, and its limit is the drift's 256. The idea of judging the places
node by node within 256 units comes from TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931 (ledger entry 371), which binds with the plain mesh-tree
bind pose and has no drift test; the centres here are the drift's own single-weight vertex
means, the question is asked only of a model the drift refuses, and nothing of that
project is copied. The doors are drawn one-sided only where they fold: drawing every slot
that leaves its box one-sided turned the title's `ANIMATING4` (a crate with an open sheet)
see-through from behind, so with the fold the Rome doors and the sliding `ANIMATING` slots
keep the two-sided draw. A depth push of the doors against the wall's art changed nothing
measurable and is not in the code; `-itempush` stays as the tool that measured it.

**Commits.** `a68a9de0` (comparison base), `73a69fde` (the tools, the rules' header),
`0828bd94` (the fit), `1b660a38` (the doors), `3a7b2934` (ModernTest), `876a8ab3` (the
records), `fb1601ca` (the header's credit), `77d8a7c6` (node centre declared), `dc8b0949`
(`-classicdots`)

### The translucent parts of HD models and JOBY2's window (#226)
2026-10-20 - 2026-10-21

**What.** A third rule of the HD object path, from the classic mesh and the `.TRM`
together: a triangle of a material 14 alpha run (the material the room art's glass
carries) on a node whose classic mesh has a see-through face is drawn as the classic draws
that face - added to what lies behind it, weighed by the page's own alpha as the additive
pass weighs its texels, with no depth write, in the bracket of the glows - and added once,
as much as the classic adds its see-through face and no more (`hd_object_rules.h`,
`HDClassicFaceSeeThrough`, `HDSeeThroughNodes`, `HDTrmTriangleIsGlass`,
`HDTrmTrianglesFaceAgainst`, `HDTrmTriangleCopies`, `HDGlassOpacity`, `HDGlassWeight`,
`HDMatrixMirrors`; `hd_object.cpp`, `see_through_nodes_of`; `hd_model.cpp`,
`HDModelSetGlassNodes`, `Range::sided`, `Range::copy`, `Range::dropped`, the draw's glass
step). Over the fifteen levels 14 bound slots are drawn so: JOBY3 and JOBY5 slots 48, 286
and 290 (`DOOR_TYPE4_JOBY3_JOBY5`), RICH1 164, 286, 290 and 296, RICH2 164 (the office
cabinet), RICH3 284, TITLE 417 and 419; the other 5 slots with a material 14 alpha run
stay solid, as the classic draws them (JOBY4's `ATTACK_SUB` (81), `CHAFF` (145) and
`PUZZLE_ITEM1` (172), JOBY5's `GEN_SLOT3` (161), RICH1's `CLOSED_DOOR5` (308)). The
pocket's walk keeps to a slot's own animations (`HDPocketAnimEnd`, `HDPocketAnimOwn`).
JOBY2's facade window is left as drawn: the frame leaves the window's reveal out by the
stand rule (`hd_cover.h`, `HDStandDraw`; `hd_level.cpp`, `BuildStandFaces`), which this
change does not touch. The `HDLOG slot=` line ends in `oneside= copies= opacity= factor=`.
ModelProbe takes the glass apart (`-alpha`, `-noglass`, `-all -alpha`, which measures the
glass against the classic's band) and `-slidecensus` prints the walk before the bound as
`open=`; ModernTest holds the rules.

**Why.** RICH2's office cabinet and RICH1's oval doors had no transparency, and once drawn
as glass the cabinet added a milky sheet that had to become much clearer. In the classic
the cabinet's doors (nodes 1 and 2) carry 12 of 25 faces each with effects bit 0, added
ONE / ONE with no depth write; in the `.TRM` its glass is part 2, material 14, an alpha
run of 24 triangles a door on pages 3068 and 10054, which the HD path drew with the alpha
test and the depth write: a solid teal sheet. RICH1's oval doors (slot 290,
`DOOR_TYPE4_RICH1`, items 21 to 26 in room 15) carry the panes between the spokes as 77
alpha-run triangles on page 12108 (alpha mean 47, 64 % under 16), and the test kept the
texels over 0.5 as a grey plate and cut the rest out: dark marks; RICH1's `DOOR_TYPE2`
(286) came out as a nearly solid pane. Drawn as added glass, the cabinet's front added
four layers at a pixel where the classic adds one face - the pane, the inward sheet 11
units behind seen through the two-sided draw (the frame page's drawing over the whole door
at alpha 1, the inside of the door, for which the classic has its own face), and the pane
twice more in the additive run one unit behind - about 243 at full light against the
classic's 84.6; not one layer is brighter than the classic's face. The pocket's walk
followed every link: JOBY4's `ATTACK_SUB` has two still animations (477 and 478) whose
state changes link to its neighbours' (481, 487, 495 and 525), and ANDREA1's `ANIMATING15`
links 678 to 680; the foreign keyframes leave the box and fold, so both were drawn
one-sided and `ANIMATING15_ANDREA1` seen from behind lost almost all its pixels. JOBY2's
windows show black and the sky where the classic draws brick and wood: the black in the
hole is the classic's own (behind it stands room 21, drawn classic as a hollow group, its
far wall opaque black, the sniper in it); the missing wall is the window's reveal and
sill, which the classic draws with the item (`ANIMATING15`, slot 444, items 173 and 174 in
room 146, a `DUMMY` the art carries, 262 triangles in each item's box) over the sniper
rooms' faces, and which the stand rule leaves out because a room drawn classic keeps no
art on its faces; room 21's faces there wear tile 2550 of page 5, black and clear.

**How.** The classic face is see-through when its effects word has bit 0 or its texture's
draw type is 2; the item path adds it (`output.cpp`, `phd_PutPolygons`; `polyinsert.cpp`,
case 2: ONE / ONE, no depth write). The `.TRM` says which of its triangles are that glass:
material 14 in the alpha run. A node gates the part, so a material 14 run on a node the
classic draws solid stays as it was. No `.TRM` of either installation's `ITEM` folders
(1,425 files, 24 with a glass run) has a glass and another alpha run triangle on one page
and node, so splitting the ranges on the glass changes no model: the model build's hash is
the same as before. The classic adds one face at a pixel and the classic is the measure:
(1) two glass triangles of a node face against each other when their normals stand more
than 135 degrees apart, halfway between the two sides of one pane and two faces at a box's
corner (over the 14 bindings every partner meets at exactly 180, except RICH1's
`DOOR_TYPE2`, from 99 to 173); a range of glass every triangle of which has such a partner
is drawn one-sided, the side turned away from the camera culled as the classic culls it
(`D3DCULL_CCW`, `HD_MODEL_CULL_BACK`; `D3DCULL_CW` under a matrix with a negative
determinant); a range with one triangle that has none stays two-sided, so no range is cut
and a single pane is seen from both sides, as RICH1's oval doors' are. (2) An additive run
triangle on a glass node whose three corners have a glass triangle's texture coordinates,
each within a 32nd of that triangle's longest edge, on the same page, is the glass again
and is left out while its node draws glass; the cabinet's copies lie one unit behind its
pane (a 319th of the edge), and its pane and sheet, 11 units apart, stay two surfaces. (3)
The part's `param[1]`, where it lies in (0, 1), weighs the glass of a one-sided range -
the weight the room art's additive pass already gives its material (`MaterialAddWeight`):
0.125 on the JOBY doors, 0.1 on RICH1's `DOOR_TYPE7`, RICH3's door and the title's two, 1
on RICH2's cabinet - through `D3DRS_BLENDFACTOR`; a two-sided range is a single sheet with
nothing stacked on it and is added as the page's alpha weighs it. (4) The classic's band
as a ceiling (`HDGlassBandFactor`, the top of the glass's band held to the top of the
classic's) is 1 on all 14 bindings once (1) to (3) are in, so the object path, which holds
no page's texels, applies none. The cabinet now adds about 54 at full light, inside the
classic's band (40.2 to 109.2), and RICH1's eight doors are drawn exactly as after the
first rule. The glass is drawn in the glows' bracket because it writes no depth, and the
shadow's cast and receive draws leave it out, as they leave the glows. The pocket: a
slot's animations run from its first to the next object's first, and the walk keeps to
that run; so bounded it takes slots 304 and 306 and nothing else, over the fifteen levels
and the randomized data.

**Decisions.** The classic's blend and not the room glass's: the room art draws its
unsplit glass with the page's alpha against one minus it, and drawn so the cabinet's pane
(alpha 0.8) stayed an opaque teal; added as the classic adds, the bottles behind it show.
The opacity goes into the blend state (`D3DRS_BLENDFACTOR`, the source weighed by it,
rounded to 255 steps) and not into a shader constant, so the model shader and its two
`.inc` stay byte for byte and the shadow draws need nothing; the step puts the blend
factor back whenever it wrote it, and a card without `D3DPBLENDCAPS_BLENDFACTOR` adds the
glass whole, the log's `factor=` saying 1. The sides are a range's own, not a triangle's,
so every model's ranges, draw calls and build hash stay; the copies are a range of their
own in the additive run. The opacity is put on the one-sided glass only: weighed on every
range, RICH1's `DOOR_TYPE2` pane went darker over the oval door, and RICH1's doors were to
stay as they were. The opacity does not go below the classic's band: a reference picture
shows less than the classic adds, but no data of the level or the model gives a smaller
weight for the cabinet (its `param[1]` is 1), and holding the opacity to the band from
below would need the glass's texels per range, which the object path does not hold (the
page cache keeps an alpha range per page, `HDPageCacheSlotAlphaMin`, no colour). No
per-face gate by the texture's alpha: on the cabinet it would draw the inward sheet solid
over the whole door. No number of a room, a level or a slot is in the rules. JOBY2's
window is left to the stand rule's files.

**Commits.** `6203c859` (comparison base), `ae1f4ff9` (the glass), `dd23825f` (the
pocket's bound), `20c0d5dd` (the tools and ModernTest), `0e11c297` (comparison base),
`13207d95` (glass added once, one-sided), `4a82ef1b` (tools and ModernTest), `c6b039cd`
(the records), `620ee117` (opacity on one-sided glass), `62e08c2c` (ModelProbe band,
ModernTest checks)

### HD models for the pickups: the EXTRA prefix, a mod's own inventory model, and lying on the floor
2026-09-08 - 2026-09-15

**What.** `bind_against` (`specific/hd/hd_bind.cpp`) has a generic third binding step.
After the level's `.MAP` and the hand table, and before a slot falls back to its own bare
name, it tries `EXTRA5_<slot>`, then `EXTRA_<slot>`, then `EXTRA4_<slot>`, each against
`5\ITEM` and then `4\ITEM`, `<slot>` being the engine's own symbol concatenated
case-insensitively. Twenty-four of the 471 slot names resolve this way and 23 of those are
loaded by at least one shipped level: the pistols, the uzi, the shotgun, the HK, the
grapple and its bolt, both medipacks, the lasersight, the binoculars, the flare in both
forms, the crowbar, the burning torch, the two shell casings, the Timex-TMX and the
crossbow ammunition. The hand table is asked first and a line may name levels: a third
field lists level stems, space separated, case-insensitive, 0 meaning every level -
`BINOCULARS_ITEM` -> `EXTRA5_BINOCULARS_ITEM_RICH` in RICH1, RICH2 and RICH3, and
`HK_ITEM` -> `EXTRA5_HK_ITEM_RICH2` in RICH2. A slot for which a mod ships a
`<BASE>_OPTION` model, and for which no mod ships an `EXTRA_<BASE>_ITEM` of any prefix,
draws that model fitted into the slot's frame, on the ring, in the corner display and on
the floor. And every pickup-family slot that came out HD is measured at level build: the
lowest of the HD model's drawn vertices against the lowest vertex of the classic mesh it
replaces, both in the animation frame the level really draws the item in; deeper by more
than half a unit and the model is lifted by exactly that difference, once, per slot,
straight up in the world, never scaled, turned or moved sideways. Over the fifteen shipped
levels the lift moves twelve slot/model pairs, the largest RICH3's `CROSSBOW_AMMO1_ITEM`
by **126.6 units**; everything else without a mod moves by 7 units or less (`COMPASS_ITEM`
6.9, `CROWBAR_ITEM` 6.2, `LASERSIGHT_ITEM` 4.2, `BURNING_TORCH_ITEM` and
`PISTOLS_AMMO_ITEM` 2.9, `UZI_ITEM` 1.6, `UZI_AMMO_ITEM` 1.5, `REVOLVER_ITEM` 1.1,
`FLARE_ITEM` 1.0), and with a mod's fitted Uzis on the floor `UZI_ITEM` lifts 19.2 and its
ammunition 6.8.

**Why.** A hand-written line per pickup was the alternative and the names need none:
`5\ITEM` carries 16 `EXTRA5_*` models and `4\ITEM` 52 (23 `EXTRA_*`, 29 `EXTRA4_*`), with
the slot names' own underscores intact. The hand table must win, because the generic rule
has no notion of the other spelling: it resolves `REVOLVER_ITEM` to
`EXTRA5_REVOLVER_ITEM`, Tomb Raider IV's six-shooter, and never reaches the Desert Eagle
variant. Level-bound lines exist because two slots carry a different object in the VCI
levels and no `.MAP` names either: `BINOCULARS_ITEM` is renamed to the headset there
(`game/newinv2.cpp`, `TXT_Headset`) and its model is a name no prefix can build, and
RICH2's HK is the scripted second weapon whose inventory angles `newinv2.cpp` rewrites for
`LVL5_ESCAPE_WITH_THE_IRIS`, so the generic HD HK came out visibly mis-rotated in that
level alone. The I-III Remaster draws the inventory out of `<BASE>_OPTION` models and
IV-VI out of `EXTRA_<BASE>_ITEM`, so a mod written for I-III carries the OPTION names and
nothing looked for them; a mod that brings the IV-VI name has said which convention it
means and wins. An HD replacement model has its own depth, and one that reaches deeper
than the mesh it replaces stands partly in the ground: RICH3 has no Tomb Raider V model
for the grappling gun's ammunition, so the binder's last resort takes
`4/ITEM/EXTRA4_CROSSBOW_AMMO1_ITEM.TRM`, an upright quiver 203 units tall of which 62 per
cent stood below the ground line on three real items. The reference is the level's own
classic mesh and not y = 0, because an item is drawn at its animation frame's own offset
and those offsets are large (ANDREA3's `PISTOLS_ITEM` mesh has its deepest point 59 units
below its node, its `CROWBAR_ITEM` one unit above). That the mesh's deepest point IS the
floor is the engine's own placement: `InitialisePickup` puts a pickup down with
`item->pos.y_pos -= bounds[3]` (`game/init.cpp:489-490`) for OCB 0, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 11 and
`GetBoundsAccurate` hands it the animation frame's own box; walking two levels' `.TRC` for
every object between slots 240 and 360, that stored box bottom equals the classic mesh's
deepest point plus the frame's y offset row for row. Stated against the mesh, the rule
needs no case for a pedestal or a wall place (OCB 2/9), which move the item and take both
meshes with them. The half-unit tolerance - half a millimetre at 1024 units to a metre -
is for float rounding on a mesh whose coordinates are SHORTs; the installation's own files
are lifted like any other, six of the eighteen pickup models ANDREA3 loads reaching below
the mesh they replace.

**How.** The trial order is checked exactly as `find_model` (`specific/hd/hd_model.cpp`)
checks a plain name. Two kinds of slot never reach it: Lara's own composite
(`LARA`..`HAIR`), whose branch returns first, and a named `extra_excluded` table holding
`GUN_FLASH` and the twelve pure light, particle and mist slots grouped beside it in
`game/objects.h` (`SMOKE_EMITTER_WHITE`, `SMOKE_EMITTER_BLACK`, `STEAM_EMITTER`,
`EARTHQUAKE`, `BUBBLES`, `WATERFALLMIST`, `COLOURED_LIGHT`, `BLINKING_LIGHT`,
`PULSE_LIGHT`, `STROBE_LIGHT`, `ELECTRICAL_LIGHT`, `LENS_FLARE`); `GUNSHELL`,
`SHOTGUNSHELL`, `FLARE_ITEM` and `CROSSBOW_BOLT` stay in the pool but are drawn outside
any `HDObjectBegin`/`HDObjectEnd` bracket, so a model bound to them costs a vertex buffer
and no page. The answer is cached per slot (`g_alt_cache`, `std::map<int, AltAnswer>`) so
the pointer `HDBindSlot`/`HDBindDonorSlot` return outlives the call, which matters because
`HDObjectLevelBuild`'s donor pass resolves every donor slot's name first and reads them
all back later. Both map loaders remember the level stem (`HDMapLoadForLevel` as given,
`HDMapLoad` from the file name, whether or not the file exists), a donor's bind hands in
the donor's stem, `HDMapFree` forgets it and `HDMapLevel()` reports it; a hand-table line
for another level is skipped and the slot goes on to the generic rule. The skeleton test
is the safety net and needed no new code: `COMPASS_ITEM` resolves to a two-part model but
in 13 of the 15 levels the classic slot's mesh tree has one node, so the model is refused
(`SKELETON: names node 1 of 1`) and only `RICHCUT2` draws it. `HDBindModOption`
(`hd_bind.cpp`/`.h`) derives the OPTION name the way the third rule derives the EXTRA
names; a file out of another game is fitted by `HDModelRingFit` and
`HDModelRingFitOverflow` (`hd_model.cpp`, both out of one `sort_axes`): centred on its own
centre, the principal axes of its vertex cloud sent onto the target's, scaled by the ratio
of the two longest extents, drawn rigidly on the root node with the correction in front of
the engine's own matrix so that the turn reaches the normals. A bounding box cannot do
this - one mod's `UZI_OPTION` is a pair of guns whose box, 147 x 253 x 159, reads like one
tall gun standing up, and matching boxes laid the pair flat; the two files measure 256 x
236 x 42 (flat along -y) for the vanilla item against 242 x 240 x 132 (flat along -x) for
the mod's, and sending the k-th axis onto the k-th lays the pair into the plane the
vanilla item lies in, the overflow figure falling from 3.73x to 3.36x for that Uzi and
1.25x to 1.00x for its ammunition. An eigenvector has no sign, so each axis points to the
side on which the cloud reaches further from its centre of mass and the third is the cross
product of the other two, which means the frame can rotate and never mirror. Fitting the
whole model inside the target's box is refused: a vanilla Uzi pickup is 41 units thick and
that rule would scale an upright gun to a sixth. The in-plane angle is deterministic but
not meaningful - the plane is decided by a factor of nearly six (132.3 against 239.5, 41.6
against 235.7) while the two axes inside it stand 242.3 against 239.5, a gap of 1.2 per
cent. The floor lift: the family is `HDSlotIsPickup` (`hd_bind.cpp`), a slot whose name
ends in `_ITEM`, so the generic prefix and the hand table's names are treated alike; the
frame is `HDFramePose` (`hd_model.cpp`), `DrawAnimatingItem`'s walk with the frame's
rotations in, twelve floats a node, once per slot at level build, the frame's OFFSET and
the item's own rotation left out because `InitialiseItem` zeroes `x_rot` and `z_rot`
(`game/items.cpp:201-202`) and the one place that tilts a pickup puts all three back
before anything is drawn (`PickUpCollision`, `game/pickup.cpp:789-793, 1124-1126`), the
two that tilt in flight zeroing the angles as the thing comes to rest (`FlareControl`,
`game/laraflar.cpp:31-37`; `FlameTorchControl`, `game/flmtorch.cpp:286-287`). Both sides
sweep VERTICES and not boxes - the classic side the mesh's own `aVtx` that
`ProcessMeshData` filled, the HD side keeping the node each vertex rides on so the bind
fold `set_joint` does per node can be undone per point (`HDModelSlot::keepPoints` on every
pickup model, given back by `HDModelReleasePoints` before the first frame; 13 bytes a
vertex, 746 KB for ANDREA3 with four mods, 241 KB for the installation's files alone).
`HDModelFloorLift` is one implementation for the plain and the fitted case, engine and
tool, and the lift is added in view space in the object path, so world up is worked out
once per camera; the ring and the corner display are untouched by it. `first_frame_of`
(`hd_object.cpp`) reads `anims[item->anim_number].frame_ptr` at `frame_number ==
frame_base` (`GetFrames`, `game/draw.cpp:2443-2467`) and not `objects[slot].frame_base`,
and logs a difference; over the fifteen `.TRC` files this changes nothing, 1,748 of 1,791
objects carrying their animation's own frame offset and the other 43 taking the rest-pose
fallback. The measure runs at level build only (ANDREA3's eighteen pickup models with four
mods are 57,378 vertices in well under a millisecond), nothing of it in a frame; the
`_OPTION` lookup runs once per loaded slot at level build and has its own line, `HDLOG
level=<L> ring asked= of= found= ms=` (asking the OPTION name before the three EXTRA
prefixes took one level's 130 slots with nine mods from 24.6 ms to 7.7 ms, 0.11 ms with no
`Mods` folder). Seams behind `-log`: one line per slot `HDLOG bind slot=<n> name=<sym>
via=<map|hand|donor|prefix5|prefix|prefix4|classic> model=<file> nodes=<trm>/<classic>`
and a level summary `HDLOG bind total=N map=N hand=N donor=N prefix=N classic=N`; `HDLOG
level=.. pickup floor slot=.. name=.. model=.. lowest point N above|under the classic
mesh's - lifted by N units|not lifted`, its fitted twin `ring floor slot=.. takes the
fitted <model> on the floor, lifted by N units`, the drawn-frame line, a `not measured:
..` line, and `item slot=.. name=.. model=.. draws nothing: its geometry sits on node mask
N and this item shows N`. Tools: `MapProbe` and `ModelProbe` compile against the new
`HDBindSlot`/`HDBindDonorSlot` signature (an added `installRoot`, since the third rule
needs a disk to ask, and an added `HDBindVia` output), `ModelProbe -all` gained a `via`
column and a bind-count summary, and `-floor`, `-nofloorlift`, `-floorcheck`,
`-inventory`, `-invrot <x> <y> <z>` and `-rigid` draw and tabulate the rest. The classic
path is untouched: every line is reached only from `HDObjectLevelBuild`, which runs only
from `HDLevelBuild`, which returns at `if (!HDEnabled() || !g_stem[0]) return;`. Files:
`specific/hd/hd_bind.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_model.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_object.cpp`, `hd_classic.cpp`,
`hd_lara.cpp`/`.h`, `game/newinv2.cpp`, `game/larafire.cpp`, `game/laramisc.cpp`,
`game/objects.h`, `game/setup.cpp`, `game/tomb4fx.cpp`, `game/init.cpp`, `game/items.cpp`,
`game/draw.cpp`, `game/pickup.cpp`, `game/laraflar.cpp`, `game/flmtorch.cpp`,
`docs/Engine-Manual.md`, `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp`, `MapProbe.cpp`,
`SfxProbe.cpp`, `Preparation/Tools/README.md`.

**Decisions.** The lift is per slot, not per item: `InitialiseItem` gives `HK_ITEM`,
`HK_AMMO_ITEM`, `CROSSBOW_ITEM` and `REVOLVER_ITEM` `mesh_bits = 1`
(`game/items.cpp:222-225`) so they draw node 0 alone while both sides sweep every node -
one row differs by it (`REVOLVER_ITEM` in JOBY2 and JOBY5, 1.1 units) - and following it
would mean a lift per item.

**Commits.** `ed39081` (pickups bound by EXTRA prefix), `a0bfcad` (grappling gun in the
hand), `7d87cd2` (headset, RICH2's HK by level), `084e88d` (a mod's inventory model),
`e5e99cd` (inventory question made cheaper), `a594bc1` (ring fit reads the shape),
`0947713` (three numbers re-measured), `cfa31ed` (comment continuations), `7964b3c` (ring
fit's picture), `2850c54` (footstep mod needs no bank), `eab9e37` (classic reader closes
file), `b9c8798` (one floor rule), `a253f40` (floor passages rewritten), `b904973` (floor
picture reads), `d2dcc62` (floor rule in drawn frame), `0775caa` (whole campaign
measured), `8105425` (two sentences made exact), `0ab707d` (camera change reaches lifted
slots)

### The grappling gun in the hand, and the Desert Eagle in the revolver's slot
2026-09-06 - 2026-09-08

**What.** TR5's revolver slot draws the Desert Eagle - in hand, laser hand, holster,
pickup and ammunition - and the weapon `LARA_CROSSBOW_LASER` draws in the hand is the
grappling gun and not Tomb Raider IV's crossbow with a scope.

**Why.** TR5's revolver slot kept its Tomb Raider IV name and changed its weapon, exactly
as `CROSSBOW_ANIM` became the grappling gun, and the randomizer settles it outright by
copying JOBY2's slots 6, 12, 16, 347 and 348 into every level (`Randomizer.cpp`,
`kWeaponRules`), so a binding by name drew the six-shooter. The Remaster ships both guns
side by side in `4\ITEM` and they are different models - `HAND_BARE_REVOLVER` has a
cylinder and a 1703-vertex `HOLSTER_REVOLVER` on node 4, `HAND_BARE_DEAGLE` is the
slab-sided automatic with a 1270-vertex `HOLSTER_DEAGLE` on the same node - so the change
is a change of names and nothing else. No `.MAP` names `REVOLVER_ITEM` at all, so the
pickup slot fell through to its own name and found nothing. For the grapple:
`game/larafire.cpp` (`WeaponObject`) draws the gun in the hand from `LARA_CROSSBOW_LASER`
whenever `lara.crossbow_type_carried` carries `W_LASERSIGHT`, and in TR5 that bit is never
off - `game/newinv2.cpp`'s pickup of `CROSSBOW_ITEM` in
`LVL5_THIRTEENTH_FLOOR..LVL5_RED_ALERT` writes `W_PRESENT | W_LASERSIGHT | W_AMMO1`
outright, the weapons cheat does the same, `game/laramisc.cpp` does it at a level start,
and `combine_crossbow_lasersight`, the one function that clears it, is not reachable from
TR5's inventory. The Remaster ships `HAND_BARE_GRAPPLE` and `HAND_GLOVES_GRAPPLE` and no
grapple-with-sight model at all.

**How.** The hand table in `specific/hd/hd_bind.cpp` takes the DEAGLE files for hand,
laser hand and holster, binds `REVOLVER_ITEM` to `EXTRA5_REVOLVER_ITEM_JOBY` (the plain
`EXTRA5_REVOLVER_ITEM` is the six-shooter, seen in a ModelProbe picture) and the
ammunition to `EXTRA5_REVOLVER_AMMO_ITEM`. `specific/hd/hd_lara.cpp` (`kSlotRole`) maps
`LARA_CROSSBOW_LASER` to `HD_LARA_PART_HAND_GRAPPLE`; the part
`HD_LARA_PART_HAND_GRAPPLE_LASER` is gone from the enum (`hd_lara.h`), the part table, the
rank table and the worn-pairs table. The holster on the back, the pickup on the floor and
the laser dot (an effect of the engine, not a mesh) are drawn as before.

**Commits.** `0f83858` (Desert Eagle, holsters), `77db026` (faces, holster rig), `ed39081`
(pickups by EXTRA prefix), `a0bfcad` (grappling gun in hand), `7d87cd2` (headset, RICH2's
HK by level)

### The inventory ring and the pickup display in HD
2026-09-08 - 2026-09-09

**What.** The objects on the inventory ring and the little turning object in the corner
after a pickup are drawn from the Remaster's models, through the same HD seam the world
uses and not through a second render path. `HDInvBegin` / `HDInvNode` / `HDInvEnd`
(`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp`, declared in `hd_object.h`) sit at the four
`phd_PutPolygonsPickup` call sites in `game/newinv2.cpp`, and `InventoryActive` routes
between the two callers: the ring pushes its object onto the frame's HD list, the pickup
display draws its one object on the spot in a bracket of its own. An item with no HD
model, one whose skeleton the model does not fit, and every item with the HD path off
answers false and is drawn classically at the same four call sites, so the ring never has
a hole in it. On the ring, three slots stay classic in every campaign level -
`COMPASS_ITEM` and the two passport pages `PC_LOAD_INV_ITEM` and `PC_SAVE_INV_ITEM` - and
in RICH1 a fourth, `PUZZLE_HOLE8`, the keypad; the pickup display has no classic object in
any playable level.

**Why.** The seam was already there and drew nothing: `DrawInventoryItemMe` walks a mesh
tree exactly as `DrawAnimatingItem` does - a matrix per node, `item->mesh_bits` deciding
which node draws - and only the last step differs, while the inventory's own loop already
calls `S_InitialisePolyList` and `S_OutputPolyList`, which already call `HDFrameReset` and
`HDFrameDraw`. The classic ring projects each item about the item's own place on the
screen (`phd_PutPolygonsPickup` moves `f_centerx`/`f_centery` for the length of one mesh)
while the HD path builds one projection per frame about the screen centre, and that
difference had to be closed without touching the node matrices: `hd_model.hlsl` skins the
vertex normal through the very same `gJoints` matrices and renormalises, so a sheared node
matrix tilts and rescales every normal and the ring's one sun then lights an item by an
amount depending on where on the screen it stands - 93.61 mean brightness with no offset
against 64.15 to 108.87 at the ring's four places, 45 per cent apart on one screen. The
pickup display could not go on the frame's list at all: `S_DrawPickup`
(`specific/output.cpp`) is called from inside `S_OutputPolyList` after `HDFrameDraw` has
drawn this frame's list, so an item pushed there would suppress its own classic polygons
and be drawn by nobody. The display's light is not the ring's: `aTransformLightClipMesh`
has one line for a sun's strength, `if (!InventoryActive) val *= 0.75F; else val += val;`,
a factor of 2.667, so handing the display the ring's scale would have made it visibly
brighter than the classic display it replaces.

**How.** The offset lives in the projection: `kx = (X - Cx) / persp`, `ky = (Y - Cy) /
persp`, and since the projection divides by `vz`, anything added to `vx` in proportion to
`vz` survives as a constant pixel offset with the depth untouched. `HDModelOffCentre`
(`hd_model.cpp`) writes `_31 = kx * _11` and `_32 = ky * _22` into a copy of the frame's
projection for the length of one draw call and the node matrices reach the card as the
engine's own; a normal never goes through a projection, so the measurement reads 93.61 at
all four ring places over the identical 3,108 object pixels, and over 26 sample normals at
each of 24 ring places this road differs from the classic shading term by 4e-9 where the
shear road differs by up to 34.6 per cent. There is no scale term: `AlterFOV`
(`specific/3dmath.cpp`) computes `f_persp` from `phd_winheight * 320 / 240`, a 4:3 implied
width whatever the window is, and the HD projection is built from that very `f_persp`, so
the factor is one by construction - measured at 24 ring places at 640x480 and 1920x1080
the projected rectangle agrees to a worst 0.00013 pixels against a budget of 1, 519.33
pixels wide at 4:3 against 1168.50 at 16:9, exactly 1080/480; the display's eight places
at 1920x1080 and 2560x1440 agree to 0.00008 pixels, 987.76 against 1317.01, exactly
1440/1080. The light is the ring's own and nothing else: the level lighting is thrown away
and `phd_PutPolygonsPickup` puts up an ambient of 8/8/8 and ONE sun of the item's
`pcbright` - `0x202020` at the side, up to `0xA0A0A0` for the selected one, always
`0x7F7F7F` for the display (`S_DrawPickup` passes 0 and `DrawThreeDeeObject2D` turns 0
into that value) - along `(0, -50, -100)` normalised over `sqrt(12500)`, with `sunScale`
`pickup ? 0.75f : 2.0f`; the classic line reads the direction out of `D3DMView`, which is
the node's matrix, so what it computes is `dot(n_view, d)`, and in view space the
direction is simply `d`. No room cube, no point lights, no dynamics, no sheen. The item's
screen centre goes to `HDModelOffCentre` at draw time and never into its matrices, and
there is no animation, because the ring stands on frame 0 and never interpolates;
`INVOBJ::meshbits` reaches `HDModelDraw` as `nodeMask`, so a node the ring leaves out
draws nothing. Depth needed nothing: the classic ring goes through the ordinary sort list
with `drawtype` 0, which `HWR_DrawSortList` case 0 (`specific/polyinsert.cpp`) draws with
the depth write on, and both paths write `a - b/z` for the same point; the frozen backdrop
sits at `sz` 0.995, the far plane with `znear` 20 and `zfar` 20480. The fog bulbs are
taken off a ring frame (`hd_level.cpp`, `HDFrameDraw`), because `ActiveFogBulbs` holds
positions the game turned into view space for the last played frame while the ring draws
through an identity view; the distance fog stays. The display's bracket is
`HDFramePickupBegin`/`HDFramePickupEnd` (`hd_level.cpp`), which are
`HDRenderFrameBegin`/`HDRenderFrameEnd`, so there is one HD path and one list of device
states; the frame's list is untouched and `g_count` is not incremented, and
`HDRenderInFrame()` (`hd_render.cpp`) reports whether a bracket is already open, because
`HDRenderFrameBegin` refuses to nest silently. Its projection is read at the call -
`f_persp`, `f_centerx`, `f_centery`, `f_a`, `f_b` - rather than from
`HDFrameProjectionInfo`, because `AlterFOV` moves `f_persp` inside a frame whenever the
binoculars are up, and the classic display projects with `f_mpersp`, which is `f_persp` to
the bit. Its place is `X = phd_winwidth - GetFixedScale(80) + PickupX`, `Y =
phd_winheight - GetFixedScale(75)` plus `INVOBJ::yoff`, so the slide of `DrawPickups`
(`game/health.cpp`; `pu->life` 45, `PickupX` from `GetFixedScale(128)` to 0) comes for
free through `kx`; there is no alpha ramp on either path, and the display sits below the
frame's second depth clear and above `Fade()`. One deviation: `DrawInventoryItemMe` scales
the matrix non-uniformly for `PUZZLE_HOLE8` in keypad mode (1.5 / 1.0 / 0.25), and RICH2's
keypad is drawn HD, so that scale reaches the shader - the classic path computes `dot(M n,
d)` without renormalising and the shader must renormalise, so that one object shades
slightly differently. The material clock is sampled on ring frames but does not run:
`HDFrameDraw` no longer returns early on an inventory frame, so `FillFrameLighting` and
`AdvanceClock` execute, but the clock is the difference of `GlobalCounter`, stepped in
`ControlPhase`'s tick loop while `S_CallInventory2` blocks inside it, so every ring frame
adds zero; the title menu has no ring, `TitleOptions` (`game/gameflow.cpp`) being
`PrintString` over the title level. Sixty frames a second changes nothing here:
`HDObjectFrameReset` runs once per drawn frame, `GameFrameMinTicks()` holds the inventory
at thirty presents, and the display's spin is `(GnFrameCounter & 0x7F) << 9` with
`GnFrameCounter` stepped once per logic tick. Seams: `HDLOG ring items=N hd=N classic=N`
once per opening plus one line per object (`slot`, `name`, `model`, `nodes`, `mask`, view
`z`, `via`), and `HDLOG pickupdisplay level=<stem> slots=N hd=N classic=<list>` at build
time plus one line per object the first time it is shown. Tools: `ModelProbe -ringcheck`,
`-ring <x> <y>`, `-ringlight <bright>`, `-pickupcheck`; with the wider state list
`RoomProbe` uses, 0 of 58 watched device, sampler and texture stage states change across
the display's draw. Classic path untouched: `HDInvBegin` answers false at `if (!g_active
|| !tomb5.hd_objects)`, so the four call sites run the same calls with the same arguments,
`g_ring_frame` is set after that test, and `HDModelOffCentre` with `(0, 0)` returns before
it touches a register; `fps_mode` is not read. Files: `specific/hd/hd_object.cpp`/`.h`,
`hd_model.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_level.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_render.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_shader/hd_model.hlsl`,
`game/newinv2.cpp`, `game/health.cpp`, `game/pickup.cpp`, `specific/output.cpp`,
`specific/polyinsert.cpp`, `specific/3dmath.cpp`,

### The seam for Lara: the HD composite drawn by the engine
2026-09-05 - 2026-09-13

**What.** `DrawLara` hands its drawing variants over to the HD composite. `DrawLara__1`
(everything but the catsuit and the diving suit) and `DrawLara__4` (the catsuit) leave the
function after `CalculateObjectLightingLara()`, popping the matrix they pushed and
restoring the clipping window as their own tail does; everything they would have drawn -
the skinned body, the fourteen seam pieces from `LARA_SKIN_JOINTS`, `DrawHair`, the two
thigh holsters and the weapon on the back - is what the composite replaces. `DrawLara__5`
(the diving suit) skips only its skin loop and still draws the two `LARA_EXTRA_MESH1`
thrusters; `DrawLara__6` (the skeleton cheat) is untouched. Her parts go on the object
path's own frame list, in the classic order, and she has no registry value of her own:
`hd_objects` covers her. What one of the hands holds is not drawn a second time on the
thigh or on the back. No outfit wears gloves: `takes_gloves` answers false for every
outfit, so no `HAND_GLOVES_*` model is ever named, while the wardrobe's `gloves` flag,
`outfit.txt`'s `gloves=` line and `kPart`'s gloves column are still parsed, printed and
logged. The `.TRM` reader folds mirrored hand weights back onto the near hand. The braid's
root sits at the hair knot while the HD wardrobe draws, it is pushed out of a backpack
box, and each drawn bone is rolled about its own axis. Known losses, named: the catsuit's
environment-map sheen, the diving suit's two classic thrusters, and the muzzle flash, gun
shells and flare in flight, which are drawn by their own routines outside `DrawLara`. A
talking head is not reproduced as a mesh swap: the engine records which of the four
speech-head slots it has put on Lara's neck and draws the ordinary head, whose spoken
lines come from the installation's track files (see *The cutscene faces speak: their lips
follow the Remaster's track files*).

**Why.** The matrices are the engine's own so that animation, frame interpolation and
`gar_RotYXZsuperpack` stay what the game computed this frame. `mesh_bits` are read for
`DrawLara__1`, which reads them, and not for the two variants that do not, because a seam
that read them where the classic path does not would make the catsuit disappear in the
very cutscenes that hide the classic joints. The ambient is per node because a body half
in the water is lit by two rooms at once and the classic path switches per node; the hands
are identified by pointer comparison because the engine keeps them in `lara.mesh_ptrs` as
pointers and not as slot numbers, and a hand it cannot place is drawn as the rest hand.
The braid is built from the base of the matrix stack and not from `aW2VMx`, because
`phd_GenerateW2V` puts the poison shake on the stack's base and leaves `aW2VMx` alone. The
mirror needs no special handling: TR5 reflects Lara by moving her - `game/mirror.cpp`
negates `x_rot` and `y_rot`, adds half a turn to `z_rot` and `CalcLaraMatrices(2)` scales
the matrix by -1 on all three axes (`ScaleCurrentMatrix`, `game/delstuff.cpp`), a
determinant of -1, so every winding flips and the classic engine turns its own software
back-face test round with `SetCullCW`/`SetCullCCW`; the HD path draws double sided
(`D3DCULL_NONE`), so a flipped winding is invisible to it, and the hair is mirrored in
world space by the same function. The braid's root had to move because the classic braid
hides the distance between root and skull by SKINNING - `DrawHair` draws meshes 1, 3 and 5
rigidly and 0, 2 and 4 as connectors stitched out of stashed vertices - while an HD link
is rigid: `game/hair.cpp` walks to the head bone and translates by (-4, -4, -48), and
measured on the skull (one mesh for all eight bodies, head joint at 1/-247/-12, root at
-3/-251/-60, nearest skull vertex at -0.7/-251.2/-43.3) the root sits 16.8 units away in
+z while `HAIR_OG`'s link 0 reaches only 1.7 units back, leaving 15.2 units open. The five
spheres `HairControl` pushes the braid out of are all CLASSIC meshes - hips, torso, head,
the two upper arms - and an HD outfit's pack stands 92 units behind the torso joint, the
same slab in all seven braided outfits (centre 1/-132/-61, radius 71 to 83, y -197..-68, z
-92..-30). The roll exists because `game/hair.cpp` gives link n-1 the spherical angles of
the vector to link n out of differences of LONGS: hanging straight down, `dy` is the whole
bone, 56, while `dx` and `dz` are single digits, so the yaw is the rounding of two small
integers and one unit of `dx` swings it ninety degrees; TR5 survives that with three rigid
meshes and three skinned connectors and `GetCorrectStashPoints`, a rigid plait of six
bones does not. Over ANDREA2's own animation table at 110 frames apiece, the standing
animation 103 moves the tip less than two units on every frame and yet turns a bone by up
to 180 degrees on 14 of them, while run and walk turn by at most 7 - the fault is in the
drawing and not the physics, and the same table with the pack spheres out, damped or
thinner moves the tip identically to two decimals. Root and pack must be changed in both
of `HairControl`'s frame branches: a root that differs between them jumps between z -48
and z -33 from frame to frame, and since `hairs[0][0]` seeds the chain and every link's
velocity is how far it moved since the last frame, that feeds the braid 15 units of
velocity for ever. The gloves are off so that the hands are uniform across outfits and
levels. The mirror fold exists because a `HAND_` file is modelled once and mirrored, and
an exporter that mirrors geometry without bone names leaves vertices of one hand carrying
weight on the other: nothing shows in the bind pose, and an animation that moves the hands
apart drags them into the gap as a sheet of skin out of the wrist. A talking head is a
MESH SWAP inside the normal draw (`handle_lara_chatting` writes `lara.mesh_ptrs[LM_HEAD]`
from one of the four `LARA_SPEECH_HEAD1..4` slots; `handle_actor_chatting` sets the node's
bit in `cutseq_meshswapbits` and writes an `ACTOR*_SPEECH_HEAD*` mesh), and both ends are
meshes the HD path has not got: no `.MAP` names the six speech-head slots and neither
`4\ITEM` nor `5\ITEM` ships a `LARA_SPEECH_HEAD1.TRM`. What the installation ships instead
is one rigged head per speaker plus a `.TRL` file per spoken line
(`LARA_HEAD_96.TRL`..`LARA_HEAD_135.TRL`, `ADMIRAL_HEAD_113.TRL`, `PIERRE_HEAD_108.TRL`,
2.6 MiB apiece); a mouth movement of its own would be an invented look.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp`/`.h` is the engine-side half that reads TR5's state
and turns it into arguments for `hd_lara` and `hd_model`; `hd_lara.cpp` stays engine-free.
Three single `if`s in `specific/drawlara.cpp`, one per variant, directly after
`CalculateObjectLightingLara()`. `lara_matrices` already holds fifteen 3x4 view-space
matrices built this frame by `CalcLaraMatrices`, in `LMX_` order, and one table turns them
into mesh-tree `LM_` nodes - the whole difference is the head, matrix 8 against node 14.
Per frame the parts come from state `DrawLara` already holds: `LHolster`, `lara.holster`
and `lara.back_gun` are slot numbers; the hands are found by comparing `lara.mesh_ptrs`
against `meshes[objects[s].mesh_index + 2 * LM_xHAND]` over Lara's own loaded slots, the
same test `game/larafire.cpp` makes for the flare, at most a dozen comparisons twice a
frame. When the two hands differ - the flare, the torch, the crowbar - both hand models
are drawn and each masked to its own arm through `hd_model`'s `mesh_bits` argument (8, 9,
10 right; 11, 12, 13 left); when they agree it is one draw with every node, and the same
split answers the two holster slots. The held-item rule is one table and one lookup a
frame in `HDLaraFrameParts` (`hd_lara.cpp`) rather than a reach into the engine's weapon
state machine, because the engine's three variables are bookkeeping and not fact -
`draw_pistol_meshes` (`game/lara2gun.cpp`) clears `lara.holster` for every weapon and
`LHolster` for all but the revolver, `draw_shotgun_meshes` (`game/lara1gun.cpp`) clears
`lara.back_gun` and neither holster, and `InitialiseNewWeapon` (`game/larafire.cpp`) sends
the revolver down the second path - so a weapon could be drawn in the hand and in the
holster at once. The braid needs all six link matrices where TR5 builds only 1, 3 and 5;
the angles for the other three are already written by `HairControl` for every one of
`hairs[0][0..5]`, so all six are built the same way the rigid ones are, with
`phd_TranslateAbs`, `phd_RotY`, `phd_RotX`. `HD_LARA_BRAID_ROOT_Z_HD` is -33 against the
classic `HD_LARA_BRAID_ROOT_Z` -48 (`hd_lara.h`), applied in `HairControl` and only while
the HD wardrobe draws, read from one flag once per frame and applied in BOTH frame
branches; with the HD path off `HairControl` is the function it was. The pack is
`HdPackFrame`/`HdPackPush` in `game/hair.cpp`, a BOX in the torso node's own frame serving
all seven adult bodies (x -60..62, y -197..-68, z -92..-30, the coat tail left to the
torso sphere), pushed out along whichever of the six faces is nearest with the rear face
preferred (a divisor of 2 on its own depth) and a margin per moving point of the plait's
own measured radius, 18, 18, 15, 13, 11 and 9. Simulated sixty steps in the bind pose the
chain comes to rest at zero movement from either root, the deepest a link stands inside
the pack falls from 38 units with spheres to 7 with the box, and under her own animations
the tip never moves more than 14 units in a frame. The roll is `HDLaraBraidRollStep` /
`HDLaraBraidRolls` (`hd_laradraw.cpp`/`.h`): a `phd_RotZ` after `phd_RotY` and `phd_RotX`
in `braid_matrices`, which costs nothing because the drawn bone's own +z is the link
direction. ONE reference serves all six bones and it is the azimuth of the WHOLE braid,
root to tip, six bones long where a link is one and ten to thirty times better
conditioned; it is HELD while even that is noise - below 16 units of horizontal span it
does not move, above 48 it follows completely, in between part of the way - so no
threshold is crossed in one frame. Over the three ANDREA2 animations its worst one-frame
turn is 0 standing, 3 running, 1 walking, against 180/7/7 for the raw yaw and 45/3/1 for
an unheld whole-chain azimuth; it is advanced from `HairControl`, the one place per frame
where the chain is new, because the draw may run twice (the mirror) or not at all (first
person). Light goes through `HDObjectLights` in view space, twelve lights, the same
conversion the object path uses; `InitObjectLighting` runs once with `bLaraUnderWater`
forced dry, answering `LaraNodeAmbient[0]`, and the wet answer is read out of
`LaraNodeAmbient[1]`, because a second call would push every dynamic light onto the list
twice. Two new calls in `hd_object.h` (`HDObjectLights`, `HDObjectPush`) and its bind-pose
walk `HDObjectBindPose` put her parts on the one frame list. `HairControl` is called from
`game/control.cpp` in the game loop and not from `DrawLara`, so the braid's simulation
runs on while it is not drawn. `HDTrmFoldMirrored` (`specific/hd/hd_trm.cpp`, counters and
layout note in `hd_trm.h`) moves the far side's weight onto that bone's counterpart on the
near side, decided by the vertex's majority side with the sign of its own `x` as the
tie-break, and renormalises the three weights to 255; only weights above
`HD_LARA_HAND_FOLD_BAR` (125 per mille, `hd_lara.h`, read at `HDLaraPlan`) are folded, so
files whose crossed weight is exporter rounding come out of the reader byte for byte. The
bar is a measurement: over all 101 hand files - the install's 94 (`4\ITEM` holds thirty
`HAND_BARE_`, thirty `HAND_GLOVES_`, thirty `HAND_XRAY_` and four `HANDS_BARE_`; games 5
and 6 have none) and seven from three gun mods - there are 6,723 crossed vertices whose
share on the far hand is one of exactly two things: 4 per mille for 6,677 of them (one
weight unit of 255, the exporter's rounding; 5,884 of these are the install's own out of
its 485,491 hand vertices) and 371 to 500 per mille for 46, all in one mod's
`HAND_BARE_PISTOL`, four of them exactly half. Nothing lies between, so an eighth sits in
a total gap, 31 times the largest share the Remaster's own files carry and a third of the
smallest a mod's do; folding below it would move the seven affected hand parts by at most
0.56 units with both forearms turned 50 degrees out, 0.84 with the upper arms straight
out, 0.97 with both, and 2.00 for one part in a contortion no animation reaches, while the
mod's 46 vertices move up to 65.49 units (mean 51.27). Of the 6,723 crossed vertices 6,719
have a majority and on every one the majority side and the sign of `x` agree; the four
without are the ties the rule exists for. In first person the head node, the separate
`LARA_HEAD` and the braid are dropped, which is what the classic path drops; the classic
reason for hiding the head through the draw rather than through `mesh_bits` - the
neighbours pull their rim points out of the head mesh's stash - does not apply, because an
HD model has no stash. `speech_head_slot()` (`hd_laradraw.cpp`) says which of the four
slots the engine has just put on her neck and the frame log carries it as `speechhead=`.
Seams with `-log`: two lines per level on the first HD Lara frame, `HDLOG laracheck` (each
of the fifteen joint origins on the screen twice, the classic transform against the matrix
the card is handed) and `HDLOG braidcheck` (each braid link's own frame stepped one bone
along, measuring how far it misses the next link); one `HAIRLOG` line per braid per frame
with the root the frame really used, the room position of the root, how many spheres it
tested, `packhits`, whether the HD wardrobe is drawing, where the tip ended up,
`rootstep`, `tipstep`, `dyaw` (the worst one-frame change of any link's raw yaw, in
degrees) and `droll` (the same after the roll, `-1` for the classic braid) - a line on
which the root or the sphere count changes is the two-branch fault back again; `HDLOG ...
lara part=` carries `held=` and `pagesheen=` per part, and the `.TRM` fold counters
`crossed`, `folded` and `tied`. `ModelProbe -laracheck` runs the joint and chain checks
without the game: 0.00000 pixels over all fifteen joints and a worst chain gap of 0.00006
units over the five braid joints; `-firstperson`, `-mirror`, `-braid`, `-braidsim`,
`-braidanim`, `-braidrest`, `-classicroot`, `-handfold`, `-nofold`, `-nohandmix`,
`-onlypart`, `-nodes`, `-meshbits`, `-handlight`, `-oldskin`, `-nosheen`, `-look head`,
`-look wrist` draw and measure the rest, `-handfold` skinning every vertex twice through
the same node matrices the card is given and calling the engine's own fold rather than a
copy, `-braidanim` reading the level's own animation table and rebuilding all eight
collision spheres and the braid root once per game frame with a floor clamp. `hd_model`
exports `HDModelFindFile` so a tool asks the engine's own model search instead of keeping
a copy. Files: `specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_lara.cpp`/`.h`,
`hd_object.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_model.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_trm.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_wardrobe.cpp`/`.h`,
`hd_pagecache.cpp`/`.h`, `specific/drawlara.cpp`, `game/hair.cpp`, `game/control.cpp`,
`game/larafire.cpp`, `game/mirror.cpp`, `game/delstuff.cpp`, `game/draw.cpp`,
`tomb5.vcxproj`, `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp`, `README.md`,
`docs/Engine-Manual.md`.
