### First person: Lara's head and neck cut away, and the lid that closes the opening
2026-09-06 - 2026-09-08

**What.** In first person the HD path removes Lara's head and neck and closes the opening
with a lid of her own skin. The cut is a BONE WEIGHT and not a shape in space: `ModelVS`
sums the vertex's share of the head node out of the three bones the skinning already walks
and `ModelPS` clips per pixel on the interpolated value, so every fragment the head node
owns at least `HD_LARA_HEAD_CUT_WEIGHT` (0.15) of is discarded. Collars stay: the Russia
jacket, the parka and the VCI catsuit's collar ring all lie below the cut and are drawn.
The lid is `HD_LARA_PART_NECK_CAP`, a two-ring triangle fan built over the RIM of the
hole - the vertices that miss the threshold but share a triangle with one that reaches it.
Every rim vertex is copied whole (position, three bones, three weights, texture
coordinate), and every spoke of the fan wears the texel of the rim vertex it hangs from
all the way in, so the fan's middle is one copy per spoke rather than one shared vertex;
it wears the SKIN material, its normal points head-ward, and it is drawn with no cut of
its own, no cull and its own node mask, because first person clears the head node from the
body's mask and the lid rides on that node. Lara's body is drawn once: the HD path has one
depth rule, `D3DCMP_LESSEQUAL`.

**Why.** The near cut of the first person view takes the neck stump off a body that is a
hollow shell and culls back faces, so one looks clean through her. A neck vertex is
skinned to two nodes at once - the one under the chin is 55 per cent torso and 45 per cent
head - so a shape defined in the bind pose falls on different skin in every animation: a
sphere about the eye takes a bite out of the chest, a cylinder with a node mask leaves the
collar standing and takes half the neck with the mask, and a plane carried by the head
node tilts with the head and runs through the chest at forty degrees of pitch. The head
node's share of a vertex is the one quantity no animation moves. The threshold is measured
over the eight wardrobe bodies (`ModelProbe -headw`): any weight at all takes 9,622
vertices on the four Tomb Raider III bodies, which carry a whisper of head weight down to
the feet, against the 6,729 that are really the head; 0.50 leaves the highest surviving
vertex inside a neck's radius 1.6 units above the head joint, a visible ring of neck
around the camera; between 0.05 and 0.35 all eight bodies read the same 24.5 units for the
widest thing taken below the chin, which is the neck's own radius and no collar. The lid's
edge is skinned by the same sum over the same joints as the skin it meets, so the two land
on the same point in every pose and no animation can open a gap. The per-spoke texel
prevents a dark point with a cone running into it: on the game 5 pages the neck is one
column six texels wide, so any texel inside it is skin, but on page 8201 it is two
separate bands (v 154..158 and v 198..202) and a single averaged middle texel makes every
triangle sweep the gap between them. The texel itself is taken from the page whose vertex
column runs the whole height of the neck - a throat runs from the head joint to the
shoulders, while a collar, a zip and a hairline are bands across it - and at the CENTROID
of the biggest triangle on that page, which is inside the paint by construction where a
real vertex sits on the edge of its texture island.

**How.** `HD_LARA_HEAD_CUT_WEIGHT` 0.15 in `specific/hd/hd_lara.h`; `HDLaraHeadCut` and
`build_neck_cap` (over `HDModelSlot::synth`) in `hd_lara.cpp`; `hd_laradraw.cpp` passes
node and threshold to `HDModelNeckCut` with nothing built per frame; `hd_model.cpp` writes
them to shader constant c162; the cut is in `hd_shader/hd_model.hlsl` (`ModelVS` adds the
head node's weight, `ModelPS` clips) with the generated `hd_model_vs.inc` and
`hd_model_ps.inc`. The rim measures 20 to 32 vertices per outfit, 60 to 96 fan triangles
over two rings. `measure_neck_skin` stays because the lid wears the throat texel of the
body it belongs to. Gone with the earlier shapes: `HD_LARA_NECK_PLANE_S`,
`HDLaraNeckPlane` and its four view-space numbers, `gNeckAxis` (c163), `gNeckNear` (c165)
and the node mask in `gNodeLight[].a`; gone with the inner skin: `HD_MODEL_SKIN_CW` /
`_CCW` / `_INSIDE`, `HDModelSetInnerSkin`, `HDModelInnerSkin`, `Model::innerPage*` and
`gInnerSkin` (c164). The cut follows the game's own choice of eye - `FP_EYE_OFFSET` 48
units forward, or the eye on the joint when `mgLOS` forbids the offset - without being
told which happened, because in first person the camera is the eye; in third person the
cut is off and the third person picture is byte-identical across the change for all five
outfits measured. The renderer's near plane is at 20 (`InitWindow`,
`specific/gamemain.cpp`). The diving suit is outside this work: it has no throat and its
helmet sits on the torso node. Everything here is inside `hd_enable`.
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp` measures and draws it (`-headw`, `-neck`,
`-firstperson`, `-noinner`, `-neckcut`, `-cutnodes <mask>`).

**Decisions.** No second, inward draw of the whole body closes the opening: with the lid
in place it changes nothing - forty first person pictures over five outfits, three
pitches, head and torso turned and tilted, identical to the pixel - while it costs a
second pass over 27,000 triangles every first person frame and has one real fault: a
strap, a shoulder piece or a flap is one layer of triangles whose two sides sit at the
same depth to the bit, the inward draw won that tie, and the piece came out in one flat
texel with its normal turned round, per pixel where float precision differed.

**Commits.** `6520654` (pack box, neck cap, hands), `84ce969` (neck cut, wrist), `36964e9`
(collar cut, inner skin), `23ce371` (cut reaches the neck), `73819d5` (first person, cut
plane), `e6debb7` (neck plane with lid), `c021cf6` (no head, skin cap)

### Lara's HD wardrobe: a scan of the installed art, its properties, and which outfit is worn
2026-09-05 - 2026-09-25

**What.** The Remaster answers Lara not with one model but with a wardrobe of separate
ones - the body outfit, the head, the braid, the hand pairs, the thigh and torso holsters
and the weapon on the back - and the engine loads the parts a level can actually use
(ANDREA1 11 models and 20 MiB, JOBY5 16 and 27 MiB, RICH1 6 and 17 MiB, JOBY4 two and 12
MiB, 34 to 79 ms to build; the full IV-VI wardrobe is 21 models, 3.5 MiB of buffers and 30
MiB of pages). The list of outfits is a SCAN and not a table: one engine-free unit walks
three places in a fixed order, which is the priority - the IV-VI install's `4\ITEM` and
`5\ITEM`, then the I-III install's `1\ITEM`, then every active mod's `5\ITEM` and
`4\ITEM`. An entry's key is the source, a slash and the file, with a mod's folder name
between (`46/OUTFIT_TR2_HOME`, `13/OUTFIT_TRX_WETSUIT_1`, `mod/outfits/aod
wetsuit/OUTFIT_CLASSIC`), forward slashes throughout, compared case-insensitively. Over
two installed bundles: 52 entries, 22 from IV-VI and 30 from I-III, with 50 files passed
over and every refusal named in the log. An entry's properties are resolved in tiers, each
tier per key: a list block, a mod's `outfit.txt`, a table of eight measured rows, a
measurement off the file, the defaults. Which outfit is worn is decided from the level's
own data unless a `REG_SZ` named `hd_outfit` under the settings key names a scanned entry,
which wins; `HDLaraOutfitFor` answers the diving suit and the catsuit from `LaraDrawType`,
the Russian cap from the engine's own level-range test, and the four Tomb Raider III guest
outfits (#122) from the header marker `data[3]`. Young Lara stays classic whatever any of
it says. Worn parts are planned by the OUTFIT and not by the slots the level loaded. An
outfit that holsters but has no holster rig of its own is given one -
`HD_LARA_PART_HOLSTER_RIG`, `OUTFIT_TR3_CATSUIT` cut to texture page 8205 - and
`Outfit::wearsRig` says who wears it: `OUTFIT_VCI` and no other body. Every wardrobe part
carries a named material, a specular strength and exponent, per texture page, and the
outfit table names which of the body's own pages are Lara's skin; `skin_sheen` and
`skin_exponent` set the material of her skin separately from her clothes and move all
thirteen skin draws at once. An outfit also decides whose head a body wears, in three
modes: `outfit` (the body's own head node and `LARA_HEAD`), `tr5` (the body's head node
left out, `LARA_HEAD` with Tomb Raider V's own head node in its place) and `hair` (all
three, a hood or hat kept with TR5's hair over it), the default being `tr5` for every
I-III entry and for every mod whose `mod.txt` says `origin=tr1|tr2|tr3` and `outfit` for
everything else. Lara's face (`LARA_HEAD.TRM`) rides rigidly on the head node, node 14,
all but its throat, which hangs on the torso, node 7, with the file's own weights; the
face's part line reads `cover=2(00004080)` (nodes 7 and 14).

**Why.** Every other creature is one slot and one `.TRM`; Lara is drawn out of five slots
in one pass and which parts are drawn changes from frame to frame, so she needs a module
of her own. The whole IV-VI wardrobe lives in `4\ITEM` rather than `5\ITEM`, the
shared-folder rule the design of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931 already follows. Only loaded slots are planned, because
a weapon whose slot is missing cannot be drawn by the classic path either - that path
reads `meshes[objects[slot].mesh_index]`. The outfit test uses the engine's own expression
rather than a second copy, because a copy can drift. The `LARA_PONYTAIL` byte means two
different things - the Rome body inside a Russia level, and every Tomb Raider III guest -
and nothing else in the level file separates them, which is why the marker byte exists and
why only values 5..8 are accepted from it: 1..4 are the vanilla bodies and letting one
through would let a stale byte overrule the level's own `LaraType`. The young-Lara test is
the script flag `GF_YOUNGLARA` or the `LARA_YOUNG` outfit byte and not the Irish level
range, because the randomizer clears that flag out of `SCRIPT.DAT` (young Lara can carry
no weapon) and replaces her skin with an adult's. A table of eight hand-measured rows
could hold only outfits somebody had measured, so a mod's `OUTFIT_*.TRM` had to be refused
outright; a scanned list carries one while the measurements stay where they belong. The
choice is a registry value and not part of a run because a seed and its settings travel
from one player to another while an installation and a `Mods` folder do not: a run that
named a scanned outfit could not be played on another machine. Planning a worn part only
where the level had loaded the matching `LARA_HOLSTERS*` object is right for a HAND part
and wrong for anything WORN, because those variables hold slot numbers written from the
INVENTORY - `setup.cpp` puts `LARA_HOLSTERS_PISTOLS` on both thighs at every level start
whatever the level loaded, and the three VCI levels load no holster slot at all, because
Core drew no thigh holsters on the catsuit, while the randomizer hands that Lara pistols
anyway. `HOLSTER_PISTOL.TRM` is the two guns and nothing else - 4268 vertices, two pistols
floating in space - while pouch, thigh strap and hip belt are built into the outfit model,
and three bodies have none (`OUTFIT_VCI`, `OUTFIT_TR3_ANTARC`, `OUTFIT_TR3_NEVADA`); a
page-derived rig rule reached all three and two of them are wrong, because the Antarctica
parka and the Nevada outfit never wore a thigh rig in Tomb Raider III and their coats are
modelled to sit flush, so straps stood off the hip at the width the London catsuit's thin
thighs want. The London catsuit is the donor rather than the Rome one because its rig is
black leather over a black leg, which is what the VCI catsuit is, where `OUTFIT_CLASSIC`'s
is brown suede over bare skin. TR5 has no specular term of any kind -
`aTransformLightClipMesh` adds an ambient and a diffuse cosine and stops - so latex,
rubber and skin all read matt, and there is nothing per texel to read instead: over the
wardrobe's pages 8001, 8008, 8016, 8018, 8027, 8028 and 8205, 100 per cent of the texels
fall in the 240..255 alpha bucket, a flat opaque channel with BC7 quantisation noise, the
one exception being page 8002, Lara's hair, at 15.2 per cent below 128, which is coverage
and not gloss. One sheen for the whole draw of a weapon hand made her skin metal, because
a `HAND_` model is a hand and what it holds on two pages of one file; and where a room
carries no dynamic lights the shader's highlight is `light * strength * pow(N.V, power) /
255`, so a difference in material between forearm and hand is multiplied by the room's
ambient and the seam at the wrist brightens and darkens from room to room - on the Rome
body forearm and hand are the SAME page, 8001, and that difference is 5.1 grey levels at
N.V = 1 in a room of 255, and 84.1 on the Tomb Raider III catsuit. Geometry cannot tell
skin from latex, so which pages are skin is a table; three outfits keep a difference on
purpose, a latex sleeve, a parka mitten and a coat sleeve meeting a bare hand being
material boundaries in the art. The measured skin rule is given only one page per new
entry because it cannot be right about more: the four Tomb Raider III guests carry a
second skin page, 8202, their bare arms, and a measurement at the neck cannot reach an
arm - the same page is bare skin under the Antarctica parka and a latex sleeve under the
London catsuit - and the diving suit's throat page, 8047, is its helmet, so a measurement
alone would make the whole suit matt. The head mode exists because a IV-VI body carries
Lara's whole hair on head node 14 - of `OUTFIT_CLASSIC`'s 9,485 triangles there, 9,483
wear page 8002 and two are nape - while the separate `LARA_HEAD.TRM` riding rigidly on the
same node is only the face and the front of the skull, open at the back: the two are
halves of one head. All thirty `OUTFIT_TRX_*` bodies of the I-III bundle carry a hood,
hat, helmet or headband on that node and nothing else (diving hood and goggles 1,987
vertices, ice hood 461, Greek headband 1,127, six of the thirty near enough nothing) and
not one wears page 8002, so drawn as it stands such a body shows a bald skull with the
open back of `LARA_HEAD` in it. Dropping the head node opens no hole: with its triangles
hidden every measured body still reaches up to y -240..-250 (the collar, which belongs to
the torso node) while `OUTFIT_CLASSIC`'s head node reaches down to y -238.7, an overlap of
1 to 11 units. There is deliberately no rule by name and none by geometry:
`OUTFIT_TR2_HOME` is both the name of a IV-VI body with a full head and the name a mod
gives an I-III conversion, and a vertex count cannot separate a 10-vertex headband and a
932-vertex converted body from a 461-vertex hood. The outfits of the two installations
have no folder at all - on a typical machine 52 of 103 scanned entries - and a mod that
ships seventeen bodies under one `outfit.txt` cannot say anything about one of them, which
is why a list file can name any outfit. The plain twin of an `_HD` file is worn because
this engine's vertex holds `u` and `v` as bytes and 14,208 of `OUTFIT_TRX_WETSUIT_1_HD`'s
14,262 coordinates lie off that 1/255 grid, and off every grid from 1/256 to 1/4096,
differing from the twin's by as much as half a step in both directions, spread and not by
a constant offset; a wide file with no twin is worn all the same, because a rounded
picture beats no picture. A face riding wholly rigid on node 14 showed, in the handstand,
in a crouch and lying on her back after a fall, a flap and a crease at the throat and a
long straight neck: the turns are the animations' own (the handstand 159 tilts the head 65
to 80 degrees back against the torso at keys 7 to 40, the crouch idle 222 60 degrees, the
death 25 more than 100), and `LARA_HEAD.TRM` reaches 27.8 units below the head joint - 541
of its 5,913 vertices lie below it - so that strip of throat, which runs down into the
body's own neck, swung with the skull and folded out under the jaw. The file says itself
where its throat belongs: of its facial rig's 33 joints (each stored as an inverse bind
matrix, 3x4 and row-major, the joint at -R^T t), joint 4 stands on the bind of node 14,
joint 1 at (-1, -49, 11) on the bind of node 7, joint 6 at the hips and joint 3 at the
left thigh, and 171 vertices carry weight on joints 1, 3 and 6. A joint farther than 120
units from the rig's head joint (the one carrying the most weight) is a joint of the body:
over the 23 rigged `*_HEAD.TRM` of the IV-VI install's games 4 and 5 the farthest joint of
a face stands 99.4 units out (ZIP_HEAD) and the nearest joint of a body 131.8
(LARSON_HEAD), the gap measured on data over 58 files of both installs by TROne (GPLv3) by
Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931, whose rule shaped this design;
LARA_HEAD's two shoulder joints stand 81 units out and count as the face's. The file's
weights match the body's own: the 66 throat vertices that lie within a unit of
`OUTFIT_CLASSIC`'s neck in the bind pose carry a head weight 0.022 from the neck vertex
under them on average (0.058 on `OUTFIT_VCI`), and with the head pitched 70 degrees the
two skins stay 0.8 units apart on average and 4.0 at most (1.5 and 9.5 on `OUTFIT_VCI`),
where the rigid face parted from the neck by 15.1 and 34.6.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_lara.cpp`/`.h` is engine-free so the diagnostic tools link the
same reader; `specific/hd/hd_wardrobe.cpp`/`.h` hold the scan, the key format, the
property tiers and the override table and are compiled into the engine, `ModelProbe`,
`Randomize.exe` and the GUI alike, because two programs working the same list out
separately will one day disagree. The composite's skeleton is Lara's classic mesh tree:
every `OUTFIT_` model skins to nodes 0..14 and names no sixteenth, so the fifteen matrices
in `lara_matrices` are the joint palette, `OUTFIT_SUBSUIT` covering thirteen, the diving
suit ending in flippers that belong to the shins. `LARA_HEAD.TRM` covers 31 nodes because
it carries a facial rig whose bone numbers are not mesh-tree nodes, so it rides rigidly on
node 14 through `HDModelSlot::rigidNode` (default -1, so every existing caller is
unchanged), passed on by `HDModelLevelBegin` - all of it but its throat, which hangs on
node 7 (below). `HAIR_OG.TRM` has six bones matching the classic `HAIR` mesh tree's
straight chain at z = 0, 56, 112, 168, 224, 280 in every adult level. A `HAND_` model
covers nodes 9 and 10 on the right and 12 and 13 on the left, `HAND_BARE_REST` adds the
upper-arm stubs 8 and 11, and three are one-sided: `HAND_BARE_FLARE` and `HAND_BARE_TORCH`
cover 12 and 13 only, `HAND_BARE_CROWBAR` 9 and 10 only. `HOLSTER_PISTOL` and
`HOLSTER_UZI` cover nodes 1 and 4, `HOLSTER_REVOLVER` node 4,
`HOLSTER_SHOTGUN`/`_HK`/`_GRAPPLE` node 7, where `DrawLara` puts the classic ones; an
empty holster draws nothing extra, the straps being painted into every `OUTFIT_` model,
which is why the Remaster ships no empty-holster file. The Russian-cap test is the
engine's own expression `(gfLevelId >= LVL5_BASE && gfLevelId <= LVL5_SINKING_SUBMARINE &&
LaraDrawType == LARA_NORMAL) || LaraDrawType == LARA_BUNHEAD`, which already stands three
times in `game/hair.cpp` and once in `game/laraskin.cpp`; read against all fifteen vanilla
level files the rules answer correctly fifteen times out of fifteen. Which model plays
which role is the wardrobe of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931. The marker: `specific/file.cpp` reads the fourth word
of the 32-byte header block behind the texture pages into `GfHdOutfit`, beside `LaraType`
at `data[0]`, the weather at `data[1]` and the foreign-speech-head flag at `data[2]`;
`hd_laradraw.cpp` hands it to `HDLaraOutfitFor` unchanged, because the randomizer writes
the engine's own `HD_LARA_OUTFIT_*` numbers, and a `static_assert` in `hd_level.cpp` holds
the enum to 5..8. Mapping: `tr3_london` -> `OUTFIT_TR3_CATSUIT`, `tr3_jungle` ->
`OUTFIT_TR3_COAST`, `tr3_antarctica` -> `OUTFIT_TR3_ANTARC`, `tr3_nevada` ->
`OUTFIT_TR3_NEVADA`; a level carrying `LARA_PONYTAIL` and `data[3] = 0` draws
`OUTFIT_CLASSIC`, and not one of the seventeen shipped files carries that byte. The
young-Lara test follows the two places the engine builds the child body,
`LaraInitialiseMeshes` in `game/laramisc.cpp` and its twin in `game/deltapak.cpp`; the
flag is cleared by the randomizer in `core/ScriptDat.cpp`. The scan passes over the
install's two `OUTFIT_YOUNG*` bodies, `OUTFIT_HAIR` and the three `OUTFIT_HANDS_*` (parts
of the composite, not bodies), the fourteen I-III copies of names the IV-VI bundle already
carries self-contained (`OUTFIT_TR1_CLASSIC`: 14,515 vertices in IV-VI against 8,382 in
I-III, with IV-VI page numbers) and the thirty `_HD` twins; the young filter does not
apply to a mod, because mod outfits are commonly grown-up bodies shipped in the young
slot. `OUTFIT_HAIR.TRM` is not a hair cap and is loaded by nothing: it is a braid, 3,542
vertices over five nodes whose boxes run 0..53, 47..107, 93..161, 93..208 and 205..242
along z, the I-III bundle's own `HAIR_OG` in another spelling. `hd_trm.cpp`/`.h` read the
thirty `OUTFIT_TRX_*_HD.TRM` files whose vertex stride is 30 and not 24, the six extra
bytes being two texture coordinates that leave the gaps in the bone and weight block and
stand at the end as floats; the layout is arithmetic and then byte comparison - the
aligned index block plus vertices times 30 ends at the last byte in all thirty files and
the leading vertices are byte-identical with the twin's in position, normal, layer, bone
and weight - and over all 2,923 `.TRM` files of both remasters exactly thirty are laid out
that way. `readable()` reads whole files to look at headers (28.8 MiB, `read_kib=29525`,
once per session) because the prefix a header needs is 140 KiB of a 480 KiB outfit file.
`specific/registry.cpp`/`.h` gained `REG_PeekString`, the string form of `REG_PeekLong`,
read-only so an absent value cannot take `init_tomb5_stuff`'s first-run detection away;
`hd_laradraw.cpp` reads `hd_outfit` once per level build, because the in-game changer
writes it while the game runs. A list file is a `.txt` lying directly in `Mods` or
directly in a category folder, read as blocks (`Outfit: TRX_Wetsuit_3` then keys), taking
the same thirteen keys a mod's `outfit.txt` takes - `name`, `hands`, `gloves`, `braid`,
`holsters`, `rig`, `sheen`, `exponent`, `skin_sheen`, `skin_exponent`, `skin`,
`footsteps`, `head` - and setting only the keys it has; the files are found by
`hd_mods.cpp`'s own walk (`HDModsListCount` / `HDModsListPath`), which never steps into a
mod folder, a leading `_` switches a list off, and they are read in lower-cased full-path
order. `#` is a comment and closes nothing, a block opens at `Outfit:` and closes at the
next one or an empty line, and a UTF-8 byte order mark is taken off the first line. A name
is matched against the outfit's file stem without regard to case, to the `OUTFIT_` prefix
or to `_` against a space, so `TR2_Swim`, `tr2 swim` and `OUTFIT_TR2_SWIM` are one name; a
key prefix (`13/TRX_Wetsuit_3`, `46/Classic`) pins one source. One reader serves both
kinds of file - `take_key` and `apply_txt` with a `where` string and a tier number -
because the rank is only real if every tier writes the same fields in the same order.
`take_number` takes 0..2 for `sheen` and `skin_sheen` and 1..128 for the exponents,
`take_flag` refuses an unknown word and the note spells the vocabulary out (`1, yes, true,
on / 0, no, false, off`), `skin=` with nothing after it is a note instead of a silent wipe
of the tier below, each page number goes through `strtol`, `name=` is 64 bytes with a
longer one cut to 63 and noted, and `read_line` reads a line however long it is. The
material is named per texture page in one table in `hd_lara.cpp` - latex 0.45/26 for the
two catsuits, rubber 0.30/22 for the diving suit, cloth 0.10/14 for the Rome top, skin
0.12/10, hair 0.14/18, leather 0.18/20 for the holster rig, gunmetal 0.35/34 for a
weapon - through `HDModelSetPageSheen`, which is already the unit a draw call is cut to,
so it costs one constant write on the ranges that have one; `skin_sheen()` out of the
wardrobe entry is the one answer for all thirteen skin draws, the eleven hand parts
(`kPart[].kind == 1`: REST, PISTOL, UZI, SHOTGUN, HK, DEAGLE, DEAGLE_LASER, GRAPPLE,
FLARE, TORCH, CROWBAR), the body's own skin pages, the face and the neck lid. The term is
Blinn-Phong in the model VERTEX shader beside the diffuse it belongs to, out of the
object's own light list with the same direction and distance falloff; when the list is
empty the camera is the lamp, weighted by the light the vertex already has so that a
catsuit in an unlit corner stays dark, the highlight is added AFTER the texel and never
multiplied through it, and never in the additive pass. One new vertex register, `c161`
(`gSpec`: strength, exponent), is written for every draw so that Lara's gloss cannot be
left on the next creature; `HDModelLighting` carries the two numbers and every object
passes 0, so the creature path is unchanged to the bit. `HDModelSlot::onlyPage` builds
only the triangles wearing one `.DDS` page and loads only that page; the cut is by page
because a page is the artist's own division into materials and the measurement says it is
exact here - 8017 appears on nodes 0, 1, 4 and 79 triangles of node 7 in the Russia coat
and nowhere else, 8205 on nodes 0, 1 and 4 alone. The head mode is `HDWardrobeEntry::head`
with `fromHead` saying who decided, settled once at scan; `hd_lara.cpp` turns it into two
answers at level build and the draw asks nothing else per frame - `HDLaraBodyMask()` is
`~0u` or every node but 14, and `HD_LARA_PART_HEAD` is node 14 of the installation's own
`OUTFIT_CLASSIC`. No file in either remaster holds that node alone, so `hd_model.cpp`
learned `HDModelSlot::onlyNode`, the page cut's twin: only triangles whose dominant node
is in the mask are built and only the pages those triangles wear are loaded, which needs a
walk of the index list at page-gathering time, paid for only by a slot that asks. The cut
is by node and not by page although for this donor the two nearly agree, so that the
part's coverage is exactly node 14 and the first person mask takes the borrowed head with
the body's own. `hd_laradraw.cpp` draws the part after the body and before the face, with
the frame's mask, the body's cut and the body's cull, because the hair is the wardrobe's
only see-through pass; a body told to drop its own head with no donor to be had keeps its
own head and the log says so. `props_of` in `hd_lara.cpp` memoises one answer keyed by the
outfit, dropped by `HDLaraLevelEnd()`, because `HDLaraPartSheen` calls it once per part
per draw; `page_number_of` strips the mod namespace and the alternate-bundle base for
every page comparison, the held-item rule using the same helper. `hd_model.cpp`'s
`build()` works a model's page answers out once per texture layer into a small table,
exact because `HDTrmPageOf` is `texture[layer-1]`; `HDPageCacheKeyOf` remembers its answer
per key, dropped in `HDPageCacheAltRoot`, the one call that can change an answer - before
that the mod branch cost 30.8 microseconds a call and was asked once per corner of every
triangle - and folds a mod-namespace key to the plain page number when neither the mod nor
its origin bundle ships that `.DDS`, safe by construction because `resolve_page` then runs
the ordinary chain; measured on one level's wardrobe with nine mods, 25 cache slots and
33.3 MiB before, 24 and 32.0 MiB after, rendered picture byte-identical. Cost of the
borrowed head, ANDREA1 with the diving suit: +27,349 vertices (641 KiB), +28,455 indices
(55.6 KiB), +3 draw calls and one new texture page; a body in mode `outfit` pays none of
it. `hd_markers.cpp`/`.h` carry no `wear` line, and `hd_mods.cpp` goes on refusing a mod's
`OUTFIT_*.TRM` as a replacement, because a mod's outfit is an entry in the scan and never
a replacement. A settings file written by an intermediate build still carrying
`outfitsOn=` or `wardrobeFollowsGameFolder=` loads with every other key intact and the
next save drops them, because `Config::load` is an `if`/`else if` chain with no final
`else`. Log seams: the level's models line carries the phases of `build_ms` (`find_ms`,
`key_ms`, `page_ms`, `buf_ms`) and `trm_open`, `trm_load`, `trm_kib`; the wardrobe scan
line carries `ms`, `probed`, `read_kib`, `geometry` (0, because it reads headers and never
a body), `lists=`, `blocks=`, `matched=`, `unmatched=` and `heads tr5=.. hair=..
outfit=..`; each entry logs `head=<mode> (from ..) donor=OUTFIT_CLASSIC#14` and its skin
pair, the Lara line carries `laratype=`, `data3=`, `skinsheen=` and `head=<mode>/<1 if
TR5's head is on the card>` with `body=` beside `mask=`, a `MISMATCH` line is written when
`data[3]` and the sidecar's `outfit` disagree (the header byte wins), `HDLOG wardrobe list
<file>: Outfit <name> -> <key>: <the keys it set>` names every list block with the file's
own `N blocks, N matched, N unmatched`, and each list file also gets a `MODLOG list<n>`
line, which the mods scan writes even with the HD path off. Tools: `ModelProbe -wardrobe`
prints the scan, every refusal, a `head` column, a `sheen` column with its tier and a
`skin glow` column; `-lara`, `-outfit`, `-guns`, `-holsters`, `-flare`, `-torch`,
`-lara-nodes`, `-lara-pose`, `-mirror`, `-onlypage <n>`, `-nosheen`, `-lara-head
tr5|hair|outfit`, `-pagelist` build the composite against a level's own Lara mesh tree
without the game; `DdsProbe -alpha` writes an alpha channel as a grey picture and prints a
histogram; `bmodel.bat` builds with the new units. `HDTrmCounters`' note records that
`loads` counts calls before the file is opened and that the reader is reached from two
threads - the load thread's `HDTrmExists` in the level scan and the main thread's
`HDTrmProbe` in the wardrobe scan - without a race, because `specific/file.cpp` joins the
load thread before `HDLevelBuild` runs. `HDWardrobeFromWord` is the phrase form of a tier
and `HDWardrobeFromTag` the one-word form. The throat: `specific/hd/hd_trm.cpp` keeps the
rig's joints while it reads a head (`HDTrmModel::rigJoints`/`rigJoint`, `hd_trm.h`; the
list is taken only when it lies whole between the joint count and the geometry the rescan
found, and is freed by `HDTrmFree`). `HDModelSlot::neckNode` (`hd_model.h`, -1 by default)
asks for the rule on a rigid face; `rig_neck_of` (`hd_model.cpp`, limit
`kNeckJointDistance` 120) renames every body joint to the lowest of them in the copy read
into memory and hands that bone to `build()`'s existing rigid branch as the neck bone, so
the file's weights are kept and `dominant_node_of` puts a triangle on node 7 where the
throat outweighs the face; it runs in pass one while the file is open, and pass two hands
the bone to the model. `HDLaraPlan` asks for node 7 on the face (`hd_lara.cpp`); the
reasoning and the numbers stand at `HD_LARA_PART_FACE` (`hd_lara.h`). A file with no rig,
or none beyond the limit, stays rigid, and the note says why: the model note reads
`LARA_HEAD (slot 23042): 171 of 5913 vertices of the face take the body's neck (node 7)
with the file's own weights - rig joints 1,3,6 stand 199.3..270.8 from its head joint 4,
the limit is 120`. It costs once per level build, 5,913 vertices walked twice. Every head
piece is placed with the frame's own matrices (`lara_lmx_of_node` maps node 14 to matrix 8
for the body, the donor head, the lid, the face and the hands alike). First person does
not draw the face (its push is guarded by `!firstPerson`), so the neck cut and the lid are
untouched. The same file's rig moves her lips in the cutscenes she acts in (see *The
cutscene faces speak: their lips follow the Remaster's track files*). Files:
`specific/hd/hd_wardrobe.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_lara.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_laradraw.cpp`/`.h`,
`hd_model.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_trm.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_level.cpp`, `hd_markers.cpp`/`.h`,
`hd_mods.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_pagecache.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_object.cpp`, `hd_render.cpp`,
`hd_outfitmenu.cpp`, `hd_shader/hd_model.hlsl` and `hd_model_vs.inc`, `specific/file.cpp`,
`specific/registry.cpp`/`.h`, `specific/winmain.cpp`, `specific/3dmath.h`,
`specific/drawroom.h`, `game/lara.cpp`/`.h`, `game/laramisc.cpp`, `game/deltapak.cpp`,
`game/hair.cpp`, `game/laraskin.cpp`, `tomb5.vcxproj`,
`TR5Randomizer/src/core/ScriptDat.cpp`, `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp`,
`DdsProbe.cpp`, `bmodel.bat`, `README.md`, `TOMB5 Code/README.md`,
`Preparation/Tools/README.md`, `docs/Engine-Manual.md`, `docs/Randomizer-Manual.md`.

**Decisions.** The ANDY/JOBY assignment of the TR5 glue of TROne (GPLv3) by
Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931 is not followed: in these level files
`JOBY` is the Russian submarine section and `ANDY` is Ireland. The throat takes the file's
own rig and not a weight copied from the nearest outfit vertex in the neck column: that
design reached the jaw and the chin as well (387 of the 541 vertices below the joint, on
average 25 units from the nearest neck vertex), handed them 0.46 to 0.61 of the head on
average and tore the jaw open into spikes at head pitches of 60 and 70 degrees and in the
crouch's head turn, where the file's rig leaves no flap, no step and no hole. Creature
faces keep `neck_bone_of`: the distance rule picks the same single joint for `BLUE_GUARD`,
`PIERRE`, `ADMIRAL` and the two `VON_CROY` faces, but adds joints 10 and 13 to `LARSON`'s
joint 1 and finds a body joint where `neck_bone_of` finds none in the two `PATRICK`,
`DEMON` and `SERGIE` faces, so it is not carried over to them.

### F4 changes Lara's outfit inside the level
2026-09-13 - 2026-09-14

**What.** F4 opens a wardrobe window in the middle of a level and Lara wears the choice at
once, without leaving the level. The window is the pause menu's twin by construction:
`CreateMonoScreen` freezes the picture, `S_UpdateInput` with `SetDebounce` drives it,
`dbinput`'s six bits are the only inputs it reads, `SFX_MENU_CHOOSE` and `SFX_MENU_SELECT`
are its sounds, `PrintString` and `font_height` draw it in the two columns the options
page uses, and a literal with no string id goes through `CustomText` exactly as the
`Language` row does; a gamepad works in it because the bits it reads are the ones the pad
already drives. `InventoryActive` is held for the whole of it, so the press that closes
the window cannot also roll Lara. It does not open in the title, with Lara dead, during a
cutscene, or while the binoculars or the laser sight are up, and the inventory and the
pause menu cannot be open under it, because both run their own frame loop and the call
site is not in it. Alt+Enter inside it toggles the display and chooses nothing; closing
the window counts as cancel. The list is the wardrobe scan in its own order, a window of
nine rows with the selection kept in view, each row naming its source (`IV-VI`, `I-III` or
the mod's folder name) and a `*` on the row in force; the first row is **Level facts**,
which is not an outfit but what clears the setting again. Under the list stand value rows:
the highlighted outfit's **Footsteps**, its **Head** mode with who decided it, its
**Shine** and its **Skin glow**, each turned over with left and right and naming the tier
that decided it; on the **Level facts** row the footsteps read *as the outfit says* and do
not answer left or right. The outfit is written to the `REG_SZ` `hd_outfit` the level
build reads; the footsteps are one `REG_DWORD` per outfit under `tomb5\hd_footsteps`, the
wardrobe key as the value's name, written for the row it was made on when that row is
left. A level may spend `HD_REDRESS_ALLOWANCE` on changes; past it the window says
*applies at the next level*, the log says how much has been spent, and the new outfit's
footsteps wait with the body. Both halves are written to the registry either way, so the
next level wears both.

**Why.** The registry value the level build reads had nothing that wrote it.
`OpenRegistry` creates the key it is handed, which is safe here and nowhere earlier,
because `init_tomb5_stuff` asks `REG_KeyWasCreated()` once at startup and has long since
run by the time a level is on the screen. The footsteps are a value per outfit rather than
a subkey per outfit because a wardrobe key holds slashes and spaces, and a subkey name may
hold no backslash while a value name may hold almost anything. The re-dress is safe on the
main thread because there is no other one: the load thread that builds a level is joined
before `HDLevelBuild` ever runs, and the caller has stopped the world. The cap is bytes
and not a count because the cost of a change is not uniform: measured over one level with
a 56-entry wardrobe, one outfit's own pages run from 9 to 28 pages and 12.00 to 37.30 MiB,
a single change costs up to 15 pages and 20.00 MiB nothing else holds, the dearest is +10
pages and +13.33 MiB, the mean over all 2,970 ordered pairs is +2.94 MiB, and wearing all
55 in one level is 106.64 MiB over 80 distinct pages - about twenty changes at the mean
and four at the worst. The allowance is the 64 MiB of slack `AutoBudgetBytes` already
holds back, and it holds back unbounded growth rather than a ceiling about to be hit -
`release\PCtomb5.exe` is x86 with `IMAGE_FILE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE` set (PE characteristics
0x0122), so the ceiling is 4 GiB, and the heaviest offline load measured (179 room pages,
53 model pages, 350.5 MiB of texture on the card, a `Mods` folder, every slot) peaks at
209.4 MiB of private commit. The persisted footstep choice is applied on every way out of
the HD level build because `HDLevelBuild` has five ways to give up - no stem, a bad room
count, `HDRenderInit` refusing the card, no page cache, no room drawing HD - while the
bare footstep set is built whenever `hd_enable` is on; a player whose card cannot do
shader model 3 keeps `hd_enable` at 1 and goes classic, and a choice applied only on the
HD path would work inside the level and be dropped at the next level start. On those ways
out there is no HD body to follow - `HDLaraDrawOutfit()` reads `HD_LARA_OUTFIT_NONE` and
Lara wears the engine's own outfit, which has boots - so the answer is given and written
into the log.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_outfitmenu.cpp`/`.h` hold the window; `game/control.cpp` holds
the F4 edge and its guard (`!gfGameMode`, Lara alive, `!BinocularRange`, `!cutseq_trig`),
the edge read before the other conditions so that a key held through a cutscene does not
open the window the moment it ends. `HDLevelRedress` in `hd_level.cpp`/`.h` is
`HDObjectRelease` plus `HDObjectLevelBuild`, the same pair a level change makes, with
`HDLevelRedressAllowed`, `HDLevelRedressRefresh` and `HDLevelRedressCount` beside it;
`HD_REDRESS_ALLOWANCE` is 64 MiB in `hd_memory.h`. The rooms, their page cache and every
classic table stay where they are - Lara's meshes, her holsters, the weapon in her hand
and the inventory are not touched - and the game clock restarts after the re-dress so its
cost does not become catch-up ticks of game logic. `HDLevelBuild`'s body is
`HDLevelBuildHD()` and `HDLevelBuild` is four lines around it, so the footstep question is
asked on every way out and none can skip it; `specific/file.cpp` carries the note at the
end of `LoadLevel` about the load thread being joined before `HDLevelBuild` runs, and
`hd_laradraw.cpp`/`.h` supply `HDLaraDrawOutfit()`. The page cost was measured with
`ModelProbe -pagelist`, which lists a level's pages per wardrobe entry. Files:
`specific/hd/hd_outfitmenu.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_level.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_memory.h`,
`hd_laradraw.cpp`/`.h`, `game/control.cpp`, `specific/file.cpp`, `tomb5.vcxproj`,
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp`, `README.md`, `Preparation/Tools/README.md`.

**Decisions.** The old outfit's pages are not freed on a change, because the page cache
never gives a page back: other models hold slot indexes, and a page given back under one
would draw white.

**Commits.** `c595d16` (F4 opens the wardrobe), `2305eb7` (F4 in a cutscene), `5f5c0c0`
(the docs), `a0e5939` (the headroom it owed), `2850c54` (footstep mod needs no bank),
`182447c` (the menu's edges)

### The outfit chooses the footsteps, and a bare foot silences the floor layer
2026-09-13 - 2026-09-14

**What.** A barefoot outfit walks barefoot. Lara's own foot reaches the mixer through an
animation command - `game/control.cpp` reads `num = cmd[1] & 0x3FFF` out of the animation
and calls `SoundEffect` - so the switch is two shorts: sound ids 0 (the step) and 4 (the
landing) are bent to a second set of samples, with no reload and no allocation after the
level is up. The bare set goes into `DS_Buffers` slots after the level's own, with two
spare `SAMPLE_INFO` entries asked of `game_malloc` in the one place where the level's bump
allocator is still open, and only with the build gate on (`HDEnabled()`: `hd_build` on and
an installation found), so a player with the gate off keeps the allocation layout of
before. What goes in them is what the ordinary chain plays for ids 0 and 4 when a mod
really replaces the footsteps, and otherwise the Remaster's own barefoot recordings, sound
id 417 of the bank, which no level carries and which is therefore reached by bank sample
number rather than through the level bridge; the landing is drawn from the same five
recordings as the steps. While boots are worn, ids 0 and 4 are taken from the first
unmodded bank of the chain rather than from a mod's bank or a mod's loose `.wav`. A step
is two sounds on one frame and the second is switched too: `game/footprnt.cpp`'s
`AddFootprint` plays the surface under Lara's foot (`footsounds[floor->fx] +
SFX_FOOTSTEPS_MUD`, sound ids 288 to 294) for every sector whose `fx` is not 5, 6 or 11,
and while a bare set is in force that layer is passed over. The footprint itself is a
picture and is untouched, and sound id 17 (`SFX_LARA_WET_FEET`), which stands beside id 0
on the same frames for the water case, is not switched. With the build gate off
(`hd_build` 0 or no installation) the two ids take the ordinary chain and a sound mod
plays as it always did. Which set a step plays is chosen at every step and for Lara alone,
by her draw and her outfit (see *Lara's footstep follows the draw and her outfit, and
nobody else's does (#232)*).

**Why.** A sound mod replaces a sound for every outfit at once, so a barefoot footstep mod
made Lara barefoot in boots, in a wetsuit and in a parka alike; with the outfit choosing
between two sets, the two have to be two, and the boots must come from an unmodded bank.
The floor layer had to be silenced with the foot because it is the loud half of a step:
over thirteen classic levels that carry footsteps at all, the foot layer is 52 takes of 35
to 43 ms while the floor layer is 111 takes of 87 to 433 ms, mean 186, which is 4.7 times
the foot layer. Id 17 is not switched because the bank has one barefoot set and it is a
dry one. The infos' fields are the level's except two: everything about how a footstep is
played - volume, hearing radius, randomness, play mode - describes the game and stays the
level's; the sample number and count are what was really loaded and the pitch is the
bank's. Two banks agree: id 0 is volume 191, radius 10, randomness 0, pitch 12, flags
0x6010 in all sixteen classic levels; id 417 is volume 191, radius 10, randomness 0, pitch
0, flags 0x6014, the bank's entry having the random pitch off for those five recordings.
The landing is drawn from the steps because the bank has no barefoot landing: the boots'
set is four steps of 33 to 41 ms and one landing of 175 ms, 4.7 times the length of a step
and 2.4 times its peak, and among the bank's five barefoot recordings (106 / 86 / 134 / 69
/ 113 ms) none stands out that way - the longest is 1.4 times the mean of the other four
and the loudest by RMS is 1.25 times theirs and is not the longest. The rule rests on the
bank's own takes alone. A mod that does distinguish its own landing - one measured at 4.4
times the RMS of its own steps - supplies the bare landing from its own id 4, and the
second spare info is used. Whether a mod really replaces the footsteps is decided by
comparing payloads and not by asking whether a mod's bank is being played: of the 390
sound ids one mod's bank shares with the install's, 387 hold byte-identical recordings and
three do not, so a door mod or a voice mod carries the install's own id 0 byte for byte
and would otherwise have had the boots' recordings handed back under the name "bare"; and
a footstep mod need not ship a bank at all - it may replace a sample with a loose
`<NNNN>.wav`, which for the footsteps are exactly `0000.wav` to `0003.wav` and `0010.wav`.
There is room for the extra samples: `MAX_SAMPLES` is 450 and the sample count over all
sixteen classic levels runs from 76 to 148, so five more fit with 297 to spare, and a
randomized level carrying all four Tomb Raider III guests adds 21 and still fits; the
check is made before a single sample is decoded, and a level that has no room says so, the
window's row reading *unavailable* as it does with no bank at all.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_feet.cpp`/`.h` hold the two sets, the spare `SAMPLE_INFO` entries
and `HDFeetSurfaceQuiet()`, which `game/footprnt.cpp` asks at its one call site and which
is false with `hd_enable` off, false with boots on and false in a level with no second
set. `specific/file.cpp` builds the bare set inside `LoadSamples`, on the load thread,
after the line that counts the level's own samples, and takes the boots from
`HQSfxPayloadBoots`; `HQSfxPayload` for sound id 0 - the ordinary chain, bank and then the
loose overlay - is compared with `HQSfxPayloadBoots` for the same sample to decide whether
a mod really replaces the footsteps, the banks each owning their read buffer so both can
be held at once, and `HQSfxWavSource` (`specific/hqsfx.cpp`/`.h`) names the mod for the
log without reading any audio. `HDFeetLevelEnd()` stands in `FreeLevel`, two lines above
`malloc_ptr = malloc_buffer`, the line that makes every `game_malloc` pointer stale,
because `LoadSamples` returns before reaching the end in seven places, is skipped entirely
when the sound is off, and one level in the script's list has no sound blocks at all, so
the next level would otherwise have found a bare set answering "available" through the
previous level's freed `sample_lut`. Log seams, all `SFXLOG`: one line per level where the
set is built, naming the ids; one the first time in each bare spell; one naming which bank
or which mod supplies the bare set; and one naming the mod whose ids 0 and 4 are bypassed
while the outfit wears boots. Tools: `AnimCmd` over a level's `LARA` slot counts the
frames carrying `PlaySound sfx 0`, `FlipEffect no 32` or both (148, 132 and 121 on one
level); `Tr5Sound` counts and times the two layers over every classic level; `SfxProbe
-wavs` reads a mod of loose files, checks each with the engine's own `SfxRiffCheck` and
prints which bank samples they claim - `SfxProbe` links `sfxbank.cpp` and `hd_mods.cpp`
and not `hqsfx.cpp` or `hd_feet.cpp`, which need DirectSound and the engine's `Log`, so
the two bypass lines are read in the game's own log. Files:
`specific/hd/hd_feet.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_level.cpp`/`.h`, `game/footprnt.cpp`,
`game/control.cpp`, `specific/file.cpp`, `specific/hqsfx.cpp`/`.h`,
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp`, `README.md`.

**Commits.** `c595d16` (outfit decides the footsteps), `3bae54d` (a step is two sounds),
`831f33a` (bare set built after count), `2850c54` (footstep mod needs no bank), `182447c`
(bare landing from five)

### Lara's footstep follows the draw and her outfit, and nobody else's does (#232)
2026-10-21 - 2026-10-22

**What.** Sound ids 0 (the step) and 4 (the landing) are chosen at every step, not at the
load, and only for Lara. Every level sample, the footsteps included, takes the ordinary
chain at the load - a mod's loose `.wav`, a mod's bank, else the unmodded bank, else the
level's own recording - so the level's own entries for ids 0 and 4 are the **ordinary
set**. Beside it, from the level's start, lie the **bare set** (the bank's barefoot
recordings in new slots, or, where the ordinary set is a footstep mod's own recording, the
ordinary samples themselves) and the **unmodded boots** (the first unmodded bank's ids 0
and 4 in new slots, loaded only where the ordinary set differs from them). `SoundEffect`
asks `HDFeetStepInfo` for the entry: while Lara is drawn HD her step plays the bare set
under a barefoot outfit and the unmodded boots under boots (the ordinary set where no
boots set was needed); drawn classic, and for every other emitter in either draw, the step
plays the ordinary set. The floor layer (ids 288 to 294) is passed over only while she is
drawn HD and barefoot at that step. `AnimateLara` names her as the caller of her animation
sounds, as `AnimateItem` does for every other item. The shotgun's weapon item, the one
weapon item that carries a footstep, is taken for Lara by its index at `lara.weapon_item`
(#234) and walks on her set. With `-log`, one line at each level load: `FEET
ordinary="<source>" boots=<unmodded|none> bare=<id,id|none> outfit=<boots|bare>
drawn=<hd|sd> boots_infos=<id,id|none>`, and a switched step's `SFXLOG` line ends in `
feet=bare` or ` feet=boots`; an F4 change has its own `HDLOG f4` line.

**Why.** Some SWATs and guards walked barefoot with Lara, a barefoot HD outfit kept its
bare feet after a switch to the classic draw, and a sound mod's footsteps were never heard
in classic play. The outfit's answer was written into the level's sound map itself
(`HDFeetBare` set `sample_lut[0]` and `[4]` to the bare entries), and `SoundEffect` reads
that map for every caller, so every enemy whose own animation plays id 0 or 4 walked on
the bare set with her: the emitters of ids 0 and 4 (`AnimCmd` over slots 0 to 470) are
BLUE_GUARD id 0, MAFIA2 id 4 and HITMAN id 4 in the classic levels, and in randomized
levels also SWAT_PLUS_MIP (36) id 0, BLUE_GUARD2 (460) id 0 and CYBORG (469) id 4, besides
Lara and her weapon sets. That answer was set at the load and by the F4 changer and never
asked the draw, while the sets are built whenever `hd_build` is on and an installation is
found, so a classic-drawn Lara with a barefoot HD outfit walked barefoot and lost the
floor layer too; the same load-time split sent ids 0 and 4 through the unmodded bank in
every draw. Commands are read only by `AnimateItem` (`game/control.cpp`) and `AnimateLara`
(`game/laramisc.cpp`); an arm's animation runs none, so the pistols', Uzis' and revolver's
id 0 never plays. The weapon item `draw_shotgun` (`game/lara1gun.cpp`) creates for a long
gun takes its object from `WeaponObject` (`game/larafire.cpp`) - SHOTGUN_ANIM, HK_ANIM or
CROSSBOW_ANIM - and goes through `AnimateItem`; of the three only SHOTGUN_ANIM carries a
footstep. Ids 0, 4 and 17 are played from animation commands only.

**How.** A footstep is Lara's when its caller is `LARA`: every other emitter of ids 0 and
4 is an item animated by `AnimateItem`, which names it. What she walks on is a fact of
what is drawn at that step: drawn classic she wears the engine's own boots, and the
ordinary chain is what the classic engine plays; drawn HD she wears the outfit, and the
outfit's feet choose. The draw asked is `HDLaraDrawActive()` - Lara's body drawn HD, which
is `HDDrawn()` with her HD composite built and `hd_objects` on. A footstep mod is a mod
whose recording on a footstep sample differs from the unmodded bank's, byte for byte, and
stands in that sample's slot: the load loop holds every payload to its length rule, and a
take it refused keeps the level's own recording, so the test asks the loop's verdict first
(`HDFeetNoteSample`) and a refused take counts as no mod there. The mod supplies the bare
set only whole: its first take of id 0 decides whether it is a footstep mod, and every
take of id 0 must have reached its slot; one refused take anywhere, and the bare set is
the bank's barefoot recordings. The boots ask every take of both ids and are all or
nothing per id, held to the same length rule. `AnimateLara` sets `SfxCommandCaller` and
its four companions around her sounds, so Lara's `SFXLOG` lines carry `obj=0 room= anim=
type= rflags=` like everyone else's. The choice follows at the next step, never
mid-sample: F12 back to the classic draw brings the boots back at her next footfall, F12
to HD the bare set; a step already sounding finishes as it began. `HD_FEET_SPARE_INFOS` is
4 whether or not a level loads the boots, so the layout of the bump allocator depends on
`hd_build` and the installation only; the sound map grows by two spare entries, 16 bytes
of `game_malloc`, and with `hd_build` 0 the sample table, the infos and every step's entry
are as before. ModernTest's `hd_feet` group (164 checks) runs `HDFeetPick` over nine
emitters times both draws, both outfits, with and without a footstep mod and ids 0 and 4,
F12 through `HDSwitchStep` itself, and `HDFeetQuietRule` in all eight cases; the gate
checks hold that the spare infos ask the build gate, no sample is redirected at the load,
and the step and the floor ask Lara's draw.

**Decisions.** `HDLaraDrawActive()` and not `HDDrawn()` alone: a level whose HD build gave
up, or `hd_objects` 0, draws her classic in boots while the switch says HD. A footstep
mod's bare set is the ordinary samples themselves, not a copy, because the ordinary set is
the mod's and a copy would hold the same bytes twice; a mod whose own landing the loop
refused keeps the level's own landing in the bare set, and a mod whose takes of id 0 all
reached their slots but only some differ from the bank's is taken as it stands. The boots
ask every take of both ids, so a mod that replaces only the landing or some steps still
leaves the HD boots whole. Sound id 17 (`SFX_LARA_WET_FEET`) is not switched; there is one
dry barefoot set.

**Commits.** `f8cdf49e` (the sets in memory), `20ccfe1d` (choice per step, the caller),
`9b0d50d3` (the floor layer), `e366a748` (checks and FEET line), `b3b09a70` (a comment),
`ac474242` (mod is what loaded), `ed27a505` (bare set held whole)

### The soft motion of the chest: an optional secondary motion for the HD Lara
2026-10-02

**What.** An HD Lara can carry a secondary motion of the chest. Each side of the chest is
one point mass on a damped spring whose anchor the torso carries through the world; the
model vertex shader moves the vertices of two regions of the body by that side's offset,
weighted by a smooth mask and by the vertex's own weight on the torso node. The two
regions are found once per outfit, at the level build, from the body model's own vertices;
an outfit whose body fails a check of the finder stays still. One new option,
`tomb5.hd_softbody` (registry `hd_softbody`): 0 off - the default - 1 subtle, 2 normal, 3
strong; a stored value out of range reads as off. One new options menu row, *Graphics* ->
*Body physics*, directly under *HD textures*: off, Subtle, Normal, Strong, saved with the
tomb5 settings and taking effect at once in the running level; the page holds thirteen
rows with it and pages in two, seven and six. Two new log lines behind `-log`: `HDLOG
softbody` whenever her composite is built or the option changes, and `HDLOG softbody
second` once a second of game time in which the motion moved. Nothing is added to a
savegame.

**Why.** An optional secondary motion for the HD model. The wardrobe's bodies are skinned
surfaces that can bend where the classic meshes are rigid, and a chest that follows the
torso without any lag reads as stiff in a landing, a run or a sudden stop. The feel can
only be judged and tuned in the game, so every number that shapes it stands in one table
and the log shows what it did.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_softbody.h` (new; no engine header, like `hd_objlight_dark.h`)
holds the table - natural frequency 3 Hz, damping ratio 0.3, gain 0.1, bound 0.3 of the
radius, front-back share 0.35, strengths 1.5 / 3 / 4.5 on gain and bound, and the
machinery under it (sub-step 1/480 s, gap 0.25 s, anchor speed 9000 units a second plus
128, rest below 0.05 units and 0.5 units a second) - and the finder's numbers.
`HDSoftMask` is a smoothstep of 1 - distance / radius. `HDSoftFindRegion`: up from the
hips joint to the head joint, her right from the left thigh joint to the right, the front
where the lower-leg vertices below the ankle joints point; per side the frontmost torso
vertex (weight 0.5 or more) in the band 0.45 to 0.75 of the hips-to-head height between
the middle strip and the outer edge, its cap's middle across; the radius half the apexes'
distance apart, so that the regions meet in the middle; the centre half a radius behind
the apex; the chest wall, the torso's front at the collarbones in the apex's column, whose
point straight behind the apex must get a mask of 0.04 or more, or the chest is deeper
than the region reaches and refused as `deep`. The other refusals are `no_front` (too few
lower-leg vertices below the ankles to tell front from back), `band_edge` (a front still
coming forward at the band's top), `radius` (the apexes too close), `sparse` (fewer than
30 torso-weighted vertices inside a region, too few to bend smoothly) and `asymmetric`;
over the 122 bodies of the wardrobe scan 98 are accepted. `HDSoftPropagator` is the exact
step of the damped oscillator, so the sub-step's length cuts nothing but the frame's
remainder; `HDSoftOutput` eases gain times travel into the bound with a tanh;
`HDSoftAdvance` takes a change of the anchor's speed out of the point's relative speed,
runs whole sub-steps and carries the rest, resets on a gap, a jump or a value that is not
finite, bounds the state and snaps both sides to exact zero below the rest thresholds;
`HDSoftClockStep`, `HDSoftAnchor`, `HDSoftToTorso` and `HDSoftConstants` complete it.
`hd_model.hlsl`: `gSoft` in c163 to c166, the torso weight beside the head weight in the
skinning loop, the two masks and the offset before the light reads the position; fxc's own
literal constants move to c167 and c168, clear of `gSoft`. `hd_model.h`: `HDModelSoft` and
`HDModelDraw`'s `soft`; `hd_model.cpp` writes the four registers for every draw, zeros
without one, so every other HD object, a cutscene actor's face and the pickup display draw
with zero constants, which add exactly nothing. `hd_object.cpp`: the frame list's entry
carries it, zeroed for every item, copied by `HDObjectPush` and handed to the draw.
`hd_lara.cpp`: `measure_softbody` in the body's measure hook while the file is still a
file, cleared at every plan; `HDLaraSoftRegion` and `HDLaraPartSoft`. `hd_laradraw.cpp`:
`soft_strength`, `soft_gate`, `soft_log` and `soft_constants` - the gates, a reset on a
cutscene's first and last frame, the clock, the anchors (the region centres carried by
`lara_joint_matrices[LMX_TORSO]` from `lara_item->pos`), the step, the per-second line and
the constants on the draw's own torso matrix; the running level takes a change of the
option on its next drawn frame (`soft_constants` compares the option with the strength it
logged last, resets to rest and writes a new `HDLOG softbody` line). `tomb5/tomb5.cpp` and
`global/types.h` for the option. The row: `game/menu_frame.cpp` `MenuValBodyPhysics` shows
the table's own `off`, `Subtle`, `Normal` or `Strong`, anything out of range as `off`;
`MenuStepBodyPhysics` steps from a stored value taken as off when out of range through
`menu_nav.h`'s `MenuSliderStep` over 0..3, the ends holding as on *Camera damping*; the
row is a `MENU_VALUE` with `MENU_SAVE_TOMB5`, so a change is written to the registry at
once by `save_new_tomb5_settings`. `game/gameflow.cpp` gives `Body physics`, `Subtle` and
`Normal` their five columns (German `K\xF6rperphysik`, `Dezent`, `Normal`); `off` and
`Strong` were there. `game/menu_frame.h`: the geometry note says that a page with more
than twelve rows pages, as *Key bindings* and *Graphics* do. With `tomb5.hd_enable` 0
`HDLevelLoad` stops at its guard before any HD model or Lara is built, so none of this
runs. The motion ignores gravity (there is no sag at rest), the torso's own turning except
as it carries the anchors, collisions with the arms and anything else, and the normals of
the moved surface, whose shading stays where it was; in a frame in which her own draw is
hidden while a mirror shows her, the mirror draws the last state. ModernTest's nine
`softbody_*` groups hold the spring against the closed form of a damped oscillator, the
same peak at 30, 60 and 165 frames a second, the bound and the absence of NaN under random
and extreme steps, the resets, the rest, the finder's refusals on synthetic torsos and the
register layout; MenuTest's `graphics_softbody_row` holds the row.

**Decisions.** Off by default. Never on a level whose gameflow flags carry `GF_YOUNGLARA`,
whatever the option says, and there is no switch for that. HD only: never for a Lara drawn
classic. Active in cutscenes like everywhere else her composite is drawn. The three
strengths scale gain and bound and nothing else, so the swing's timing is the same at all
three; with the bound at 18 units on a region radius of 41 (`OUTFIT_BARE`, at a strength
of 1.5) the swing of a landing was barely to be seen in the game, so that size became
*Subtle*, and *Normal* and *Strong* stand at twice and three times it. Only the torso's
motion through the world drives it: the anchors come from `lara_joint_matrices` and
`lara_item->pos`, which no camera enters, and the view enters last, as the torso matrix of
the very draw that turns the offset into view space - which also gives a mirror's draw the
offset reflected. The clock is `GlobalCounter` plus `InterpFrameAlpha`; one step per drawn
frame, by the first draw of Lara that is not a mirror's. The motion's offset is taken into
the torso's own axes and its front-back part kept at 0.35. The parts that carry it are
those skinned on her skeleton in the body's bind space - the body, TR5's borrowed head,
the face with its throat on the torso, the neck lid and the holster rig - and never the
hands with what they hold, the thigh holsters, the weapon on the back or the braid. The
constants travel in `hd_object.cpp`'s frame list from `HDObjectPush` to the draw, because
Lara's parts are queued there and drawn later; the option is a field of `tomb5_options` in
`global/types.h`, where its neighbours live. The finder's numbers were set over the 122
bodies of the scan: in the 98 it accepts the apexes stand between 0.53 and 0.60 of the
hips-to-head height. A chest deeper than its region reaches is refused and not given a
larger region: a radius grown until it reaches the wall of the deepest chests would take
in the collarbones and the armpits as well. The limit, a mask of 0.04 at the wall, lies
between the lowest accepted body (0.068, the TRX biker) and the highest refused one
(0.023, `OUTFIT_THICC`). The menu row stands under *HD textures*, the switch it depends
on, though the thirteenth row makes *Graphics* page; it is not greyed, because no row of
that page is greyed while HD is off. Its first state is the table's own `off` (German
`aus`), as on *Camera damping*, rather than a second spelling of the same value.

### The projected shadow: Lara's outline on the HD rooms, cast by one fixed light
2026-10-03

**What.** In an HD room the HD Lara throws a projected shadow in place of the classic
blob: her composite of the drawn frame is drawn into a depth map as seen along a key
light, and the HD room groups near her are drawn a second time with a small pixel shader
that looks the map up and darkens the picture where she stands between the light and the
surface. The shadow is soft-edged, lies on floors, steps and slopes as they are and climbs
a wall she stands close to. `tomb5.shadow_mode` (registry `shadow`) gains the value 5,
*Projected*, and a fresh installation starts with it; 1 Original, 2 Circle, 3 Faded circle
and 4 PSX keep their meaning and their pictures. With 5, every blob still drawn - a
creature's or an item's that does not give way to the second map (see *The projected
shadow: the creatures cast as well, into a second map*), and Lara's in a frame the
projected shadow does not run in - is the faded circle. Three new log lines behind `-log`:
`HDLOG shadow target`, `HDLOG shadow mode` and `HDLOG shadow second`. The *Shadow mode*
row on the *Graphics* page offers *Projected* as its fifth state while HD is on and steps
the four blobs while it is off, showing a stored 5 then as *Faded circle*, which is what
is drawn for it. The shadow is thrown by one fixed light for the whole game - 30 degrees
off straight down, from one side, at one darkness - so it lies the same way in every room
and moves only as she does. The lights that light her model can turn and deepen it by one
number of the table, `HD_SHADOW_PULL`, which stands at 0; above 0 the shadow lies where
her movement through the light puts it in every frame and stands still the frame she
stands still, and only a change of the lights themselves - another room's list coming in,
a lamp that goes out or fades - is blended in, over about half a second of game time.

**Why.** A shadow that shows her outline. The blob says where she stands and nothing more;
a silhouette laid on the floor and the steps, offset to one side, ties her to the room she
stands in. The light is a fixed one because the lamps of the levels are set to colour the
walls - low, close and one at a time - and each throws the shadow somewhere else, so a
shadow turned by them wanders by itself: over 45 seconds of ANDREA2 with the lamps' full
part (pull 1) her list held no lamp or one at a time, and the drawn direction turned by
more than 40 degrees from one second to the next in 27 of the 44 steps, by up to 104, and
stood within a degree of the 55-degree slant limit in 19 of the 45 seconds. The darkness
the lamps gave there, 0.28 to 0.43 and 0.32 on average, is what the fixed darkness, 0.45 x
0.75 = 0.34, stands near.

**How.** The arithmetic is one pure header, `specific/hd/hd_shadow.h` (new; no engine
header, like `hd_softbody.h`), with one table of the numbers that shape the look (map 512
texels, box 2048 units across and 2048 along the light, darkness 0.45, LOW 0.75, PULL 0,
W_REF 0.5, W_FALLBACK 0.15, the fixed slant 30 degrees, slant limit 55 degrees, TAU 0.5 s,
FULL 1024 and END 2048 units below her lowest node, EDGE 0.1, FACING 0.2, BIAS 8 units)
and the machinery under it. The key light, `HDShadowKeyTarget`, takes the pull as a last
parameter that defaults to the table's `HD_SHADOW_PULL` and is held to 0..1;
`HDShadowFollowLights` takes it the same way. Every sun, point and spot of her two engine
light lists (`HDObjectShadowLights`, `hd_object.cpp` - the dynamic lights are not in them,
so a gun flash does not swing it) gives a weight, its luminance times the model shader's
own falloff (`HDShadowFalloff`), and the direction it travels at her torso node; the key
light uses the weight times the pull. The weighted sum plus W_FALLBACK times the fixed
slant is made unit and held to the slant limit with its bearing kept (`HDShadowLimit`),
and a sum of nothing leaves the fixed slant exactly as `HDShadowFallback` gives it; the
darkness is DARK times LOW..1 by how far the pulled lights agree and how far their pulled
weight reaches W_REF. At pull 0 every product is 0, so the target is the fixed slant at
DARK x LOW, the same bits for any lights at any place, while the log's `lights=` and
`weight=` still count her list before the pull. The following, `HDShadowFollow`, tells her
movement from a change of the lights: `HDShadowFollowLights` weighs the frame's lights at
the last step's torso position with the same pull, and `HDShadowFollowStep` takes that
minus the last step's target, which is what the lights alone changed, into an offset and
lets the offset decay by exp(-dt / TAU) (`HDShadowDecay`) on a clock of its own on the
soft motion's `HDSoftClock`. The drawn direction is the frame's target plus the offset,
made unit and held to the slant limit, the drawn darkness the target's plus its offset
held to 0..DARK; with the lights unchanged - at pull 0 in every frame - the offset is
nothing and her own movement shows at once, and with a pull above 0 a change of the lights
reaches the new target along exp(-t / TAU), the same at 30, 60 and 165 frames a second.
The pause and the inventory stand the clock still. A level start, a load, a jump further
than she can move, a gap of a quarter of a second and the first frame after the shadow was
off snap and clear the offset; a step given only a target, with no measurement before it,
counts the whole change of the target as the lights'. The box (`HDShadowBasis`,
`HDShadowBoxMake`): right is fwd x (1, 0, 0), which cannot flip inside the slant limit;
the centre between her lowest and highest node, snapped to whole texels so a still light
does not let the outline crawl; one mapping, `HDShadowMapUVD`, as a matrix on view space
(`HDShadowViewToMap`) and as the cast's clip matrix with Direct3D 9's half-texel rule
(`HDShadowCastMatrix`). The gate, `HDShadowGate`: the option, the level drawn HD, Lara
drawn as the HD composite, her room drawn HD or counting as HD for her shadow
(`HDRoomShadowHD`: drawn as another group's art keeping no classic face she can stand on,
or with no classic face at all and no bare floor), and last the map. The receive side:
`HDShadowEdgeTerm`, `HDShadowHeightTerm`, `HDShadowFacingTerm`, `HDShadowLookup` (the 4 x
4 texels round the position weighted 1 - f, 1, 1, f along each axis, so the result is
continuous in the position), `HDShadowReceiveConstants` (the receive shader's seven
registers out of the same mapping) and `HDShadowReach` (the world box a room group must
touch to be drawn again). The mode: `HDShadowBlobMode` draws a stored 5 as the faded
circle, `HDShadowEffectiveMode` is 5 exactly when the gate is open. The shaders:
`hd_shader/hd_shadow.hlsl` (new) includes `hd_model.hlsl` and calls `ModelVS`, replacing
only the projection, and writes the depth into an R32F map, alpha-tested by the part's
page; `hd_shader/hd_shadow_receive.hlsl` (new) reads `RoomVS`'s outputs by semantic
(TEXCOORD0, 2 and 5), runs the range's alpha test, the three terms and the lookup in a
dynamic branch with explicit-level taps, and writes 1 - strength x lookup x terms; both
are compiled by `bshader.bat` and checked by `be.bat`; `hd_room.hlsl`, `hd_model.hlsl`,
`hd_glow.hlsl` and their `.inc` are untouched. `hd_render.cpp`:
`HDRenderShadowTargetReady` asks the adapter for R32F as a render target texture and D24X8
or D16 and their match before it makes the 512 texture and its own depth surface in
`D3DPOOL_DEFAULT`, and a refusal stands for the device's life; it is released by
`HDRenderShutdown`, which every path that drops the default pool takes - a lost device
before `Reset` and `DXClose` (also on Alt+Enter and a resolution change) through
`HDLevelDeviceLost` - and made again on the next frame that asks.
`HDRenderShadowCastBegin` and `End` read back and put back the render target, the depth
surface, the viewport, the scissor, thirteen render states, the shaders, the declaration,
stream 0, the indices, texture 0 and the constants the pass writes.
`HDRenderShadowReceiveBegin` sets `RoomVS` with the room path's buffers, the receive
shader and its registers c96 to c102 (above every register a room, gloss, glow or model
pixel shader names), the map on sampler stage 3 (point, clamp; no room or model draw
samples it), the depth test EQUAL with no depth write, the blend source ZERO, destination
SRCCOLOR, colour write RGB only, and - where the depth surface has a stencil, which the
engine's D24S8 has and never uses otherwise - clears the stencil and lets each pixel be
darkened once; `HDRenderRoomShadow` draws a group's opaque and alpha passes and its clear
floors again through `draw_receive`, with every vertex constant `draw_pass` writes per
range, its cull, its page (`receive_page`, the flipbook and book choice) and its alpha
reference, so `RoomVS` puts every triangle on the very depth it wrote;
`HDRenderShadowReceiveEnd` puts back every state Begin read and unbinds the map.
`hd_model.cpp`: the cast draw of a model, `HDModelCastBegin` and `HDModelCastDraw`, the
joints with the bind fold, the soft motion and the speaking face, passes 0 and 1.
`hd_object.cpp`: a mark on a frame-list entry - cast as well, or into the map only - set
by `HDObjectPush`'s two defaulted parameters, and `HDObjectCastFrame`. `hd_laradraw.cpp`:
`HDShadowFrameDecide`, the one decision of a frame, also asks for the receive shader;
`shadow_step` takes the key light and the box from her main draw's own matrices and the
frame's world-to-view (`aW2VMx`), weighing the lights at the last step's torso position
before the step; her main draw marks every part it pushes, and in first person the face
and the braid go into the map only, so the shadow keeps its head; `shadow_log` writes the
two state lines. `hd_level.cpp`: `ShadowCastPass`, then `ShadowReceivePass` - every room
group of the frame whose box, moved by its room's origin, touches the reach, again in the
windows and scissors `DrawRoomWindowed` used (`DrawRoomShadowWindowed`), only in a frame
whose map was drawn just now - and `ShadowSecond`, which ends its line in `lag=`, the
largest angle of the second between the drawn direction and the frame's target, 0 at pull
0; all three in `HDFrameDraw` after the room loop, the clear floors and
`HDRenderScissorOff`, before the models' solid passes. The shadow multiplies the finished
colour of the room, so the distance fog fades it with the floor; receivers never cast, so
a shadow that reaches past a wall falls on the floor beyond it as well (the height term
stops a storey below); a face turned away from the light is not darkened. The blob:
`specific/drawlara.cpp` calls `S_PrintShadow` only in a mirror's draw - where the HD
level's mirror has zeroed her slot's shadow size, so it draws nothing - or when
`HDShadowFrameDecide` says no; `specific/specificfx.cpp` reads the option through
`HDShadowBlobMode`. `tomb5/tomb5.cpp` and `global/types.h` for the default and the
comment. The row: `game/menu_frame.cpp` includes `hd_level.h` and `hd_shadow.h`;
`MenuShadowModeShown` is the stored value while `HDEnabled()` answers true - the *HD
textures* option and an installed Remaster, no level asked, so the title screen answers as
a level does - and `HDShadowBlobMode` of it otherwise; `MenuValShadowMode` shows 1
Original, 2 Circle, 3 Faded circle, 5 Projected and any other value PSX, and writes
nothing; `MenuStepShadowMode` steps from the shown value with 5 as the top while HD is on
and 4 while it is off, past the top to 1 and below 1 to the top, with the select sound and
the same storage as the rows beside it. `game/gameflow.cpp`: *Projected* in `CustomText`'s
table, German *Projiziert*, the English repeated in the French, Italian and Spanish
columns. A change reaches the running level on its next drawn frame: `HDShadowFrameDecide`
reads the option every frame, a frame without the projected shadow resets the following,
and the first step after that reset snaps. With `tomb5.hd_enable` 0 the HD path is not
reached and the stored 5 draws the faded circle; with the option on 1, 2, 3 or 4 the gate
answers `option` before anything touches the device, neither pass runs and the blob is the
one it was. The two passes cost under a tenth of a millisecond a frame at 2560 x 1440
(ModelProbe `-shadowtime` and `-shadowdevice`); ModelProbe `-shadowroom` with
`-shadowreceive` draws the shadow without the game. ModernTest's fourteen `shadow_*`
groups (`shadow_key`, `shadow_pull`, `shadow_fixed`, `shadow_follow`,
`shadow_follow_move`, `shadow_follow_lights`, `shadow_follow_both`, `shadow_follow_edges`,
`shadow_box`, `shadow_gate`, `shadow_terms`, `shadow_lookup`, `shadow_receive`,
`shadow_mode`) and MenuTest's `graphics_shadow_row` hold the rules.

**Decisions.** On by default. The four classic blobs stay selectable in HD too. The new
state of the *Shadow mode* row is reachable only while HD is on. The shadow's light is a
fixed one - one slant for the whole game, 30 degrees, and one darkness, 0.34 - so the
shadow moves only as she does; the lamps' part stays in the arithmetic behind one number
of the table, `HD_SHADOW_PULL`, set to 0, which multiplies every light's weight in the
direction and in the darkness alike, so that the lights' rule stays built and checked and
a pull between 0 and 1 mixes the two. The key light takes the pull as a defaulted last
parameter, so the engine's calls and the lines MenuTest reads stay as they were. With a
pull above 0, a change of the lights is blended over time and never stepped, the darkness
as well as the direction, while her own movement through the light is drawn at once, so
the shadow comes to rest the frame she does. The lights are told from her movement by
weighing the frame's lights where she stood in the last step, in a call of its own before
the step, so the step keeps its arguments; a step without that measurement counts every
change as the lights' and blends it, the soft side. The HD rooms and the statics that are
part of their art receive, and Lara casts. The receive draws the room groups again with
their own vertex shader and a pixel shader of its own, instead of a lookup inside the room
shader, which has no instruction slots left. The key light reads her two engine light
lists in world space rather than the model shader's view-space list, which cannot tell the
dynamic lights apart. The row asks `HDEnabled()` for HD, the setting and the installation,
not whether the level on screen is drawn HD, so it answers in the title screen too and
does not change with the room she stands in. With HD off a stored 5 is shown as what is
drawn for it and stepped from there, but not written back, so switching HD on again brings
*Projected* back.

### The projected shadow: the creatures cast as well, into a second map
2026-10-04

**What.** In a frame the projected shadow runs in, every creature and item the classic
engine gives a blob (its object's `shadow_size` is not 0) and that is drawn as an HD model
gives up its blob and throws a projected shadow along the same fixed light: it is drawn
into a second map beside Lara's, and the HD room groups take both maps in the one receive
pass. The second map reaches four sectors to every side of her and along the light; a
creature whose feet stand up to 819 units beyond its sides still casts what of it reaches
in, so its shadow fades out at the map's edge on every side, and a creature farther than
that has neither blob nor projected shadow. Its texels are of her map's size, so a
creature's outline is as soft as hers and its shadow as dark; where two shadows overlap
the floor is as dark as under one. A receiver up to OTHERS_FULL units behind a creature
along the light takes its whole shadow, from OTHERS_END on none (1536 and 2560 as this
change set them; *The projected shadow: its arrival, a block's depth and the fog bulbs'
haze* cuts them to 1024 and 1280). Lara's own shadow is the one of before, to the bit, and
so is every frame without a creature in the second box. An item drawn classic or baked
into a room's art keeps its blob, and so does every item when the frame list is full.
`HDLOG shadow second` gains `others=`, `omap=`, `orooms=` and `oms=` (the second cast
pass's time) at its end, and a new line, `HDLOG shadow others`, reports the second map's
target.

**Why.** With Lara's projected shadow in the room, the creatures beside her stood on round
blobs: two kinds of shadow under one light. Now they carry the shadow she carries. The
