object slots with a `shadow_size` (`game/setup.cpp`) are DARTS (drawn by `S_DrawDarts`,
which prints no blob), LARA (her own), SAS, BLUE_GUARD, SWAT, SWAT_PLUS, MAFIA, SCIENTIST,
CRANE_GUY, BLUE_GUARD2, ATTACK_SUB, LION, DOG, HUSKIE, CROW, REAPER, MAFIA2, PIERRE,
LARSON, HITMAN, CYBORG, SNIPER, CHEF, TWOGUN, HYDRA, IMP, WILLOWISP, MAZE_MONSTER,
SKELETON, GLADIATOR, ROMAN_GOD and ROMAN_GOD2 at 128, SAILOR at 85 and GREEN_TEETH at 256;
only those drawn by `DrawAnimatingItem` ever had a blob, and of the Tomb Raider III
imports only the vulture's slot, CROW 43, carries one.

**How.** The table (`specific/hd/hd_shadow.h`) gains OTHERS_MAP 2048 texels, OTHERS_BOX
8192 units across, OTHERS_MARGIN 0.1 of it, OTHERS_DEPTH 8192 along the light, OTHERS_FULL
and OTHERS_END, each with what it does to the picture; its numbers are this project's own
(OWN, ledger entry 171), each carrying this project's own reason or measurement
(OTHERS_BOX and OTHERS_DEPTH 8192 are 2048 texels of 4 units each, a texel of her map's
size). The box carries its own extent, depth and map size (`HDShadowBox`):
`hd_shadow_box_snap` snaps a centre to whole texels of the box's own map,
`HDShadowBoxMake` gives her box the table's BOX, DEPTH and MAP, `HDShadowBoxAround` makes
the second box round hers - the same light, basis and middle, snapped the same way, so
with texels of her size its centre is hers to the bit - and the mapping, the matrices, the
receive block and the reach read the box's own size; `HDShadowBoxHolds` says whether a
point lies inside the box grown by a margin, a part of its extent on each of its four
sides across the light and the same part of its depth on the two along it. The rule with
its two faces: an item's blob gives way when the projected shadow runs, her step ran, the
second target exists, the item is drawn HD and it is not mirrored; the item casts when it
also has a blob and its place lies inside the second box grown by OTHERS_MARGIN. The frame
(`HDShadowFrame`) gains `stepped`, the second box and its two matrices, filled by
`shadow_step` (`hd_laradraw.cpp`), `stepped` cleared every frame. The blob's one call,
`game/draw.cpp`, asks `HDObjectBlobGivesWay` (`hd_object.cpp`): her step first, the frame
second, then `begin_decision`, the decision `HDObjectBegin` acts on, must answer HD, then
the item must not be a reflection and the two-map receive shader, the cast shaders and the
second target must exist (the target and the variant as the frame's decision,
`HDShadowFrameDecide`, asked for them beside her map). `HDObjectBegin` takes the answer
over, and `HDObjectEnd` marks the entry for the second map when the item's place, its
world position, lies inside the grown box, with the node mask it is drawn with. The place
is one point, the feet; at the fixed slant a head 760 units above them lies 0.035 of the
box further in on its u = 1 side and 0.030 on its v = 0 side, so without the margin a
creature leaving the box there would lose a shadow still at 0.64 within ten units; the
margin, 819 units across the light, keeps it casting until no part of a caster up to 2160
units tall reaches into the box, the map's border clips the cast, and the edge term fades
what lies inside. The targets (`hd_render.cpp`): one road makes a pair,
`shadow_pair_make`, for hers and for the second (`HDRenderShadowOthersReady`, R32F 2048 x
2048 with a D24X8 or D16 depth surface of its own, 32 MiB in `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT`); a refusal
of the second leaves hers running; `HDRenderShadowTargetRelease` releases both, so every
road that drops hers drops the second; `ShadowCastOpen` opens the cast bracket on either
(`HDRenderShadowOthersCastBegin`). `ShadowOthersPass` (`hd_level.cpp`, called after hers)
draws the marked items with `HDObjectCastOthersFrame` - each body, or its swapped model,
and its separate face, with the cast draw her parts use - only when the shadow runs, her
step ran and an item is marked. The rooms: `hd_shader/hd_shadow_receive.hlsl` gains a
second entry point, `Receive2PS`: her part line for line as `ReceivePS`, and the second
map on sampler stage 4 with the registers c103 to c107 - the same sixteen taps and
weights, the edge term of the second box, the same facing term and, in place of her height
plane, a term per tap from how far the pixel lies behind that tap's caster, saturate(y - x
(depth - tap)); it writes the smaller of 1 - strength x hers and 1 - strength x theirs.
About 244 instruction slots (65 texture, 179 arithmetic); `bshader.bat` compiles it into
`hd_shadow_receive2_ps.inc` and `be.bat` checks it; the one-map receive's bytecode is
unchanged. Its arithmetic in the header: `HDShadowBehindTerm`, `HDShadowLookupBehind`,
`HDShadowReceiveFactor`, `HDShadowReceiveWithoutHer`, `HD_SHADOW_RECEIVE2_FIRST` and
`_COUNT`, `HDShadowReceiveOthersConstants` and `HDShadowReachOthers`, the second box's
prism from its near side to OTHERS_END beyond its far side. The draw: `receive_open`
serves `HDRenderShadowReceiveBegin` and `HDRenderShadowReceive2Begin`; the one-map Begin
makes exactly the calls it made, the two-map one remembers and sets stage 4 as well
(`receive_stage`) and the second block of registers, and `HDRenderShadowReceiveEnd` puts
stage 4 back; the variant is made beside the receive shader and asked by
`HDRenderShadowReceive2Ready`. `ShadowReceivePass` takes the variant in a frame whose
second map was drawn (`g_others_cast_now`, set by `ShadowOthersPass`) and then also draws
the groups within the second reach; should only the second map have been drawn, her block
is silenced, so a map an earlier frame left in her target is never read. The log:
`ShadowSecond` ends its line in the four new fields; `shadow_log` writes `HDLOG shadow
others` whenever the second target's state changes. The mirror pass zeroes `shadow_size`
around its items (`game/mirror.cpp`), and a reflection is a fact of the gate. With
`tomb5.hd_enable` 0, with the stored modes 1 to 4, for a classic Lara and in every frame
her main draw did not step, every blob is drawn as before (`stepped` is 0 there, the
gate's first fact). Receivers never cast, so a creature's shadow, like hers, passes
through a floor or a wall. With one creature the two passes and the two-map receive cost
about a hundredth of a millisecond more than hers alone at 2560 x 1440; ModelProbe
`-shadowcreature` with `-shadowroom` and `-shadowreceive` draws it without the game.
ModernTest's eight `shadow_others_*` groups (`box`, `margin`, `rule`, `gate`, `behind`,
`lookup`, `factor`, `receive`) hold the rules, among them that her box built through its
own size gives the old bits, the second lookup is hers bit for bit where every caster lies
within FULL, and the factor is hers bit for bit where the second map gives nothing.

**Decisions.** A second map beside hers rather than one larger map for both: her texel and
her picture stay as they were, and the second map has a texel of the same size, so the two
shadows match. Overlapping shadows take the darker of the two, not their product, so a
crowd does not blacken the floor. The two-map shader writes the smaller of the two
factors, the form in which her factor is `ReceivePS`'s own expression, so a pixel the
second map does not reach is that shader's pixel to the bit. The variant is a second entry
point of the same file, its own `.inc` beside the first. In place of her height plane,
which measures from her lowest node, each tap measures from its own caster, because the
second map holds many casters at many heights. A creature's place is its world position,
the point its blob is laid under; the box that place is asked against is grown across the
light by a fixed part of its width rather than by each caster's own height, one number
that covers every caster up to 2160 units tall, because the map's border clips the rest
and a caster with nothing inside costs one model in the cast pass and changes no pixel.
The blob gives way only on a device that has the variant, the cast shaders and the second
target, so it never gives way to a shadow that cannot be drawn. The receive draws the
groups within either reach; the second reach is the second box's prism with OTHERS_END
beyond its far side and no height bound. Should only the second map be drawn in a frame,
her block is silenced rather than her map read.

**Commits.** `1bb7ad5f` (creatures cast, blobs give way), `86fc680f` (the suites),
`6fe9b5ac` (rooms take both maps), `fc13d01f` (the suites), `7449693e` (the record),
`57a11610` (the corrections), `7871ca22` (the suites), `1d6e1289` (the record)

### The projected shadow on the HD models, in a mirror and from a creature out of view
2026-10-04

**What.** The HD models take the projected shadow as the rooms do: her outline falls on a
creature or an HD item that stands down-light of her, a creature's on her and on the HD
items, each at the darkness it has on the floor, and two shadows over one model are as
dark as one. A mirror's image shows the shadows of the room in front of it, reflected: the
copy behind the glass takes them at the place it reflects, and so do the reflections of
Lara and the items. A creature the picture has clipped away - its bounds outside the view
or its door's window - still casts into the second map, so its shadow lies on the floor
before the creature comes into view. The second map's shadow fades out over the box's near
and far side along the light as it does across it, so no creature loses its shadow in one
frame. Her shadow on herself, a creature's on itself or on another creature, and a second
light for walls turned away from the fixed one are not built; a creature's reflection
drawn classic takes nothing. `HDLOG shadow second` gains `models=`, `mcalls=`, `castonly=`
and `mirror=` at its end. The table gains one number, OTHERS_FADE.

**Why.** With the rooms darkened and the models not, a creature in her shadow stood lit on
a dark floor, and her outline stopped at its feet; the mirror's copy looked the maps up at
its own place behind the glass, where none of the shadows in front of it lie, instead of
at the place it reflects, and the reflections took none; and a creature walking into view
brought a strip of shadow with it at the screen's edge.

**How.** The number: `HD_SHADOW_OTHERS_FADE` 0.05 (`specific/hd/hd_shadow.h`), with what
it does to the picture and which way to turn it in the table's comment. The fade:
`HDShadowFadeTerm` weights each casting tap of the second map by saturate(min(tap, 1 -
tap) / OTHERS_FADE), exactly 1 in the box's middle, in `HDShadowLookupBehind` and in the
shaders' `OthersShade` (`hd_shader/hd_shadow_receive.hlsl`, the slope in c107.z);
`HDShadowBoxHolds` grows all six sides of the box by its margin, so a caster's mark holds
along the light as across it and the fade has eaten its shadow before the mark drops. The
second target is asked for in the frame's decision beside hers (`hd_laradraw.cpp`, read
through `HDShadowFrameOthersReady`), so its state line is written in the frame it changes
and no blob asks for a target; the receive pass reads `g_others_cast_now`. The models: who
takes which map is a pure rule of what an entry is (`HDShadowReceiverTakes`) - Lara's
pieces the second map only, never her own; an item whose object has a blob her map only,
never the one it is cast into; every other HD item both; the ring and the pickup display
nothing - and a block not taken is silenced through its u row
(`HDShadowReceiveWithoutHer`, `HDShadowReceiveWithoutOthers`), so one shader serves all
and reads no map it is not to read. `ModelReceivePS` is the two-map body on ModelVS's
outputs with ModelPS's three clips; `HDModelReceiveDraw` (`hd_model.cpp`) draws an entry
again with ModelVS, the same joints, neck cut, soft constants, lips stream, indices and
cull as the solid draw, the opaque and alpha ranges only; `HDRenderShadowModelsBegin`
(`hd_render.cpp`) sets EQUAL, no depth write, ZERO / SRCCOLOR, RGB and guards each pixel
with stencil bit 1, which the rooms' receive leaves 0; `HDObjectShadowReceiveFrame`
(`hd_object.cpp`) walks the frame list, tests each entry's bounding sphere
(`entry_sphere`) against the reach of the maps it takes (`HDShadowSphereTouches`), and
`ShadowModelsPass` (`hd_level.cpp`) runs it after the models' solid pass, only in a frame
whose rooms' receive ran. The mirror: for a mirror in the plane of constant `axis` at
`plane`, `HDShadowMirrorView` makes the reflected world-to-view R' = R S, t' = t - R S c
(S negates the axis, c is 2 plane on it); a pixel of the image at view position v stands
for the world point R'^T (v - t'), the place it reflects, so every receive block made with
R', t' is the block of the image - for the copy's art, drawn through the real view at the
image point, and for a reflection, whose node matrices the mirror's view puts at that same
view position. `HDShadowMirrorPlane` is the glass in view space, `HDShadowMirrorFaces`
whether the camera sees it from its room's side. The rooms: `ShadowReceivePass` draws a
mirror's group first with the mirror's blocks (`ShadowMirrorBlocks`) through a new
variant, `MirrorReceivePS`, which clips everything in front of the glass (c108,
`HD_SHADOW_RECEIVE_MIRROR`) and marks the copy's pixels in the guard's stencil bit, then
the group as every group, which the guard keeps off the copy;
`HDRenderShadowReceiveMirrorBegin` and `End` switch the shader and the blocks inside the
open receive and put the receive's own back. The reflections: `DrawOneMirror` hands the
seam its index (`game/mirror.cpp`) and, before it zeroes an item's `shadow_size` for the
draw, whether the object has a blob (`HDObjectReflectedBlob`); `HDObjectBegin` reads the
class from that, every entry recorded while the reflection is on carries its mirror, and
`HDObjectShadowReceiveFrame` gives it its mirror's blocks (`receive_blocks_mirror`),
taking its sphere back to the world through the same reflected view. Out of view:
`HDShadowItemWalk` is the rule of an item's node walk - a drawn item walks as always; a
clipped one walks for the second map alone when it is HD, its blob gave way and its place
lies inside the grown second box; every other clipped item walks nothing.
`DrawAnimatingItem` asks it through `HDObjectCastUnseen` (`game/draw.cpp`,
`hd_object.cpp`) and walks the nodes under `clip || unseen`, without
`CalculateObjectLighting` and without `InterpRootNow`; `HDObjectEnd` leaves the light out
for it and marks it `HD_OBJ_CAST_OTHERS_ONLY`, which the second map's cast pass draws and
no picture pass does. An item in a room that is not on the frame's list is never visited
and casts nothing; an item walked unseen takes a slot of the frame list, which holds 128.
The log: `ShadowSecond` ends its line in `models=`, `mcalls=`, `castonly=` and `mirror=`,
counted by `ShadowModelsPass` and `ShadowOthersPass`, and is called after the models' pass
so its line holds the whole frame. Builds: `bshader.bat` compiles the two new entry points
into `hd_shadow_receive_model_ps.inc` and `hd_shadow_receive_mirror_ps.inc`, and `be.bat`
checks them; `hd_room.hlsl`, `hd_model.hlsl`, `hd_glow.hlsl`, the cast shaders and the
one-map receive bytecode are untouched. With `tomb5.hd_enable` 0, the stored modes 1 to 4,
a classic Lara or a frame without her step, nothing of this runs: the gate stops the cast
passes, the models' pass runs only after a rooms' receive that ran, the second target is
asked only in a frame hers runs in, and an item clipped away walks nothing because its
blob never gave way; a frame without a mirror's group in the receive pass binds nothing
new. ModernTest's groups `shadow_others_fade`, `shadow_others_holds`, `shadow_takes`,
`shadow_mirror_view` (a point of the copy through the mirror's blocks gives its
reflection's place, both axes and both sides), `shadow_mirror_engine` (against the
engine's own `MirrorView` and `MirrorClipPlanes`) and `shadow_walk` (all sixteen cases)
hold the rules; ModelProbe's `-shadownomodels`, `-shadowcount`, `-shadowunseen`,
`-shadowmirrorview` and `-shadowmirrormask` draw and count them.

**Decisions.** Which maps a model takes is what it is, not whether it cast in the frame,
so a creature does not change its look as it walks into the second box; Lara never takes
her own map and a caster never the map it is cast into, because the fixed light is not the
light that lights them and a model's own outline would darken half of it. The models guard
with a stencil bit of their own, because the rooms' receive leaves its bit set on the room
pixels behind them. The mirror's image takes the same two maps through a reflected view
rather than maps of its own: nothing is cast twice, and the copy's art and the reflections
share one arithmetic. The copy is told from the room by the glass's plane in the pixel
shader and kept apart by the stencil guard; on a depth surface without a stencil the copy
takes the ordinary receive, and so it does while the mirror is seen from behind. A
reflection takes the class of what it reflects from the value the mirror's loop hands
over, not from `shadow_size`, which that loop zeroes so that a reflection has no blob and
casts nothing. The fade along the light is a fade of each tap's own caster depth, so a
caster in the box's middle casts as before. An item walked unseen takes the frame's own
root offset and no light: those belong to a drawn item and their counters to the picture.
The log's line is written after the models' pass, so `models=` and `mcalls=` count the
frame they belong to; the new fields are means over the frames the shadow ran, `mirror=` a
count over them. A second light for walls turned away from the fixed one is not built.

**Commits.** `d8c6d4db` (HD models take the shadow), `751f47fe` (the suites), `e7c382d9`
(mirror, unseen creature casts), `609f9119` (the suites), `fbc5ba8b` (the record),
`70ea4468` (second box's depth comment), `666773ba` (the record)

### The projected shadow: its arrival, a block's depth and the fog bulbs' haze
2026-10-11

**What.** Where the projected shadow starts to run - the Shadow mode row stepped to
Projected, HD switched on with it, Lara walking from a room drawn classic into an HD one,
the map made again after a lost device - it comes in over a quarter second of game time
instead of in one frame, and her blob and every creature's blob that gives way to it go
out over the same quarter second; the way back to the blob is one frame. The depth terms
are cut so that a floor a block or more below her soles, or about a block below a
creature's feet, takes nothing of the shadow - a storey under it, and the floor of the
room beside behind a wall - while the floor a creature stands on, a step and half a block
below it take its whole outline: the creatures' map keeps each creature's feet beside its
outline. The receive gives the fog bulbs' haze back: a shadow no longer stands dark inside
a glowing bulb. The shadow's log line times the models' pass and counts the arrival.
ModelProbe surveys where the shadow lands behind a face, draws the models' glows after
their receive and leaves its Resets out with rooms.

**Why.** The switch between blob and projection happened inside one picture; the shadow
reached through walls and floors; a shadow stood dark inside a glowing fog bulb. Surveyed
with ModelProbe `-shadowsurvey` on the thirteen levels' classic originals (23,063 floor
sectors as the place, a ray along the fixed light from every 32 units of three columns of
the body; the first face it meets takes the shadow, every face behind it that the terms
still weigh takes it through that face), at the old terms her shadow went through a wall
at 1,107 places and through a floor at 4,160, a creature's at 1,244 and 4,481, a third of
the rays through a wall landing in a room not joined to hers by a door; more than a block
below her feet the faces that should not take the shadow outnumbered those that should 1.7
to 1. The distance fog left the shadow's share at 0.578 of the floor's brightness at every
depth, but in a fog bulb in front of the shadow the floor kept only 0.575 of its
brightness where it now keeps 0.934.

**How.** The arrival: `HDShadowPresence` (`specific/hd/hd_shadow.h`) is 3f^2 - 2f^3 of f =
t / `HD_SHADOW_FADE_IN` 0.25, exactly 1 from there on; `HDShadowArrive` sets t back to 0
in a frame the shadow does not run in and adds the frame's game time in one it runs in;
`HDShadowBlobAlpha` scales a blob vertex's alpha byte, and a weight of 1 gives the colour
itself. `HDShadowFrameDecide` steps it on a clock of its own
(`specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp`), so her blob, drawn before her step, and the strength the
step draws (the following's strength times the presence) read the same value;
`HDShadowFrameBlob` draws her blob while the presence is below 1, the three `DrawLara`
variants ask it (`specific/drawlara.cpp`), and `HDShadowFrameBlobWeight` gives her blob's
weight. A creature: `HDObjectBlobGivesWay` (`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp`) lets it cast as
before and answers false while the presence is below 1, remembering the item and 1 minus
the presence for `HDObjectBlobWeight`, which `S_PrintCircleShadow` reads for the alpha of
every vertex (`specific/specificfx.cpp`). The way back is not faded: a frame the gate
refuses draws no map. The cut: `HD_SHADOW_FULL` 576 and `HD_SHADOW_END` 1088 below her
lowest node - half a block and a block below her soles, her ankle's 58.6 units rounded up
to 64 - and `HD_SHADOW_OTHERS_FULL` 1024 and `HD_SHADOW_OTHERS_END` 1280 behind a
creature's place; her reach shrinks with hers, and the second reach
(`HDShadowReachOthers`) runs OTHERS_END past the farthest place a caster may have,
OTHERS_MARGIN of the depth beyond the far side. A floor 1024, 1536, 2048 and 2560 below
the feet takes 0.011, 0, 0, 0 of her part (0.94, 0.44, 0, 0 at the old terms) and 0.38, 0,
0, 0 of a creature's feet (1, 0.77, 0.19, 0). A creature's part h above its feet darkens a
floor d below them 1.155 d + 0.289 h behind its place at the fixed slant, so every blob
carrier keeps its whole outline on its own floor and a step below, and every one up to
1,499 units tall half a block below (the blob carriers stand 691 to 809 units tall in
their rest pose, the sniper 907, the skeleton 1199, the Hydra 1249 and the Roman god 1546,
`-surveyslots`). A creature's place is its position, the point at its feet: `HDObjectEnd`
keeps its depth in the second box, `HDObjectCastOthersFrame` hands it to the cast through
`HDRenderShadowPlace` (`hd_render.cpp`, pixel c18, which the cast bracket saves and puts
back), `CastPS` writes it into the green channel (`hd_shader/hd_shadow.hlsl`) of the
second map, a G32R32F target (hers stays R32F), and `OthersShade` measures each tap's
distance from it (`hd_shader/hd_shadow_receive.hlsl`), as `HDShadowLookupBehind` does with
the places beside the depths. The fog: every receive variant ends in `ReceiveOut` - the
bulbs' haze, `BulbIntensity` copied from the room shader, summed and saturated as RoomPS
sums it, times gPass.w, times 1 - k in colour, k in alpha - and the two receive brackets
blend ONE / SRCALPHA (`HDRenderShadowReceiveBegin` and `HDRenderShadowModelsBegin`), so a
pixel is surface * k + haze; without a bulb the colour is 0 and the picture is the picture
times k. With the camera under water the haze given back is the bulbs' sum, not passed
through the water's scattering as the surface's is (`ReceiveOut`'s comment). The log:
`ShadowModelsPass` (`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`) times itself, and `HDLOG shadow second`
gains `mms=` and `arrive=` at its end. ModelProbe
(`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp`): `-shadowsurvey` with `-surveyplace`,
`-surveyrooms`, `-surveyterms`, `-surveyslots` and `-surveyout`, her term measured from
her lowest node and a creature's from its place, as the engine measures them; the
creatures' cast hands each place to the map, and `ShadowMapRead` reads the G32R32F map;
`-shadowpresence`, `-shadowfog`, `-shadowwith`; a receive picture draws the models'
additive passes after the room's glass and glows, where `HDFrameDrawGlow` draws them
(after `ShadowModelsPass`); `-shadowdevice` leaves its two Resets out when rooms hold
`D3DPOOL_DEFAULT` buffers (the rooms' vertex and index buffers, which the game drops with
the whole HD path at a device loss, `HDLevelDeviceLost`). ModernTest's `shadow_arrival`
and `shadow_cut` groups and the place's lookup in `shadow_others_lookup` hold the rules; a
frame without a transition, a bulb, a floor more than half a block below her soles or a
receiver past the old depths draws what it drew before. Receivers still never cast, so a
shadow reaches through a step or a low ledge onto the floor in front of it and through a
wall onto a floor less than a block below the feet; a creature whose HD draw falls back to
classic for one frame (a full frame list) switches without a fade.

**Decisions.** The way back from the projected shadow to the blob is not faded, because
the frame that cannot draw the shadow has no map. The cut is the table's four depth
numbers, not a rule by room: after it the room beside behind a wall took the shadow at 15
of 494 surveyed sector places, and a rule asking each range for a door to her room could
have cured at most 116 of those 243 rays and never a wall of her own room, where the worst
three stand. A creature's term measures from its feet, which the second map keeps beside
its outline: measured from each texel's own part, a cut of a block took a tall creature's
top off its own floor and a man's head off a floor a step below, and keeping OTHERS_FULL
at 1536 with a shorter OTHERS_END left a floor half again a block below in the shadow and
cut the creatures' wall weight by 46 per cent where the place cuts it by 80; the place
costs 16 MiB more of map and one register. A face turned away from the light takes no
shadow, even where the room's baked light lights it: a second light for such walls is not
built, and neither is a self-shadow on Lara. Classic rooms keep the blob and the classic
statics of an HD room do not receive: HD only. The log's times stay processor times, as
`ms=` and `oms=` are; the cards' times are the probe's.

**Commits.** `f9529ec` (comparison base), `c47591b` (comparison base), `6910dcfb` (fog
bulbs' haze back), `c62187fa` (quarter second, block down), `defef449` (log times, arrival
count), `dab41aee` (probe survey, glows last), `b67c5e71` (the suites), `b727a070` (the
record), `d48ae10b` (second map keeps place), `bfbd25be` (cut from feet, soles),
`483b14c8` (survey as engine measures), `9fec7e87` (the suites), `e3caad0e` (cut's comment
counts rays), `49e9aa94` (the record)

### The Mods folder: models, texture pages and sounds from a mod
2026-09-13 - 2026-09-14

**What.** The engine reads mods in the drop-in layout
`Mods\<Category>\<Mod>\{4,5}\{ITEM,TEX,DATA}`, which mirrors the installation's own
folders. A mod is a folder directly under `Mods`, or one level deeper, that has a `4` or a
`5` subfolder or a `mod.txt`; a name beginning with `_` is switched off at every depth,
which is the whole way back to vanilla and needs no uninstall. The order is the relative
path compared as lower-case ASCII, and that order is the priority. The scan runs once per
session and both the HD level build and `HQSfxOpen` ask for it, so the two see one list. A
mod may supply models (`.TRM`, resolved in front of the installs), texture pages, a whole
`MAIN.SFX` sound bank, and single replacement samples as loose `<NNNN>.wav` files -
exactly four digits, at any depth under an active mod, first active mod wins per number.
`OUTFIT_*.TRM` is refused as a replacement, because a mod's outfit is an entry in the
wardrobe scan. `mod.txt` may carry `origin=tr1|tr2|tr3`, which puts that game folder of
the Tomb Raider I-III bundle and its two siblings into the mod's page chain. The sound
half does not depend on `hd_enable`. `HQSfxOpen` walks three bank candidates: the first
active mod that ships `5\DATA\MAIN.SFX`, then `audio\MAIN.SFX`, then the installed
Remaster's own `5\DATA\MAIN.SFX` read where it lies, the third making a hand copy into
`audio\` unnecessary. Two further rules act on a mod's models. A weapon hand whose pages
resolve into the origin bundle is drawn on the install's own hands: the mod's triangles on
those pages are dropped and the install's file of the same name is loaded into a companion
slot cut to the pages it shares with `HAND_BARE_REST`, the two drawn together with the
same matrices, node mask and light. And a `.TRM` inventory model a mod brought over from
Tomb Raider I, II or III is put into the donor game's own pose before the ring fits it.

**Why.** A mod may never change a page of a model it did not supply: vanilla is
untouchable, and the mechanism makes that impossible rather than merely unlikely, which is
why the page namespace is arithmetic with compile-time assertions behind it. `origin=`
exists because a mod's model may name pages belonging to another game of the collection: a
measured hand model names 6111 and 6112, its own, and 8002 and 8010, which are Lara's skin
sheets of the I-III bundle, while in the IV-VI bundle those numbers hold other art
(`4\TEX\8002.DDS` is a cut-out sheet that reads 14.5 per cent holes) - without the line
the hand is painted with it, with it both pages come from `1\TEX` and read 0.0 per cent
holes. `4\DATA\MAIN.SFX` is deliberately not used: that is Tomb Raider IV's bank with its
own numbering. The plausibility rule that has guarded the HQ bank since #117 compares the
bank's sample against the level's own - at twice the rate the same recording must be about
twice as long, and anything further off than a fifth is a wrong pairing - and a sound mod
breaks it on purpose: at one measured sound id the unmodded bank holds 3388 bytes at 44100
Hz (0.038 s) against a mod's 28782 bytes at 48000 Hz (0.300 s), 7.81 times longer, and the
landing 1.64 times, so the rule as it stood would have refused precisely the samples the
mod exists to change. A mod's file is a stranger's file, so the bank and wav readers had
to be safe against a crafted one: `long` is 32 bit in this build, so a chunk guard written
`at + 8 + len > bytes` overflows to a negative number on a length near `LONG_MAX`, the
test comes out false, the cursor is driven negative and the next read lands about two
gigabytes below the buffer - a 60-byte file ended the process that way. A legal wav need
not begin with its format block: a `fact` or a `LIST` may stand in front of `fmt`, and the
shape audio workstations write is a 28-byte `JUNK` block first, so a `WAVEFORMATEX` laid
over offset 20 reads the middle of that header, the format test comes out false, the mod's
recording is dropped without a word and the log goes on claiming an overlay nobody will
hear; of six crafted files the gate accepts four and three of those have their format
block at +56, +48 and +28. Without the hand rule a mod's hand is painted with the donor
bundle's skin sheets and comes out looking gloved; the decision is made inside `hd_model`
and not by the caller, because only `hd_model` has the file open and the pages resolved,
and the twin's pages are cut against `HAND_BARE_REST` because that file's pages are skin
and nothing else, so the cut cannot bring the install's own gun in beside the mod's.
Without the classic pose a converted model stands in half a pose: a Remaster `.TRM` stores
each node's vertices with the classic mesh tree's offsets applied and no rotation at all,
the game it came from putting the rotation on when it draws out of the classic object's
own frame 0, so no turn of the rigid file can reproduce the picture the donor game draws.
Applied, the two guns of a mod's `UZI_OPTION` go from parallel to the crossed pair its
home game shows - the angle between their long axes from 0.0 to 65.5 degrees, the pair
from 132 units thick to 60, its overflow of the ring's place from 3.36x to 1.65x - and the
ammunition crosses the same way (0.2 to 42.1 degrees).

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_mods.cpp`/`.h` are the scanner, engine-free like `hd_install.cpp`
so the diagnostic tools link the same file; `winmain.cpp` starts it. The model resolver
sits in front of `find_model` (`hd_model.cpp`): the active mods in order, each `5\ITEM`
then `4\ITEM`, then the installs exactly as before - a replacement by resolution and never
on disk. The page namespace (`hd_pagecache.h`/`.cpp`) offers a mod's page to the cache as
`HD_PAGE_MOD_BASE + modIndex * HD_PAGE_MOD_STRIDE + page`, `HD_PAGE_MOD_BASE` = 0x50000000
and `HD_PAGE_MOD_STRIDE` = 0x00010000, so a mod's 6111 and the install's 6111 are two
cache slots holding two pictures; three `static_assert`s prove the three namespaces -
plain, the I-III bundle's `HD_PAGE_ALT_BASE` (0x40000000) and the mods' - cannot meet, and
a build in which they could fails to compile. A page a vanilla model asks for never
carries a mod key. The chain for a mod's page is the mod's own `5\TEX`, then its `4\TEX`,
then - only with `origin=` - that game folder of the I-III bundle and its two siblings,
then the ordinary IV-VI chain with the plain number, which lets a mod ship models and no
art. `hd_lara.cpp`'s rule that tells a weapon hand's gun from its skin ("every page this
model has that `HAND_BARE_REST` has not got is the weapon") strips the namespace and
compares page numbers. Sound: `specific/sfxbank.cpp`/`.h` hold the `MAIN.SFX` layout, the
chain walk that tests it, the RIFF check and the chain's order (`SfxBankChainLink`, lazy
so nothing pays for `HDInstallRoot()`'s walk through the registry and every game library
folder unless the link that needs it is reached), and both the engine and `SfxProbe` walk
that one order; `hqsfx.cpp`/`.h` keep the level bridge, the substitution and the log. A
loose `.wav` is checked the way the bank's own samples are - RIFF WAVE, uncompressed PCM,
mono, 16 bit, a `data` chunk inside the file - with a 4 MiB cap so a mistyped name cannot
pull a video into memory; without any bank there is no bridge from a level's sample number
to a bank number and the log says so once. The ruler is the first unmodded bank of the
chain, opened beside the mod's and never played from, walked through its own sound id
table rather than by sample number, because the two banks have different sample counts
(473 against 463 in the measured case) and nothing says a number means the same sound in
both; if the ruler's sample for this level sample is the right length the bridge is right
and the mod's recording plays whatever its length. The chunk guards subtract instead of
adding - `len > bytes - at - 8`, where the loop's invariant `at + 8 <= bytes` makes the
difference non-negative by construction - in `SfxRiffCheck` and in `SfxBankOpen`'s outer
chain walk, and a bad file is refused with `a chunk runs past the end of the file`.
`HQSfxPayload` goes through that same bounds-checked gate, which matters because a mod's
`5\DATA\MAIN.SFX` stands at the head of the chain and `SfxBankOpen` validates only the
outer chain of RIFFs. `SfxRiffCheck` hands back where it found the chunks as
`SfxRiffParts` and `HQSfxPayload` passes that on; `LoadSamples` (`specific/file.cpp`)
reads the format block at `parts.fmtAt` and the audio at `parts.dataAt` and takes the PCM
branch on `hq` alone, because everything the payload path returns has already been shown
to be mono 16-bit PCM, and the contract that makes `HQSfxSubstituted()` and
`HQSfxOverlaid()` true by construction is written into `hqsfx.h`. The level's own samples
are untouched - their tag is still read at 20, and the one call that still lays a
`WAVEFORMATEX` over offset 20, `DXCreateSampleADPCM`, is only ever handed
`samples_buffer`, which no mod can reach; the two walks differ in one point (`file.cpp`'s
breaks at the first `data` chunk, `SfxRiffCheck`'s reports the last) and over 1409 samples
of three banks and five loose files not one has a second `data` chunk, a second `fmt`, or
a `fmt` anywhere but +20. The hand rule: `hd_model.cpp` asks `HDPageCacheOriginOf`, which
calls `resolve_page` and loads nothing, for where each of a model's pages really resolves
(`hd_pagecache.cpp`/`.h` export it); measured on one level with nine mods, the mod's hand
keeps 2 pages and 31,267 vertices on nodes 10 and 13, the install's twin brings 1 page,
and the mod's holster model stays whole at 27,624 vertices on nodes 1 and 4. The twin is
counted in every column of the part line - vertices, indices, ranges, pages and both byte
counts, about 155 KiB of buffer under one Uzi mod - its own fold counters are printed
there, and its second `.TRM` read is counted into `read_ms`; the twin's page cut and a
caller's own `onlyPage` cut are one mechanism, combined as a DROP set with a line in the
log, because dropping every page of a file is representable and keeping none of it is not.
The classic pose: `specific/hd/hd_classic.cpp`/`.h` is engine-free, plain C on the
outside, with no engine global and no `Log`; it walks `<I-III bundle>/<game>/DATA` in name
order until a level file holds the object with at least one mesh and hands back the mesh
count, the bones, frame 0 and the level file it used, every count read out of a file
checked against the bytes that are left and the texture pages seeked past rather than
loaded, one parse per (game, id) per session with refusals cached. The three level layouts
are the published TR1/TR2/TR3 formats; the `.TRM` says which node a vertex rides on and
the classic level file says where the mesh tree puts that node, and both are the player's
own data files - nothing of any Remaster binary is in it. Two format facts were settled by
measurement against the files' own data: in a TR1 frame the SECOND of the two rotation
words is the high half (read that way the walk reproduces the frames' own bounding boxes
to 2.1 units at worst over the eight weapon and ammunition objects of `1/DATA/GYM.PHD`,
against 50 to 107 units the other way, and Tomb Raider 1's object 102 then gives the same
rotations, bones and bounds as Tomb Raider 2's 160 and Tomb Raider 3's 188), and the pose
is `phd_RotYXZ` (y, then x, then z) with the point taken as a column and the frame's
offset part of the pose, reproducing those boxes to 2.1 units where the next family of
conventions misses by 40.8 and the worst by 184.7. "The first level in name order" is a
rule and holds: over the eight option objects of games 1 and 2 every level file that holds
the object holds the same mesh count, bones and frame 0, and game 3 agrees on 17 of its
20, the three exceptions being `TITLE.TR2` and `AREA51.TR2` carrying a stub or a
left-over. The pose is applied in `hd_model.cpp` where the mirror fold is, right after the
`.TRM` is read and before `build()` takes the box and the principal axes, and it is real
skinning - three nodes, three weights, normals turned and re-normalised; it refuses with a
line unless the model came from a mod with an `origin=` game, its name is in the table,
and the classic object's mesh count IS the `.TRM`'s node count, which is the proof that
the two belong together because a `.TRM`'s bone numbers are classic mesh numbers. The
table in `hd_classic.cpp` has thirteen rows - the four weapons and the ammunition boxes
under the donor games' own names and under this engine's slot names - and its object ids
come from GPL sources: TR3's out of the **tomb3** sources (`game/objects.h`), TR1's and
TR2's out of the **TRX** project (LostArtefacts), `catalog_objects.csv`, whose TR3 column
agrees with tomb3 on every id; each was then found in the player's own installation. Cost,
whole process: 85 to 93 ms once per (game, id) per session. Seams behind `-log`: `MODLOG
folder=` (with `mods=` on both branches), one `MODLOG mod<i> path= origin= models= pages=
bank= wavs=` per mod, `MODLOG disabled <path>`, `MODLOG model <NAME> <- mod<i>` once per
replaced model per session, written where `find_model` accepts the answer and keyed by
name and mod so a face looked up for a body from another mod cannot log a replacement that
was never drawn, `MODLOG page mod<i>:<n> comes from ...`, `MODLOG bank <label> (<path>) -
opened/not opened`, `MODLOG bank ruler:`, `MODLOG bridge:`, `MODLOG bank sample <n> ...`,
`MODLOG wav <nnnn> <- mod<i>` and `MODLOG wav <nnnn> refused - <why>`; a mod page prints
as `mod<i>:<n>` wherever a page number is printed, `HDLOG models` gained a `mod:` column
and `HDLOG models budget` a `frommod=`, the `HQ SFX:` summary line names the bank really
used, and `HDLOG classic <game>/<level> object <id> meshes=.. bones=.. frame0 ..`, its
refusal, and `HDLOG level=.. ring pose slot=.. model=.. classic=<game>/<level>#<id>
nodes=.. applied (box .. -> ..)` or `not posed: <why>` cover the pose. Tools: `ModelProbe
-mods <folder>`, `-tr3 <3-folder>`, `-nohandmix`, `-classicpose <game> <MODEL_NAME>`,
`-noclassicpose`, with the page list naming the folder every page was really read from;
`SfxProbe` and `bsfx.bat` are new, `-samples` pushing every sample of the chosen bank and
of the ruler through the gate with a `layout` line per accepted file. Both tools link the
engine's own files. Not supported and documented as such in the README: a mod that ships
`<NAME>_HEAD.TRM` without the body's `<NAME>.TRM` is inert, because a face is resolved
wherever its body came from so that the two wear pages from one source. Files:
`specific/hd/hd_mods.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_model.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_pagecache.cpp`/`.h`,
`hd_classic.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_lara.cpp`/`.h`, `hd_bind.cpp`, `hd_object.cpp`,
`specific/hqsfx.cpp`/`.h`, `specific/sfxbank.cpp`/`.h`, `specific/file.cpp`,
`specific/winmain.cpp`, `tomb5.vcxproj`, `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp`,
`SfxProbe.cpp`, `bsfx.bat`, `bmap.bat`, `bmodel.bat`, `broom.bat`, `btrg.bat`,
`Preparation/Tools/README.md`, `README.md`.

**Decisions.** A page a mod's model shares with the install is loaded twice, +4 pages and
+5.3 MiB on one wardrobe (21 to 25 pages, 28.0 to 33.3 MiB) and nothing on the whole
level; sharing the slot would be safe, but the rule that a mod's model never shares a slot
with a vanilla one is worth more than 1.5 per cent of a wardrobe.

**Commits.** `8156128` (the Mods folder), `1ca834e` (docs: a Mods section), `d67ea4a`
(crafted .wav cannot crash), `20318c7` (format block where stated), `6a2bef2` (bare hands,
weights folded), `0947713` (three numbers re-measured), `260a844` (donor game's frame 0),
`247fee5` (ModelProbe prints the pose), `b80c407` (what an origin buys), `f48e890`
(classic reader's cost)

### Imported enemy sounds are named in the sidecar, not guessed at by length
2026-09-13

**What.** A run that imports a Tomb Raider III enemy writes the sound ids it wrote into
the level as one `sfximport <id> <id> ...` line in the `.hdm` sidecar, ascending out of a
`std::set` so that the same seed gives the same file, and no line at all in a run that
imported nothing. The HQ sound bridge refuses to pair those ids with the Remaster's bank
and writes a line for each; ids the run merely moved between TR5 levels are not in the
list and keep their pairing. Beside that the bridge works out, from the level's own sound
map alone, which of the bank's 64 level bits is the level being loaded - the bit whose ids
cover this level's and no others, every id the level has and the bit claims counting for
it and every one it does not counting against it - and writes a line for every pairing
that bit excludes. The sidecar is read above the HD gate, so the list is in force in the
shipping build with `hd_enable` off.

**Why.** The guests take free slots of the TR5 sound map - the vulture 420..423, the Compy
430..434, the raptor 438..444, the T-Rex 445..449 - and free means free in a TR5 level; it
says nothing about the Remaster's bank, where ids 418..423 are six voice lines. The bridge
pairs by sound id and judges a pairing by length, and a length cannot tell a wrong pairing
from a different recording: on one randomized level the level's own 420, 421 and 423 (322,
425 and 406 ms) were refused against the bank's 624, 624 and 1037 ms, but 422 at 604 ms
against the bank's 624 was accepted at 1.03 times the expected length, so an imported
vulture died speaking an English voice line. A mod's bank with 390 sound ids against the
install's 396 simply has not got 418..423. A length cannot decide this and a name can: the
run knows exactly which ids it wrote. The level bit is worked out and not tabulated,
because a table of level names would be silently wrong about a randomized level or a level
pack, and it is sound: over all sixteen classic levels each matches exactly one bit and
matches it completely while the runner-up covers at most two thirds (ANDREA1 bit 1,
ANDREA2 2, ANDREA3 3, JOBY2 4, JOBY3 5, JOBY4 6, JOBY5 7, ANDY1 8, ANDY2 9, ANDY3 10,
RICH1 11, RICH2 12, RICH3 14); on one randomized level it names 32 excluded pairings,
every one an enemy the run moved there. The sidecar is read above the HD gate because it
is a level fact and not an HD fact: read below it the list is empty with `hd_enable` off
while the bank chain the refusal protects is deliberately not gated, since sound does not
care whether `hd_enable` is on, so the wrong pairing would come back with the summary
reporting nought imported ids - and no tool could show it, because a tool calls the
sidecar loader unconditionally by construction.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_markers.cpp`/`.h` read the `sfximport` line and answer
`HDMarkersSoundImported`. `hd_level.cpp`/`.h` call `HDMarkersLoad` above the `HDEnabled()`
gate; the other half of the bracket, `HDMarkersFree` in `HDLevelUnload`, is not gated. The
order is unchanged and all on the load thread: `FreeLevel` -> `HDMarkersFree`,
`HDLevelLoad` -> `HDMarkersLoad`, then `LoadSamples` -> `HQSfxBuildMap` -> the refusal.
`specific/hqsfx.cpp`/`.h` hold the bridge and the refusal lines; `SfxBankLevelBit` and
`SfxPairPlausible` live in `specific/sfxbank.cpp`/`.h`, so a tool judges a pairing with
the engine's own arithmetic rather than a copy, and the mask counter counts first and
prints second, so the summary is not capped at the 32 lines it prints. On the writing
side, `TR5Randomizer/src/core/Tr5Level.cpp`/`.h` collect the ids and `core/ApplyPatch.cpp`
writes the line, the slot ranges being `Tr5Source::dinos`; an engine older than this has
no rule for the word and ignores the line, which is what the sidecar format was built for.
Tool: `SfxProbe -level <path.trc>` reads a finished level and the sidecar beside it and
prints the whole decision table, `-samples` checks the bank's 473 samples, and
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/bsfx.bat` builds it.

**Commits.** `2b88f8c` (the vulture's English line), `52c6f0e` (refusal inert in shipping
build), `a0e5939` (the headroom it owed)

### The font in HD
2026-09-09

**What.** Every line of text the game draws - the title menu, the names under the
inventory ring, the options pages, the load and save lists, the statistics, the ammunition
counter, the name of a pickup, the subtitles of a cutscene - is drawn from the Remaster's
2048 x 2048 font atlas when it is installed, through one branch in `DrawChar`
(`game/text.cpp`). Position, size, `FontShades` colour and specular stay the classic ones,
because they stay the classic code. Thirteen of the 106 glyph rectangles keep the classic
picture: the twelve PlayStation pad icons, which the atlas does not carry, and the
c-cedilla.

**Why.** All text in the engine comes out of ONE 256 x 256 page and ONE table of 106
rectangles, so a single branch covers every text path and there is no second one to
forget. The big atlas is a new drawing and not the small picture times eight: shrunk back
to 256 with an 8 x 8 box filter it differs from `FONT0_OG.DDS` in 12.6 per cent of the
texels of the matched rectangles, its letters reach up to three classic texels past the
eightfold rectangle, and it carries a dark rim and a drop shadow the small one has not
(over the 93 matched glyphs, fully opaque texels have a mean brightness of 224 of 255 and
the half-transparent ones 44), which is what makes white letters readable over a bright
wall.

**How.** The page is the same in every level - one MD5 over all sixteen shipped `.TRC`
files, the title included - so the match runs once in a session and every further level
load is a comparison of that MD5 (`HDFontLevelPage`, `specific/hd/hd_font.cpp`); it is
keyed on the page and not on a flag, so a level file carrying a different font page would
be matched again rather than drawn with another alphabet's table. Matching: the classic
rectangle's ink mask is slid over `5\TEX\FONT0_OG.DDS` (256 x 256, uncompressed B8G8R8A8,
the classic glyph bitmaps re-typeset in ASCII order) and scored intersection over union
(`specific/hd/hd_fontmatch.cpp`, `HDFontMatchAll`), accepted at 0.94 and above. The idea
and the threshold come from TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931, and the reason too: a similar character is the wrong
character. 93 of the 106 rectangles are found, 92 at score 1.000 and the K at 0.975;
`FONT1` is checked in the same run and matches 22 - it is a Cyrillic alphabet and those 22
are the letters both scripts draw alike - so which atlas is used is decided by the count
and not by the file's name, and an installation that ships them the other way round still
works. Drawing: `5\TEX\FONT0.DDS` is 2048 x 2048, BC7, six mip levels, the same alphabet
in the same places at eight times the size, so a normalised coordinate on the one is a
normalised coordinate on the other and the glyph sits at the same place plus a whole
number of classic texels; the UV is therefore not recomputed but SHIFTED by that number,
and rendered classic and HD the texels a screen pixel walks agree to 1.6e-06 relative. The
margin is per glyph: the classic arithmetic samples the rectangle inset by half a texel on
each side, which the classic page needs because it packs its glyphs with no gap, and at
eight times the size that inset is four HD texels and cuts off exactly the antialiased rim
and the drop shadow, 12.6 per cent of a glyph's ink; the sampling window and the quad are
widened by the same fraction of themselves (the rule of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931), which changes what is visible and not where anything
is. A uniform margin does not work - at every margin from half a texel upwards a slice of
the neighbouring tick appears beside the apostrophe and beside the comma - so
`HDFontMargins` works out per glyph how far the window may open before it touches another
letter, with one texel as the ceiling: 90 of the 93 get the whole texel, the apostrophe
0.25, the asterisk and the comma 0.125, none gets zero. The flood fill runs over WHITE
ink, which the dark shadow between two letters separates where alpha does not; it runs on
the big picture and is seeded from the classic page's ink rather than from the whole
matched rectangle, because a neighbour's larger letter can reach a texel or two into that
rectangle. Accents keep their classic arithmetic: `PrintString` composes an accented
letter from two ordinary glyphs - the base at the letter's place and the mark at `def->w /
2 + x - 3, y + def->YOffset` - and each goes through `DrawChar` on its own, so the
relative position between them is the classic one. Colour and alpha needed no change: the
engine multiplies the texture by the vertex colour and adds the specular half
(`D3DTOP_MODULATE` with `D3DTA_DIFFUSE`, `specific/function_table.cpp`), the atlas's ink
is white so it takes that colour as the classic page's white ink does, the dark rim stays
dark whatever it is multiplied by, and `D3DRS_ALPHAREF` is 0 with `D3DCMP_NOTEQUAL`, so
the alpha test throws away only what is completely transparent. `Textures[]` must not
grow, because the font is addressed as `nTextures - 2`, the sky as `- 1` and the two title
pages as `- 4` and `- 5`, so the glyph quad carries `HD_FONT_TPAGE` = 4096, which is not
an index at all, and `HWR_DrawSortList` (`specific/polyinsert.cpp`) turns it into the font
texture before any of its cases can read `Textures[4096]`; nothing else can write that
number, a tpage being otherwise always an index and `LoadTextures` refusing a level with
more than the 256 entries the array has, and the sort list already groups by tpage, so
every glyph of a frame ends up in one draw call. Mips and a LOD bias: at 1920 x 1080 a
thirteen-texel glyph is drawn 58 pixels high out of 104 atlas texels, so the atlas is
minified by 1.8 - by 2.7 at 1280 x 720 and 1.35 at 2560 x 1440 - and without mips that is
a bilinear undersample in which thin strokes crawl, so the whole six-level chain out of
the `.DDS` is uploaded and the draw sets `D3DTEXF_LINEAR` with `D3DSAMP_MIPMAPLODBIAS`
-0.7, which lands at level 0.14 at 1080p and 0 at 1440p, the sampler states being put back
the way the classic path keeps them the moment the call returns; the three minification
figures are this project's own measurement and the bias -0.7 is the number of TROne
(GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931, cited as such in
`specific/polyinsert.cpp`. Where it lives: `game/chardef.inc` holds the 106 rectangles,
moved out of `text.cpp` unchanged, and `game/accent.inc` the 46 accented letters, so the
engine, the HD font and `FontProbe` read the same numbers; `specific/hd/hd_fontmatch.cpp`
holds the matcher, the margins, an uncompressed-DDS reader and an MD5 with no engine
dependency at all, so `FontProbe` compiles that very file; `specific/hd/hd_font.cpp` finds
the atlas, runs the match on the load thread, makes the texture on the main thread and
answers `DrawChar`'s one question; `game/text.cpp` gains one branch,
`specific/polyinsert.cpp` one, and `specific/file.cpp` two lines - the font page to the
matcher where it is read, and `HDFontBuild` beside `HDLevelBuild`. Seam: `HDLOG font
atlas=FONT0 matched=93/106 below=13 page=<hash>`, one line per glyph that did not make it
with its score, and one line saying how many glyphs got the whole margin. Classic path:
`HDFontLevelPage` returns at its first line with `hd_enable` off, so no file is opened and
not a byte of the page is copied, `g_matched` stays false, `HDFontBuild` returns, there is
no texture, `HDFontGlyphAt` returns 0 on its first test, and `DrawChar` runs the same
arithmetic with the same `tex.tpage = nTextures - 2`, while `HWR_DrawSortList`'s new
branch tests for a tpage no quad can then carry; `fps_mode` is not touched. Files:
`game/text.cpp`, `game/chardef.inc`, `game/accent.inc`, `specific/hd/hd_font.cpp`/`.h`,
`hd_fontmatch.cpp`/`.h`, `specific/polyinsert.cpp`, `specific/file.cpp`,
`specific/function_table.cpp`, `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/FontProbe.cpp`.

**Commits.** `a1a22cb` (the font in HD)

### Where the HD rules come from, counted on our own data
2026-10-06

**What.** Every rule of the HD path that came by way of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931 or of TRForge (MIT) carries this project's own evidence,
is declared this project's free choice, is credited to its source under that source's
licence, or is gone; `THIRD-PARTY.md` keeps the list as an origin ledger of 39 entries,
each with its class and its evidence. Five `TrgProbe` switches count the rules on the
player's own files: `-shadeorder` (how the two colour triples of a `.TRG` vertex make the
room light), `-uvbytes` (which bytes are u, v and the layer), `-normals` and `-trmnormals`
(the normal bias of a `.TRG` and of a `.TRM`, and the sway range) and `-ddssizes` (the
size of every page). With the room light settled as the SUM by that count, the room shader
drops the spare scale it carried on the first triple, the one place where a scale with no
count of this project's stood in the code; the room vertex shader reads nothing of `c4`,
which `fxc` gives a literal of its own, so the room passes write `c4` to the pixel file
alone. `HDScanPagePath` no longer tries `<n>_2048.DDS` and `<n>_1024.DDS` for ids
8000..8499, a branch that never applies. `vendor/trforge/src/trf_remaster/Trg.h` leaves
out its two prose passages over the vertex and over the point lights, and its dangling
"see below"; `VERSION.txt` and `NOTICE.md` say so with the new hash. Sentences that stated
a rule without its count become the file facts they rest on; a citation into the files of
another project names the function it falls in and the copy it was read in, never a line
number; sentences about another project's state are dated. The picture of the game is the
same.

**Why.** Four rules of the HD path that came from those two sources stood in this tree as
plain prose rules and nowhere as code, an address, a table or shader text: the room light
as `colour1 * factor + colour2` with the factor at 1 (from TROne (GPLv3) by
Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931); which bytes of a `.TRG` vertex are u,
v and the biased normal (TRForge's names); which of material 16's `param[0]` and
`param[2]` is the ripple's scale and which its rate (the order named in TROne's prose);
and `param[0]` of materials 6, 7 and 8 as the cut-out threshold. The first three had no
evidence of this project's own; the fourth already had its own count here. The vendored
`Trg.h` carried prose passages over the vertex and the point lights besides. Beside them
stood numbers with no stated origin - eleven pages "of 4096x4096" (they are 4096x2048),
the slot names "strength, scale, scale" of materials 7 and 8, the three-resolution id
range of TRForge's - and a shortened origin note over material 16's order.

**How.** `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/TrgProbe.cpp`: `classicRoomData` walks a classic
room's 28-byte vertices and faces straight out of the `.TRC` the way `Tr5Level::roomFaces`
does and keeps each vertex's prelight, the colour `aRoomletTransformLight` lights it with;
`dumpShadeOrder` pairs them with the `.TRG` vertices of the same group at the same
room-local position (several `.TRG` vertices at one position are averaged) and prints, per
level and over all, the Spearman rank correlation of the classic shade with `c1+c2`,
`c1*c2`, `c1` and `c2` (each the sum of its three channels), the agree / disagree / tie
counts over 200,000 sampled vertex pairs, and the pairs that sum and product put in
opposite order with the side the classic shade takes; `dumpUvBytes` interpolates the
classic texinfo's u and v at every `.TRG` vertex lying inside one classic face (in its
plane, inside one of its two triangles with a margin of 0.02), counts per face the order
of every two vertices under the classic coordinate against the byte, fits each byte on the
classic (u, v) and holds the fits of the faces wearing one texinfo against each other;
`dumpTrgNormals` and `dumpTrmNormals` hold every triangle corner's normal against the
triangle's plane; `dumpDdsSizes` reads the width and height of every `.DDS` header. The
counts on the player's files: of the 126,170 classic room vertices of the fifteen levels
107,118 have a `.TRG` vertex of their own group at exactly their position, and the sum
orders them by the classic prelight better than the product in 14 of the 15 levels and
over all of them (rank correlation 0.553 against 0.460), and better than either triple
over all (0.397 and 0.527); JOBY4, the sea, orders by none of the four; `c1+c2` reaches
exactly 2.0 in eleven files and lies above 1 in 3.3 % of the 39,788,013 channels; no scale
on either triple can change these rank counts. On the 475,529 `.TRG` vertices inside
15,999 classic faces the byte at +15 follows the classic u (3,157,175 pairs agree,
1,465,989 disagree) and the byte at +19 the classic v (3,354,530 against 1,340,180), while
the crossed readings split evenly; the bytes run over 0..255 in every file and the layer
from 1 to the file's own texture count. The remaster does not keep one place per classic
tile (246 of 1,263 texinfos met on two faces or more put their corners at one place on one
page within three steps), so only the order within a face carries the reading. Of the
45,170,724 `.TRG` triangle corners 53.9 % lie within 10 degrees of their triangle's normal
read as biased by 127, 0.5 % read as signed (38.1 % against 0.6 % over the 565 `.TRM` of
`5\ITEM`), almost all on the side opposite the winding's cross product, a convention of
the files; the sway field runs 0..32767. No page of the bundle's three `TEX` folders is
4096x4096 or wider than 4096; the 70 files named `<n>_1024.DDS` or `<n>_2048.DDS` are 35
ids from 8001 to 8432, all in the I-III bundle's `1\TEX`, every one beside its plain
`<n>.DDS`. Materials 6, 7 and 8 over the fifteen levels carry `param[0]` 0.5 in 42 of
their 44 tuples (the other two ANDY1's 0.503 on material 6 and ANDY2's 0.12 on material
8). In the code: `specific/hd/hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl`: `o.light = lerp(inC0.rgb +
inC1.rgb, 1.0f, gFlat.x)`; the header, the light note and the register note name the
count. `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`: `gPass.z` is written 0 and `c4` goes to the pixel file
only; `MaterialRipple` states the order of scale and rate as a free choice and the
ripple's structure as the design of TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931 (also `PartUvSpan`, and `hd_room.hlsl`'s ripple note);
the material list names the ranges of materials 7 and 8 in place of slot names.
`specific/hd/hd_scan.cpp`: the plain page name only. The page sizes: `hd_render.cpp`,
`hd_level.cpp`'s `kWidestPage` note, `hd_pagecache.cpp`'s staging and batch notes,
`hd_memory.h`. The water surface the `.TRG` has no geometry for: the notes in
`hd_level.cpp` say 0 of 13 levels, 61 of 93 reflecting rooms. `hd_pagecache.cpp`:
`WHITE.DDS`, the install's white tile in `4\TEX`, and the cut-out threshold, 42 of 44
tuples. Credits to TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931:
its measurement of a facial rig's inverse binds (`hd_trm.h`, `hd_trm.cpp`), its six
default control constants (`game/modern_move.h`), its ripple design, its caustic shape and
scale with the strength 0.32 named as this project's, and the notice in `hd_wardrobe.h`.
Citations by function and copy in `hd_render.cpp/.h`, `hd_model.cpp/.h`,
`hd_object.cpp/.h`, `hd_lara.cpp/.h`, `hd_laradraw.cpp`, `hd_level.cpp`,
`hd_fontmatch.cpp`, `hd_pagecache.cpp`, `hd_room.hlsl`, `hd_model.hlsl`, `game/draw.cpp`,
`specific/polyinsert.cpp`, `game/modern_move.cpp`, `game/modern_camera.h` and
`ModernTest.cpp`. `vendor/trforge/src/trf_remaster/Trg.h` carries the one-line notes.
Apart from the factor in `hd_room.hlsl` and `hd_room_vs.inc`, the three `c4` writes fewer
in `hd_render.cpp`, the page name in `hd_scan.cpp` and `TrgProbe.cpp`, every changed
source is the same to the token with its comments stripped.

**Decisions.** The room light is the sum because the rank counts order the vertices by it;
a picture compared against a reference frame cannot tell the sum from a scaled other rule
and is not the evidence. Which of material 16's `param[0]` and `param[2]` is the scale and
which the rate stays a free choice of this project, with no measurement behind it.

**Commits.** `8877f88` (comparison base), `2feea83` (room light measured, factor goes),
`a0b439d` (plain page name only), `e6d1a7f` (Trg.h without the prose), `7e9d977`
(citations by function and copy), `97f322c` (missing credits added), `803d210` (comments
name their counts), `20ffb9c` (the suites), `d27639c` (TrgProbe names refused .TRM),
`46c6735` (room shader with true counts), `a74e780` (material counts in one unit),
`a42e4e4` (ring cites by function), `885ef33` (the remaining lows), `e69455b` (six places
outside)

### The water sheets: this project's own water surface
2026-10-07 to 2026-10-21

**What.** Every water square of an HD level that lies over an underwater room, in a room
drawn HD, gets a water surface of this project's own design, built at level load from the
classic level's data: a *sheet*, a moving grid that reflects, shows the floor under it
bent and tinted by the water, and foams at its banks. A water plane with no underwater
room below keeps the level's restored classic faces. With the sheet come: eight wave rows
broken into short crest pieces; the rings of the game's own ripples; bank foam in patches,
drawn in a pass of its own; rivers and streams with a visible flow; a foam zone at the
foot of a waterfall; the look under the water (an extinction with a clear zone round the
camera, the deep look of a sea level, and the sea's surface seen from below with its
sheet, its sun glow and its light shafts); the HD splash of a dive and of a breaking fish
tank (cards, a film on the floor, the dome, the burst at the glass); the wet floor a shot
tank leaves, with its own mirror; the water's life (floats, schools of fish, drips); and,
for the HD path as a whole, a crash seam, the classic pages and the HD level carried
across an Alt+Enter, and every HD motion on the drawn state's clock. The wave, the swell,
the UV wobble on the HD art's own marked water (the HD art: the room art read from the
player's own Remaster installation) and the caustic are this project's design (OWN) and
replace the shapes the entry "Water in the HD rooms" had taken over with credit; the wind
keeps its shape from TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931
(THIRD: the wind's numbers are its author's own design, as its author confirmed). New are
the option `tomb5.hd_water` (registry `hd_water`, on by default) with its options row
*Graphics* -> *HD water* (both removed later by the entry "The water sheets are part of
the HD look; their row goes (#236)"), the text file `hd_water.txt` beside the executable,
the log lines `WATERLOG`, `SPLASHLOG`, `LIFELOG`, `LARALOG`, `DXLOG` and `CRASH` behind
`-log`, new shader files and variants, and switches of RoomProbe, ModelProbe and TrgProbe.
The main files: `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp` and `.h`, `hd_level.cpp`, `hd_laradraw.cpp`,
`hd_room.hlsl`, `hd_glow.hlsl`, `hd_model.hlsl`, `hd_wet.hlsl`, `hd_water_look.hlsl`,
`hd_water_under.h`, `hd_splash_math.h`, `hd_life_rules.h`, `hd_life.cpp`;
`specific/crashseam.h`, `devicemove.h`, `devicewindow.h`, `dxshell.cpp`, `texture.cpp`,
`fmv.cpp`, `LoadSave.cpp`, `specificfx.cpp`, `winmain.cpp`; `game/traps.cpp`,
`game/control.cpp`; the option's places in `global/types.h`, `tomb5/tomb5.cpp`,
`game/menu_frame.cpp` and `game/gameflow.cpp` (German `HD-Wasser`); `bshader.bat` and
`be.bat`.

**Why.** At the first places looked at - ANDREA2's fountain hall (rooms 144, 229, 231),
its fountain 194, its sewer under room 60, JOBY2's water along the submarine (rooms 42,
76) and its southern half (143) - the HD levels had no water surface of their own: the
surfaces were the restored classic faces with the HD art's glint pages, drawn by the
classic path, and ANDREA2 room 76 had no surface by either path. The water was to come
from general graphics knowledge and from counts on the project's own data, for every water
room of every level by one data rule, secured by the option, a sweep over the fifteen
levels and the text file. What was then seen in play shaped the rule as it stands: waves
over solid floor, white blotches on a swimming Lara, on rats and on posts, a zigzag foam
edge, foam that read flat and as regular as a tablecloth's edge, restless rings, water
that looked flat when seen level, a milky surface from below, a waterfall that seemed to
stop short of the water, land and deck plates torn in wave shapes at the banks, a
chequered pattern of crossing crests and a grid of glints close up, rivers whose flow
showed at a few angles only, golden light under the night levels' water, a strip of bank
between ANDY3's pond and its grass, JOBY4's sea surface vanishing from below and later its
glow burning white, a crash on Alt+Enter, a classic splash where a fish tank was shot; and
requests for a wet floor after the shot and for some life in the water.

**How.** *The data rule* (`HDRenderSetWaterSheets`, `water_depth`; DATA). A square of a
room that is not under water whose room below (`FLOOR_INFO::pit_room`) is an underwater
room is water. Its surface is the top of its water room there - the highest corner of that
room's ceiling over the square, the height where Lara's head breaks the surface - and a
square whose dry floor stands more than a click over that top at every corner is no water
square (ANDY2's sixteen such squares have no water under them; RICH2's two corner plates
and the edge of ANDY3's island are split sectors, and the level's raised triangle covers
the part of the sheet under it). The corners come out of the floor data's slope entries
through one function, the engine's `GetHeight` and `GetCeiling` with the corner
substitution of the randomizer's `Tr5Level`; the engine hands it its `floor_data` words,
RoomProbe those of the classic `.TRC`. The depth walks down through further water portals
to the first floor that is not one, at most six rooms. Squares join four-connected at one
world height across rooms into bodies; a flipmap twin joins the body of the square at its
place. A square over a room that is dry while its flipmap alternate is an underwater room
is water once `FlipMap` swaps the two, its top and depth read in the alternate: such
squares form bodies of their own, drawn with their feet and drops only while that room is
swapped (`HDRenderWaterFlipRoom`, handed on by `HDFlipRoom`) - JOBY5's leaks over rooms 2
and 37, 14 and 20, 30 and 52, 36 and 50, and RICH3's rooms 185 to 192. A square draws a
sheet when its room draws its own HD group, whatever flat art lies over it, unless a row
of class `none` reached its body.

*The classes* (`WaterClassOf`, `kWaterClass`). Sea when a room of the body carries
`ROOM_OUTSIDE` or `ROOM_NOT_INSIDE`; channel when indoors with 16 squares or more and
twice the area over the perimeter under 2; river when its water names a sink (*The
rivers*); basin otherwise. A class has eight wave rows, ranked by wavelength: basin 260,
197, 150, 113, 85, 63, 47 and 29 units; channel 420, 311, 230, 166, 120, 88, 64, 41; sea
1,500, 1,025, 700, 481, 330, 222, 150, 98; river 300, 237, 187, 149, 117, 93, 73, 47 -
four of the design's own (basin 260, 150, 85 and 47 units long and 2.0, 1.4, 0.8 and 0.45
high; channel 420, 230, 120 and 64, 3.0, 1.8, 0.9 and 0.45 high; sea 1,500, 700, 330 and
150, 38, 16, 7 and 2.8 high; river 300, 187, 117 and 73, 2.4, 1.6, 1.0 and 0.56 high, a
channel's steepness) and between them three at the geometric mean of two neighbours and
one at the shortest over 1.5, each as high as 0.8 of its neighbours' mean steepness times
its wavelength, so heights fall with the wave number. Their speeds follow deep-water
dispersion, omega = calm sqrt(g k), with g = 4,300 units/s^2 (`kWaterG`: 9.81 m/s^2 at 2.3
mm a unit; TEXTBOOK) and calm 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0 for basin, channel and sea, 0.2 for a
river, whose crests are carried as one with its current; a channel's current runs 180
units a second along its long axis. Swell 0, 0.6 and 1.0; absorption lengths 4,000, 1,500
and 900 units; bank foam 0, 0.7 and 0.85 in a 300-unit band; whitecaps 0.6 on a sea above
half the wave height; the highlight indoors 55 degrees up at azimuth 40 (exponent 90 for a
basin at strength 0.8, 70 for a channel), out of doors 22 degrees up at azimuth 200
(strength 0.5); a channel and a river take 0.4 - a channel's water hides its floor within
a square and a half, so its waves stand at their whole height over a dark body and at 0.8
they lit the canal a glaring yellow. Each row's height carries a slow envelope, 1 - e + e
(0.5 + 0.5 sin(2 pi t / P + i times the golden angle)), P 8 to 15 seconds and different
for every row (`kWaterGroupPeriod`), e 0.30, 0.35 and 0.50 for basin, channel and sea; the
processor wraps each phase to one turn in double precision (`water_rows_now`).

*The colour* (`kWaterPalette`, `water_look`, `water_lit`). Per section, shallow / deep /
highlight / foam in RGB: Rome: 150,170,90 / 62,98,50 / 255,232,170 / 238,232,200; Russia:
96,150,160 / 28,62,80 / 205,228,255 / 240,248,255; Ireland: 100,125,98 / 34,60,44 /
235,240,230 / 248,248,242; VCI: 64,92,150 / 14,28,70 / 190,210,255 / 215,225,245; all
times the body light, the mean colour1 + colour2 of its rooms' light samples weighted by
squares, times 1.8, never under 0.30 and never over 1.5 (`kWaterLightGain`,
`kWaterLightFloor`, `kWaterLightCap`; gain and floor set on RoomProbe pictures, the cap a
free choice). The absorption per channel stands in the ratio of ln(shallow / deep) of the
section's palette, its mean the class's 1 / absorb. Ireland (ANDY1 to ANDY3) carries a
night flag, a project decision on how those levels look: there a body takes the moon's
light, the luma of its rooms' light times 0.90, 1.01, 1.22, its highlight and foam the
same tint, under the sky at 0.4 and 0.6 of the day's; RoomPS's caustic is off at night and
a river's drifting caustic stays at half strength in the moon's tint (c146) - the gold
under that water was the stream beds' own red-orange art seen through clear water with the
caustic's bright lines on it. Open-air bodies reflect sky rows measured on the levels' own
domes (`RoomProbe -sky`); indoors a stand-in reflects 0.65 of the body light at the
horizon and 0.25 overhead and swings +-40 % with a finer second pattern for 0.4 of it;
under the sky the swing is +-25 % over the measured sky rows. JOBY2's bodies of rooms 7,
42 and 143 take foam 0.5 (`kWaterOverride`, a project decision on pictures of four foam
strengths).

*The grid and its draw* (`hd_render.cpp`, `hd_room.hlsl` `WaterVS`, `WaterPS`). 5 x 5
vertices a square in MANAGED 16-bit buffers of their own; colour1 carries the depth over
32, the distance to the nearest square without water within three squares and, for a river
or a channel with a current, the way along the flow to the first point without water; one
range per body of a group; the buffers go with the level's others (`release_buffers`), so
a lost device takes them along. `upload_water_room` writes c16 to c23 for every room in
`prepare()`. `draw_water_sheet` draws a room's sheet in `HDRenderRoomMask`'s blend phase
after its glass, premultiplied ONE / INVSRCALPHA, two-sided, without depth write.
`HDRenderWaterCopy` copies render target 0 by `StretchRect` into a render-target texture
once a bracket, before the first blend phase of a frame with a sheet (`HDFrameDrawGlow`),
so the copy holds every opaque thing of the frame; `WaterPS` reads it on s5 at `VPOS` plus
half a pixel. Where the adapter offers `INTZ` as a depth-stencil texture,
`HDRenderWaterDepthBind` makes one the device's depth-stencil in `BuildWaterSheets` (the
device's own surface kept and put back by `HDRenderWaterDepthUnbind`, both released before
a `Reset`; `depth_has_stencil` counts its 8 stencil bits, so the shadow receive keeps its
stencil guard), and the depth variant of `WaterPS` reads it on s6: `SceneZ` undoes the
projection (z = b / (a - d)), `WaterDepthBelow` gives the path through the water. The
sheet writes F x reflection + (1 - F) x (copy x T_rgb + (1 - T) x scatter) + highlight
with alpha 1, the fog on its own colour; an adapter without `INTZ` draws a fallback that
reads the vertex depth. The refraction (`RefractMove`) moves the floor's read by the
wave's slope times the absorption length times (1 - 1/1.33) times (1 - T) - for a short
path the small-angle refraction of a ray through a tilted surface (TEXTBOOK), for a long
one no further growth where the floor fades - carried to the screen through the pixel's
footprint (`ddx`, `ddy` of the world position), at most 256 units and 4 % of the screen;
`bend <s>` scales it per row (default 1). A guard refuses a bent place whose frame lies
within 96 units of the surface at rest or above it and scales the move to the shorter of
the two paths: a swimming rat's belly lies 60 units under the surface (`game/rat.cpp`, its
mesh 10 under its place), and at 48 a neighbour's bent place read it, a piece of the rat
drawn beside itself. A bent place deeper than the pixel's own is found before the water's
colour and seen through that longer path, its extinction and scatter the floor's own: a
thin body just under the surface otherwise took the colour of a deep, lit floor through
its own few units of water (the violet patches on Lara in ANDREA1). The depth variant
`clip()`s where the frame lies less than its body's clip depth under the surface at rest:
8 units by default (`kWaterClip`, `HDRenderWaterBody::clip`, c148), above the depth
buffer's error (about 1.2 units at the far plane of 20,480) and wide enough for the HD
art's planes 2 to 9 units off the classic height, so a deck, a rim or a bank at the
water's height shows itself; `clip()` and not alpha 0, because with the copy the sheet
writes the whole pixel. The distance fog takes the same share of the water's colour as of
the body's light (`gWaterZen.w`), so the water goes dark where its banks do.
`HDRenderWaterSheetAt` answers `BuildWaterSurfaces`, which leaves out a classic face whose
square draws a sheet, before the majority over the HD art's flat faces decides the rest.
`bshader.bat` compiles the water's shaders and variants, and `be.bat` checks each compiled
header against its source, `hd_glow_ps.inc` against `hd_room.hlsl` through a `//
bshader-include` line.

*The crests* (`hd_room.hlsl` `WaveSum8`, `CrestRows`, `WaveBend`, `CellHash`;
`hd_render.cpp` "the crests", `kWaterFan`). The rows lie in a fan round the body's own
direction - a channel's long axis, a river's flow, else the class's: longest first at 0,
0.25, -0.375, 0.5, -0.625, 0.75, -0.875 and 1.0 times the class's width, the negative side
half a step further out, so no two rows are mirror images and no two lie within a quarter
of the width, modulo pi as well, a crest's line having no way; width 1.5 for a basin
(ripples from all round a fountain), 1.2 for channel, sea and river (crests mostly across
a canal and askew to a current). Each row is cut into cells: across, three crests from
trough to trough, numbered by the crests' own count - the processor wraps a row's phase to
three turns and hands the shader the whole cells it has run (`kCrestAcross`, kept modulo
4,096; `kCrestOffset`, 977 from row to row) - so a crest keeps its cell while it travels;
along, three of the row's wavelengths (`crestLen`, at most `kCrestReach` 1,536 units, so a
sea's long rows lay no piece longer than a pool), every other cell across moved along by
half a cell, so the cells stand like bricks. The hash of a cell's whole numbers
(`CellHash`, the fractional parts of two sums of products with multipliers n / 4,096:
exact in single precision, repeating after exactly 4,096 cells and nowhere before, precise
anywhere in a level) gives its piece: a height of 0.4 to 1 times `kCrestGain` 6, a length
of 1.5 to 3 wavelengths, a lean of up to about 15 degrees (`HD_CREST_LEAN`) and a shift of
up to 0.1 of a turn. The piece is the row's own curve under two windows, along the piece
and across the cell, each the smoothstep of a tent, both 0 with their slopes at the cell's
edges; across, the middle crest weighs fully and its neighbours a quarter; the slope is
exact for the pieces as drawn. One squeeze bends them: a push along a value noise of the
same hash, cells 1.5 of the longest wavelength wide, by up to 0.3 of that wavelength
(`kBendPush`), drifting 0.031 and -0.023 cells a second. Why: straight rows crossing at
fixed angles lit the same diamond cells again and again and beat into quadrilaterals of
337 to 851 units; a periodic envelope along each crest drew a grid of dashes; a glint
field aligned to the world's axes drew a grid of dots close up. The highlight is
Blinn-Phong over the waves' normal and nothing else. One crest a cell drew every piece as
a round bump; a sixth of the cells left empty drew flat stretches; a gain of 4.49 keeps a
row's mean square and read faint against the floor seen through, 6 was judged on RoomProbe
pictures; the hash's constants passed a count on 128 x 128 cells (even over 64 bins,
neighbours correlated by under 0.03, a flat spectrum). The rows' phases and heights go to
the shaders four to a register (c156 to c159, vertex c175 to c178). `WaterVS`'s swell
