takes the same pieces at a gain of 1 (`kCrestSwellGain`: at 6 a long row's trough sank
ANDY3's pond under the ground beside its island); `RiverPS` (which takes no squeeze), the
variants under the water and of RoomProbe's views and the foam's draw take the pieces
without lean and shift. `crest <s>` (0 to 1) fades a row's bodies from the straight,
unbent rows (0) to all of this (1, the default). The first four rows of the class table,
unfanned, still move the HD art's marked water in RoomVS: its swell, and its wobble, which
moves the art's texture 4/512 of a page a unit of slope (`HD_WATER_UV`, set on RoomProbe
pictures), so a plane of that art is not a mirror.

*Seen level and seen from below.* The rows' fade over distance is measured along each
row's own direction - the phase step to the next pixel right and down, worked out per
vertex from the projection's derivative (`gWaterView`, c19) - so the rows whose crests run
toward the camera stay when the water is seen flat (measured by a pixel's longest step, a
basin's rows were gone at 3,000 units and 5 degrees over the surface). The slopes are
raised by 3 for a basin, 2 for a channel and 1 for a sea where the view runs within about
9 degrees of the surface, not at all where it looks down by 37 degrees or more, linearly
between. A slope turned away from the camera takes the Fresnel term of the slope it
mirrors, |N.V| (with N.V under 0 the term was 1 and laid the sky's horizon colour flat
over the water); the side drawn is the camera's (c148.y, 1 while the camera is in the
air); near the camera every vertex keeps at least 32 units off the camera's height on its
own side (`HD_SWELL_GAP`: at any pitch the near plane reaches at most 24 units below or
above the camera, 32 leaves room for a rolled camera), the hold fading out over a square
and a half. From below, the sheet draws with the `HD_WATER_UNDER` variant, the depth
variant without the foam: outside the Snell window it shows the bent frame under 0.35 of
the shallow colour, moved by a quarter of the bend (at the whole move the walls standing
on the far bank swung in wide bands), inside it the whole bend under 0.1 of the reflection
colour; the window's edge spans 0.61 to 0.71 of N.V round the critical angle's 0.66, and
the room's underwater fog and the screen's wobble are the engine's.

*The bank* (`WaterPS`, "the patches", "the foam's draw"). The bank foam is a density, at
most 0.75, lacy at its outer edge and dense at the bank; its reach swings with a swash of
4.5 seconds whose phase runs along the bank and with the wave's height there; its pattern
drifts at two speeds and grows and dissolves through a third slow layer whose threshold
swings over 5 seconds; a smooth variety field of two Wave2 layers (about 6,700 and 8,900
units), worked out per vertex, moves it and shifts its phase but never turns it - a blend
between two orientations of world coordinates far from the origin multiplied the pattern's
rate of change and drew a comb along the banks. Where along a bank foam lies at all is a
slow field per vertex: three layers of cells, each the product of two Wave2 along axes
turned by 0.35, 1.25 and 2.20 radians (none along the classic grid's banks), periods
3,800, 5,400 and 7,400 units, each times a clock of its own, 26.3, 33.7 and 45.9 seconds;
a patch where the field stands over 0.05, its band reaching 1.5 times the square root of
the excess over 0.4, a rounded lobe - lobes of a third of a square to two squares, the
size of the lobes on a reference sketch supplied for this project read on ANDY1's pools
(PICTURE; lobes of one to four squares would make a whole side of those pools one patch or
none); in a channel the field drifts at 0.3 of the current. In the depth variant the reach
is the real depth under the pixel, full at nothing and gone at a click (256 units), within
three squares of a classic bank; the fallback keeps the class's band. The foam is lit as a
layer up to 24 units thick, its rise toward the light shading it softly, never under 0.3,
thin foam at 0.65, a darker rim where a blotch's cover is half. On a sea `WaterVS` lifts a
breaking crest by up to a quarter of the whole wave height, so the whitecaps ride the
crests, and they trail where the two longest rows stood half a second earlier. The
waterline (depth variant) is full under 24 units of depth and gone at 48, a straight ramp,
weighed by how fast that depth changes from one pixel to the next (`fwidth`): whole from 6
units a pixel - round a post, a hull, a swimming body - and fading toward a flat shore,
where a floor rising at 1:10 had put the band hundreds of units out into the water as a
thick white band. It is held to 0.25 within a bank's band outside a patch and 0.75 inside
a patch and out in the water (posts, floes, hulls); without the depth texture the band's
innermost 24 units carry a line of 0.25. Lara has no line within 320 units of her place,
full again 64 further out, while she swims at the surface or wades (`lara.water_status`,
`gWaterLara` c123; she stands 768 units tall and lies about 700 long swimming). Creatures
carry none: the HD objects' solid draw sets the stencil's bit 4 under every pixel it
draws, and `HDFrameDrawGlow` marks every live rat in a water room of the frame before the
copy (`MarkWaterCreatures`) - rats are drawn by the classic buckets, outside that bracket:
their mesh as `DrawRats` picks it, placed by the engine's matrix stack, pulled toward the
camera by `HD_STAND_PUSH` (1/512 of its distance) so that it passes against its own depth,
drawn into the creature bit alone. The foam is drawn in a pass of its own over every range
of a body whose bank foam or whitecap strength is above 0, from above, on the unmarked
pixels only (`HD_WATER_FOAM`, `hd_room_water_foam_ps.inc` and its depth twin): under ONE /
INVSRCALPHA the sheet with its foam equals the sheet without foam with a second
premultiplied draw of the fogged foam colour times foam at alpha foam over it, which freed
the sheet shader's slots for the crests (its depth variant stood at 511 of ps_3_0's 512).

*The rings* (`HDRenderWaterRipples`, `gather_rings`, `kRingBody`; `hd_room.hlsl`
`RingSlope`). Once a frame, with sheets built, `FeedWaterRipples` hands the live slots of
the game's `ripples[]` with flags 0x10 or 0x02 and without 0x20 to the renderer, which
starts a ring where a slot is new and ages it by what its `init` has counted
(`UpdateSplashes` adds 4 a logic frame, 8 with flags 2). One body makes one ring: a new
ripple of the same kind - a body's (0x10) or a small one's (a bubble, a shell, a rat) -
within 192 units of a live ring goes into it while that ring is younger than 0.6 seconds
and starts it again when older; a wading Lara sets up a ripple every four logic frames,
and each had become a ring of a quick, uniform train. A ring is two low swells of 90 units
behind a front that runs out at 150 units a second from half the ripple's first size and
lives 3.5 seconds, its strength 0.5 times its size over 128 times the square of the life
left. A ring that starts over 128 - only a barrel's - counts its size past 128 and is 4
times stronger: at night the water mirrors a dark sky nearly alike at every slope, and at
2 the ring did not read from Lara's camera. A sheet draw takes the eight youngest within
512 units of its squares and 256 of its surface, the small rings after every other, each
kind youngest first (a rat ripples one logic frame in sixteen, and eight rats pushed a
wading Lara's ring out); `RingSlope` adds each to the slope, its amplitude over the square
root of 1 + d / 256, in a loop over eight registers. `S_DrawSplashes`
(`specific/specificfx.cpp`) leaves a ripple's flat sprite out where `HDWaterRippleOnSheet`
finds a drawing sheet under it with `hd_water` and `hd_motion` on; raindrops (flags 0) and
the underwater blood keep their sprites. A row's `ripple <x> <z> <size> <seconds>` is a
ring source on the surface under that place; ANDREA2 194's basin, where no item and no
object's control makes a ripple, carries `ripple 55808 32768 80 0.7` in the engine's own
override row, and its floats a current away from the spring (`HDLifeSpringPush`, 40 units
a second at the spring, nothing 1,536 out).

*The HD art and the classic faces under a sheet.* A draw call that is wholly the HD art's
own still water - horizontal triangles of material 16 or water-marked at every corner
(`HDRange::artTris`) - within 32 units of a sheet's surface is hidden over the squares
whose sheet draws, asked first by its box and then by the floor squares its art triangles
cover (`HDRange::artCells`, an edge on a square's line not counted); a call that its box
reaches but none of whose triangles lies over such a square is kept and counted
(`artSpared`). A river's flow-material calls (material 1, wholly flat, within 32 units:
`HDRange::flowTris`, `flowCells`, through the helper `NoteBoxCells`) take the same rule:
the HD art's own moving surface three units over ANDY3's rivers. `art keep` and `art hide`
(the default) choose per row; with `hd_water` 0 nothing is hidden. In a room whose body
draws its sheet and hides the art, RoomVS's flood lays no swell, wobble or surface caustic
on anything (`set_room_rows`, a gate in c18.z): the flood had lifted the bank's own mesh
by up to 36 units and laid the caustic on dry decks at the water's height. In a room where
the sheet takes the place of faces, a restored classic face over a square with no water
room below, whose plane the art draws flat there (`HDRenderGroupFlatArt`), is left out: no
water lies under it, it is a second copy of the art's own floor, and in JOBY5's room 4 it
drew the bands of a depth fight. The classic water marks the art's test rests on are the
engine's (`BuildWaterMarks`); RoomProbe builds a twin of them with `-watermarks`, which
shuts the closed doors' portals first as `InitialiseDoor` does.

*The caustic* (`hd_room.hlsl` `CausticOf`, `CausticFace`; `hd_glow.hlsl`). One minus half
the absolute sum of two warped waves, to the sixth power, 0.0224 radians a unit, its mean
0.2310 and spread 0.2964 (counted over 400,000 samples) divided out; read in the plane of
the face normal's major axis - x and z on a floor, z and y or x and y on a wall, the
normal from the screen derivatives of the position, one sample, the planes never blended -
so a wall takes no vertical streaks; in RoomPS's plain and gloss variants and in GlowPS;
its footprint fade full to 10 units a pixel and gone at 20. On the floor and the walls of
a pool it carries 0.30 of the light (`HD_CAUSTIC_FLOOR`, set on RoomProbe pictures), the
submerged weight, fading out over 2,048 units, two squares, under the surface. It lies
under a surface only in a level built with sheets (`g_caustic_on`) and is off at night.

*The rivers* (`hd_render.cpp` "a sink in the water", `kRiverCover`, `kWaterFlow`,
`draw_river`; `hd_room.hlsl` `RiverPS`; DATA). A body whose water a `TO_SINK` trigger of
its squares names, or that holds a sink lying inside one of its squares at or under its
surface where the squares naming its lying sinks number at least a quarter of its own
(`kRiverCover`, a free choice between the 1.0 of a true river and the 0.05 of ANDY3's sea
with its drain), is a river: its flow the mean way from those squares toward their sinks,
its speed the mean of 120 times the strength in units a second (`LaraWaterCurrent` steers
Lara toward strength x 4,096 / 4 in 1/256 units a logic frame, 4 units for strength 1 at
30 a second), what the water shows of it held to 720 (rows of a few hundred units carried
a square a second slid past as a smear). Over the fifteen levels that is ANDY3's two
rivers, of rooms 0, 42, 43 and 182 (about 1,063 units a second) and of rooms 38, 41, 184
and 185 (640). The streams beside ANDY3's pond are rivers by table (`kWaterFlow`: room 66
toward -z, 70 toward -x, 67 toward +x, at 400 units a second - a wading stream slower than
the sink rivers; the ways read from reference pictures supplied for this project against
the level's axes and the water rooms' falling floors), and ANDREA2's canal carries a
current of +z at 90 units a second (a row of the same table with its class kept, half its
rows' 180), its water running on under the grate into water room 133. A table row's room
names a square by its own room or, where it holds none, by the water room under it. A
river has no bank foam, waterline or whitecaps; its rows stand at a channel's steepness
with half its highlight. `RiverPS`, drawn over the river's sheet, lights the rows' relief
against the class light - lighter toward it by 7 times the slope of the highlight's
colour, darker away through alpha at 0.6 of that share, with no Fresnel and no reflection
- so the crests read as streaks along the flow from every angle, carried with the current;
draws long thin sheen lines, the lighter adding 0.35 of the reflection's colour, the
darker taking 0.6 of that share of what lies behind, faded where a line is narrower than
24 units a pixel; lays the caustic on the floor seen through the river at the floor point
under the pixel, carried with the current, on the colour of the frame's copy there (a
water room a river is seen through leaves its standing caustic to it); and draws the end's
foam where a river - or a channel with a current, within twice `kRiverEdge` of its end -
meets a wall or a drop: one blob the river's width, three layers of cells about 830, 360
and 150 units across on axes turned by 0.6, 2.1 and 1.3 radians, the finer warped by the
coarser, carried into the end, its reach swinging across the river from 0.3 to 1.5 of 768
units (three quarters of a square, inside the half to one square of a weir's foam on a
reference picture supplied for this project), dense and holed at the wall, ragged at its
upper rim. Every number of the river's look is a free choice judged on RoomProbe pictures.

*The waterfall's foot* (`hd_render.cpp` "the foot of a waterfall", `lay_curtain`,
`draw_feet`; `hd_room.hlsl` `FootPS`; `hd_level.cpp` `MoveWaterfallMist`). Every
WATERFALL1 to 3 and WATERFALLSS1 and 2 object - the slots the game scrolls as falling
water - has its classic mesh placed as `DrawAnimatingItem` places it; its foot is the
vertices within 64 units of the lowest (an object no taller is a scrolling face), and it
stands over a sheet where one of its points lies over a drawing square with the surface at
most 256 units over its lowest vertex or 1,024 under it. Where the room is drawn HD and
its art has falling water there - a flow part more than 512 units tall whose lowest
vertices lie within a square of the classic foot, over the same sheet - those points take
the classic foot's place. The objects over one body whose feet come within 512 units of
each other are one curtain: its points, gathered every 512 units along their principal
axis, give a polyline of the steps' means; a step without points is open water (its
segment kept in the line with `wet=0` and left out of the draw), and each wet stretch of a
curtain with a gap closes in a head at both ends, half the reach past its last point and
beside a gap at most 0.4 of the gap's length over the reach, so two strands touch only
where their strands do (a reference sketch supplied for this project shows two ovals with
open water between them). The zone's reach is 614 units plus 0.3 of the longest wet
stretch, held to 614 to 1,229 - 0.6 of a square from a narrow jet, 1.2 from a strand two
squares wide. `FootPS` takes per segment the pixel's distance, way along and side; the
pattern is carried outward at 220 units a second times the square root of the reach left,
so a blotch leaves the curtain fast, slows down and gathers at the rim; across the line at
0.75 of its scale along it (0.45 drew a comb), so near the curtain a blotch is a streak
pointing away; the bank foam's two layers ride at two speeds, the fine one at 0.55; the
two sides are moved 260 units apart over 160 units either side of the line; the outline
breathes with the patch field and a lobe field of its own; the density is the bank foam's
with its threshold along the reach left to the power 0.75 (0.5 filled the zone, 1 left a
thin line); nothing turns. Up to eight segments a draw, in c124 to c131 and c137 to c144.
The rings and the drops come from a point every 512 units of a wet stretch: each a ripple
source of size 64 re-armed every 0.4 to 0.8 seconds by a hash of its place, and on the
logic frame, beside `AnimateWaterfalls`, two `TriggerSmallSplash` drops at every source
within eight squares of the camera, sixteen a logic frame at most - the engine's own
splash of a rat or a shell landing in water, rising about 150 to 200 units and living 24
logic frames; they draw on `GetRandomControl` as the classic mist does. A WATERFALLMIST
emitter whose line's middle lies within a square (`kFootSnap`) of a wet stretch the art's
feet placed is moved to its nearest point - ANDREA2 room 231's two, about 500 units, so
the classic mist's white column stands in the foam; a projection, so a second build moves
nothing further. Nothing of it runs without sheets or with `hd_motion` 0. The falling
water itself is not stretched: every waterfall object over a sheet ends at its surface,
and what read as short was the curtain's fading light, which the foam, rings and drops now
meet.

*Under the water* (`hd_room.hlsl` `UnderWater`; `hd_model.hlsl`; `hd_render.cpp` "under
the water", `water_under_constants`; `hd_water_under.h`). With the camera in a water room
of a level with sheets, `RoomPS`, `GlowPS` and the model pixel shader take every pixel as
col exp(-L sigma_rgb) + scatter (1 - exp(-L sigma_s)): L the length of the view ray in the
water - the whole distance to a point under the surface, the distance times the camera's
depth over the point's height to a point above it - less a clear zone of 2,048 units round
the camera (`gUnderClear`, c145: two squares, the third-person camera's reach, so Lara
keeps her colour); sigma the sheet's own absorption times 0.3 (`kUnderReach`; 0.35 turned
the far end of JOBY2's flooded base into flat water, 0.25 thinned ANDREA2's corridor's
depth); the scatter the body's shallow colour lit by its light with its brightest channel
held to 0.45 (`kUnderLightTop`), times 1 + 0.6 of the ray's upward cosine; a glow is only
dimmed. The registers: c134 sigma, c135 the scatter and the upward gain, c136 world up in
view space and the camera's depth; all zero in every frame whose camera is not under
water. The body is the one over the camera's room, walked six rooms down; a water room no
sheet lies over takes the level's largest body at a depth of 1,000,000 units
(`kUnderNoSurface`: all it sees lies in the water). While the camera is under water the
distance fog's start moves past any view, the frame carries no fog bulbs, and the gloss
variant's faces draw with `RoomPS` without the sheen (the extinction's 20 slots would
cross its 512). The extinction and the scatter follow the rules over 0.25 seconds of game
time, a share 1 - e^(-dt / 0.25) a frame; the camera keeps the body of the last room it
was in that has one of its own. Fog bulbs of a water room a sheet lies over are not handed
to the frame over the water either (`BulbUnderSheet`, found by their place): they are the
classic path's stand-in for that water's murk and laid a pale haze on Lara at the surface.
The gate (`HDFrameDraw`) asks the room holding the drawn camera (`InterpEyeRoom`) for its
own `ROOM_UNDERWATER` flag together with `HDRenderWaterUnderOn`: `camera.underwater` is
never set in `LVL5_DEEPSEA_DIVE`, a logic frame behind the drawn room elsewhere and stale
through a fly-by, and the logic room put a dive's blended frames on the wrong side of the
surface. The screen wobble keeps `camera.underwater` (`FillFrameLighting`), as the classic
dive shows none. Lara (`hd_laradraw.cpp`, `HDRenderWaterAirRoom`): in water a sheet lies
over, her wet nodes take the ambient of the dry room that sheet lies in, carried down the
six rooms of the walk (the water rooms' own ambients are violet-blue - ANDREA1's pool room
26 holds 16, 16, 32); in a water room without one, that of the last room over water she
was in; her colours follow the rules over 0.25 seconds while she is in the water, and
after she leaves it until they lie within half a step of the rules', where
`InitObjectLighting`'s own fade is stopped; on land, without sheets and in a level without
water the classic rule stands, `CalcAmbientLight`'s own fade over 8 frames the only one. A
new level, and the camera coming out of the water, start at the new colours. Creatures
keep the classic rule.

*The deep look* (`hd_render.cpp` "the deep look"; `hd_water_under.h` `HDWaterDeepLook`,
`HDWaterUnderDepth`). A level whose water rooms under no sheet outnumber those under a
sheet more than four times (`kUnderDeepShare`) and whose water has a sea's surface
(`HDWaterSurfaceRoom`, below) takes in all its water rooms the sea class's absorption and
the section's deep colour, dimmed by the camera's depth under the highest top of the
level's water rooms, exp(-depth / 30,000) and never under 0.25, its reach 0.4 and its
upward gain 0.8: over the fifteen levels JOBY4 alone; RICH3's one flooded room keeps its
body's channel look, a flooded room having its own ceiling over its water. There a water
room no sheet lies over counts the largest body's surface as its own wherever the camera
is.

*The sea seen from below* (`hd_water_look.hlsl` `LookPS`; `hd_render.cpp`
`HDRenderWaterLook`, `water_look_constants`, `water_sea_art`; `hd_level.cpp`
`HDFrameSkyLook`; `hd_water_under.h`). JOBY4's sea surface is the HD art of one water
room: room 19's part 3, material 16, additive, 73,728 flat triangles at y -4,269 over the
whole dive. The rule finds it from the data (`HDWaterSurfaceRoom`; no room number in the
code): of the water rooms, the one whose art reaches highest, when that lies at most 2,048
units under the water's top, the highest ceiling of a square of any water room (2,048 a
free choice of two squares between JOBY4's 851 and the next room's 3,840). The dive's
rooms have no portal to it, so `HDFrameDraw`'s room phase adds it whenever no entry of the
frame holds its group - the whole screen as its window, the frame's first room's matrix
moved by the difference of the two rooms' origins, its own lighting, the frame's
extinction - at every frame of a level whose deep look names it, under the water or not,
with `hd_water` on or off; its classic faces are never drawn, and the walk's list is left
as it is (`WATERLOG ... undergate ... surface=<room>`). Where the sea's sheet is drawn and
the camera stands under the basin that stands in for the sea's surface (room 7), the
extinction counts the way up to the sheet's plane (`HDWaterUnderSeaDepth`); over the basin
the camera is out of the dive and counts the whole way, so the surface fades out over the
playable area. The look is drawn with the sky, before the rooms, in a level that takes the
deep look, with the sheets on and the camera in a water room the under look holds, so
every opaque thing stands in front of it; its light is the hue of the water's scattered
colour, its surface the water's top. (1) The sea's sheet, in its first draw (depth 0.9999
tested LESS): the water's own colour dimmed along the room shader's own way
(`HDWaterSheetPath`), over the art's box and the level's water rooms' box together, grown
by the plane's height over the lowest water floor (from any camera in the water the edge
lies 45 degrees or more from straight up) and by the way over which the fog leaves a
twentieth (`HDWaterSheetBox`, `HDWaterSheetMargin`); its edge ragged over 4,096 units by a
value noise of the cells' hash (`HD_LOOK_SEA_RAGGED`, `CellNoise`); faded along the
horizon, the way past the camera's own height counting at 1/32 of itself
(`HD_LOOK_SEA_FOG`, the largest halving step that kept every measured view in its band);
rippled by the body's two longest rows at 0.8 of its light, broken per 1,600-unit cell of
the shafts' grid by the hash - a phase, a turn of both rows of up to 0.9 radians
(`HD_LOOK_SEA_TURN`), a loss of up to half their height (`HD_LOOK_SEA_SWELL`;
`SeaRipple`), the four cells round a point blended by smoothstep - and 1.5 where a shaft
leaves the surface. Where the look drew the sheet, the art's additive ranges draw at
weight 0 (`HDWaterSeaGivesWay`; a frame drawn without the sky, and every frame before the
look's first sheet, keeps the art): its turquoise vertex colours and grey page laid a
pattern of a third of its own light that swallowed the look. (2) The sun's disc through
the surface: the view ray meets the surface at the camera's depth over its upward cosine,
takes the normal of the body's first four rows (their slope held to 1,500 / t of itself, t
the way to the surface, so far up they draw no noise), and bends out into the air by
Snell's law (n 1.333, the window 48.6 degrees; TEXTBOOK); a broad glow whose cosine's
power halves its light at the 22.5 degrees of a reference picture supplied for this
project, carried out through the surface at the light's own height
(`HDWaterGlowPowerUnder`, `HD_LOOK_SEA_POWER` 0: 3.57 for the sea's light 22 degrees up),
strength 1.5 under the sheet (a cosine's power over the sky carries a light of 2 pi over
the power plus 1, so the light of the power 8.75 at strength 4 comes to 1.88 at the power
3.57, and 1.5 is the largest half step down from 1.88 that keeps every measured view in
its band); the lit underside inside the window, 0.35 to 1 toward straight up, its rim
spread over 0.3 of cosine inside the window's own span of 0.339. (3) The light shafts,
untested: 24 steps along the view ray up to 5,000 units (the water's sigma_s of 0.000444 a
unit leaves a twentieth of the light at 6,700), at each the light's way followed back to
the surface, a value noise of the cells' hash there (cells of 1,600 units, the noise's
floor 0.62, drifting with the clock), faded over 40,000 units under the surface and by the
extinction along the ray, brighter toward the light, the steps' start jittered by the
pixel's hash; under the sheet the march's sum is held to 2.49 times the light the cells'
mean (0.0537, `HDWaterShaftMean`) would give over the same samples' weights
(`HDWaterShaftBound`, `HD_LOOK_SEA_PEAK`; PICTURE: a reference picture's peak over its
open water's median), because every sample's way back ends near one point of the surface,
a few cells lit or dark for the whole picture, and a lit patch burnt the view toward the
light to white. Strengths under the sheet: shafts 24, underside 0.24; over the stand-in's
surface the disc 0.2 at the power 600, the shafts 8, the underside 0.12. The band's open
poles are closed by the sky's own caps (the entry "The sky"). The look takes the place of
JOBY4's scripted SD sky layers; with `hd_water` 0 none of the look is drawn and those
layers stay.

*The splash and the fish tank* (`hd_render.cpp` "the cards", "the tank's film", "the
tank's water"; `hd_splash_math.h`, all of it a function of the age alone; `hd_level.cpp`
`HDWaterSplash`, `HDWaterSpray`, `FeedWaterFilms`; `game/traps.cpp`). A splash over a
drawing sheet (within 256 units of height) is taken from `SetupSplash`, which marks the
struct with bit 0x10, and `S_DrawSplashes` leaves its sprites out; the struct runs on as
before. `HDSplashAt` steps the struct's own numbers line for line as `UpdateSplashes`
does, drawn on linearly between logic frames: two rings on the sheet at the classic middle
and outer rings' outer edges, at 1.0 and 0.6 of the classic life (twice a wading ring's
start); a crown of 12 cards on the inner ring and 16 on the middle one at the column's
height times 0.7 to 1.0, 24 to 160 units wide, leaning up to 0.3 radians; 24 drops from
the inner ring under the column's own gravity (7,200 units/s^2). A tank's spray spark is
taken from `TriggerFishtankSpray` (`SF_UNUSED2`; `S_DrawSparks` leaves it out) and drawn
as a card standing on its point at a share of 0.8 (`kTankSprayShare`, the crown's middle
ring's: the spray is the same water thrown up), moving by the classic spark's recurrences
(`HDTankPuff`) with this file's hash where the game rolls `GetRandomControl`, so the
game's random stream is untouched. At the break (`HDTankBurst`) 40 spray cards and 24
drops leave the opened glass within 0.2 seconds at sqrt(2 g (height - h0)) times 0.6 to
1.0 (Torricelli, TEXTBOOK), up or down by up to 400 units a second, so from RICH2's 1,276
units they land at most 1,276 out, the dome's own reach. The dome: the FISHTANK mesh is
drawn by the HD path (`DrawScaledSpike` returns when `HDWaterTank` takes it), every vertex
scaled as the classic scales it by the tank's own logic frames, the apron drawn out of the
glass over 0.25 seconds, the whole in over two logic frames and out over the 0.5 seconds
before `KillItem`, as a see-through sheet of share 0.15 where the view looks through it
and up to 0.65 along it, the installation's spray page 3243 stretched 384 units across and
2,048 down into streaks running down at 1,660 units a second, half the speed of a fall of
the dome's height; the tank's shape comes from its classic mesh (`HDTankShapeOf`, the
glass the furthest z within 32 units of the top, `kTankBand`). The film: per FLOOR_LASERS
item sharing its room with a FISHTANK, a basin body of the lasers' box at rest 8 units
over their floor (`kFilmHair`, about 2 cm, under the lasers' 128), rising by 16 units
(`kFilmRise`) times its strength - (4,096 - `item_flags[1]`) / 1,024 while the tank pours,
after it the lasers' own count over 64 - cross-faded by the blend factor over the floor,
its rim a channel's bank foam times its strength, its clip 0 (at 8 it lost a band before
the tank's plinth); it is no water square for anything else. The cards (`CardVS`, `CardPS`
under `HD_CARD`, c92 and c93): quads facing the camera, a window of the installation's
pages 3242 and 3243 (spray) and 3160 (drops) cut round, soft over 64 units against the
frame's depth, the body's foam colour times 1.5 for the light spray catches, at most 512 a
frame, drawn after the rooms' blend and additive phases. The splash and the spray need
`hd_motion` as well; the film needs `hd_water` alone. The tank in RICH2 room 122 has no
floor lasers and no film. The warm-up (`HDRenderWaterWarmUp`, called once a level from
`BuildWaterSheets` after the depth bind): each of the water's pixel shaders draws one
triangle of the level's first sheet range with `WaterVS` into a 16 x 16 target of its own,
the cards one card, the wet floor's targets and `WetPS` are made and drawn once, and in a
level with a tank's wet floor the models' shaders are made once more out of the model
path's bytecode and draw a triangle through five clip planes that cut it away; the
device's state is put back and nothing reaches the frame. Without it the driver readied
the water's vertex shader at its first draw, a wait of about 42 ms on the first water
frame, and the models' shaders for user clip planes at the first wet mirror (about 100
ms); the first frame of a level with a tank still draws its objects once through five such
planes as a guard (`wet_warm_models`).

*The wet floor* (`hd_render.cpp` "the wet floor", `build_wet_floors`, `kWetRooms`;
`hd_splash_math.h` `HDWetFront`, `HDWetAt`, `kWetRadius`, `HDWetSlope`, `HDWetCell`;
`hd_wet.hlsl` `WetPS`; `hd_level.cpp` `FeedWaterWet`). A tank's row names the rooms its
water may reach (a tank without a row keeps to its own room) (RICH2: tank 182's rooms 122,
121, 45 and 46, tank 33's room 23); a square counts as a room's when it lies inside it or
its flip twin, off its ring of walls and doors, at that floor's height. From the squares
under the dome's foot the water runs across every edge whose next square stands level or a
click lower at both corners - level and down a step, never up one, never down a drop,
never behind the glass - each point on its own square's floor plane (a ramp rising from
the floor keeps its head dry, a slope falling away is wet to its foot and passes the water
on), and it stops `kWetRadius`, 2,048 units, past the dome's foot: the dome lands 3,186
units wide at the floor and spreads past its foot by half that, taken up to whole squares.
Points stand every 256 units, each with its shortest way from the glass, pushed back by up
to 384 units by a hash of its place so the front is ragged; the front leaves with the
apron and runs on at 321 units a second, sqrt(g h) at the film's 24 units (the speed of a
wave in water that shallow; TEXTBOOK); a point is wet a quarter square behind it. The
floor stays wet once the tank is gone, a tank first seen shot (a loaded game) is wet all
over at once, and with `hd_motion` 0 the floor is wet all over from the frame the tank
breaks. Each 256-unit cell is halved along the diagonal its square's crease follows
(`HDWetCell`). The layer lies 4 units over the floor (the depth buffer resolves 1.2 units
at 20,000) and draws twice a frame: its darkening over the opaque frame before the sheets'
copy - the floor kept by 1 - 0.4 x wet (`kWetDark`) - and its mirror after the rooms'
glass and glows and before the cards and the objects' glows (`HDRenderWaterWetMirror`),
out of a copy of the frame as it stands there, so the glows are mirrored and the dome and
the spray lie over the mirror. The mirror: Schlick's Fresnel at water's F0 of 0.02
(TEXTBOOK) times 4/3 (`kWetMirror`, `gWetGain`); a screen-space march of 22 steps from 32
units, each 1.2 times the last (about 8,700 units), each crossing halved 8 times, taken
where the frame's depth fits the ray's within 32 units and 2 per cent of the depth - steps
longer than a thin thing passed it by and took what lay behind - the copy's clip undone as
Reinhard's x / (1 - x) held at 8 (TEXTBOOK), else the light field's colour times 0.35;
over both the lamps as a Blinn-Phong highlight at the exponent 128 with the normalisation
(n + 8) / 8 (TEXTBOOK), all held under 0.75; faded where the frame lies more than 32 units
under the layer and toward the screen's edge. Lara and the frame's objects are drawn twice
more into a target and an `INTZ` depth of the mirror's own, through the floor's reflection
folded into the projection (a planar reflection, TEXTBOOK; the plane the floor height most
wet points stand at; lit as they stand), and into the target's alpha alone as a place mask
written with both alpha factors zero, so every drawn pixel counts whatever alpha its
shader returns; both flipped left to right and clipped by five planes to what stands over
the wet points' box grown by a square (`HDWetPlaneTo`). `WetPS` marches past a model's
place as past a hole, and a ray that went behind a model's place and met nothing takes the
colour of a copy taken before the objects (`HDRenderWaterWetRoomCopy`, from the second wet
frame on): the room the model hides, not a grey veil in her shape. The mirror is softened
on the screen (`g_wet_soft`): drawn into a layer whose alpha is the blur's radius, the
screen length of the march's last step, at most 15 pixels and whole from 2,048 units on
(`kWetBlur` 1, `kWetBlurNear`), then blurred across and down, a Gaussian of sigma r / 2
over four taps a side - a reflection need not be HD, and the ceiling's cove lights' rows
rippled with distance. A square whose HD art carries its own mirrored copy of the room
under a clear floor (`HD_PASS_CLEAR`; 8 mirrored cells and a third of those under,
`kWetCopyCells`) takes no march mirror and no stand-in: the march mirrored the ceiling's
glows there as yellow bands over the art's own reflection. On a polished floor of the
marble floors' mirror (the entry "The marble floors' mirror (#205)"), the marble's planar
mirror is kept - the wet points carry no wet in its mask - and the water's own mirror
gives way (`wet_give_way`, `wet_polished`: a cell whose wet corners, three at least, stand
at one height overlapped by a marble face there), keeping the darkening and the highlight:
water on polished stone lies flat in the same plane and mirrors the same room, so one
exact mirror stands for both, and the march had drawn a drier-looking area behind a hard
stepped outline. The water's life is not drawn while `MonoScreenOn` holds a picture (the
pause menu, the inventory, the load and save screens), where its fish had been drawn over
the frozen picture.

*The water's life* (`specific/hd/hd_life_rules.h`, pure functions the engine, RoomProbe
and ModernTest share; `hd_life.cpp`; the getter `HDRenderWaterBodySquares`, read only).
The models `BOTTLE`, `WET_CLOTH`, `CLOTH_RICH2_RICH1`, `ANIMATING3_ANDY1` (a barrel) and
`FISH2` are found by name through the model resolver in the player's installation into
synthetic slots from `0x7800`, after Lara's wardrobe, preloaded with every other model;
their boxes give the floating heights and the reach across the water. Where
(`kHDLifeLevels`): ANDREA2's channel bodies of 16 squares or more (bottle 4, green cloth
3, ochre cloth 3, barrel 1, no fish); ANDY3's rivers of three squares or more and its
bodies of eight or more, ANDY1's bodies of eight or more (ochre cloth, a dead leaf, 4,
green cloth 1, barrel 1, and a school); RICH2's tank (a school only). One float for three
squares with water under them, twelve a body, two barrels at most - twelve keeps three
bodies inside the 32 entries the life draws a frame at most, a quarter of the frame's 128;
places rolled at level load with `GetRandomDraw`, no savegame field; the pool is kept
through an HD rebuild after a lost device when the bodies are the same
(`HDLifeSameBodies`). A float drifts with the body's current plus a wander of 60 units a
second (its way a hash of the float and a 4-second step), turning at 40 degrees a second;
a step nearer a bank or shallow water than its reach is refused, its x or z part alone
tried, so it slides along a bank; floats keep apart by 0.75 of their two reaches; one a
current holds square-on against a bank turns along it toward a way on. It bobs on a sine
of 2.5 to 4 seconds, a quarter of its floating height but never more than the body's sheet
rises or than its draft leaves over that rise, with tilts of 3 and 2 degrees; a kind
floats only where its draft reaches deeper than the sheet falls (on a sea only the barrel
stays in the water), and only over water as deep as its lowest point. On a river or
ANDREA2's canal, a conveyor with an inlet in `kHDLifeInlets`, a float comes back at the
inlet's slot point 384 units past the first row's edge, its top 64 under the surface,
rises over the first square, and dives over the last into the outlet's slot, its light
falling to a quarter as the water's own absorption would. A school: 4 to 8 `FISH2` on a
ring of 150 to 300 units in a depth band from 128 units under the sheet's rise down to 87
over the floor, each rising and sinking 192 units at 0.45 radians a second; Lara within a
square of a fish or a live splash on its water sends each on a dart of its own, away and
turned up to 25 degrees by a hash, at 2,800 units a second falling off with a time of 1.5
seconds, pitched 10 to 25 degrees toward a depth of its own; at d units from the edge of
768-deep water the share of the way pointing away from it is at least (384 - d) / 512, so
a dart bends along a wall; the school regroups where its whole ring keeps 428 units off
the edge, rejoins at 600 units a second, and ends a flight within 10 seconds of its last
dart; a fish turns at 720 degrees a second and is pitched to its way at most 30 degrees; a
still Lara scares a school again only once she has moved 256 units. A school in a body
whose deep squares span more than eight squares roams, waypoint by waypoint, to the square
whose way crosses the most squares it never came to, at 175 units a second (one `FISH2`
length); a tank's school never flees and swims lines 96 apart along the tank, there and
back in 20 to 30 seconds, 215 units off each end. The tank is whole while its item is
neither active nor deactivated and its water stands at the full 4,096. Drips: a body of
four squares or more not in the open air gets one for eight squares, two to six, each at a
period of 3 to 9 seconds, ringing only within six squares of Lara and once in two seconds
a body; the drop falls from the ceiling over its point as `UpdateDrips` moves a drip (from
rest, 4,300 units/s^2), held and drawn by the pool itself as a line of the sort list, and
its ring of 96 to 111 starts on arrival - it is written into a free slot of `ripples[]`
with the fields `SetupRipple` writes, and the pool keeps out of `Drips[]`, so the game's
random sequence never depends on what is drawn. A float 160 units high or more (the
barrel) rings the water once a bob at its top, size 240 to 255. `LIFELOG` (with `-log`)
writes a level line, a line per body and a line a second.

*The device and the clock.* `specific/crashseam.h` (`CrashSeamFilter`, installed in
`WinMain`, which names the game thread) writes `CRASH code=<hex> at=<address>
module=<file>+<offset> thread=main|game|other` through `Log` with `-log` and into
`crash.txt` without it, and a minidump `PCtomb5_<date>_<time>.dmp` beside it
(MiniDumpNormal through `dbghelp.dll`, loaded at that moment). Every classic page of
`Textures[]` and the inventory's and load screen's picture are `D3DPOOL_MANAGED` textures
of the device they were made on, and nothing made them again at an Alt+Enter: the first
classic draw on the new device, the sky's `DrawPrimitiveUP` in `HWR_DrawSortList`'s case
4, failed inside `d3d9.dll` once the pages differed in when they were last drawn.
`DeviceMoveTexture` (`specific/devicemove.h`) makes such a texture again on the new device
- same size, levels and format, managed, every level copied through `LockRect` - or
releases it and sets its pointer to 0 (drawn untextured until the next level) when it is
not managed, of an unknown texel size or its copy fails; `DXCreate` calls
`MoveTexturesToDevice` (`specific/texture.cpp`: every entry, then `MonoScreenToDevice`)
after `DXCreateD3DDevice` on a recreation - Alt+Enter and the resolution keys - and not at
startup or at `DXShowFrame`'s reset of the same device. `FmvDeviceLost`
(`specific/fmv.cpp`) releases the films' Bink playback texture in `DXClose`, which had
kept the start device alive and would have been bound by the next film on the new one;
`PlayFmv` makes it again. `HDLevelDeviceRecreated` then builds the level that was drawing
HD with `HDLevelBuild` itself (everything it reads is still loaded): the pairs whose flip
stands set are swapped back for the build and again after it, keeping each number's
`flipped_room`, `item_number` and `fx_number`, and `HDFlipRoom` moves the art with each
pair; `HDFontBuild` remakes the font; the HD clock runs on. The window code of `DXCreate`,
`WinSetStyle`, `DXShowFrame` and `CreateMonoScreen` moved unchanged into
`specific/devicewindow.h`, so RoomProbe `-windowcycle` drives the engine's own code. The
lines: `DXLOG device recreated - pages=<n> moved=<m> dropped=<d> kept=<k> picture=<0|1>
old_device_refs=<r> hd=<rebuilt|classic> ms=<n>`, `HDLOG device recreated - level=<stem>
rebuilt=<0|1> flipped_pairs=<n>`, `DXLOG window <start|toggle|mode> ...`, `DXLOG
screenshot hr=<0x...> file=<TombNNNN.tga> bytes=<n>` and `DXLOG mono picture hr=<0x...> -
no picture`. The clock: `FillFrameLighting` and the two brackets hand the frame
`HDBookClock`, the logic clock less the part of a logic frame the blended pose stands
behind it, so the water's waves, foam and rings, the wind, the caustic, the scroll and the
flipbooks move on every frame drawn; at `fps_mode 0` the time is the logic clock (a clock
of the logic count plus the blend factor would run a logic frame ahead of the pose drawn).

*The text file and the option.* `hd_water.txt`, read at every level load: one row a line,
`<LEVEL> <room> <class|-|none|river>` and any of `tint <r> <g> <b>`, `waves <s>`, `foam
<s>` (each 0 to 4), `bend <s>` (0 to 4), `ripple <x> <z> <size> <seconds>` (size 1 to 255,
0.1 to 60 seconds), `art keep|hide`, `foot <x1> <z1> <x2> <z2> <reach>` and `foot off`
(`swirl <x> <z> <r>` is read as a foot of length 0, `swirl off` as `foot off`, counted as
`old=`), `flow <dx> <dz> <speed>` (the way -1 to 1 each and not both 0, the speed 0 to
4,000; a `river` row without it runs along the body's long axis at 240), `lift <units>`
(-256 to 256), `clip <units>` (0 to 256), `swell <s>` (0 to 4) and `crest <s>` (0 to 1);
`-` keeps the class, `none` draws no sheet over the bodies the row reaches and brings
their classic faces back, `#` starts a comment, an unreadable line is counted, a row holds
38 tokens at most. Rows apply after the compiled tables (`kWaterOverride`, `kWaterFlow`,
`kWaterBank`) to every body their room has water in; the file wins, a later row over an
earlier. No default file ships. `lift` sets a body's sheet that many units over the data's
height: the grid stands level at that height (the free surface of still water, the bank
climbing out of it), a skirt carries the same plane out over land squares up to three
squares (`kWaterSkirtReach`) whose lowest corner stands under the lift and less than 16
units over the water's top (`kWaterSkirtMargin`), drawn only, and the shallows hold a
lifted body's rows to their whole height only where the depth under the pixel is at least
2.56 times that height - a wave stands no higher than about 0.78 of its depth (the
breaking index of a solitary wave; TEXTBOOK). No body is lifted by default: ANDY3's pond
(water room 73) stands at the data's height with clip 0, so its sheet ends where the depth
test ends it on the line where the HD art's ground leaves the water, and the class's whole
swell (`kWaterBank`). With `hd_water` 0 no sheet is built, every classic face is restored
as without the sheets, and the caustic under a surface is off; the caustic's shape and
footprint fade and the wave rows stay on the HD art's marked water, which they live in the
compiled shaders for. With `hd_enable 0` nothing of this runs.

*The lines and the tools.* `WATERLOG level=<stem>` carries the option, section, sectors,

`fall=`, `foot=` and `seg=` per waterfall, curtain and segment, `mist=` per moved emitter,

`-waterdepthview 1` to `5`, `-waterbend`, `-ripple`, `-rippleat`, `-lara`, `-wader`,

**Decisions.** The sheet replaces the restored classic faces wherever a square draws one;
the HD art's own still water over a sheet is hidden by default (`art keep` brings it
back), which reversed the first decision that ANDREA2 room 231's art stays over the sheet,
after the fountain hall showed half art and half sheet. The water stands at the data's own
height: a lift of 96 units hid a black sliver at ANDY3's pond, but the lifted surface
stood over land Lara walks dry, so the pond went back with its clip at 0 and its whole
swell, and the lift, the skirt and the shallows stay for a row of the text file. The foam
left the sheet's shader for a draw of its own instead of a split of `WaterPS` by class,
which freed room only for the classes that do not need it. The glints, the periodic
envelopes and the periodic pushes of the crests were dropped for pieces placed by a hash.
The default bend stays 1 (1.5 was asked for; the refraction is what the view from above
shows, and that view was kept); a basin gets no swell, since the sheet's vertex every 256
units cannot carry rows shorter than 512. The pond's arms are no rivers by any data of the
level, so the streams are rivers by a table row. A waterfall is not stretched down; its
foot is one foam zone per curtain with open water at its gaps. The swimming rats are
marked late in the glow phase rather than by a creature list in the sheet's shader, which
had no slots left. The gloss variant's sheen gives way under the water, for want of slots.
The gate under the water reads the drawn room's flag; the screen wobble keeps the classic
flag. Alt+Enter rebuilds the HD level at once instead of falling back to classic until the
next level. The polished floor keeps its own mirror under the water; Lara and the objects
are mirrored as geometry in the wet floor, the room art is not. The floor stays wet; the
laser-less tank of room 122 gets no film (it cost 0.20 ms in its view against a bound of
0.15). The sea's look, the surface room drawn at every frame and the deep look belong to a
level whose water has a sea's surface; the surface room comes from the data, never from a
room or level number. The look's shafts are bounded rather than replaced by the cells'
mean, which took the flip out but moved too many views out of their band.

### The marble floors' mirror (#205)
2026-10-16 to 2026-10-21

**What.** Polished stone floors mirror the room as a planar reflection. Each floor height
and each sloped floor is a plane; the frame's rooms, stand ranges, static pieces and
models, the rooms over and beside the plane's own rooms, and the sky where a mirrored room
opens to it are drawn a second time through each plane that shows, into a target of their
own, and laid over the floor's own faces. The polished pages are a column of the sheen's
page table; the HD art's copies of rooms built mirrored under RICH2's floors leave the
level when the mirror is on; the clear floors on mirror pages are drawn opaque. A menu
row, Reflections, switches the mirror. Files: `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp/.h` (the faces,
the planes, the frame's pass: `HDRenderMarbleDraw`, `marble_build`, `marble_copies`,
`marble_lean`, `marble_note`, `marble_replay`, `marble_plane_rooms`, `marble_box_out`,
`marble_over_world`, `marble_sky`), `hd_marble_math.h` (the pure rules),
`hd_gloss_pages.h` and `hd_gloss_math.h` (`HDGlossMirror`), `hd_splash_math.h`
(`HDMarbleFace`), `hd_shader/hd_wet.hlsl` (`MarblePS`), `hd_model.cpp/.h`
(`HDModelMirrorWarmUp`), `hd_levelkey.h`, one call line in `hd_level.cpp`'s
`HDFrameDrawGlow` (before the wet floor's models) and the frame's notes of its room draws,
`tomb5.cpp` (the keys) and `game/menu_frame.cpp` (the menu row; MenuTest counts it).

**Why.** A mirror on the marble floors was asked for. The level data alone does not name
polished stone: the footstep material marble (`fx` 9) stands only in ANDREA2, ANDREA3 and
RICH1 while RICH2's marble is `fx` 6 (stone) everywhere, the sheen's marble class names
only RICH2's washroom pages, material 3 resolves to glass on facades and ice, and RICH2's
black marble and green tiles are pages the sheen bars - so the floors are named page by
page. In RICH2 the HD art carries copies of its rooms built mirrored under clear floors,
sporadic and partial, which tore the reflection and then flickered against the planar
mirror; a sloped floor, a tread beside two larger floors and a room seen only in the floor
lost their reflection, rooms in the mirror came and went at a room change, and the floor
showed the walls' flat light where the sky belonged.

**How.** *The page column* (`hd_gloss_pages.h`, `hd_gloss_math.h` `HDGlossMirror`). The
sheen's page table carries a sixth column, `mirror`, set on 40 pages (RICH, RICHCUT2,
ANDREA and the title, picked by looking at the thirty largest floor pages of each level,
plus RICH2's banded marble 3314 and 3315 and ANDREA1's church mosaic 169, 170 and 183); a
page the sheen does not name stands as a line of class `A` (`HD_GLOSS_ASIS`), which names
nothing of the sheen. `hd_gloss.txt` takes a last word `mirror` or `nomirror`, or a page
and that word alone; the file's word stands over the table's and a later line over an
earlier one, so a page is switched without a rebuild. The tiled floors of ANDY2 and JOBY2
to JOBY5 are no marble and carry no mirror page.

*The faces* (`HDMarbleFace`, `marble_build`). A triangle of a room's opaque pass or of its
clear floors on a mirror page, flat and facing up (the normal's height over 0.95 of its
length, `HD_MARBLE_FLAT`), is kept with its group in the group's own space, its height the
corners' mean y; after the rooms' flags (`HDRenderSetWaterSheets`) a water room's faces
leave. The faces are the mirror's extent, so the mirror runs to the art's own edges, not
the classic squares'. Heights within 2 units of the next are one plane at the height most
faces hold (`kMarbleHeightJoin`), since two faces of one floor differ by up to 2. A face
rising 15 units and more across itself (every face lies within a unit of its plane or
rises that much, nothing between) lies in a sloped plane of its own, its normal turned up
and its distance in world space (`HDMarbleTiltPlane`); a triangle leaning past the flat
face but less than 60 degrees (`HDMarbleLeanFace`, `HD_MARBLE_LEAN` 0.5, the line in the
gap the levels' faces leave between 56.3 and 85 degrees, where only walls lie above) is
taken by the group's fill (`marble_lean`) and laid into a sloped plane the same way, a
sliver within the clip's offset of its own height staying out. A face joins a sloped plane
found already when each corner lies within 4 units of it (`HDMarbleTiltFits`, the clip's
offset), so a ramp tessellated at slightly different leans is one plane and is mirrored
about one plane, not part by part with its reflection set off. The faces of the planes of
their own stay in a store by group (`g_marble_store`) and join the level faces at every
run of `marble_build`, which tests a face's rise against its own height, so a resident
load finds the same planes. A face lying wholly under higher faces of its own room (16
units and more over it, asked at its centroid and at its corners and edge middles drawn an
eighth of the way in) is buried and no mirror face.

*The copies* (`marble_copies`, at the level's build while `hd_marble` is on). A group's
triangle leaves the level when it is the room turned corner for corner about one of its
mirror planes (each corner within 2 units of a corner of a triangle of the group on the
same page), lies wholly under that plane's faces with each corner pushed 64 units out,
stands in no classic room's box (in its height, within the overhang's 128 units across),
and its 1,024-unit square is a copy's (at least 8 such triangles and a third of those
under it); none lies in a water room. Each part answers a case: a centroid test alone took
the corridor's own walls and the gallery's art, the room boxes give them back, and the
corners pushed out keep two triangles beside a floor's edge that were otherwise holes. A
triangle the rule is not sure of stays: hidden under the opaque floor it costs a draw and
shows nothing. In RICH2 the rule takes 119,319 triangles. Cracks between floor pieces that
a copy filled show what lies behind as a hairline.

*The clear floors* (`HDRange::marbleOpaque`, `draw_pass`). A clear-floor draw call on a
mirror page, in a room that is no water room, is drawn with the blend off in
`HD_PASS_CLEAR`, opaque, the depth written as before; no shader changes, the room shaders
keep 510 (plain) and 507 (gloss) of 512 slots. Such a floor is no clear floor for the wet
floor's copy rule (`clearFlats`), so a tank's march runs over it.

*The planes a frame draws.* Every `HDRenderRoomMask`, `HDRenderRoomStand` and
`HDRenderStaticPiece` call of the frame is noted with its matrix, lighting, passes and
window (at most 4,096 draws, each checked against the ones before it), the solid phase
first; the frame's first bracket starts the list over. Each plane's faces are drawn
against the frame's depth with an occlusion query (`marble_seen_ask`, `marble_seen_read`;
`HDMarbleScore`), made once and used again, at most one in flight a plane, read as the GPU
answers and never waited for; a plane scores the share of the screen it shows, its cover
until a count is read, and a count older than six frames (`kMarbleSeenOldest`) scores no
more. A plane showing less than a thousandth of the screen (`HDMarbleShown`,
`HD_MARBLE_LEAST`) counts as showing nothing, which bounds the cost: in RICH2's lobby a
view shows up to 21 planes, most of them step bevels and floor edges seen through doors, a
few hundred pixels each, and every plane is a whole mirrored draw of the rooms. The places
(`g_marble_slots`, `HDMarbleSlotsStep`) take every plane that shows, up to a ceiling of 64
(`HD_MARBLE_PLANES_MOST`, far over the most a view shows); a plane coming into view fades
in once over 133 ms (`HDMarbleFadeStep`, `kMarbleFadeMs` 8000/60, eight frames at 60, the
step a frame the frame's time over the fade's, a frame counted at most 50 ms), so the fade
is the same at any frame rate; a plane that shows nothing leaves at once.

*The mirrored draw.* Per plane: the projection folded with the plane's reflection in view
space and turned left to right (two flips keep the winding), one device clip plane keeping
what stands 4 units (`kMarbleClipOver`, the layer's lift) over the plane, and the
reflection taken about the clip's plane, not the floor's, so the floor's own two-sided
faces never stand at zero distance to the clip and blink into the mirror, and the kept
part of every wall begins at the mirror's line (the reflection moves by 8 units). One
A8R8G8B8 target and its INTZ depth serve every plane in turn. Each plane's draws are cut
to its faces' box on the screen, turned as the target is and two pixels wider
(`HDMarbleTargetRect`, `kMarbleScissorMargin`; the layer reads the target nowhere else,
bilinear neighbours included), and every noted draw or room whose box lies past a side of
the mirrored view, wholly under the clip or beside the scissor is not drawn
(`HDMarbleBoxOut`, `marble_box_out`). The noted draws are made again with the scissor off,
the sky groups and the water sheets left out, then the frame's object list
(`HDObjectFrameDraw`) through the same projection, the frame's lighting and the vertex
constants c0 to c3 put back after. The mirror walks its own rooms: from the drawn rooms
holding the plane's faces out through every portal, over and beside, to three portals
(`HDMarbleWalk`, `marble_plane_rooms`, `g_marble_walk`), a room asked once and walked on
only where the plane's mirrored view can show its box; and from each room's ceiling
portals (a portal's normal points into its room) the rooms over the drawn rooms, over the
rooms beside them and over those, to depth 3 (`HDMarbleOverRooms`, `HDRenderMarbleOver`,
`HDRenderMarbleBeside`, `HDRenderMarbleRooms`, `g_marble_over_depth`). A room the frame
did not draw is drawn whole with the matrix and light of the room it was found from, moved
by the two origins (`marble_over_world`); the rooms are named by number and turned into
groups through the level's flip table at each frame. The frame's own room list therefore
no longer decides what a mirror holds, which is what made rooms come and go in it at a
room change.

*The sky* (`marble_sees_open`, `g_marble_open`, `HDMarbleOpen`, `HDMarbleSkyTurn`,
`HDMarbleSolidRun`, `kMarbleSkyFloor`). As the classic walk draws the sky for a frame
whose list holds a room under the sky (`game/draw.cpp`), the mirror asks the same of its
own rooms, with each room's `ROOM_OUTSIDE` kept by group at `marble_build`. Where one is,
the sky (`HDRenderSky`, its depth slice and order, centred on the camera and turned as the
view is, without fog or bulbs) goes in after the noted solid draws and before the
see-through ones, and only over the plane's own faces: the faces mark the stencil through
the frame's projection turned in x and one row of the target up and down (the layer reads
between the two rows a row of the frame has); every sky pass is tested against the mark
and writes no depth, so the tests stay early; the passes drawn without depth are drawn
once more with the depth write and no colour through the layer's pixel shader in its mask
form, so the held depth lies exactly where the sky's triangles reached. `HDRenderSky`'s
third call is left out of the mirror, since the sky groups of the fifteen levels hold only
opaque and alpha parts.

*The layer over the frame.* The plane's faces, lifted `kWetLift` (4 units), mark stencil
bit 16 under the depth test (bits 1, 2, 4 and 8 are the shadow's receive, the creatures'
mark and the spring's crack); the wet floor's points take it away (`MarblePS`'s mask
mode), so where a tank's water has come its mirror is the wet floor's own; the faces are
then drawn through `MarblePS` (93 slots) where the bit stands, clearing it: the wet
floor's composition at a dry floor's numbers - Schlick's term at F0 0.04, the textbook
dielectric, no darkening, the walls' light where the target holds nothing, the lamps'
highlight, the soft cap, the fog. In Direct3D 9 a pixel's centre lies on the whole number,
so pixel x shows what the turned projection drew at 2 X + W - x, read at its texel centre
a half further. The target is drawn at two rows a row of the frame and read bilinearly
half way between them, which keeps a reflected edge within about a fifth of a pixel of its
line instead of a stair. `WetPS` and the march debugger are unchanged.

*Warm-ups, keys and switch.* `HDRenderMarbleWarmUp` (from `BuildWaterSheets`, after the
water's) makes the target at the frame's size and draws the plain, gloss and glow room
shaders once each with the clip plane on and the layer's pair once, and
`HDModelMirrorWarmUp` (after `HDObjectLevelBuild`, once a graphics device) draws one
triangle through the model shaders with the clip plane on into a 16 x 16 target of its
own, because the driver remakes the shaders for the clip plane at their first use, a wait
of up to about 100 ms in play. `hd_marble` (0|1, default 1) and `hd_marble_ceiling` (1 to
64, default 64) are read in `tomb5.cpp` beside `hd_vis` and handed over before a level is
built (`HDRenderMarbleSet`); `hd_marble_planes` is no longer read, because `REG_ReadLong`
writes its default where a key is absent and every earlier registry holds it as 2. The
level key carries `hd_marble`, so a kept load is built again when it changed; nothing goes
into a savegame. The Reflections row stands under HD water, writes `hd_marble` and hands
it over at once; a level built with the mirror keeps its build until the next load
(`HDMarbleBuildAfterSwitch`, `HDRenderMarbleOn`), because its see-through floors were made
solid and their copies left out - off stops the mirror's draw from the next frame. With
`hd_marble` 0 nothing of this runs and every picture is as without the mirror. The
resident load keeps the faces with the groups and sets the water rooms again; flip twins
carry faces each and the frame mirrors the one drawn.

*What the mirror does not draw.* The classic statics (drawn by the classic path, which the
mirror draws for no room) and classic objects; the stand ranges a carrier room holds for
another room's static, which only the frame's own rooms draw; a room found by the walk
draws with the light of the room it came from. A plane falling under the least share
leaves at once and fades in again when it comes back over it.

*Probe and suite.* RoomProbe: `-marble 0|1`, `-marbleplanes n`, `-marblerows 1|2` (a
`marble:` line), the census `-marblecensus`, and `-marblevoid` (the target cleared to
magenta, to count floor that shows no mirrored room), `-marbleplanefloor`, `-marblerise`,
`-marbleslots`, `-marblesim`, `-marbletarget`, `-marbleover`, `-marblecracks`,
`-marblelag`, `-marblemodelpart`, `-marblenomodelwarm`, `-marblelist`, `-marblesteep`,
`-marblepages`, `-marbleleast`, `-marbleslopes`, `-marbletread`, `-marblewalk`,
`-marblesky`, `-marblepop` and the `marblerooms` line. ModernTest's marble groups check
the page column, the face rule, the coverage, the planes, the places and the fade, the
counts, the rooms over, `marble_every` and `marble_walk` (with `HDMarbleSolidRun`).

**Decisions.** A planar mirror rather than a march over the screen on the wet floor's
layer: the march costs less (0.04 to 0.19 ms a frame) but finds only what the frame shows,
nothing beyond the view's edge, and it showed a lit room through a door as a few broken
rows where the planar mirror drew it whole; the march's probe path was removed. The art's
mirrored copies leave the level rather than only the mirror, because they cost a mirrored
draw each and their faces took mirror places. A slope gets a plane of its own rather than
borrowing a floor's, which would have shown a ramp of 256 units reflected up to 512 off.
Every plane that shows is drawn rather than a fixed cap: a cap of two left treads, a
raised floor and a ramp's part beside two larger floors plain and swapped planes in one
frame on a stair; the least share of a thousandth rather than a twentieth keeps faint
reflections on slivers while the worst view measured keeps its mirror at about 2 ms of the
GPU without the sky. TROne's renderer was read as a reference (GPLv3, read only, nothing
of its code in this repository); taken from it is one number, the lean line of 60 degrees,
credited as THIRD in the origin ledger and at `HD_MARBLE_LEAN` - TROne (GPLv3) by
Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931; its cap of six planes a frame was not
taken, as it would leave planes unmirrored wherever more show. A multisampled target was
not built, because its depth cannot be read as a texture and the composite reads the
depth; the wet floor's soft blur was not applied, since its radius is the march's last
step, which the planar mirror has none of. The walk stops at three portals, where what
remains is the floor's own rooms coming and going in the direct view. The sky is drawn in
every level whose mirrored rooms open to it; what remains of its cost is the sky's own
pixels, and a cheaper sky would be another picture. No rule for cracks between floor and
wall: a census of every mirror face's edges found the floors meeting their walls, and what
showed through were rooms the mirror had not drawn.

**Commits.** `2341a7f` (classic path reference build), `5bd916e8` (reference build for
comparisons), `d3486f39` (the page column), `d8269022` (faces, stencil, planar pass),
`5f23eb4c` (clear floors drawn opaque), `0d359cb2` (the edges), `1c220a9a` (wet floor's
points), `0e0481bd` (keys; prototypes removed), `baba72b2` (reference build for
comparisons), `46dfd71f` (clip over the floor), `87812007` (copies left out, buried
faces), `7ccb2c81` (pages 3314 and 3315), `49ec9663` (mirror warm-up at load), `0cdf3c8e`
(one floor, one height), `21ec8bba` (buried face wholly under), `838748f2` (reference
build for comparisons), `2c234eb4` (plane in the clip), `6bab8ae4` (sloped planes),
`1b197923` (places, counts, fade), `9fb919ef` (the rooms over), `493dcded` (models'
shaders warmed), `35ad1c12` (rooms over to depth 3), `23ff6120` (the record), `a68a9de0`
(reference build for comparisons), `fd4d6271` (RoomProbe plane lists), `84b048ab` (every
plane mirrored), `f990b865` (ModernTest every plane), `2ae94fae` (leaning floors, own
planes), `3fbe2e4d` (church mosaic pages), `115d9d7b` (the Reflections row), `9a316e36`
(comments, one start value), `c68c535f` (records name the 60 degrees), `6203c859`
(reference build for comparisons), `7e5a28df` (each plane walks its rooms), `5ac27ef8`
(sky behind mirrored rooms), `a63200e2` (whole sky drawn first), `75420996` (RoomProbe
