### The spring (#200)
2026-10-14 to 2026-10-15

**What.** A spring is the engine's own: a point under water with its own hashed clock that
rings the sheet over it, sends a few small bubbles up its jet, bends what stands behind
its rising current, and rises out of a crack in its floor - a jagged slit with two to four
fine side branches, its walls carrying the floor's own texture down over the lip, its
bottom black. The first spring is the ring source of ANDREA2 room 194's fountain basin
over water room 120, where the game itself makes no ripple and no item stands; it is the
first entry of a compiled table, `hd_water.txt` can change, add or take away springs, and
a hashed rule places a spring now and then in the levels' other water. Files:
`specific/hd/hd_spring.h` (the rules as pure functions, without the engine and Direct3D,
included by ModernTest), `hd_spring.cpp` (a level's springs, their rings, their draw; its
first part reads the level only through `hd_render.h` and is linked by RoomProbe with `/D
HD_SPRING_TOOL`, its last part is the engine's), `hd_shader/hd_spring.hlsl` (`ColumnPS`,
`BubblePS`, `CrackPS`, `HolePS`), and two lines in `hd_level.cpp`'s `HDFrameDrawGlow`
(`HDSpringCrackDraw()` where its bracket opens, `HDSpringCopy()` beside the sheets' copy).

**Why.** The request was that ANDREA2's underwater spring get a visible rising current and
a few small bubbles in its jet, and that springs then appear now and then under water in
the levels where they fit. Before it the place rang through the ripple field of the
compiled override row for ANDREA2 194 (`kWaterOverride`), a ring of size 80 every 0.7 s
with no current and no bubbles: rings alone read as rain on a pond, not as a jet. A jet
out of a flat floor reads as a fountain nozzle hidden under the paving; a jet out of a
hole reads as water forcing its way up from below, so a crack was asked for at its foot
that carries the floor's texture and is a black void inside. In play the crack vanished
when the camera stood below the highest point of its rim on a slope or under its bottom,
and the column vanished at some turns of the view under the water; the gate and the copy
below fix both.

**How.** Every random choice is a hash of the spring's level and place (the life's mixer),
never a generator's draw: the same level and clock give the same picture. The cards'
vertex shader draws the column and the bubbles (`CardVS`'s bytecode,
`hd_room_card_vs.inc`).

*The rings.* One a period, each up to a fifth of a period early or late by hash so the
train does not beat evenly; size 80 times the strength (at least 16) and the period 0.7 s,
as tuned in play - a ring's slope is its size over 128, so a jet's landing stays under a
wading Lara's 112 to 127. They go into the sheets' live rings as they are
(`HDRenderWaterRingAdd`, without the merge a game ripple goes through), from
`FeedWaterRipples` once a frame, only for springs within 6,144 units of the camera (the
drips' reach), so far springs do not crowd the 64 kept rings; at a spring's first frame or
after a jump of the clock the rings of the last four seconds go in at their own ages (a
ring lives 3.5 s). A `ripple` row of the file within a quarter of a square of a spring
rings that place already, and the spring then rings no more, so the place does not ring
twice.

*The bubbles.* Three a second at strength 1 (the middle of the two to four asked for; a
denser stream is the one number `kHDSpringRate`), each born at a hashed moment in its
slot. Without a crack they start over the jet's core within 0.4 of the column's
half-width; with one, on its bottom at a hashed place in the slit (on the main line
between a quarter and three quarters of its way, across it at most half the side's
half-width there), their spread and sway growing from nothing there to whole at the
crack's depth, so they rise out of the slit and not through its walls. They rise at 200 to
300 units a second by hash: a few millimetres of air rise at about 0.25 m/s in still water
(110 units at 2.3 mm a unit) and the jet carries them faster; the classic bubble's law
(`game/tomb4fx.cpp`, `UpdateBubbles`) speeds up a game frame at a time without a cap,
which a bubble in a steady jet does not, so it is not used. They sway in the classic
bubble's form, 8 to 20 units and a third of it across at 1.0 to 1.8 s by hash; radius 5 to
12 units, the classic breath bubble's drawn size over its rise (`DrawBubbles`). One in
three by hash leaves a small ring where it reaches the sheet, 48 to 63 like the classic
bubble's (`SetupRipple`, flags 2), moving with it. A bubble is a card facing the camera,
premultiplied (`BubblePS`: a bright rim from 0.55 to 0.9 of its radius, a faint body, a
small highlight), soft against the depth texture over 32 units, with the cards' distance
fog, under the water the frame's extinction, from over the water the water's own
absorption per channel along the camera's path under the surface; its colour the body's
spray colour as the cards wear it.

*The rising current.* A quad on the jet's line from the floor (the crack's bottom where
there is one) to the sheet, turned to the camera in eight rows, half as wide at the floor
as 32 units and 96 per step of strength (128 at 1) and widening by a tenth of its height
as a round jet does. It is drawn after the sheets, with the cards, as a multiply: the
blend `DESTCOLOR` / `INVSRCALPHA` with rgb `a r` and alpha `a`, `r` the ratio of the
frame's copy at the bent place to the copy at the pixel (floor 0.02, at most 2), `a` the
share, whole from half the column's weight up - the target becomes `target (1 + a (r -
1))`. Under the water, where the target is the copy, that is the refraction itself; from
over the water, where the sheet writes its pixel whole from the copy, the multiply moves
the floor's pattern inside the sheet's colour and keeps its tint and mirror, and adds no
light (no milk, no beam). It reuses the copy the frame took for the sheets. The bend: two
octaves of value noise (cells 24 units across the line and 96 along it, and half that),
rising at 400 units a second, at most 96 units of view space at strength 1, strongest on
the line and gone at the edge as `(1 - u^2)^2`, falling with height as 1,200 over 1,200
plus the height, faded over the last eighth at each end; the weight scales the bend, the
share follows it. A bent place nearer than the column keeps the pixel's own. It fades as
the camera looks along its line (a flat quad seen along its line is a line) and as its
half-width at mid height falls from 16 to 6 pixels. The noise's lattice values are a table
of 64 by 64 texels the processor fills with the life's mixer (`HDSpringNoiseTexel`, a salt
per channel), bound with wrap and a linear filter, so the shader reads each octave in one
fetch; the rise wraps at 64 cells along, where the table repeats, so the pattern never
jumps. With `hd_motion` 0 the bubbles and the column stand at the clock motion last had,
and the sheets draw no ring, as for every ring.

*The column's copy* (`HDSpringCopy`, `HDSpringFrameCopy`; `HDSpringColumnFront`,
`HDSpringColumnWeight`, `HDSpringColumnOnScreen`, `HDSpringColumnInFrame`). Under the
water the sheet lies in the dry room over it, and a view along the floor can leave that
room off the frame's list, so the frame would take no copy. Where the sheets' copy is
taken - after the opaque frame, before the blend phase - a frame that has none yet takes
it when a spring's column is drawn in it and reaches its screen: both ends more than a
unit in front of the camera (the draw's own test), a weight over 0, a way across, and the
box of its ends, each widened by its half-width at its nearest and farthest depth, on the
screen. Still one copy a frame; RoomProbe asks the same where it takes the sheets' copy. A
column whose foot or top lies behind the camera is left out whole; a column hidden behind
walls in a frame with no sheet still takes the copy, since a spring does not know the
water rooms its jet rises through.

*The table.* `kHDSprings`: ANDREA2, room 194, x 55,808, z 32,768, floor y 2,560, strength
1, period 0.7 s. The compiled override row for room 194 keeps its class and no longer
carries the ripple; a spring marks its body's spring (`HDRenderWaterBodySpring`) unless a
ripple row marked it, so the life's floats still drift away from the fountain. *The file
row:* `<LEVEL> <room> - spring <x> <z> <strength> [<seconds>]` in `hd_water.txt`
(`ParseWaterLine`, the numbers read by `HDSpringParseKey`). A row for the level and room
of a table spring changes it - place, strength, and the period where it gives one - and
strength 0 takes it away; any other row adds a spring, whose period is 0.7 s over its
strength without seconds. A row whose one key is `spring`, with class `-`, tunes no body,
so it cannot reset a compiled row's foam. Where two sheets lie over one place (the
fountain over the sewer) the spring takes the one in the row's room, else the highest. A
`ripple` row keeps its meaning; to have the spring ring that place, it is written as
`ANDREA2 194 - spring 55808 32768 1.0 0.7` or removed.

*The placement rule* (`HDSpringRulePick`). A candidate square draws a sheet over 768 units
of water or more (the life's deep water), lies three squares or more from Lara's start and
from every opening of its water - a portal through a wall that reaches into the water and
leads out of the body; a portal with the body's squares on both sides only parts two rooms
of one water - and under no static (a static blocks the square its origin stands on). A
body that is no river, has no current, holds no spring of the table or the file and has
six candidates or more (the life's school size) holds one spring in two, by the hash of
its level and its first square (least z, then least x), at the middle of a candidate the
hash picks, strength 0.5 to 1 by hash - over the fifteen levels three rule springs
(ANDREA1, ANDREA2, JOBY2), a spring found now and then, not one per pond. The level's
facts come from the engine as loaded (the build runs before a saved game is restored, so
Lara's item stands at the level's start) and in RoomProbe from the classic `.TRC`.

*The crack's outline* (`HDSpringCrackMake`), every choice a hash of the spring's seed (its
level's name and its place). A main line 256 to 512 units long turned any way, bowed by up
to 8 % of its length to one side and jagged by up to 4 % at each of its 14 steps; its
width 32 to 96 at the widest, each side's half at a step 0.6 to 1 of the profile `sin(pi
t)^0.6`, the two sides apart and each side point slid along by up to 0.3 of a step, so the
rim is torn and the slit closes to a point at both ends. Two to four branches, each a
third of the main line long (0.8 to 1.2 of that), rooted between a fifth and four fifths
of the way, the sides taking turns, leaning 20 to 45 degrees (and up to 5 more either way)
off square to the line - one lean a side -, a third of the side's half wide at the root
and closing to a point in four jagged steps; a branch is a spike in place of the side's
point at its root, so the outline is one polygon of 28 points plus 8 a branch. Where a
spike would cross the rim or another, the branches alone are drawn again with the next
round of the hash, at most 16 rounds; of 4,000 cracks none crosses after it (ModernTest).
The strength scales all of it from half (strength 0) to whole, so a weaker jet opens less
ground; a crack that does not lie on its body's squares of deep water (768 or more) is
made again at 0.8, 0.64 and 0.5 of its size. The sizes make the slit one to two jets long
and narrower than the jet.

*The crack's floor* (`read_floors`). The floor the HD picture draws under the outline is
the `.TRG`'s, not the classic level's: per outline point the floor triangle under it
(facing up, its height nearest the spring's floor) gives the rim's height there and the
floor's light (`colour1 + colour2`, as `RoomVS` sums them); per edge the triangle under
its middle gives the page and the page's place as a function of world x and z. The file is
read in pieces by the layout TRForge's reader documents (`vendor/trforge`, MIT): the
header and the part tables, then only the index runs of the rooms whose box meets the
crack and the span of vertices they name - a few kilobytes, once at the level's build. The
floor's texture is the player's own data; nothing of it is copied. The bottom is a flat
plane 64 to 128 units (scaled) under the outline's lowest point; a crack whose floor parts
by more than 192 units (three quarters of a click) keeps none. At the build the plane of
least squares through the outline's heights and its middle is fitted
(`HDSpringCrackFloor`, `HDSpringCrackFloorFit`; points on one line give the flat floor at
their mean), its highest point kept, and the floor-facing triangles of the `.TRG` within
`kCrackReach` (4,096, over twice the farthest camera under a bottom seen in play) of the
outline are read for the gate.

*The walls.* A wall under every edge from the floor's height to the bottom. Its texture is
the floor folded over the lip: a place d units down the wall takes the floor's page at the
point d units further into the crack along the edge's inward normal, so the floor's
pattern runs on over the lip and down (the page sampled with wrap). Its light is the
floor's at the rim times the share a wall of the slit still sees of the light on the
floor: a wall d units down sees the open sky only above the far lip, w units across (the
slit's width there), a cosine-weighted share of `0.5 (1 - sin a)` with `sin a = d /
sqrt(d^2 + w^2)` - a half at the lip -, times a dark band from the bottom, black there and
whole at the crack's depth over it. No light of its own reaches into the crack; the
distance fog is subtracted as `RoomPS` subtracts it, and the water round a camera under it
is the rooms' own.

*The hole* (the depth trick). The crack must be in the depth buffer before the sheets read
it and in the frame's copy they bend, and the room's floor is drawn whole, so it is drawn
where the opaque frame is complete and the blend phase not begun - the start of
`HDFrameDrawGlow`, before the copy - in four draws with the stencil's bit 8 (the receives
keep bits 1 and 2, the creatures' mark bit 4; the crack leaves its bit at 0). The volume
is the outline from 8 units over the floor to 8 under the bottom. (1) The volume sets the
bit to 0. (2) The volume against the frame's depth turns the bit over at every face in
front of what was drawn: an odd count is a pixel whose surface lies inside the volume -
the floor the crack opens, and nothing that stands over it; the fans of a concave outline
cancel out the same way. (3) The volume again on the marked pixels alone, black, at the
depth of the bottom's plane along each pixel's own ray (`HolePS` writes the depth), the
bit back to 0. (4) The walls with the depth test and write. Seen from over the water the
sheets' depth variant shades the pit with the water's absorption and scatter like a real
pit. Not drawn: without a stencil in the frame's depth, where the volume reaches the near
plane (the count would be cut), past half the far plane's distance (an empty place of the
frame holds the sky's depth there), off the screen, under 2 pixels, or while the room of
its floor is not on the frame's draw list (`RoomOnDrawList`). Anything within 8 units over
the floor inside the outline lies inside the volume and turns black; statics on the floor
do not cut the crack, and the blend and additive room polygons drawn after it in
`HDFrameDrawGlow` paint over the hole as over the floor.

*The gate* (`HDSpringCrackSeen`, `HDSpringCrackBottom`, `HDSpringCrackGround`). A crack is
seen from a camera 8 units (`kCrackLift`) over the highest point of its outline, or else 8
over the floor's fitted plane at the camera's own column; on a flat floor the plane is the
floor. The highest point comes first because away from the outline the plane is only a
guess at the floor. Under the bottom's plane the fitted plane is a guess at a slope that
falls away, so a camera there sees the slit only where it stands 8 over the level's own
floor at its column (the read triangles' height nearest the camera); no floor within reach
means not seen. For such a camera a ray into the slit enters at the floor rising and
leaves through a wall, never through the bottom, so the hole then writes no bottom: its
plane is 0, `HolePS` writes the far plane's depth in black, and the walls fill the slit.

*Keys, log and probe.* `hd_springs`, a DWORD beside the options, read at the level's build
with `REG_PeekLong` and never written: absent the rule as built, `0` no spring of the rule
(the table's and the file's stay), `n` one body in two times n. `hd_springcrack`, read the
same way: absent or 1 every spring has its crack, 0 none, the springs then drawing exactly
as without the crack. `SPRINGLOG` behind `-log` at the level's build, nothing per frame:
one line for the level (`springs=`, `table=`, `file=`, `rows=`, `dropped=` springs with no
sheet over them, `rule=`, `bodies=`, `fit=`, `candidates=`, `key=`) and one per spring
(`room=`, `x=`, `z=`, `floor=`, `surface=`, `strength=`, `period=`, `body=`,
`how=table|file|rule`, `rings=own|row`, and `crack=length,width,depth,branches,bottom
y,page` or why there is none: `off`, `fit`, `file`, `floor`, `rough`). WATERLOG's
`spring=` is written before the springs mark theirs. RoomProbe with `-hdwater 1` builds
and draws the springs as the engine does: `-spring x,z,s` adds one, `-nospring` none,
`-springparts 1|2` the columns or the bubbles alone, `-springs` prints the SPRINGLOG
lines, a SPRINGRULE line per body and a SPRINGCRACK line per crack and outline point,
`-springkey <n>` and `-springcrack 0|1` as the keys, `-springcrackmap` the outline over
the body's squares as text, 16 units a character. The springs' shaders are not in the
water's warm-up, so their first draw in a level may wait once. ModernTest's spring group
checks the rules, the crack's outline, the gate and the column's copy.

**Decisions.** The own bubble card was kept over the classic breath-bubble sprite: drawn
side by side through the same card path they cover the same pixels, and the own card takes
the body's colour and the water's absorption as the cards do, without a classic page in
the HD path. The noise's lattice values are this project's own table; the first column's
commit took them from a published third-party shader hash and `c4069084` replaced it. From
over the water the column stays faint, because a bend of the floor as the sheet sees it
would need a second copy or the sheet's own shader (its depth variant at 512 slots), and
light of its own would read as milk. A cut of the column at the near plane, for a camera
beside the jet that looks up or down it, was built and taken out again (`c559f8a6`): it
changed crack views close over the fountain and bent the whole screen from a camera inside
the jet.

**Commits.** `ba7f3301` (fountain ring, the earlier source), `1fafd47b` (reference build
for comparisons), `2341a7f` (classic path reference build), `9bb16995` (rings, bubbles,
rising current), `ed4419fe` (table, file row, SPRINGLOG), `07e1a99f` (hashed placement
rule), `c4069084` (own noise table), `7c1b98ec` (reference build for comparisons),
`a80ffb80` (the crack at the foot), `4eafdda7` (probe and suite: crack), `5f9f2cc5`
(reference build for comparisons), `0186a5d2` (crack seen on a slope), `21c41715` (merge:
the crack's gate), `71f594d3` (column's own copy), `b077e5c3` (crack seen under its
bottom), `c559f8a6` (near-plane cut taken out), `a1159212` (level's floor under the
bottom).

### The level load on several cores
2026-10-11

**What.** The HD part of a level load runs on the machine's cores and says in the log
where its time goes. The rooms' build - the vertex buffer, every room's triangles sorted
into draw calls and tagged, the mirror search - runs one room or group at a time on a pool
of threads and is put together in room and group order afterwards, so the buffers come out
the same on one thread as on sixteen; the models' texture pages decode on the same pool as
the rooms' pages. One new registry value, `tomb5.hd_threads` (`0`, the default, takes the
machine's count; never above 16). New fields end three log lines and one line is new: the
`built` line ends in `phases=`, `threads=`, `hash=` and `hash_ms=`, the `trg=` line in
`scan_ms=`, the `models` line in `hash=` and `hash_ms=`, and `HDLOG level=<L> hd_share
ms=` sums the level's whole HD share. Files: `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp/.h`,
`hd_level.cpp`, `hd_pagecache.h/.cpp`, `hd_model.cpp`, `hd_object.cpp`; ModernTest's
`load_pool`.

**Why.** The HD share of a level load stood at 1.2 to 3.9 s per level (TITLE and RICH2 the
longest), of which the room build on one core took 0.7 to 3.0 s and the models 0.4 to 1.2
s; the page decode already ran on sixteen threads. The room build, the model builds and
the TITLE level (1.85 million vertices) were the parts worth taking on.

**How.** *The phases* (`HDRenderLevelBegin`, `HDBeginPhase`, `HDRenderBeginPhaseName`): a
lap after each part books its time - `prep` (the sheen field, the gloss seed), `pages`
(`HDPageCacheCreate`), `owners` (which group owns a water mark, the wind, the falls),
`verts` (the vertex buffer), `setup` (the glow parts, the stand holders), `fill` (every
group's triangles), `index` (mirrors, sheen, windows, the index buffer). `hd_level.cpp`
(`LoadPhase`) times its own steps before the build (marks, boxes, gloss, intr, air, pairs,
cuts, stand, places) and after it (tables, statics, sheets, surfaces, frames, objects)
with the performance counter, and `HDLevelLoad` times the `.TRG` scan on the loading
thread (`scan_ms`). The `built` line carries the steps before the build, the read and the
build's own parts; the `hd_share` line the scan, the build as one part and every step
after it.

*The fingerprint* (`BuildHash` in `hd_render.cpp`, the models' in `hd_model.cpp`): FNV-1a
64 (`HDFnv64`, `hd_pagecache.h`) over the vertex buffer in blocks of 65,536 vertices (each
vertex as `ComposeVertex` puts it together out of the `.TRG` and its three mark bits),
then every group in group order (each draw call's fields and the index bytes it names, the
group's cells, flats, pieces, stand ranges and samples), then the level tables the index
fill writes (destructibles, stand covers and their face flags, stand triangles, book parts
and runs, static pieces, clear pages, hits, air pairs, the counts); block and group
answers are fed in as 8 bytes each. The models' fingerprint runs over each model's vertex
and index bytes and its draw calls' start, count, page slot and node, in build order. The
fingerprints are on with `-log` in the engine and always in RoomProbe and ModelProbe; they
are taken after the build's last lap, and their time is only in their own `hash_ms` fields
(`HDModelStats::hashMs`, `HDModelHashMs`): `built ms=`, the `begin` step, the `objects`
step and the `models` line's `ms=`, `build_ms=` and `buf_ms=` leave it out, so that the
load's numbers measure the load. The fingerprint is what proves each lever below: the same
level gives the same hash on one thread and on sixteen.

*The pool* (`HDPoolThreads`, `HDPoolRun` in `hd_pagecache.h`), header-only so that the
suite tests it as the engine runs it: items handed out in index order from an atomic
counter, the calling thread one of the workers, no thread outliving the call, the first
exception thrown again on the caller. The thread count is `tomb5.hd_threads` through
`HDPoolThreads` (1 to 16 kept, above 16 is 16, 0 or less `hardware_concurrency`), used by
`DecodeThreads` for the rooms and by `hd_object.cpp` for the models. Sixteen is the page
decode's ceiling, which keeps its batches of two pages per thread inside the 32-bit
address space.

The levers and what each must not race on: the page decode (`hd_pagecache.cpp`) runs its
batches on the pool, a page decoding into its own slot of the batch, the uploads on the
calling thread; the models' pages, which decoded on one thread, take the pool's count. The
vertex buffer is built in blocks of 65,536 vertices: a vertex reads the `.TRG` and the
mark tables, which nothing writes then, and writes its own slot of the buffer, of the
shimmer marks and of the hash's bits, each block counting into its own row; a vertex is
put together on the stack and stored whole into the locked WRITEONLY buffer, because
reading fields back from write-combined memory per vertex cost most of the `verts` time
(TITLE 402 ms down to 33 on one thread by this alone). The index fill (`fill_group`,
`FillOut`): a group writes its own slot of `g_groups` and its own `FillOut` - its index
run (start and static-piece indices moved by the run's place at the join), its
destructibles, book parts, stand covers and face flags, stand triangles and static pieces
(ids and first flags moved at the join), its hits and counts (added at the join; the
smallest span, the ripple cap and the add weight folded there), the wind-weighted corners
and the clear pages it sees first (counted at the join for the first group). The two
tables the fill used to make on first use are made before it in their own order - the book
runs (`MaterialBookSlots`; the fill asks `MaterialBookSlotsMade`, which writes nothing)
and every page's plain sheen (`PageGloss`; the fill asks `PageGlossKnown`); everything
else it reads is handed in before the build and written by nobody during it. The groups
are handed out biggest first; the join is in group order. The sort of a pass's triangles
runs stably over their numbers with the same key and lays the 33-word records out in
place, one cycle of the permutation at a time - the order a stable sort of the records
gives. The mirror search (`FindMirrors`) runs one room at a time on the pool, each room's
mirrors in its own row, joined in room order; the other rooms' cells are a sorted list
searched by binary search instead of a hashed set built one insert per triangle.

*The fill's memory* (`kFillBudget`): a group starts when the groups running and it hold
under 96 MiB of triangle records and sort lists, or when nothing else runs - the page
decode's own batch budget, because without it the peak commit on sixteen threads stood 160
MiB over one thread's on TITLE in the 32-bit process. A group holds its share as an
`HDByteGate::Share` (`hd_pagecache.h`), whose destructor gives the bytes back and wakes
the waiters however the fill ends, so a fill that throws (`std::bad_alloc`) reaches
`HDPoolRun`'s caller and leaves no thread waiting. ModernTest's `load_pool` checks the
pool and the gate on 1, 4 and 16 threads, with an item that throws while it holds its
share. `air_ms` on the overlap line is processor time summed over the threads. With
`hd_enable 0` nothing of this runs: the registry value is read with the others, and every
timing, the pool and the hash sit behind `HDEnabled()` in the level build. The result: the
rooms' read and build over the fifteen levels about halved on sixteen threads (21.1 s to
10.8 s in sum), the HD share of rooms and models together 24.4 s to 12.2 s; the page
decode is now the largest part on every level, bound by the BC7 decoder's throughput
(`specific/bc7.cpp`), and the fill is bound by each level's largest group.

**Decisions.** Overlapping the page decode with the fill was not done: the fill asks each
triangle's page whether it is part-way clear (`HDPageCacheSlotClear`), which the decode
measures, the device is not created multithreaded, and the decode's batches are budgeted
for the 32-bit address space. Batches of four pages per thread instead of two gave 7 % on
two levels and nothing on a third and were not kept, since the decode is held by its own
throughput, not its batch tails. A cache of the built buffers across loads was not built:
it could save at most the parts that are not the pages, while its key would have to cover
every input of the build (the randomized classic level's boxes, sectors, faces and
statics, the sidecar's cuts, `hd_gloss.txt`, `hd_water.txt`, `hd_reach`, `hd_air`,
`hd_water` and the engine's build) or draw a wrong level without a word. Splitting a
group's own triangles across threads was not done, as it would have to keep the numbering
of its pieces, stand ranges and destructibles in the order the triangles meet them.

**Commits.** `c947dc6` (phases and fingerprint in log), `956abee` (reference build for
comparisons), `1a4762a` (fill memory held to budget), `2341a7f` (classic path reference
build), `4562db5` (record, manual, tools README), `720147a` (fingerprints' time kept
apart), `d742da0` (pool comments, present tense), `761cdeb` (one pool; model pages),
`c8c087a` (vertex buffer in blocks), `4e0ef51` (index fill per group), `e74e5d9` (triangle
sort, mirror search), `0165045` (pool header-only, ModernTest tests), `be27b71` (gate
share on every exit).

### The level load measured, and the save-load path (#203)
2026-10-14 to 2026-10-15

**What.** Every step of a level load has a time in the log, and a savegame loaded inside
the level being played keeps what that level already holds instead of reading and building
it again. The parts: the `LOADLOG level=<L> step=<step> ms=<n>` lines behind `-log`
(`specific/file.cpp` `LoadLogStep`, `LoadLogLevel`; `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`;
`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp` `ObjectLoadStep`); the level key (`specific/hd/hd_levelkey.h`)
and the resident build (`HDLevelBuildResident`, `HDObjectLevelRebind`), which keep the
level's HD data across a save load inside it; the `.TRG` read once a load and read, with
the first texture pages decoded (`HDPageCacheAhead`), beside the classic level's read; the
models found by one listing of each model folder (`specific/hd/hd_folderlist.h`); the
loading bar shown full in one frame once the work is done (`S_FinishLoadBar`,
`specific/drawbars.cpp`); the classic texture pages kept on such a load
(`TexturePagesKeep`, `LoadTexturePagesKept`, `FreeTexturesFrom`, `HDLevelKeepsNext`); the
decoded HD loading picture kept (`HDScreenReadKept`, `specific/hdscreen.cpp`); the loading
picture drawn under the bar in every bar frame, with one lock on texture stage 0 for the
two threads (`TextureStageLock`, `TextureStageUnlock`, `specific/texture.cpp`). RoomProbe
gains `-loadtime`, `-reload`, `-reloadas <LEVEL>`, `-ahead` and `-aheadverify`.

**Why.** Loading a savegame inside the level being played took as long as a fresh load of
that level - 1.8 to 4.8 s a load, the HD build 50 to 77 % of it - because the load
released and rebuilt everything. The request was first to measure the load's phases, then
to shorten it. The bar's tail - the bar running up from where the loading thread had left
it at 2 percent per drawn frame, after all the work - added 0.2 to 0.8 s to every load,
classic or HD; the bar must take only as long as the load really takes. After the HD data
were kept, a save load inside the level still spent about 140 ms reading the classic
texture pages, about 60 decoding the HD loading picture and 50 in frames that each waited
out a 1/60 s step; those three were taken out as well.

**How.** *The log.* One step is a clock read (`QueryPerformanceCounter`) and a `Log` call
on lines of their own beside the call they time; no call changed. The loading thread's
steps in `LoadLevel` (`free` around `FreeLevel`, `textures`, `read`, `rooms`, `moveables`,
`sprites`, `cameras`, `sound_fx`, `boxes`, `anim_tex`, `tex_infos`, `hd_load`, `ai`,
`items`, `cinematic`, `samples`, `game_setup`) and the main thread's in `S_LoadLevelFile`
(`screen`, `thread`, `ainit`, `hd_build`, `font`, `cutscenes`, `warmup`, `profile`, `bar`,
`total`), one lap per thread. `HDLevelLoad` writes `markers` and `scan`; `HDLevelBuildHD`
writes `release`, `budget`, every `LoadPhase` step, `begin`'s parts (`trg_read`, `prep`,
`pages`, `owners`, `verts`, `setup`, `fill`, `index`, `hash`), `models_hash`, `life` and
`redress`; `ObjectLoadStep` writes `obj_end`, `obj_map`, `obj_mods`, `obj_plan`,
`obj_ring`, `obj_wardrobe`, `obj_models`, `obj_bind`, `obj_lara`. Without `-log` every
line returns in `Log`; `file.cpp` and `hd_object.cpp` read no clock then, `hd_level.cpp`
reads it six times a load. The `S_LoadLevelFile:` lines and the HDLOG lines are unchanged.
The engine's `fill` is one step. `RoomProbe -loadtime` prints the same lines for the
tool's twins of the steps before the build, the game's `HDScanLevel` call and the build's
parts, and takes no picture; it has no classic load, `aInit`, static tables, water steps,
objects, font, `life` or `redress`.

*The key* (`hd_levelkey.h`, pure, so that ModernTest checks the engine's own comparison):
the level's number (`gfLevelId`) and file name; size and last write time of the `.TRC` as
`LoadLevel` opens it, of its `.hdm` sidecar, of the `.TRG` read from the player's Remaster
installation, of `hd_gloss.txt` (read by the room build) and of `hd_water.txt` (read by
the sheets, whose bodies decide the water's life and so its models); the two install
roots; the settings the kept data are made of - `hd_air`, `hd_water`, `hd_objects`,
`hd_texture_budget_mb`, `hd_texture_format` - and `hd_outfit` (Lara's parts). Not in the
key: `hd_threads` (the build's bytes do not depend on it, the fingerprint of every level
says so), `hd_motion`, `hd_reflect`, `shadow_mode`, `hd_softbody`, `hd_reach`, fog and
shimmer (read per frame, not by the build), the HD/SD switch (read only by the objects'
binding, which runs again), the framebuffer and the device (a lost device releases the
data and its key, `HDLevelDeviceLost`). Refused before any field: no key (HD off at this
load), nothing built (released, lost or built with HD off) and an outfit change made in
the level (each appends pages a fresh build does not have). A file changed inside the
installation or a mod between two loads of the same level is not in the key; the session
takes the mods as fixed.

*The keep.* `LoadLevel` names the level it is about to read (`HDLevelKeyNext`, behind the
HD gate, inside the `free` step); `HDLevelUnload` holds that key against the key of the
data in memory, which a full build records at its end, and writes `HDLOG level=<L>
resident=1` or `resident=0 refused=<field>`. Kept, it clears what it clears for every
level - the restored water faces, the water frames, the markers, the objects' level state,
the life - but not the static tables, which number this same level's rooms and statics;
otherwise it frees as before, and the Direct3D objects of the level before are released on
the main thread at the next build, so one level's data are never held through the load of
another. The key a full build records is taken once at the build's top: a rebuild with no
load in front of it (`HDLevelDeviceRecreated` after Alt+Enter or a resolution change)
records none, so the next load of the level builds again. `HDLevelLoad` reads the sidecar
and skips the scan (`LOADLOG step=scan ms=0.0 skipped=1`; the budget takes the kept
level's scan counts). `HDLevelBuildHD` resets the frame counters and clocks and hands over
to `HDLevelBuildResident`: kept are the room art, its pages and buffers, the room tables
(`g_group_hd`, the stand rule and its pieces), the static tables and the models;
`release`, `budget`, `marks` to `places`, `begin` with its parts, `pages_ahead`, `tables`,
`statics` and `models_hash` are logged at 0 with `skipped=1`. Run again: the flip table
(each room drawn by its own group again, so that `sgRestoreGame`'s `FlipMap` flips the
save's rooms through `HDFlipRoom` as on a fresh level), `sheets` (the water sheets with
their splashes, rings, sprays, wet films, tanks and falls, cleared first by
`release_water_sheets`), `surfaces`, `frames` (their pages given back and borrowed again
into the classic `Textures[]` the load has filled again), `objects`
(`HDObjectLevelRebind`: the map, the plan, the ring, the wardrobe with the braid's reset,
every slot's verdict and Lara's build over the models in memory, `obj_models` skipped; a
speaking cut's clips closed; the floor rule's answers taken from the full build), the
springs (`HDSpringLevelBegin`, before the life, after the sheets and the objects' rebind,
the full build's order, timed in `life`), `life` and `redress`. A keep the device no
longer allows falls through to the full build. The HD units' pointers were inventoried for
this: the two into the game's pool (`hd_feet.cpp`) are cleared in `FreeLevel` and made
again by `LoadSamples`, two in `hd_object.cpp` (`g_gave_way`, `g_blob_fading`) are
compared and never read and reset every frame, the build's borrowed lists in
`hd_render.cpp` (`g_marks`, `g_boxes`, `g_grids`, `g_sectors`, `g_intrusions`,
`g_pair_faces`, `g_room_air`, `g_air_links`, `g_carry_sky`, `g_carry_twin`,
`g_stand_rooms`, `g_stand_holders`, `g_stand_faces`, `g_places`, `g_cuts`) are zeroed by
`hd_level.cpp` after the build, `g_book_watch` is kept with the groups it names, and
everything else holds indices, values or device objects.

*Read once and ahead.* The scan keeps its parse (`HDScanKeepTrg`, `HDScanTakeTrg`) and the
build takes it; the `trg_read` line ends in `kept=1`. From `HDLevelKeyNext` on, for a
level the load does not keep, a thread of the load reads the `.TRG` (`HDScanReadTrg`)
beside the classic level's read and then decodes the level's first pages on threads of
their own (`HDPageCacheAhead`): the `.TRG`'s own order, at most one batch budget (96 MiB)
of decoded texels - 72 pages of 512 x 512 - each with the first level and format the build
gives it. The scan waits for the read (`LOADLOG step=trg_ahead ms= waited=`); the build's
create takes every page whose path, first level and format match and decodes the rest; the
upload stays on the main thread (`LOADLOG step=pages_ahead ms= pages= taken=`). A build
that stops before the room build gives the parse and the pages back (`AheadDrop`). *The
folders listed.* `hd_folderlist.h` answers "is this model's file in this folder" out of
one listing of the folder (names without regard to case, regular files only, a missing
folder holding nothing, one that cannot be listed asked of the file as before) for
`HDTrmExists`, `hd_bind.cpp`'s `file_exists` and the mods' model lookup; a level's scan
lists again, the callers ask in their own order so the same folder's file wins, and the
`models` line ends in `listings=`.

*The bar.* `LoadLevel` starts the bar with `S_InitLoadBar(OTPages + BTPages + RTPages +
20)` and calls `S_LoadBar` after each step; while the thread runs, `S_LoadLevelFile` draws
the bar once a turn and each drawn frame moves it by 2 while it is below the target, each
Present waiting in `S_DumpScreenFrame` for a whole 1/60 s step of `Sync()`.
`S_FinishLoadBar` now sets the drawn position to 100 beside the target and keeps
`loadbar_maxpos` at 100 (the done test `loadbar_maxpos <= loadbar_steps` cannot hold by
counting alone from about 80 texture pages on); it is the existing function extended,
since it has one caller and "the load is done" is what it stands for. `S_LoadLevelFile`
draws the bar once under the same `DXF_HWR` test and returns; the loop after the work is
gone, and `S_DrawLoadBar` at position and target 100 returns done. The step `bar` times
the one frame. This is a change of the classic path, at `hd_enable 0` as well: the load's
timing changes, no picture does. The bar does not move during the HD build of a fresh
load.

*The classic pages kept (K).* `LoadLevel` asks once, after `HDLevelKeyNext` and before
`FreeLevel`: `g_pages_kept = TexturePagesKeep()` keeps the pages when `HDLevelKeepsNext()`
(the same `HDLevelKeepRefused` with the same keys `HDLevelUnload` asks a moment later)
says the HD data stay, a record of the pages exists and every recorded entry still holds
its page. The key already holds what the pages are made of: the `.TRC`'s size and write
time and the device; a full `FreeTextures` (`GameClose`) or a page a new device dropped
leaves a hole and the level is read in full. The record (`g_pages`: `nTextures` after the
page blocks and the three counts) is written after every read of the pages, behind the
build gate. `FreeLevel` releases only the entries from the record's end up to `nTextures`
- the misc pages (`FreeTexturesFrom`). `LoadTextures` is split where its own lines stand:
`LoadTextures` keeps the checks and the pixel format, `LoadTexturePages` the page blocks,
`LoadTexturesMisc` the misc block. On a kept load `LoadTexturePagesKept` seeks past the
two page blocks (each starts with its size and packed size), makes the bar's calls a read
makes so that the `pages + 20` count stays exact, leaves `Textures[1..end)` as they are,
sets `nTextures` to the end and binds the last object page to stage 0 as the read leaves
it. A header that does not match the record gives the pages back and reads them; so does
`LoadLevel` when the level file does not open after a kept `FreeLevel`, since the pages
would otherwise stay above `nTextures`, out of every `FreeTextures`' reach. The misc block
(the title's logo pages, the shine, the font, the sky) is read and made as on every load.
The step's line is `LOADLOG level=<L> step=textures ms=<x> kept=1`, and `LoadTextures: <n>
pages kept (RTPages .. OTPages .. BTPages ..)` stands in place of the three page-count
lines.

*The picture kept (P).* `HDScreenReadKept` keeps the last picture `HDScreenRead` decoded,
keyed on its name, the largest edge asked for and the file's size and last write time
(`GetFileAttributesExA` on the path the read opens); the same key hands the pixels back
without opening the file and writes `HD screen: <path> kept, <w> x <h>` instead of
`decoded`; a different key drops the kept picture before its own read, so there is one at
most. Pixels and not the texture, because `LoadScreenHDPixels` makes the texture again in
6.5 to 11 ms while the texture is twice the memory and a Direct3D object a new device
would have to move. `LoadScreenHD` asks the keep only with `HDEnabled()`; the title's
composed logo (`LoadScreenHDLogo`) and the classic `LoadScreen` are untouched. The pixels
(7.9 MiB at 1920 x 1080) go when another picture is read, and with the process - not with
the HD data, because `S_LoadLevelFile` reads the picture before `FreeLevel`, and given
back there at a level change the picture of the level being loaded would go; with
`tr4_loadscreens` on (its default) only the title's loads show a picture, so the title's
pixels stay kept while the levels are played.

*The picture under every bar frame (F).* `S_LoadLevelFile` draws the picture in one frame
and starts the loading thread; `S_DrawLoadBar` draws `DrawLoadingScreen()` before the bar
in every frame it draws, after its own render states (blending off), and `ReleaseScreen`
follows the bar's last frame. The classic code drew the picture in four frames, each but
the first waiting out a 1/60 s step, and then the bar alone onto whatever the back buffer
held; with `D3DSWAPEFFECT_DISCARD` that content is undefined after a `Present` by the
Direct3D 9 contract. Drawing the picture in every bar frame shows it under the bar on any
swap chain; with no picture up (`tr4_loadscreens` on, a level that is not the title)
nothing is drawn under the bar, as before. The picture's texture (2048 x 2048, 16 MiB
`MANAGED`) is now held through the HD build; the texture budget does not read the free
memory (`AutoBudgetBytes`), so no page changes. Both threads now bind texture stage 0,
which Direct3D keeps once per device - `D3DCREATE_MULTITHREADED` makes each call whole,
not a bind and the draws after it - so a loading-thread bind between `S_DrawTile`'s bind
of the picture and its draws would show the picture as a level page or untextured for a
frame. Both therefore hold one critical section: `S_DrawLoadBar` from before the picture
to after `DrawSortList` (covering the bar's own bind of draw type 0 as well), the loading
thread around each of its four binds (`FreeTextures`, `FreeTexturesFrom`, the kept walk,
`LoadTexturePages`); the `Present` and the 1/60 s wait stay outside, and the loading
thread never takes the lock inside a device call, so the locks are always taken in one
order. A test harness on a multithreaded device showed bad frames without the lock and
none with it, at a cost of well under a millisecond per load. The lock lines belong to *F*
and are in the classic path as well. ModernTest counts the decision's place, the keeps'
gates and keys, the one loading frame, the picture first in every bar frame and its
release after the last, the four locked binds, the bar frame's draws under the lock with
its `Present` outside, and the failed open's release.

*The probe.* `RoomProbe -reload` builds the level, takes it as read again, keeps the build
by the engine's key comparison, sets the water sheets a second time over it and draws; the
pictures must equal a run without it. `-reloadas <LEVEL>` shuts the build down and makes
the run again for that level in the same process (`ProbeReloadOther`), with its own room
inputs out of `-roombox` and its statics read again, and prints its fingerprint; with
`-ahead` that level's `.TRG` is read and its first pages decoded while the first level's
build is still in memory, the engine's order at a level change. `-loadtime -reload` writes
the resident load's steps as `LOADLOG` lines; `-aheadverify` decodes every page taken
again and counts the ones that differ. A save load inside a level came down from about 3.6
s to about 1.1 s with the HD data kept, and is expected at about 0.1 s with the pages and
the picture kept as well.

**Decisions.** Keeping the whole classic level resident as well was set aside: the game's
pool goes back to its mark after the load, every pointer into it made in play (creatures'
data, LOT, effects, Lara's mesh pointers) would have to be made again as a fresh load
makes it, and state outside the pool that only a fresh load sets would have to be found to
the last field; the classic reload stays as it was and only the HD data are kept. The read
ahead stays as built although it holds the next level's parse (18 to 56 MiB) and up to 96
MiB of its pages beside the level before's HD data at a level change, because the 32-bit
address space has the room and nothing of it reaches the level's pool. The faster HD build
parts that live in the room build's fill (the hulls per group, the largest groups split,
`MarkCarryCells` on the pool, a sidecar of the whole build) were left to the room-art work
that changes that code. A decode started only after the scan was measured first and gained
less, so the read and the decode start at the top of the load.

### The loading screen's third state and the brake (#204)
2026-10-15 to 2026-10-16

**What.** The *Loadbar style* row on the *HUD* page has three states: *TR5*, *TR4* and
*off*. With a bar, the **brake** keeps the loading screen up for at least `loadbar_min_ms`
(500) from its first frame while the bar runs smoothly to its end, and the bar follows the
work through the HD build as well. Off, a short load - one that keeps the HD art or builds
none - has no loading screen (no picture, no bar, no text) and the level follows the
screen before it through black; a load that builds the HD art shows the TR5 state's
screen. With *Loading text* on, every shown loading screen carries the name of the level
being loaded at the top centre; the script's `TXT_LOADING2` lettering is drawn nowhere.
The *TR4 loadscreens* row is gone with its setting `tomb5.tr4_loadscreens` and its
registry bool `tr4LS` (no longer read or written; an old value stays in the registry,
unread and harmless), and *Loadbar style* and *Loading text* each move up one row on the
page: every shown loading screen is the level's picture - the HD one out of `screens\HD`
with *HD textures* on, else the original. These are changes of the classic path as well,
at `hd_build 0` too: the load's frames and timing change, no room picture does. New: the
registry DWORDs `loadbar`, `loadbar_min_ms` and `loadfade_ms`; `specific/loadbar_math.h`
(`LoadBarModeOf`, `LoadBuildsHD`, `LoadScreenModeOf`, `LoadFadeAlpha`, `LoadBarDone`,
`LoadBarTicksMs`, `LoadNameDrawn`, `LoadNameReach`, `LoadNameY`, `kLoadNameStyle`,
`kLoadNameMargin`); `S_LoadScreenBegin`, `S_LoadScreenDraws`, `S_LoadBarBuild`,
`S_LoadScreenJoin`, `S_LoadScreenEnd`, `S_LoadScreenStatsGet`, `S_LoadScreenName`,
`S_LoadScreenKeepName` (`specific/drawbars.cpp`, `drawbars.h`); `CaptureLoadingScreen`
(`specific/LoadSave.cpp`); `ScreenFadedToBlack` (`specific/specificfx.cpp`);
`LoadEntryBlack` (`specific/file.cpp`); `HDLevelKeyEarly`, `HDLevelNextLoad` and the
helper `KeyStampOf` (`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`, `hd_level.h`); the `LOADLOG` words
`frames=`, `wait=` and `shown=` at the end of the step `bar` and the line
`step=hd_frames`. Gone: `RenderLoadPic`, `GetLoadScreenCam`, `tr4_load_screens`,
`load_cam`, `load_target`, `load_roomnum` (`specific/output.cpp`, `output.h`), `struct
TR4LS` (`global/types.h`), `MenuValTr4Loadscreens` and `MenuStepTr4Loadscreens`
(`game/menu_frame.cpp`), the row's label in `game/gameflow.cpp`'s five-language table.

**Why.** A savegame loaded inside its level took about 52 ms, and the bar was hardly to be
seen. A third state was requested so that the player can choose to see the bar and the
picture - the picture staying for roughly half a second, the bar running through smoothly
- or go straight on with off, also with speedruns in mind; 500 ms was chosen as the
brake's middle value and the fade's length made a value. A load across levels or back to
the title takes seconds because of the HD build; without a screen it shows black for that
time, which looks like a crash, and the HD pictures never appear. The *Loading text* row
drew the script's `TXT_LOADING2` lettering, entry 211 of the language file's PSX block:
"LOADING" in the English and US files, but in the German file (58 entries in a block the
enum counts as 56) a memory card message of three lines, whose third line fell below the
screen's bottom edge at 1920 x 1080, 2560 x 1440 and 3840 x 2160. The TR4 view, a fixed
camera per level drawn from the level being left, is this port's inheritance of Tomb
Raider 4's PC loading screens through the TOMB5 project it starts from; Tomb Raider 5
itself loads over its pictures, the view showed the level being left under the name of the
level being loaded, and naming it right needed a mirror of `DoGameflow`'s switch.

**How.** *The state.* The row cycles TR5, TR4, off (`MenuStepLoadbarStyle`; "off" is the
menu's own entry). It is the registry DWORD `loadbar` (0, 1, 2), read by `LoadBarModeOf`:
present and 0 to 2 it is the state; absent or out of range the older bool `tr4LB` decides
- 1 the TR4 bar, 0 the TR5 one - and that is written as its value, so no player's loading
screen changes. `tr4LB` follows the state (`tr4_loadbar` is the TR4 state) and is still
saved, for the bar's look that asks it. The bar looks are as before: the TR4 bar (wide, x
20, 7 high) or the TR5 bar (x 170, 5 high), each in the three `bar_mode` looks.

*The decision before the load.* `S_LoadLevelFile` forms the level's file name first and
asks `HDLevelKeyEarly(name, &next)`: behind the build gate (`HDEnabled`) it stamps the
keep's key with `KeyStampOf` - the level's name, five file stamps (`GetFileAttributesExA`
on the `.TRC`, its `.hdm`, the `.TRG`, `hd_gloss.txt` and `hd_water.txt`, no file opened),
the two install roots, five settings and the outfit's registry value - keeps it with the
file name, and answers whether the gate is open, whether the `.TRG` is there and whether
`HDLevelKeepRefused` keeps the data. A load builds when the gate is open, the art is there
and the data are not kept (`LoadBuildsHD`); the screen's state is the row's, but TR5 where
the row is off and the load builds (`LoadScreenModeOf`), with the TR5 bar's look.
`HDLevelKeyNext` at `LoadLevel`'s top takes the early key for the same file instead of
stamping again and clears it; any other caller stamps as before. So the screen's decision,
`TexturePagesKeep` and `HDLevelUnload` read one key through one comparison; only the stamp
moves from the loading thread's step `free` to the main thread's step `screen`. The stamp
costs about 0.2 ms. The line is sharp: a load that keeps its data (a savegame of the level
being played, 34 to 94 ms) and a load that builds (another level, the title, the first
load, 0.96 s and more) do not meet. With `hd_build` 0, no installation found or a level
without its `.TRG`, every load is short and off shows no screen. A device made anew clears
the built key (`HDLevelDeviceLost`), so the early answer is a build and the screen is
shown. A device lost before the loading thread reaches its first line clears the built key
after the decision, so that load builds without its screen. With `hd_build` 1 and *HD
textures* off the art is still built: such a load is long and shows the classic picture.

*Off for a short load.* `S_LoadLevelFile` reads no picture, the load's first and last
frames are not drawn and the loop while the loading thread runs draws only while a fade
runs (`S_LoadScreenDraws`); the loading thread, the HD build and every `LOADLOG` step run
as before. `ScreenFadedToBlack` is 1 while the last screen fade ran to black (`DoFade` 2,
its end 255) and nothing set another; `LoadEntryNoteBlack` (`game/gameflow.cpp`) asks it
in `DoTitle` and `DoLevel` before their own `SetFade(255, 0)` resets it, and counts a
movie played after the fade as not black (`fmv_on_screen`), into `LoadEntryBlack`. Over
black nothing is drawn. Over a frame that is not black (a level's end, a movie's last
picture, the credits' last frame), `CaptureLoadingScreen` reads it back once and the loop
draws it under black that thickens with the time since (`LoadFadeAlpha`, 255 x elapsed /
`loadfade_ms`, default 150, with the quad and draw type of `DoScreenFade`); the frame at
full black ends the fade, and `loadfade_ms` 0 is a cut: one black frame, nothing read
back. A loading thread shorter than the fade would leave the frame half faded through the
HD build's long steps, which draw no frame; `S_LoadScreenJoin` ends such a fade at the
join in one black frame. The level's own fade-in takes over after the work.

*The brake.* Position = 100 x min(work, elapsed / T), T = `loadbar_min_ms`, elapsed the
whole 1/60 s ticks of `Sync()`'s grid from the loading screen's first frame to the last
boundary the frame stands past (`LoadBarTicksMs`, on `QueryPerformanceCounter`, the
counter `Sync()` and the `LOADLOG` lines read), so that a frame drawn a little after its
tick moves the bar by that tick's share and no more. Work = s x thread + (1 - s) x main:
the thread's part is its `S_LoadBar` calls (pages + 20); the main thread's part advances
at fixed points by the medians of the main thread's work measured over 18 fresh loads (the
room build's `begin` to 0.730, `objects` to 0.932, the build's end to 0.987, the font and
the cutscenes to 0.989, the warm-up the rest; on a save load the resident build's `sheets`
to 0.186, `objects` to 0.573, `life` to 0.621, the end to 0.968); s = 0.10, the median
thread share of those loads (0.038 to 0.164), when an HD build follows - `hd_build` on and
an installation found (`HDInstallRoot`, not asked with `hd_build` 0) - and 1 when none
does. Both parts only grow, so the bar never goes back and never runs ahead of the work or
the clock; it is full when both are done (`LoadBarDone`): at T on a short load, at the
work's end on a long one. T = 0 is no brake; `loadbar_min_ms` has no upper bound.
`S_DrawLoadBar` waits out the tick first and takes the position then, so the bar shows its
Present's time. While the loading thread runs it draws one frame a tick; after the join
the main thread's points draw a frame only when `TIME_SubTick()` says a whole tick has
passed, so the work never waits: `S_LoadBarBuild` (in `HDLevelBuildHD`'s `lap()` and after
the resident build's five steps, `hd_level.cpp`) and `S_LoadScreenStep` (`file.cpp`: the
join, aInit, the build's end, the font, the cutscenes, the warm-up), and nothing outside a
load's screen, so the rebuild after a new device draws nothing. These frames cost about
0.9 ms each, under 0.5 percent of a fresh load's build, and the end of a fresh load up to
one tick. The bar stands through `begin` and `objects`, whose loops (`HDRenderLevelBegin`
in `hd_render.cpp`, `HDObjectLevelBuild` in `hd_object.cpp`) draw no frame. From the join
to the tail the frames present held (`LoadBarPresentHeld`: `S_DumpScreenFrame`'s and
`DXShowFrame`'s steps without the screenshot key and the reset), because `DXShowFrame`
would reset a lost device and with it release the HD path's objects (`HDLevelDeviceLost`)
while the build still has steps to run on them; a lost device is noted, no further frame
drawn, and the tail's first present resets it. After the work `S_LoadScreenEnd` draws one
frame a tick until the brake is done, its last the full bar; `S_FinishLoadBar` ends the
work (the thread's count and the build's part at their ends), no longer the position. A
save load with a bar ends 500 ms after its first frame.

*The picture and the name.* Every shown load reads the level's picture (`if (shown)`) and
gives it back after its last frame (`ReleaseScreen`, `MonoScreenView`). A frame carries
the name when the row is on, the screen is shown and the slot is a level, not the title's
0 and not -1 for no load (`LoadNameDrawn`); `gfCurrentLevel` is the slot being loaded
while `S_LoadLevelFile` draws. Bar frames cannot print: the classic glyphs come from the
page `nTextures - 2`, which the loading thread frees (`FreeLevel`) while the frames draw,
and the HD atlas is not there before the first level's build or with the HD path off. So
`S_LoadLevelFile` prints the name once, in its first frame after the picture and before
the sort list, then reads that frame back before its present (`S_LoadScreenKeepName`: the
scene ended for the read and begun again for the present) and takes it as the loading
picture, so every bar frame draws the picture with the name and no text of its own; a read
that fails leaves the picture without the name. The name is drawn with `PrintString`, so
the HD font atlas draws it when the HD path draws, in style 2, the title's level list's
style for a name not selected. Its highest ink stands `GetFixedScale(20)` under the top
edge - the bar's own margin from the bottom edge, so name and bar frame the picture alike
- and its baseline lies that plus the font's reach above a baseline at this size
(`LoadNameReach`: the highest of the 106 scaled glyphs and of the accents `PrintString`
composes). A name is one line: no level name of the six language files breaks. The read
back copies the 32-bit back buffer pixel for pixel (`LoadingScreenTexture`) into the mono
picture (`MonoScreenOn` 2, colour, full brightness, window-sized): a `MANAGED` texture of
14 MiB at 2560 x 1440, held from the first frame to the last in place of the HD picture's
16 MiB texture. `CaptureLoadingScreen` has three uses: the fade of an off short load, the
first frame with the name, and the screen where no picture could be read (`LoadScreen`
finds no `SCREENS.STR` or makes no surface). The title shows the logo picture on the first
start (the HD logo with *HD textures* on), afterwards the three title pictures in turn,
with no name; the load into the credits reads the title's picture.

*The comments.* Four comments that named the TR4 view's fade loop as the loop that waits
on `DoScreenFade` (`game/interpolate.cpp`, `interpolate.h`, `specific/specificfx.cpp`,
`InterpTest.cpp`) name the loops that still wait on it: the load and pause menus'
(`S_LoadSave`, `S_PauseMenu`), which present at 30 Hz and leave only on `DoFade == 2`, and
`TitleOptions`. `TOMB5 Code/USING.md` keeps its section on the dropped row: it is the
TOMB5 project's guide as it came. ModernTest's groups `load_mode` and `load_brake` hold
the rule, the state's reading, the fade, the brake on made-up loads and on 34 logged ones,
the name's place at 1080, 1440 and 2160 rows, and the dropped names' absence.

**Decisions.** An off load that builds shows the level's picture with the TR5 bar's look
rather than black, so that a long load never looks like a crash. The TR4 view and its row
were dropped rather than kept beside the pictures: the view showed the wrong level and
only it needed the mirror of `DoGameflow`. The *Loading text* row keeps its name, which
fits and stays more general if something is added later. The read back goes pixel for
pixel rather than through `ConvertSurfaceToTextures`' per-pixel mask arithmetic: the same
pixels for an X8R8G8B8 buffer, about 11 ms against about 41 at 2560 x 1440.

## 2.5 Sixty frames a second

The engine presents up to sixty pictures a second while its simulation keeps the thirty
logic steps a second it has always had. Nothing of the game's arithmetic moved: what a
frame that carries no logic tick shows is interpolated from the two ticks around it, and
every counter that used to measure time in drawn frames was put on the logic tick
instead. The setting is `tomb5.fps_mode`, default 1 (sixty); `fps_mode 0` is the engine
as it was, and every rule below is guarded so that at that setting no line of it is
reached. Engine paths are relative to `TOMB5 Code/TOMB5`. Where TROne (GPLv3) by
Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931 - solves the same problem differently,
its idea was re-derived and credited in the header rather than taken, and nothing of it
is copied; nothing here comes from the Remaster's programs.

### The frame rate option and the clock
2026-09-06 - 2026-09-07

**What.** `tomb5.fps_mode` is a `ulong` in `tomb5_options` (`global/types.h`), read and
written under the registry name `fps_mode`: `0` is thirty presents a second, `1` is sixty
and is the default, `2` hands the pacing to the display. A value above 2 is clamped back
to 1 (`tomb5/tomb5.cpp`). The option is the *Frame rate* row and prints `30`, `60` or
`Display`. The simulation runs thirty logic steps a second in every mode. The modal
screens that stop the world - the pause menu, the load and save screens, the death menu,
the special features, the F4 outfit screen and the loading fade - keep their two-tick
present; the inventory ring and the title screen have since been given the frame rate by
rules of their own.

**Why.** The thirty hertz cap was a single busy wait and nothing else. `Sync()`
(`specific/time.cpp`) counts whole sixtieths of a second (`frequency = pfq / 60`) and
`S_DumpScreen()` (`specific/output.cpp`) waited for two of those ticks before it
presented, while everything downstream was already built for a 60 Hz tick:
`ControlPhase()` (`game/control.cpp`) runs `for (framecount += nframes; framecount > 0;
framecount -= 2)`, where `nframes` is how many sixtieths the frame really took and a logic
step costs two of them. Feeding one tick per present therefore yields sixty presents and
thirty logic steps with no line of the simulation touched. A modal loop steps its own
animation counters once per present and those counters were written for a thirty hertz
present, which is why two ticks is what leaves them alone.

**How.** `gPresentMinTicks` (`specific/output.cpp`, declared in `specific/output.h`)
replaces the constant `2` in `S_DumpScreen`'s wait. `DrawPhaseGame()` (`game/draw.cpp`)
sets it to `GameFrameMinTicks()` around its own present and puts it back to `2` after
`ProfileFrameEnd`, so a frame is judged against the slot it really waited for.
`GameFrameMinTicks()` returns 2 at `fps_mode 0` and while `InventoryActive`, 0 when the
present itself blocks (`fps_mode 2`) and 1 otherwise; `ActiveFpsMode()` reports the mode
the device really got and `TargetPresentHz()` is the same decision as a rate (30 or 60).
The blend factor is `InterpAlphaNow()` (`game/interpolate.cpp`): at `fps_mode 2` it is the
clock (`InterpTickFraction()`), otherwise 1 for any mode but 1, and 1 again for any frame
whose present waits two ticks (`GameFrameMinTicks() >= 2`) - the same test the
display-bound branch makes, so a modal frame is never drawn between two ticks. `DoTitle`
clears `framecount` as `DoLevel` has always done (`game/gameflow.cpp`): the accumulator
survives a level change and the two-ticks-a-present loop returns it to where it started,
so a title entered with `framecount` at -1 read a factor of 0.5 on every frame, every
frame counted as an in-between frame, every counter guarded on the logic tick stood still
- among them `DoScreenFade`, the only thing that sets `DoFade` to 2 - and the fade-in from
black never advanced, leaving a black quad over the menu that swallowed every key. The
clearing costs at most half a logic tick at the moment the title is entered and runs at
`fps_mode 0` too. The *Frame rate* row stands on the *Display* tab of the table-driven
options frame (`game/menu_frame.cpp`) that replaced the tomb5 options pages
(`tomb5/troyestuff.cpp`). At `fps_mode 0` every branch is inert: `gPresentMinTicks` is 2,
`S_DumpScreen` reads `while (n < 2)`, `TargetPresentHz()` is 30 and the frame budget
constants are the old ones to the bit. `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/InterpTest.cpp` carries
a `title_cadence` section that runs the title's two-ticks-a-present accumulator from both
start values of `framecount` and checks that no frame of either is a tween frame and that
the logic tick count is unchanged.

**Commits.** `290c66f`, `ab139d8`, `5301765`, `e0448e4`, `73819d5`

### VSync and the rate the monitor sets
2026-09-07

**What.** `tomb5.vsync` (on by default) switches on the vertical sync the port never had,
and `fps_mode 2` waits for nothing of its own and lets `Present` wait for the panel. The
two rows stand together on the *Display* tab; the *Display* row reads `Display (60)` when
VSync is off, because the blocking present is what paces that mode, and the VSync row
reads `on (restart)`, being a device-creation parameter and the one setting in the build
that is not instant. There is no uncapped mode and no path to one: without a blocking
present `ActiveFpsMode()` reports 1 and the sixty hertz spin is back.

**Why.** With the panel pacing the frames the blend factor can no longer come from whether
`framecount` ended at -1 or 0, and two further rules break with it. "`alpha < 1`" is only
the same thing as "this frame carries no logic tick" while the cadence is two frames to a
tick; at 144 Hz it is true on four frames out of five, and every fade, raindrop, corpse
and caption would have stopped. The clock also has to be read on the other side of the
flip: every other present reads `Sync()` first and flips afterwards because there the wait
is the read, but here the wait is inside `Present`, and a `Sync()` taken before it lands
the waiting ticks in the next frame's count - the factor would ask for a state the logic
has not reached and the picture would stand still for a frame at every logic step. A
driver can also lie: a control panel forcing vsync off leaves the device claiming the
interval while `Present` returns at once, and then nothing bounds the loop at all.

**How.** `PresentationInterval` is part of `D3DPRESENT_PARAMETERS`, so the option is read
in `DXCreate` (`specific/dxshell.cpp`) at startup, on Alt+Enter and on a resolution
change, and the device-lost path in `DXShowFrame` resets from the same `PresentParams`.
`DXCreateD3DDevice` checks `caps.PresentationIntervals` first and drops back to
`IMMEDIATE` with a log line rather than failing to create a device; `DXVSyncActive()`
afterwards answers what the device really got. Because `init_tomb5_stuff` runs on the game
thread that `WinMain` starts after the first `DXCreate`, `load_tomb5_present_settings()`
(`tomb5/tomb5.cpp`) reads that one value ahead of time through the read-only registry
helper `REG_PeekLong` - `OpenRegistry` uses `RegCreateKeyEx` and `init_tomb5_stuff`
decides from `REG_KeyWasCreated()` whether to write the whole set of defaults, so a second
reader opening the key early would have taken a first run's defaults away.
`GameFrameMinTicks()` returns 0 for a display-bound game frame, so the spin is never
entered; at 144 Hz two frames out of three come back from `Sync()` with no whole tick,
`ControlPhase(0)` runs no logic step and the frame is drawn from the clock.
`specific/time.cpp` gained `TIME_SubTick()`, how far past the last tick the clock stands,
read without consuming it and deliberately not capped at one; `InterpRefreshAlpha`
(`game/interpolate_math.h`) is `(framecount + subTick + 1) / 2`, the only mapping that
never has to be clamped - the loop spends two ticks per step but runs one as soon as the
accumulator is positive, so the newest state is the world at `S = 2k+1` and the factor
walks 0 to 1 across every logic step at any refresh rate with no accumulator of its own.
The clamp is for hitches and for the early returns inside `ControlPhase`, both of which
draw the newest state, which is what thirty hertz shows on a slow frame. Logic ticks are
counted rather than inferred (`g_tickSerial`, stepped in `InterpCapturePrev`), and the
drawn frame that finds a new one claims the per-tick counters, so exactly one frame per
logic tick steps them whatever the panel does. `S_DumpScreen` flips first and reads the
clock afterwards in this one mode, which leaves `PROF_SPIN` empty and `PROF_FLIP` carrying
the wait. `NoteDisplayBoundPresent` is the watchdog: six hundred display-bound presents in
a row under half the panel's period is an overridden interval, and the frame rate falls
back to the sixty hertz spin for the session with one line in the log; an iconic window is
not counted, because `Present` on a minimised window can return at once and coming back
from the taskbar must not cost the player the setting. The mode costs one 1/60 s tick more
display latency than `fps_mode 1`, which is why 60 remains the default; in exchange the
busy wait is gone and the core that spun inside `while (!Sync());` waits inside the
driver. Options rows in `game/menu_frame.cpp`.

**Commits.** `e0448e4`

### The in-between frame: the root snapshot
2026-09-07 - 2026-09-20

**What.** A drawn frame that carries no logic tick shows the midpoint between the two
ticks around it instead of a duplicate of the frame before it. New files
`game/interpolate.cpp`, `game/interpolate.h` and `game/interpolate_math.h` (the arithmetic
alone, so that an offline test can include it). Three call sites are the whole seam:
`InterpCapturePrev()` as the first statement inside `ControlPhase`'s tick body, before
`GlobalCounter++` (`game/control.cpp`); `InterpBeginFrame(InterpAlphaNow())` as the first
line of `DrawPhaseGame` after `ProfileFrameBegin`; and `InterpEndFrame()` after
`S_AnimateTextures`, before `ProfileFrameEnd` (`game/draw.cpp`). The snapshot holds
`items[512]` (position, three rotations, room, object, anim, frame, valid), `effects[24]`,
`hairs[2][7]`, the camera and Lara's nine aim angles (the torso twist, the head turn and
the two arms, eighteen shorts) - 15.0 KB, beside 10.7 KB for the live values a frame
overwrites and 1.1 KB of touched-index lists, 27 KB of statics before the particle movers
join them, with no allocation and no pointer into the `game_malloc` pool. Only slots that
moved in the tick are touched. A node whose y angle differs by exactly 32768 between two
ticks keeps the live rotation instead of blending it; its position still blends.

**Why.** `InterpCapturePrev` is the first statement of the tick body because when one
`ControlPhase` runs several ticks - a hitch, the two priming ticks of a level start - each
overwrites the last, and what stands at draw time is the state before the final tick, the
only neighbour the drawn state has. `room`, `object`, `anim` and `frame` are stored so
that a slot handed to a different object can be told apart, otherwise a dead enemy's slot
reused by a spawn would be drawn sliding from the grave to the spawn point. The braid is
in the snapshot because `HairControl` derives every link from the head, and a head that
moves half a step while the braid does not is a plait hanging in the air. Cut scenes are
snapped whole as a correctness requirement: their camera is decoded from a frame index
(`game/deltapak.cpp`) and `frigup_lara()` moves Lara from inside `DrawPhaseGame` itself,
so blending the first would fight a decoder and restoring after the second would undo what
it did (the entry *The cut scenes at the frame rate* below finds otherwise and blends
them). The simulation's own generator had to be protected: the draw path calls
`GetRandomControl` in five places and the star twinkle alone takes four thousand draws out
of the logic stream on every drawn frame, so without a restore two runs of the same level
with the same inputs would drift apart between the frame rates. The half-turn rule answers
`turn180_effect` (`game/effects.cpp`), which does `x_rot = -x_rot; y_rot -= 0x8000` on an
animation command - Lara's roll, its second half, the water roll and four more, seven over
her slot in a level and six of them in every level: on that tick the animation's own root
bone turns the other half, so at thirty the picture is continuous, but the interpolator
blends root and pose apart, `InterpLerpAngle` took exactly half a turn the arbitrary
anticlockwise way while the pose blend was refused on that same tick, and Lara was drawn
sideways for one tween frame. The braid's own flips are the same case: a segment hanging
straight down has an undefined yaw that flips by exactly half a turn from tick to tick,
five or six times a second while she stands still.

**How.** At `fps_mode 1` the blend factor needs no clock: after `ControlPhase` returns,
`framecount` is `-1` when a tick ran and `0` when none did, so the drawn states are `T1,
(T1+T2)/2, T2, ...`. The frame is drawn live instead of blended when there is no previous
state, when `object_number` changed, on a teleport (`abs(dx)+abs(dy)+abs(dz) > 512` in one
tick - nothing in TR5 crosses half a sector under its own power in 33 ms, a terminal fall
is about 130 units), on the same test across a room boundary, on a camera cut, and while
`GLOBAL_playing_cutseq` is set, in which case `InterpBeginFrame` returns before it writes
anything. `InterpInvalidate(why)` drops the previous state at a level and a title start
(`game/gameflow.cpp`), in `FreeLevel` (`specific/file.cpp`), when a savegame is read
(`game/savegame.cpp`, beside `JustLoaded = 1`) and on the return from the inventory, the
save screen, the load screen and the pause menu. `InterpBeginFrame` remembers `rand_1` on
an in-between frame and `InterpEndFrame` puts it back (`GetRandomControlSeed()`,
`specific/function_stubs.cpp`), so the consumption per logic tick is what it is at thirty
whatever the drawing code does; the star twinkle (`DrawStars`, `specific/specificfx.cpp`)
and the floor lasers' water pulse are guarded on top because both write their result back
into persistent state. Angles blend the short way round; Lara's nine aim angles are
blended here rather than by the pose machine because they are per-tick values that come
from the player, written by `LookLeftRight` and the weapon code and read by both halves of
`CalcLaraMatrices` through `phd_RotYXZ`. The half-turn case is named by `InterpHalfTurn`
(`game/interpolate_math.h`) - a y difference of exactly 32768 - and `ApplyNode`
(`game/interpolate.cpp`) then leaves the whole rotation at the live value, the effect
negating `x_rot` in the same breath so that the rotation goes as one; on such a tick the
previous animation root offset is also turned by the same flip before the root-offset
blend of the next entry runs (`InterpRootFlip`, `game/interpolate.h`/`.cpp`,
`game/interpolate_math.h`), because the underwater roll's animation change flips `y_rot`
while the two offsets are the same world point one turn apart and would otherwise drag her
through her own pivot by about 140 units - two sign changes are the whole correction,
since `Rx(a) * Ry(180) * Rx(a) = diag(-1, 1, -1)` for every `a`. Of the seven
`turn180_effect` animations three reach that rule on the flip tick, whose tween is
refused: the roll 147 fires on its first frame, so the change 146 to 147 is the flip tick
(`INTERPLOG root lara anim 146->147` prints `flip=1` there, and RootProbe `-grab 146 147 0
0 -51` over ANDREA1 shows the same turn); the underwater roll 205 fires on a key its rate
1 far-pose rule refuses the tween across; and the tightrope turn 451 fires on the second
key of its held far pair. The other four, 48, 207, 210 and 212, fire on their last frame
and step the frame by one on the flip tick, so the pose is accepted there; that frame
belongs to the old yaw and is drawn from turned copies (see *Lara facing the wrong way for
one tick in the jump twists*), and the change that follows it turns the previous offset
the same way (`g_rootTurned`, `game/interpolate.cpp`). Nothing downstream knows about any
of it: `DrawRooms`, `InsertRoom`, `phd_PutPolygons`, the bucket sorter, the shadows, the
lighting, `HDFrameRoom`, `HDObjectNode` and `HDLaraDraw` read the same globals and get the
interpolated ones - not one line of `specific/hd/` changed, because the HD seam takes its
matrices off the engine's own stack; `HDLOG frame lara` gained `interp=`, what the frame
was drawn at, and `INTERPLOG` gains `halfturn=N` per second (the braid's flips show as
`HAIRLOG dyaw 180` on the same seconds). `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/InterpTest.cpp` holds
the rule in its sections `angles` (exactly half a turn either way, and `turn180_effect`
from every angle on the 512-unit lattice, is a half turn; one unit short of it is not) and
`root_flip`. At `fps_mode 0` `InterpAlphaNow` returns 1 and both frame functions return
before writing a byte.

**Decisions.** The blend is this project's own (OWN). Two larger ways were priced and set
aside: blending the composite yaw of item and root bone, which buys one frame of facing
smoothness in a somersault at the price of a gimbal case where the root bone is pitched;
and recording each tick's finished view-space node matrices and replaying them blended -
in which an item's half turn and the animation's opposite half have already cancelled, so
no half-turn rule is needed - which is a rewrite of the pose path.
