### The options menu as one table-driven frame
2026-08-24 - 2026-09-20

**What.** The options menu is one tree of pages built from tables instead of hand-written
page functions. A root *Options* page offers seven tabs: **Audio** (Music volume, SFX
volume, Sound quality, Language); **Controls** (the sub-tabs *Key bindings*, *View* and
*Modes*, then Control type, Action, Control layout, Camera speed, Dead zone, Targeting,
Ammotype hotkeys — ten rows on one page); **Graphics** (the *Display* sub-tab, then HD
textures, Fog, Distance fog, Shimmer, Mono screen style, Shadow mode, PSX skies, Static
lighting, UW Effect, Look transparency, Footprints); **HUD** (Bar mode, Bar positions,
Enemy bars, Ammo counter, Gameover menu, TR4 loadscreens, Loadbar style, Loading text);
**tomb5 options** (Cutscene skipper, Cheats, Level Select, Fix climb up delay, Flexible
crawling, Crawl Tilting); **Special Features**; **Credits**. The *View* sub-tab carries
the six first-person rows — First person view, Field of view, Death camera, Follow head
bone, Camera damping, Body — and *Modes* the four hold-or-toggle rows. A row that opens
another page is drawn centred; a setting is drawn left-aligned with its value
right-aligned; rows use stepped values rather than free sliders wherever a step is plainly
visible, and *Camera speed* and *Dead zone* are bars driven by a continuous `input &
IN_LEFT/IN_RIGHT`, written once per adjustment when the value stops moving, when the
cursor leaves the row or when the page is left. Forty-seven settings exist, each exactly
once, with the variable, range, default, registry name and side effect they had before. A
list too long for one page splits into pages walked with the left/right arrows on the
bottom line, with a centred `1/N` indicator between the arrows while there is more than
one page, and *Key bindings* carries a centred *Reset to defaults* action above its list
on every page. Entering Options from the title screen or from the pause menu always starts
on the *Options* page. Every label, title and value of a framework page goes through
`CustomText`, which has an English and a German column (86 rows; French, Italian and
Spanish repeat the English literal), keyed by the exact English literal, one literal per
setting. Settings of the *Game* registry block are written when a page holding a changed
value is left, instead of only at a clean exit.

**Why.** The engine grew more settings than hand-written pages hold, and those pages had
no common geometry: the *Controls* page had to force its own glyph pitch and still could
not grow, and a page with nothing on it should not appear in the cycle at all. Four
defects went with them. The key-binding reset copied 72 bytes with `memcpy(layout[1],
layout, 72)`, 36 bytes past `layout` and overlapping its own source. The two blocks that
turned a selected bit back into an array index shifted by one place too few after rows
were added above them, so they wrote three slots too far ("Up" into "Right", "Duck" into
"Jump", "Inventory" into "Load"), the last keyboard row wrote `layout[1][18]` one past the
end of `short layout[2][18]`, and the three last pad rows landed outside the `k < 15`
duplicate-unbind loop — in the default Tank configuration. The *Game* block lived only in
memory until a clean exit, so anything short of one lost the player's settings. And on the
two legacy pages the frame returned before its own `IN_PAUSE` line, so the pause key
closed Options with a page still on the stack and the next visit opened straight into it.
A slider meant to be held rather than tapped is driven by `input &`, so a held direction
was opening the registry key and rewriting every setting up to sixty times a second.

**How.** `game/menu_nav.h` is pure arithmetic with no engine include — `MenuCursorStep`,
`MenuFirstEnabled`, `MenuClampCursor`, `MenuPageCount`, `MenuRowsPerPage`,
`MenuPageFirstRow`, `MenuRowsOnPage`, `MenuPageStep` — and has its own harness,
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/MenuTest.cpp`, built by `bmenu.bat` and listed in
`Preparation/Tools/README.md`. `game/menu_frame.h` is the contract: `menu_row_kind` (TAB /
ACTION / VALUE / SLIDER / BINDING), `menu_page_id`, the three `MENU_SAVE_*` targets
(`MENU_SAVE_GAME` through a dirty flag when a page is left, `MENU_SAVE_TOMB5` at once,
`MENU_SAVE_NONE`), the five callback types, `struct menu_row`, `struct menu_page`, the
four geometry constants and `MenuFrameRun()`. `game/menu_frame.cpp` holds one table per
page with every row's existing logic carried over, the draw-and-drive loop, the key
capture and the `MENULOG` seam; `MENU_PAGE_OPTIONS` stays 0 and `MENU_PAGE_MODES` is
appended after every existing id, so no page already in `menu_pages[]` changed number.
`specific/LoadSave.cpp`'s `DoOptions()` is three lines calling `MenuFrameRun()` (55 lines
added against 917 removed), with `SpecialFeaturesPageRun()` split out for the still
legacy-dispatched *Special Features* page and `specific/LoadSave.h` declaring it; the
legacy branch of `MenuFrameRun()` reads the same `IN_PAUSE` line before returning as every
other page, and the reset copies `sizeof(layout[0])` from `layout[0]`.
`tomb5/troyestuff.cpp` / `.h`, which had carried the tomb5 option pages and for that
reason pulled declarations from `specific/input.h`, `specific/dxshell.h`,
`specific/output.h`, `specific/texture.h`, `specific/drawbars.h`,
`specific/function_table.h`, `specific/dxsound.h`, `specific/audio.h`, `game/camera.h`,
`game/lara.h`, `game/laramisc.h` and `resource.h`, lost `TroyeMenu`, `TroyeMenuPage`,
`Page0`, `Page1`, `Page2`, `PageDisplay` and the page-number constants; `CreditsScreen` is
unchanged. Geometry is one recomputed rule for every page: at `font_height =
GetFixedScale(28)`, which scales with the window so the row count is the same at every
resolution, the title is row 2, rows 4 to 15 are usable and row 16 is the arrow row —
twelve rows, eleven in a list page that also carries the fixed Reset row. Paging splits
balanced, `pages = ceil(n / max)` and `rows per page = ceil(n / pages)`, with wrap; the
`1/N` indicator is drawn in its own colour on `MENU_BOTTOM_ROW`, and the widest string the
tree can produce is `1/3`, 27 pixels wide scaled at 640x480. The settings themselves live
in `global/types.h` (`control_modern`, `combat_hold`, `action_split`, `camera_speed`
default 40, `dead_zone` default 50, and the rest) and are read, clamped and written by
`tomb5/tomb5.cpp` as `ctrl_modern`, `combat_hold`, `action_split`, `cam_speed`,
`dead_zone` beside every other `tomb5.*` value; the *Control type* row calls
`ModernResetControls()`, `ModernCameraResetOrbit()` and `ApplyJoyScheme()` on every
change, so a stale held course, blocked counter, orbit or unhonourable binding never
survives a switch. `game/gameflow.cpp` holds the `CustomText` rows, the German column
writing umlauts as the Latin-1 bytes `0xE4`, `0xF6`, `0xFC`; `AccentToCode`
(`game/text.cpp`) maps them to 128+4, 128+20 and 128+1 and `PrintString` composes each
from `CharDef` plus its row of `AccentTable` (`game/accent.inc`) — the sharp s has no row,
so the table avoids it, and a matched row returns its column unconditionally, which is why
the other three languages repeat the English literal rather than leaving a cell empty.
`specific/input.cpp`'s `ModernMenuReadsPad()` mirrors the seam's own "is this a menu"
predicate (`InventoryActive`, `gfLevelId == LVL5_TITLE`) and feeds the classic assembly
the left stick together with the d-pad while it holds, a medipack bound to a d-pad bit
being declined for the one tick that predicate holds so one press cannot mean two things.
`TOMB5 Code/tomb5.vcxproj` lists the new files and `docs/Engine-Manual.md` describes the
tree.

### A credits screen
2026-08-22 - 2026-08-30

**What.** The game has a credits screen of its own, reachable from its own row in the
options menu, with a Contributors section. Groups are separated by colour rather than by
blank lines, and the running state is not a function static, so an abort lets the next
roll start from the bottom again.

**Why.** GPLv3 courtesy and a project requirement: the names without which this would not
exist belong in the game, not only in a readme. It is not a page of the options, because
as a page it turned up unasked while paging through the settings and the paging arrows are
drawn at a fixed row that landed across a line of names. The screen holds fifteen rows, so
four blank separators would push the tool credits off it.

**How.** `specific/alexstuff.cpp` / `.h` hold the screen and its roll,
`tomb5/troyestuff.cpp` the `CreditsScreen` page and the Contributors list, and the
*Credits* tab of `game/menu_frame.cpp` opens it.

**Commits.** `061e330`, `df04a37`, `a975ecf`, `8a4bc4e`, `a82d979`, `c05ed61`, `23a73d3`

### Skipping cutscenes and the intro flyby with the controller
2026-07-31 - 2026-10-16

**What.** Cross on a controller, and Enter, skip a cutscene and the level-intro camera
flyby, as Escape already did. The skip fires only while `cutseq_trig == 2`, the actual
playing state, and Cross must be freshly pressed; Escape keeps its original held
behaviour. The end credits roll can be aborted and the intro can no longer be skipped
twice. A skipped camera flyby fires the heavy trigger under its last camera, as a flyby
played through does; the skip itself stays as it is: the same keys, the same edge, one
camera a frame, the fade, the credits and the intro. The files: `game/control.cpp` (the
state test and the edge), `game/spotcam.cpp` and the new `game/spotcam_math.h` (the intro
flyby and its triggers), `specific/alexstuff.cpp` (the credits roll and the intro videos),
the `FLYLOG` line behind `-log`, and `TrgProbe -flyby`, the census of every level's flybys
and the triggers they test.

**Why.** The skip check ran for any non-zero `cutseq_trig`, so entering a cutscene trigger
while firing meant Cross — the fire button on controllers — was still held when the
pre-start fade finished, and `do_cutseq_skipper_stuff()` aborted the scene before
`Load_and_Init_Cutseq` ever ran. The played flag, set inside `Load_and_Init_Cutseq`, was
therefore never written, Lara still stood on the floor trigger, and the scene was
requested again the next frame: an endless approach-and-abort loop that only Alt+F4 ended.
The edge is required because an earlier form of the Cross check read already-masked input.
In play, a skipped flyby left triggers unfired that a flyby played through fires: RICH2's
lifts and RICH3's helicopter at the start; both are flybys (spotcam sequences), neither is
a CUTSEQ cutscene. That a skip can fire them was observed on a TR4 level in TROne (GPLv3)
by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931; the cause below is this project's
own reading of `CalculateSpotCams` (THIRD-PARTY.md, entry 227). The frame takes the
spline's place from the position it starts with, steps it, and the skip then jumps it to
0x10000; the camera is placed afterwards at the frame-start place. The segment's end arms
the test of the camera just reached, the refill makes that camera knot 1 of the next
segment, and the next frame, starting at position 0, stands exactly on it and tests there
- for every camera but the last the skip tests where a played run does. The last camera of
a SNAPBACK sequence is tested in the frame it is reached and the flyby ends: played
through, that frame stands within one speed step of the last camera; skipped, it stands at
the camera before the last. Its trigger is never tested, and the one before it is tested
twice. A sequence without SNAPBACK ends on the spline to the chase camera, whose first
frame stands on the last camera and tests it there; the skip changes nothing there. The
look-key break clears the armed test without running it and is not the skip.

**How.** `game/spotcam_math.h`: `SpotEndTestCamera(first_flags, skipped, title,
last_camera)` gives the last camera when the frame's segment end was forced by the skip,
the sequence has SNAPBACK and the level is not the title, otherwise -1 (the camera's
place); `SpotSeqEndsShort` is the census rule; the flag values are asserted against
`spotcam.h`. `game/spotcam.cpp`: `skip_now` is set where the skip jumps; the end branch
asks the rule and tests at `SpotCam[last]`'s place and room, the other tests as before.
`check_camera` is kept where a test is armed; `FlyLog` writes `FLYLOG seq=<n> cam=<i>
flags=<hex> test=<x>,<y>,<z> room=<r> skip=0|1 tick=<GlobalCounter>` at both tests.
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/TrgProbe.cpp` `FlybyCensus` and its helpers: the spotcam block
found behind the fixed cameras by the counts up to the `TEX` marker, the GetFloor door
walk and the GetHeight descent to the trigger's sector, the trigger read as
`_TestTriggers` reads it. Over the classic `.TRC` files the census counts 64 sequences,
359 cameras, 58 of them with SP_TESTTRIGGER; 11 sequences end short on a skip, and five of
them have a heavy trigger under the last camera that the skip left unfired: RICH2 3 (the
lift: LIFT_DOORS1, LIFT_DOORS2, two BLUE_GUARDs, music 1, TWOGUN), RICH3 6 (the helicopter
at the start: TWOGUN), ANDREA2 5 (DOOR_TYPE3), ANDREA3 5 (TELEPORTER, music 16) and RICH1
0 (cutscene 11, which now starts on a skip as well); the title never skips. ModernTest's
`spotcam_end` group models the frame order (`spot_run`): played through, skipped without
the rule and with it, the title, a skip from the middle of the last segment, a skip let go
before the end, the chase-camera end skipped and played, no test on the last camera, the
rule alone and the census rule on the levels' flags.

**Decisions.** The CUTSEQ skip (`do_cutseq_skipper_stuff`, `game/deltapak.cpp`) is
involved in neither example and is not changed. Two sequences take the chase-camera end
with a test on the last camera (ANDY3 6, whose last camera starts cutscene 44, and RICH2
0, no trigger): on a skip their second test runs at the last camera instead of near the
chase camera, and that is left as it is, since the trigger there has already been tested.
RICH2's sequence 3 jumps from camera 5 to 7 (SP_JUMPTO), so camera 7's test (music 14) is
never armed, played or skipped - a data fact, left as it is.

### The HD/SD switch: F12 and a pad chord (#202)
2026-10-13 - 2026-10-15

**What.** A switch between the HD draw and the classic draw, for comparing the two at one
spot: F12 on the keyboard, Modifier+Options on the pad, and the *HD textures* row of the
options are one switch, and a press draws the whole world - the rooms, the statics, the
sky, the items and enemies, Lara, the water and its life, the splashes and the tank, the
shadows and the fog bulbs - and the interface - the inventory ring and the pickup display,
the HD font, the loading screens and the F4 outfit changer - classic or HD from the next
frame on, with no pause. Two settings carry it. The build gate is a new registry DWORD
`hd_build` beside `hd_air`, 1 by default, with no row in the options: with it on and the
installation found, a level's HD data are built at its load whatever the row says; with
`hd_build` 0 nothing of the HD art is opened or built and the engine is the classic one.
The draw is `tomb5.hd_enable`, which keeps its registry name and its row *HD textures*
(on/off): F12, the pad chord and the row move this one value through one setter, the row
shows every flip, and a flip is saved at once. Where the level on screen has no HD data -
`hd_build` 0, no installation, or a level the `.TRG` has nothing for - a press changes
nothing and says why in the log. The sounds stay as built: the HQ samples and the barefoot
set are loaded into the sample memory at the load. The files: `specific/hd/hd_switch.h`
and `hd_switch.cpp` (new), `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`, `hd_object.cpp`, `hd_laradraw.cpp`,
`hd_life.cpp`, `hd_font.cpp`, `hd_outfitmenu.cpp`, `hd_spring.cpp`, `game/key_scheme.h`,
`game/pad_scheme.h`, `game/menu_frame.cpp`, `specific/input.cpp`, `specific/registry.cpp`,
`specific/output.cpp`, `specific/file.cpp`, `global/types.h`, `tomb5/tomb5.cpp`, `TOMB5
Code/tomb5.vcxproj`, and RoomProbe's `-hddrawn`.

**Why.** A key was wanted to switch HD and SD at one spot without delay, the HD look
against the classic look; F3 was planned for the photo mode, so the key is F12, with a
binding for the controllers as well. The build stays at the load, synchronous on the
threads it ran on before, because it is the slow part (about one to two seconds a level
with `-log`'s `HDLOG ... built ms=` lines) and the switch must cost nothing, while the
classic data are resident anyway, so both draws have what they need for the whole level; a
build in the background during play would bring a stretch with nothing to switch to and
upload hitches. The data are built whenever the installation is found, whatever the row
says, so that the switch works at once in every level and no state remains in which a
press flips something not drawn until the next load; the cost is that a player with an
installation who plays classic pays the HD build and its memory at every load. The
interface follows the draw so that the whole picture is uniform. The sounds cannot follow
a state that changes from frame to frame, since they are loaded into the sample memory at
the load.

**How.** The key: `game/key_scheme.h` has `KEY_SCHEME_ROLES` 35 and `KEY_ROLE_HD_SWITCH`
34, F12 (0x58) at the end of `KEY_SCHEME_MODERN_ROW`; `specific/input.cpp` puts F12 at the
end of both Tank rows, asserts that the Modern slot is `DIK_F12`, names "F12" in both
key-name tables so the page shows and captures it, and makes the one call
`HDSwitchInput(Key(KEY_ROLE_HD_SWITCH) != 0, ControlMethod == 1 &&
JoyRole(JOY_ROLE_HD_SWITCH), !gfGameMode && !InventoryActive)` in `S_UpdateInput`; it sets
no input bit. A press is the edge from up to down of the role's key or its pad chord, read
as one `down`, so a held key flips once and key and pad together are one press; the held
state is kept on every reading, so a key still down when a menu closes is no new press. A
press switches only in a level and under no menu (the ring, the pause menu, load and save,
the outfit window and the Key bindings page), so binding F12 there switches nothing. The
pad: `game/pad_scheme.h` has `JOY_ROLES` 29 and `JOY_ROLE_HD_SWITCH` 28; the two
DirectInput-numbered Separate rows end in 9, Options, and `JOY_SEP_CHORD_DINPUT` carries
the role's bit, so the default is Modifier+Options; the XInput-ordered rows and every
One-key set leave it unbound, as they do every chord, since they have no Modifier. The
chords already in use were Modifier+R1 (flare), +R3 (save), +L3 (load) and
+Cross/Circle/Triangle/Square (the first four weapons); of the buttons no chord used,
Options is the game's own system button, the PS button may belong to the system, and the
d-pad and the right stick are each blocked by one scheme; plain Options stays pause,
because a plain role stands aside while the Modifier is held. `PadSeatAppended` seats a
role a stored set has no value for: the default pair whole, or unbound when the pair has
no button, is the Modifier's own button or is already another role's.
`specific/registry.cpp`: `JHd` and `SJHd` at the end of the two name tables; a set stored
without `SJHd` carries an `SJChord` without the role's bit, so its default button read
alone would be a second plain pause - the load seats it through `PadSeatAppended` and
writes `SJHd` and `SJChord` back at once; a set the load strips of its chords keeps the
role unbound until *Reset to defaults*. A keyboard set without `Key34`/`MKey34` reads F12,
which no stored set can hold, since the page had no name for F12. `game/menu_frame.cpp`:
the row *HD / SD* last in both binding lists, and the cheat filter of
`MenuResolveKeybinds` named at both ends, so the row is always shown.
`specific/output.cpp`: Core's F12 toggle of `App.BumpMapping` in `S_OutputPolyList` and
its counter are gone - a debug leftover; no picture depends on it, since the registry load
sets `App.BumpMapping` to 0 and the toggle was its only other writer.

The state: `specific/hd/hd_switch.h` holds the rule as pure arithmetic, `HDSwitchStep` (a
press) and `HDSwitchSet(s, on, hd)` (a step of the row: the state takes the row's value;
`held` is not touched, so the row's step is never an edge of the key).
`specific/hd/hd_switch.cpp`: the key's held state is the only state of its own;
`Current()` reads `{hd_enable, held}`, `Commit()` is the one setter, `HDDrawn()` returns
`tomb5.hd_enable`, `HDSwitchHasData()` is `HDLevelBuilt() || HDObjectActive() ||
HDLaraActive()` - HD rooms, HD objects or an HD Lara built at the load, one test for the
key, the pad chord and the row - and `HDSwitchInput` and `HDSwitchOption` run the pure
rule on `Current()` and commit it. `MenuStepHdTextures` is the sound and
`HDSwitchOption()`, and `MenuAfterChange` saves the value with the tomb5 settings as for
every row. A press writes the one value it changed at once (`SaveDrawn`: the tomb5 key
opened, one `REG_WriteBool`, closed), because `save_new_tomb5_settings` has one caller,
`MenuAfterChange`, and `WinClose` writes the Game key's bindings alone: a flip left to the
exit would be lost, and so a crash loses no flip, as it loses no step of a row. The row
with nothing to switch still moves its value, as a step of an option does, and says
nothing to switch; the key does not move it. The build gate: `hd_build` (`ulong`,
`global/types.h`) is defaulted, read with `REG_ReadLong(buf, tomb5.hd_build, 1)` and saved
in `tomb5/tomb5.cpp` beside `hd_air`, and written into the registry with its default the
first time the game reads the settings. `HDEnabled()` is `if (!tomb5.hd_build) return
false; return HDInstallRoot()[0] != 0;`; `HDLevelBuilt()`, new, is the rooms' build flag
`g_level_active` alone; `HDLevelActive()` is `g_level_active && HDDrawn()` - the
`HDEnabled()` term is inside `g_level_active`, which is set only past an `HDEnabled()`
test of the same load, and `HDEnabled()` cannot change in a session: `hd_build` is read
once and has no row, and the installation is searched once. Migration: no new value for
the player. A saved `hd_enable` 0 draws classic and now builds HD when found, so F12 works
at once; a saved 1 draws HD; the default stays 0, so a new player with an installation
starts classic, presses F12 and sees HD.

The gates: every reader of `HDEnabled()`, `tomb5.hd_enable` and `HDDrawn()` is either a
BUILD reader (whether HD data exist or are to be built) or a DRAW reader (whether HD is
drawn), and each changed line is the gate's own line, changed in place. The build readers
- the scan, the build, the kept build, the read-ahead's drop (now `tomb5.hd_build`), F4's
rebuild, the device's rebuild, the HQ samples' table, the two spare sample infos (16
bytes) of `LoadSamples`, the barefoot set, the HD font's page and atlas, and the #203
key's `valid`, which now follows `hd_build` and not the draw - ask the build gate and none
the draw. The draw readers: the room walk's question `HDLevelActive`; the rooms
(`GroupOfRoom`), the rooms drawn as art (`StandHolderRoom`), the dropped classic faces,
the carried rooms and `HDCarriedRoom`, the statics, the sky, the shadow room and the
art-listed room, which ask `!HDLevelActive()` where they asked `!g_level_active`; the
items and cutscene actors (`|| !HDDrawn()` in `hd_object.cpp`), Lara, her braid and the
arm path (`&& HDDrawn()` in `hd_laradraw.cpp`), the life's frame (`HDLifeFrame`, `||
!HDDrawn()`); the ring and the pickup display (`HDInvBegin`), the HD font per character
(`HDFontGlyphAt`), F4 (`|| !HDDrawn()`), the loading screens (`!tomb5.hd_enable ||` in
`file.cpp`) and *Shadow mode*'s fifth state (`HDEnabled() && HDDrawn()`). The reach of the
walk, the mirrors, the projected shadow's gate, the ripples on a sheet, the waterfall
drops, the splash flag 0x10, the spray flag and the fish tank's mesh ask `HDLevelActive()`
already; the blobs follow from those gates; the sheets, the glow parts, the bulb rule, the
wet floor, the roam, the covered faces and the hull push follow the rooms, so with nothing
HD on the frame `HDFrameDraw` and `HDFrameDrawGlow` return at their first test. The flips
go on through `HDFlipRoom`, which keeps `g_level_active`; the build, the device and the
life built at the load (`life_on`) are data and stay. The life's gate sits in
`HDLifeFrame` and not in `life_on`, because `HDLifeModelPlan` and `HDLifeLevelBegin` ask
`life_on` at the load and a level loaded while classic is drawn must still build its life
for the flip back. The models' release at the load (`HDObjectLevelBuild`) asks
`!(tomb5.hd_objects && HDLaraActive())`, the build and not the draw, so a level with an HD
Lara and no HD object loaded while classic is drawn keeps its HD Lara. The springs:
`HDSpringLevelBegin` asks only `tomb5.hd_water` and the sheets
(`HDRenderWaterSheetsBuilt()`, true only after an HD build), so the springs and their
cracks are built with the HD data whatever is drawn, and the life built after them reads
them as its bodies' springs; the frame asks the draw: `HDSpringFeed` (the rings),
`HDSpringDraw` (the columns and the bubbles) and `HDSpringCrackDraw` (the cracks and their
holes) return on `!HDLevelActive()`; the resident build of #203 (a save loaded inside its
level) makes the same call after its sheets and before its life. The loading screens
follow the files in `screens\HD` alone, which need no installation, so their gate is the
draw only. The title menu's HD wordmark, read from the same folder at the title's load
(`LoadTitleLogoHD`), follows the files alone and is not gated by the draw. The HUD has no
HD bars or icons; its HD parts are the font and the pickup display. The classic draws the
HD path leaves out come back through the gates that now answer false: `InsertRoom` draws
every roomlet with no face dropped and the classic water faces among them, the statics
through `HDStaticDrawnClassic`, the horizon and both colour layers, every item and
cutscene actor by its classic mesh (`begin_decision` answers `BEGIN_NONE`), Lara's classic
composite and braid, the fish tank's classic mesh, the ripple, splash and spray sprites,
and the blobs at the option's own mode (`HDShadowGate` answers `hd_off`).

While classic is drawn a flip changes one integer and nothing else: the next frame takes
the other branch at each gate; no HD data is freed or rebuilt, nothing is uploaded and no
shader changes - the HD pages, buffers, models and sheets stay resident as the load built
them, and the one D3D object the HD frame makes on demand, the projected shadow's map,
lives as long as the device. The clock-driven things ride the HD clock, which steps by the
difference of `GlobalCounter` since its last frame, so the first HD frame after a stretch
drawn classic is at the time it would have been - exact for stretches under 36 minutes,
where the ushort counter turns over. The fish tank's film, burst and wet floor are worked
out from the tank's own item every frame. What starts again whenever its gate opens: the
projected shadow fades in over 0.25 s (`HD_SHADOW_FADE_IN`) while the blob goes out; the
soft motion of Lara's chest starts from rest; her braid's root follows the draw (-33 for
HD against the classic -48), so on the switch back it moves 15 units and the chain is
pushed out of the pack's box over the next frames. What catches up in one frame: the
water's life, whose tick runs inside `HDLifeFrame`; the first HD frame ticks the whole
stretch in steps of a tenth of a second (`HDLifeTick`), so the floats and fish stand where
they would have, within 23 units, and every ring of the stretch is written into the game's
ripples at once, which costs 8 to 21 ms more in that frame after ten minutes drawn
classic. Short effects: a splash or spray keeps the look of the draw it was born in for
its life, under a second; waterfall drops already in the air live out their 24 ticks. The
sheets' ring tracker (`HDRenderWaterRipples`, fed by `FeedWaterRipples` from
`HDFrameDrawGlow` only) keeps every ripple slot as the last HD frame saw it, so a slot a
new ripple took during the stretch, past its fade-in and larger than the one remembered,
gets no ring and, as its classic sprite stays out, shows nothing for at most about two
seconds (`SetupRipple`, a life of 48 to 63 ticks).

The log behind `-log`: `HDLOG settings hd_enable=<0|1> hd_build=<n>` once at the end of
`init_tomb5_stuff`; `HDLOG switch drawn=0|1 level=<stem> tick=<GlobalCounter>
frame=<GnFrameCounter> by=key|pad|option` per press or step that reaches a level, which
with nothing to switch ends in its cause, `hd_build=0 nothing to switch`, `install=none
nothing to switch` or `built=none nothing to switch`; `level` is the stem of the one file
of the table whose identity (`LevelIdFromFile`) is `gfLevelId`, `?` when none or more than
one is. With `-log`, a level loaded while classic is drawn writes its `HDLOG softbody`
line with `state=off reason=classic`, documented as "no HD Lara drawn". The probe:
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/RoomProbe.cpp` takes `-hddrawn 0|1` (`HDDrawnSwitch`) and
keeps the switch's state as the engine does, an `HDSwitchState` from `HD_SWITCH_START`
moved by `HDSwitchStep`; while its own `HDDrawn()` answers false the frame draws, in place
of the art, the classic faces of every room it lists - the seed room and every `-with`
room - as `-classicroom` with `-classiconly`, after the whole HD build, flat grey from the
`.TRC`, so it cannot show the game's classic draw; the option chain is at the compiler's
nesting limit (C1061), so the chain's last `else` calls the switch's function, which also
reports any other argument as unknown. The tests: ModernTest's switch, wiring and option
groups (one flip per press, the gate lines counted in the engine's text so that a gate
taken back shows as a count, `HDSwitchSet` over every state, and the truth table over
`hd_build`, installation, level data and row) and MenuTest's binding, round-trip and
row-step groups.

**Decisions.** In every case the world and the interface are HD exactly when the level on
screen has data and the row is 1; the row shows the state because it is the state. The
rule that the classic engine stays as it was moves from `hd_enable` 0 to `hd_build` 0:
with the gate off every reader of the load returns where it returned with `hd_enable` 0
before - no installation is looked for by the HD path, no file opened, no HD data built,
the two spare sample infos not allocated - and every draw reader answers classic because
nothing was built; the record's earlier entries that prove "`hd_enable` 0" measured the
engine when that value was the build and the draw in one, and read as `hd_build` 0 now.
Two things the switch leaves after a long stretch drawn classic are kept with no fix,
because the mode serves a short before-and-after comparison: the water's life writing
every ring of the stretch at once, and a ripple whose slot was taken again showing no ring
for up to two seconds. The softbody log line keeps `reason=classic` for both a classic
draw and a level loaded while classic is drawn, because telling them apart would need a
new reader of the switch beside the gate lines and a new value in the middle of an
existing log line. A known limit stays as built: the barefoot set and the two spare sample
infos follow the build gate, not the draw, so a player with `hd_build` 1 and an
installation who plays classic hears the outfit's footsteps from the unmodded bank, where
Beta 2.0 played a footstep mod, and `game_malloc`'s layout lies 16 bytes further on than
with the gate off. A player who copied the loading screens into `screens\HD` and keeps the
row at 0 sees the classic loading screens until F12 or the row, by the uniform rule.

state), `b5d39ba`, `a24dd9b`, `7b836b8`, `7779464` (the gates wired), `7887938`,
`fff824b`, `2409d71`, `25c2320` (the row sets the switch), `254a0ce2` (the gates' census
base), `d9803eb1` (the springs' merge base), `8eb0c2a` (build gate, draw gates), `6366176`
(row and switch one state), `c440b8e` (the build gate's comment)

### The installation gate: the HD build row and the TR3 sources (#230)
2026-10-21 - 2026-10-22

**What.** The engine's half of the work around the installations the engine and the
randomizer read at run time (the randomizer's half is its row in section 3). The search
for the Remasters, the Mods scan and the two readers that walk a found root (the wardrobe
and the classic object reader) walk every folder with wide names and error codes and
cannot throw any more; a root the system code page cannot spell is refused with one line.
One `INSTALL` line behind `-log` says what the search found and why. A row *HD build* on
the *Graphics* page, right above *HD textures*, switches the HD build off for good, from
the next level load on, so a player who plays classic gets the short loads back while HD
can still be switched on the fly when the row is on. The files:
`specific/hd/hd_install.cpp/.h`, the new pure header `specific/hd/hd_install_names.h`,
`specific/hd/hd_mods.cpp`, `specific/hd/hd_wardrobe.cpp`, `specific/hd/hd_classic.cpp`,
`specific/hd/hd_switch.cpp`, `specific/file.cpp`, `game/menu_frame.cpp`,
`tomb5/tomb5.cpp/.h`.

**Why.** The engine runs in the system's ANSI code page (no manifest code page, character
set "not set"). Folder names outside it made the search and the readers throw: the search
walked an override folder holding a Cyrillic or CJK entry into a `system_error` and left
both roots empty, and passed over a library path with such a letter (UTF-8, as
`libraryfolders.vdf` spells it) without a note; the Mods scan kept its paths in the code
page (`path::string()`) and asked the file system about them through `u8path`, which
throws on any byte that is not UTF-8, so a German umlaut in a mod's folder name ended the
game at the first level load - with `hd_build` 0 as well, since the sound bank chain scans
the Mods folder first; and once the search found a root in a library with a Latin-1 name,
the wardrobe's walk (`add_from_install`) and the classic reader's (`HDClassicRead`) read
its code-page spelling back as UTF-8 through `u8path`, which throws on it, with no catch
above them - the end of the game at the first HD level build; the wardrobe also read each
file name through `path::string()`, which threw on a Cyrillic one. The HD build costs a
player who never presses F12, measured in play over nine loads, 1.25 to 4.78 s more per
level load (median 3.2 s), 232 to 475 MiB of texture pages and 10 to 62 MiB of room
buffers on the card and 7 to 17 MiB of managed model buffers; a way to switch it off
completely was wanted, with no build on demand.

**How.** The rule: a name is compared wide and turned into the code page only where a
narrow file call needs it, and only when it survives the trip there and back
(`WC_NO_BEST_FIT_CHARS`). Seventeen narrow opens and listings in twelve files take a path
made from a root (the page cache three, the `.TRM` and `.TRL` readers two each, the binder
two, the `.TRG` scan, the font, the springs, the debris, the classic pages, the sound
bank, the level key's stamp and the folder listing one each): over the twelve set as the
limit for turning them wide, so the root is refused at the source and the sites stay
narrow. *The resolver* (`hd_install.cpp`, `hd_install_names.h`): `child` walks with
`increment(ec)` and compares with `_wcsicmp`; Steam's folder is read with `RegGetValueW`,
the vdf's paths as UTF-8 (the code page as the fallback); the roots are found wide and
handed on by `narrow_root`; `search` runs the walk inside a try/catch whose catch writes
the reason; a root that does not fit says "install path not representable in the system
code page: HD off". `HDInstallSearched` asks nothing; `HDInstallAddLibrary` is for the
tools. *The Mods scan* (`hd_mods.cpp`) keeps its paths in the code page and asks the file
system in that same code page; a name that does not fit is skipped with one `MODLOG
skipped` line; the scan has the same net. *The readers of a found root*
(`hd_wardrobe.cpp`, `hd_classic.cpp`) read it in the code page it is handed on in
(`HDNameWide`), take each file name through `HDNameFits` and pass over one the code page
cannot spell - the wardrobe counts it among the files its scan line says it passed over;
the classic reader cuts the level's name out of the path without a conversion. *The
`INSTALL` line* (`specific/file.cpp`, once, after the first load thread has joined):
`INSTALL hd=<root|none> tr3=<root|none> reason=<notes joined with " | ">
bank=<mod|audio|install|level>` - after the join rather than at the first resolver call,
because with `hd_build` 0 that call is the sound bank chain's on the load thread, and the
bank is known only once the chain ran; the line looks nothing up, so `hd_build` 0 walks no
library it did not walk before, and the engine's output at `hd_build` 0 differs from
before by that line alone. *The row* (`game/menu_frame.cpp`): *HD build*, on and off,
default on; it shows and steps `tomb5_hd_build_next` (`tomb5/tomb5.h` and `.cpp`), which
the save writes as `hd_build`; the gate in force, `tomb5.hd_build`, takes it at the top of
`S_LoadLevelFile`, before `HDLevelKeyEarly` asks `HDEnabled` for the first time. Every
reader of `tomb5.hd_build` - `HDEnabled`, the load bar's share, `HDLevelBuild`'s
ahead-drop, the switch's cause, the outfit window's text - reads it and none writes it, so
a step in a running level changes nothing until the next load; turned off, the level
before is still released (`HDLevelUnload` and `HDLevelBuild` release whatever the gate
says). F12 with the gate off shows "HD is off" for 30 drawn frames in the ammo hotkeys'
caption (`hd_switch.cpp`), where the switch line names `hd_build=0`. The tests:
ModernTest's `install_names` group and MenuTest's `graphics_build_row` group.

**Decisions.** No build on demand. The row's value becomes the gate at the next load only,
because the gate is one fact for a whole level and the gate lines are not touched; the row
says so in the manual rather than in its caption. The notice uses the one caption the
engine already draws in play, so it fits eleven letters. The roots are refused rather than
the seventeen sites turned wide. The `INSTALL` line comes after the first join, not at the
first resolver call (above). The HD font, made once a session, stays after the row turns
the build off while *HD textures* is on (`HDFontGlyphAt` asks the draw alone); this is
accepted and written into the Engine Manual's `hd_build` row. A notice for a stale
`hd_install` override in the options, and a wide spelling of the override itself, were
left out. RICH1's `DOOR_TYPE4` animation that a tool listed with sound and flipeffect
commands was examined and nothing was changed: its record, like ten records of seven
vanilla levels (ANDY1 587, ANDY3 593, JOBY2 698, JOBY4 481 and 482, RICH1 655 and 739,
RICH3 649, TITLE 567 and 568, none of them a slot the randomizer transfers), carries a
command count of 43690 (`0xAAAA`) where the next animation's index shows it owns none; the
engine reads the count as `short`, -21846, and runs commands only for a count above 0
(`AnimateItem`), so none runs, while AnimCmd read it unsigned and walked on into the
following animations' commands. `Tr5Transfer.cpp` likewise reads a donor animation's
command count unsigned and walks it without a bound; no slot it transfers carries a
negative count. Lara's duck roll in the randomized RICH1, animations 218 to 220 (stubs in
the vanilla level), is handed over intact with its own frame data, the donor's rates, its
three sounds rebased onto RICH1's frame numbers and its chain to 222.

**Commits.** `560558da` (walks and wide names), `07e7dca2` (the code page line),
`a4473076` (the `INSTALL` line), `d646c5cc` (the HD build row), `58c3be5e` (the TR3 bank),
`7c546579` (Gold in `DATA\LA`), `e5f67a87` (the planner's test), `ba3608b5` (the
editions), `9f7bd23e` (outfit without its level), `7ef31994` (the `.hdm` cleanup),
`f89a2564` (`spoiler.txt`), `23ef8f49` (readers of a found root)

### The gamma row (#220)
2026-10-18

**What.** A slider row, *Gamma*, on the *Display* page under *Frame rate* and *VSync*,
from 0 to 100 with 50, the middle, as the default. Away from the middle every picture the
engine presents goes through one curve just before the present - the world, the menus and
the inventory over it, the loading bar, the credits, the films - in a window and in full
screen alike, and the picture under the menu follows the bar while it moves. At the middle
nothing runs and the picture is the engine's own, byte for byte. The files:
`specific/dxshell.cpp` (`DXGammaStart`, `GammaPass`, `DXGammaFinish`, `GammaRestore`,
`GammaRelease`), the new shader `hd_shader/hd_gamma.hlsl`, `specific/drawbars.cpp`,
`game/menu_frame.cpp`, `global/types.h`, `tomb5/tomb5.cpp`, and RoomProbe's `-gamma`.

**Why.** In a dark place lit only by the flare in Lara's hand something can stay
invisible, and the engine had no gamma setting, so the flare was sometimes needed where
the level means none; a gamma slider in the options menu was asked for.

**How.** The engine presents in two places. `DXShowFrame`: `S_DumpScreen` (the game frame,
the inventory, the title and pause menus), `S_DumpScreenFrame` (the loading bar outside
the HD build, the credits) and `fmv.cpp` end there. And the loading bar's held frames from
the loading thread's join to the tail, while the HD build runs: `LoadBarPresentHeld`
(`specific/drawbars.cpp`) calls the device's `Present` itself. Both presents call
`DXGammaStart` just before the device's `Present` and `DXGammaFinish` after
`HDFramePresented` has taken the clock, so the loading screen keeps the curve through the
build instead of jumping to the plain picture and back. Away from 50 `DXGammaStart` calls
`GammaPass`: the back buffer copied by `StretchRect` into a render-target texture of its
size, then drawn back over it as one pretransformed quad, half a pixel up and left so that
every pixel reads its own texel, point sampled, through `hd_gamma.hlsl`'s `GammaPS`
(`ps_2_0`, because the quad has no vertex shader and `ps_3_0` needs one). Every state it
sets - twelve render states, six sampler states, two stage states, the texture, both
shaders, the FVF or vertex declaration, stream 0 (which `DrawPrimitiveUP` empties), the
constant `c0`, the target and the viewport - is read first and set back after; no state
block, which would hold references to whatever was bound and stand in the way of a
`Reset`. The pass runs before the apostrophe screenshot, so the file is the picture as
shown. After the present `GammaRestore` copies the plain picture back into the back
buffer: the inventory and the pause menu read the last presented frame out of it
(`CreateMonoScreen`) and draw over it, and without the copy back that picture would carry
the curve once and get it a second time. `GammaRelease` goes with `DXClose` and before the
device-lost `Reset`; a size change makes a new copy. The curve, in the shader alone: gamma
= 2 ^ ((n - 50) / 50), output = input ^ (1 / gamma) per channel, so 0 is gamma 0.5 (a
channel of 0.5 sinks to 0.25) and 100 is gamma 2 (0.1 rises to 0.32); black and white stay
where they are. The pass costs about 0.03 ms for the copy and the draw and 0.015 ms for
the copy back at 2560 by 1440, under one percent of a frame at 165 Hz.

The row is the volume rows' kind, `MENU_SLIDER`, so it takes their keys and pad (held left
or right through `MenuSliderDir`), steps through `MenuSliderStep` as the mouse slider
does, and is saved with the tomb5 settings; the value lives in `tomb5.gamma`
(`global/types.h`), registry key `gamma`: 50 on a first run, 50 for a missing key and for
one above 100 (`dead_zone`'s rule), saved with the other tomb5 keys. One new `-log` line
names the value at the first present and at each change: `DXLOG gamma row=<0..100>
gamma=<g> power=<1/g> pass=<on|off>`, with `refused=<copy texture|shader|copy|draw>
hr=<0x...>` at its end once per device when a step fails; the picture is then left as it
is. RoomProbe's `-gamma` runs the engine's bytecode with `GammaPass`'s steps written again
on the probe's target, because `dxshell.cpp` is the engine's device shell and cannot be
linked there. `hd_gamma.hlsl` is not listed in `tomb5.vcxproj`'s `None` items as the other
shaders are; the build does not need it. MenuTest checks that both presents take the pass,
the start before the device's `Present` and the finish after it.

**Decisions.** A final pass over the back buffer and not a Direct3D 9 gamma ramp: a ramp
acts on a full-screen exclusive swap chain only, and this engine never makes one -
`DXCreate` (`specific/dxshell.cpp`) creates the device windowed in both of its modes (full
screen is a border-less window over the monitor at its desktop size, chosen in the port
because an exclusive device stayed lost after Alt+Tab), and Alt+Enter
(`DXToggleFullScreen`) only makes a new windowed device for the other mode - so the ramp
would do nothing in either mode; the pass works in both. The curve and its span are a free
choice: the textbook power law, the middle at 50 as the dead zone and mouse sliders hold
their neutral value, and one octave of gamma each way so that every step is the same
factor, 2 ^ (1/50); the top is enough for the dark place, which reaches a mean of 121.9 of
255 at 100 from 64.0 at 50 - as light as lit HD views at 50 (90.4 to 133.0) - and its peak
203, nowhere white. The label is the literal *Gamma*, the same word in the five languages
of the string table, so it has no `CustomText` row. The row is on *Display*, the page of
the picture's own rows, rather than among the fourteen of *Graphics*. A lookup table in
place of the power was weighed: it would make the curve exact to the step instead of
within one, and needs a second texture and a dependent read; the one step is below what
can be told apart by sight.

**Commits.** `838748f2` (the comparison base), `5b2f9649` (the row and the key),
`616ba534` (the pass), `c35a8ff6` (the tools), `73892629` (the record), `d75cafaf` (the
loading bar's held present), `b9bb34e9` (the record's second commit)

### The number beside every slider (#221)
2026-10-18

**What.** Every slider row of the options menu draws its number beside its bar: *Music
Volume* and *SFX Volume* on *Audio*, *Camera speed*, *Dead zone* and *Mouse sensitivity*
on *Controls*, *Gamma* on *Display*. The number is the row's value as the menu stores it,
0 to 100, right of the bar, in the font and colours the value rows draw their values in,
and it is drawn every frame, so it moves with the bar while a key or the pad is held. It
carries a percent sign where the screen has room for it - from about 1.46:1 on: 3:2,
16:10, 16:9 and every wider shape - in the classic font and in the HD one; on the narrower
shapes, 4:3, 5:4 and 1:1 among them, it stands without the sign. The six slider keys are
held to the sliders' span, 0 to 100, at the registry read, so that a hand-edited or stale
value can neither move the bar past its ends nor push the number past the edge, from the
first frame on. The bar, the label, the keys, the pad and the writing of the value when
the bar stops are as before. The files: `game/menu_frame.cpp/.h`, `specific/registry.cpp`,
`tomb5/tomb5.cpp`.

**Why.** The volume rows showed only the bar, and the new *Gamma* row raised the question
whether it should show its number; a number beside every slider was asked for, read as a
percentage rather than in decibels. The registry read `MusicVolume` and `SFXVolume` with
no check at all and held the four tomb5 keys only above 100, so a stray value moved the
bar and the number past their ends until the row's step clamped it, which happened only
while the cursor stood on the row. A stray volume also reached the sound as it stood: an
SFX Volume above 100 raises every sound by (v - 100) * 50 hundredths of a decibel, up to
`specific/dxsound.cpp`'s own limit of 0, and one below 0 attenuates further; a Music
Volume over 100 makes `ACMSetVolume`'s `-4000 * (100 - v) / 100` turn positive, but
`DSVolumeToLinear` turns every volume of 0 and over into 1.0, the slider's top's own
factor, so it played no louder than 100, and one below 0 played at the curve's value,
audible down to -149 where the slider's 0 is silence.

**How.** All six are `MENU_SLIDER` rows (`game/menu_frame.cpp`), and no other table holds
one; each row's number function (`MenuNumMusicVolume`, `MenuNumSfxVolume`,
`MenuNumCameraSpeed`, `MenuNumDeadZone`, `MenuNumMouseSensitivity`, `MenuNumGamma`)
returns the stored value as it is, and `DoSlider` (`specific/drawbars.cpp`) fills `pos * w
/ 100` of its bar. The volumes run 0..100 too: the game turns them into its own scales
only at the sound's door - music `-4000 * (100 - v) / 100` hundredths of a decibel with 0
silent (`ACMSetVolume`, `specific/audio.cpp`), effects `(100 - v) * 50` hundredths taken
off (`specific/dxsound.cpp`). In the slider kind's own block of `MenuFrameRun`'s draw,
after the bar and before the block's `continue`, two statements: the value the bar is
given written with `sprintf` as `"%d%%"` where `MenuSliderSignFits` is true and `"%d"`
where it is not, and `PrintString(MenuSliderNumberX(), y, colour, buf, 0)` with the value
rows' colour rule (1 on the cursor's row, 6 on the others, 3 on a greyed row);
`MenuSettleSlider`'s `MENULOG` value stays `"%d"`. Tabs and actions leave the loop before
the slider block, value and binding rows draw after its `continue`, so no other kind
reaches the number. The position: the bar is `DoSlider(400, y + 4 - (font_height >> 1),
200, 16, ...)`, x = 400 * `phd_winxmax` / 640 in floats, width `GetFixedScale(200)` (the
smaller of the width's and the height's scale against 640x480, `specific/output.cpp`), a
white frame one pixel wider on each side; `DrawColoredRect` passes those x to Direct3D 9
unshifted as pre-transformed vertices, and Direct3D 9 puts pixel centres on whole numbers
and covers a pixel when its centre lies at or right of the left edge and left of the right
one, so the first free pixel right of the frame is its edge rounded up (600.375 at 640x480
makes 600 the frame's last pixel and 601 the first free one). `MenuSliderNumberX` is
`DoSlider`'s arithmetic for the frame's right edge plus one gap of `GetFixedScale(4)`: the
integer part of 400 * `phd_winxmax` / 640, plus `GetFixedScale(200)`, plus the frame's one
pixel, plus the gap. The gap comes from the tightest layout: at 640x480 the room right of
the frame is 39 free pixels (601 to 639) and "100", the widest number of 0..100, is 31;
the 8 left over go 3 to the bar's side and 5 to the edge's. The one new include is
`specific/output.h`, for `GetFixedScale`.

The sign: `MenuSliderSignFits` is true where `MenuSliderNumberX()` plus the width of the
widest text, `"100%"` written from `MENU_SLIDER_TOP` and measured with `GetStringLength`,
plus one `GetFixedScale(4)` - the gap the number keeps after the frame - is at most
`phd_winxmax + 1`. Up to 4:3 the bar is scaled by the width and the room right of it is a
sixteenth of the screen, so "100%" (49 pixels at 640x480 against 39 of room) is short of
it at every size; wider screens scale the bar by the height, and the room on the right
grows. Both fonts hold a percent sign, and `DrawChar` (`game/text.cpp`) draws a glyph at
the same place and size in both: it shifts the classic quad's texture window onto the HD
atlas and widens quad and window by the glyph's margin, a pixel or two of nearly clear
rim, and never moves or scales the letter, so the widths are the classic table's
(`game/chardef.inc`, the sign 15 wide unscaled) in both fonts. The span:
`MENU_SLIDER_TOP`, 100, in `game/menu_frame.h`, the value of `DoSlider`'s full bar, and
the six steps name it instead of their own 100. The hold: `MenuSliderHeld(value, out)` in
the same header keeps a value inside 0..`MENU_SLIDER_TOP`, puts one outside on `out` when
that lies inside the span and on the nearer end otherwise (`MENU_SLIDER_NEAREST`); it
takes a `long`, as the two volumes are, so a negative DWORD lies under the span.
`MenuSliderHeldUlong` beside it takes the four tomb5 keys in their own `ulong`, where
every value outside lies over the span, and sends such a value through `MenuSliderHeld` as
`MENU_SLIDER_TOP + 1`, so the fallback rule stays in one place. Each of the six reads is
followed at once by the hold of its field's type: `MusicVolume`, `SFXVolume` and
`cam_speed` to the nearer end, `dead_zone`, `mouse_sens` and `gamma` to 50. Nothing is
written to the registry by it; the next save writes the held value, the volumes with
`SaveSettings`, the four others with `save_new_tomb5_settings`. The hold lives in
`game/menu_frame.h` beside the rows; `specific/registry.cpp` and `tomb5/tomb5.cpp` include
it, and MenuTest compiles it with the engine's own headers (`tomb5/pch.h` before it),
since the header needs `global/types.h`. Below 640 pixels of width, which the menu is not
laid out for (`game/menu_frame.h`), the number is not kept clear of the edge. The tests:
MenuTest's `slider_numbers`, `slider_sign_room` and `slider_reads` families, which read
the engine files as text, hold the position's arithmetic against `DoSlider`,
`DrawColoredRect`, `GetFixedScale` and the font over every width from 640 to 3840 in seven
shapes, and run the compiled holds.

**Decisions.** Left-aligned at the bar's end, as a value row's text is at its column,
rather than right-aligned to the screen's edge, so the number reads as the bar's own at
every shape of screen; at 16:9 the right edge would have stood 165 pixels from the bar at
1920x1080. One gap, scaled, rather than a gap per layout: wider layouts only gain room.
The number is the stored 0..100 for the volumes as well, rather than their decibels: the
step, the registry and the log name that number, and the two volumes' decibel scales
differ (0.4 and 0.5 a step, music's 0 silent), so the bar's number would be two units for
one kind of row. The record of the table-driven frame above says a setting's value is
"right-aligned": it is drawn in the right-hand column, left-aligned there, which is the
convention this follows. No sign below about 1.46:1 rather than any of the other ways to
make room: the number crossing the edge (13 pixels at 640x480), the bar or the number
moved (the position stays as it is, and every slider picture would change by more than the
sign), the font's small form (`FF_SMALL` takes a quarter off each advance but draws each
glyph at full size, so "100%" still covers 42 pixels against 36) or a sign out of another
font. The rule is decided per layout from the widest text and not per value, so the sign
does not come and go while the bar moves. The *Gamma* row's number is a percentage of the
slider's span, its position, 50 the middle where no pass runs - not a strength of the
curve. `dead_zone`, `mouse_sens` and `gamma` keep landing on their middle: their reads
give the reason, a hand-edited value says nothing about which end was meant; what changes
for them is that the span comes from the one definition. Each key is held in its field's
own type, so the four `ulong` keys come out exactly as their reads had them - a
`cam_speed` of 2^31 or more lies over the span and goes to 100 - and only the two `long`
volumes, which had no check at all, read a negative DWORD as under the span; the first
commit of the hold took every key as a `long` and so sent such a `cam_speed` to 0, and
`MenuSliderHeldUlong` takes that back. Commit `050e1182`'s message says a Music Volume of
150 played louder than the top; it did not, as the Why says.

**Commits.** `ef726bf7` (the number), `971d16dd` (the tests), `75ae006e` (the record),
`77d588d9` (the gap's comment), `41ee14d2` (tests read the engine's draw), `889c8ce4` (the
record's correction), `050e1182` (the span and held reads), `e03df719` (the sign),

## 2.7 First person view, cheats and the -log seams

Three things that share one property: they are switched on by the player and are off in
a default game. The first person view (#126, #134) hangs the camera in Lara's head joint
and is a row of the *View* sub-tab; the cheats are reached only while the *Cheats*
option is on; and `Log()` returns on its first line unless the game was started with
`-log`, behind which sit all the diagnostic seams the engine carries. The seams are a
permanent part of the build, not scaffolding: every feature that can fail in a way a
screenshot cannot explain has one, they are formatted only when the switch is given, and
nothing in the engine branches on them.

### The first person view
2026-09-05 - 2026-09-08

**What.** With *First person view* on, the camera sits in Lara's head joint and her body
is drawn around it. Her HD body is cut at the head and drawn one-sided for as long as the
view runs; both are per draw, since `HDModelDraw` takes a cut and a cull argument and only
her body asks for either — every other model, including her own hands, holsters, back
weapon and the lid that closes the hole, gets no cut and `HD_MODEL_CULL_NONE`, so a hand
brought up to the camera is never taken. The cut is one bone weight: every fragment whose
head weight reaches `HD_LARA_HEAD_CUT_WEIGHT` (0.15 of 1) is discarded while the view
runs, which takes the neck stump and the diving suit's helmet, both of which hang on the
torso node, without touching a chest or an arm; a level with no HD body has no cut. The
binoculars and the laser sight never reach the HD seam at all, and nothing of her is left
behind when the scope comes down. The braid is not drawn in first person while its
simulation runs on, so it hangs where it belongs on the first third-person frame.
`FirstPersonEnabled()`, which decides whether the camera runs, refuses the title level, a
flyby and a cutscene, the way `FirstPersonActive()`, which the draw asks, already did. A
setting *Body* (`tomb5.first_person_body_still`, registry `ego_body_still`, default
`animated`) offers `still`: at `still` her body is held on one stored frame while she is
standing, crouching or kneeling still on the ground — the states `AS_STOP` (which aiming
while standing keeps, so a rifle held on a target stops breathing too), `AS_POSE`,
`AS_DUCK` and `AS_ALL4S`, each only while `current_anim_state == goal_anim_state` — on the
key frame the idle began on. Not held: the head's own look angles, which are not in the
frame at all; the arms, which the weapon slot drives, so drawing, aiming, firing and
reloading are untouched and keep their blend-in time; and every state that is not in the
list, meaning every step, jump, climb, pull, roll and swim. The hold is dropped the moment
the state stops being an idle one, the animation changes underneath it, or the view leaves
first person, so a savegame, a cutscene or a death cannot leave her frozen.

**Why.** The classic path answers a camera in the head joint by leaving the head *mesh*
out, and for a classic body that is the whole of it, `LM_HEAD` being head and neck in one
piece. An HD body is a single skinned surface whose neck stump under the head is weighted
to the torso, so masking node 14 takes the head off and leaves the stump standing in the
camera — a collar of triangles 18.6 units from the eye when a wall holds the camera at the
joint, inside the near plane of 20 (`InitWindow`, `gamemain.cpp`). A bone weight is
written in the `.TRM` file, is the same number in every pose, at every angle and in every
level, and the shader already has it in hand for the skinning, where any shape carried by
the head node tilts with the head; between 0.05 and 0.35 every one of the eight wardrobe
bodies reads the same 24.5 units (25 on the Russia coat) for the widest thing taken below
the chin, which is the neck's own radius and no collar, and 0.15 is taken out of that
plateau, three times clear of the TR3 conversion's noise and the one threshold at which
the rim below is a single texture page on all eight bodies. The one-sided drawing is
needed because the HD path draws every model double sided (`D3DCULL_NONE`), which is what
the classic engine appears to do — `specific/function_table.cpp` sets `D3DCULL_NONE` for
the whole session — while TR5 in fact culls back faces in software, per polygon, through
the `IsVisible` function pointer, so the card never sees one. No camera stands inside an
object except this one, which stands inside Lara: with the camera in her neck the inside
of her own chest is the whole picture, and cutting a hole in a closed body only shows more
of it. `D3DCULL_CCW` is the mode that keeps the outside, measured and not assumed: from a
normal camera, `CCW` and `NONE` give the identical background share and the identical mean
brightness (162.1 of 255) while `CW` differs (160.1), so outside first person the culling
is a no-op, and the wardrobe's winding carries it — over the eight bodies, 25,384 to
39,440 triangles each, at most 59 have their geometric normal on the other side of the
vertex normal (0.06 % to 0.18 %). One consequence of the mirror being a true reflection
(determinant −1): in first person, and only there, the reflected draw culls the other
side, because that is the only frame where the HD path culls at all. The gate on
`FirstPersonEnabled()` is needed because `DoTitle` calls `InitialiseCamera`, which ends in
`CalculateCamera`, at a moment when `bUseSpotCam` is still 0 because the flyby is
triggered two lines later: without it one full pass of `FirstPersonCamera` ran on the
title level's Lara, moved the camera onto her head, took the field of view through
`AlterFOV` and left `fpFovSet` and `fpHeadHidden` standing with nothing to hand either
back. The still body exists because in first person the camera hangs in the head joint, so
every breath of the idle animation moves the whole picture, and it is the one thing about
the view a player cannot avoid by looking elsewhere; holding by state and not by a list of
animation numbers is necessary because which animation she idles in depends on what she is
holding and what she did last, and holding the idle's own starting key frame means the
pose really exists in the file, nothing can drift, entering the hold cannot jump because
it is the pose she was already wearing, and leaving it costs at most what the idle travels
in one cycle, on the frame she starts moving anyway.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_model.cpp` / `.h` and `hd_object.cpp` / `.h` carry the two
arguments; the cut rides in `gPass.z`, the pixel-side constant `hd_model.cpp` already
writes per pass, and the cull mode is set and put back around the model's own draw calls.
`gPass.z` is read by the model shader alone, and it is safe because `hd_model.cpp` writes
all of `c4` to the pixel constant file before every model pass, whatever a room pass left
there (the room shaders read no `z`); the register table at the top of
`hd_shader/hd_model.hlsl` names it accordingly and `hd_shader/hd_model_ps.inc` is the
compiled form. `specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp` and `hd_lara.h` decide when the body asks and
hold `HD_LARA_HEAD_CUT_WEIGHT` with its measurement. The eye's position comes from
`FirstPersonCamera` (`game/camera.cpp`), which reads the head joint with
`GetLaraJointPos(&head, LMX_HEAD)`, lifts it 16 units and asks `mgLOS` whether it may go
`FP_EYE_OFFSET` = 48 units forward — 48 in the open, 0 with a wall, ledge or doorway in
front; `FirstPersonEnabled()` is in the same file. The binoculars: `BinocularCamera`
(`game/camera.cpp`) sets `lara_item->mesh_bits = 0` for the scope and the laser sight
both, `game/draw.cpp` asks `if (lara_item->mesh_bits && !SCNoDrawLara)` before it calls
`DrawLara` at all, and leaving the scope puts `mesh_bits` back to −1 in the same function;
the scope's mask lies above the HD world by the drawing order, since `HDFrameDraw()` runs
immediately before `DrawBuckets` and the depth clear that separates the world from mask,
pickup display and fade (#127) comes after all of it, while `AlterFOV` moves `f_persp`
inside the frame during the zoom, which is why the projection is taken when the world is
collected (`HDFrameCaptureProjection`) and not when it is drawn. The black frame on
zooming out was a vanilla inheritance: the depth buffer was cleared only in mid-frame, so
the binocular mask's depth values stood until the next frame and the world was tested
against them. `S_InitialisePolyList` (`specific/output.cpp`) now clears depth together
with the colour at the top of every frame, and `DXSaveScreen` (`specific/dxshell.cpp`),
which read the D3D9 back buffer as 16-bit and started one row past its end, writes a
correct 24-bit TGA (`a3fcb87`). `HairControl` is called from `game/control.cpp`, in the
game loop and not from `DrawLara`, which is also how the classic path skips `DrawHair`
(`specific/drawlara.cpp`). `LaraBodyStillFrame` in `game/delstuff.cpp` puts the held frame
in both key frame slots with the factor 0 beside it, so both draw paths wear it — the
classic first person path draws her body too, leaving out only the head mesh — and so that
the interpolated branch stays reachable; a blend of a pose with itself is that pose, and
`frac` is lifted to 1 only on a frame that had no pair of its own, while
`GLaraShadowframe` takes the held frame's own bounds. The option field is
`first_person_body_still` in `global/types.h`, its default and its stored value
`ego_body_still` in `tomb5/tomb5.cpp`, and its row is the last of the *View* page,
directly under *Camera damping* (`game/menu_frame.cpp`); it needs `tomb5.first_person` as
well, and it is the one change of this view that alters the picture at thirty hertz too.
Seams with `-log`: `HDLOG firstperson on|off headcut=0.15` once on the edge, `HDLOG
headcut cut=1 w=0.15 node=14 head=.. torso=.. min=..@node.. lid=1` once a second, `HDLOG
binoculars lara_pushed=N mesh_bits=N` one frame after the scope comes up when the frame it
describes was wholly inside the binocular view, and `HDLOG binoculars off` when it goes
down. `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp` `-firstperson` puts the camera where
`FirstPersonCamera` puts the eye (head joint, 16 up, `-fpforward` units in front, default
48) looking along +z with `-pitch` as the look-down angle, and `-nearcut`, `-cull` and
`-neck` switch the halves and print the stump table. `docs/Engine-Manual.md` describes the
view.

**Commits.** `a3fcb87` (the screenshot's TGA), `1605750`, `73819d5`, `c021cf6`

### The cheats: DOZY as a toggle, and five bindable hotkeys
2026-08-23 - 2026-09-20

**What.** The DOZY key combination reacts to the rising edge and switches flight off again
if it is already on; the Walk-key exit inside `LaraCheat` stays, and both exits share one
function, `LaraCheatEnd`, which also sets `current_anim_state` and `goal_anim_state`. The
typed DOZY chord works under the Modern key table. Five cheat roles are bindable on the
keyboard (slots 29-33, defaults F2 fly mode, F7 all weapons, F8 all items, F11 heal, F1
skip level) and on the pad (roles 23-27, unbound by default); they are offered on the *Key
bindings* page and can fire only while the *Cheats* option is on, only with a living Lara
in a level — not on the title screen, not in a cutscene, not dead — and each on its own
press edge. BITS has no role. The five typed cheat words are unchanged and still fire
every tick their letters are held.

**Why.** Vanilla had only a way in; the only way out was the Walk key, which nobody
discovers unaided and which leaves a player stuck in flight, and upstream also left the
two animation states on the swim-cheat state for one frame. Under the Modern key table the
step-left key is Z, one of DOZY's four letters, and it also carries `IN_WALK` while
`IN_LOOK` is stripped; `LaraCheat`'s exit reads `IN_WALK && !IN_LOOK`, so the chord's own
switch and its own exit fired in the same tick and she rose 128 units and fell straight
back out of `LW_FLYCHEAT` before a frame was drawn. A role that cannot fire must not claim
a key: with *Cheats* off the five rows are not offered and nothing reads them, so counting
their keys in the conflict table would have silenced another role's default-key fallback
in favour of a binding that can do nothing.

**How.** All of the cheat logic is in `game/laramisc.cpp`. `LaraCheatLetterDown()` makes
the exit ignore the walk key while any of the four DOZY letters is still physically down;
the walk key and the other three original exits are untouched, so a Tank player holding
walk and a cheat letter at once also keeps flying. `LaraCheatFlyToggle()` is shared by the
chord and the fly hotkey; the other four hotkeys call exactly what GUNS, ITEM, HEAL and
SKIP already do from the inventory ring, reached from `LaraControl`. The roles are
`KEY_ROLE_CHEAT_FLY`..`KEY_ROLE_CHEAT_SKIP` (`game/key_scheme.h`) and
`JOY_ROLE_CHEAT_FLY`..`JOY_ROLE_CHEAT_SKIP` (`game/pad_scheme.h`), read through
`specific/input.cpp`; `KeySchemeConflicts` takes a `cheats` argument so the five slots are
inert exactly as *Secondary* is under *One key*, and the *Cheats* row in
`game/menu_frame.cpp` recomputes the table like every other row that makes a role live or
inert. The default keys are the free F keys: F4 belongs to the outfit changer
(`specific/hd/hd_outfitmenu.cpp`), F10 to `IN_E` and F12 to `specific/output.cpp`,
F5/F6/F9 to save and load, and F3 is left unassigned because Core's own level skip in the
`_DEBUG` branch of `LaraCheatyBits` uses it, which no release build contains. Seam behind
`-log`: `CHEATLOG f=%ld what=<fly_on|fly_off|weapons|items|heal|skip> src=<word|hotkey>`,
for every cheat that fires including the typed words. `docs/Engine-Manual.md` lists the
roles.

**Commits.** `6e9bb3b`, `608a292`, `e509535`, `32d9a95`

### The -log switch and the diagnostic seams
2026-08-25 - 2026-09-21

**What.** `Log()` is compiled in and returns on its first line unless the game was started
with `-log`: without the switch nothing is opened, nothing is formatted and no `log.txt`
appears. Behind the switch sit the engine's diagnostic seams, printed on a change or
throttled per item and per 30 frames rather than per frame wherever a one-tick pulse would
otherwise be buried: `SFXLOG` (which sample a sound really played, and which anim command
asked for it), `CLIPLOG`, `SKIPLOG`, `MESHLOG`, `SLOTLOG` and `CLIPDETAIL` (why an enemy
is not drawn — bounds check, status branch, slot allocation or mesh discard); `FPSLOG`,
which writes one line per second of wall clock — frames presented, shortest, longest and
average gap, how many gaps missed the budget, and the heaviest HD room, object and
draw-call counts of that second — plus one summary per level; the HD seams `HDLOG
firstperson`, `HDLOG headcut` (the cut's threshold and node, the distance from the lens to
the head joint, to the torso joint and to the nearest of all fifteen, in view space, with
the lid's presence), `HDLOG creaturelight` (up to six intelligent items a second with the
classic and the HD colour side by side, their difference, the distance to the lens, the
ambient and the light counts), `HDLOG clip` with `items_spared=`, `view=` and `view_obj=`,
and `HDLOG frame` with `clipped=` lights; `INTERPLOG` with `camcut=` (which cut rule
fired), `pose_far=`, `pose_hd=`, `stretch=` (the node, animation and frame of the worst
bone of the second) and `arms=<blended>/<refused>/<tween frames>`; `MODERNLOG` with its
`init`, `pad` and per-tick lines and a separate `mode=tank` line; `MENULOG enter` and
`MENULOG set`; `COMBATLOG`, `MODELOG` and `CHEATLOG`. The engine build script compiles the
whole engine on every run.

**Why.** Upstream compiled `Log()` out entirely, so a player who ran into something could
never produce a log; the only way was a special build. The switch is read by hand as the
first thing `WinMain` does rather than through the `commandlines` table, because the run
check and the gameflow load have already logged by the time that table is worked off, and
those startup lines are the ones a diagnosis needs most; it is matched as a whole word, so
a stray "log" inside a path cannot silently turn on per-frame logging. A picture cannot
answer how far the cut plane stands from the lens, whether an HD creature is darker than a
classic one, whether all rooms and objects of one frame were collected with one camera,
which frame of an animation stretched a bone, or which half of an input seam answered; a
counter can. The frame rate has to be counted where the player actually sees a frame,
including the wait and the driver time: `DXShowFrame` is the engine's only present — the
game frame, the inventory and the title menu through `S_DumpScreen`, the loading bar and
the credits through `S_DumpScreenFrame`, and the movies in `fmv.cpp` all end there — so
one call counts every frame exactly once, where counting inside `S_OutputPolyList` would
miss the loading bar and the movies and counting in the main loop would count message
pumps that drew nothing. Two counters and not one, because the logic is a fixed 30 Hz
built on a 60 Hz tick: `slow` is every gap over the 33.3 ms budget, which half a healthy
second reaches on jitter alone, and `late` is every gap over 41.7 ms, which jitter cannot
reach because a missed slot costs a whole tick. `MODERNLOG`'s derived rate is printed
beside the setting it came from, so a log can tell "the slider is wrong" from "the mapping
came out wrong", the live `modern_cfg` rates being read back rather than restated so a
hand edit of the registry shows up too; `dead_l=` and `dead_r=` print the one zone
actually in force this session, chosen by `joystick_is_xinput`; the `pad` line exists
because a dead zone sized from a claim rather than a measurement can only be corrected by
a log that says where the pad really rests; the tank line is separate because the bypass
runs instead of `ModernUpdateInput`, so that function's line cannot describe it;
`aim_strafe=` prints 0 and `mode=aim` therefore cannot appear in a default log, the field
and the enum value staying so the absence is not read as a dropped field; and `MENULOG`'s
`row=` is always the English label even in a German menu. `COMBATLOG`'s `draw` field is
the bit that actually leaves `S_UpdateInput`, and `seam` says which half answered, because
printing the weapon half's produced bit alone read as the opposite of what happened
whenever the seam was off while the key's own `IN_DRAW` was still in the word. The build
stamp: `winmain.cpp` writes the first line of every `-log` run, `PCtomb5 built <__DATE__
__TIME__>`, and those macros are fixed when that one file is compiled, so an incremental
build that touched a shader or a file in `specific\hd` left yesterday's stamp on today's
binary and a log could name a build that never ran; `setupdlg.cpp` carries the same
`__DATE__` in the launcher's window. An incremental build can do worse: `msbuild` goes by
file dates, so a source file put back with a date older than its object file is passed
over although its content is new, and the link joins object files of two states of one
header - a binary that compiles, links and dies at the end of the level build, where
`HDRenderGlossLevel` had grown by 28 bytes in the object file that fills it and not in the
one that holds it on its stack.

**How.** `specific/function_stubs.cpp` and `.h` hold `Log()` and `gLogEnabled`;
`specific/winmain.cpp` reads the switch and writes the stamp. A seam that has to build
something before it can log — walking a list, formatting a name — tests `gLogEnabled`
itself at the call site, because the gate inside `Log()` only saves the writing, not the
preparing. The seams live in `game/draw.cpp`, `game/lot.cpp`, `game/sound.cpp` / `.h`,
`specific/output.cpp`, `specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp` (`HDLOG headcut`),
`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp` (`HDLOG creaturelight`), `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp` / `.h`
(`HDLOG clip`, `HDLOG frame` and the frame counting), `game/interpolate.cpp`
(`INTERPLOG`), `game/modern_state.cpp` (`MODERNLOG init` and tick lines),
`specific/input.cpp` (`MODERNLOG pad`, the `mode=tank` line, `COMBATLOG` and `MODELOG`),
`game/menu_frame.cpp` (`MENULOG`, through `MenuAfterChange`), `game/laramisc.cpp`
(`CHEATLOG`) and `specific/hqsfx.cpp`, whose eleven lines are formatted only inside `if
(gLogEnabled)`. Every camera number `MODERNLOG` prints comes through `game/camera.cpp` /
`.h`, whose `ModernCameraLogState` and `ModernCameraLogConfig` were widened rather than
given accessors of their own; `view_err=` is abs(`cam` - `cam_world`) wrapped the short
way, in the same raw units `cam`, `cam_world`, `err` and `yawd` share, and the camera
fields read one tick behind because the line runs before `CalculateCamera`. The frame
counter is one line in `specific/dxshell.cpp`, in `DXShowFrame` directly after
`IDirect3DDevice9::Present`, calling `HDFramePresented`; without `-log` its first line
returns, no clock is read, no counter stepped and nothing allocated. The per-level summary
is flushed at the top of `HDLevelBuild` for the level before and in `HDLevelDeviceLost`,
so the level the player quits from gets one too, both on the main thread after the load
thread has joined. The build: `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/be.bat` calls `msbuild` with
`/t:Rebuild`, so every object file - `winmain.obj` and `setupdlg.obj` with the stamp among
them - is of the build's own source state; the full build takes about half a minute. The
diagnostic tools that carry these measurements — `InterpTest`, `ModelProbe`, `AnimMap`,
`ModernTest` and `MenuTest` — are listed in `Preparation/Tools/README.md`, with
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/InterpTest.cpp` and
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/ModelProbe.cpp` in the tree; `docs/Engine-Manual.md` carries
the field tables.

**Commits.** `43f9a07`, `eb57719`, `a250791`, `73819d5`, `e6debb7`, `c021cf6`, `89b2ae3`,
`6b0405a`, `41fe965`, `e491c0d`, `079c7b8`, `f70c40e`, `4220e49`, `fb93f02`, `608a292`,
`96e9fd7`, `ec32365`, `f4b43e4`

## 2.8 What the push audit corrected

Before the repository was made public it was walked once against the licence and against
its own statements. The result is this: every file the project modified carries the
GPLv3 section 5(a) modification notice, every origin sentence in the code names the
lawful source the code really rests on - TRForge's MIT format description, TROne's GPLv3
code with its file and function, or a measurement made here on the player's own data
files - and a fresh clone builds on a Windows checkout. Nothing in the tree opens, maps,
links, parses or disassembles a program of the Tomb Raider IV-VI Remaster;
`hd_install.cpp` tests that `tomb456.exe` or `tomb123.exe` exists and nothing more. Four
rules of the HD path and two prose passages of the vendored `Trg.h` that rested on no
count of this project's were measured on the player's own files or declared this
project's choice (section 2.4, the entry "Where the HD rules come from").

### Licence notices, origin sentences and the corrections made before the public push
2026-09-21 - 2026-09-22

**What.** Seven engine files changed long before and never marked — `game/draw.h`,
`game/tomb4fx.cpp`, `game/rope.cpp`, `game/sphere.cpp`, `game/deathsld.cpp`,
`game/flmtorch.cpp`, `specific/polyinsert.h` — carry the modification notice; the twelve
diagnostic tools that still lacked one and `Preparation/Tools/EmbedData.ps1` carry theirs,
so all eighteen tools under `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose` now have one; the randomizer's
`TR5Randomizer/src/core/Tr5Tr3Import.cpp` carries the project header, the last source file

**Why.** GPLv3 section 5(a) requires every modified file to carry a prominent notice of
the change. An origin sentence that names the wrong source is a licence claim that cannot
be honoured: every rule in the engine is to rest on TRForge's MIT format description, on
TROne's own GPLv3 code with its file and function, or on a measurement made here on the
player's own data files, and the sentences are to say so. Three of the four rules named in
