from" (2.4) measured them on this project's own data or declared them a free choice - the
room light, the u, v and normal bytes, material 16's order: they had stood as prose with

already. A byte-hashing shader guard fires falsely when git rewrites line endings on
checkout, which breaks the build from a clean clone. A diagnostic seam that formats its
lines without testing `-log` costs work on every level load for output nobody reads. A
checkbox that promises a feature the program does not have misleads the player, and a
hard-coded German string cannot be translated. `RANDO_BUILD_ID` distinguishes builds whose
output can differ: four commits since Beta 1.0 change where an enemy may stand, so 18

## 2.9 The cleanup before the public push

The record and the project's own comments were rewritten to state facts: the record was
condensed from a diary into a licence document (`a8b038e`), and every comment this project
had added or changed was rewritten to say what, why and what for instead of narrating the
work. The
entries of this section record what that pass changed in the text of the code; the origin
facts already in place - TRForge (MIT), TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931, tomb3 (Troye's
decompilation of Tomb Raider III) and the measurements made here on the player's own
files - stand as before.

### Comments in the engine, the randomizer and the tools say what, why and what for
2026-09-22 - 2026-09-23

**What.** Every comment this project added or changed in the engine, the randomizer and
the tools now states what the code does, why, and what it is for. Task numbers, round and
stage names, dates and narration of the work are gone. Facts measured here, failure modes
and origin sentences (TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931,
TRForge, tomb3 by Troye, or a measurement made here) stand as facts, all but the one over
material 16's slot order (`hd_render.cpp`, `MaterialRipple`), whose note keeps that the
order is the one TROne's prose names, that it is unproven, and that this project's
measurement cannot decide between `param[0]` and `param[2]`; since #212 the ripple reads
neither number. Nothing changed about what the code does. Line numbers that pointed into
another file of this project were dropped; file and function names stayed.

**Why.** The same reader GPLv3 section 5(a) and the record itself serve needs what a
comment states now, not the round, the stage or the question that produced it.

**How.** Files were rewritten in batches by folder - `game`, `specific`, `specific/hd`,
`specific/hd/hd_shader`, `tomb5` and the global headers, `TR5Randomizer/src`,
`Preparation/Tools` - each batch checked before its commit by a script that strips
comments and collapses whitespace from the old and the new version of every file and finds
the rest identical: line endings, high bytes, the modification notice and every upstream
comment of Core's and Troye's stayed untouched. After the batches the engine and the tools
were rebuilt, the three test suites (ModernTest, MenuTest, InterpTest) were run, and the
corrections in `aa3568a` and `5d17c45` followed. In all 272 distinct files changed: 165
under `TOMB5 Code`, 39 under `TR5Randomizer/src`, 68 under `Preparation/Tools`.

**Commits.** `aa3568a`, `5d17c45` (the corrections after rebuilding), `ec9a248`,
`8bbfa1b`, `888f154`, `0c40f3a`, `728ab29`, `3965ee7`, `166f62d`, `ba2701d`, `5b14893`,
`87fd3e7`, `91289b2`

### The water art's ripple from the project's own data, and the origin sentences (#212)
2026-10-17

**What.** The ripple of the still water art read from the player's Remaster files
(material 16, the pixel constant `c36`) reads none of the `.TRG` part's numbers any more.
Its scale, travel and rate come from the water the part lies over: the body whose squares
in the part's own room lie under the part's box within 32 units of its height - the body's
class as drawn, its squares and its row's `waves` - or, for a part over no body, the
squares its own up-facing triangles cover (never more than its box spans) and the class
the data rule (`WaterClassOf`) gives them with its room's open air and no sink.
`HDArtRipple` (`hd_splash_math.h`) turns that into the three numbers: the length a fifth
of the water's width (the square root of its squares) and never under its class's longest
wave row; the rate the deep-water rate at that length, `calm * sqrt(g k)`, at 0.35 of the
class's calm; the travel a tenth of the part's own smaller UV span at the sea row's
steepness (height over wavelength), a basin's 0.30 and a channel's 0.28 of that, times the
row's `waves` and never more than a tenth. Every part now ripples, the soup pots of
JOBY5's kitchen among them, which stood still under the old reading's zeroes; most small
waters ripple slower and finer than under the old reading, JOBY3's kitchen pots slower and
wider, ANDY2's two water rooms finer and faster, JOBY5's seas longer and slower, and
JOBY4's sea as before. A `WATERLOG level=... art` line per part names the body, the class,
the squares, the length, the period and the travel; `TrgProbe -mat 16` prints the file's
four numbers as facts of the file, as before. Beside it the public text states the origins
in this project's own words: the origin ledger's header in `THIRD-PARTY.md` lists every
rule of the HD path with its origin and defines its classes as the entries use them - OWN
this project's design, THIRD TROne's or TRForge's, credited - and the entries that cite
TROne's design are THIRD; the modern control is described as what it is, the design of
TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931 reworked here almost
throughout, its numbers with this project's own reasons.

**Why.** Which of material 16's first and third numbers is the scale and which the rate
was a free choice with no measurement of this project's behind it, so the art takes its
ripple from this project's own water data instead. The origin sentences of
`THIRD-PARTY.md`, `vendor/trforge/VERSION.txt` and this record are to state each rule's
origin and class and nothing else; the fact of every modification stays, two prose
passages of `Trg.h` are no longer relied on, and each rule is re-counted here or declared
a free choice. The ledger's header had defined OWN as TROne's design and the scope as what
came by way of TROne or TRForge, while the later entries used OWN for this project's
design and THIRD for TROne's. The modern control's comments, tests, record and manual
named another product as its model and as the source of its turn rate, its camera's
return, its orbit rate and the mouse row's defaults; the control is a mix of TROne's base
and this project's reworking, almost everything re-tuned.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`: `HDWaterArt` and `WaterArtOf` (the part's span, box,
own squares and the ripple it has until the bodies are known; RoomProbe without `-hdwater`
builds no body and keeps that one); `HDRange::ripplePart` and the triangle's in the sort
key and the join - every draw call without water first, then the parts, the later part of
a group first, so the draw calls and the vertices the groups' light samples take
(`group_light`) stay what they were (JOBY5's room 49 holds the game's only two parts on
one page and in one pass); `ArtRippleClass`, `ArtRippleOf` and `water_art_ripples`, called
in `HDRenderSetWaterSheets` once the bodies stand (also with `tomb5.hd_water` 0, which
builds the bodies and no sheet); `HDRenderWaterArtLine`, printed by `hd_level.cpp` behind
`-log` and by RoomProbe `-hdwater`. `specific/hd/hd_splash_math.h`: `HDArtRipple`. The
shader and its slots are unchanged; a water part's pixels take the same branch as before,
only with other constants, and the shader's ripple note says the three numbers come from
the water the part lies over (`63b3d921`, `833a1c4b`). ModernTest gains `art_ripple`. The
words: `THIRD-PARTY.md` (the ledger's header and the classes of its entries, the TRForge
paragraph, the water block, entry 248 new), `vendor/trforge/VERSION.txt`, this record (the
HD path's opening, the water entry's ripple paragraph, "Where the HD rules come from",
section 2.6's opening and Why, the mouse entry's Why and Decisions, sections 2.8 and 2.9),
`game/modern_move.h`, `modern_move.cpp`, `modern_state.cpp`, `modern_camera.h`,
`modern_camera.cpp`, `key_scheme.h`, the comments and strings of ModernTest and MenuTest
(TROne's back-input test is cited by what it tests), and `docs/Engine-Manual.md`.

**Decisions.** The art takes its ripple from this project's own data, and the file's
numbers are not read. The body's size sets the length, because over the whole game the
file's tuples grew with the area of the water, and a fifth of the width with the class's
longest row as the floor stays within one per cent of the length of JOBY4's sea (12,182
units against the file's 12,288), the one place where the art's ripple had been accepted
as seen in play; the rate is the deep-water law the sheets use, at 0.35 of the class's
calm so that the same sea keeps its twelve seconds. The part's UV span bounds the travel
and does not set the scale: the parts' maps onto their pages are not planar (JOBY5's small
basins lay 48 texels over 944 units along x and over 3,826 along z), so no length on the
page stands for a length in the room. A part over no body takes the class its own squares
and its room's open air give it and not the nearest body's: the nearest body to JOBY4's
sea is a basin of two squares 16,000 units under it. The sort keeps the draw calls and the
light samples as they were, so nothing but the ripple changes; the build's fingerprint
(`HDRenderBuildHash`) changes in the water levels with the ripple's numbers.

**Commits.** `8a599fd9` (the comparison base), `63b3d921`, `833a1c4b` (the shader's ripple
note), `4e5e3389`, `2a31aa7b`, `24564ec0`, `2157aab0`, `7aff6d3a`

### The build from a stranger's checkout (#213)
2026-10-17

**What.** A checkout made with other settings than this project's own machine builds the
same way. The batch files check out with CRLF on every machine, the shader guard checks
all 36 `.inc` and the three shaders that include another `.hlsl`, `bshader.bat` writes its
`.inc` with line feeds, the documents name the v142 toolset and the Windows SDK's
`fxc.exe`, the project files list every header and shader of the engine, and ModernTest
and MenuTest find the engine sources they count from whatever folder they are started in.

**Why.** The 51 `.bat` files had no line-ending rule, so a checkout with
`core.autocrlf=false` or `input`, or a ZIP from GitHub, wrote them with bare line feeds,
and cmd then missed labels - `be.bat` reported `:onestamp` missing and skipped the guard,
`bshader.bat` wrote six wrong stamps. The guard compared 33 of 36 stamps and no include
stamp for the water look and the shadow caster. `tomb5.vcxproj` pins `PlatformToolset`
v142 while the documents named only the C++ workload, and `bshader.bat` needs `fxc.exe`,
not `vcvars`. Sixteen headers and seven `.hlsl` were missing from the project files. The
two suites read sources relative to the working directory and reported false failures when
started elsewhere.

**How.** `.gitattributes`: `*.bat text eol=crlf` and `*.cmd text eol=crlf`; a "text" file
is stored with line feeds, which the 51 files already were, so `git add --renormalize`
changed nothing in the index, and the working-tree bytes stayed the same. `be.bat`, both
guard blocks: `:onestamp` for `hd_water_look_vs.inc`, `hd_water_look_ps.inc` and
`hd_wet_marble_ps.inc`, `:incstamp hd_room` for the two water look `.inc` and `:incstamp
hd_model` for the two `hd_shadow_cast_*.inc`. `bshader.bat`: the matching `:incstamp`
calls before each `:stamp`, and a PowerShell pass after the stamps that rewrites the 36
`.inc` with line feeds (fxc and `echo` write CRLF); four `.inc` gained their `//
bshader-include` line and nothing else. `README.md` (Building) and `docs/Engine-Manual.md`
(Building the engine): one sentence on the toolset, "MSVC v142 - VS 2019 C++ x64/x86 build
tools". `Preparation/Tools/README.md`: the `fxc.exe` sentence in Building, the include
stamps in the guard paragraph, one sentence each in the ModernTest and MenuTest rows.
`tomb5.vcxproj` and `.filters`: 16 `ClInclude` and 7 `None` items, BOM and CRLF kept, so
every tracked `.h` under `TOMB5 Code/TOMB5` and every `.hlsl` is in both project files,
except the vendored zlib's internal headers, which the project never listed.
`ModernTest.cpp` and `MenuTest.cpp`: `tree_open()` opens a tree file by its path from the
EXE's own folder (`_get_pgmptr`), then from the working directory.

**Commits.** `402b671`, `e98d954`, `7575bd8`, `df9302b`, `b17c1a8`, `739f60f`

## 2.10 Rounds after the cleanup (2026-10-16 to 2026-10-27)

The rounds that followed the cleanup of section 2.9, each one change to the engine with
its reason, recorded in the same form as the entries above.

### The speaking heads of the cutscenes on the HD path (#215)
2026-10-17

**What.** In HD, Lara's face speaks her cutscene lines again when a mod supplies the face.
A mod's face whose own folder holds no track file of it speaks the track files of the
install's face of the same name, out of game 5's `ITEM`, when the two `.TRM` carry the
same rig and the same joint block header bit for bit; the mod's own vertices, bones and
weights take the deform, so its geometry speaks. A mod that ships track files of its own
keeps them; an install's face and a Tomb Raider III guest's are not touched. `CutseqProbe
-actors` lists every cutscene's audio track and actor slots. The files:
`specific/hd/hd_trl.cpp/.h`, `specific/hd/hd_model.cpp`,
`Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/CutseqProbe.cpp`, LipsTest.

**Why.** In play, the speaking heads were gone from the cutscenes, noticed on Lara in
ANDREA2, where they had worked before, at 60 frames a second too. With `-log`, ANDREA2's
cutscene 8 drove `LARSON`'s lips alone, Lara's face wrote only the blinks of the loop
between her lines, and at every level build her face's lips line read `slot=23042
face=LARA_HEAD file=- ... reason=no file` while the `MODLOG` line for `LARA_HEAD` said
that `LARA_HEAD.TRM` came from a mod. The chain: an installed mod ships a
`4\ITEM\LARA_HEAD.TRM` of its own; `find_model` (`hd_model.cpp`) asks the active mods
before the installs, a rule since the Mods folder (#153), so her face is the mod's;
`make_lips` looked for a mod face's track files only in the mod's own folder (the rule of
#163, since a mod's rig need not be the install's), and the mod's `4\ITEM` holds no
`LARA_HEAD_*.TRL`; in a cutscene Lara acts in, the Lara draw hands the cut's track to
`choose_face` (`hd_laradraw.cpp`), `HDModelLipsOpen` finds no clip and the face keeps the
loop. No commit lost the heads: `make_lips`, the cut block of the Lara draw and the cut
branch of `choose_face` are unchanged since `d9b7bb2`, `4e540c7` and `11026db`, and a
cutscene is drawn on its integer frame, without a tween, so the frame rate does not enter.
The mod's `LARA_HEAD.TRM` against the install's, both read with `HDTrmLoad`: 5916 vertices
against 5913, and the same bytes for the rig (33 joints and their inverse binds), the
block's nodes and parents (55), its columns and column map (40), its frame 0 and the whole
block (508 frames at 2264, loop 499). Over the install's faces, `LARA_YOUNG_HEAD` (12740
vertices) and `LARA_CREEPY_HEAD` (5409, its block at 2260) carry `LARA_HEAD`'s rig and
header bit for bit; `LARSON_HEAD` and `PIERRE_HEAD` (41 joints) do not.

**How.** `HDLipsSameRig` (`specific/hd/hd_trl.cpp`, declared in `hd_trl.h`) is true when
the joint count and every inverse bind matrix, the block's node count and parents, its
column count and the joint each column drives, and its frame 0 are the same bytes -
everything a track file's frame is read against (`HDLipsMapBuild`, `HDLipsSkins`); bytes
rather than floats, so a NaN or a signed zero counts as itself. `HDLipsTrackFiles` lists a
face's `<STEM>_<digits>.TRL` in a folder, the rule `lips_files` used and now calls.
`HDLipsModRig` takes a mod's face, whether its own folder holds track files and the
install's face of the same name; without own files it reads that face once with
`HDTrmLoad`, and where `HDLipsSameRig` holds, it answers `install` with game 5's `ITEM` as
the folder, else `differs`, `none` or `own` with the face's own folder (`HDLipsRigName`
gives the word). `make_lips` (`hd_model.cpp`), for a face of `HD_MODEL_ORIGIN_MOD`, finds
the install's face (`find_model` with `kModsNone`) only when its own folder holds no track
file, calls `HDLipsModRig` and keeps the outcome in `Lips::rig`. The choice lives in
`hd_trl.cpp` so that LipsTest, which builds that file beside itself, runs it (its section
9). Nothing else of the face changes: its map, its loop, its blinks and its deform are its
own file's. With `-log` the level build's lips lines of a mod's face end in ` rig=own`, `
rig=install`, ` rig=differs` or ` rig=none` (no install face of that name); every other
lips line is as it was. A mod's face without its own tracks costs one more `.TRM` read at
level build. `CutseqProbe -actors [n]` prints, for every cutscene of `data\cutseq.bin` or
for cutscene n, its frame count, its audio track and each actor's `actor_data[i].objslot`
and node count, the file's own slots before `stealth3_start` puts a guard's slot on actor
1 of the four stealth3 cutscenes. `docs/Engine-Manual.md` (the lips row of the log table)
and `Preparation/Tools/README.md` (the `CutseqProbe` and `LipsTest` rows) say the same.

**Decisions.** The install's tracks go to a mod's face only on a rig that is the same bit
for bit, never on a near one, because a track frame is read against exactly those bytes; a
mod's face on another rig keeps no lips (`rig=differs`). A mod's own track files win over
the install's. The randomizer and the binder stay as they are: in a randomized JOBY5,
`-log` showed cutscene 32 binding slots 58, 48 and 62 to names of other levels' objects,
but those slots hold the classic level's moveable records and meshes byte for byte and
JOBY5's own `.MAP` binds them as in the classic level (58 is Sergie, whose face speaks
track 120, 48 and 62 one-node props of the cutscene), the cross mix having written the
slots just below them, 47, 57 and 61; no actor the camera sees carries a foreign model. No
tool lists which cutscenes a level plays - a cutscene starts from the level's script
(`gfCutNumber`), from a floor trigger, from a pickup whose OCB is above 1024 (the cutscene
is the OCB minus 1024) and from fixed numbers in the code - so the actor slots the
randomizer changes in an existing slot rest on a mapping by hand: ANDY1's 89 (the imp of
cutscenes 9 and 10), whose vertex positions stay the classic ones, and JOBY5's 37
(`BLUE_GUARD`, the two guards of cutscene 15), which the cross mix fills with RICH1's
guard; HD binds `BLUE_GUARD.TRM` to slot 37 by name, so the HD cutscene is unchanged, and
with HD off the cutscene draws RICH1's guard there, which stays as it is.

**Commits.** `d9b7bb2`, `4e540c7`, `11026db` (the lips lines, unchanged since), `baba72b`
(the base, same answers), `a24dd9b`, `4f4b65a`, `b74f1fd`, `c447876`, `bfbd25b`,
`c62187f`, `454ecc4`, `2bd3f8e`, `3439980` (draw changes, not the cause), `58eff46`,
`4096e48`, `3de1661` (the track folder's choice), `12ce564d` (tools find `cutseq.bin`)

### The far plane (#217)
2026-10-18

**What.** The far plane moves from twenty sectors (20,480 units) to forty-one (41,984),
for the HD path and the classic draw alike: an object, a static the art leaves to the
classic path, and the sprites and effects cut at the plane (debris, shockwaves, splashes,
shadows, footprints, rain, sprite sparks) are now drawn between the two distances; the
sparks, fire, smoke, blood, drips and bubbles with a cut of their own at 20,480 keep it.
The rooms' faces were never cut by the plane, in either path, and are drawn as before. The
depth curve, the rain's tint, the circle of the fog bulbs and the count of an object's box
corners stay on the plane the game shipped with (`ZFAR_SHIPPED`), so that everything
nearer than 20,480 units is drawn as it was. The number and its reason are one constant,
`ZFAR_SECTORS` in the new `specific/zrange_math.h`, which the engine, ModernTest and
RoomProbe include. RoomProbe gains `-zfar`, `-farcull`, `-farsurvey` and `-farobjects`.

**Why.** In play, the closed double door at the end of JOBY2's corridor (items 128 and 129
of room 106), seen from up to about 34 sectors away, was not drawn while the art of the
room behind the doorway was: `S_GetObjectBounds` (`specific/output.cpp`) returns 0 for an
object whose origin lies at or past `f_mzfar` unless the frame lists an outside room. A
longer view distance was asked for, in HD and SD.

**How.** What moves to the new plane: `GameMain` (`gamemain.cpp`) and `WinProcessCommands`
(`winmain.cpp`, after a display mode change) call `InitWindow` with `ZNEAR_UNITS` and
`ZFAR_UNITS`; `InitWindow` sets `phd_zfar` (shifted by 14), `f_zfar` and `f_mzfar` from
it; the cull of `S_GetObjectBounds` in an inside frame; the clip flag 256 and the `f_zfar`
sort key of an effect vertex past `f_mzfar` (`setXYZ3`, `setXYZ4` in `specificfx.cpp`:
debris, shockwaves, splashes, shadows, footprints), the same in `ClipCheckPoint` and
`DrawSkySegment` for the classic sky's layers (never reached, the layers' corners lie
within 15,458 units of the eye); a rain drop's cut in `DoRain`; the switch-off of a sprite
spark in `S_DrawDrawSparksNEW`; `DrawEffect`'s test against `phd_zfar` (`draw.cpp`); and
`aTransformClip_D3DV` (`alexstuff.cpp`), which has no caller. What derives from it: the
classic horizon of `phd_PutPolygonsSkyMesh`, drawn at the plane's rhw before the world
without depth writes (sz 0.99550, the pixels the same), the stars of `DrawStars` in the
sky's phase, and `DelDrawSprite` (`newinv2.cpp`, no caller); ROOMPOP's `far_plane=` field
prints 687865856. What stays on `ZFAR_SHIPPED`: the depth curve; the corner count of
`S_GetObjectBounds`; the fog bulbs of `aBuildFogBulbList` (`drawroom.cpp`), nearer than
20,480, since a bulb past it would fog faces nearer than it; and a rain drop's tint, 8 to
16 and 16 to 32 over the plane, through `ZRainTint` (`zrange_math.h`). What stays as it
was: the literal `0x5000` cut and fade of `S_DrawSparks`' line sparks, fire and smoke
sparks, blood, drips, bubbles and the rope (the line sparks take a negative colour past
it, as before), and the falling drops of `hd_life.cpp`; the distance fog
(`tomb5.distance_fog` times 1024, 3 to 30 sectors), which above 20 had no object to darken
before; and the looks that are distances but no cut - the light under water dimmed as
exp(-depth / 30,000) (`kDeepDim`), the surface light's fall-off seen from below and the
light shafts' reach (`HD_LOOK_REACH`, `HD_LOOK_DEEP`, 40,000). The water sheets, the sea
seen from below and the room art have no cut of their own: they are room art and were
drawn past 20,480 before, on the same depth curve.

The depth curve is sz = a - b / z with 0.005 at the near plane and 0.995 at the scale it
is built on; its slope b / z^2 is set by the near plane, b being 0.99 times the near
plane's 20 times scale / (scale - 20). Built on 20,480, as before: a = 0.99596775, b =
19.819355; 0.99500 at 20,480, 0.99550 at 41,984, under a = 0.99597 at any distance - under
the sky's slice from 0.996 (`HD_SKY_MINZ`) everywhere. `SetupZRange` takes `f_a` and `f_b`
from `ZDepthCurve` (`zrange_math.h`), the function ModernTest checks bit for bit against
the expression on 20480: one arithmetic, not a copy of it. So the HD projections, which
take `f_a` and `f_b`, `hd_room.hlsl`'s `SceneZ` with the water's `kWaterClip` and the wet
floor's `kWetLift`, and the springs' cracks (drawn to half of the depth 0.995, 10,240
units) are unchanged, and `HDRenderZConstants`, `SetupZRange`'s twin for the tools, is
still called with 20 and 20480, the curve's scale. A 24-bit depth step is 0.30 units at
10,000, 1.20 at 20,000, 2.71 at 30,000 and 5.30 at 41,984; the rooms' art past 20,480 had
these steps before, and the objects now drawn there take them, with no depth fight seen in
a sweep of far faces. The corner count stays on the shipped plane: `S_GetObjectBounds`
counts the box corners between the near plane and the plane, answers -1 (drawn clipped,
the window test skipped) under eight; on the moved plane an object nearer than 20,480
whose box reaches past it would be window tested instead, which changed the answer at many
camera positions of JOBY2's corridor seen in play. Counted under `ZFAR_SHIPPED` none does,
and a thing past 20,480, which the moved cull now lets through, is drawn clipped - as a
thing past the plane in an outside frame always was.

The number from the data: `RoomProbe -farsurvey 1` puts the eye at the centre of every
square inside every room's wall ring, at the room's middle height, walks the classic
portal walk from it over yaws 0 to 345 (step 15) and pitches -20 to 20 (step 10) at 2560 x
1440 and a field of view of 80, and asks the engine's rule for every item and static of
the listed rooms with no plane and its box against its room's window: the deepest it is
ever drawn from an inside frame (in an outside frame the plane cuts no object; flip maps
are not walked, the survey walks every level in its first flip state). Over the fifteen
levels 224 things lie past 20,480 - JOBY2 149 (12 of them doors), ANDREA3 40, ANDREA1 15,
RICH2 11, ANDREA2 4, RICH3 3 (2 lift doors), JOBY4 1, RICH1 1 - and the deepest is a
static of JOBY2's room 3 at 40,806 units (with yaws every 3 degrees), the corridor's door
at 34,340, 33.5 sectors. 41 sectors is the smallest whole count that holds the deepest
thing and the margin of one square (an eye elsewhere in the sampled square stands at most
a square farther from it): 40,806 + 1,024 = 41,830 under 41,984; 40 sectors (40,960) does
not. `-farobjects` draws the items the rule lets in, flat and orange, into the picture
(the HD art, or `-classiconly` the classic faces; the tool draws a door as its classic
mesh, where the HD path draws the door's HD model), with the walk's list and windows and
the level's flips; `-farcull` prints the walk's list against a plane. The things that join
cost one object draw each; the art's draw calls are the same.

The sparks: `S_DrawDrawSparksNEW` switches a sprite spark off (`sptr->On = 0`) the first
time it is drawn at or past the plane; a spark off screen is never switched off there.
With the plane at 41,984 a spark on screen between 20,480 and 41,984 lives its life out
instead: `UpdateSparks` (`game/effect2.cpp`) moves and fades it, keeps its dynamic light,
and runs its `extras`, the explosion's later bursts, out there. It holds a slot of the
pool of 1,024 longer; on a full pool `GetFreeSpark` takes the slot with the least life
that is neither `SF_NOKILL` nor a light's. The burn and the damage a spark does
(`SF_FIRE`, `SF_DAMAGE`) need it inside Lara's box: a spark 20,480 units from the camera
reaches her only where the camera stands that far from her. This is a change in the
sparks' state, not only in their drawing. The tests: ModernTest's `far_plane` group (the
constant, its margin and the next sector less, the shifted plane in a long, `ZDepthCurve`
bit for bit `SetupZRange`'s with 20480, the curve under the sky's slice, the depth steps,
`ZRainTint` against `DoRain`'s expression at every eighth unit to 45,000). `tomb5.vcxproj`
does not list `zrange_math.h`, a header the build finds by its include.

**Decisions.** The plane moves for both paths and the four cuts that are looks stay: the
depth curve (every depth nearer than 20,480 the float it was, the HD projection, the
water's reading and the sky's slice with it; built on 41,984 instead it would be a =
0.99547184, b = 19.809437, and every depth on screen would move, by 4.9e-4 at 1,000 units,
8,150 steps of a 24-bit buffer, for 0.05 % of resolution), the rain's tint, the fog bulbs'
circle and the corner count. 41 sectors from the survey and a square's margin, not the 34
of the corridor: JOBY2 lists statics of room 3 to 40,806. No new key: the request was the
extension, not a switch. Both `InitWindow` calls take the plane, the one in `winmain.cpp`
too, or the plane would fall back to 20,480 after a display mode change. The sprite
sparks' switch-off moves with the plane and does not stay at 20,480: a spark the moved
plane draws is not killed for being drawn.

**Commits.** `838748f2` (the comparison base), `787da34d` (the plane, curve kept),
`34889b87` (RoomProbe's switches, ModernTest's group), `7a812d88` (the record), `b4639be2`
(comments, `SetupZRange` on `ZDepthCurve`), `a1a153c3` (the record's site table)

### Volumetric fog from the fog bulbs (#218)
2026-10-19 to 2026-10-20

**What.** The level's fog bulbs are drawn as fog with a body of its own. Per bulb in view
the engine draws one quad over the sphere's rectangle on the screen, at the end of the
bracket that asks the rooms' additive pass - the last HD pass of the frame, after the
glass, the glows and the water, before the classic path's sprites and the HUD: each
pixel's view ray is cut by the sphere and by the frame's depth, the bulb's density is
integrated along the piece that is left, and the pixel is veiled by it in the bulb's own
colour. A bulb the pass draws leaves the per-pixel haze of the room, model, glow and
shadow receive shaders, so no bulb counts twice in what those shaders draw. The art's own
mist - the `.TRG`'s additive flow parts whose page drifts on both axes and which stand in
the air, such as the lumps around ANDY3's mill and the title's drifting sand - is drawn at
a weight of 0.35 instead of 1, as faint fog. The registry key `hd_fog` (1 by default)
switches the pass and the mist's weight; 0 draws every picture as before. New files:
`specific/hd/hd_fog.h` (the rule as pure functions: `HDFogStrength`, `HDFogArtMist`,
`HDFogArtWeight`) and `hd_shader/hd_fog.hlsl` with its `hd_fog_vs.inc` and
`hd_fog_ps.inc`. The HDLOG frame line ends with `fog_taken=` and `fog_drawn=`, the
settings line with `hd_fog=`. RoomProbe: `-fogbulbs`, `-fogprofile <bulb>`, `-hdfog 0|1`
(or `-fog 0|1`), `-fogpass 0`, `-fogart` (or `-fogbook`), `-fogartweight`, `-fogstrength`;
ModernTest's groups `fog_body` and `fog_art`.

**Why.** The fog around ANDY3's mill was to become volumetric fog. The classic haze, even
weighted at its rim with a `smoothstep` (the record's entry "The engine's own per-vertex
lighting, as shader arithmetic"), drew each bulb as a disc with an outline on the surfaces
behind it. In play a body at the classic's own strength was too faint to read as fog:
inside one of the mill's bulbs it added less light than the haze it took out. The mottled
yellow lumps around the mill, which are the art's additive parts and not bulbs, read as
solid balls rather than fog.

**How.** The bulbs are the level's own: the classic `.TRC`'s room headers hold `fogbulb`
at +148 and `nFogBulbs` at +156, nine floats a bulb, and `aRoomInit` gives the density d,
about 1/72 in every level (halved first in ANDREA2 and ANDREA3); JOBY2 to JOBY5 and
RICHCUT2 hold none. The density at a point inside the sphere is S x d x 1.5 x (1 - rho^2),
rho the distance from the centre over the radius r: 1.5 makes the column through the
centre 2 r d, the classic's own most, and the column at distance b from the centre, 2 r d
(1 - b^2)^1.5, leaves the rim with zero slope, so the bulb has no visible rim. The column
is integrated exactly along the view ray between the camera (or the sphere's near side)
and the frame's depth (or the far side): a surface inside the bulb is veiled by the fog in
front of it alone, the sky behind a bulb by all of it. tau is the column over 255, the
classic's own scale, and the pixel becomes dst T + colour (1 - T), T = exp(-tau); 1 - T
never exceeds tau. S, the strength, is per bulb (`HDFogStrength`, taken in `fog_take`, the
shader unchanged): the factor that makes the densest line veil black by 33 of 255 in the
bulb's colour, 1 - exp(-S 2 r d / 255) = 33 / 255 over the colour's luma, at most a veil
of one half (`HD_FOG_VEIL_MOST`). The top of 33 (`HD_FOG_TOP`) is the 95th percentile of
the wisps over the ground under them in a reference picture supplied for this project;
ANDY3's bulbs (radius 1,312, colour 134, 168, 148) get S 1.66. The breath: the density
times 1 - 0.5 n, n a value noise of hashed lattice points (the sky cloud's hash) over
cells of half the bulb's radius, anchored in the world and rising a quarter cell a second
on the drawn clock (also with `hd_motion` 0); the column is taken in four equal pieces,
each exact for the smooth density and weighted with the breath at its middle. The mist
(`HDFogArtMist`, `fog_add_coat`) is an additive flow part whose page drifts on both axes -
every water flow scrolls along one axis - and whose coat lies under a tenth
(`HD_FOG_ART_COAT`): the coat is the share of the range's corners with a corner of its
group's opaque or alpha triangles in their 16-unit cell or one of the 26 around it. Parts
in the air (the mill, the title's sand) have a coat of 0.009 at most, the golden washes
laid on ANDREA2's and ANDREA3's tunnel walls 0.398 at least and keep their weight. The
mist's weight, 0.35 (`HD_FOG_ART_WEIGHT`), is the top over the most the mist adds at
weight 1 (94.3 of 255 at the 95th percentile at the brightest view of the mill). The pass
comes after the additive pass, so the mist and everything else inside a sphere lie under
the bulb's veil and no fog is added to the fog's own light twice. A drawn bulb's haze is
taken out by uploading its density as 0, which takes it out of every `BulbIntensity` to
the bit. The pass needs the frame's depth, the INTZ texture the water binds in a level
that built sheets; in ANDREA3, RICH1 and TITLE (no water square) and with `hd_water` 0 no
depth texture is bound and the bulbs keep the haze. A bulb under a sheet, or with the
camera under water, stays as `hd_level.cpp` hands it: not in the frame. The bulbs are
taken once a bracket (`fog_take`, its first call; `fog_draw` in `HDRenderFrameEnd` ends
it): the marble floors' mirror (`HDRenderMarbleDraw`) hands the frame's lighting back
through `apply_frame_lighting` with the mirrored projection still set, and a second take
inside the bracket keeps the bulbs, their rectangles and the due flag and only takes the
same bulbs' haze out of the upload once more; taken afresh there, every bulb on the screen
lost its haze and its fog alike. The mirrors draw their rooms with the frame's upload, so
a drawn bulb's haze is out of the mirror too and the pass does not reach into it. Two
kinds of faces carry their own haze and are veiled once more where they stand in or behind
a drawn bulb: the faces of a room the HD path leaves classic and the items it draws
classic (`drawroom.cpp`, `output.cpp`), and the broken pieces, which `hd_debris.h` uploads
with the bulbs' own density. The hooks in `hd_render.cpp`: the three includes at the top
(`hd_fog.h` and the two `.inc`), the take in `apply_frame_lighting`, the pass in
`HDRenderFrameEnd`, the note in `HDRenderRoomMask` that makes the pass due and places the
breath, and the shaders' release in `HDRenderShutdown`; the frame line's log words are in
`hd_level.cpp`. The pass costs under 0.3 ms a frame at 2,560 x 1,440, so `hd_fog` is 1 by
default.

**Decisions.** The haze of a drawn bulb is taken out, not kept as the fog's far term: it
is the same bulb's column on the surface behind, so kept it would veil that surface twice,
and the integral to the depth already holds it. The rim's fall is not fitted to a fixed
number of screen pixels: that would be a screen rule no bulb's data gives, and it would
draw the outline back on every large bulb. The fog takes the bulb's colour alone, as the
classic lights a bulb's haze, and not the room's light: `HDRoomLighting` carries no
ambient and the frame hands no room for a bulb. The strength is per bulb, from its own
radius, density and colour, so the top holds for every bulb; it raises the faint ones and
lowers the bright ones (ANDREA2's canal bulbs, TITLE's); the cap of one half is a free
choice for a bulb darker than the top (ANDY1's one dark bulb, 40, 68, 48), whose veil
could otherwise never reach it. The breath's numbers - 0.5 of the density, half a radius a
cell, a quarter cell a second, four pieces - are free choices: the breath only thins. The
mist is weighed down and not tied to the bulbs: none of its parts' centres lies in a
sphere, and a weight per bulb would give one cloud of the same art two strengths; the rain
rings on the water (book 3,273, flat, weight 0.06) are not the lumps and keep their
weight. The criterion is the level's data alone - the material, its drift and its coat;
the coat is asked at a 16-unit cell because at 64-unit cells the gap between the cards in
the air (0.333) and the washes (0.514) closes. The title's sand is weighed as mist because
it is the same art, cards drifting askew in the air by the level's bulbs. The weight is
one number for every mist (the views' 95th percentiles lie within 12 per cent of each
other). No room or level number is in the code.

**Commits.** `a68a9de0` (the base before the fog), `4e5c311e` (the rule and the pass),
`ac27a880` (the key), `905ff5a4` (RoomProbe and ModernTest switches), `42864c7b` (the
record), `f541c9ff` (two lines wrapped), `fb81edb2` (the record's commits), `2f1ff73c`
(bulbs taken once a bracket), `6203c859` (the base before the strength), `5bb8f7a9` (the
record), `cfcb14c4` (the log lines), `9e636a37` (the art's mist), `94475e76` (the body's
strength), `c089d26d` (RoomProbe and ModernTest), `28648b2b` (the mist's coat).

### The glow's normal, re-derived (#233)
2026-10-22

**What.** The normal the glow's `|N.V|` term takes is this project's own choice on its own
measurement. The renderer keeps what it drew: per part, the file's normal where the file's
normals agree with the faces and the face's normal where more than half of a part's
corners disagree. New is a setting that forces either normal on every part, for the
diagnostic tool alone, and the A/B over the glow's 46 views that it made possible. Nothing
that the game draws changes.

**Why.** The choice was to be re-derived on this project's own data rather than kept or
re-tuned by taste, and the tool could not force either normal on every part: the choice is
made per part when the level is built.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_render.h`: `HDGlowFaceNormal(mode, disagree, corners)`, the
decision as a pure function, with `HD_GLOW_NORMAL_PART` (the per-part choice),
`HD_GLOW_NORMAL_FILE` and `HD_GLOW_NORMAL_FACE`; `HDRenderGlowOverride` takes the mode as
a fourth value. `specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`: `g_glow_normal` beside `g_glow_no_shader`,
`HD_GLOW_NORMAL_PART` in the engine, which never calls the override; `BuildGlowParts`
takes the part's choice from the function where it took `disagree * 2 > corners`, and
counts the corners and the disagreeing ones as before. The shader and its constants are
unchanged: `out[9]` still carries the part's choice to `gGlowMode.y`. The setting is read
only in `BuildGlowParts`, behind `HDEnabled`, and only the tool sets it. Tools: RoomProbe
`-glowface shipped|file|face`, set before the level is built and parsed in `-glowps`'s
branch, because the switch chain stands at the compiler's limit of nested blocks;
ModernTest's `glow_normal`, 8 checks. Over the fifteen levels the census of
`BuildGlowParts` holds 253 parts; 31 have more than half of their corners disagreeing
(from 0.514 of them up), the other 222 at most 0.486, so the per-part choice puts the face
normal on exactly those 31: JOBY2's 21 lamp cones, ANDREA3's seven window slabs of page
3232, ANDY2 room 34, ANDY3 room 150 and TITLE room 43. On those parts the file normal
fades the card as if it were seen edge-on. The A/B's rule, written down before the
verdict, follows the aims the glow's measurement of #179 set (fewer clipped, white and
hue-pinned pixels, fewer steps over 40 of 255 at equal means), with this project's own
pairwise thresholds: per view and pair of settings, the lower sum of the three shares wins
when the sums differ by more than 0.05 percentage points (a twentieth of the pass mark of
1 per cent); else the fewer steps win when they differ by more than 5 per cent and by 2 or
more, and only if the winner's mean is at least 95 per cent of the loser's; else the view
is a tie. A forced normal replaces the per-part choice only if it wins clearly, on most of
the views. All 46 views are ties in all three pairs.

**Decisions.** The per-part choice stays as built, OWN, re-derived on this project's own
A/B: no forced normal wins, and the per-part choice is the census's own split, the face
normal exactly where the file's normals do not describe the card and the file normal,
which the renderer interpolates across the card, everywhere else. The forced settings stay
in the tool for the next measurement.

**Commits.** `6a4eef5b` (the base), `73bee6fb` (the setting, tool and checks), `518906fe`
(the record).

### The captions in German, and Lara's weapon item steps as she does (#234)
2026-10-22

**What.** Two things. (1) Every word the project draws on the options pages, in the F4
outfit window and as the F12 notice has its German: 23 new rows in `CustomText`'s table
(`game/gameflow.cpp`, 93 rows before, 116 after), the German word in its column and the
English word in the French, Italian and Spanish columns, as in every row. The F4 window
(`specific/hd/hd_outfitmenu.cpp`) passes its literals and the head and shine phrases it
asks the wardrobe for (`HDWardrobeHeadPhrase`, `HDWardrobeFromWord`) through `CustomText`;
the log lines that print the same phrases stay English. The F12 notice *HD is off*
(`specific/hd/hd_switch.cpp`) goes through `CustomText` into the ammo caption. (2) Lara's
weapon item - the shotgun, HK or crossbow she holds, an item of its own
(`lara.weapon_item`, made by `draw_shotgun`) - counts as her for the footstep's choice:
`AnimateItem` hands the item's index in `items[]` and `lara.weapon_item` to
`HDFeetStepItem` around an animation command's sound, beside `SfxCommandCaller`, and
`HDFeetStepInfo` asks the pure `HDFeetCallerOf`, which answers `LARA` for the item at
`lara.weapon_item` and the caller itself for every other item. Her draw and her outfit
then choose as for her own step.

**Why.** Some captions did not switch with the language: `CustomText` returns the table's
column for French, German, Italian and Spanish when the English matches a row and the
English literal itself when none does, so a project word without a row was English in
every language; the F4 window had no rows for its literals and printed the wardrobe's
phrases raw, and the F12 notice was copied into the caption raw. In randomized levels,
where the weapon import brings the shotgun's animation set with sound id 0, the step of
the drawn shotgun played the level's ordinary set - boots - even while Lara was drawn HD
and barefoot. Only German is translated by this project; the other languages keep the
English word, as the table does.

**How.** A row of the options pages (`game/menu_frame.cpp`, the `MENU_*` tables) draws its
caption from the game's language file when it carries a string id (`SCRIPT_TEXT`) and
through `CustomText(label)` otherwise; a value comes from the row's `MenuVal...` function;
a page's title the same way as a caption. The pages that run the game's own screens,
*Special Features* and *Credits*, are handed to `MenuRunLegacy` before a title is drawn
and have none. The rule: a word the project draws has its row in the table; a word that is
the same in German (*Gamma*, *HD / SD*, *Display (60)*, *Original*, *PSX*, *TR4*, *TR5*,
the arrow glyphs `\x18` to `\x1B`), a name (*outfit.txt*, *origin*, *I-III*, *IV-VI*, *PS5
Controller*, *Xbox Controller*) or a mark (`---`) stays without one. The width rule, on
the game font's glyph table (`game/chardef.inc`, added up as `GetStringLength` does, an
umlaut as its base letter): `InitFont` makes a glyph w * (W - 1) / 512 pixels wide at a
screen W pixels wide, rounded down, and a space W / 80; the value column starts at 0.625 W
and holds 0.375 W, so a value whose glyph units plus 6.4 per space stay at or under 192
fits at every width, without the help of the rounding. A rule in pixels at 640 x 480 does
not carry over, because the rounding takes up to a pixel from every glyph, which counts at
640 and hardly at 1920. Every German label is 133.4 units or less, every German value
189.8 or less. A footstep is Lara's when its caller is `LARA` or the item that plays it is
the one at `lara.weapon_item`, asked by its index; `AnimateItem` hands over `NO_ITEM` for
an item that is not one of the level's. `SfxCommandCaller` keeps the object number: the
`SFXLOG` line's `obj=` still names the weapon object, and its end says `feet=bare` or
`feet=boots` as for her own step; the FEET line is unchanged. Tests: ModernTest's
`caption_rows` (76 checks: every German word has its one row, fits its column by the width
rule at every screen width, every literal of the F4 window has its row, the phrases go
through `CustomText`, the widest German head value fits, the notice goes through
`CustomText`) and 117 new checks in `hd_feet` (her shotgun, crossbow and HK, a shotgun not
hers, the guard, no item, over both draws, both outfits, with and without a footstep mod).
With `hd_build` 0 the footstep harness's whole output is unchanged.

**Decisions.** (1) The words: *HD-Aufbau* for *HD build* - the gate decides whether a
level is built with its HD data, and it stands above *HD-Texturen*; *Spiegelungen* for
*Reflections*; *HD ist aus*, ten letters where the caption's buffer holds eleven; the F4
window's *Outfit*, *Levelvorgabe*, *nach Level und Lauf*, *Schritte*, *Kopf*, *Glanz*,
*Hautglanz*, *laut Outfit*, *Barfuss*, *Stiefel*, *Barfuss - fehlt hier*, *Stiefel - fehlt
hier* and `"gilt ab dem n\xE4" "chsten Level"` (split at the umlaut because `c` is a hex
digit); the phrases *TR5* for TR5's head, *mit Zopf* for the outfit's own head under TR5's
braid, *eigener* for its own head alone (the row's label already says *Kopf*), *gemessen*,
*Tabelle*, *Liste*, *Standard*. (2) *Barfuss* is written with "ss": the font has no sharp
s. (3) Every German value fits the value column at every screen width, also where the
English word it replaces does not; *TR5-Kopf (outfit.txt)* and *TR5-Haar (outfit.txt)* ran
past the column above 2,559 and 1,536 pixels of width and gave way to *TR5* and *mit
Zopf*. (4) *Outfit* has its row although the German is the same word, as *Audio* and
*Normal* have theirs. (5) The weapon item is asked by its index, never by its object
number, so no other item can be taken for hers. (6) All three long guns count, though only
the shotgun's animation carries a step in the levels measured. (7) MenuTest's check of the
notice follows the call it reads; its count stays. The Credits screen's headings, the ammo
hotkeys' captions, the pad's button names and the English F4 values wider than the value
column are settled in #237.

**Commits.** `8a535bf2` (captions in German, the notice), `117244dd` (the weapon item's
step), `4b4ef293` (the record), `403847b4` (head words, width rule), `5ff33459` (width
figures corrected).

### The water sheets are part of the HD look; their row goes (#236)
2026-10-22

**What.** The options row *HD water* is gone from the Graphics page, and with it the
option field `tomb5.hd_water` (`global/types.h`), its registry value `hd_water` (the first
run's default, the read and the save in `tomb5/tomb5.cpp`), the row's two value functions
`MenuValHdWater` and `MenuStepHdWater` (`game/menu_frame.cpp`), its caption row in
`CustomText`'s table (`game/gameflow.cpp`) and the level key's water field
(`specific/hd/hd_levelkey.h`). The water sheets are drawn whenever the HD look is drawn:
every HD build lays them, and the F12 switch to the classic look still shows the classic
water. A `hd_water` value an older build left in the registry is not read; a player who
had switched the row off gets the sheets back (its removal at the next save is #238's).
The other rows are unchanged; the Graphics page holds fifteen rows, paged eight and seven.

**Why.** The water sheets were judged good enough in play to be part of the HD look, so
the switch went.

**How.** The water's gates ask exactly the question they asked beside the value. In
`specific/hd/hd_level.cpp` the five hooks `HDWaterRippleOnSheet`, `HDWaterFallsTick`,
`HDWaterSplash`, `HDWaterSpray` and `HDWaterTank` ask `HDLevelActive()` (the level built
and drawn HD, `g_level_active && HDDrawn()`) and `tomb5.hd_motion`;
`AppendWaterCardPages`, `life_on` (`hd_life.cpp`) and `HDSpringLevelBegin`
(`hd_spring.cpp`, which loses its include of `tomb5/tomb5.h`) ask what was built,
`HDRenderWaterSheetsBuilt()`, alone. The build hands nothing to `HDRenderSetWaterSheets`,
which lost its `sheets` parameter: the renderer lays the sheets unless the tool's override
asks for the classic water. The classic water under the HD look is no state of the game
any more; the diagnostic tool keeps it for the water entries' comparison pictures through
`HDRenderWaterSheetsOverride(int off)`, an override of the tools' kind beside
`HDRenderShoreOverride` and the glow's: off by default, never called by the engine, no
option and no registry key. RoomProbe's `-hdwater 0|1` keeps its name and sets the
override before the build. The `WATERLOG` level line keeps its `option=` field, now
printed by the renderer from the override (1 in the game), because the WATERLOG sweeps
compare the engine's and RoomProbe's lines whole; `HDRenderWaterLogLine` lost its `option`
parameter. The level key lives in memory only and decides whether a savegame loaded inside
a level keeps the HD data built for it; with the sheets in every HD build its water field
could no longer differ between two keys. No gate line carrying `g_level_active`,
`HDEnabled()` or `HDDrawn()` changed. The remaining changes are comments (`hd_render.cpp`,
`hd_render.h`, `hd_level.h`, `hd_laradraw.cpp`, `hd_life.h`, `hd_water_under.h`, the room
shader's flood comment in `hd_shader/hd_room.hlsl`, whose `.inc` files differ in their
header line alone) and the tools: RoomProbe's copy of the key and its `-hdwater` usage,
MenuTest's water row family, now checks of the row's absence, and ModernTest's four wiring
checks (no water gate reads an option, the five hooks ask the draw and the motion, the
override off by default and set by no engine file).

**Decisions.** The log field stays, so the sweeps compare as before. The suites search for
the removed name in two halves, so that a search of the tree finds it only in this record
and the ledger. The manual says that the game reads no registry value for the water,
without the value's name.

**Commits.** `92f1423c` (the base), `20af4637` (the row, value and gates), `217983db` (the
override and checks), `787898bf` (the name in halves), `63f623bd` (the record and
manuals), `c013cefa` (tool comments, manual sentence), `ff522928` (the list, one word).

### Two words renamed; the credits, the pad's names and the ammo captions in German (#237)
2026-10-22

**What.** Four things. (1) The options row *HD build* reads *HD-Installation* in German
(it read *HD-Aufbau*), and the F4 window's first row *Level facts* reads *Leveleigen* (it
read *Levelvorgabe*); its value *nach Level und Lauf* stays, and so do *TR5* and *mit
Zopf*. (2) The English values of the F4 window that ran past the value column have shorter
words of the same meaning: *level and run decide*, *Bare - no 2nd set* and *Boots - no 2nd
set*. The head row draws the window's own head word (`head_word`,
`specific/hd/hd_outfitmenu.cpp`: *own*, *TR5*, *TR5 hair*) and the head, shine and skin
glow rows the one-word tier of `HDWardrobeFromTag` (*default*, *measured*, *table*,
*outfit.txt*, *origin*, *list*); the log lines keep the wardrobe's phrases. The German
rows follow the new English keys, the key of a row being the English literal; the row of
*TR5 head* goes, because *TR5* is the same in German and falls back to itself. (3) The
Credits screen's title and its five headings (`CreditsScreen`, `tomb5/troyestuff.cpp`),
the pad's button names in the Key bindings' value column (`MenuValBinding`,
`game/menu_frame.cpp`) and the ammo hotkeys' captions (`DoWeaponRequest`,
`specific/input.cpp`) go through `CustomText`, and every word among them has its German
row: 22 new rows, the table from 115 rows to 136. (4) ModernTest's `caption_rows` measures
the English key of every row as well as its German word, and checks the new rows, their
routing and every name of the pad's four pages.

**Why.** The German words *HD-Installation* and *Leveleigen* (as the row's name, in place
of *Levelvorgabe*) were requested; the English F4 values that ran past the right edge were
to be shortened; and the Credits headings, the pad's button names and the ammo captions
were to get German too. They were raw literals of the project's own path, none from the
game's language file: the Credits screen (`MenuRunLegacy` hands it to `CreditsScreen`)
printed its title and headings raw although the options row that opens it draws *Credits*
through `CustomText`; `JoyButtonName` returns a literal of the page's table
(`JoyNamesPS5DInput`, `JoyNamesPS5XInput`, `JoyNamesXbox`, `JoyNamesGeneric`) and
`MenuValBinding`, its only reader, printed it raw; `DoWeaponRequest` copied the five
captions raw into the twelve bytes of `ammo_change_buf`, which `game/health.cpp` draws
centred at the top of the screen. Only German is translated by this project; French,
Italian and Spanish keep the English word, as every row of the table does.

**How.** #234's rule, carried on: a word the project draws has its row, and its German
word and its English key both fit the column it is drawn in, at every screen width - in
#234's units (glyph units of `game/chardef.inc` plus 6.4 per space, an umlaut as its base
letter) the value column holds 192, the label column 223, a centred line 512. A pad's
button that is a letter or a number, an unnamed bit (*Joy 13*) and a name printed on the
pad (*Share*, *Options*, *Touchpad*) is a name and has no row; a pad's name is measured
behind *Mod+*, as a chord prints it (*Mod+Stick R Runter*, the widest, 188.8 of 192);
every column of an ammo caption's row holds eleven letters at most, for the twelve-byte
buffer. The new words: the Credits headings *TOMB5-Engine*, *TR3-Gegner aus tomb3*,
*Randomizer und Windows-11-Port*, *Mitwirkende*, *Werkzeuge und Bibliotheken*; the pad's
*Quadrat*, *Kreuz*, *Kreis*, *Dreieck*, *PS-Taste*, *Ansicht*, `Men\xFC`, *Stick R* and
*D-Pad* with *Hoch*, *Runter*, *Links*, *Rechts*; the ammo captions *Breitschuss*,
*Salve*, *Einzelfeuer*, *Dauerfeuer*. The keyboard's names (the German keyboard table),
the mouse's (`KeySchemeMouseName`) and *Waiting* (the language file) were German already.
The ammo captions are written as the F12 notice is, `strcpy(ammo_change_buf,
CustomText(...))`. `caption_rows` checks every new row with its German, its width in both
languages, the caption buffer's bytes, a row for every literal the Credits screen and the
ammo hotkeys hand to `CustomText`, the routing at each place, and every one of the 48 pad
names (15 words with rows, 33 names without). Words only: no draw, sound or data path
changed, so `hd_build` 0 and the classic draw are unchanged by construction.
`HDWardrobeHeadPhrase` (`hd_wardrobe.h`) has no caller since the window prints the head
word itself; it stays, its header comments corrected.

**Decisions.** (1) The English values are shortened in the window and nowhere else: the
log lines that print the wardrobe's phrases keep them, and `hd_wardrobe.cpp` is untouched.
The tiers take `HDWardrobeFromTag`, the form the wardrobe already keeps for a counted
column, in all three rows alike; the head word drops "head", which the row's label says,
as the German *eigener* does. (2) The Credits title's row is the options row's own, so
Italian and Spanish read *Crediti* and *Creditos* on the screen as on the row that opens
it; German and French stay *Credits*. (3) The pad's shapes are the German shapes; the
stick's and the d-pad's directions are the German keyboard table's arrow keys behind
*Stick R* and *D-Pad*, which stay as they are; the Xbox pad's View button takes the
existing *View* row's *Ansicht*, its German name. (4) The ammo captions: *Breitschuss* for
the shotgun's wideshot, and the fire selector's German words for the HK's three modes;
*Normal* had its row. (5) The names are routed in `MenuValBinding`, their only reader, and
`JoyButtonName` keeps the English name. (6) The Credits screen's lines of names stay as
they are written, those with English joining words among them: they are not headings
(settled in #239).

**Commits.** `dabb6b67` (two words, shorter F4 values), `ea4881a8` (credits, pad names,
ammo captions), `dd02d677` (a comment names *list*).

### The old water value leaves the registry at the next save (#238)
2026-10-22

**What.** `save_new_tomb5_settings()` (`tomb5/tomb5.cpp`), the function that writes every
tomb5 option, deletes the value `hd_water` from the options' registry key while the key is
open. An older build wrote that value for the water sheets' options row, which #236
removed; since then it was neither read nor written and stayed in a player's key. It goes
at the first save after this build: the first change of an options row that saves the
tomb5 options. A new helper `REG_DeleteValue` (`specific/registry.cpp`,
`specific/registry.h`) removes one value from the open key, beside `REG_WriteLong`,
`REG_WriteBool` and `REG_WriteString`. The read path (`init_tomb5_stuff()`) and the first
run's defaults are unchanged and do not name the value. ModernTest's `registry_old_water`
checks that the save's body holds the call with the name and that the file names and
deletes the value once.

**Why.** The leftover value was to be deleted from a player's registry at the next save
rather than stay ignored; the Engine Manual was not to name the old value again.

**How.** The rule: the options' key holds only values this build reads; a value an older
build wrote and this one no longer reads is deleted by the save, in the open key, and
named nowhere else in the engine; the read path never asks for it. The save's one caller
is `MenuAfterChange` (`game/menu_frame.cpp`), at every change of an options row whose save
is `MENU_SAVE_TOMB5`. The save opens the key first (`OpenRegistry("tomb5")`,
`Software\Core Design\Tomb Raider Chronicles\tomb5` under `HKEY_CURRENT_USER`) and closes
it last; `REG_OpenKey` opens it with `RegCreateKeyEx` and `KEY_ALL_ACCESS`, which holds
`KEY_SET_VALUE`, the right `RegDeleteValue` needs. `RegDeleteValue` returns
`ERROR_SUCCESS` when it removed the value and `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` when the key holds
none of that name, and changes nothing else; an absent value is the usual case, so the
result is not asked, as the writes do not ask theirs - the value's absence is the state
the call makes.

**Decisions.** (1) The deletion sits at the end of the save, before the key is closed, and
only there: the read path stays as #236 left it, and the first run, whose key was just
created, has nothing to delete. (2) The call's literal is written in the suites' two
halves (`"hd_" "water"`, one string to the compiler), because MenuTest asserts that
`tomb5/tomb5.cpp` holds no name with its closing quote; the comment over the call names
the value plainly, so a search of the tree finds the deletion site, and says why the
literal is split. (3) The Engine Manual keeps not naming the value; its registry section
says in one sentence that a water value of an older build is removed at the next save. (4)
The helper takes the value's name as `char*`, as its neighbours do.

**Commits.** `34cbab80` (the base), `991bb2d8` (helper, deletion and check).

### Every language gets all its texts; Japanese for the HQ audio (#239)
2026-10-23

**What.** Five things. (1) The ammo hotkeys' caption at the top of the screen
(`DoWeaponRequest`, `specific/input.cpp`) shows the language file's own name of the
shotgun's ammunition and of the HK's fire mode - the strings the inventory shows for the
same items (`TXT_Shotgun_Normal_Ammo`, `TXT_Shotgun_Wideshot_Ammo`, `TXT_HKSTRING2`
sniper, `TXT_HKSTRING3` burst, `TXT_HKSTRING4` rapid) - copied by `AmmoCaption` into
`ammo_change_buf`, which grows from 12 to 64 bytes; `CustomText`'s table loses the rows
*Wideshot*, *Burst*, *Sniper* and *Rapid*. (2) The German pad names read *Stick R oben*,
*unten*, *links*, *rechts* and *Steuerkreuz oben*, *unten*, *links*, *rechts*. (3) Every
row of the table carries a French, an Italian and a Spanish word of the same meaning as
its German cell; two rows are new, *Display (60)* and *Original*; the Language row's names
*Français* and *Español* carry their accents (`LanguageName`, `game/gameflow.cpp`). (4)
The project's words can also come from `extrastrings.txt` beside the executable
(`LoadExtraStrings`, `game/gameflow.cpp`), read once at start; the file's word goes before
the table's, and `Preparation/extrastrings.txt` is the shipped copy with every word of the
table. (5) The Language row reaches the Japanese entry when the folder `audio\HQ JP` is
there: the Japanese HQ audio with English text (`SwitchLanguage`).

**Why.** Every text the game shows was to be visible in every language: the language files
first, the project's own `extrastrings.txt` where they do not suffice, and the project's
own menu words in all four languages. The ammo captions had got words of the project's own
although the language files name those items already. The German pad words *Steuerkreuz*
and *oben/unten* were requested. The Japanese HQ audio was to stay usable: a Japanese
language file of the TR5 layout passed the header check and printed symbols on the HUD,
while the audio needs no Japanese text. The missing language files are the player's to
get.

**How.** The rule: the language file is the first source of every word the game names; the
project's own words come from `extrastrings.txt` when it has them, then from the table,
then the English literal. Every row of the table carries all four words; a cell repeats
the English only where the language uses that word itself (*Pause*, *Action*, *Modes*,
*Audio*, *HUD*, *VSync*, *Normal*, *Original*, *table*, *Triangle*, *Menu* in one or more
of the three languages). Every cell fits the column its key is drawn in, at every screen
width, by #234's rule (labels 223 units, values and pad names behind *Mod+* 192, centred
lines 512). An accented letter is a Latin-1 hex escape the font composes: `AccentToCode`
(`game/text.cpp`) maps 33 Latin-1 bytes to the font's codes and `accent.inc` composes all
33; a letter outside them (À, È, Ç, Í, Ú) would be left out by `PrintString`. The HK's
modes: `W_AMMO1` is the sniper mode (`FireHK`, `HKTimer = 12`), `W_AMMO2` the burst,
`W_AMMO3` the rapid fire; the inventory binds `TXT_HKSTRING2`, 3 and 4 to ammo types 0, 1
and 2, which `update_laras_weapons_status` turns into `W_AMMO1`, 2 and 3, and the cycle's
caption takes the string of the mode it sets. `ammo_change_buf` is written by the five
captions and by the F12 notice (`specific/hd/hd_switch.cpp`) and read only by
`game/health.cpp`, centred at the top; the longest of the five names in the language files
is 37 bytes (Spanish wideshot). `extrastrings.txt` is opened by `fopen` with its bare
name, as `LoadFile` opens `SCRIPT.DAT`, from the working directory, and the load writes
one `STRINGS` line (`keys= french= german= italian= spanish= skipped=`, `rejected=1` for a
refused file). A word holds 63 bytes at most, the caption's buffer, because the F12 notice
copies its word with `strcpy`; at most 512 keys; a Latin-1 sign from 0x80 to 0xBF other
than ¡ and ¿ becomes *?*, because as a byte it would read as one of the font's accent
codes 128..173, some of which have no glyph; a file over 64 KB, in UTF-16 or holding a NUL
byte is left out whole. Japanese: `SwitchLanguage` offers the entry only where `audio\HQ
JP` is (one `GetFileAttributesA`); the entry is decided by its value, before any file is
read, and loads the English entry's file under the same header check, so no Japanese text
file is loaded; without the folder it returns 0 as before, so the row skips it and a saved
choice of 6 leaves the language as it was at start. With `JAPAN` (6) `ACMEmulateCDPlay`
plays `audio\HQ JP\<track>.OGG`, then `HQ EN`, then the WAV; `CustomText` returns the
literal, as for Dutch; Lara's "no" plays the engine's `SFX_LARA_NO_JAPANESE`
(`game/sound.cpp`) and the boot screen asks for `japan.bmp`, as the engine always did for
that value. MenuTest reads a row to its closing brace (`tree_row_cols`), because rows wrap
at 80 columns and split around escapes. ModernTest's groups `caption_rows`,
`caption_columns` (every site of the census in its source, every row with a site, every
cell against its column, every accented letter composed), `caption_share`, `extra_strings`
(the shipped file equals the table in all four sections, CRLF without a byte order mark;
the loader's place and order) and `japanese_audio`. No draw, sound or data path changed;
`specific/audio.cpp` changes in its comment only and `Gameflow->Language` keeps its
values.

**Decisions.** (1) The ammo caption is the language file's string, copied bounded
(`snprintf`) so that a longer string of another file is cut at the buffer's 63 bytes. (2)
The four *Steuerkreuz* chords behind *Mod+* run past the value column (up to 222.4 of
192), and the requested word stays. (3) Vocabulary and register: the game's file first
where it names the thing - French *Munitions*, *niveau*; Italian *Munizioni*, *livello*,
*Scatto*, the file's imperatives (*Salta livello*, *Cura*); Spanish *Munición*, *nivel*,
*Mirar*, the file's infinitives - and the German words as the meaning. *on* and *off* are
*activé*/*désactivé*, *attivo*/*disattivo* and *activo*/*inactivo* (the Spanish
*desactivado (reinicio)* was 2.4 units too wide, so all four Spanish values take
*activo*/*inactivo*); the French restart is *(relancer)*, *(redémarrage)* being too wide;
Italian and Spanish shorten left and right in the pad's names (*sx*/*dx*, *izq.*/*der.*),
and Italian names its mode rows *Modo ...* (*Modalità combattimento* was 6.4 units over);
the d-pad is *Flèche*, *Freccia* and *Cruceta*, so that French and Italian do not call it
by the Cross button's *Croix* and *Croce* on the same page; the F4 head words are *à
tresse*, *treccia*, *trenza*; the French tier *default* is *par défaut* (*défaut* alone
reads as a flaw), the Spanish *estándar* (*predeterminado* ran over); further *Telecamera
di morte*, *Première personne* beside *Troisième personne*, *Lissage caméra*, *Modo
agachado*, *HD desactivado*, the Italian duck mode *Modo accovacciato* (*abbassamento*
reads as lowering), *Improved* in the feminine of its label (*Améliorée*, *Migliorata*,
*Mejorada*), *Style d'écran mono* and *Estilo de pantalla mono*. (4) *Display (60)* and
*Original* get rows because their French, Italian or Spanish word differs (*Écran (60)*,
*Originale*); their German is the English word, so the German output is unchanged. (5) The
Credits' name lines with English joining words stay as written. (6) Dutch and Japanese
keep the English literal in `CustomText`; a language file of TR4's layout is not loaded
either. (7) The table stays the embedded copy, so that an executable copied alone keeps
its words; `extrastrings.txt` only goes before it. (8) *PS5 Controller* and *Xbox
Controller* stay raw English literals.

**Commits.** `e3a102d1` (the base), `7940a54f` (captions, buffer, pad words), `f0b77eea`
(French, Italian, Spanish words), `9a8ef033` (`extrastrings.txt`), `07e05c91` (Japanese
for the HQ audio).

### A second shell is never a guest of the visibility walk (#240)
2026-10-23

**What.** On the visibility path (`hd_vis` 1) the walk lists, beside the rooms the portals
reach, the guests: rooms whose art reaches out of their own room into a listed room. A
hull - a group whose art beyond its own room is for the most part a second copy of other
rooms' art (`MarkAirHulls`, `hd_render.cpp`) - is no longer listed so: `HDVisRoomGuests`
(`hd_level.cpp`) hands the walk the guest table without a hull's pairs (`g_vis_guests`,
`VisKeepGuests`, made once a level at the first walk, after the build has marked the
hulls). A hull is still listed by the portals, the openings and the wide portals. The
`HDLOG level= vis=1` line ends in `hull_guests=`, the pairs left out. RoomProbe's walk
takes `-visnoguest <group,...>` to do the same, since the walk alone builds no hull list;
the caller names the level's hulls (the `HDLOG hull` lines with `hull=1`).

**Why.** In RICH2's lift shaft, with `hd_air` 1 and 2, the shaft's art (group 61) was
drawn at the bottom of the shaft and flickered with the camera, textures lay doubled over
one another, the car's open door showed the shaft's front wall instead of the corridor,
and the lift's cables ran through the car (room 31). Group 61 is a hull: 51,475 of its
triangles stand in the air of rooms it has no link with, 36,285 of them where the host's
own art stands. Listed as a guest because its art box reaches into the car's inside and
the lower rooms, it was drawn whole, its copy of other rooms' art tying in depth with
theirs.

**How.** The rule: a guest is listed so that art no listed room draws, standing in a
listed room, is seen - a palm's crown through a doorway. A hull's art beyond its own room
is for the most part another room's art again, so listing a hull by its art lists a copy,
and what the copy holds that the room does not: a hull is listed by the portals, the
openings and the wide portals alone. Where a hull is listed by the portals, its air art
stays held to its window and pushed back by 1/512 of its distance (the hull push). The
rule changes nothing with `hd_vis` 0, `hd_air` 0 (no hulls), `hd_build` 0, `hd_marble` 0,
`hd_fog` 0 or on the classic path: it is in the visibility walk's guest accessor. Art only
the hull has - in RICH2's shaft the counterweight, the pulleys and the braced cage frames
in its middle - is no longer drawn from the rooms where the hull was only a guest.

**Decisions.** The rule leaves the guest table (`hd_vis.cpp`) and the walk
(`game/draw.cpp`) as they are and filters where the engine hands the table to the walk; a
hull is known only after the renderer's build, so the filtered list is made at the first
walk.

**Commits.** `408a4985` (the base), `741e5648` (no hull guests, `-visnoguest`).
