### A room's second shell is left out at the level build (#242)
2026-10-24

**What.** On the visibility path (`hd_vis` 1) the HD level build finds the art of a room
that is a second copy of other rooms' art and leaves it out of the level's index buffer
for good: `MarkSecondShells` (`hd_render.cpp`) runs before the hulls are marked and the
fill skips every triangle it marks, so the range table never sees them; `BuildShellRooms`
(`hd_level.cpp`) hands it the rooms' boxes, their flipmap twins and their floor squares'
air, and with `hd_vis` 0 hands nothing in. With `-log` one `HDLOG shell level= group=
host= tris= covered= exact= dropped=` line per pair the scans weighed (`refused=` and the
reason at its end when it was not taken whole), one `HDLOG shell level= group= rest= air=`
per group with a taken pair and one `HDLOG shell level= groups= pairs= dropped= rest=
air=` for the level; the `HDLOG hull` line ends in `shell=`, what the group lost.
RoomProbe takes `-shellscan` (the scans as a twin of the engine's code over the two files,
no device), `-shelldump` and `-shellgroups` (the triangles and their verdicts), `-shell
0|1` (the build with and without, on by default with `-vis 1`) and `-flipindex <n>` (the
walk and the picture with flip index n applied). ModernTest checks the rule's nine
numbers, that the scans examine every group, and the gate.

**Why.** In play RICH2's lift shaft looked as if it were doubled: with Lara standing still
and the camera turning, textures and lamps came and went on the walls, and looking down
the shaft from the lift car's roof a braced cage frame lay at the bottom that belongs on
the lift in room 61, gone when Lara came near it and lying over the fallen car after the
lift's fall. The frame is group 61's art: 14,922 triangles across the shaft at y -9,728 to
-10,300, 14,014 of them in the box of room 64, three floors below, drawn wherever 61 is
listed; it is not a moved copy of the car rooms.

**How.** Three scans over every group of a level (the sky's not asked); boxes are the
classic rooms' vertex boxes in world units, and a triangle stands where its centroid does.
*The pairs*: a group's triangles outside its own box widened by 64 and inside exactly one
other room's box widened by 16, a room with art of its own (the host); covered are those
in the plane of a triangle of the host's art (the normals within 0.98 in either direction,
within 16 of its plane and of its box widened by 16), exact those whose rounded corners
are a triangle of the host's. With 200 covered, a fifth of the pair or more and exact
under half of covered, the pair is a second shell and all of it drops. *The rest*: of a
group with such a pair, its triangles outside its box widened by 64 in no other box or in
several, within 512 of a host's box in x and z and 64 in y, covered by that host. *The
open air*: of the same group, its triangles outside its box in the open air of a room
standing in the hosts' column (its x and z box inside a host's widened by 512), no room of
the group's pair lines and no flipmap room - on a floor square with air, more than 32
below its ceiling and above its floor. There is no exemption by a group flag. For a host
with a flipmap twin, covered and exact ask the host's art and the twin's; a flipmap room's
pair drops only what every state of its host carries (covered by both, a twin with no art
carrying nothing), and a pair with the group's own twin nothing. A pair behind a mirror of
the group's room, and a pair whose host's box shares a face with the group's own, stay.
The scans examine every group of a level; over the fifteen levels they take 4 pairs and
12,158 triangles (9,064 pair triangles, 3,094 of the rest), none of them in the 37 groups
whose flag word carries the bit 0x40000; those are examined like every other group and
reach at most 54 covered triangles in one host against the pair's 200; no picture of the
probe's comparison sets changes.
The rule and its thresholds are TROne's - TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931 -; the code, the two refusals and the flipmap reading
are this project's (`THIRD-PARTY.md`, entry 480).

**Decisions.** The drop is the fill skipping the triangles, not a degenerate triple: the
range table, the index buffer and every count after the fill are made without them. The
hull census still counts the whole group, so a hull stays a hull and its remaining art is
drawn pushed back as before. The shared face is refused because the rooms' own art there
is the same surface but the walk shows those rooms through their doorway windows only, or
not at all, so dropping the copy left pixels with no art (in RICH2's shaft; in JOBY3 a
cloth over a machine was cut through, in ANDREA3 room 129's walls changed their light).
The mirror pair is refused because a room standing behind the washroom mirror (RICH2's 134
in 137) is the far half of its reflection. The open air asks no room of a pair line, taken
or refused: asking only the taken hosts' rooms let the air scan take the copies the shared
face keeps. With these refusals the shaft's top room keeps its copy of the floor directly
beneath (rooms 35, 37 and 38). A flipmap pair is not dropped while the other state's group
lacks the triangles, since dropped it leaves an opening with no art (RICH3's group 23 in
room 62, the alternate of 60), and drawing it in one state only would need a range per
state in the fill, which the fill does not keep; dropping what either state carries was
built and reverted for that reason. #240's rule stays: a hull is never a guest; with the
shells dropped its remaining art still ties where it would come in, and the lower rooms
would gain next to nothing back. The car's roof at the top (room 39) is not drawn from the
shaft's top room, since the walk never lists it from there: a walk question, outside this
rule.

**Commits.** `b848c417` (the base), `86812994` (scans, drop, refusals, logs, checks),
`60c92991` (the header comment), `fafa1b38` (flipmap: either state, reverted), `2d99daa5`
(flipmap: every state, `twin_covered=`).

### A room group stored too low is drawn at its world height (#243)
2026-10-24

**What.** A `.TRG` corner holds its y as an int16, absolute; a room group whose art
reaches above y -32,768 is held in the file a multiple of 16,384 too low, the corners that
still do not fit clamped at -32,768. On the visibility path (`hd_vis` 1) the level build
reads every room group's shift out of its classic room before anything reads the `.TRG`
(`BuildYShiftRooms` in `hd_level.cpp` hands the rooms' corners in, `HDYShiftScan` in
`hd_scan.h` counts them), and every reader of a corner's y reads the world y, the stored y
plus its group's shift: the hull census, the three shell scans, the pair faces, the cuts,
the stand and the places of the statics, the statics' covers (`hd_vis.cpp`), the mirrors,
the glow, the gloss seed (`hd_gloss_seed.h`), the water marks and the groups' bounds and
cells. The vertex buffer keeps the stored y, a short; the draw moves the group by its
shift (`GroupRow` in `prepare`, with the room origin's y, the surface and the lights,
which the shader compares with the vertex as it is held). A group's cells read back below
y -32,768 (`CellAxisOf`). In a shifted group the triangles whose three corners all sit at
the stored -32,768, the file's clamp, are dropped right after the count, before anything
reads the `.TRG` (`HDYShiftDropClamped`). With `-log` one `HDLOG yshift level= group=
shift= corners= unshifted= moved= clamped_dropped=` line per shifted group and one `HDLOG
yshift level= groups= of` line for the level. RoomProbe takes `-yshiftscan` (the count of
every room group of a level, no device), `-yshiftdump <path>` (the corners and triangles
of the groups with a shift or a near miss) and `-yshift 0|1` (on by default with `-vis 1`;
0 draws the file as stored), and its `-shellscan`, `-staticcover` and walk see the world
height. Separately, a lift door keeps its running delay while its pad is held: the lift
door's delay rule (`game/lift_door_rule.h`, asked from `game/control.cpp`), with 14
ModernTest checks of the condition case by case.

**Why.** In RICH2's lift shaft the art that belongs to room 61 was missing there, the
shaft still looked doubled in parts as the camera turned, and the floor art of the cars'
roof was missing - the braced decks, the turquoise anchor boxes and the pulleys that a
reference picture supplied for this project shows there. Above room 61 the classic shaft
converges, its meshes making it look so, while the HD shaft went on without them and
looked wrong. The cause was named by TROne (GPLv3) by Todesengel1931 -
https://github.com/todesengel1931: RICH2's group 61 lies in its `.TRG` 16,384 units too
low. Of its room's 112 distinct classic corners 98 lie in the group 16,384 lower; at its
world height it is the machine room in room 61's box, the decks with the anchor boxes and
the pulleys on the cars' roof plane, the cables down into the cars and the shaft going on
above. In the left lift the doors shut and never opened while Lara stood on the pad before
them, and an open door shut when she stepped back on.

**How.** Per room group g (room g's; the sky's groups have no room) the distinct classic
corners of room g are looked for among the group's corners at each shift k * 16,384, k =
-2..2: a corner counts at a shift when a group corner lies within 4 units of (x, y -
shift, z) on every axis, x and z room local on both sides. The best shift is taken when it
is not 0, has 16 hits or more and at least twice the hits of shift 0; otherwise the
group's shift is 0. The world y of every corner of the group is its stored y plus the
shift; a corner another group names keeps its stored y there. The rule and its thresholds
are TROne's (`THIRD-PARTY.md`, entry 481). Over the fifteen levels one group takes a
shift, RICH2's 61; RICH2's group 3, a tie (39 hits at 0 and 39 at 16,384 higher), keeps
its stored y. In a group with a shift, a triangle whose three corners all sit at the
stored -32,768 is dropped (29,272 in RICH2's group 61, a flat plate over the whole shaft
at -49,152 when drawn); one with one or two corners there keeps them as stored, so the
shaft's walls end open at that height (this project's own). The lift door: a trigger's
timer is not written into a lift door (`LIFT_DOORS1` to `LIFT_DOORS2`) that holds all its
code bits when the timer is negative, the hit is not heavy and the trigger is no switch,
heavy switch, antipad, antitrigger or heavy antitrigger (entry 482); the byte 253 is the
delay of 3.

**Decisions.** The shift is kept per group and added wherever a corner's y is read, not
made by copying the group's corners: the vendored reader's y stays an int16 (its code is
unchanged), so a copy could not hold -49,152, and the per-group shift needs no second
vertex array; a reader that compares a group's corners only with each other (a stacked
copy's key, a flow's height span, the coat of a flow range) needs none. The vertex buffer
holds the stored y and the group is drawn moved by its shift; a group with a shift and a
water sheet of its own would draw its sheet moved, which none of the fifteen levels has.
The shift is read on the visibility path only, like the shells: with `hd_vis` 0 nothing is
handed in, so `hd_build` 0 and `hd_vis` 0 are unchanged by construction. Whole group, not
per band or per piece: the 30 unshifted hits lie on tower pieces that are found at the
shift as well and have no piece of their own. The earlier shaft findings for RICH2 (#240,
#242) - the second shell of 61 in rooms 62 to 64, the cage at the shaft's bottom, the
frame over the fallen car, the bare car roofs and the pop-in - were this art 16 sectors
low; their rules stand and act on RICH2 at the world height, where 61 is no hull and no
shell pair of it is taken. The gloss seed reads the world y too, so the decks' page 12042
on the machine room's floor becomes a metal page of the seed; `hd_gloss_seed.h` is changed
for that reason alone. The clamp is dropped, not drawn: a triangle with all three corners
at the stored -32,768 is art above the storable range collapsed onto the int16 floor, not
art of its own, and the HD shaft has no such top (it goes on higher, as seen in play), so
a flat plate at -49,152 would be a lid the art never has. Only a group with a shift is
asked: in any other, -32,768 is a height like the rest. The lift door's commit changes the
classic path by design, in both looks: the condition is the trigger code's, not the
renderer's.

**Commits.** `06961e27` (the base), `a15c5a63` (the count, the rule), `373129fa` (the
shift in build and draw), `d02864b1` (the lift door), `c310ccec` (cells below y -32,768),
`58742450` (the record), `c7b543d2` (the clamp dropped).

### A hollow group's art is drawn where its room is listed (#245)
2026-10-25

**What.** On the visibility path (`hd_vis` 1) the art of a hollow group - a room's group
with triangles none of whose centroids stands in the room's own box widened by
`HD_OVERHANG_SLACK` - is drawn beside its classic room wherever the walk lists the room,
with the room's lighting, inside the union of the room's window and its hosts' windows,
and pushed back in depth (`hd_level.cpp`: `g_group_hollow`, set at the level build beside
`g_group_hd` for a hollow group of a room the randomizer did not mark; `HollowGroupOfRoom`
through the flip table; `HDFrameRoom` queues the group with `FrameRoomAdd` before the
classic rules answer for the faces; `FrameRoom::hollow` makes `DrawRoomWindowed` and
`DrawRoomShadowWindowed` draw the whole group inside its window, or nothing when the
window is empty; `g_hollow_host` set at the level build and `HollowWindows` once per frame
before the solid phase). The room stays classic: its faces are decided as every classic
room's are, and one more rule leaves them out - a room whose hollow art is drawn, none of
whose faces any art covers, standing enclosed in a linked room whose art stands in its
inside (`HDVisTables::enclosedBy`) draws none of its faces (`hd_vis.h`,
`HDVisClassicRoomEnclosed`, asked by `HDVisClassicRoomVerdict` with `hollowDrawn`), and
opens no sky (`HDVisRoomOpensSky`). The level build notes every hollow group and where its
art stands (`hd_render.cpp`, `NoteHollowGroups`; `HDRenderHollowGroups`,
`HDRenderHollowGroup`, `HDRenderHollowText`). With `-log` the `HDLOG room` line ends in
`drawn=` (1 for a room drawn HD or a hollow group drawn beside its room), one `HDLOG
hollow level= group= tris= art= own= rooms= none= in= grid_rooms= grid_none= grid= drawn=
hosts=` line per hollow group and one `HDLOG level= hollow groups= tris= drawn=` follow
the room lines, the `HDLOG level= vis=1` line ends in `hollow_hidden=`, the rooms whose
faces go, and with the clip line and on a ROOMLIST frame one `HDLOG hollowwin level= room=
group= own= drawn= took= hosts= full=` line is written per hollow group drawn
(`LogHollowWindows`). RoomProbe takes `-hollowlist` (the same lines from the build, and
per group its room's faces, portals, enclosing room, stand state and `hidden=`),
`-hollowdraw` (a hollow group drawn as the engine draws it) and `-hollowwin` (per hollow
group drawn its window, its art's screen box, its hosts' windows, `union=`, `took=`,
`union_full=`, `outside_union=` and the background pixels in that box); ModernTest checks
the enclosed rule, the verdict over the tables, the union and the push's wiring.

**Why.** In JOBY2's courtyard facade the broken-out holes of the two sniper rooms' glass
block windows showed black, with sky at their edges, where a reference picture supplied
for this project shows a texture, not black, in the room behind the window; with the art
drawn inside the room's own window, the sky still showed from below, in a strip under the
window's bottom edge, where the art was cut off at its room's window. The sniper rooms'
own art - the dark walls and the grate of bars behind the glass, groups 19 and 21 - is a
hollow group that the hollow rule never drew: a room deeper and wider than the classic one
(group 21's art reaches 1,024 units past the classic side walls and 409 past the far
wall), so the twelve classic faces stand inside it, in front of its walls, and no centroid
of it stands in any room's own box. The reading - a hollow group is art to be drawn with
its room, the classic faces are what has to leave the hole, and a triangle in another
room's box passes the clip against that room's rectangle too - is that of TROne (GPLv3) by
Todesengel1931 - https://github.com/todesengel1931 -, as read in its renderer by this
project for the comparison; no code of it is taken (`THIRD-PARTY.md`, entry 483).

**How.** A hollow group is drawn with its room, as every group is, on the visibility path,
and inside a window, because its art by its definition stands outside its room's own box,
where the walk shows the room only through that window. The window (`hd_vis.h`,
`HDVisHollowWindow`) is the union of the room's window and the windows of its hosts - the
rooms whose grids hold its triangles (`HDHollowGroup`'s `gridRoom`, the `grid=` of its
`HDLOG hollow` line) - that the frame's list holds with the same camera, each clipped as
every window is; a window of no width or height adds nothing; covering the backbuffer, the
art is drawn whole. It is one rectangle per group, as the walk joins a room's windows
itself, where TROne tests the clip per triangle. The hole seen from below is the opening
of room 146's art, whose edge from below is the hollow art's near face, 141 (group 19) and
149 (group 21) units behind the classic portal's plane, so it shows below the room's own
window and inside the host's. The art is drawn pushed back in depth by `HD_STAND_PUSH`, a
512th of its distance (`hd_render.cpp/.h`, `HDRenderRoomBehind`, asked by the draw and by
the shadow's receive): drawn in its hosts' windows its walls meet the facade in its plane
around the hole, and there the host's art is what stands; without the push the union drew
a dotted seam around the art's outline on the facade. The room keeps its classic verdict
(`g_group_hd` 0): the stand, cover, statics, shadow and air rules answer as before, so
ANDREA2's room 124 stays drawn as group 121's art where 121 is not listed. Of the faces,
the cover rule cannot take JOBY2's - the art stands 409 to 1,024 units behind them,
covering none - and the enclosure the visibility tables measure does: rooms 19 and 21
stand wholly in room 146's box, linked with it, 146's art in them with 160 and 177
triangles. Over the fifteen levels nine groups in ANDREA2, JOBY2, RICHCUT2 and TITLE are
hollow, the enclosed rule takes JOBY2's rooms 19 and 21 and no other, and JOBY2's 19 and
21 have four hosts each, TITLE's 70 and 101 one (room 87), the other five none. The hollow
art is no second shell for #242's scans: it stands in no room's own box (but one title
triangle in room 87's) and no pair reaches 200 covered triangles, so nothing of it drops.
Room 146's reveal (`HDStandDrawBaked`) is drawn in place with its group: its holder draws
no faces to stand in front of. `hd_build` 0, `hd_vis` 0, `hd_marble` 0 and `hd_fog` 0 are
unchanged by construction: `g_group_hollow` is set on the visibility path only,
`HollowGroupOfRoom` answers -1 elsewhere, `HollowWindows` changes nothing and
`HDRenderRoomBehind` is never turned on, and the renderer's notes only count; no classic
path file changed. A randomized level that marks a hollow room keeps it classic without
its art.

**Decisions.** The room is not made HD: drawing a hollow room as HD would drop the faces
of every hollow room, ANDREA2's 124 among them, whose floor only group 121 draws - the
black hole the hollow rule was made against. The enclosed rule comes back only for a room
whose hollow art is drawn, since without that art nothing but the sky was left in the
hole. Such a room opens no sky, its art closing what its faces closed. All twelve faces
go, the floor too: kept, it would show tile 2550 (half black, half clear) in the hole from
every view through the window, and from inside its clear texels near the window would
still show the courtyard through the facade's back; a rule by the camera's room was not
taken. TROne has no hollow verdict and draws no classic face in its HD view; this project
keeps its stand and cover rules, draws the hollow art inside the window and leaves the
faces out by the enclosure it measures. The window is widened to the hosts' windows rather
than drawing the art whole, so that the art stays held to where its rooms are seen; where
the one rectangle is wider than the hosts' windows together, the depth test holds the art
behind the hosts' walls.

**Commits.** `af7ac796` (the base), `f4aa9d01` (`hd_vis.h`: the title's triangles),
`f72c2329` (`NoteHollowGroups`, `-hollowlist`), `c3670132` (the rule, logs,
`-hollowdraw`), `6ff54e2b` (the records), `a64fa48e` (`hd_vis.h`'s comments), `6c9c3762`
(the first rule merged), `34dd1ae4` (the push), `c7a3bb62` (RoomProbe `-hollowwin`),
`fd9270a3` (the union, logs, checks).

### The record as a licence notice, the shell scans without an exemption, Beta 4.0 (#246)
2026-10-25

**What.** The change record, the origin ledger, the manuals and the READMEs are brought
back to what an outside reader needs: what was changed, when, why and how. Every entry of
this record has one form (What, Why, How, Decisions where a choice was made, Commits);
the measurements, rounds and reviews behind the entries live outside the repository.
Section 2.9 keeps the cleanup before the first public push and section 2.10 holds the
rounds after it; the randomizer-only tasks #214, #223 and #244 are rows of section 3,
#230's randomizer half has its row, and the appendix maps every task number of a commit
subject to its entry. In the engine the second-shell scans of the level build
(`hd_render.cpp`, `MarkSecondShells`; `hd_level.cpp`) examine every group of a level: the
exemption of groups carrying the flag `0x40000` is gone, with its `flagged=` field of the
`HDLOG shell level=` line and of RoomProbe's level line. The four places that carry a
rule read in TROne name its credit in the ledger's form (`hd_render.cpp/.h`, the shells;
`hd_level.cpp` with `hd_vis.h`, a hollow group's window; `hd_scan.h`; `game/
lift_door_rule.h`), and `tomb5.vcxproj` with its filters file lists `game/
lift_door_rule.h` and `specific/hd/hd_install_names.h`. The picture
`docs/hd-loading-screen.jpg` and its caption are removed from the README. The version is
Beta 4.0 (`tomb5.rc`, `TR5Randomizer.rc`, `BuildId.h`, the READMEs and the manuals; the
randomizer's build id stays 21).

**Why.** The record had grown from 6,090 lines at the first public push to 34,200: more
than half of it narrated rounds, reviews and per-view measurements that mean nothing
outside the sessions that produced them, and some of it named the pictures and logs of a
play test. A change record under GPLv3 section 5(a) owes a reader the modifications and
their dates, not the work's diary. The flag exemption rested on a reading of the flag's
meaning that no measurement of this project had made; measured, the 37 flagged groups of
the fifteen levels form no pair and change no view, so the scans need no exemption. The
loading-screen picture showed one painted artwork of the player's Remaster almost full
frame; the README shows this engine's own output.

**How.** The entries were rewritten one by one against their earlier text, every commit
hash kept, every constant that carries a rule kept with its reason; the origin ledger's
entries were trimmed to the measurement facts in their classes; section 1 states the
form. The scans: `MarkSecondShells` and `BuildShellRooms` take every group through the
pair, rest and air rules unchanged (4 pairs and 12,158 triangles over the fifteen
levels, as before; the 37 formerly exempt groups reach at most 54 covered triangles in
one host against the pair's 200); `HDRenderShellCounts` has no flagged argument;
ModernTest's shell checks test the rule as it stands.

**Decisions.** The record's measurements are not kept in an archive file of the
repository: they are reproducible with the tools and switches the entries name. The
TROne rule of the second shells and its thresholds stay credited; only the flag's
reading goes. The flag is not read anywhere in the engine any more.

**Commits.** `eb035afc` (the scans ask every group), `6e93d0e5` (the credit lines, the two
headers in the project), `22c00a7c` (the tools' README), `33c2ae5d` (the record,
the ledger, the manuals and the version).

### The window and the resolution (#247)
2026-10-26

**What.** In the windowed state the game window is an ordinary overlapped window: caption,
system menu, minimize, maximize and close buttons and a sizing frame. It moves, sizes at
every edge and corner, maximizes, snaps, minimizes and restores, and the back buffer takes
the client's size when a drag of the frame ends and at once on maximize, restore and snap;
the smallest client is 640x480. The window opens where it was last left when that place
still lies on a connected monitor's work area, maximized again when it was; otherwise at
the setup dialog's resolution, made small enough that the whole window fits the work area
of the adapter's monitor, and centred on it. In the window Alt+Plus and Alt+Minus step the
client from its own size to the next larger or smaller entry of the mode list that fits
the monitor's work area, the window keeping its centre; in full screen they change
nothing and log one line. The place is stored in the registry under `System` as
`WindowLeft`, `WindowTop`, `WindowWidth`, `WindowHeight` and `WindowMaximized`. The setup
dialog opens with the stored choices of every control, its defaults only where nothing is
stored. Full screen is unchanged: a border-less window over the adapter's monitor at the
desktop's size.

**Why.** The windowed state sized its client to the desktop and grew a frame without
sizing border, maximize box or system menu round it at 0,0, so that the window was taller
than the screen and Windows pulled it back to the bottom edge whenever it was dragged.
Alt+Plus and Alt+Minus made a new device of the same size, because a border-less full
screen window renders at the desktop's size whatever the mode list says.

**How.** `specific/windowplace.h` holds the arithmetic free of Windows calls:
`WinPlaceFit`, `WinPlaceMinWindow`, `WinPlaceCentre`, `WinPlaceAround`, `WinPlaceUsable`
(a remembered client rectangle whose window, less the sizing border, lies inside one work
area) and `WinPlaceStep` (the mode list judged by area against the client, one colour
depth, the work area as the upper limit). `specific/devicewindow.h` gives the windowed
state the whole `WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW` style with `SWP_FRAMECHANGED`, hands the monitors'
work areas and the frame to that arithmetic and puts the window round a client.
`specific/dxshell.cpp`: `DXCreate` places the windowed state (`DXPlaceWindow`, from
`DXWindowPlace`) and sizes the back buffer from the client; `DXResizeToClient` makes the
device anew the way Alt+Enter does, so the HD level is released with the old device and
built again on the new one (`MoveTexturesToDevice`), and when a device of the new size is
refused it tries the old size; a recreate that released the old device and could not make
the next leaves the classic pages to be moved by the attempt after it
(`dx_pages_waiting`); `DXWindowBusy` marks the window's own placements;
`DXChangeVideoMode`, which no key calls any more, is gone. `specific/winmain.cpp`:
`WM_SIZE` outside a drag and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` take a new size with the game thread held
at the start of its scene, followed by `InitWindow` with the field of view kept,
`InitFont` and the matrices; a size that cannot be taken at once (the thread parked while
the window is inactive, a film, a level load) waits for a timer; `SIZE_MINIMIZED` resizes
nothing; `WM_GETMINMAXINFO` holds the smallest client; `SC_KEYMENU` is swallowed, so that
a tap of Alt does not enter the system menu (Alt+Space still opens it); `WM_CLOSE` stores
the place and takes the close path as before; Alt+Enter, the keys and a new size end in
the same `WinRenderSize`. `specific/registry.cpp`: `REG_ReadWindowPlace` and
`REG_WriteWindowPlace` use a key of their own, and `SaveSetup` drops the place when the
dialog's resolution changes. `specific/setupdlg.cpp`: `LoadStoredChoices` reads `DD`,
`VMode`, `Window`, `Filter`, `TextLow`, `NoFMV` and `DisableSound` through `REG_PeekLong`,
which creates nothing. New `-log` lines: `DXLOG window place`, `stored`, `resize` (with
the whole recreate's milliseconds) and `keys`. ModernTest's group `window_place` checks
the arithmetic with made-up monitors, work areas, mode lists and remembered rectangles (25
checks). No file of the drawing code changed (`game/` and `specific/hd/` are untouched),
so the pictures of `hd_build` 0 and 1, `hd_vis`, `hd_marble` and `hd_fog` are the previous
ones by construction.

**Decisions.** Full screen stays at the desktop's size: a real mode switch is what the
border-less window replaced, and its keys do nothing there. The picture takes the new size
at the end of a drag, not during it, since every new size is a new device with the HD
level built again; during the drag the last picture stretches. The recreate path is taken
over a `Reset`: a reset needs every `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT` object released as well and the
reset path leaves the HD level away until the next level load, so the HD build, which is
the cost either way, would have to be added there. A resolution chosen anew in the setup
dialog is the window's size at the next start, so it drops the remembered place.

**Commits.** `dc646d02` (the arithmetic and its tests), `f46ebf6e` (the window, the keys
and the remembered place), `1931a40a` (the dialog), `74d93b7c` (the manual, the tools'
README and this entry), `cc2f6bf9` (the pages after a refused device), `ce96392b` and
`02252971` (`DXChangeVideoMode` removed; the second commit removes a stray line the first
left, which kept `dxshell.cpp` from compiling at `ce96392b`), `6e29d3f6` (this list) and
`9c501b5d` (the manual's stale line on the dialog's defaults removed, the resize log line
once per wait, Alt+Space opens the system menu).

**The last step up (#254).** Past the last entry of the mode list that fits the work area,
Alt+Plus takes the largest client the work area holds, the size Maximize gives; the
dialog's entry stays, and the `DXLOG window keys` line says `mode=-1`. Commit `23b54aab`.

### The cursor lets go while the window is moved or sized (#252)

2026-10-27.

**What.** While the player drags the window by its caption or sizes it by its frame, the
cursor is free; the clip that holds it inside the client under *Modern* control returns
when the drag ends.

**Why.** The clip followed the client on every move. During a drag by the caption it
pushed the cursor into the client, Windows moved the window after the cursor, and the
window ran to the bottom edge of the screen; during a drag by the frame the edge followed
the cursor inward until the window stood at its smallest size.

**How.** `specific/winmain.cpp`: `WinMouseCapture` reads the time between
`WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE` and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` as a term that turns the clip off, and both
messages call it, so the cursor is released when the drag starts and seated again when it
ends. `docs/Engine-Manual.md` says so.

**Commits.** `328d7bc5`.

### A click in the picture takes the mouse back (#253)

2026-10-27.

**What.** From the moment the player clicks the window's caption, frame or a button, the
cursor stays free: a second adjustment and the close button work without leaving the
window first. A click into the picture, or a return by the keyboard, seats the cursor
again; so does Alt+Enter.

**Why.** The clip returned the instant a drag ended or the window became active, so the
close button and a second adjustment were out of reach until the window had been left and
re-entered by the keyboard.

**How.** `specific/winmain.cpp`: a term `mouse_free`, set at the end of a drag and when a
click activates the window outside the client (`WM_NCHITTEST` on the cursor at
`WA_CLICKACTIVE`), cleared by a client click, by `WA_ACTIVE` and by Alt+Enter; while it
stands, `WinMouseCapture` keeps the clip off and `WinMouseInput` counts neither buttons
nor moves, so the click that takes the mouse back is not a shot. The `MOUSELOG capture`
line ends with `free=`. `docs/Engine-Manual.md` says so.

**Commits.** `1d96c038` and `41c9e7b8` (the second makes the first build: the term was
declared after the Alt+Enter handler that clears it, which now goes through a function).

### The game ends when its window is closed from the taskbar (#255)

2026-10-27.

**What.** Closing the window while it is in the background - from the taskbar's thumbnail,
or by any other way that reaches an inactive window - ends the game like the close button
of an active one.

**Why.** An inactive window has the game thread parked (`WM_ACTIVATE` suspends it). The
close path asked that thread to leave and waited for it; a parked thread never leaves, so
the wait at the end of `WinMain` spun for ever, the window was gone, the music played on,
and only the task manager could end the process.

**How.** `specific/winmain.cpp`: `WM_CLOSE` wakes a parked game thread before it posts the
quit; the wait at the end of `WinMain` sleeps instead of spinning and gives up after five
seconds with `ExitProcess`, so a thread stuck anywhere cannot hold the process either.

**Commits.** `7b77e0ea`.

### The visibility path's room walk ends (#256)

2026-10-27.

**What.** A camera position from which the visibility path's room walk never ended - the
game thread spinning in `GetRoomBounds`, the window frozen, the music playing on - ends
like any other: the walk lists its rooms and the frame is drawn. Seen with `hd_vis 1` at
ANDY1 rooms 121 and 113 and ANDREA2 room 69, independent of the seed.

**Why.** `VisQueue` keeps a room's window in whole pixels but tested what the room already
held on the float rectangle. A right or bottom edge with a fraction - 1326.3, stored as
1326 - was never held, so the room was queued again with the same window at every visit;
and where the path's sources - guests, openings, near portals, wide and edge portals -
form a ring of rooms, every dequeue queued the next, for ever. The dump of a hung process
showed 25.7 million dequeues of one frame and six rooms circling, one of them with a
window narrower than a pixel. The classic walk is not affected: `SetRoomBounds` tests the
parent's window, whole pixels against whole pixels.

**How.** `game/draw.cpp`: `VisQueue` makes its test on the whole pixels it stores and
refuses a rectangle that is empty in whole pixels; `GetRoomBounds` cuts a walk past 32
dequeues per room of the level (4,096 at the least), releasing the rooms still queued, and
the count goes out on a `ROOMWALK runaway=` line that must never appear.
`docs/Engine-Manual.md` says how a freeze is reported. `hd_vis 0` is untouched.

**Commits.** `67e2445b`.

### A frozen game names where its thread stands (#257)

2026-10-27.

**What.** When the game thread stops answering - the picture frozen, the window alive -
the engine writes where that thread stands and a minidump, the way it does for a crash:
`HANG at=0x... module=PCtomb5.exe+0x... thread=game id=0x... when=focus|close`, then `HANG
dump=<file>` with `PCtomb5_hang_<date>_<time>.dmp` beside the log, or into `crash.txt`
without `-log`. `when=focus`: the window lost the focus, the game thread never reached its
frame wait, and thirty seconds passed without a frame. `when=close`: the window was closed
and the thread did not end in five seconds.

**Why.** A freeze leaves no trace a crash leaves: no exception, so the crash seam never
runs, and the log stops at the last seam written, which says where the game was, not where
it stays. The hang of #256 was found only through a dump taken by hand from the task
manager; a report from another machine has no such dump.

**How.** `specific/crashseam.h`: the crash seam's tail - the line, the dump, `crash.txt` -
becomes `CrashSeamReport`, shared with the new `CrashSeamHang`, which suspends the named
thread for the read of its instruction pointer, resumes it before anything that takes a
lock, and reports; the crash's own line and file name are unchanged.
`specific/winmain.cpp`: a watch thread starts where the focus loss finds the game thread
stuck (`Game Thread appeared stuck`) and asks once a second whether a frame was presented
since, the thread parked after all, the window closing, or a level loading; thirty seconds
without any of that (sixty while loading) capture, once per process. The close path
captures after its five seconds unless a level is loading. `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`:
`HDFramesPresented`, the frame count the watch reads, moving with or without `-log`.
`specific/file.cpp`: `g_level_loading`, 1 while `S_LoadLevelFile` runs. `RoomProbe -hang
<folder>` is the seam's own test, beside `-crash`: the tool runs itself with a circling
thread, reads the `HANG` line back and checks the dump. `docs/Engine-Manual.md` says what
to send.

**Commits.** `7b23e79e`.

4; none of them is bound here.

**Why.** (a) The art that models the benches is the underfloor room's, group 123, whose
box ends at the mess hall's floor line; the classic bench stands on that line, and the

`docs/Engine-Manual.md` says what the grilles show.

### The suit's console states and Lara's legs inside the suit (#262)

2026-10-29.

**What.** The top of the diving suit at room 40's console in JOBY3 shows the console as
the puzzle stands: the empty bezel with its plate until the player has put anything in,
the console with the battery's slot empty once the console is in, the whole console once
the battery is. In the two cutscenes that put the suit on Lara and take it off again her
legs stay hidden whatever outfit she wears. The outfit menu no longer offers Russia
Extra, the install's Russia body without legs made for those two cutscenes.

**Why.** The top was bound to the half-filled file, so the console stood in place before
the player had found it. The classic slot is a pair per item, and a hole turns into its
done slot in place when its item goes in: PUZZLE_HOLE3's mesh is the empty frame,
PUZZLE_HOLE4's is PUZZLE_DONE3's 76 vertices with every face on 16 transparent texels,
so it draws nothing, PUZZLE_DONE3 is the console with the battery's slot empty and
PUZZLE_DONE4 the console with the battery. The three top files are those looks: every
vertex of the plain one is in the other two, which add 825 and 1297 vertices inside the
holes' box. Her legs: the game hides them with the mesh bits 0x81FF01FF from frame 542
of JOBY3's cutscene 5 and up to frame 440 of JOBY5's cutscene 32. DrawLara__1 reads the
bits, the catsuit's and the diving suit's variants do not, and the HD seam honoured them
for __1 alone - so with the randomizer's catsuit in JOBY5 the HD body showed its legs
bent backwards in the air beside the suit's. Russia Extra has no vertex on her six leg
nodes; worn in play she walks without legs.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_bind.cpp`: the top binds the plain file, and the table of DUMMY
hosts names for each hole the slot it becomes and the top's model from then on
(`HDBindGuestStates`). `specific/hd/hd_object.cpp` loads the two other files as the
top's alternative models, as the cyborg's stages are loaded, and picks one per drawn
frame by the object numbers of the items at the top's place; the last done hole in the
table's order decides. The bind, dummy and swap lines name the states, and an
`HDLOG guests` line the state drawn, at the first draw and on every change.
`specific/hd/hd_lara.cpp`: `HDLaraNodesShown`, DrawLara__1's own test on a mesh-bits
word; `specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp` masks every body with it, ends the `SWAPLOG` line
in the hidden nodes and writes a `HIDELOG` line on every change no swap line carries.
No level or cutscene table is needed: the classic data hides exactly these nodes, and
Russia Extra lacks the same six. `specific/hd/hd_wardrobe.cpp`: an entry is offered
unless a table names its file; `specific/hd/hd_outfitmenu.cpp` lists the offered ones,
and a registry choice of another falls back to the level's facts. ModelProbe takes
`-larabits <bits>` and draws her as such a word leaves her. `docs/Engine-Manual.md`
says all three. The verdict census over the fifteen levels changes in the top's row
alone. With `hd_build` 0 none of it runs.

### The title menu's sliders follow the pad (#264)

2026-10-29.

**What.** On the title screen the six sliders of the options pages follow the stick, the
d-pad and the direction keys of the active layout, as they do in the pause menu; before,
only the arrow keys moved them there, at every frame rate. With `-log` a `MENULOG slider`
line names the way a selected slider is held, the hand holding it and the title's input
shadow.

**Why.** A slider reads the held word beside the raw arrow keys, and it read `input`. On
the title screen ControlPhase masks `input` down to `IN_LOOK` after every `S_UpdateInput`
while bDisableLaraControl stands and zeroes it while a cutscene runs; `dbinput` it keeps
for the title alone (`game/control.cpp`). The title's flybys raise the flag in game mode 1
(`InitialiseSpotCam`, `game/spotcam.cpp`), the title's mode from the start of the game; a
title reached from a level has it from its first cutscene on, and none of the title's 55
cameras lowers it. So the word never brought the slider a direction there, and the arrow
keys reached it only through `keymap`; the value rows step on `dbinput` and worked. The
pause menu calls `S_UpdateInput` itself, outside ControlPhase, so in a level `input`
carried the pad's bits. The title's input shadow (`TitleInputShadow`) is not the cause: at
30 frames a second it never acts.

**How.** `game/menu_frame.cpp`: `MenuSliderDir` reads `inputBusy`, the word
`S_UpdateInput` writes for every caller before any caller's mask, beside the two arrow
keys, through `MenuSliderHeldDir` (`game/menu_nav.h`). In a level `input` and `inputBusy`
carry the same two direction bits - the one mask between them, under `lara.Busy`, keeps
both - so the pause menu reads what it read before. On a title present without a game
step the shadow still zeroes `input` and `dbinput` and leaves `inputBusy` standing, as it
leaves `keymap`: a held slider moves on every present by key and pad alike, and every edge
is still read once. The value rows, the ring and `do_debounced_joystick_poo` are
untouched. `MenuLogSlider` writes the line - `dir=`, `src=` (`key`, `pad`, `pad+key` or
`-`, from `MenuSliderHands`) and `shadow=` - once per change and never while both stay;
for it alone `specific/input.cpp` keeps the pad pair's own direction bits of the last call
(`InputPadDirection`) and `game/gameflow.cpp` the shadow of the running `TitleOptions`
call (`TitleInputShadowed`). MenuTest's `slider_held_word` holds the rule;
`docs/Engine-Manual.md` says it.

**Commits.** `f8b6a5a1`.

### An item the randomizer adds is drawn, its slot baked or not (#265)

2026-10-29.

**What.** An item the randomizer puts into a level is drawn in an HD room whatever its
slot: as every item of its slot draws - HD where the slot binds a model, classic where
none binds - and classic where the level's `.MAP` calls the slot `DUMMY`. The shelf
(SEARCH_OBJECT3) that the glitchless secret list adds to JOBY3's bunk room 52, around the
secret it moves there, stood invisible in HD and now draws its classic mesh, with its
search animation and the secret inside. The level's eight vanilla shelves still draw
nothing, because the art carries them.

**Why.** The `DUMMY` rule marks a slot baked, and `begin_decision` answered BEGIN_BAKED
for every item of a baked slot in an HD room: right for the items Core placed, which the
remaster baked into the room art, wrong for one the run added, which the art has not got.
The mark is per slot, the art's copies are per place. Counted with `TrgProbe -boxes` in
each item's classic box (its first frame's bounds at its place and yaw, as
`HDStandItemBox` makes it): 34 of the remaster's triangles in the added shelf's box in
room 52, a strip of the room's wall at 256-unit steps, against 5,435 to 5,469 in each of
the eight vanilla boxes in rooms 26, 107, 139 and 164 - the shelf itself. No level's
`.MAP` names a model for the slot (four call it `DUMMY`, eleven are silent) and neither
model folder holds a SEARCH_OBJECT3.TRM, so classic is its only look and there is no
donor road. A slot that binds a model drew every item already, added ones included:
ANDY3's slot 284 binds `DOOR_TYPE3_ANDY2_ANDY3`, and both doors its secret list makes of
it, item 13 retyped and one added, draw HD. Only the randomizer knows which items it
added; a table by level or a box heuristic would not survive the next list.

**How.** On the writing side, `TR5Randomizer/src/core/Tr5Level.cpp`/`.h` record every
index `addItem` appends - the one way an item gets into a level, for the roll's extra
enemies and pickups and a secret list's `add` lines alike; nothing is ever inserted before
an item or removed, so the index is the item's index in the saved file - and
`core/ApplyPatch.cpp` writes one `item <index>` line each, ascending, at the end of the
`.hdm`. The line needs no version: an engine that predates it counts each as a line it
has no rule for and draws the item as before. `specific/hd/hd_markers.cpp`/`.h` read it
(`HDMarkersItemAdded`). `specific/hd/hd_object.cpp`: `begin_decision` no longer answers
BEGIN_BAKED for an item the sidecar names (`item_run_added`, an index of `items[]` below
`level_items`), so the item reaches the guard and draws as a slot without a model draws,
classic; the objects' build writes an `HDLOG level=... added item=...` line for each
added item of a baked slot, whether `hd_objects` is on or off. `specific/hd/hd_level.cpp`:
`BuildBakedBoxes` leaves such an item out of the boxes of the art's objects, and the
`markers` summary line ends in `items=`. `MapProbe -hdm` answers each `item` line with
its slot, room and drawing, `HdmDump` lists them, and RoomProbe's copy of
`BuildBakedBoxes` leaves them out too; `docs/Engine-Manual.md` and
`docs/Randomizer-Manual.md` say it. The same seed 380 through the randomizer before and
after, over the thirteen campaign levels plain and with `mix cross allsanity 8 weapons
items20 weather` and the glitchless list: every `.trc` and log byte-identical, every
`.hdm` the old file plus its `item` lines. The verdict census over the fifteen levels is
unchanged. With `hd_build` 0 nothing of it runs - no HD room, no baked answer - and a
level without a sidecar, or with one written before the line, draws as before.

**Commits.** `c8cb7cd0`, `0ae57756`.

the speech heads are the same mechanism on a face. An HD model is drawn out of its own
file whatever the table says.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_object.cpp` keeps the mesh table as the level loaded it,
after `InitialiseObjects` (`HDObjectMeshTableTake`, called by `HDLevelLoad` with the HD
path on); a node whose drawn mesh is not that entry has borrowed it from the slot whose
own mesh it was, Lara's slots first and then slot order. A mesh of one of Lara's slots
and a mesh on the node a separate HD face rides on are speech heads and are not
borrowed. `HDObjectCutActor`, called by `DrawCutSeqActors` before `HDObjectBegin` with
one pointer compare per node, decides per node and per frame: the install's model of
the actor in that state where it ships one, a new swap kind keyed on the model name and
the set of borrowed nodes (PIERRE_SWAP for node 11, PATRICK_1_TORCH and
PATRICK_2_TORCH for node 8, TWOGUN_LEFT for node 5 and TWOGUN_EMPTY for 5 and 8,
measured node by node with ModelProbe `-name -nodes`); else, where the lending slot's
model draws HD and has geometry on that node, the node of that model hung rigidly on
the actor's node in its bind pose (`specific/hd/hd_model.cpp`, `HDModelBorrowJoints`)
with the actor's light, and the actor's own node left out; else the actor's own node.
The classic mesh is never drawn into an HD body: it is the whole node, a hand with the
thing in it, and the swap rule refuses that patchwork. `specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp`
does the second rule for Lara while a cutscene plays, out of the same table;
`specific/hd/hd_bind.cpp`'s hand table binds the four holder slots to the install's
hand files: CROW_MIP in ANDY1 to HAND_BARE_CATAPULT, MESHSWAP2 in ANDY1 to
HAND_BARE_IRON_CLAPPER, MESHSWAP3 in RICH1 to HAND_BARE_HAMMER, MAFIA_MIP in ANDY3 to
HAND_BARE_CHALK - holders with her fifteen-node tree and no item, each file's hand bone
10 to 25 units from the holder's mesh. The suit's hips have no model and stay her
own, as #261 left them. The state models, the lending slot's node and the prop hands
are TROne's rules. `HDLOG cutseq actor` ends in `swap=`, every borrowed node with its
slot, mesh and what drew it; a change later in the cutscene writes `HDLOG cutswap`;
`SWAPLOG` ends in `shows=` and finds a mesh's slot in the load-time table, which also
names the catapult's holder after the exchange. ModelProbe takes `-meshes` and
`-borrow`. The verdict census over the fifteen levels changes in the four holders' rows
alone, from classic to `hand`. With `hd_build` 0 nothing of it runs.

**Commits.** `aa2732b2`.

2026-10-29.

**What.** On the classic path the two thigh holsters are drawn only while the thigh
each hangs on is shown: in the two cutscenes that hide Lara's legs inside the diving
suit's, from frame 542 of JOBY3's cutscene 5 and up to frame 440 of JOBY5's cutscene 32,
they go with her legs, in the classic outfit as in the catsuit. A seam piece the
skinning leaves out no longer shifts the pieces after it. The `SWAPLOG` and `HIDELOG`
lines of the classic draw end in the holsters it drew, the loader's
`OBJLOG skinning done` line in the seam pieces it sewed and left out.

**Why.** DrawLara__1 and the catsuit's DrawLara__4 drew the holsters on the thighs'
matrices with no test of her mesh bits, so with the word 0x81FF01FF, which hides nodes 1
to 6, they hung at thighs that are not drawn - in the shipped game as well, whose two
levels dress her through __1. The HD composite masks its holster rig, which covers the
belt and both thighs, with the nodes the bits show. The joint loops of __1, __4 and the
skeleton's __6 leave out a seam piece whose seam found nothing to sew by `continue`, and
the step to the next piece's mesh stood at the end of the loop's body: after a piece
left out, every later seam drew the piece of a seam before it on its own rim - the
left-out piece among them - and the last seam's own piece was not drawn.

**How.** `specific/drawlara.cpp`: `LaraHolstersDrawn` gives the holsters of the frame,
each by __1's own skin test, `mesh_bits >> 0x10 & 1 << (15 - i)`, with i the place of
`LM_LTHIGH` or `LM_RTHIGH` in `lara_mesh_sweetness_table` - 1 and 4, the places whose
matrices, `LMX_THIGH_L` and `LMX_THIGH_R`, the holsters are drawn with - inside the
draws' own brackets: none on young Lara, and for __4 both holster slots loaded. With the
bits at -1 both thighs are shown and the holsters are drawn as before; the two cutscenes,

loops take the step before `continue`, so a piece left out is still neither drawn nor

### Lara in the X-ray scanner and the X-ray outfit, in HD (#268)

2026-10-29 to 2026-10-30.

**What.** The scanner in Escape with the Iris X-rays Lara, and with the HD path she is now
drawn there in the remaster's X-ray set: a translucent green body over solid bones, its
own skull and headset, X-ray hands, no braid and no face. The X-ray outfit of the outfit
menu wears the same set wherever it is worn; it showed her braid, her face, her bare hands
and solid black guns on the translucent body. The body's shell is drawn from the front
alone: the figure is green with its bones readable where it was white, and in a bright
room it stays a pale green over visible bones instead of a white outline. Every part of
the set - the shell, the bones, the hands with what they hold, the holsters and the weapon
on the back - takes one darker, greener tone, and no piece of it looks like ordinary gear
beside the body.

**Why.** The scanner's 36 squares, in rooms 11 and 151 of RICH2 and nowhere else in the
fifteen levels, set `lara.skelebob` for every frame she stands on one, and DrawLara hands
such a frame to DrawLara__6, which the HD seam did not touch: the classic X-ray body - her
skin translucent, LARA_EXTRA_MESH1's bones solid, the HK and the grappling gun as the
level's own X-ray meshes (game\draw.cpp, SetupSkelebobMeshswaps) - stood in the HD world.
The remaster ships the look as files of its own in 4\ITEM: OUTFIT_XRAY, fifteen nodes, its
bones in the opaque run and the body's shell in the additive run (material 6), its skull
on node 14; thirty HAND_XRAY_ files, one for every HAND_BARE_ one; seven HOLSTER_*_XRAY
files, none for the uzis or the Desert Eagle; no X-ray head and no X-ray braid. Worn from
the outfit menu, OUTFIT_XRAY took the outfit's other parts: LARA_HEAD's face over its
skull, HAIR_OG, the bare hands and the plain holsters. Drawn from both sides like every HD
model, the closed shell lay on every pixel twice, and the back half added a second, whiter
layer - at full light 121/86/127 over the front layer's 112/163/117 on the abdomen - which
turned the figure white in a bright room and hid the bones. The classic adds every face of
its X-ray body single sided (specific\output.cpp, phd_PutPolygonsSpcXLU, double_sided 0).
Page 8030's alpha is 240 or more on every texel, so the additive pass's weight by alpha
changes nothing, and the part's param[0] of 0.5 is the alpha reference of material 6, not
a weight. Beside the shell the opaque parts were lit as ordinary gear, up to twice the
light where the shell stops at its full value and the holsters with a gunmetal sheen, and
the figure added more light than the reference: in the same flooded tunnel the shell adds
61.6/82.2/83.9 to the wall behind her belly, the reference pictures of the remaster's
X-ray Lara 41.2/60.7/32.3 (the mean of a front and a side view).

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_lara.cpp`: a table names the X-ray set part by part (`kXray`) -
OUTFIT_XRAY, the eleven HAND_XRAY_ parts, HOLSTER_PISTOL_XRAY and the three weapons on the
back - and a part without a row draws nothing in the X-ray look: no face, braid, borrowed
head or holster rig, no uzi or Desert Eagle holster. An outfit whose body is OUTFIT_XRAY
takes the set as its own parts. In a level whose floor carries a SKELETON trigger the set
is planned beside the outfit in a block of slots of its own, on the same slot list and
bind pose (eight models in RICH2), and `HDLaraFrameParts` lists its parts on request.
`specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp` counts the trigger's squares at the level build and, while
`lara.skelebob` holds, draws the body and what she holds and wears out of that block, the
body with its own sheen and its own node 14; an `XRAYLOG` line names the look's edges and
the models it put on, `HDLOG lara xray` lines the set. `specific/drawlara.cpp`:
DrawLara__6 hands the frame to the composite when it has the set (`HDLaraDrawXray`), with
her blob and her light as DrawLara__1 has them and her own hands and back gun put back for
the length of the draw, and otherwise draws the classic figure as before. The translucency
is the file's own additive run through `hd_model`'s additive pass, as every additive part
is drawn (one plus one, no depth write, weighed by the texel's alpha): the green of the
figure is the art's own and the room's light, and no shader changed.
`specific/hd/hd_object.cpp` makes room for the block in the plan. The rule is TROne's
(TROne-main, copy of 2026-10-23, commit a3c0c633: S_InitialisePolyList in
`hostglue_draw5.cpp`, `lara_build_models` and `lara_head_for_outfit` in

for every part of the X-ray set, in the level's block and on an outfit that is the X-ray
body. The bones stay two-sided, because their right half is wound the other way round.
Every other model keeps both sides, its additive runs included: the classic draws those by
each face's own double-sided flag, which a .TRM does not carry.
`specific/hd/hd_model.cpp`: a model whose plan entry asks for it
(`HDModelSlot::lightAsAdditive`) draws its other runs with the pixel shader's own additive
switches - the light held under 1.0, no sheen, weighed by the alpha, a glow under the
water; `hd_lara.cpp` asks for it for every part of the X-ray set. `hd_lara.cpp` keeps the
set's tone, a choice made from the reference pictures and written down there with its

### Cut-out cards back to back are one-sided; a hanging guest is refused (#269)

2026-10-29.

**What.** Two rules of the HD level build on the visibility path (`hd_vis` 1). A cut-out
card - a triangle of the opaque pass with an alpha test, or of the alpha pass but for its
glass, never water - that lies wholly on cut-out cards of another group drawn with it,
facing the other way, is drawn one-sided, culled as an opaque range is
(`specific/hd/hd_render.cpp`: `MarkBackToBackCards`, run after `MarkSecondShells`;
`g_card_cull`, read by the fill into `HDTri::cull`, so the marked cards get draw calls of
their own). And a room under the sky no longer takes as its guest the art of a room it has
no link with when that art hangs below the other room, inside its floor plan, and that
room is not under the sky (`specific/hd/hd_vis.cpp`, `guestRule` 2;
`HDVisTables::guestsHanging` and `hanging`). With `-log`, after the shell lines, one
`HDLOG cards level= group= with= one_sided=` line per pair of groups and one `HDLOG cards
level= cutout= one_sided= ms=` for the level; the `HDLOG level= vis=1` line ends in
`guests_hanging=`, with one `HDLOG visguest level= room= group= tris= box=
refused=hanging` line per refused guest; the `HDLOG flippair` line ends in `start=` (the
group drawn at the pair's place when the level starts), `classic=` (per state, 1 where the
state is drawn by its classic faces) and `kept=` (other groups' art the second shells keep
in the pair's rooms because one state lacks it). RoomProbe prints the cards lines,
`TrgProbe -vistable` ends in `guests_hanging=` with a `hanging` line per pair, and
ModernTest checks both rules.

**Why.** In RICH1 the catwalks showed two gratings at once, one shimmering through the
other. In RICH2's stairwell a door frame with an orange-brown panel hung on the brick
wall, with the door of the corridor it belongs to; beside the HD stairs stood a blue
classic flight with its railing on a dark steel floor. No flipmap pair is involved:
RICH1's room 72 and RICH2's rooms 14, 18 and 55 have no twin. The catwalk grating is group
72's floor, facing up, and group 70's ceiling under it, facing down, its bars turned the
other way; both are cut-outs, drawn two-sided, so both showed from either side and tied in
depth (157,683 pixels at one eye over the catwalk at 1,280 x 720). The door frame is group
55's art: room 55 is a corridor from room 49 to room 56 running through the stairwell's
column over room 18, with no portal, door or floor link to it, and 63 triangles of its art
hang 1,024 units below its floor into room 18's inside. Room 18 is under the sky - the
stairwell's windows show the city - and the guest table took the art of an unlinked room
for a room under the sky, as it must for ANDREA2's brick tower over room 232; listed, room
55 drew its art and its door there and walked on into room 49 behind it. This is the kind
of ghost the entry "Art in the air of an unlinked room draws inside its own window" (#181)
handled for ANDREA1, come in by the guest table. The blue flight, its railing and the dark
floor are room 18's and room 19's own classic stair and railing statics and floor faces,
where group 14's art, which draws the whole stairwell, has no flight and no landing: no
group's art lies on more than 14 of the flight's 39 points, and the classic floor there is
the one Lara walks on, so the static and stand rules keep them classic, as they should.

**How.** A card is asked when its group has cards and another group drawn with it - the
rooms of the two linked by a portal or a floor link (`g_air_links`), never a flipmap room
and its twin - has cards whose box meets its own, grown by 16 units; the cards then stand
in 256-unit world cells. A card is culled when its centroid and its three corners, each
pulled 1 unit inward, lie on such cards facing the other way (normals within `kShellDot`),
within 16 units of their plane and inside them with 1 unit to spare. From either side the
card facing the eye shows. Over the fifteen levels 1,138 triangles are drawn one-sided:
RICH1 828 (the catwalks over rooms 69, 70 and 72, and the grating between rooms 14 and
16), RICH3 216, TITLE 72, ANDY1 22; at the catwalk eye the tie falls from 157,683 pixels
to 693. A group's own cards back to back stay two-sided: culled as well, the tie fell by
26 pixels at most at four catwalk eyes and only the light of the card that shows changed.
The scan costs 108 ms at most (TITLE, 725,744 cut-out triangles), 22 ms or less in
thirteen levels. A flipmap room's card keeps its two sides, as a flipmap pair keeps what
one state does not carry. The guest rule refuses one pair over the fifteen levels, RICH2's
group 55 in room 18; every other guest stays, ANDREA2's tower among them. The second
shells and their flipmap refusal are unchanged: RICH3 room 23's pictures, before and after
its flip, are those of the base. `hd_build` 0 and `hd_vis` 0 are unchanged by
construction: the card scan runs only with the shell rooms handed in and the guest table
only on the visibility path; no classic path file changed.

### The game comes back after Ctrl+Alt+Del (#270)

2026-10-29.

**What.** After Ctrl+Alt+Del, the lock screen or a UAC prompt the game comes back when the
player returns to its window, in the look it had, HD included. Before, the picture stood
still with the sound playing on, and the process never recovered. A game parked behind
another window also wakes when its window is in front again without an activation message.

**Why.** A full dump of the frozen process showed the game thread parked at the start of
its scene (`HWBeginScene`, `game_parked` 1), the window thread idle in `GetMessage`, the
music stream and XAudio2 running. The secure desktop had lost the windowed D3D9 device. In
two frames running the device-lost road in `DXShowFrame` released the HD level and called
`Reset` on the game thread; the log's last lines, still in the dump's memory, give the
answer: `D3DERR_INVALIDCALL`. D3D9 refuses a `Reset` on any thread but the one that made
the device, the window's, and while any `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT` object lives; the second release
also forgot that the level was to be built HD again. Within the same millisecond of the
log `WM_ACTIVATE` (`WA_INACTIVE`) parked the game thread, and in the ten seconds to the
dump neither `WM_ACTIVATE` nor `WM_SETFOCUS` came, only a mouse move. Woken, the thread
would have met the refused `Reset` in every frame.

**How.** `specific/dxshell.cpp`: `DXShowFrame` resets nothing; it marks the loss
(`DXDeviceLost`) and posts `WM_APP_DEVICE` to the window once per loss. `DXRestoreDevice`
makes a new device as a new size makes it (`DXResizeToClient`: the HD level released with
the old device and built again on the new one); `DXDeviceCoop` and `DXCoopName` give
`TestCooperativeLevel`'s answer. `specific/winmain.cpp`: `WIN_DEVICE_TIMER` asks four
times a second whether the player is back in the window - the game thread not parked, the
window in front and not minimised, no film, no level loading - and whether the device can
be given back; then the game thread is held at the start of its scene, the device made
anew, the render states and the projection set and the thread let go. The park has one
partner, `WinWakeGame`, and every road back leads to it: `WA_ACTIVE` and `WA_CLICKACTIVE`,
`WM_SETFOCUS` and `WM_ACTIVATEAPP` with the window in front, `WM_CLOSE`, and
`WIN_PARK_TIMER`, which asks four times a second and wakes a parked thread as soon as its
window is the foreground window and not minimised, whatever message did or did not come.
The wake also comes past the film guard (a thread parked at a film's first frame would
have waited for good), a second `WA_INACTIVE` leaves a parked thread alone instead of
calling it stuck two seconds later, and Alt+Enter does nothing while the thread is parked
(its hold would have waited for ever). New `-log` lines, family `WINLOG`, one per message
or event: `activate`, `activateapp`, `focus set|kill`, `park result=`, `wake by=`,
`front`, `device lost coop=`, `device waits why=` and `device restore coop= ok=`.
`specific/drawbars.cpp`: its comments on the lost device. `MenuTest`'s gamma row checks
that no `Reset` is left. `docs/Engine-Manual.md` says how the game comes back and what the
lines show. Every mode takes the same road, the windowed state and full screen alike (full
screen is a windowed device too); a classic level gets its pages moved as after Alt+Enter,
an HD level its HD build again, with its seconds. No drawing code changed (`game/` and
`specific/hd/` are untouched), so the pictures of `hd_build` 0 and 1 are the previous
ones. The hang seam is unchanged: a parked thread ends its watch, and a thread that never
reaches its frame wait is caught as before.

**Decisions.** A new device rather than a `Reset` on the window thread: the reset needs
every `D3DPOOL_DEFAULT` object released, which nothing here can prove, and its failure is
the picture that never comes back; the new device is the road every Alt+Enter and new size
has taken since #247. The window does not pull itself to the front when nobody has it
after the secure desktop: a click into the picture or Alt+Tab is the player's way back,
and the `WINLOG front` line says when nobody has it.

**Commits.** `1ee2cc9a`, `c588b6f5` (the restore asks the window in front, not the mouse's
term).

### The Game Over menu takes the d-pad and the arrow keys (#271)

2026-10-29.

**What.** Under the Modern scheme the Game Over menu after Lara's death, and the load list
it opens, take the d-pad and the arrow keys beside the left stick, and Return whatever the
layout binds, as every other menu does; before, the stick alone moved the cursor there.
With `-log` a `MENULOG death` line names the menu's opening and each press its two rows
see.

**Why.** `S_Death` (`game/control.cpp`) runs a loop of its own around `S_UpdateInput` and
steps its two rows on `dbinput`'s edges, but it raised no term of `ModernMenuReadsPad`
(`specific/input.cpp`), so the input read the screen as play. Under Modern the movement
pair is then the left stick's own axes through the radial zone, which the d-pad never
writes into; the d-pad's own buttons reached only the roles bound to them, by default the
medipacks; the arrow keys and Return, the menus' fixed keys, are added only where the
predicate holds. The stick's bits came through as classic direction bits because the
movement seam stands aside on a call that follows no game step. `S_Death` never raised
`InventoryActive`, which also chooses the ring's object light, the pickup display and the
HD key. Tank reads the shared pair and its own arrow keys there and was right.

**How.** `game/control.cpp`: `DeathMenuActive`, raised by `S_Death` before its loop - the
two rows and the load list - and lowered on both of its ways out. `specific/input.cpp`:
`ModernMenuReadsPad` names it beside `InventoryActive` and the title, and the movement
seam carries it with the opposite sign, as the two must. The game-over menu then gets the
per-axis pair of stick and d-pad, the menu keys, and the rule that a medipack bound to the
d-pad rests while the d-pad steers a menu; its edge rule stays one step per press on
`dbinput`. Tank, the title, the pause menu, the ring and the options pages read what they
read before. `DeathLogStep` writes the line: `open` with `load=`, `scheme=` and
`method=`, then one `step` line per press with `step=` (up, down or select), `row=` and
`src=` (`key`, `pad` for the d-pad or a pad button, `stick`; `MenuStepSource` in
`game/menu_nav.h`), for which `specific/input.cpp` keeps the pad pair's own direction
bits of the last call (`InputPadDirection`). MenuTest's `death_menu_pad` holds the rule;
`docs/Engine-Manual.md` says it.

**Commits.** `94ef93a1`.

### The diving suit's thrusters on the HD body (#272)

2026-10-29.

**What.** In Deepsea Dive with the HD path, the diving suit's two propulsion units now
keep the place they have on the classic suit against the back of whatever body the
wardrobe or the outfit menu puts on her: 22 to 26 units nearer her on the bodies with a
backpack (24 on the Antarctica outfit), 50 to 74 on those without one; on the HD diving
suit they move 1 unit out, as far as its back lies behind the classic suit's. The mist
out of their nozzles goes with them. The height on her back and the distance from her
spine stay the classic ones.

**Why.** DrawLara__5 hangs the units - LARA_EXTRA_MESH1, a separate object of the level,
drawn twice on the torso's matrix at (-80, -192, -160) and (80, -192, -160) and turned
about x by `subsuit.XRot` - with numbers made for the classic suit's hard shell. No .TRM
of either install models the units on their own (the cutscenes' EXTRA5_SUBSUIT_FULL has
them grown into its torso), so over the HD composite they stay the classic mesh, and on
any outfit but the HD diving suit they floated a shell's thickness off her back.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp` hands the plan the level's classic LARA_EXTRA_MESH1
mesh and the skin's torso mesh wherever DrawLara__5 draws her. `specific/hd/hd_lara.cpp`
(`HDLaraThrusters`) measures both backs alike, in the torso node's frame with the units at
rest: the most backward point under the units' box, leaving out what lies inside the box -
on the classic suit the corners of the block between the units, whose sides they rest
against. The classic back comes from the torso mesh at the plan, the worn one from the
body file's node 7, each vertex on its heaviest bone, while the file is read; the level
build keeps the difference, rounded. `specific/drawlara.cpp` adds it to both translations
while the composite draws her (`HDLaraThrusterShift`), `game/subsuit.cpp` to the mist's
origin. JOBY4 measures the classic back at -112, OUTFIT_TR3_ANTARC at -88 (shift 24),
nineteen more bodies with a backpack at -86 to -90, the thirty-one without one at -38 to
-62 and OUTFIT_SUBSUIT at -113 (shift -1). The difference and not the units set onto her
back: they turn by up to 45 degrees, their corners then reach 43 units further forward,
and the classic suit leaves them 15 units of air at rest - the difference keeps that
relation in every pose. An `HDLOG lara thrusters` line per level build names the body,
both backs, the shift and what was measured; ModelProbe `-thrusters` prints the same for
every body of the wardrobe and draws the units, `-thrustersclassic` at the classic
numbers. `docs/Engine-Manual.md` says it. With the HD path off, or `hd_build` 0, the shift
is 0 and the units and their mist are the classic ones. The verdict census over the
fifteen levels is unchanged.

2026-10-30.
