from_mesh= tris= shift= turn= faces= face_tris=` line per copy; the level's statics line
ends in `copies= copied= copy_ms=`, the `HDLOG room=` line in `copied=` (the triangles
copied into the room's place) and a copied static's line in `copied`. RoomProbe prints the
same `artcopy` lines (`-artcopy`, `-artcopytable`), and ModernTest checks the rule, on
RICH2's fifteen flights among others.

**Why.** In RICH2's stairwell - rooms 14 to 19, all of their art in room 14's group - a
flight in a blue classic texture, its blue railing and a dark classic plate floor at its
foot stood among the art's steel flights. The stair (slot 60) has fifteen flights with
railings (slot 66) and posts (slot 4), and the art models twelve of the flights: rooms 16,
18 and 19 each have one it leaves out (12, 14 and 12 of 39 points on the art), with four
railings and two posts - nine statics drawn classic, and the landing floors of rooms 18
and 19 kept classic beside them (#194). The same slots stand at the same turn one turn of
the stair (4,096 units) above or below, where the art models them: room 15's flights are
what rooms 18 and 19 lack, 4,096 units lower, and room 14's what room 16 lacks, 4,096
units higher - a shift, with no turn and no mirror.

**How.** A static is a donor when every one of its points stands in a 256-unit cell
holding a corner of its group's art, and a target when fewer than nine twentieths do (in a
room drawn by its own art also fewer than a twentieth of its box's cells) and no other
group's art holds it either. A target's donor is a donor of its slot in a room the same
group draws, whole quarter turns from it: no turn first, then the nearest (the three
distances summed), then the first in the level's order. The art must model the slot alike
at its donors - the triangles wholly inside each donor's box grown by 32 units at most
three halves of the fewest - or the slot gets no copy. The targets of one motion take
together the group's triangles every corner of which lies in their donors' grown boxes, so
that a handrail running on through the boxes of two flights and a post comes whole; less
those that are a room's surface at the donor or at the target (lying whole on a classic
face, or with every corner within 16 units of a face's plane and 512 of the face, facing
its way within a cosine of 0.98) and less those whose image would stand on the group's art
already there (more than half of its corners, centroid and samples within 16 units of a
triangle facing its way). A classic face of the target's room touching its box, whose
image at the donor is a face carrying the group's art - the landing at a flight's end -,
takes that art too and then falls to the art as any covered face. The vertices go in after
the group's last vertex and the triangles at the end of their run; every later index and
run start moves up, as the sky's caps do. A copy keeps the donor's baked light and not its
new place's: the flights come in at about 41 on the first colour, as at their donors,
while the art round their new places reads 61 to 76, and warmer in rooms 18 and 19; the
railings and posts land within about 20 of it either way.

On RICH2: nine copies, 5,881 triangles and 8,192 vertices; the nine statics are answered
by the art afterwards (seven `art`, two `groups`), every point of each on it. Room 18
keeps no classic face (16 of 16 covered, its landing taking 58 triangles), room 19 one (14
of 15, its landing taking 54). Where flights were copied the fight of group 14's art (the
pixels that change when it is pushed by 1/2,000 of its distance either way) rises at two
eyes from 3,672 to 3,962 and from 1,738 to 2,558 pixels; it stays with the art drawn
alone, and leaving out the copied triangles that touch the art already there takes fewer
than 90 of those pixels away: they lie on the copied gratings themselves, near-coincident
surfaces of the art's own flight. The card census stays 1,138 one-sided triangles; RICH2's
cut-out triangles grow from 60,123 to 64,991, none one-sided. Over the other fourteen
levels nothing is copied and the build's fingerprint and every static's answer are the
base's: their few targets have no donor, all but RICH3's room 79 mesh 2 (slot 46), which
is refused: its three donors hold 260 to 15,290 triangles round them, the art models other
objects there, and a copy would have put another object, in another light, into its niche.
The rule costs 132 ms on RICH2, about 4 % of its build, and 5 to 56 ms elsewhere. Room
16's sixteen kept ceiling faces at the top of the shaft stay classic and black by
decision: the open top is meant to suggest that the shaft goes on into RICH3. Room 19's
wall square (face 8) stays classic: the stair repeats every 4,096 units and the rooms
every 1,536, so no face at the donor has its corners. Room 14's flat wall square (mesh 2,
slot 7) is no copy's case: all nine of its points lie on the art, whose wall stands 1 to 8
units from its plane, and the statics' rule draws it classic by its box's cells (1 of 25),
a flat static on a cell boundary. `hd_build` 0 and `hd_vis` 0 are unchanged by
construction: the statics are handed to the build on the visibility path only, and without
them nothing is copied; no classic path file changed.

**Commits.** `14b9afa5`.

### The diving suit's thrusters hang from her shoulders on the HD body (#276)

2026-10-30.

**What.** In Deepsea Dive with the HD path, the diving suit's two propulsion units now
hang from the shoulders of the body she wears: their top stands at the top of its torso,
where it stood 76 to 91 units higher before, beside her head. On the Antarctica outfit
they come down 79 units and reach from her shoulders to 42 units under the bottom of her
backpack (-68 in the torso's frame), so they now cover its lower half as well, which they
left free before; the backpack's rear face stays 11 units before them. On the HD diving
suit they stay where they were. The mist out of their nozzles goes with them. The move
onto her back of #272, their distance from her spine and their depth stay as they were.

**Why.** #272 kept the classic suit's height. On the classic suit the units' tops stand at
-276, 55 units under the top of its torso (-331), a shell that reaches far over the
shoulders of a slim body: the top of a slim body's torso lies at -185 to -200, so the
units stood above her shoulders, beside her head, and not at her shoulder blades.

**How.** `specific/hd/hd_lara.cpp` reads the top of the worn torso with its back
(`HDLaraThrusterBack`: the least y of the body file's node 7, each vertex on its heaviest
bone), and the level build settles both moves in one place (`HDLaraThrusterSettle` in
`specific/hd/hd_lara.h`): the move down is that top minus the units' top at rest, rounded
half away from zero as the shift is, and never up - a torso whose top stands above the
units' keeps them where they are, which is the HD diving suit's (-330).
`HDLaraThrusterShift` (`specific/hd/hd_laradraw.cpp`) hands back both moves at once, so
that no caller can take the one and lose the other: `specific/drawlara.cpp` adds the move
down to both units' y, `game/subsuit.cpp` to the mist's origin and its two targets. JOBY4
measures OUTFIT_TR3_ANTARC's top at -196.6 (down 79), the nineteen other bodies with a
backpack at -188.5 to -199.6 (76 to 87), the thirty-one without one at -185.2 to -196.6
(79 to 91) and OUTFIT_SUBSUIT at -329.6 (0). The back the shift was measured against at
the classic height holds at the new one: every body keeps 14.5 to 15.5 units of air
before the units, the classic suit's 15, and no point of any torso lies inside them but
the HD diving suit's block corners, as before. Turned by up to 45 degrees, a corner rises
4 units over the top at rest. The `HDLOG lara thrusters` line carries the move as
`shift=0,<down>,<back>` and ends on `hd_top=`, `classic_top=` and `down=`; ModelProbe
`-thrusters` prints both tops and the move down for every body of the wardrobe, the air
at the new height and the worn body against its pack, and `-thrustersdown <units>` draws
the units at another height. ModernTest `thruster_move` (12 checks) holds the arithmetic;
`docs/Engine-Manual.md` says it. With the HD path off, or `hd_build` 0, both moves are 0
and the units and their mist are the classic ones. A second height, the units' centre a
third of the torso's height under its top (50 down on the Antarctica outfit), was drawn
to compare and not built. The verdict census over the fifteen levels is unchanged.

**Addendum.** The air bubbles the suit loses once JOBY4's cutscene 40 has played
(`TriggerAirBubbles` in `game/subsuit.cpp`; `game/laramisc.cpp` drains her air from then
on) leave it between the two units, at their height and depth - (0, -192, -160) on the
torso, the midpoint of the units' own two points - and so are a third reader of the
moves: their start and their aim move with the units as the mist does, and they keep
their path but rise from between the units rather than from the water beside her head
(on the Antarctica outfit 79 lower and 24 nearer her). ModernTest `thruster_wiring` (7
checks) counts in the engine's text that all three readers ask for both moves and that
none of the suit's numbers for the units' height and depth stands without its move.

**Commits.** `3c4f255d`.

## 3. Randomizer changes since Beta 1.0

The randomizer itself - `TR5Randomizer/`, the CLI `Randomize.exe` and the GUI
`TR5Randomizer.exe` - is this project's own work from the first line, so it owes
nobody a GPLv3 section 5(a) notice and has no record of the kind above. What
changed in it since the public Beta 1.0 is listed here by task number.
Forty-three files under `TR5Randomizer/src` changed in that span, five of them
new.

- **#123 - the HD markers.** `Tr5Level.cpp` / `.h`, `ApplyPatch.cpp` / `.h`,
  `Randomize.cpp` and `gui/Main.cpp`: the randomizer writes the HD room markers
  into the `.TRC` so the engine can find the right room again after the levels
  have been shuffled, keeps a marker room's HD art across the portal cut, and
  carries material 16 as the still-water surface.
- **#137 - secret lists.** `SecretList.cpp`, `ApplyPatch.cpp`, `Tr5Level.cpp` /
  `.h`: two further forms in the secret list, and geometry built for rooms that
  have none.
- **#141 - where an enemy may stand.** `Randomizer.cpp` / `.h`,
  `ApplyPatch.cpp` / `.h`, `Tr3Source.cpp` / `.h`, `Tr5Level.cpp` / `.h`: the
  headroom check, the Hydra's footprint of five free tiles out of nine, and its
  doubled weight in the kind roll.
- **#142 - the data baked into the binary.** `EmbeddedData.cpp` and `.h` are new
  and **generated** by `Preparation/Tools/EmbedData.ps1` - the fifteen
  `zones_*.json` and the two checksum tables as zlib streams, 7,186 lines.
  `core/DataFile.cpp` is new and hand-written: it unpacks them, looks a name up
  and implements the rule that a real file in `data\` wins and the baked copy is
  the floor. It is kept apart from the generated file on purpose, so
  regenerating the tables cannot overwrite logic. `DataFolder.cpp` / `.h` gained
  `loadChecksumsText()`, a second entry point for callers that hold the checksum
  text rather than a path.
- **#144 - the weather roll.** `Config.cpp` / `.h`, `Randomizer.cpp` / `.h`,
  `ApplyPatch.cpp` / `.h`, `Tr5Level.cpp` / `.h`, `Randomize.cpp`,
  `gui/Main.cpp`, `gui/Language.cpp`: the option, the roll and the level fields
  it writes. Six of the thirteen playable levels can show it.
- **#146 - the cyborg in the cross pool.** `Randomizer.cpp` and
  `gui/Language.cpp`: slot 469 joins the pool the cross mix draws from.
- **#147 - the flipmap mirror.** `ApplyPatch.cpp` / `.h`, `Randomizer.cpp`,
  `Randomize.cpp`, `gui/Main.cpp`: an enemy waker moved into a room is mirrored
  into that room's flipmap partner, and (#147b) a moved key trigger with it.
- **#153 - the Mods folder.** `Config.cpp` / `.h`, `Randomizer.cpp` / `.h`,
  `Tr5Level.cpp` / `.h`, `ApplyPatch.cpp`, `Randomize.cpp`, `gui/Main.cpp`,
  `gui/Language.cpp`: the randomizer rolls out of the same scan the engine's
  wardrobe uses, and knows again when there are no scanned outfits.
- **#172 - the push audit.** `core/BuildId.h`: `RANDO_BUILD_ID` 18 to 19 with a
  ledger line naming the four commits since Beta 1.0 that move where an enemy
  may stand (`098e0f6`, `28380e8`, `a886a1b`, `332dedd`); the number is printed
  in the launcher and written into `spoiler.txt` and is not part of the seed.
  `core/Tr5Tr3Import.cpp` got the project's licence header, the only source file
  under `src/` that lacked it. `gui/Main.cpp` and `gui/Language.cpp` lost the
  never-wired checkbox *Patch remaster textures* with its tooltip and both
  language rows, and the folder picker's German title now goes through the
  translation table like every other string. `TR5Randomizer/.gitignore` keeps
  the tracked `build/b1.bat` and `b2.bat` out of its own blanket ignore. The
  change is harmless in the sense `Preparation/Verification.md` prescribes: the
  same seed 380 through the old and the new build gives byte-identical `.trc`
  and `.hdm` for a bare `andy1` run and for a `rich2` run with the enemy, weapon
  and cross-mix switches on.
- **#214 - ANDREA2's arch window.** `core/LevelFix.cpp` / `.h`,
  `core/Tr5Level.cpp` / `.h`: a new kind of level repair, `SightWindow`, writes
  on every run the view window between ANDREA2's rooms 231 and 102 that the
  level lacks, so the portal walk no longer refuses the rooms over the arch and
  the clear colour no longer shows there; `Tr5Level::addSightWindow` writes one
  portal record per room and nothing else, sharing `appendPortalRecord`, split
  out of `addViewWindow`. ANDREA2's `.trc` gains the two records and the counts,
  offsets and sizes they move (`a8d49552`, `08482483`, `b321047c`, merge
  `2409e079`).
- **#223 - RICH2's floor lasers.** `core/LevelFix.cpp` / `.h`,
  `core/Tr5Level.cpp` / `.h`: a new kind, `TriggerOneShot`, sets on every run
  the one-shot bit in the setup word of the two triggers in RICH2's room 5 that
  wake the floor lasers, item 34, so that walking back through room 5 after the
  water and before the switch can no longer re-arm them for good; `FixCheck`
  holds the result against the file. RICH2's `.trc` differs in those two bytes
  and nothing else (against `2409e079`; `2d4dcd4e`, `c7c0ef51`).
- **#230 - the TR3 sources.** `Randomize.cpp`, `core/DataFolder.cpp` / `.h`,
  `core/EmbeddedData.cpp`, `core/Tr3Source.cpp` / `.h`, `gui/Main.cpp`,
  `Preparation/Tr3Checksums.csv`: TR3 is read from the Remastered folder `3` too; one
  presence test serves the GUI, the planner and the guest-free CLI; a file hash names the
  edition; Copy drops stale `.hdm` files; `spoiler.txt` gains `TR3 SOURCES` (`58c3be5e`,
  `7c546579`, `e5f67a87`, `ba3608b5`, `9f7bd23e`, `7ef31994`, `f89a2564`).
- **#231 - audit round B1.** `core/BuildId.h`: `RANDO_BUILD_ID` 19 to 20
  (`0.20`), because #214 and #223 change what a seed writes (`a8d49552`,
  `08482483`, `2d4dcd4e`), and `RANDO_VERSION_STRING` `Beta_3.0`;
  `gui/TR5Randomizer.rc` carries `Beta_3.0` with `FILEVERSION` 3,0,0,0
  (`19f4168f`). The number is printed in the launcher and written into
  `spoiler.txt` and is not part of the seed or of any level file. The same
  seed 380 through the build before and after the bump, over the thirteen
  campaign levels, once with no switches and once with `mix cross allsanity 8
  weapons items20 weather`: all 78 `.trc`, `.hdm` and log files byte-identical.
- **#244 - RICH2's HK wait.** `core/LevelFix.cpp` / `.h`, `core/Tr5Level.cpp` / `.h`: a
  new kind of level entry, `TriggerTimer` (`kTriggerTimers`: a level, a sector, the
  trigger kind and the byte it expects, the byte it writes), sets on every run the timer
  byte of the HEAVY trigger under RICH2's X-ray controller, room 12 (2,3), from 240 to
  255, so the cutscene in which Lara puts the HK down follows the headset call after one
  second instead of sixteen, the wait having no purpose in a shuffled run. The trigger
  stores the byte as a signed char times 30 frames, so 255 is -30, one second.
  `Tr5Level::setTriggerTimer` checks the kind and the byte, refuses a chain another sector
  reads, and writes only the setup word's low byte (`3EF0 -> 3EFF` in the chain words
  `8504 3EF0 800B`); the entry sets the pace of a shuffled run rather than mending a fault
  of Core's, and the file's opening comment says it holds such a place too. `FixCheck`
  reports the kind. `core/BuildId.h`: `RANDO_BUILD_ID` 20 to 21 (`0.21`), because the
  entry changes what a seed writes on RICH2; `Preparation/Verification.md` gains the
  bullet for this kind. The same seed 380 through the build of `06961e27` and the new one,
  plain and with `mix cross allsanity 8 weapons`: every `.trc` and `.hdm` byte-identical
  but RICH2's `.trc`, which differs in that one byte (`42a49f2d`, `f0c84774`, `79987926`).
- **#248 - the executables declare what they are: manifest, version block, Control Flow
  Guard; the release lists their SHA-256.** `Program.manifest` is new, the application
  manifest that `TR5Randomizer.exe`, `Randomize.exe` and `FixCheck.exe` embed as resource
  1: `asInvoker`, the `supportedOS` GUIDs of Windows 7 to 11, `longPathAware`, no DPI
  awareness. `Tools.rc` is new, the manifest and the version block of the two
  command-line programs, which had no resources at all. `gui/TR5Randomizer.rc` embeds the
  manifest, and its version block reads `FILEVERSION` 4,0,0,0 in step with `Beta_4.0`
  and names `CompanyName` ChrisChanSan. `b1.bat`, `b2.bat` and `bfc.bat` compile and link
  with `/guard:cf` and link with `/CETCOMPAT`; `Preparation/Tools/BuildRelease.ps1` writes
  `SHA256SUMS.txt` into the package root. The same seed 380 through the build of
  `24ea0290` and the new one, over the thirteen campaign levels, once with no switches and
  once with `mix cross allsanity 8 weapons items20 weather`: all 78 `.trc`, `.hdm` and log
  files byte-identical.

- **#258 - no pickup under a carrier.** `core/Randomizer.cpp`: the roll bars the
  sector of every enemy and every searchable crate that stands there at level
  start, since the engine hands a pickup within half a sector to that carrier at
  the first frame and a dormant enemy never gives it back - a key under one was
  a lost playthrough. The burning roots of Gallows Tree go invisible when the
  heart has left them, because the engine finds the heart by its kind and would
  lift it to the roots' height wherever it lies. `core/Randomizer.h`: the list
  of carriers is the engine's own now - it lacked SWAT_PLUS, Mafia, Sailor,
  Crane Guy, Scientist and the two slots past the file boundary. Trajan's
  Markets' puzzle 4 keeps its OCB 5 when it travels and the guardian's trigger
  stays as Core wrote it: the guardian sets the puzzle's height by item number
  when it explodes, and a puzzle moved with OCB 0 sank into its new floor;
  hidden until the guardian falls, it now lands where the roll put it. The
  earlier void of that trigger is gone (`core/LevelFix.h`,
  `Preparation/Tools/ZoneAnalysis.ps1`). `docs/Randomizer-Manual.md` says all
  three.

## 4. Building this yourself

The published binary need not be trusted. Either:

- build from this tree directly - open `tomb5.sln`, configuration `Release`,
  platform `x86`; the result is `release/PCtomb5.exe`. `Release|x64` builds the
  same sources (#143) and is there for whoever wants it; `x86` is the shipped
  configuration and the one every measurement in this record was made on. The
  39 `TOMB5/specific/hd/hd_shader/*.inc` are `fxc` output of the eleven `.hlsl`
  beside them and are tracked, so nothing has to be regenerated to get a working
  binary - but after editing a shader, run
  `Preparation/Tools/Diagnose/bshader.bat` (`be.bat` carries the same guard and
  regenerates them; a build from the Visual Studio window does not check them); or
- start from upstream <https://github.com/Trxyebeep/TOMB5> and apply these
  changes on top. Every change is a commit in this repository, so
  `git diff "$(git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD)" HEAD -- "TOMB5 Code"`
  is the complete change set. It asks git for the repository's first commit -
  the unmodified decompilation - rather than naming a hash, deliberately: this
  history has been rewritten before, and a written-down hash does not survive
  that.

Unlike upstream, this build produces a **single self-contained executable**.
Upstream ships `PCTomb5.exe` plus `tomb5.dll` - **the upstream TOMB5 project's
own DLL, built from this very source tree's ancestor, and not the `tomb5.dll` of
the Tomb Raider IV-VI Remaster, which this project never opens, links or reads**
(the two names are spelled the same and mean different files). The upstream DLL
carries the game code and does its work from `DllMain`; that is why upstream
updates can ship as "dll only". This fork builds the Win32 target as an ordinary
application with its own `WinMain`, so there is no DLL.

**No game data is included, here or in any release made from this tree.** Tomb
Raider Chronicles itself remains the property of its rights holders; a copy of
the game is needed to play.
